structured_extraction.program_name: Frostburg Main Street Structural Stabilization Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides targeted financial support to address structural repairs and stabilization work for at-risk historic buildings located along Frostburg's Main Street corridor. Eligible work includes foundation repairs, framing, roof support beams, roofing, and other structural improvements to the four walls and interior walls of commercial and mixed-use properties. The funding comes from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Strategic Demolition Fund through the FY 2025 State Revitalization Program Awards. The program helps bring vacant or deteriorating properties back into productive use through structural stabilization and revitalization.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants to cover structural stabilization and repair costs for eligible buildings. Allegany County Economic Community Development received $250,000 in state funding under the Strategic Demolition Fund to support these projects. Grants are provided to support structural stabilization work on historic Main Street properties, enabling property owners to restore and redevelop vacant or deteriorating buildings. Funding is competitive, and a review committee evaluates applications based on a project rubric to determine awards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications will open later this summer
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit property owners in good standing with the city, county, and state who own commercial or mixed-use buildings located within Frostburg's Main Street district.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Structural repairs and stabilization work including foundation repairs, framing, roof support beams, roofing, and other improvements to the four walls and interior walls needed to make buildings safe and stable for renovation and reuse.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within Frostburg's Main Street district in Frostburg, Maryland in Allegany County.
requirements_list: Be located within Frostburg's Main Street district
Be commercial or mixed-use (for example, first floor storefront with residential units above)
Be owned by a for-profit or non-profit, tax-paying entity in good standing with the city, county, and state
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: City staff manages applications and intake. County staff oversees fund distribution and compliance. A review committee evaluates applications based on a project rubric. Interested property owners are urged to begin gathering information about their properties' structural needs and project timelines.

Funds may be used for structural repairs, system upgrades, and conversion to residential, commercial, or mixed-use space. Example: The McMullen Building project received $250,000 to support adaptive reuse of a historic building into residential apartments and commercial space.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides forgivable loans to small businesses in Allegany County, helping new companies establish themselves and existing companies grow to create more jobs, increase their ability to sell products outside the area, or improve their local community presence. Companies that meet their success metrics can have up to half of their loan forgiven over the agreed-upon term. Loans range from $10,000 to $50,000 with low interest rates. The county may defer payments for up to six months after the business receives the loan.
structured_extraction.agency: Allegany County Economic and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers low-interest loans from $10,000 to $50,000. Businesses can have up to 50% of the loan forgiven if they meet performance goals, such as job creation. Loans over $40,000 require a one-to-one match from the business. The county may defer payments for up to six months after the business receives the loan.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for small, for-profit businesses in Allegany County with fewer than 15 full-time employees that are ready to expand.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: You can use the loan to buy tangible assets that help your business grow, such as equipment and furniture. You cannot use the funds for staff salaries, buying or improving an existing building, or constructing a new building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Your business must have a physical location in Allegany County. You must own the property or have a long-term commercial lease. A home-based business can apply if its expansion plan includes moving to a commercial location.
requirements_list: Business must be based in Allegany County
Must meet specified success metrics to qualify for loan forgiveness
Must be a for-profit entity in good standing with Allegany County and the State of Maryland.
Must have fewer than 15 full-time employees.
Must have a physical presence in Allegany County.
Must receive a formal invitation from Allegany County Economic and Community Development to apply.
A 1:1 funding match is required for loans over $40,000.
Must provide a business plan approved by the local Small Business Development Center.
Funds must be spent within 24 months of loan approval to qualify for forgiveness.

The committee then submits its recommendations to the County Commissioners for final approval.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $50,000 for research projects developing new environmental technology. The program offers a grant that matches a company's research costs, with the grant paying for up to half of a project's total cost and a maximum grant amount of $50,000. Funds can be used to pay for costs of research or lab use contracted through the Appalachian Laboratory.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Research conducted at University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science Appalachian Laboratory in Allegany County. Applicant businesses must have a physical location in Allegany County through ownership or a long-term commercial lease. requirements_list: Project must be conducted at UMCES Appalachian Laboratory
Must focus on development of new environmental technology

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the Allegany County Economic and Community Development team to discuss your project. structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for full-time employees of Anne Arundel County who work as 911 specialists, including those who receive and process emergency requests, provide support functions related to emergency requests, or dispatch emergency services. The credit reduces property tax liability on County property. Eligible applicants must own a dwelling in Anne Arundel County and use it as their principal residence. The credit is available for up to ten taxable years, with a maximum credit of $2,500 or the total county tax due on the dwelling, whichever is less. A 1% administrative fee may be assessed. The credit is renewable annually upon application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit that reduces county property tax liability on a dwelling owned and used as principal residence by eligible 911 specialists. The credit amount is the lesser of $2,500 or the total county tax due on the dwelling. A 1% administrative fee may be assessed. The credit is available for up to ten taxable years total and is renewable annually upon application.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the tax credit is sought. For example, for taxable year beginning July 1, 2026, application must be filed by April 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time Anne Arundel County employees who work as 911 specialists
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit reduction on county property taxes for a dwelling used as principal residence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland. The dwelling must be located in Anne Arundel County and used as the applicant's principal residence.
requirements_list: Must be employed full-time by Anne Arundel County as a 911 specialist
Duties must include receiving and processing 911 emergency requests, support functions related to emergency requests, or dispatching emergency services
Must file application by specified deadline
Completed at least one year of full-time employment with Anne Arundel County as a 9-1-1 specialist
Own the dwelling to which the credit applies
Use the property as principal residence
Occupy the property for more than six months of the taxable year
Eligible for Maryland state tax credit under § 9-105 of Tax-Property Article
Credit cannot be combined with any other optional property tax credits
Must reapply each year for renewal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the 9-1-1 Specialist Property Tax Credit Application form provided by the County Controller's office. Submit the application on or before April 1 of the year immediately preceding the taxable year for which the credit is sought.

structured_extraction.program_description: A matching grant program providing up to $10,000 in funding to farm-based business owners and commercial watermen in Anne Arundel County to support projects including new fencing, purchase of plant stock, livestock, or equipment, and infrastructure upgrades such as greenhouses, pole barns, timber harvest equipment, storage facilities, barn construction and repairs, cattle handling infrastructure, crab pots, shucking stations, oyster larvae equipment, cold storage, and deer fencing for produce production. Funds also support vehicles for direct-to-consumer sales. Grants support operational improvements, business growth, increased revenue, employee retention or expansion, increased efficiency, increased local-grown food supply, or agricultural education opportunities. Grant awardees must contribute at least 50% of their own money to the project as a one-to-one match.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants of up to $10,000 for eligible farm-based business and commercial watermen projects. Grant awardees must contribute at least 50% of their own money to the project as a one-to-one match. Matching funds may not include labor or state and federal grants or cost share. Funds can be used for fencing, livestock, plant stock, equipment and infrastructure upgrades such as greenhouses, pole barns, timber harvest equipment, storage facilities, barn construction and repairs, cattle handling infrastructure, crab pots, shucking stations, oyster larvae equipment, cold storage, deer fencing for produce production, and vehicles for direct-to-consumer sales. Administrative expenses, events and décor are not eligible. Proof of project completion is due within one year of the grant award. Grant applications are numerically scored based on impact to increase revenue, increase or retain employees, expand operations or increase efficiency, increase local-grown food supply or provide agricultural education opportunities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application period for the third round of ABIG funding ran from November 1 – December 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers, farm-based business owners, and commercial watermen in Anne Arundel County seeking to grow and improve their operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fencing, livestock, plant stock, equipment and infrastructure upgrades including greenhouses, pole barns, timber harvest equipment, storage facilities, barn construction and repairs, cattle handling infrastructure, crab pots, shucking stations, oyster larvae equipment, cold storage, and deer fencing for produce production to support operational improvements and business expansion. Vehicles for direct-to-consumer sales are also eligible. Administrative expenses, events and décor are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be residents of Anne Arundel County and own and operate a farm or commercial watermen operation in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Farms must be agriculturally tax assessed by the State of Maryland, or commercial watermen must possess a Commercial TFL License with proof of docking of the harvesting vessel in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a resident of Anne Arundel County

Own or operate a farm in Anne Arundel County that is agriculturally tax assessed by the State of Maryland, or possess a Commercial TFL License with proof of docking of harvesting vessel in Anne Arundel County
Applicants must submit a letter of reference from Anne Arundel Soil Conservation District, University of Maryland Extension, Anne Arundel County Farm Bureau or 4-H/FFA Leader
Grant awardee must contribute at least 50% of their own money to the project
Matching funds may not include labor or state and federal grants or cost share
Proof of completion of the project is due within one year of the grant award

Applications evaluated based on potential to boost revenue, create or retain jobs, expand operations, improve efficiency, increase supply of locally grown food, or offer agricultural education opportunities
Submit all project details including contractor or product estimates if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an application during the designated application period with project details, contractor or product estimates if applicable, and a letter of reference from Anne Arundel Soil Conservation District, University of Maryland Extension, Anne Arundel County Farm Bureau or 4-H/FFA Leader. Each grant application is numerically scored based on its impact to increase revenue, increase or retain employees, expand operations or increase efficiency, increase local-grown food supply or provide agricultural education opportunities. Selected applicants receive grant awards.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Agricultural and Woodland Preservation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County's comprehensive local preservation program established in 1990 to protect agricultural and forest land in perpetuity. The program voluntarily acquires permanent easements on agricultural and woodland properties, allowing property owners to sell conservation easements to the county, the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), or Rural Legacy program, or participate in a district designation that provides tax benefits. The program operates through multiple components: (1) County Agricultural and Woodland Districts - establishes districts for land devoted to agriculture or woodlands with minimum 10-year commitment periods and tax credits; (2) Purchase of Development Rights (easement) program - the County pays 60% of appraised fair market value for an agricultural or woodland preservation easement on an eligible property, with recent easement offers ranging from $8,000 to $11,000 per acre, subject to county funding availability and contingent on approval by the County Executive and County Council; (3) Tax Credit program - provides property tax credits to qualifying landowners in Agricultural or Woodland Districts for 10-year periods (renewable for additional 10-year periods); (4) Options to sell conservation easements to MALPF or Rural Legacy program. Landowners receive cash payments at settlement for selling development rights and can continue agricultural and timber use of the land. The program has protected 6,583 acres to date.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County offers multiple forms of assistance: (1) Easement Purchase - County pays 60% of the appraised fair market value for development rights on an agricultural or woodland property. Recent offers ranged from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre, subject to county funding availability. Landowners receive cash payments at settlement. (2) Property Tax Credits - Participants in County Agricultural and Woodland Districts receive 10-year real property tax credits (renewable for additional 10-year periods). Early termination results in liability for all back taxes plus interest. (3) Alternative Options - Property owners can also sell conservation easements to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) or Rural Legacy program. MALPF compensates based on the lower of: asking price, calculated easement value, county cap, or 75% of appraised value. Rural Legacy program offers grants to acquire easements with potential increased value for voluntary habitat enhancement or stream buffer measures.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Watershed Restoration and Forestry Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds on-the-ground watershed restoration and forestry activities in Anne Arundel County and the City of Annapolis. The program provides annual funding for projects that reduce pollutants and stormwater flowing into local waterways, implement cost-effective reforestation and greening efforts, increase protected forested land, treat and filter pollutants from impervious surfaces, and improve water and air quality, habitat, and tree cover through on-the-ground watershed restoration practices, forestry initiatives, and resident engagement in restoring and protecting local rivers and streams. Grants are awarded to certified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, individuals, and government agencies to implement projects on nonprofit property, private property, public property, or public school properties with landowner support. The program supports the County's 20% impervious restoration goal and Chesapeake Bay TMDL compliance. Total funding of $1,000,000 is available for awards in Anne Arundel County and $300,000 available for awards in the City of Annapolis.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Total funding of $1,000,000 available for awards in Anne Arundel County and $300,000 available for awards in the City of Annapolis. Individual funding requests generally do not exceed $300,000. Requests larger than $300,000 require prior approval from the Chesapeake Bay Trust. Matching or leveraged resources are not required but are viewed favorably. In-kind match funding through experienced partner expertise is welcomed. The program provides annual funding for watershed restoration and forestry projects, including stormwater management, reforestation, greening efforts, pollutant reduction in waterways, and protected forested land expansion through on-the-ground restoration practices implemented on community, public, nonprofit, private, or school properties. Projects may include stream restoration, shoreline stabilization, impervious removal, septic upgrades, and other Best Management Practices (BMPs). Applicants must account for permit fees and bonds for projects requiring local, state, or federal permits.

Projects may include stream restoration, shoreline stabilization, impervious removal, septic upgrades, and other Best Management Practices (BMPs). Applicants must account for permit fees and bonds for projects requiring local, state, or federal permits.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provided financial assistance to Anne Arundel County small businesses and non-profit entities affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, funded through the county's allotment of CARES Act funding. The program offered grants of up to $10,000 per qualified applicant for reimbursement or purchase of personal protective equipment, sanitation products, technology for online sales and customer communication, mobile or delivery operations, signage, training for compliance with regulations, and other services to enhance safety practices and customer engagement. Eligible uses included protective barriers, digital signage, technology for wellness scans and e-commerce, delivery vehicles and equipment, and professional consultation services. Grants approved during the program period from June 3 through July 24, 2020 totaled over $5 million for more than 790 small businesses, with approved grants averaging approximately $6,370. The program supports projects that foster safe and vibrant community environments, support spaces that promote emotional well-being, and enhance community disaster preparedness and resilience. The program builds on the legacy of BGE's former Emergency Response and Safety Grants program and has collectively provided over $3.5 million to 671 community safety and emergency response programs during the past 13 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $2,500 to $10,000 are available to eligible organizations, with grant periods running June 2025 to June 2026 and ongoing cycles. The program is now in its third year of operation and eligible 501(c)(3) organizations are prioritized.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 16, 2025 for 2025 round; March 22, 2026 for subsequent rounds
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, for-profit entities, and community groups working on community safety, emotional well-being, emergency preparedness, and resilience projects. Priority given to 501(c)(3) organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that foster safe and vibrant community environments, support spaces that promote emotional well-being, enhance community disaster preparedness and resilience, and focus on Community Placemaking, Safe Space Support, Community Emergency Response, and Resilience Building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: BGE's geographic service area in Maryland, with primary focus on Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Applicant should be a 501(c)(3) organization or nonprofit entity
Must work in one or more of the following focus areas: Community Placemaking, Safe Space Support, Community Emergency Response, or Resilience Building
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications by the posted deadline. Visit the BGE website to access additional details and the application form. Detailed eligibility requirements are available on the BGE Community Safety Grants page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit from County real property taxes on qualified brownfields sites. Credit equals 50% of property tax attributable to increase in assessment of qualified brownfields site over pre-cleanup assessment. Additional 20% credit available for sites in O-Cor Zone of Odenton Growth Management Area. County contributes 30% of tax increase to Maryland Economic Development Assistance Fund. Credit applies for five taxable years following revaluation notice.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 50% of property tax attributable to increased assessment following voluntary cleanup or corrective action plan completion. Additional 20% credit available for sites in O-Cor Zone of Odenton Growth Management Area. County contributes 30% of tax increase to Maryland Economic Development Assistance Fund. Credit applies for five taxable years following revaluation notice.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/Ongoing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of qualified brownfields sites
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit reduction for five taxable years following revaluation notice
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County; additional eligibility for sites within O-Cor Zone of Odenton Growth Management Area
requirements_list: Property must be a qualified brownfields site as defined by Maryland Economic Development Article § 5-301(r)
Completion of voluntary cleanup program or corrective action plan
Notice of Revaluation from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Documentation from Maryland Department of the Environment and/or Maryland Department of Commerce
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application form with required supporting documents to Anne Arundel County Office of Finance. Applicant must certify eligibility and declare information under penalties of perjury. County sends receipt confirmation within 10 business days if email provided. Written notification of approval or denial issued.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Revitalization District Program Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for qualified property owners who make substantial improvements to commercial or industrial properties located in Anne Arundel County's designated Commercial Revitalization Areas, including the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area. Property owners who improve properties by at least $100,000 receive a property tax credit for up to five years equal to the incremental increase in their real property tax assessment, or up to ten years for investments of at least $10,000,000. The property must be certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning as qualified. Qualifying improvements include construction of new buildings, rehabilitation of existing buildings, demolition and subsequent construction, full site redevelopment, façade improvements, landscaping, signage, lighting, and replacing pavement with green spaces.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual property tax credit against real property tax for up to five years equal to the tax attributable to the incremental increase in assessment resulting from qualified improvements of at least $100,000. Credit can be extended for an additional five years (total of ten years) for investments of at least $10,000,000 in private funds. The credit reduces County property tax liability. Credit cannot be combined with other tax credits, PILOTs, or payment alternatives.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 120 days after the issuance of the Notice of Assessment by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners of commercially or industrially zoned property in Anne Arundel County's designated Commercial Revitalization districts with properties available for improvement and rehabilitation who have completed qualified improvements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction of new buildings, rehabilitation of existing buildings, demolition and subsequent construction of commercial or industrial properties, full site redevelopment, façade improvements, landscaping, signage, lighting, replacing pavement with green spaces, and property improvements and rehabilitation of at least $100,000
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County's eleven designated Commercial Revitalization Areas: Area 1 (Brooklyn Park - Ritchie Highway), Area 2 (Glen Burnie Town Center North), Area 3 (Glen Burnie Town Center Core), Area 4 (Glen Burnie Town Center South), Area 5 (Pasadena - Mountain Road), Area 6 (Riviera Beach - Fort Smallwood Road), Area 7 (North Odenton - MD 175), Area 8 (Maryland City/Russett - MD 198), Area 9 (Ferndale - B&A Blvd.), Area 10 (Glen Burnie/Harundale - Ritchie Highway), or Area 11 (Glen Burnie/Marley - Ritchie Highway and Mountain Road). Properties must be located totally or partially within designated commercial revitalization areas, including properties in the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area.
requirements_list: Property must be located in one of the eleven designated Commercial Revitalization Areas
Property must be zoned for commercial or industrial use
Qualified improvements must have full cash value of at least $100,000
Improvements must be constructed per building permit issued by County
Property must be certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning as a qualified property
Owner must apply to the County Office of Finance within 120 days after the issuance of the Notice of Assessment from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Applicant must be current on all taxes owed to County
Credit cannot be combined with other tax credits, PILOTs, or payment alternatives
Extended eligibility of ten years requires $10,000,000 or more in private funds
Property cannot be used primarily for public utilities
Property cannot be in tax increment development district (except Odenton Town Center)
Property cannot qualify for enterprise zone tax credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: After completing qualifying improvements of at least $100,000, property owners receive a Notice of Assessment from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. The owner must then submit the Commercial Revitalization District Program Property Tax Credit Application form (provided by the Controller) to the County Office of Finance within 120 days of receiving this notice. The property must be certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning before the tax credit can be approved.

structured_extraction.program_description: A place-based, multi-sector community improvement initiative using a coordinated systems of care approach that engages local communities and provides wrap-around services and supports to families and youth living in high-need areas to reduce poverty, prevent children from entering out-of-home placements, and address youth success, safety, health, and economic opportunity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides coordinated wrap-around services and supports to families and youth in high-need communities through evidence-based practices, trauma-informed approaches, and collaboration with local agencies, community organizations, residents, faith leaders, business owners, and service providers. Services include mobile outreach, decentralized service delivery, bilingual services, job training and vocational programs, mental health resources, affordable childcare, mentorship programs, home visiting, community health ambassadors, safe recreational spaces, youth development programming, food assistance, healthcare and dental services, housing support, violence interruption, and leadership development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families, youth, children, and community residents living in high-need communities in Anne Arundel County, particularly in Brooklyn Park (zip code 21225), West County/Severn/Meade, Annapolis (zip codes 21401, 21403), and South County areas. Focus on communities disproportionally impacted by youth violence and residents of public and subsidized housing communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wrap-around services and supports to help families with wellness and stability, reduce poverty, and prevent children from entering out-of-home placements. Funds support community resource coordination, programming development, service delivery expansion, leadership capacity building, safe space creation, bilingual service development, job training, childcare, healthcare, transportation, housing support, youth development, mental health services, substance abuse support, and food assistance programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program operates in four designated Communities of Hope areas in Anne Arundel County: Brooklyn Park (North County, zip code 21225), West County (Severn/Meade), Annapolis (zip codes 21401, 21403), and South County. Focus on public and subsidized housing communities within these areas.
requirements_list: Families must reside in one of the four designated Communities of Hope areas
Adoption of Evidence-Based Practices
Trauma-informed approach
Collaboration and resource braiding capability
Commitment to addressing systemic barriers, racism, and inequality
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals or organizations can contact Tracey Cherry, Community of Hope Director, to learn more about the program or to become a partner in a Communities of Hope initiative.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support festivals, cultural events, parades, and other celebrations that provide economic and social benefits to the community.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 11, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations seeking to host festivals, cultural events, parades, and other celebrations in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting festivals, cultural events, parades, and other celebrations that foster a sense of belonging, local identity, quality of life, and learning opportunities while providing economic and social benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Must meet eligibility criteria outlined in program policy
Event must provide economic and social benefits to the community
Must be a community-based festival, cultural event, parade, or celebration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the provided Google Form link.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF) Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants funded by a portion of sales tax revenue from adult-use recreational cannabis sales. The funding supports community-based initiatives intended to benefit low-income communities and communities disproportionately impacted by cannabis prohibition enforcement, with priority given to organizations serving residents in Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs) - areas that historically had elevated cannabis possession charge rates. These grants support community reinvestment and repair initiatives through the Community Reinvestment & Repair Commission.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded from the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund to support community reinvestment and repair initiatives. Funds are distributed to counties proportionate to the total number of cannabis possession charges in each county. Priority funding areas include mental health and substance abuse services, education and youth enrichment and after-school activities, housing and homelessness prevention services, workforce development and employment training, reentry and reintegration, entrepreneurship, and non-profit management training. Organizations apply through the Neighborly Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/Participant. Award amounts and specific terms are determined by the CRRC's recommendations and available fund balance. Total FY2026 awards: $1,691,200 distributed across 12 Mental Health programs, 7 Housing programs, 4 Workforce programs, and 12 Education/Youth programs. Funds cannot be used for law enforcement agencies or activities and must supplement rather than supplant pre-existing local government program funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 25, 2026 at noon
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based nonprofit and community organizations serving low-income communities and underserved communities in Maryland, with priority for organizations in Disproportionately Impacted Areas. Specific focus on individuals experiencing homelessness, job seekers, youth, victims of domestic violence, and formerly incarcerated individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects and activities addressing one or more of the following priorities: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services, Education and Youth Enrichment and After School Activities, Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services, Workforce Development and Employment Training, Reentry and Reintegration, Entrepreneurship and Economic Development, Non-profit Management Training for BIPOC organizations, Criminal Justice Reform, Healthcare Access, Youth Engagement and Mentorship, Parks and Recreational Facilities, or Direct Support for the Illegal-to-Legal Transition. Funds cannot be used for law enforcement agencies or activities and must supplement rather than supplant pre-existing local government program funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland counties and Baltimore City. Within Anne Arundel County, priority is given to the following ten zip codes identified by the CRRC: 21060, 21061, 21113, 21122, 21144, 21225, 21401, 21403, 20724, 20755. These zip codes are within the eight Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs) designated by Maryland's Office of Social Equity based on 20-year cannabis possession charge data.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a community-based organization with or without non-profit designation
Project or activity must be intended to benefit low-income communities or communities disproportionately impacted by cannabis prohibition enforcement

Project or activity must address one or more of the strategic priorities: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services, Education and Youth Enrichment and After School Activities, Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services, or Workforce Development and Employment Training
Organizations serving residents in Disproportionately Impacted Areas receive priority consideration
Funds must supplement and not supplant pre-existing local government program funding
Cannot be used for law enforcement agencies or activities
Each county must adopt a law establishing the purpose for which received money may be used
Organizations with annual budgets over $1,000,000 are encouraged to subcontract with smaller, local-based organizations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the Neighborly Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/Participant or through the ACDS website. Registration for a free Neighborly account is required. Application trainings are available at multiple locations and times in January to help applicants prepare. Deadline is February 25, 2026 at noon.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental and utilities assistance for families at risk of eviction, homelessness, or already experiencing homelessness.

requirements_list: Families and students must be enrolled in an Anne Arundel County Community School
Must be at risk of eviction, losing housing, or experiencing homelessness
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were previously accepted but the program is not currently accepting new applications. structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding for non-profit organizations in Anne Arundel County to support programs that provide services to underserved populations, address community health and well-being, promote equity and inclusion, and help eliminate the opportunity gap in education. Funding can support continuing existing programs, increasing program impact, piloting new programs, or making one-time equipment purchases that improve and enrich the lives of Anne Arundel County residents and communities. The County Executive's Office administers grants to eligible non-profit organizations for community initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $2 million total anticipated to be available for FY2027. Funding can support program/project staff costs, supplies, travel, equipment, and proportional administrative overhead. One-time projects and small equipment purchases are also eligible. Proposals should align with the County Executive's priorities including providing services to underserved populations, addressing health and well-being, promoting equity and inclusion, and eliminating the opportunity gap in education.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: All applications are due by 12 p.m. on Wednesday, February 18, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations serving Anne Arundel County residents and communities, particularly those providing services aligned with County Executive priorities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program or project support including staff costs, supplies, travel, equipment, administrative overhead, one-time projects, and small equipment purchases that improve services to underserved populations, address community health and well-being, promote equity and inclusion, or help eliminate the opportunity gap in education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Organization must be a non-profit
Programs must benefit Anne Arundel County residents and communities
Proposals must align with County Executive's priorities
Collaborative projects are preferred but not required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be completed online through Arundel Community Development Services' Neighborly Portal. Applicants must create an account at the Neighborly portal (portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/participant). Applications opened January 7, 2026 and are due by 12 p.m. on February 18, 2026. Training was provided on January 9, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Conservation Land Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit from Anne Arundel County real property taxes levied on conservation land that is used to preserve natural areas, provide environmental education, promote conservation, or maintain natural areas for public use or wildlife sanctuaries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credit calculated based on the total taxable assessment on conservation land, excluding improvements. If consideration was received for the easement, the tax credit percentage equals the percentage of the donation based on appraised value. Credit is valid for 5 taxable years from approval. Tax credit reduces property tax liability on County real property taxes for conservation land.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought; for taxable year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027, application must be received on or before June 1, 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified conservation organizations (land trusts) and property owners with conservation land in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property taxes on conservation land
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Applicant must be a qualified conservation organization (land trust) as defined in Natural Resources Article § 3-2A-01 of Maryland State Code

Property must be subject to a perpetual conservation easement donated to the land trust on or after July 1, 1991, OR acquired by the land trust on or after July 1, 1991 and owned in fee with a letter of intent, agreement, or option agreement for resale to a government agency
Land must be used for conservation purposes: preservation of natural areas, environmental education, conservation promotion, or maintenance of natural areas for public use or wildlife sanctuary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Conservation Land Real Property Tax Credit Application form (or Renewal form if renewing) to Anne Arundel County Office of Finance by June 1 of the year preceding the taxable year for which credit is sought.

structured_extraction.program_description: Complimentary consulting services to help technology entrepreneurs and companies move their businesses forward, including technology commercialization, federal contracting guidance, and intellectual property legal consultation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free consulting services including DoD technology commercialization support to help entrepreneurs search for patents from defense research labs, connect with product development resources, and navigate the licensing process. Federal contracting guidance through TargetGov partner provides one complimentary hour of consultation per year per company for market analysis, opportunity identification, strategy development, partner identification, and business development support. Intellectual property and legal consultation available for government contractor businesses, including cyber security and CMMC compliance guidance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs developing innovative technology in service of national defense as government contractors or for the commercial market; Anne Arundel County companies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical consulting and guidance for technology commercialization, federal contracting, and intellectual property matters
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Companies can contact AAEDC for a referral to access consulting services. For TargetGov services, companies need an AAEDC referral to receive the complimentary one-hour initial consultation.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Agricultural and Woodland District Agreements
structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax credits available to eligible landowners who establish a 10-year District Agreement on their land to preserve agriculture and woodland resources. The property owner receives a credit against their annual County Property Tax bill in recognition of agreeing to protective covenants similar to those in permanent easements. District Agreements must be renewed every ten years to maintain the tax credit benefit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Land owners receive an Ag ric ultural Tax Credit on the County Real Estate Tax portion of their Real Property Tax Bill. Landowners are invoiced only for State property taxes, County fees, and charges. The amount of the credit is based on the property's qualification and district agreement terms.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications may be submitted anytime, but the County encourages applications be made by March 31 if a tax credit is sought for the following fiscal year tax bill
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Anne Arundel County with eligible agricultural or woodland properties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit for establishing and maintaining a District Agreement to preserve agriculture and woodland resources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be within Rural Agricultural (RA) or Residential Low Density (RLD) zoning districts and outside existing or planned Water and Sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
requirements_list: Land (in whole or in part) must consist of 50 contiguous acres devoted to agriculture, or at least 10 contiguous acres of woodlands
Multiple contiguous properties under different ownership are acceptable if each individual property is no less than 10 acres and the total meets or exceeds 50 acres
Must meet certain USDA Soil Capability Classes criteria
Must have an active Soil and Water Conservation Plan in place
For woodland districts, a Forest Management Plan is required
Must be within Rural Agricultural (RA) or Residential Low Density (RLD) zoning districts
Must be outside existing or planned Water and Sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
Property owner must agree to 10-year District Agreement with protective covenants
Agreement must be renewed every ten years to maintain tax credit benefit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners contact the Agricultural and Woodland Preservation Staff to determine property qualification and eligibility requirements. Staff can assist in preparing the District and Tax Credit applications. Applications may be submitted anytime, though applications by March 31 are encouraged for tax credit in the following fiscal year. Upon approval, the landowner enters into a District Agreement which is recorded in the County Land Records.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helped small brick-and-mortar businesses and nonprofits in Anne Arundel County adapt to a digital economy and engage with customers and stakeholders by adopting digital tools and services. The program was part of the County's COVID-19 economic recovery strategy and was funded with federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds designated by the Maryland Department of Commerce under the state RELIEF Act. The program provided grants to support new purchase of or subscription to digital platforms and services including email and mobile marketing, customer relationship management systems, customer rewards and loyalty programs, e-commerce capabilities for online ordering and sales, website development, and social media advertising. A total of 144 businesses received grants, with typical grants of $3,200 and a total distribution of $460,800.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants of $3,200 per eligible applicant funded with federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds designated by the Maryland Department of Commerce under the state RELIEF Act. Grants were awarded to qualifying businesses with a total distribution of $460,800 to 144 businesses. Funds can be used for new purchase of or subscription to digital platforms and services including email and mobile marketing, customer relationship management (CRM), customer rewards and loyalty programs, e-commerce including online ordering and sales, website development, and social media advertising.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 5:00 p.m. on Friday, October 1, 2021
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with 1 to 20 employees, woman-owned businesses, minority-owned businesses, and veteran-owned businesses in Anne Arundel County, as well as nonprofits seeking to strengthen their digital presence and online capabilities. Priority consideration given to businesses with fewer than ten employees and those that had not previously received state-funded COVID-19 relief grants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New purchase of or subscription to digital platforms and services including email and mobile marketing, customer relationship management (CRM), customer rewards and loyalty programs, e-commerce capabilities for online ordering and sales, website development, and social media advertising.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must have a brick-and-mortar location in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, specifically within County Council Districts (1-7) and State Legislative Districts (21, 30A, 30B, 31A, 31B, 32, 33), and be in good standing with the State of Maryland and Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Small brick-and-mortar businesses or nonprofits in Anne Arundel County
Business or nonprofit organization must have 1 to 20 employees
Fewer than ten employees prioritized (received 77 percent of grants awarded)
Must have been established and operating prior to March 9, 2020
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland and Anne Arundel County
Must have a brick-and-mortar location in Anne Arundel County
Must operate in retail, beauty and personal wellness services, adult and children's activity centers, arts and crafts businesses, or be a nonprofit organization
Must not have previously received state-funded COVID-19 relief grants
Must submit appropriate certificate or license for their sector
Must submit completed and signed W-9 form
Must submit budget outlining proposed use of grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program was launched on September 14, 2021. Applications went live on September 20 at 9:00 a.m. All applications must be submitted via an online portal by 5:00 p.m. on Friday, October 1, 2021. The application window has closed and the program is no longer accepting applications. A total of 144 businesses received grants of $3,200 each, for a total distribution of $460,800.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Law Enforcement Officers and Rescue Workers Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax credit for permanently and totally disabled law enforcement officers, correctional officers, rescue workers, or surviving spouses of fallen officers/workers in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. The credit is calculated at 100% of total tax due on the dwelling based on real property assessment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% tax credit on County real property taxes for eligible dwellings owned by disabled law enforcement officers, correctional officers, career and volunteer rescue workers, or surviving spouses of fallen officers/workers. The credit applies to the total tax due on the dwelling based on real property assessment and is applied after mandatory property tax credits, supplements, and deferrals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Permanently and totally disabled law enforcement officers, correctional officers, career fire/rescue/EMS employees, volunteer fire company or rescue squad members, and surviving spouses of fallen officers or rescue workers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: County real property tax reduction on primary residence dwelling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must reside in Anne Arundel County, Maryland as primary residence; property must be located in Anne Arundel County. Applicant/spouse must have been domiciled in Maryland within the timeframe specified in § 9-210 of Tax-Property Article.
requirements_list: Dwelling must be owned by disabled officer/worker at time of disability determination, or by fallen officer/worker at time of death
Permanently and totally disabled by administrative body or court of competent jurisdiction
Disability arose from employment or volunteer service
Disability not result of willful misconduct, alcohol/drug abuse, or occupational disease
Must be member of specific law enforcement, correctional, fire, rescue, or EMS entity
Must own property as primary residence in Anne Arundel County
Maryland residency established within required timeframe per § 9-210 of Tax-Property Article
Current property purchased and occupied within required timeframe of disability determination or death
Valid Maryland government identification required
Application must be notarized
Verification of eligibility required
Credit ceases upon determination that officer/worker is no longer permanently and totally disabled
Credit ceases upon remarriage of surviving spouse
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application form provided by the Controller's office. Section 1 requires applicant to complete personal information. Application must include verification of eligibility and be notarized. Applications can be for new credit or renewal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disaster Recovery Micro Grant Program (Tropical Storm Ida – Anne Arundel County)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps Anne Arundel County businesses recover from damage and operational pauses caused by Tropical Storm Ida in September 2021. Grants of up to $5,000 can be used for physical property repairs, replacement of business equipment, replacement of inventory, lease or rental support, vendor bill support, or moving expenses support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation assistance program providing door-to-door, on-demand rides to eligible Anne Arundel County residents at approximately 50 percent of normal cost. Residents can schedule rides by calling a reservations number, with same-day service available with at least two hours notice. Participants receive a county match of up to $75 per month, or can purchase vouchers at a discount with double value (e.g., $5 purchase = $10 in ride credit), up to a maximum of $150 in vouchers per month. The program serves residents aged 55 and older, or residents aged 18 to 54 with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Professional drivers operate appropriately equipped cars, vans, or SUVs to provide door-to-door service. Fares are offered at approximately 50 percent of the normal cost. Each qualified resident receives a county match of up to $75 per month. Alternatively, participants can purchase vouchers at a discount with double value (e.g., $5 purchase = $10 in ride credit), up to a maximum of $150 in vouchers per month. Service is available within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line (excludes airport trips).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents aged 55 and older, or residents aged 18 to 54 with disabilities; includes both ambulatory and non-ambulatory individuals, and those needing assistance getting from door to vehicle
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Door-to-door transportation within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line (excluding airport trips)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County residents; service available within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident
Must be 55 years of age or older, or 18 years of age or older with a verifiable transportation disability that precludes use of public transportation
Income at or below $1,255/month (single) or $1,703/month (with spouse)
Must provide a completed ETA Application and Liability Form
Must provide a copy of Maryland State driver's license or Maryland State Issued ID from Motor Vehicle Administration with Anne Arundel County address

For persons 18 or older with a disability, must provide SSI or SSDI award letter or Disability Verification Form from physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, or program director of qualified social agency
Must schedule own trips and pay for all scheduled trips
Must adhere to requirements set by Rides-On-Demand service providers and Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities
Must sign liability waiver/indemnification agreement
Maximum purchase: $150 in voucher value per month
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit one of two locations (2666 Riva Road, 2nd Floor, Annapolis or 7320 Ritchie Highway, Glen Burnie) during walk-in hours (8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.) or mail application materials to 2666 Riva Rd, Suite 400, Annapolis, MD 21401. Submit completed ETA Application, Liability Form, proof of Anne Arundel County residency, disability verification if applicable (completed by health care provider), ETA Order Form for Rides-On-Demand, and payment by check or money order. After enrollment, call the Rides-On-Demand reservations number to schedule rides. Applications are also submitted through an online form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Easy Travel Access (ETA) Taxi Voucher Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation assistance program that offers discounted taxi vouchers to help qualified residents of Anne Arundel County pay for taxi fares with participating cab companies. Eligible residents are 55 years of age or older, or 18 years of age or older with a disability. Residents purchase voucher books at a discounted rate ($5.00 per book, with each book worth $10.00 in taxi fare value) and can use them for errands, shopping, voting, and grocery shopping. Up to 15 books per month can be purchased (maximum $75 monthly county match). The program may also offer rides-on-demand transportation services as an alternative to taxi vouchers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents purchase taxi voucher coupon books at $5.00 per book, with each book worth $10.00 in taxi fare value. Up to 15 books per month can be purchased (maximum $75 monthly county match), or up to $150 in vouchers per month. Vouchers may not be used for tips and are non-transferable and non-refundable. Payment by check or money order only.

Individuals with low income at or below $1,255/month for single households or $1,703/month for married couples. Includes both ambulatory and non-ambulatory individuals needing assistance getting from door to vehicle.

structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-departmental program coordinated by Anne Arundel County's Department of Inspections and Permits (Forestry Section) and Department of Recreation and Parks that provides eligible property owners, community associations, and county residents with emergent marsh grasses (Spartina alterniflora and Spartina patens) for planting in intertidal zones, areas above intertidal zones, and marsh areas. The grasses are provided at no cost to eligible applicants implementing qualifying living shoreline or other tidal restoration projects. County personnel conduct field visits to evaluate site conditions, determine appropriate plant types based on shore position, tides and salinity, and provide guidance on recommended spacing and plant quantities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free emergent marsh grasses (Spartina alterniflora or Spartina patens) and technical assistance to eligible Anne Arundel County property owners, community associations, and county residents. County personnel conduct field visits to evaluate site conditions, determine plant types based on position on shore, tides, and salinity, and calculate the number of plants needed based on area dimensions and spacing requirements. Grasses are provided at no charge for qualifying living shoreline or other tidal restoration projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: Full Delivery of "Turnkey" Water Quality Improvements Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County funds design-build-maintain contracts with private firms to construct cost-effective nature-based stormwater best management practices on privately owned properties. Private firms submit competitive bids on behalf of property owners or groups of property owners to implement restoration projects. The program uses public-private partnerships where contractors front initial implementation costs and are reimbursed by the County after the project is built and verified to generate water quality credits. Bid opportunities are typically announced each fall.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County reimburses private contractors for design, construction, and maintenance of stormwater best management practices after project completion and County verification. Full award is paid upon completion and verification of project benefits, typically within one year of construction. Maintenance payments are evaluated and released annually for 5 years after project completion. Private firms submit competitive bids to construct cost-effective nature-based restoration projects on behalf of property owners or groups of property owners. Projects are selected and funded through a bidding process.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, construction, and maintenance of cost-effective nature-based stormwater best management practices such as living shorelines, stream restoration, wetland enhancement, and regenerative stormwater conveyance systems for stormwater management and water quality improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Sites must be located on private property within Anne Arundel County's Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) geography and cannot conflict with existing projects underway. Anne Arundel County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A professional development training program for 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations in Anne Arundel County to develop fundraising expertise and organizational sustainability strategies. The program is offered in multiple cohort levels: an introductory Fundraising & Sustainability cohort for organizations new to resource development planning, and an advanced Fundraising & Sustainability 2.0 cohort for nonprofit leaders with baseline fundraising knowledge. Programs include group training sessions held every two weeks, expert facilitation, peer learning, networking opportunities, one-on-one consulting, and lifetime access to resource materials and templates. Teams of 2-3 people from participating organizations attend sessions together to help develop diverse revenue sources and secure long-term financial viability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost training and technical assistance program offered through multiple cohort levels. The introductory cohort includes 4 in-person training sessions and 2 virtual coaching sessions at no cost to participants. The advanced Fundraising & Sustainability 2.0 cohort includes five group training sessions (2:00 p.m. to 4:30 p.m., held every two weeks) with costs based on organization budget: $75 for organizations with budgets under $500,000, and $150 for organizations with budgets over $500,000. Up to twelve organizations participate on a first-come, first-served basis. Both programs accommodate teams of 2-3 people from participating organizations and include expert facilitation, peer learning opportunities, one-on-one consulting time on a project of choice, and lifetime access to resource materials, examples, templates, and tools for resource development planning. Training and technical assistance is provided through cohort-based learning to help nonprofit organizations develop diverse revenue sources and strengthen long-term financial sustainability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by cohort cycle; check website for current openings and deadlines. Fall 2025 cohort is now full; Spring 2026 cohort will be offered.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations located in Anne Arundel County with administrative offices in Anne Arundel County that serve Anne Arundel County residents. The introductory cohort serves organizations new to resource development planning; the advanced cohort serves nonprofit leaders with baseline fundraising knowledge or prior cohort participation. Organizations seeking to diversify revenue sources and improve financial sustainability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and professional development in fundraising strategies, resource development planning, financial sustainability, grant development, organizational storytelling, and diverse fundraising planning to help nonprofit organizations develop or update resource development plans and strengthen long-term financial viability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must have administrative offices located in Anne Arundel County and serve Anne Arundel County residents (at least 75 percent of population served).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in the program should contact the Nonprofit Center or register through their website. Applications are reviewed on a rolling or first-come, first-served basis depending on cohort availability. For cohorts utilizing online applications, submit through SurveyMonkey or the Nonprofit Center website by the stated deadline, providing organization information, mission statement, founding year, 501(c)(3) status, annual budget, staffing levels, board fundraising participation, current resource development strategies, and learning goals. The advanced cohort is filled on a first-come, first-served basis and limited to twelve organizations. Organizations can bring up to three people to sessions. The Nonprofit Center will contact all organizations regarding payment requirements once the cohort is full. Applicants will be notified of selection following the application deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program to help non-profits, homeowner associations, private landowners, and others enhance the habitat and ecological balance of natural areas. Activities may include pruning for vegetation health and safety, non-commercial timber stand improvement, and removal of non-native invasive vegetation with replanting of native species. This applies when removing more than 5,000 square feet of existing natural vegetation in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or Bog Protection Areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides review and approval of habitat enhancement plans. Applicants must submit a completed Habitat Enhancement Plan application to the Forestry Program for review before work begins. An approved plan must be posted onsite during work performance for inspection purposes. All required State and Federal permits must be obtained prior to Forestry's approval. The program allows site grading without a separate grading permit if approved and provides technical guidance for sediment and erosion control.
