structured_extraction.program_name: High Performance Building Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for high performance buildings that meet national green building standards (LEED Silver or higher, or ICC 700 National Green Building Standard Silver or higher) on residential and commercial properties in Anne Arundel County, as authorized by Tax-Property Article Section 9-242 of the State Code. The credit reduces County real property taxes for certified high performance buildings and is applied to the building (not land) for five consecutive taxable years beginning the year application is approved. Credit amounts vary by certification level: Residential—LEED Silver or NGBS Silver (40% credit, max $1,000), LEED Gold or NGBS Gold (60% credit, max $2,000), LEED Platinum or NGBS Emerald (80% credit, max $3,000). Commercial—LEED Silver or NGBS Silver (40% of County property tax, max $20,000), LEED Gold or NGBS Gold (60% of County property tax, max $40,000), LEED Platinum or NGBS Emerald (80% of County property tax, max $60,000). Cannot be combined with other optional property tax credits.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A real property tax credit that reduces County real property taxes for high performance buildings on residential and commercial properties that meet national green building standards. Credit is applied to the building (not land) for five consecutive taxable years beginning the year application is approved. Residential: LEED Silver or NGBS Silver (40% credit, max $1,000), LEED Gold or NGBS Gold (60% credit, max $2,000), LEED Platinum or NGBS Emerald (80% credit, max $3,000). Commercial: LEED Silver or NGBS Silver (40% of County property tax, max $20,000), LEED Gold or NGBS Gold (60% of County property tax, max $40,000), LEED Platinum or NGBS Emerald (80% of County property tax, max $60,000). Cannot be combined with other optional property tax credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: on or before June 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is first sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of high performance residential and commercial buildings that meet national green building standards in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax liability reduction on real property taxes for certified high performance buildings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Building must be assessed as residential or commercial by Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Building must meet or exceed Silver rating in current version of LEED for Homes or LEED Green Building Rating System, or ICC 700 National Green Building Standard (NGBS)
Applicant must provide LEED/NGBS rating certificate and workbook or NGBS documentation
Building and systems must be regularly maintained to comply with applicable standard
Statement under penalties of perjury required
County may enter property for inspection purposes
Cannot be combined with other optional property tax credits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the appropriate High Performance Building Property Tax Credit Application form (residential or commercial) to Anne Arundel County Finance Department on or before June 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is first sought. Include documentation of LEED/NGBS rating certificate and workbook or NGBS documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County's tax credit program helps property owners offset expenses for rehabilitation work on historic landmarks and properties in Landmark Historic Districts. The program provides property tax credits ranging from 5% to 25% of qualified expenses, with a maximum credit of $50,000 claimable over five years. Property owners of landmark properties and buildings contributing to historic districts can apply 25% of qualified rehabilitation expenses against their annual property tax bill for historic residential or income-producing properties, or 5% for qualified new construction in a Landmark Historic District. If the annual tax credit exceeds the property's tax bill for that year, the balance carries forward for up to five years total. Qualified expenses include in-kind repairs to original features, in-kind replacement of deteriorated original features, reversing modern treatments, structural repairs, roof repair/replacement, chimney repair and lining, storm windows/doors, masonry repointing, life-safety and ADA improvements, plumbing/electrical/mechanical work, new architecturally-compatible infill construction (County Landmark Historic Districts only), and architectural/engineering/archeological fees. Non-qualifying expenses include remodeling, modern material replacements, appliances, landscaping, tool purchases, outbuilding work, interior décor, and permit fees.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a county real property tax credit of 25% of qualified rehabilitation expenses for historic residential or income-producing properties, or 5% for qualified new construction in a Landmark Historic District. The maximum credit is $50,000, which can be claimed over a five-year period. If the annual tax credit exceeds the property's tax bill for that year, the balance carries forward for up to five years total. The tax credit is calculated based on eligible historic preservation expenses incurred on qualifying properties. Qualified expenses include in-kind repairs to original features, in-kind replacement of deteriorated original features, reversing modern treatments, structural repairs, roof repair/replacement, chimney repair and lining, storm windows/doors, masonry repointing, life-safety and ADA improvements, plumbing/electrical/mechanical work, new architecturally-compatible infill construction (County Landmark Historic Districts only), and architectural/engineering/archeological fees. Non-qualifying expenses include remodeling, modern material replacements, appliances, landscaping, tool purchases, outbuilding work, interior décor, and permit fees.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Part 3 form must be submitted by March 1 immediately before the taxable year; Part 4 tax credit application must be submitted by April 1 immediately before the taxable year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners of historic landmarks and contributing properties in Landmark Historic Districts in Anne Arundel County who undertake qualifying preservation and rehabilitation work
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified expenses for rehabilitation or restoration work on historic properties, including interior and exterior preservation work, provided the work does not compromise the landmark status and complies with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties. Eligible work includes in-kind repairs to original features, in-kind replacement of deteriorated original features, reversing modern treatments, structural repairs, roof repair/replacement, chimney repair and lining, storm windows/doors, masonry repointing, life-safety and ADA improvements, plumbing/electrical/mechanical work, new architecturally-compatible infill construction (County Landmark Historic Districts only), and architectural/engineering/archeological fees. Work on non-historic additions does not qualify. Non-qualifying expenses include remodeling, modern material replacements, appliances, landscaping, tool purchases, outbuilding work, interior décor, and permit fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Eligible properties include County Historic Landmarks and contributing resources within the four Landmark Historic Districts (Davidsonville, Linthicum Heights, Owensville, and Woodwardville). Three additional historic districts have been determined eligible: West Benning, Glen Burnie, and Odenton. New infill construction qualifies only in County Landmark Historic Districts.
requirements_list: Structure must be at least 65 years old
Structure must have high significance in history, architecture, archeology, engineering, and/or culture
Structure must retain integrity in location, design, setting, materials, workmanship, feeling, and association
Property must be listed on National Register, associated with significant events/persons, embody distinctive design/construction characteristics, or have information potential
Property must be eligible for the historic preservation tax credit
Property must be a landmark property or contribute to a historic district
Applicant must follow the established procedure for applying for the tax credit
Applicant must meet eligibility criteria as defined in the ordinance
Expenses must be for qualified historic rehabilitation
The historic resource must meet criteria for designation as a County Historic Landmark, including requirements for age, historic significance, and integrity
All rehabilitation work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties and Article 4, Title 2 of Anne Arundel County Code
Work must not compromise integrity of historic structure
Work must not negatively impact historically significant features
Work must be reversible where possible
A historic preservation easement must be executed and recorded in Anne Arundel County land records to protect the county's investment
For new construction in a Landmark Historic District, the construction must be architecturally compatible with the surrounding district

Applicants cannot combine this tax credit with other optional property tax credits enabled by Maryland State Code Title 9, including agricultural, conservation, energy, airport noise zone, or veteran-related credits
Certificate of Eligibility (Part 1) and Certification of Proposed Work (Part 2) must be approved before rehabilitation work begins
Proof of payment for all qualified work items must be submitted with the Certification of Completed Work
Part 3 form must be submitted by March 1 before the taxable year to apply credit to that year's bill
Part 4 tax credit application must be filed by April 1 before the taxable year
Owner authorization required
Property must undergo periodic on-site inspections by Office of Planning and Zoning
All applicable permits must be approved/completed
Applicant must certify eligibility and that all submitted information is true, correct, and complete under penalties of perjury
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process has four parts. Part 1: Submit a Certificate of Eligibility form confirming the property meets historic landmark criteria with property information, eligibility documentation, and supporting materials; the county responds within 30 days with approval, denial, or a request for more information. Part 2: Schedule a presubmittal meeting with Cultural Resources staff to discuss proposed work and methods, then submit a Certification of Proposed Work form with supporting materials including detailed documentation (work descriptions, photos, site plans, architectural drawings); the county responds within 30 days with certification, denial, or comments to resubmit. Do not begin work until Part 2 is approved. Submit any project changes as a Part 2 Addendum. Part 3: After work completion, submit a Certification of Completed Work form with proof of payment for each line item and color photos from same locations as Part 2 application; the county verifies the work matches Part 2 approvals within 30 days and the historic preservation easement is executed. Submit by March 1 before the taxable year. Part 4: Submit the Tax Credit Application form to the Office of Finance by April 1 before the taxable year; the office applies the tax credit to the property's tax bill. Property owners must apply each year by April 1 to receive the tax credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A business education and training program designed to help small, minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Anne Arundel County succeed and grow. The program provides business owners with resources including business education and training through a seven-week curriculum covering law, human resources, and accounting, mentorship from business consultants and expert advisors (including legal, human resources, and accounting professionals), access to capital through seed grants, and support for accessing relief grants. Each participant receives a $5,000 seed grant to serve as working capital for their business. The seven-week program consists of weekly three-hour classes led by a business consultant who is a recruiter for the Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses program. Participants receive consultations with legal, human resources, and accounting experts, and present their business growth plans to a panel of judges. The program provides ongoing mentorship to early-stage entrepreneurs and established businesses to help them understand financial metrics, address hiring needs, and grow their enterprises.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each participant receives a $5,000 seed grant to serve as working capital for their business. Participants engage in seven consecutive weeks of weekly three-hour classes led by a business consultant who is a recruiter for the Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses program. The curriculum covers law, human resources, and accounting with consultations from legal, human resources, and accounting experts. Participants receive mentorship and ongoing support after program completion, and present their business growth plans to a panel of judges. Businesses work with mentors to understand financial metrics, hiring needs, and access to relief grants.

The program addresses losses in revenue, increased costs, and operational challenges to help businesses stabilize operations, pivot business models, and invest in long-term viability. Businesses can receive between $10,000 and $50,000 to help regain stability and build resilience. A total of $3 million was awarded to 66 small businesses through the program.

Supplies provided with MPU rental include personal protective equipment (gloves, aprons), cleaning supplies (bleach, Dawn soap, sponges/scrub brushes), processing equipment (knives), and accessories (garden hoses, extension cords, food-grade hoses, drainage hoses for scalder, buckets for offal and waste collection, thermometers, and poultry crates). Renters must provide or have access to a water source, electricity, and drainage capability.

structured_extraction.program_description: A zero percent interest loan program providing financing to technology companies in Anne Arundel County, including small government contractors and startups at the mezzanine stage of growth. Supports workforce expansion, scaling operations, compliance certifications such as CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, and DFARS requirements, and covering costs while awaiting federal contract payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest loans ranging from $50,000 to $250,000 with flexible payment terms (one to five years) for technology companies and small government contractors to support workforce expansion, scaling operations, compliance certifications including CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, and DFARS requirements, and costs while awaiting federal contract payments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Technology companies and small government contractors in Anne Arundel County, particularly startups and mezzanine-stage businesses needing cybersecurity compliance funding, workforce expansion support, or scaling assistance. Companies must have gross revenue of less than $5 million and fewer than 100 employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce expansion, scaling operations, compliance certifications including CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, and DFARS requirements, covering costs while awaiting federal contract payments, bringing on additional team members, expanding marketing efforts, and developing products.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County. Businesses must be located in Anne Arundel County or have a signed lease demonstrating their intent to move into the county.
requirements_list: Gross revenue of less than $5 million
Fewer than 100 employees
Located in Anne Arundel County or have a signed lease demonstrating intent to move into the county
Technology sector business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested businesses can request a consultation with the AAEDC finance team through the Next Stage Tech Fund webpage or submit an application through AAEDC.

structured_extraction.program_name: Non-Profit Economic Development Recovery Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing financial support to community-serving non-profit organizations in Anne Arundel County that have been impacted by the pandemic economy. The program supports non-profits focused on economic development, economic recovery, health and human services, and housing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants to support the workforce and operations of eligible non-profit organizations. Individual grant amounts are calculated after the application round closes. The program is supported by approximately $1.9 million from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, May 21 at 5:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-serving non-profit organizations based in Anne Arundel County that have been impacted by the pandemic economy and focus on economic development, economic recovery, health and human services, or housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants support the workforce and operations of non-profit organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be based in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Be based in Anne Arundel County
Have at least one W-2 employee
Be prepared to detail how it serves populations in the county with a mission focus on economic development, economic recovery, health and human services, or housing
Provide information on the need for funding based on adverse economic impact resulting from the pandemic economy
Include information on any COVID-19 relief funds received to date and the remaining gap of needed funds
Provide a 2019 IRS Form 990
Provide a completed and signed IRS W-9 form
Provide a voided organization check or official bank letter confirming routing number and account number with the same organization name as listed on the Form 990

Unable to pay rent due to COVID-related loss of income

structured_extraction.program_description: The program helps residents in Anne Arundel County neighborhoods near the Chesapeake Bay reduce the costs of converting from private septic tanks to the County's public sewer system. It aims to improve water quality, protect local waterways and the Chesapeake Bay, enhance water resiliency, and support public health. The program plans to convert up to 6,000 private septic systems over the next 30 years, approximately 200 per year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides financial assistance to reduce the costs of converting from private septic tanks to the County's public sewer system. The program plans to convert up to 6,000 private septic systems over the next 30 years, approximately 200 per year. Eligible residents can apply by entering their address on the program website.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Anne Arundel County living in neighborhoods near the Chesapeake Bay with private septic tank systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Converting from private septic tanks to the County's public sewer system

requirements_list: Must be a resident of Anne Arundel County
Must live in an eligible neighborhood near the Chesapeake Bay
Must have a private septic tank system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can determine eligibility by visiting www.ourwaater.com and entering their address into the search bar. Additional information is available by emailing info@ourwaater.org or calling (410) 222-7500.

structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 6 months of filling the pool

Property owner of swimming pool in Anne Arundel County

structured_extraction.program_description: A special program designed to encourage current drive-alone commuters to start or join a vanpool by offering monthly subsidies to newly formed van or car pools.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pool Rewards offers up to a $200 monthly subsidy to newly formed van or car pools.

Be a newly-forming vanpool not previously in operation within 30 days prior to application
Be registered with Commuter Connections
Have 7 to 15 passenger capacity including the driver
Submit an application through qualified vanpool providers VPSI Inc. or Enterprise Rideshare

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Safety Officer Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available to public safety officers employed by Anne Arundel County, including full-time employees (firefighters, EMTs, detention officers, police officers, deputy sheriffs), retired officers, and volunteer members who reside in the county. The credit provides relief on real property taxes for dwellings owned and occupied as principal residences by eligible officers. The maximum credit amount is the lesser of $3,500 or total County taxes due on the dwelling (for taxable years beginning July 1, 2025 or after). The credit is available for up to 25 taxable years with annual reapplication. The program has been extended through ordinances, including Bill 86-21 (extending from 5 to 10 years), Bill 91-23 (expanding eligibility and increasing maximum credit to $3,500), and Bill 96-25 (extending maximum duration to 25 taxable years).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit of the lesser of $3,500 or total County taxes due on the dwelling for qualifying public safety officers, including full-time employees, retired officers, and volunteer members. The credit reduces County real property taxes on dwellings owned and used as principal residences by eligible public safety officers. The credit is available for up to 25 taxable years (extended from 10 years by Bill 96-25) with annual reapplication required. Submit the appropriate application form (full-time employee, retired from service, or volunteer member) to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance on or before April 1 immediately before the desired taxable year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the tax credit is sought (e.g., April 1, 2026 for taxable year beginning July 1, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time, retired, and volunteer public safety officers of Anne Arundel County (including firefighters, EMTs, detention officers, police officers, and deputy sheriffs) who reside in the county, own a dwelling, and use it as their principal residence. Volunteers must have at least 50 service points in the preceding calendar year with Anne Arundel County volunteer fire companies or Anne Arundel Alarmers Association.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property tax liability on owner-occupied dwellings used as principal residences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland only. Property must be located in Anne Arundel County and used as applicant's principal residence.
requirements_list: Must be a public safety officer as defined in Tax-Property Article Section 9-260 or as defined by Anne Arundel County ordinance (firefighter, EMT, detention officer, police officer, or deputy sheriff)
Must own the dwelling and use it as principal residence

Must have completed at least one year of full-time employment with Anne Arundel County as a public safety officer, OR be retired from such employment, OR be a volunteer member with at least 50 service points in the preceding calendar year, OR be entitled to benefits under § 12-1-304 for volunteer service
Must live in Anne Arundel County
Must occupy the property for more than six months during the taxable year (July 1 - June 30)
Must not currently receive credit on another Anne Arundel County property
Must be eligible for Maryland's homeowner property tax credit under § 9-105 of the Tax-Property Article
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the appropriate Public Safety Officer Tax Credit Application form (full-time employee, retired from service, or volunteer member) to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance on or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought. Initial application determines eligibility for one taxable year. Renewal applications must be submitted annually to continue credit for additional taxable years (up to 25 taxable years maximum).

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property County Tax Exemption for Community or Civic Associations
structured_extraction.program_description: Exemption from Anne Arundel County Real Estate Taxes for community or civic associations meeting specific criteria. An exemption that removes County real estate tax liability for community or civic associations in accordance with Anne Arundel County Code Section 4-2-201(b).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exemption from Anne Arundel County real estate taxes (County taxes only, not state or federal). This removes County real estate tax liability for community or civic associations. Property must be dedicated to use of lot owners within the community. Use contingent only on assessments for improvement or maintenance of roads, property, or other community facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community and civic associations serving lot owners within a community
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property dedicated to use of lot owners within the community. Common facilities, roads, and community property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Title held by nonprofit community civic association or corporation
Property dedicated by appropriate record plat or deed restrictions to use of lot owners within community
Current with all taxes and fees due to Anne Arundel County
Use not contingent on dues/fees except for assessments solely for improvement or maintenance of roads, property, or facilities
Must have 501(c)(3) determination letter if applicable

Submit with supporting documentation including 501(c)(3) letter, property records, plat/deed copies, and narrative description. Mail to: Anne Arundel County, Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, MD 21401; or email to taxcredits@aacounty.org

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property Tax Credit for Disabled Veterans and Their Surviving Spouses
structured_extraction.program_description: A county property tax credit available to disabled veterans and their surviving spouses who own and reside in a dwelling house in Anne Arundel County. The credit reduces county real property taxes based on disability rating: 50% of county property tax if disability rating is 75% or higher, or 25% if disability rating is 50-74%. The credit is applied after mandatory credits, supplements, and deferrals. The credit is available through an annual application process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A real property tax credit that reduces county real property tax liability on a primary residence (dwelling house). Credit amounts are: 50% of county property tax for disabled veterans with a disability rating of 75% or higher, or 25% of county property tax for those with a disability rating of 50-74%. The credit is applied after mandatory property tax credits, supplements, and deferrals, and applies only to county taxes (not state taxes or other assessments/fees). Maximum duration is 5 years for disabled veterans and 5 years for surviving spouses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the tax credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans who are honorably discharged or released under honorable circumstances from active military, naval, or air service with a permanent service-connected disability rating of at least 50% declared by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, or a nonpermanent 100% disability rating. Also eligible are surviving spouses of deceased disabled veterans who qualified for and received the credit at the time of death, have not remarried, and have federal adjusted gross income not exceeding $100,000.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of county real property taxes on primary residence (dwelling house) only
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Property must be located in Anne Arundel County and used as the applicant's legal residence (primary residence not occupied by more than two families).
requirements_list: Honorable discharge or release under honorable circumstances from active military, naval, or air service
Service-connected disability declared by U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs: permanent rating of at least 50% OR nonpermanent 100% rating
Disability must result from blindness or other disabling cause reasonably certain to continue for life
Own the dwelling house property in Anne Arundel County
Occupy the dwelling as primary residence (not occupied by more than two families)
Federal adjusted gross income not exceeding $100,000 for the preceding taxable year
For surviving spouses: deceased veteran must have qualified for and received the tax credit at time of death
For surviving spouses: must not have remarried since veteran's death
Application must be filed on form provided by Controller's Office by April 1 deadline
Must be a disabled veteran or surviving spouse of a disabled veteran
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the appropriate Disabled Veterans Property Tax Credit Application form to the Anne Arundel County Finance Department (Controller's Office) on or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought. Applications must include certification of eligibility and any additional information the Controller deems necessary. Applications filed after April 1 are disallowed for that taxable year but treated as an application for the following taxable year. Surviving spouses and certain veterans must re-apply annually to maintain eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Restaurant and Food Service Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing funding to restaurants and food service businesses in Anne Arundel County. The program provides grants to eligible applicants, including those experiencing reduced revenue due to COVID-19 related restrictions, with funding made available through Anne Arundel County and MD Commerce. Grants can be used for operating expenses including rent, payroll, utilities, personal protective equipment, sanitary improvements, and online customer engagement tools. The program is operated by the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $10,000 for catering businesses, bed and breakfast establishments, and dine-in non-drive-through restaurants. Grants of $5,000 for food trucks. Total program funding of $10 million available. Funds are disbursed via ACH deposit to business bank account. Additional funding made available through MD Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Restaurants, food trucks, catering businesses, bed and breakfast establishments, and other food service businesses located in Anne Arundel County that were operating prior to March 13, 2020 and experienced reduced revenue due to COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses such as rent, payroll, utilities, personal protective equipment, sanitary physical space improvements, and online customer engagement and transaction systems. Grants cannot be used for expenses covered by other federal, state or local COVID-19 programs, insurance-covered losses, or capital improvements.

Be in good standing with the State of Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Submit a copy of an active food service license issued by Anne Arundel County Department of Health

The credit is applied to County real property taxes levied on a dwelling owned by an eligible disabled officer/rescue worker or surviving spouse. The credit provides 100% of the total tax due on the dwelling based on real property assessment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Substantial Financial Hardship Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows residential property owners in Anne Arundel County to reduce or waive the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (stormwater fee) if they meet financial hardship criteria. Eligible applicants must meet at least two of the following conditions: receiving energy assistance subsidy, receiving supplemental security income (SSI) or food stamps, receiving veterans or Social Security disability benefits, or meeting specific income thresholds. Mobile home park tenants with a valid lease receive a 40% reduction of the base rate. The program must be applied for annually with a deadline of December 31st for the fiscal year.

The program must be applied for annually with a deadline of December 31st for the fiscal year.

Must meet financial hardship criteria
Property must contain detached single-family dwelling or dwelling unit in attached/multifamily residential property
At least one property owner must be an occupant of the property

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Management Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for residential and commercial property owners in Anne Arundel County who install or implement permanent stormwater management practices approved by the Department of Public Works. The credit equals 10 percent of the cost of materials and installation of qualified practices, including living shoreline projects, rain gardens, rain barrels, porous landscaping materials, living roofs, sidewalk infiltration planters, permeable pavers, bioretention installations, cisterns, removal of impervious surfaces, swales, dry wells, infiltration trenches, sand filters, green roofs, constructed wetlands, regenerative step pools, wet ponds, retrofitting existing wet ponds with CMAC systems, and other approved stormwater controls. The credit is capped at a maximum total of $10,000 over the five-year life of the credit program.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

The credit is capped at $10,000 total over the five-year life of the credit program and is applied annually for up to five consecutive taxable years.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program established in 2021 and expanded by the Maryland General Assembly in 2022 that provides emergency financial assistance to small businesses, minority-owned businesses, women-owned businesses, veteran-owned businesses, and non-profits to recover from disaster damage and loss of operations. The program is funded by the Maryland Department of Commerce through the Video Lottery Terminal (VOLT) fund, which is replenished by slot machine tax revenue from Maryland casinos. Grants of up to $50,000 can be used to cover physical damages to buildings and equipment, offset lost revenue during business closure, inventory losses, cleanup labor, equipment replacement, working capital needed to resume operations, and other legitimate business expenses related to disaster recovery. The program has been activated for multiple disaster events including the January 9-10, 2024 flooding in Annapolis and the October 29-30, 2021 flooding in Anne Arundel County, with $1,000,000 allocated for recovery assistance per activation. The program distributed $647,095 to 21 small businesses following the 2021 flooding event.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grants up to $50,000 per recipient to support recovery from designated disaster events. Grants can be used to cover physical damages to buildings and equipment, offset lost revenue during business closure, inventory losses, cleanup labor, equipment replacement, working capital needed to resume operations, and other legitimate business expenses related to disaster recovery. Recipients must provide receipts for damages and documentation of losses. The program is funded by $1,000,000 from Maryland's video lottery terminal (VLT) loan program per activation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis beginning January 16, 2024. Most recent activation began January 16, 2024 following the Mayor's declaration of a State of Emergency on January 12, 2024. Previous activation began accepting applications on November 1, 2021 for the October 29-30, 2021 disaster event.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and Veteran-owned businesses, as well as non-profits and nonprofit organizations affected by designated disaster events with commercial brick-and-mortar locations. Program coverage varies by activation; for the January 9-10, 2024 flooding, eligible applicants were located in the City of Annapolis following the Mayor's State of Emergency declaration. For the October 29-30, 2021 flooding, eligible applicants were located throughout Anne Arundel County and surrounding areas including the Eastern Shore.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recovery from damage and operational disruptions caused by designated disaster events, including physical damages to buildings and equipment, lost revenue during business closure, equipment replacement, inventory losses, cleanup labor, working capital needed to resume operations, and other legitimate business expenses related to disaster recovery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program activation varies by disaster event. For the October 29-30, 2021 flooding, the program covered Anne Arundel County and surrounding areas including the Eastern Shore. Applicants must have a commercial brick-and-mortar location in eligible disaster-affected jurisdictions. Nonprofit organizations must be located within eligible disaster-affected jurisdictions.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications with receipts for damaged equipment, inventory, and documentation of losses along with required documentation including tax returns (2022 business tax returns, Schedule C, or Form 990), damage statements, photos/videos, budget, receipts, W-9 form, and proof of purchases. AAEDC reviews applications, determines damages, and distributes funds to eligible businesses and organizations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program designed to help Maryland-based high-growth innovative and technology product companies implement a go-to-market strategy and accelerate sales. The program offers flexible underwriting standards and payment terms to allow companies to grow revenue and workforce while facilitating future equity investment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan of up to $100,000 with a term of up to 10 years. No interest or closing costs. Interest recollection amount of 10% is due when an event of recapture occurs, defined as when the company raises 5 times the original loan amount in equity investment or after 5 years, whichever comes first. After the event of recapture, the loan is repaid over 5 years in equal monthly principal payments. Collateral is a blanket lien UCC filing on company assets. Personal guaranty is required from all active owners over 20% ownership.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based high-growth innovative and technology product companies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of go-to-market strategy and sales acceleration
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based companies

Pre-revenue and minimal revenue companies may apply
Applicant must provide realistic financial projections showing cash flow positive within 12 months
Borrower must provide a business plan or investor deck showing pathway to growth and profitability
Personal guaranty required from all active owners over 20% ownership

structured_extraction.program_name: Video Lottery Facility Local Impact Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program that distributes revenue from Maryland Live! Casino video lottery terminals to support improvements in communities near the casino through Local Development Councils. The Local Development Council (LDC) awards grants to nonprofit organizations and community associations for community development projects including infrastructure, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development including housing, and other public services. Community grants range from $10,000 to $40,000 available on a competitive basis, with larger capital grants considered in unique circumstances by invitation only. All grants are distributed through the Video Lottery Facility Local Impact Grant Special Revenue Fund. The program supports community revitalization, beautification, education, workforce development, transportation, and social service programs. Grant types include General Operating Support, Program Support (new, existing, or expanded programs), Equipment and Supplies, and Physical Improvements/Capital Projects (renovation, construction, rehabilitation, alterations).

Larger capital grants may be considered in unique circumstances by invitation only. All grants distributed through the Video Lottery Facility Local Impact Grant Special Revenue Fund. Both capital and non-capital project options are available. Grant types include General Operating Support, Program Support (new, existing, or expanded programs), Equipment and Supplies, and Physical Improvements/Capital Projects (renovation, construction, rehabilitation, alterations). Non-Capital grants support organizational capacity building and operational efficiency. Capital grants support equipment, supplies, and building improvements. The program derives its funding from revenues generated by Maryland Live! Casino operations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by Anne Arundel County that allows property owners with small-scale stormwater management practices on their property to reduce their annual Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF) by up to 50%. Property owners can enter into a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement with the County to receive credits against their WPRF stormwater remediation fee. The credit amount depends on the water quality treatment provided by the practice, with full credit available for practices that treat a minimum of 1 inch of rainfall and partial credit available for less treatment. Eligible practices include rain gardens, rain barrels, native plantings, and other approved stormwater management practices designed to provide proactive and sustainable management of stormwater runoff. The program supports implementation of small-scale stormwater best management practices (BMPs) under 5,000 square feet of land disturbance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners with qualified stormwater management practices on their property receive a reduction of up to 50% on their annual Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF). Property owners can install small-scale stormwater management practices such as rain gardens, rain barrels, native plantings, and other approved practices under 5,000 square feet of land disturbance and enter into a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement with the County to receive a credit against their WPRF stormwater remediation fee. The credit amount depends on the water quality treatment provided by the practice, with full credit available for practices that treat a minimum of 1 inch of rainfall and partial credit available for less treatment.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of small-scale proactive and sustainable stormwater runoff controls such as rain gardens, rain barrels, native plantings, and other approved stormwater management practices under 5,000 square feet of land disturbance. The credit applies toward the property owner's Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF) stormwater remediation charges.

If the credit is not approved, the agreement becomes void and is not signed by the County. For application details and information on eligible practices, contact the Bureau of Watershed Protection and Restoration.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Disabled Law Enforcement Officers, Rescue Workers and Surviving Spouses
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available for disabled law enforcement officers, correctional officers, firefighters, and rescue workers (including volunteers) who have suffered permanent and total disability during their service, as well as surviving spouses in some jurisdictions. The credit reduces property tax liability on primary residential real property in Anne Arundel County, Baltimore County, and Calvert County, Maryland. In Baltimore County, the credit equals 100 percent of real property tax and continues annually for the lifetime of the disabled person. Baltimore County public safety retirees who retired on a medical disability pension due to a line of duty injury and are currently residing in the county qualify for a property tax exemption. In Anne Arundel County, the credit is calculated at 100% of total tax due on the dwelling based on real property assessment and applies after mandatory property tax credits, supplements, and deferrals. In Calvert County, the credit is available to totally and permanently disabled law enforcement officers, rescue workers, or their surviving spouses. The credit applies only to the eligible dwelling and does not extend to other charges on the bill. Anne Arundel County credit applies to county real property taxes only and does not apply to state real property taxes or other taxes, assessments, fees, or charges.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County / Baltimore County / Calvert County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit and exemption that reduces real property tax liability on the principal residence for disabled law enforcement officers, correctional officers, firefighters, and rescue workers (including volunteers) who have suffered permanent and total disability during their service, and in some jurisdictions their surviving spouses. In Baltimore County, the credit equals 100 percent of real property tax on the eligible dwelling and continues annually for the lifetime of the disabled person. In Anne Arundel County, the credit is calculated at 100% of total tax due on the dwelling and is applied after mandatory property tax credits, supplements, and deferrals, and applies only to county real property taxes. The credit applies only to county real property tax obligations and does not extend to state taxes or other charges on the bill.

Career employees of fire, rescue, or emergency medical services entities. Members of volunteer fire companies or volunteer rescue squads.

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property Tax Credit for Day Care Centers
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for real property dedicated exclusively to day care centers and day care services, including registered family day care homes, licensed childcare centers, and licensed day care centers for the elderly or medically handicapped. The credit is available to owners of real property and taxpayers making improvements to property used exclusively for day care operations. In Montgomery County, the credit is limited to the lesser of $10,000 per year or the amount of General County and Special Area taxes attributable to the improvement. In Anne Arundel County, the credit is limited to the lesser of $4,000 per year or the amount of general county real property tax attributable to the improvement. The credit applies to property owners whose real property is dedicated to day care operations and taxpayers making improvements to real property used exclusively for day care services, including businesses with at least 25 employees.

list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

In Montgomery County, the credit is limited to the lesser of $10,000 per year or the amount of general county and special service area taxes attributable to the improvement. In Anne Arundel County, the credit is limited to the lesser of $4,000 per year or the amount of general county real property tax attributable to the improvement. Property owner must own and operate the facility with area set aside and dedicated exclusively for licensed or registered day care use. A taxpayer may receive a property tax credit for an improvement on real property owned by a business with at least 25 employees, if the improvement is used exclusively for day care services. Duration, amount, and calculation of the tax credit are established by county ordinance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit for Property Leased by Religious Organizations
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit against county real property taxes on property that is leased, occupied, and used by religious organizations exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or office space supporting those activities. The credit applies to property in commercial zoning districts in Anne Arundel County and Prince George's County, and to qualifying property in Montgomery County. Property owners are contractually obligated to reduce the amount of taxes the religious organization is liable for by the amount of the tax credit. The credit does not apply to property used for profit-making activities or when the organization no longer occupies the property.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% tax credit on the assessed value of the property portion used by the religious organization, up to the amount of tax for which the organization is contractually liable. In Anne Arundel County and Prince George's County, the credit applies to property in commercial zoning districts, and the property owner is contractually obligated to reduce the amount of taxes the religious organization is liable for by the amount of the tax credit. In Montgomery County, the credit is granted against the County real property tax for that portion of property leased, occupied, and used by a religious organization exclusively for the eligible purposes. The credit does not apply to property used for profit-making activities or when the organization no longer occupies the property.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permanent trust fund established by Baltimore City to support affordable housing development and programs for both renters and homeowners, creating housing options for low-income working families. The fund supports very-low and low-income households with incomes at or below 50 percent of the Area Median Income (AMI), with at least half of funds supporting those at or below 30 percent of AMI. The City allocates funds annually to the Trust Fund, with allocations of $2 million (FY2020), $3.5 million (FY2021), $5 million (FY2022), and $7 million (FY2023 and subsequent years). Up to $8.1 million in funding is available for Community Land Trust homeownership projects, with qualified applicants able to request up to $1,000,000 to $2,000,000 per project depending on the funding round. Additional funding of up to $7,500,000 is available for new construction and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing, with individual projects able to request up to $1,000,000. The program supports three homeownership strategies: Acquisition & Rehab, Buyers Choice/Buyer-Initiated, and Innovation approaches. The program enables perpetually affordable housing through a shared equity model where the land trust owns the land and purchasers build equity as property values grow. The program includes set-asides for Community Land Trusts and emerging developers. Applications for Community Land Trust homeownership projects are accepted on a rolling basis through June 30, 2026 or until funds are allocated. Rental housing funding rounds occur periodically with specific NOFA deadlines; recent rounds include Round 4 (closed March 17, 2023) and Round 7 (accepted applications through January 9, 2026).

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City allocates funds annually to support affordable housing development and programs. Annual allocations include $2 million (FY2020), $3.5 million (FY2021), $5 million (FY2022), and $7 million (FY2023 and subsequent years). Up to $8.1 million in total funding is available from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund for Community Land Trust homeownership projects, with qualified applicants able to request up to $1,000,000 to $2,000,000 per project depending on the round. Funds can cover up to 50% of Total Development Cost (TDC) for units at ≤50% AMI, or up to 66% TDC for units at ≤30% AMI. Maximum per unit: $75,000 for 50% AMI units or $120,000 for 30% AMI units. For rental housing, funding for 30% AMI units is up to $150,000 per unit (requires minimum 10 units at 30% AMI for bonus points), and funding for 50% AMI units is up to $75,000 per unit. Up to 25% of award can be used for predevelopment/acquisition; up to 20% for operating costs; up to 10% for support services. Up to $7,500,000 is available for new construction and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing projects, with individual projects able to request up to $1,000,000. Additional rental housing funding rounds may provide up to $10,750,000, including $2 million in set-asides for Community Land Trusts and emerging developers. Applications for Community Land Trust homeownership projects are accepted on a rolling basis through June 30, 2026 or until funds are allocated, with award notification provided within 90 days of submission. Rental housing funding rounds occur periodically with specific NOFA deadlines; the most recent round (Round 7) opened on November 21, 2025, with a submission deadline of January 9, 2026, and award notifications sent the week of April 13, 2026. A total of up to $1.7 million was made available in prior rounds for new construction and rehabilitation of existing rental projects. Ten percent of the funding has been designated for emerging developers, defined as developers who have completed at least three and no more than five projects. Applicants may receive up to 50% of total development costs. Up to 25% of award can be advanced (for grant recipients only). Funds are provided on a reimbursement basis; applicants should arrange line of credit for project cash flow.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis through June 30, 2026 for Community Land Trust projects; Round 7 rental NOFA deadline January 9, 2026 or until all funds allocated; Round 4 closed March 17, 2023
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters at 30% or less of AMI, homeowners at 50% or less of AMI, very-low and low-income households with incomes at or below 50 percent of the Area Median Income, with priority for those at or below 30 percent of AMI; Community Land Trusts organized or managed by nonprofit organizations exempt from taxation under § 501(c)(2), (3), or (4) of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code seeking to develop affordable homeownership projects; non-profit and for-profit developers seeking to build new affordable rental housing or rehabilitate existing rental projects in Baltimore City; real estate developers and community development organizations seeking to create or preserve affordable rental housing; emerging developers with experience completing at least three and no more than five projects; homeless individuals and families; tenants at 30% AMI and below; residents who received rental assistance; residents who received homeownership program assistance; low-income working families; and organizations including nonprofit affordable housing developers, homebuilders or realtor associations, social service providers, and lending institutions with community development and affordable housing finance experience.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certification to operate as an air monitoring contractor under the Baltimore Clean Air Act. Entities are certified to provide air monitoring services for commercial solid waste incinerators. Contractors must design, install, operate, and maintain continuous emissions monitoring systems (CEMS) that measure specified air pollutants including dioxins/furans, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, hydrochloric acid, hydrofluoric acid, nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide, particulate matter, volatile organic compounds, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, arsenic, cadmium, chromium (VI), lead, manganese, mercury, nickel, selenium, and zinc. Contractors must receive daily emissions reports from incinerators, report violations to the Health Department, display historical and daily emissions data on a public website with graphical representations, and conduct unannounced inspections of CEMS equipment at least four times per calendar year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Historic Rehabilitation and Restoration Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A ten-year property tax credit program administered by the Commission for Historical and Architectural Preservation (CHAP) that provides financial incentives to property owners who undertake qualified historic restoration and rehabilitation work on designated historic properties in Baltimore City's local historic districts and designated landmark properties. The program was established in 1996 to help preserve and revitalize Baltimore's neighborhoods by encouraging home and business owners to restore or rehabilitate historic buildings, with an amended goal to promote equitable and inclusive economic growth and vitality of the City of Baltimore. The credit is applied to the increased property value resulting from qualifying rehabilitation work and can be used by both residential and commercial property owners. The credit appears as a special credit on the property's tax bill and is calculated by the Department of Finance based on the rehabilitation investment. Projects must invest a minimum of 25% of the property's full cash value to qualify. The credit is fully transferrable to a new owner for the remaining life of the credit. Properties eligible include those in Baltimore City's 33 local historic districts and 182 local landmarks, including residential, commercial, and mixed-use properties. Over $1.2 billion in private sector investment across 3,500+ historic properties has been completed since 1997.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A ten-year tax credit on property taxes computed on the increased property value resulting from qualifying rehabilitation work. The credit amount is calculated by the Department of Finance based on the qualified rehabilitation investment in the historic property and is used for the entire 10-year period. The credit appears on the property's next issued tax bill as a 'Special Credit' and is fully transferrable to a new owner for the remaining life of the credit. Projects must invest a minimum of 25% of the property's full cash value to qualify. For projects ≤$5.0 million, 100% of the credit is granted for years 1-10. For projects >$5.0 million, a graduated percentage applies (80% years 1-5, declining to 30% year 10). Credit equals the difference between City real property tax on post-improvement full cash value and City real property tax on base year full cash value. The credit is calculated as: (post-rehabilitation appraisal value minus pre-rehabilitation appraisal value) × city tax rate. Eligible costs include material and labor costs, architect fees, engineering fees, design fees, architectural design, appraisal, and interior and exterior rehabilitation and restoration work. Ineligible costs include property acquisition, utility bills, property taxes, and holding costs. The Historic Tax Credit can be combined with the Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program and Federal Historic Preservation Tax Incentives Program, but cannot be combined with other City credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No new applications for the tax credit may be filed after August 28, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in historic districts of Baltimore City undertaking major rehabilitation and restoration projects on residential, commercial, or mixed-use properties and designated local landmarks, including individual homeowners, for-profit developers, non-profit organizations, first-time home buyers, local developers, and business owners. Both residential and commercial property owners are eligible. The program attracts developers, contractors, and investors interested in historic property rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified rehabilitation work on historically designated properties that meets CHAP Design Guidelines. Eligible costs include material and labor costs, architect fees, engineering fees, design fees, architectural design, appraisal, and interior and exterior rehabilitation and restoration work on historic structures. Work requiring Authorization to Proceed from CHAP, demolition and site preparation, restoration and alteration work, electrical, plumbing, mechanical work, and interior and exterior finish work are eligible. Ineligible costs include property acquisition, utility bills, property taxes, and holding costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Properties must be located in one of Baltimore City's 33 local historic districts, be one of 182 local landmarks, or be historically designated as a Baltimore City Landmark, National Register Individual Designation, contributing to a Baltimore City Historic District, contributing to a National Register Historic District, or contributing to the Baltimore National Heritage Area. Approximately 20% of Baltimore City land area is in eligible districts, covering 38 of 55 Community Statistical Areas (CSAs). Properties in Enterprise Zones have additional requirements if the property is commercial.
requirements_list: Property must be located in a historic district or be a designated local landmark in Baltimore City

Property must be historically designated as: individually listed on National Register of Historic Places, located in National Register Historic or Landmark District, designated on Baltimore City Landmark List, or located in Baltimore City Historic and Architectural Preservation District (certified by CHAP)
Rehabilitation work must comply with CHAP Design Guidelines
Work must be qualified historic restoration or rehabilitation
Both residential and commercial properties are eligible
Project must receive preliminary CHAP approval before work begins
Minimum investment of 25% of the property's full cash value (significant improvements threshold)

Completion timeline: 2 years for projects under $3.5 million in rehabilitation costs (with one-time 2-year extension available), or 3 years for projects $3.5 million or more (with one-time 3-year extension available)
Final certification from CHAP required
Appraisal must meet Department of Finance requirements
Pre-improvement appraisal must be submitted within 90 days of application
Post-improvement appraisal must be submitted within 90 days of final Use and Occupancy Permit or last permit inspection
Commercial buildings and properties with 4+ rental units must provide own appraisals
Projects $3.5 million or more require additional Department of Finance review and approval
If in Enterprise Zone with commercial component, must submit Enterprise Zone Verification Form
Property must meet City Building, Fire, and Related Codes
Property must increase in full cash value after improvements to qualify
No other local optional real property tax subsidies can be applied (except Maryland Enterprise Zone Tax Credit)
Cannot be altered to lose historic compliance or have major historic features removed during 10-year credit term
Pre-improvement and post-improvement appraisals by certified appraiser required (for applications after October 1, 2014)
Appraiser must be licensed in Maryland
Appraisals must be 'as is' as of effective date and assume private sector purchaser ownership
Property owner must maintain major historic features and comply with city codes
Design review required for minor and major work
Work must be appropriate to historic character of property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Read the Tax Credit FAQ, CHAP Design Guidelines, and Program Rules and Regulations. Apply online through the Historic Tax Credit Application system. Property owners must work with CHAP to ensure their restoration or rehabilitation plans comply with historic preservation guidelines. Submit complete application with required documentation including color photographs of exterior and interior, existing and proposed drawings if applicable, detailed scope of work, proof of ownership, appraisal, and $50 review fee. For non-residential properties, submit draft appraisal report (PDF format) to Department of Finance Review Appraiser within 45 days of assignment commencement. CHAP staff reviews and issues written approval via email. Complete rehabilitation work following CHAP guidelines. Submit final certification through online system by going to 'DOCUMENTS/UPLOADS' tab to upload final certification materials, then go to 'SIGNATURE' tab and select 'SUBMIT FINAL' with completion photographs, permits, notarized cost documentation, and final appraisal. Once final certification is approved, the credit appears on the next issued tax bill.

The program applies to City-awarded contracts over $300,000, City-subsidized projects over $5,000,000, and City contracts valued between $50,000 and $300,000 (excluding emergency and professional services). Businesses receive free services including recruitment help, pre-screening of applicants, job posting distribution, free interview space, employment analysis, and local hiring coordination through the B2Gnow vendor portal system. No direct financial payments are made; assistance is in-kind service support to help meet hiring requirements.

No direct financial payments are made; assistance is in-kind service support to help meet hiring requirements.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: After a contract is awarded by the City, the City agency submits a Vendor Contact Form to MOED. MOED contacts the vendor and completes an employment analysis within two weeks. The business or vendor meets with MOED Employer Services staff to discuss staffing needs and available free services. When ready to hire, the business sends job postings to MOED through the B2Gnow vendor portal system. The MOED team shares openings, pre-screens applicants, and offers free interview space. Businesses enter new hire information in the vendor profile Employees tab or contract profile Workforce Employee List, complete required fields with worker details, and assign employees to contracts. Vendors submit monthly employment reports via B2Gnow system beginning at the start of each month for the previous month's data.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Strategic Investment – Rapid Re-housing
structured_extraction.program_description: A rapid re-housing intervention informed by Housing First approach that rapidly connects families and individuals experiencing homelessness to permanent housing through tailored assistance packages. The program provides time-limited financial assistance and targeted support services to help solve practical and immediate challenges to obtaining permanent housing, reduce time experiencing homelessness, and link clients to community resources for long-term housing stability. It includes three primary components: housing identification and securing permanent housing options, rental assistance administration, and intensive case management/wraparound support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MOHS received $5,663,850 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding to support rapid re-housing efforts through qualified non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations and city government agencies. The funding supports implementation and operation of rapid re-housing programs providing: (1) Rental assistance: short- and medium-term financial subsidies (4-24 months) for rent, security deposits, moving expenses, and utilities, using FY2022 Fair Market Rent data and progressive engagement models (declining subsidy, fixed percentage, or fixed subsidy); (2) Housing identification services: unit identification and location, transportation coordination, lease review, and housing inspections to ensure units pass approved inspection and meet safety/maintenance requirements; (3) Case management and wraparound support services: individualized service planning, employment and workforce referrals, health and mental health services, behavioral health referrals, mainstream benefits brokerage, budgeting assistance, life skills support, and transition planning. Supportive services also include landlord incentives and assistance with moving costs. Multiple providers were selected to operate rapid re-housing projects, with rental assistance provided for approximately 12 months per household using scattered site rental units across different neighborhoods in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, July 15, 2022 @ 4pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organizations and city government agencies with capacity to implement and operate rapid re-housing programs in Baltimore City. Target beneficiaries are individuals and families currently experiencing Category 1 (Literally Homeless) or Category 4 (Fleeing/Attempting to Flee Domestic Violence) homelessness with income under 30% of Area Median Income for 2022, referred through Baltimore City's Coordinated Access System. Priority populations include: people of color, seniors, individuals with multiple health conditions, pregnant/parenting individuals, LGBTQ individuals, survivors of domestic violence/intimate partner violence, survivors of sexual trafficking/exploitation, individuals with lived experience in institutional settings, and veterans. Program also serves households without children, households with children, and youth households (18-24).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing identification and coordination; rental assistance payments (security deposits, moving expenses, utilities); case management and wraparound supportive services; staff salaries and benefits for housing identification, case management, and supportive services staff; office operations (utilities, lease, supplies); professional services; equipment and machinery; landlord incentive payments; and workforce development partnerships and employment support. Cannot screen out based on income, substance abuse history, criminal record, or domestic violence history.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Applicant organizations must be located in or provide services in Baltimore City. Services provided through scattered site rental units across different neighborhoods in Baltimore City.
