structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Two-stage application process: (1) Proposal Stage: Organizations submit proposals (Letters of Intent) by November 23, 2025, 11:59 p.m. EST through the Mayor's Office of Recovery Programs Application Portal. Proposals are scored based on criteria outlined in appendices. Eligible organizations that score above threshold advance to the next stage. (2) Full Application Stage: Selected organizations submit detailed full applications by January 25, 2026, 11:59 p.m. EST. Applications are scored on 9 criteria using a point-based evaluation system (maximum 100+ points including bonus points). Scoring criteria include project description, alignment with program goals, risk analysis, performance measures, equity impact, financial planning, partnerships, organizational track record, and alignment with city's strategic plan. Organizations with local yearly operating budgets under $15 million receive additional points (5-10 points). Awards are determined based on approved applications, funding tier amounts, and total available funding. MORP coordinates fiscal management and oversight for all opioid restitution fund grantees and programs. Technical assistance and project management support available throughout process. Projects close upon fulfillment of agreement terms or conclusion of agreement period.

Applicants select results and indicators aligned with B-CIITY priorities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ryan White Part A HIV/AIDS Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Ryan White Part A Program provides HIV-related medical and support services to people living with HIV who lack sufficient health insurance coverage or financial resources. The program works across Baltimore City and six surrounding counties to serve more than 10,000 people annually, filling gaps in care not covered by insurance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program funds core medical services including outpatient and ambulatory medical care, oral health, health insurance premium and cost-sharing assistance for low-income individuals, medical nutrition therapy, hospice services, mental health services, substance abuse outpatient care, and medical case management. Support services include outreach, medical transportation, substance abuse residential treatment, legal services, housing assistance, psychosocial services, child care, and food bank services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People living with HIV disease who do not have sufficient health care coverage or financial resources for coping with HIV disease. The Planning Council gives particular focus to individuals who know their HIV status but are not currently in care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Core medical services such as outpatient medical care, oral health, insurance premium assistance, medical nutrition therapy, hospice, mental health services, substance abuse treatment, and medical case management. Support services including outreach, transportation, legal services, housing, child care, and food assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Baltimore Epidemic Management Area (EMA) includes Baltimore City and six surrounding counties: Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Carroll County, Anne Arundel County, and Queen Anne's County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Safe City Baltimore: Immigrant Education and Defense Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Safe City Baltimore provides education about immigrant rights, legal assistance for individuals with viable claims to remain in the United States, and deportation defense services. The program operates in three levels: community education and family safety planning, legal assistance through screening clinics and pro bono coordination, and deportation defense with rapid response and bond assistance for families with limited resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides three levels of support: Level 1 offers Know Your Rights information sessions, family safety plans, and guidance on ICE arrest procedures. Level 2 provides immigration screening clinics, coordination with pro bono legal providers, Department of Justice accreditation expansion for immigration lawyers, and assistance with immigration applications. Level 3 offers rapid response services, legal representation coordination, case management support for families, and immigration bond assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Immigrant families and individuals in Baltimore facing deportation or seeking legal assistance to remain in the United States
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support Know Your Rights education, family safety planning, legal assistance including immigration applications, deportation defense, case management, and immigration bond assistance for families with limited resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Immigrant status
Viable claim to remain in the United States (for Level 2 and 3 services)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs at mima@baltimorecity.gov for assistance and to access the three levels of services offered through the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides reimbursement to Baltimore City residential customers (homeowners and tenants) who have experienced sewage backups, including basement backups, caused by capacity-related wet weather events (at least 1/4 inch of precipitation in 24 hours that causes sewer lines to surcharge or overflow). Eligible applicants receive compensation for documented cleanup, disinfection, and disposal costs, including insurance deductibles in some cases. Reimbursement is provided up to $5,000 per dwelling unit, per occurrence for events occurring on or after April 6, 2018.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners and tenants who experience sewage backups can apply for reimbursement of cleanup, disinfection, and disposal costs up to $5,000 per dwelling unit, per occurrence. If the property is insured against sewage backups, applicants must receive a final written determination from their insurance company before processing. Insurance deductibles may be eligible for reimbursement if costs are directly linked to cleanup or disinfection. Applications are processed within 60 days of receiving all necessary documentation. Once approved, applicants receive a release for signature before their reimbursement check is processed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be received within 90 days after the backup
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-396-3100 between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.; 410-396-3500 to have an application mailed or inquire about the program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residential customers (homeowners and tenants) who have experienced sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet weather events.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cleanup, disinfection, and disposal costs resulting from sewage backups or basement backups caused by sanitary sewer system surcharging during capacity-related wet weather events. Insurance deductibles are eligible if demonstrably linked to cleanup, disinfection, or disposal.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Sewage backup events prior to April 6, 2018 are not eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a City residential customer (homeowner or tenant)
Sewage backup must be caused by a capacity-related wet weather event (at least 1/4 inch of precipitation in 24 hours)
Sewage backup events must occur on or after April 6, 2018
File application within 90 days after the incident
If insured against sewage backups, obtain a final written determination from insurance company before application processing
Provide all documentation received from insurance company, including proof of any deductible paid
Document all cleanup and disinfection expenses incurred
Sign and return the release form before check processing
If tenant, must provide copy of lease signed by property owner
If filing on behalf of an owner or tenant, must include written proof of power of attorney
Backup must be the result of surcharging in the collection system caused by wet weather events
Costs must be documented
Maximum reimbursement of $5,000 per dwelling, per occurrence
Notify City through 311 system within 24 hours of discovery
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online through the website, or by email (reimbursement@baltimorecity.gov), certified U.S. Mail, or commercial delivery to 200 Holliday Street, Baltimore, MD 21202 within 90 days of the sewage backup incident. If insured, obtain a final written determination from your insurance company (you have up to 30 days after receiving it to provide this). Include all insurance documentation, proof of deductibles paid, and documentation of all cleanup, disinfection, and disposal expenses with your application. The city processes applications within 60 days of receiving all necessary information. If approved, you will receive a release form to sign and return before your reimbursement check is processed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sewage Onsite Support (SOS) Cleanup Program provides free professional cleaning, disinfection, and disposal services to Baltimore City residential customers whose properties have been damaged by sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet-weather events (heavy or sustained rain that causes sewer lines to surcharge or overflow). Professional contractors remove hazardous materials, clean and disinfect affected areas, dispose of soiled property, deodorize, and dry the property to help remove health risks from raw sewage contamination. On-call cleaning contractors contact customers within approximately one hour to schedule cleanup appointments available from 8 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free professional cleaning, disinfection, disposal, deodorization, dehumidification, and drying services provided by contracted third-party vendors at no cost to eligible residents. Services include disinfection and cleaning to eliminate viruses and bacteria, removal and disposal of soiled carpets, flooring, furniture and other affected property, professional deodorization using specialized equipment, and dehumidification and drying of affected areas. On-call cleaning contractors contact customers within approximately one hour to schedule cleanup appointments available from 8 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: As soon as the sewer backup is discovered
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 311 (to report sewage backup) or 410-396-3500 (for service concerns)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residential customers, including homeowners, residents, tenants, and property managers whose properties have been damaged by sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet-weather events.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cleaning and disinfection of property damaged by sewage backup, removal of soiled carpet, flooring, furniture and other affected property, professional odor removal, dehumidification and drying of affected areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Services are available only to residential customers who reside in Baltimore City. Program does not cover stormwater flooding, water main breaks, or dry weather events such as grease clogs or root intrusion.
requirements_list: Damage must be caused by a backup occurring during a capacity-related wet-weather event (at least 1/4 inch of precipitation within 24 hours that causes sewer lines to surcharge or overflow)
You must be a Baltimore City residential customer (homeowner or tenant)
Property must be a residential property (single-family or multi-family); commercial properties are not eligible
The residential property owner, tenant, or property manager must report the damage to DPW by calling 311 or visiting 311.baltimorecity.gov as soon as the damage is discovered
The City must confirm that the damage was caused by a capacity-related wet-weather event
Eligibility is limited to either the SOS Cleanup Program or the Expedited Reimbursement Program for Sewage Backups, not both
Not covered: stormwater flooding, water main breaks, or dry weather events (grease clogs, root intrusion)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: The residential property owner, tenant, or property manager must call 311 or visit 311.baltimorecity.gov to report the sewage backup damage to DPW as soon as it is discovered. Step 2: DPW will send an inspector to determine the cause of the sewage backup. If the backup is confirmed to be caused by a capacity-related wet-weather event, DPW will offer the cleaning program and an on-call cleaning contractor will contact the customer within approximately one hour. Step 3: Schedule a cleanup appointment (available 8 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week). Step 4: The cleaning contractor provides services and the customer signs a satisfaction/job completion form after service.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Side Yard Program allows property owners adjacent to city-owned vacant lots to purchase these side lots to expand their property. Owners can transform the lots into gardens, landscaping, parking pads, decks, or other uses to increase property value and beautify their neighborhood.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners can purchase adjacent city-owned vacant lots at fixed pricing for lots up to 1500 square feet. Lots larger than 1500 square feet incur additional cost per square foot. The maximum lot size is 5000 square feet. Purchasers pay a full amount via certified check, money order, or cashier's check at settlement. Some properties are subject to annual ground rent.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners adjacent to city-owned vacant lots in Baltimore City who want to expand their property and beautify their neighborhood.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchased side lots can be used for gardens, landscaping, fencing, driveways, existing property expansion, and other purposes subject to Baltimore City laws and zoning requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Side yard properties must be physically contiguous to the adjacent owner's principal residence.
requirements_list: Side yard properties must be vacant and unimproved
Side yard properties must be physically contiguous to adjacent owner's principal residence
Applicant must have a record of responsible property ownership and management
Priority given to owner-occupants
Side yard properties shall consist of no more than two lots incapable of independent development
Fixed pricing applies only to lots up to 1500 square feet; lots greater than 1500 SF subject to additional cost per square foot
Maximum side yard size is 5000 square feet
Intended use is subject to Baltimore City laws and regulations
Some uses may require Zoning approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners complete an application disclosing intended uses. The application is reviewed and a determination is made within approximately 30 days. If approved, the applicant submits payment via certified check, money order, or cashier's check. The application then proceeds to Board of Estimates approval (approximately 45 days) and settlement (approximately 45 days). Total estimated timeline is 120 days.

structured_extraction.program_name: Staying Alive Drug Overdose Prevention and Response Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Staying Alive program, begun in 2004, is a public health intervention to reduce overdose deaths in Baltimore City due to opioid-related overdoses. The program provides free naloxone (Narcan) kits and training in recognizing the signs and symptoms of opioid and heroin overdose and responding appropriately to maximize survival chances. Participants receive naloxone and are trained to administer it during overdose emergencies. The program has distributed nearly 26,000 naloxone kits between 2023 and 2025. Between 2015 and 2023, the program trained more than 155,000 Baltimore residents and saved the lives of more than 18,000 people. In 2015, the program gained state certification allowing trained staff to certify third parties in addition to individuals with substance use disorders.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free training in overdose recognition and response, free naloxone kits to trained individuals at no cost, and overdose prevention education. Training is offered through virtual community trainings via Eventbrite registration, in-person training requests, or kit request forms. Residents can visit any MDH-registered Overdose Response Program or Syringe Service Program to receive free naloxone. Training is available at various treatment centers, Syringe Exchange Program sites, and the Baltimore City Detention Center. The program offers virtual naloxone training sessions and instructional videos on how to administer naloxone. Free naloxone kits can be requested by calling 443-615-7792. The program maintains state certification allowing trained staff to certify third parties. Support and resources are provided for substance use disorder treatment referrals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline specified; ongoing program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anyone in Baltimore City who wants to obtain naloxone and overdose prevention training, including residents, individuals with substance use disorders, inmates, drug treatment clients, healthcare providers, correctional staff, friends, family members, and bystanders who want to be prepared to respond to an overdose. Specifically targets people at risk of opioid overdose, friends and family members of people using opioids, and individuals leaving correctional facilities, rehab, or detox.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Naloxone kits for opioid overdose reversal, overdose prevention education and training, and certification of trainers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. The program serves residents and anyone in Baltimore City who wants to access naloxone and overdose prevention training.
requirements_list: Must be located in Baltimore City to access free naloxone through this program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can access naloxone and training through multiple methods: call 443-615-7792 to request free naloxone kits, register for live virtual community naloxone training through Eventbrite, submit a naloxone training request form, submit a naloxone kit request form, visit one of the listed MDH-registered Overdose Response Program or Syringe Service Program locations throughout Baltimore City, or attend training at Syringe Exchange Program sites, treatment centers, and the Baltimore City Detention Center. A map of locations is available online.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Credit Program for Non-Single Family Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: Program established by Maryland Legislature in 2012 providing fee reductions and credits to non-single-family property owners in Baltimore City who implement stormwater management practices, including treatment practices, green space, small development projects, participation in water quality improvement activities, NPDES permits, and direct harbor discharge. The program aims to reduce flooding and erosion and keep waterways cleaner by providing a dedicated revenue source for maintaining, operating, and improving the City's stormwater management system. Businesses, churches, non-profits, industries, and other non-single family property owners can receive credits or fee reductions for installing stormwater best management practices, maintaining green space, holding stormwater permits, or meeting other environmental criteria such as maintaining private storm drains that discharge to Baltimore Harbor.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Stormwater fee reductions and credits ranging from 10% to 85% depending on credit type and combinations, applied to stormwater remediation base fee. Base fee calculated on impervious surface area measured in Equivalent Residential Units (ERUs) at $6.50/ERU/month. Specific credits include: Religious Structure Special Fee ($1/ERU/month capped) for tax-exempt religious structures; Maximum Fee Cap at 20% of real property taxes; Green Space Credit (45% of initial fee for parcels less than 50 sq ft impervious area); Small Development Credit (33% for parcels 50-820 sq ft impervious area); Treatment Practice Credits (up to 45% for Best Management Practices); NPDES Industrial Permit Credit (55%); Harbor Discharger Credit (30%); Participation Credit for participation in public water quality improvement projects; and Hardship Exemption (full exemption possible with approved alternative compliance plan). Credits reduce stormwater fee bills for properties implementing water quality improvements, meeting stormwater treatment standards, or meeting permit requirements. Maximum credit cannot exceed 100% of base stormwater fee.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Renewal applications must be received within 30 days before end of credit period
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-single-family property owners, property managers/designated representatives, NPDES Industrial Permit holders, religious institutions with tax-exempt status, and other non-single family property owners in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stormwater fee reductions and credits applied to stormwater remediation fees for properties implementing approved stormwater management practices, treatment practices, green infrastructure, or meeting permit and environmental criteria. Funds support maintaining, operating, and improving stormwater management system, reducing nutrients and pollutants in waterways, and reducing flooding and erosion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Off-site treatment practices must be located in the same 8-digit watershed as the property receiving credit.

Small developments and lots with 50-820 square feet of impervious or non-absorbent area
Hold a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Industrial Stormwater Discharge Permit
Own and maintain private storm drains that discharge directly to Baltimore Harbor
Maintain streets in cemeteries that are privately maintained and open to the public
Religious structures with tax-exempt status used exclusively for places of worship or K-12 education
Veterans' organizations exempt under IRC § 501(c)(4) or (19)
Charitable nonprofit organizations under IRC § 501(c)(3) or (d) experiencing financial hardship
Best Management Practices (BMPs) must be installed and application approved before credit issued
Execution of inspection and maintenance agreement required
Department may inspect BMPs at least once every three years
Property owners responsible for proper BMP maintenance
Improper maintenance may result in credit rescission
Total credit cannot exceed 100% of property's stormwater fee
Must complete and submit the stormwater fee credit application
Submit narrative for off-site treatment justification
Provide documentation: site drawings, topographic contours, impervious area calculations, proof of ownership
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Determine eligibility based on property characteristics and stormwater practices. Install and maintain eligible Best Management Practices (BMPs) if applicable. Execute inspection and maintenance agreement with Department. Complete and submit the appropriate stormwater fee credit application renewal within 30 days before the end of the credit period. Reference the Non-Single Family Property Guidance Document for detailed instructions and application forms.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Credit Program for Single-Family Property Owners
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that offers credits on stormwater fees to single-family property owners in Baltimore City who install stormwater treatment practices such as trees, rain gardens, and rain barrels, or who volunteer in organized community activities like tree planting and clean-ups that provide water quality benefits and reduce stormwater runoff. The program was established by a 2012 Maryland Legislature mandate for the 10 largest state jurisdictions and aims to protect water quality, create payment equity, reduce public expenditures on stormwater management, and promote private sector stormwater management.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive credits on their stormwater fee by installing and maintaining stormwater treatment practices such as trees, rain gardens, and rain barrels, or by volunteering hours in organized community activities including tree planting and clean-up events that provide water quality benefits. Credits are applied to reduce stormwater fee bills. Specific credits available include: participation in certified public water quality projects ($10 per 4 hours, maximum $30 per year); tree planting ($5 per year per tree, minimum 2 trees); small rain gardens ($8 per year); large rain gardens ($16 per year); rain barrels ($25 one-time per barrel, 50+ gallons); and other residential best management practices (up to 45% of stormwater fee). Credits are typically valid for 12 months to 3 years depending on the type.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline; applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family property owners in Baltimore City who pay water bills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credits reduce stormwater fee bills for property owners who implement water quality improvements through stormwater treatment practices or volunteer participation in community activities that provide water quality benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only; residents who pay Baltimore City water bills
requirements_list: Must own a single-family property in Baltimore City
Must be an individual property owner or designated representative
Property must be single-family residential
For participation credits: must volunteer for certified City water quality events (4 hours earns $10 credit, maximum $30 per year); register event with DPW by calling 311
For tree planting: minimum 2 trees planted, 1+ inch diameter, conforming to City landscaping guidelines
For rain gardens: small rain gardens minimum 50 square feet; large rain gardens minimum 100 square feet
For rain barrels: 50+ gallons minimum
Must complete and submit the Stormwater fee credit application with required documentation including photos of BMP and sketch showing location relative to lot lines and impervious areas
Maintenance documentation required for renewal applications
Must execute right-of-entry agreement with Department if applicable
Must receive certificate(s) of event participation if applicable
Must install and maintain stormwater treatment practices such as trees, rain gardens, or rain barrels, OR participate in organized volunteer activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a stormwater participation event or install stormwater best management practices. Call 311 to register volunteer cleanup events. Participate in registered Volunteer Community Cleanup and receive certificate via email or mail. Complete and submit the Stormwater fee credit application form with required documentation (photos, sketches, maintenance records) to the Bureau of Water and Wastewater by mail or email. Single-family property owners can reference the Single Family Property Guidance Document for detailed application instructions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Hardship Exemption and Alternative Compliance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program established in 2012 by the Maryland Legislature mandating stormwater fees in Baltimore City to provide a sustainable, dedicated revenue source for maintaining, operating, and improving the City's stormwater management system. The program aims to reduce flooding and erosion, keep waterways cleaner, and reduce nutrients and pollutants to bodies of water. Eligible tax-exempt organizations and non-single family properties can apply for hardship exemptions and fee reductions from stormwater fees based on impervious surface area. Eligible tax-exempt organizations can receive a full waiver of the Stormwater Remediation Fee by submitting an approved Alternative Compliance Plan demonstrating environmental protection efforts. Other property types can receive fee reductions through credits for treatment practices, green space, participation, and other stormwater management activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt organizations (501(c)(3), (c)(d), (c)(4), (c)(19), or places of worship or K-12 education) can receive a full waiver of the Stormwater Remediation Fee by submitting an approved Alternative Compliance Plan. Religious structures may receive capped fees at $1/ERU/month. Other property types can receive fee reductions and credits including: participation credits ($10/4hr/yr), green space credits (45%), small development credits (33%), treatment practice credits (structural and activity-based, up to 45%), NPDES industrial permit credits (55%), and harbor discharge credits (30%). Maximum fee cap is 20% of real property taxes. Maximum credit cannot exceed 100% of property's stormwater base fee. Waived training fees for National Green Infrastructure Certification Program (NGICP). Support and resources provided by DPW, EPA, MDE, Blue Water Baltimore, and other partners.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual renewal required within 30 days before credit period ends
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable and nonprofit organizations exempt under § 501(c)(3) or (d), veterans organizations exempt under § 501(c)(4) or (19), religious nonprofits used exclusively for places of worship or K-12 education, non-single family property owners, commercial and industrial property owners, and multi-family property owners located in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption or reduction of stormwater remediation fees for organizations implementing approved environmental compliance plans and property owners installing or maintaining best management practices and stormwater management systems. Fees support maintaining, operating, and improving the City's stormwater management system.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only; properties claiming off-site treatment practice credits must be within the same 8-digit watershed; off-site treatment must be justified with narrative explanation of appropriateness
requirements_list: Must be tax-exempt organization (501(c)(3), (c)(d), (c)(4), (c)(19), or religious organization) OR non-single family property owner in Baltimore City
For hardship exemption: annual stormwater fee must exceed 0.75% of total annual revenue; total annual revenue must not exceed $1,000,000

structured_extraction.program_description: Pediatric and adolescent immunization clinics provided by the Baltimore City Health Department offering COVID-19, influenza, pneumonia, RSV, and other vaccinations. Blood lead testing is also available. The program provides no-cost or low-cost vaccinations to children, adolescents, and adults who qualify, helping prevent vaccine-preventable diseases.

The Baltimore City Health Department offers a sliding scale discount on vaccine administration fees based on household size and income. Blood lead testing services are also available. Those who lack the ability to pay for services will not be denied services.

By appointment only

First name, last name, and date of birth

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-396-4454 (Monday-Friday, 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM) to schedule an appointment. Clients are seen by appointment only. structured_extraction.program_description: A financial instrument used by the City of Baltimore to fund development projects within designated TIF districts. The increase in property tax revenue generated by development in the district is set aside to repay the bonds. Once the TIF debt is repaid, the district is dissolved and increased tax revenue goes to the City's general fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TIF bonds are issued to fund development projects in designated districts. The bonds are repaid using the increase in property tax revenue generated by the development project within the TIF district.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers seeking to undertake development projects in designated TIF districts within Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding for development projects within designated TIF districts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Specific designated TIF districts within Baltimore City. Current active districts include Center/West at Poppleton, Perkins Somerset Oldtown Neighborhoods, and Vacancy Reduction and Affordable Housing areas.
requirements_list: Submit a TIF bond application to the Board of Finance
Application must include details on the specific district or area covered by the TIF
Application must include estimates on future property value increases
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developers must submit a TIF bond application to the Board of Finance that includes information about the specific district or area to be covered by the TIF and estimates of future property value increases.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual city program that defers unpaid property tax liens, city fines, or citations to prevent homes from being sold at the annual Tax Sale auction in May. The program removes eligible homeowners' properties from tax sale for one year by allocating $2 million in funding. The program does not forgive unpaid bills; deferred balances remain due and may place the property at risk in future years. Each applicant's property tax lien amount is deducted from the $2 million balance. Once the funding is exhausted, the program closes for that year. Applicants must reapply each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city allocates $2 million annually. Each applicant's property tax lien amount is deducted from this balance. Once the $2 million is exhausted, the program closes. Selected homeowners have their properties removed from tax sale for that year only. The program defers unpaid property tax liens, city fines, or citations to prevent foreclosure through Tax Sale auction.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 15 – April 15 each year. The 2026 deadline has been extended to May 31.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City homeowners who have received Final Bill and Legal Notice in February, have unpaid property taxes, city fines, or citations, and meet income and residency requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Defers unpaid property tax liens, city fines, or citations to prevent property tax sale.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Property must be located and owner must reside in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Assessed value of home is $250,000 or less
Property is primary residence and homeowner has lived there at least 15 years
Must have $1,000 or more in unpaid city bills (excludes motor vehicle citations, utility bills, water bills)
Must be homeowner or co-homeowner in Baltimore City and live in the property owned

One of the following: (a) gross annual household income of $36,000 or less; OR (b) homeowner is at least 65 years old with annual income of $75,000 or less; OR (c) homeowner receives Federal Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income with annual income of $75,000 or less
Must provide photo ID and proof of address
Must provide income verification from 2025
Must receive Final Bill and Legal Notice in February
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted February 15 through April 15 each year (extended to May 31 in 2026). Applicants can apply online through the provided portal (https://bit.ly/TaxSalePrevention), submit a paper application by mail, or apply in person at the Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development, 417 E. Fayette Street, Suite 1125 (11th floor), Baltimore, MD 21202. Applicants can also contact the Tax Sale Ombudsman via email or phone. Applications are reviewed first-come, first-served. Applicants must reapply every year.

Funds can be used for down payment assistance, closing cost reduction, and renovation. Applicants must contribute at least $1,000 of their own money towards the home purchase.

structured_extraction.program_description: A city-wide initiative providing free vision screenings, eye exams, and eyeglasses to pre-kindergarten through 8th-grade students enrolled in Baltimore City Public Schools. Students who do not pass screening receive free comprehensive eye exams in a mobile vision clinic operated by Vision To Learn that visits schools. Students needing glasses receive frames and lenses manufactured by Warby Parker at no cost. All services are provided regardless of ability to pay. Medicaid may be billed if the student is enrolled.

Parent or guardian must sign a universal consent form to allow student to receive eye exam and glasses if student does not pass vision screening
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application or enrollment is required. All students in participating schools are automatically screened. Parents receive a consent form and mark yes or no for whether they want their child who fails screening to receive an exam and glasses. Students who fail screening and whose parents return a signed consent form are scheduled for eye exams in the mobile clinic. After exam, students pick up fitted glasses at their school.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that lowers your water or sewer bill if you used more water than usual because of a leak or a problem with something like a toilet or appliance. For underground leaks, you may get a discount on the sewer part of your bill if the leak is fixed by a licensed plumber and you provide proof of repair.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The bill adjustment is calculated based on your average daily water consumption. For interior or situational usage adjustments, half (50 percent) of the extra water usage is subtracted from the amount owed, except for senior or hardship customers who receive 100 percent of the extra water subtracted. For underground leak adjustments, any extra water used because of the leak is removed from your water bill and your sewer charges are updated to match the new amount. Credit applied to water and/or sewer portion of utility bill. One underground leak adjustment per property every two years. One interior/situational usage adjustment per property every three years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within sixty (60) days of the bill being issued
structured_extraction.contact_name: DPW Customer Support and Services Division

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bill adjustments for qualifying leak repairs or usage adjustments.

requirements_list: The property owner or an authorized person designated by the property owner must request the adjustment within sixty (60) days of the bill being issued
Water loss due to theft or vandalism is not covered
Customers may only be granted an underground leak adjustment at a property once every two years
Customers may only be granted an interior or situational usage adjustment at a property once every three years

Repairs must be completed prior to submitting the form
Verification that necessary repairs have been made
Leak must be documented with occurrence and repair dates
Authorization for DPW to process adjustment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete Water and Sewer Adjustment Request form with account details, leak information, and repair description; submit to DPW either online or by mail to 200 Holliday Street, First Floor, Room 8, Baltimore, MD 21202. If your request is approved, you will see the change on your bill about 4 weeks after DPW receives your form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A payment assistance program that helps Baltimore City residents, including qualifying seniors and low-income households, pay their water and wastewater bills. It calculates the maximum a household should pay for yearly water and sewer services based on a percentage of their annual income, providing a discount on water bills. Assistance rates have been increased to ensure recipients do not have to pay more as a result of rate increases.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the Water4All application online at cityservices.baltimorecity.gov/Water4All/Initial-Eligibility-Check, print out a PDF application, or call 410-396-5555 or 410-396-9500 to request an application be mailed. structured_extraction.program_description: The Youth Homelessness Demonstration Program supports communities in developing and implementing a coordinated community approach to prevent and end youth homelessness. The Diversion and Kinship Projects component specifically serves unaccompanied youth experiencing homelessness, including unaccompanied pregnant or parenting youth where no household member is older than 24. The program provides funding for projects that coordinate with existing YHDP initiatives and the Baltimore Continuum of Care. Services include outreach and coordinated access to quickly assess if youth can be diverted from shelter, short-term flexible financial assistance (up to six months), supportive services to keep youth housed or quickly re-house them, and connections to host homes established through referrals, including kinship care where youth connect to relatives or close friends (fictive kin).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Total anticipated funding available is $397,804. Grants support the development and implementation of Diversion and Kinship Projects that coordinate with current YHDP projects including Permanent Supportive Housing, Rapid Re-housing, Family-Based Setting Diversion, and Transitional Housing. Funding covers supportive services (case management, employment assistance, mental health services, life skills), housing problem-solving activities (search assistance, mediation, deposits, moving assistance), host home and kinship care connections, referrals to mainstream benefits and services, HMIS costs, staffing (FTE/PTE positions), and utility and security deposits. Short-term flexible financial assistance is available for up to six months and may include rental application fees, utility deposits, food, transportation, and childcare. A 25% match requirement (in-kind and/or external resources) is required. Services must follow Housing First approach and provide comprehensive individualized needs assessment, case management, housing support, and financial assistance.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Unaccompanied youth and young adults (ages 0-24) at-risk of or experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City, including unaccompanied pregnant or parenting youth where no household member is older than 24. Priority given to vulnerable populations including youth of color, LGBTQ+ youth, victims of sexual trafficking or exploitation, youth involved with juvenile justice, jail, or foster care systems, unaccompanied minors under 18, and immigrant and undocumented youth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supportive services including case management, conflict resolution, mediation, family-focused support, employment assistance, mental health services, life skills training, substance use treatment and behavioral health services, education, legal services, outpatient health services, and transportation; Housing problem-solving activities including search assistance, barrier removal, rental application fees, utility deposits, security deposits, moving assistance, and landlord-tenant mediation; Host homes and kinship care placement services; Referrals to education, legal services, and mainstream benefits; HMIS costs; Staffing (FTE/PTE positions); Administrative costs. Funds cannot be used for religious instruction, counseling, or proselytizing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Buy Into Bmore Fixed Pricing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A sales program for City-owned vacant buildings and lots in Baltimore City, offering simplified property transfers at fixed prices to homeowners, developers, non-profits, and community land trusts. Properties are sold at fixed prices determined by the city, ranging from $1.00 to $3,000.00 depending on property type and purchaser category. The program streamlines the disposition process while promoting transparency in pricing and can be used for restoration, new construction, rehabilitation, green space development, and side yard acquisitions. The program prioritizes Baltimore City residents planning to live in homes as primary residences during initial phases, followed by rolling availability for community land trusts, non-profits, and for-profit developers.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Properties are sold at fixed prices based on property type and purchaser category. Homeowners and community land trusts can purchase vacant buildings for $1 and vacant lots for $1. Nonprofits with 50 or fewer employees pay $1,000 for vacant buildings and $500 for vacant lots. Nonprofits with 51 or more employees and for-profit developers pay $3,000 for vacant buildings and $1,000 for vacant lots. Purchase prices range from $1.00 to $3,000.00 depending on property condition and project type. Homeowners must maintain purchased properties as primary residence for 5 years after obtaining use and occupancy permit. Applicants must provide proof of minimum $90,000 available funding for rehabilitation per property and pay a $100 application fee.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis with priority period of 90 days beginning April 1, 2024, followed by first-come-first-served. Ongoing since March 20, 2024. Phase 1 (Homeowner Priority): April 1 - June 30, 2024; Phase 2 (Charm City Roots): April 15, 2024; Phase 3 (All Fixed Pricing Applicants): July 1, 2024 onwards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents planning to live in a home as primary residence (Phase One priority); community land trusts, non-profits, and for-profit developers; individuals with familial or legacy connection to vacant properties; homeowners, nonprofits, and for-profit developers interested in purchasing vacant properties in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property purchase and rehabilitation. Properties must be developed for residential or mixed-use (including residential) purposes with use and occupancy permit obtained within 12 months of settlement. Can also be used for restoration, new construction, rehabilitation, green space development, and side yard acquisitions. Applicants must have $90,000 available for property rehabilitation per property. Maximum 12 properties per application.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Properties must fall within the E-J Housing Market Typology in Baltimore City, with exceptions for side yard use in A-J. Properties must be listed on the BuyIntoBmore site.

Pay $100 application fee (credited to settlement if approved, refunded if rejected)

Pass vetting process including: proof of funding for rehabilitation, review of vacant property ownership history, legal issue clearance, verification of no unpaid federal or state liens or court orders
Homeowners must maintain property as primary residence for minimum of 5 years after issuance of use and occupancy permit
Community land trusts must be registered Affordable Housing Land Trust registered with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Property must obtain use and occupancy permit within 12 months of settlement date
Must be interested in purchasing vacant properties through the city's disposition process
Applicants cannot have any open legal issues or federal or state liens that could prevent them from completing the project
Current with State Department of Assessments and Taxes (if applicable)
No open or pending criminal cases that would impede project completion
Executed construction contract prior to settlement
Maximum 12 properties per application
Settlement within 90 days of agreement execution
Commercial General Liability insurance minimum $1,000,000 per occurrence ($3,000,000 aggregate)
Environmental Liability insurance minimum $2,000,000
Workers' Compensation and Commercial Automobile Liability insurance required
All permits obtained within 90 days of conveyance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through the Buy Into Bmore interactive map portal or by direct submission. DHCD reviews applications and renders award or rejection decisions within two weeks of receipt. If multiple applications are submitted for the same property and all applicants pass vetting, applications are reviewed by order of submission. Applicants who fail vetting have five business days to remedy issues; if unable to remedy, the next eligible applicant is reviewed. Properties are purchased through Board of Estimates approvals after application review. Settlement must occur within 90 days of agreement execution.

structured_extraction.program_name: Blind Individual and Surviving Spouse Tax Exemption or Refund
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax relief program that exempts property from real property tax obligations for blind individuals or their surviving spouses who are Maryland residents. The exemption applies to the applicant's principal residence and exempts $15,000 of a property's assessed value from real property tax obligations. Eligible individuals must have central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the better eye with corrective glasses, or a field defect with peripheral field contracted to 20 degrees or less, with blindness certified as permanent by a licensed medical professional. Eligible individuals may also receive a refund of property taxes paid in prior years when an exemption was authorized but not granted, retroactive for up to three years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program exempts $15,000 of assessed property value from real property tax obligations. Blind individuals may also receive a refund of property taxes paid in taxable years when an exemption was authorized but not granted, with refunds available retroactively for up to three years. The exemption applies to the principal residence and applicants must meet specific medical certification standards for blindness and provide proof of Maryland residency and property ownership.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides financial stipends through the National Family Caregivers Support Program to support caregivers. Stipends vary yearly and can be used for respite care (funding for someone to stay at home or at a nursing home for a night or two) or medical supplies such as incontinence supplies not covered under Medicare. The stipend is non-emergency, non-expedited support available once per year for up to five years with a maximum of one stipend per household for one care recipient. The program also provides educational outreach events, webinars through Trualta website, a community resource guide, quarterly newsletters, individual caregiver consultations, and referrals to disease-specific and general support groups.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit that exempts owners of conservation land from Baltimore County real property taxes. The credit covers 100 percent of annual Baltimore County property tax obligations for five years. Conservation land includes real property subject to a perpetual conservation easement donated to a land trust on or after July 1, 1991, or real property owned in fee by a qualified land trust and acquired on or after July 1, 1991. The program aims to preserve natural areas, provide environmental education, and promote conservation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit equal to the total tax assessment on the property for a five fiscal year period. The credit exempts 100 percent of the annual Baltimore County real property tax obligation for five years for properties meeting eligibility criteria. If the property is transferred to an entity other than a government agency or another qualified land trust, the credit lapses and the property owner becomes liable for all property taxes that would have been owed, plus interest.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners of conservation land in Baltimore County; qualified land trusts under § 170(h)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code that have executed a cooperative agreement with the Maryland Environmental Trust
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief for conservation land; the credit reduces or eliminates Baltimore County real property tax obligations for properties designated as conservation land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland only. Credit applies only to Baltimore County real property tax obligations.
requirements_list: Real property must be subject to a perpetual conservation easement donated to or acquired by a land trust after July 1, 1991
Land trust must own property in fee
Easement must be with qualified organization under IRC § 170(h)(3)
Land trust must have executed cooperative agreement with Maryland Environmental Trust

Property must serve an environmental use including preservation of natural area, environmental education, promotion of conservation, community parks, conservation and use of agricultural land, maintenance of natural area for public use, or wildlife sanctuary
Application must be submitted no later than June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application form with property and owner information and indicate environmental use of land trust property. Submit supporting documents evidencing that the property meets the conservation land definition. Submit completed application to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204, no later than June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought. Application will be reviewed and approved or denied by the Director of the Office of Budget and Finance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Veteran and Surviving Spouse Property Tax Exemption or Refund
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides property tax exemption or refund for disabled veterans with 100% permanent and total or 100% permanently unemployable service-connected disability ratings, and surviving spouses of eligible disabled veterans. The program exempts eligible properties from all Maryland real property tax obligations and may provide refunds of taxes paid for up to three years prior to receiving the exemption.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides exemption from property taxes on eligible residential property for qualifying disabled veterans and surviving spouses. Eligible individuals may also receive a refund of property taxes paid for up to three years before the exemption takes effect under Tax Property Article 7-208.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans with 100% permanent and total or 100% permanently unemployable service-connected disability rating, and surviving spouses of eligible disabled veterans who are Maryland residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption or refund on residential property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. Applicants must be Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a disabled veteran or surviving spouse of a disabled veteran
Must have 100% permanent and total or 100% permanently unemployable service-connected disability rating
Must own residential property in Maryland
Must provide Honorable Discharge or DD-Form 214 (copy)
Must provide VA rating notification showing 100% permanent and total disability OR 100% permanently unemployable rating
Must provide disability rating effective date and VA decision date documentation
Must be a Maryland resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply for an exemption, obtain an application form from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and file it with that agency. To apply for a refund, first file for and receive an exemption from SDAT. Then submit a copy of the approved exemption to the appropriate county council or equivalent governing body along with a letter requesting the refund.

structured_extraction.program_description: A congregate meal program that provides nutritious meals and social companionship to Baltimore County seniors aged 60 and over and their spouses of any age. Meals are served at multiple senior centers and nutrition sites throughout the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive nutritious meals at participating senior centers and nutrition sites. Meals are planned as the main meal of the day and contain three ounces of protein, two servings of starch or grains, three servings of vegetables and fruits, and one serving of low-fat milk. Meals provide at least one-third of recommended daily nutritional needs. Participants are asked to make a voluntary contribution of at least $4 for regular meals ($5 for Kosher and Halal). Full meal costs are $6.20 for regular meals, $6.94 for box meals, and $8.19 for super special meals (Kosher meals cost $8.45 to $12.68). Participants under 60 must pay the full meal cost. Reservations are required two to five days in advance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County seniors aged 60 and over and their spouses of any age
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nutritious meals served at senior centers and community nutrition sites
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Baltimore County resident. Meals are served at senior centers and nutrition sites throughout Baltimore County including Essex Co-Op, Center Place, Village Oaks, Tabco Towers, Trinity House, Weinberg House, Reister's View, St. Elizabeth's, Weinberg Gardens, St. Luke's Place, Golden Ring Co-Op, Weinberg Village I, Park View at Towson, Park View at Dundalk, Park View at Catonsville, and Islamic Society of Baltimore.
requirements_list: Age 60 and over
Baltimore County resident
Spouse of participant (any age)
Reservations required two to five days in advance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants visit a meal site and make reservations. Reservations are made at the meal site directly. Participants under 60 pay full cost; those 60 and over are asked for a voluntary contribution starting at $4.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for single and multi-family residential property owners in Baltimore County who install solar or geothermal devices that meet national safety and performance standards to heat, cool, supply electricity, or provide hot water for use in residential structures. The credit equals 50 percent of the eligible cost or $5,000 whichever is less for heating, electricity generation, or cooling systems, or $1,500 for hot water supply systems. Eligible costs must be incurred within 12 months before initial application. Credits cannot exceed county property taxes owed in any year; excess credits carry forward up to two additional years. Due to a $1.5 million annual budgetary limitation, a waiting list is in effect where approved applications are processed in the order received.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit is 50 percent of the eligible cost or $5,000, whichever is less, or $1,500 for a hot water supply system. Eligible costs include expenses incurred within 12 months before the initial application, including parts, components, accessories, and reasonable installation costs. The credit applies only to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation. A credit claimed during a tax year may not exceed the amount of property taxes owed that year, and excess amounts may be carried forward for up to two additional tax years. Due to a $1.5 million annual budgetary limitation, a waiting list is in effect where approved applications are processed in the order received.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 of the year immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Baltimore County who have installed or are planning to install solar or geothermal energy devices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation costs for solar energy devices or geothermal energy devices, including component parts, accessories, and reasonable installation labor costs. The credit applies to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland

Solar or geothermal device must meet national safety and performance standards set by nationally recognized testing laboratory
Device cannot be a household appliance
Detailed receipts listing amounts and dates of payment must be submitted

Permit Number for electrical inspection completed by Baltimore County Electrical Inspection Office must be provided

Credit does not transfer with property and terminates upon change of ownership

Provide evidence of national safety and performance standards compliance. Applicant must provide Permit Number for electrical inspection completed by Baltimore County Electrical Inspection Office. Submit application online using a valid email address, or apply by mail or in person by submitting the application form and supporting documentation to the Director of Office of Budget and Finance at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204. Application will be reviewed by Director of Office of Budget and Finance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enterprise Zone Employment and Real Property Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credit program designed to retain existing companies, spur expansions, promote development of vacant or underutilized properties, encourage job creation, and revitalize older office and industrial areas. A tax credit program for businesses located in Baltimore County's three designated Enterprise Zones (Chesapeake, Southwest, and Federal Center at Woodlawn) that expand operations, add employees, or make capital improvements. The program provides both County and Maryland tax credits to encourage redevelopment in distressed areas. Three types of assistance are available: (1) Real property tax credit offering 80% of increased property tax for the first 5 years, declining 10% annually for the remaining 5 years; (2) Employment credit allowing up to $1,000 per new full-time employee, up to $3,000 for disadvantaged workers, with additional credits up to $2,000 and $1,000 in years 2-3; and (3) BGE Rider 7 electricity price reduction program for qualifying businesses. The program has historically spurred 160 business expansions or relocations, resulting in over $300 million in real property improvements, $270 million in machinery and equipment investments, and 3,000 new jobs created.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three types of assistance available: (1) Real property tax credit offering 80% of increased property tax for the first 5 years, declining 10% annually for the remaining 5 years after major capital improvements are made; (2) Employment credit allowing up to $1,000 per new full-time employee hired in the Enterprise Zone, up to $3,000 for disadvantaged workers, with additional credits up to $2,000 and $1,000 in years 2-3; and (3) BGE Rider 7 electricity price reduction program for businesses with 200kW+ electricity load increases and 10+ new full-time employees. Businesses that expand or add employees within the three Enterprise Zones—Chesapeake, Southwest, or Federal Center at Woodlawn—are eligible for both County and Maryland tax credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 31 (to receive property tax credit on next July 1 tax bill)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses making new investments in real property or hiring new employees in Baltimore County's designated Enterprise Zones, including those considering relocation or expansion, property developers, and property owners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New investments in real property including new construction, rehabilitation, machinery and equipment costs, land and building acquisition; new employee hiring.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only properties located within one of Baltimore County's three designated Enterprise Zones are eligible: Chesapeake Zone (designated June 15, 2015), Southwest Enterprise Zone (designated December 1996), or Federal Center at Woodlawn (designated June 2011). Applicants can use the My Neighborhood Interactive Map to determine if a property is within an Enterprise Zone.
requirements_list: Business must be located within one of the three designated Enterprise Zones in Baltimore County (Chesapeake, Southwest, or Federal Center at Woodlawn)
Business must make new investment in real property in the zone OR hire new employees in the zone
For real property credit: major capital improvements must be made; application must be submitted before project completion and User/Occupancy Permits issuance
For employment credit: must hire qualified new full-time employees meeting Maryland Department of Commerce criteria
Property owner concurrence required if developer applies on behalf of owner
Must submit completed eligibility application to Baltimore County
Retail businesses are explicitly excluded
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Verify the eligibility of an address using the My Neighborhood Interactive Map or contact the Enterprise Zone Coordinator. Download detailed maps of specific enterprise zones and the eligibility application form. Complete the application form with Sections A and B (required for all applicants); include Section C for property tax credit applicants and Section D for employment tax credit applicants. Send the completed application to the Enterprise Zone Coordinator at the Baltimore County Department of Economic Development, Historic Courthouse Suite 100, 400 Washington Avenue, Towson, Maryland 21204. You can also contact them by phone at 410-887-8030, fax at 410-887-8017, or email at businesshelp@baltimorecountymd.gov. Upon approval, receive certification letter indicating eligible tax credits.

Services are free to both employers and participants.

Once accepted, participants meet weekly with employment coordinators who evaluate their readiness and develop a job search strategy. Coordinators provide referrals to entry-level positions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program for residential property taxpayers who have experienced temporary financial hardship and need extra time to pay their property taxes. Eligible applicants can spread their tax payments over time based on their repayment ability and financial situation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program allows residential taxpayers experiencing temporary financial hardship to make installment payments on their property tax liability over time rather than paying in full by the deadline. Eligibility is based on demonstrated hardship, repayment ability, and financial disclosure. Once approved, eligibility applies only to the fiscal tax year in which the application is made. All future taxes must remain current to maintain ongoing eligibility. Applications must be filed by the end of February to avoid property sale at the annual tax sale in June.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for commercial buildings that achieve at least a silver rating under the LEED Green Building rating system or the NGBS (American National Standards Institute's National Green Building Standard) rating system. For LEED-certified buildings, the credit ranges from 10 to 80 percent of the real property tax obligation depending on the rating level (silver, gold, or platinum) and building category (new construction, core and shell, or existing buildings), with credit duration of 3 to 5 years. For NGBS-rated buildings, the credit ranges from 50 to 80 percent depending on the rating level (silver, gold, or emerald), with a duration of five consecutive years. The credit applies to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation only.

list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

LEED-NC: 40% (Silver), 60% (Gold), 80% (Platinum). LEED-CS: 40% (Silver), 50% (Gold), 70% (Platinum). LEED-EB: 10% (Silver), 25% (Gold), 50% (Platinum). NGBS: 50% (Silver), 60% (Gold), 80% (Emerald). Credit duration is 3 to 5 years for LEED and 5 years for NGBS.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for residential properties that achieve high energy efficiency standards. The credit reduces Baltimore County real property tax obligations based on the percentage of energy efficiency achieved. The credit applies to new construction and renovated residential structures that meet specific energy efficiency ratings including LEED certification, National Green Building Standard certification, or HERS Index ratings. Tax reduction is calculated as a percentage decrease from the Baltimore County real property tax obligation equal to the percentage of energy efficiency achieved in the home. For LEED-certified homes: LEED Silver provides 40 percent property tax reduction, LEED Gold provides 60 percent reduction, LEED Platinum provides 100 percent reduction. For National Green Building Standard: NGBS Silver provides 40 percent reduction, NGBS Gold provides 60 percent reduction, NGBS Emerald provides 100 percent reduction. For HERS Index rated homes, the tax reduction percentage corresponds to the energy efficiency percentage achieved. The credit runs for three consecutive years beginning with the first year it is awarded and continues with the property upon change of ownership. A 5-year credit is available if the project is carbon neutral.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit that reduces Baltimore County real property tax obligations by a percentage equal to the energy efficiency achieved. For LEED-certified homes: LEED Silver provides 40 percent property tax reduction, LEED Gold provides 60 percent reduction, LEED Platinum provides 100 percent reduction. For National Green Building Standard: NGBS Silver provides 40 percent reduction, NGBS Gold provides 60 percent reduction, NGBS Emerald provides 100 percent reduction. For HERS Index rated homes, the tax reduction percentage corresponds to the energy efficiency percentage achieved. Other charges or fees are not included in the calculation. The credit runs for three consecutive years beginning with the first year it is awarded and continues with the property upon change of ownership. A 5-year credit is available if the project is carbon neutral.
