structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit is provided to homeowners whose property taxes (based on no more than $300,000 of assessment) exceed a specified tax limit tied to household income. The credit reduces the homeowner's property tax liability. The exact credit amount is determined by comparing the homeowner's household income and property tax burden against eligibility thresholds shown in the income-to-tax-limit table.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Baltimore County who own their principal residence and meet income and net worth requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces property tax liability on the homeowner's principal residence. Property taxes eligible for this credit do not include metropolitan charges, buildings or portions used for business purposes, taxes for excess land acreage, or other buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Net worth (excluding the principal residence and certain retirement accounts) cannot exceed $200,000.
Combined household income cannot exceed $60,000.
The property must be the homeowner's principal residence.
Property assessment must not exceed $300,000.
Property taxes must exceed the tax limit amount specified in the eligibility table for the homeowner's income level.
A new application must be filed every year to be considered for the credit.
Homeowners age 70 or older may qualify for an additional credit.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). The same application serves for both the state and Baltimore County programs. Applications are available from SDAT. A new application must be filed every year. Contact SDAT at 410-767-4433 for application forms and more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal rental assistance program that provides subsidies to help low-income, very low-income, and extremely low-income families afford housing. Participants receive vouchers they can use to search for and lease rental housing in the private market that meets program standards. The program promotes freedom of choice in housing and supports economic self-sufficiency. The program also covers multiple special housing types including SRO, congregate housing, group homes, shared housing, cooperative housing, manufactured homes, and homeownership options for eligible families. The program includes Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) protections for survivors of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, stalking, and human trafficking, with emergency transfer provisions available for safety reasons. Additionally, the program includes a Project-Based Voucher (PBV) component that allows vouchers to be attached to specific housing units in projects rather than remaining portable to families, covering existing housing, newly constructed housing, and rehabilitated housing. Includes special purpose vouchers such as Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH), Family Unification Program (FUP), Foster Youth Initiative (FYI), Mainstream, and Non-Elderly Disabled (NED) vouchers. Also includes the Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) Project-Based Voucher program converting public housing to long-term project-based Section 8 rental assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental subsidies are provided directly to landlords on behalf of eligible families through monthly Housing Assistance Payments (HAP). The maximum subsidy is determined by HUD-established fair market rents and payment standards set for Baltimore County, which must fall within 90-110% of HUD-published Fair Market Rents (FMRs), with reasonable accommodations for families with disabilities permitting up to 120% of FMR. Payment standards for FY 2026 range from $1,498 (efficiency) to $3,733 (6 bedroom). The rent must be reasonable compared to other rents in the neighborhood and the unit must meet housing quality standards or NSPIRE standards. Monthly HAP is calculated as the lower of: (1) applicable payment standard minus family's total tenant payment, or (2) gross rent minus family's total tenant payment. Utility allowances and disability-related deductions are included in subsidy calculations. For homeownership assistance, monthly payments cover mortgage principal and interest, real estate taxes, public assessments, mortgage insurance premiums, home insurance, utility allowance, maintenance expenses, and major repairs and replacements. Includes special vouchers such as Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH), Family Unification Program (FUP), Foster Youth Initiative (FYI), and Mainstream vouchers. Project-Based Voucher (PBV) component provides housing assistance payments to property owners for eligible families leasing PBV units in specific projects, with at least 75% of admissions required to be extremely low-income families. Vacancy payments available for up to two months following tenant move-out on a case-by-case basis. Utility reimbursements paid to families when utility allowance exceeds total tenant payment. Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) PBV provides long-term, project-based Section 8 Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) contracts for converted public housing and assisted properties, preserving and improving assisted housing and attracting private market capital for property renovations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No waiting lists are currently open; extension requests must be received at least 7 calendar days before voucher expiration; 15 business days for VAWA claims notification; Applicants denied assistance may request informal review within 15 business days; Informal hearing requests must be submitted in writing within 15 business days of BCOH decision; VAWA documentation must be provided within 14-15 business days of written request; Project-Based Voucher submission deadlines vary by RFP cycle; postmarks not acceptable, date and time stamp upon receipt
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and individuals whose incomes are below set income limits (30%, 50%, or 80% Area Median Family Income); very low-income families; extremely low-income families; homeless individuals; disabled individuals; veterans; special-needs families; single persons; elderly persons; displaced persons; near-elderly persons; youth aging out of foster care; survivors of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, stalking, or human trafficking; persons with disabilities; foster youth aged 18-24. Priority is given to families with the earliest application date and time. Local preferences apply for families with Baltimore County residency or employment. Program also serves VASH (Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing) families, Family Unification Program (FUP) families, Foster Youth Initiative (FYI) families, and Mainstream families. Eligible homeownership participants include first-time homebuyers and families with disabilities seeking accessibility modifications. Project-Based Voucher program serves low-income families, elderly households, persons with disabilities, families needing supportive services, and families with persons with limited English proficiency. Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) PBV serves existing public housing residents, moderate rehabilitation property residents, rent supplement and rental assistance payment program participants, and extremely low-income families (at least 75% of admissions). Family Unification Program (FUP) serves families at risk of child placement or with children in out-of-home care, and FUP youth ages 18-24 who have left or will leave foster care within 90 days. Foster Youth Initiative (FYI) serves youth ages 18-24 with prior foster care involvement who are homeless or at-risk-of-homelessness, including pregnant and/or parenting youth. Special purpose vouchers also serve non-elderly persons with disabilities (Mainstream and NED).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance for housing that meets program standards. Funds cover the difference between the family's contribution and the approved rent amount up to the payment standard. Includes support for Family Self-Sufficiency program services, housing mobility programs, homeownership program support, and new construction and/or extensive rehabilitation through Project-Based Vouchers. Utility allowances, disability-related expenses (attendant care, auxiliary apparatus, service animals), medical expenses (for elderly or disabled households), and childcare expenses enabling work or education may be deducted from family income calculations. For homeownership assistance: mortgage principal and interest payments, real estate taxes and public assessments, home insurance premiums, utility costs, maintenance expenses and major repairs, mortgage insurance premiums, condominium or cooperative fees, and accessibility modifications for persons with disabilities. Down payment and closing costs may include FSS escrow account funds. Administrative expenses for program operation. Security deposit assistance. Landlord recruitment and incentive payments. Unit modifications for accessibility. Monthly rental subsidy payments to landlords. Utility allowances for tenant-paid utilities, appliances, and housing services (space heating, air conditioning, cooking, water heating, water, sewer, trash collection, other electric, appliances). Project-Based Voucher relocation assistance (from owner funds, local public funds, or other sources; PHA may use administrative fee reserve after other expenses satisfied); relocation assistance up to two months withheld/abated payments for security deposits, temporary housing, and moving costs. RAD PBV relocation assistance including security deposit assistance for families relocating to new units and moving cost support. Supportive services for special purpose vouchers including VASH case management and clinical services, FUP youth supportive services (life skills, job preparation, educational advancement counseling), and FYI youth supportive services (money management, credit use, housekeeping, nutrition, health care access, job preparation, educational and career advancement counseling).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland. Policy encourages participation by owners of suitable units located outside areas of low-income or minority concentration. Portability procedures available for families moving outside PHA jurisdiction. Portable vouchers can be used in other PHA jurisdictions nationwide. Specific census tracts identified as areas of poverty and minority concentration are subject to outreach prioritization. Homeownership assistance available within Baltimore County jurisdiction. Area-wide utility allowance schedules maintained by locality. For Project-Based Vouchers: Projects in areas where vouchers are difficult to use (poverty rate ≥20%, rental vacancy <4%, or where 90% of Small Area FMR exceeds 110% of metro/county FMR). Sites must meet deconcentration of poverty standards. Census tracts with poverty concentrations of 20% or less preferred. Exceptions granted for enterprise zones, renewal communities, areas undergoing revitalization. RAD PBV projects subject to site selection standards and civil rights review. Families with VASH vouchers may use within jurisdictions accessible to case management services and have portability allowed within and outside initial catchment area with approval.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested families apply via the Applicant Portal at https://baltimorecounty.myhousing.com. Head of household or designee submits one- or two-step application with basic eligibility information. Families are placed on the waiting list and selected based on application date/time and documented local preferences (Baltimore County residency or employment). When selected from waiting list, families provide complete application information and undergo eligibility interview with required documentation. Income and citizenship status verified through third-party sources and EIV system. USCIS secondary verification of immigration status conducted. Upon eligibility determination, families receive written notification. Eligible families attend mandatory briefing (in-person, group, or remote options available) and receive briefing packet before voucher issuance. Families receive rental subsidy voucher (Form HUD-52646) specifying unit size and issuance/expiration dates. Vouchers allow initial 60-day search period with up to two 30-day extensions available (extension requests must be submitted at least 7 days before expiration). Families must find a rental unit meeting program standards and securing landlord participation. Family and owner submit completed Request for Tenancy Approval (Form HUD-52517) and proposed lease with all required documentation. PHA conducts housing quality inspection within 15 business days and verifies rent reasonableness using commercially available rent reasonableness systems (AffordableHousing.com and other platforms); owner has 5 business days to submit additional comparable unit information if needed. Rent increase requests require 15 business days for determination. PHA approves lease and begins providing subsidy through HAP to landlord. Families may use online portal or submit requests for family composition changes or portability. For portability, participants may request to transfer voucher to another housing authority's jurisdiction outside Baltimore County. Initial PHA contacts receiving PHA to confirm administration or absorption of voucher. Landlords can register for online portal at https://baltimorecounty.myhousing.com/Account/Login to review HAP, tenant information, and inspections. Landlords may submit rent increase requests (no earlier than 150 days or no later than 120 days prior to HAP contract anniversary) for rent comparability review, with increases capped at 7% of current contract rent. Annual and interim reexaminations required to verify continued eligibility and adjust subsidy amounts. BCOH begins reexamination process 120 days in advance of effective date, conducted by mail or housing portal; in-person upon request or as reasonable accommodation. Families must provide updated information and supporting documentation; missing documentation must be provided within 15 business days or non-compliance results in termination notice. Form HUD-50058 required for reporting changes. VAWA emergency transfer procedures: Notify BCOH Integrity Unit via email (vawa@baltimorecountymd.gov) or phone (410-887-2866) to request emergency transfer. BCOH acts quickly to assist tenants who qualify for emergency transfers to safe units. If no safe units available within BCOH inventory, assistance provided in identifying other covered housing providers. Expedited voucher issuance generally within 5 business days. Internal and external transfer options available. Assistance provided in identifying alternative housing and local victim support organizations. Tenant may decline units deemed unsafe. Applicants denied assistance may request informal review within 15 business days. Participants may request informal hearing for determinations regarding income within 15 business days of BCOH decision. Families must request informal hearings in writing. Families must provide relevant documents at least 24 hours before hearing. Families may be represented by counsel at own expense. All participants must comply with hearing procedures and professional conduct guidelines. Informal hearing conducted by approved officer; written decision issued within 10 business days. For Project-Based Vouchers: Applicants can be placed on separate waiting lists for specific PBV projects or use central waiting lists. Owner-maintained waiting lists permitted. In-place families receive absolute selection preference. Eligibility determined within 60 days before commencement. Owner conducts tenant screening based on specified factors. PHA or owner places applicant on project waiting list. PHA determines final program eligibility. PHA provides notice of approval/denial to applicant and owner. For RAD PBV: Applications follow standard HCV process with RAD-specific requirements. In-place residents at converting properties receive absolute selection preference. Right-to-return provisions apply for temporarily or permanently relocated residents. For FUP and FYI: PCWA (Public Child Welfare Agency) certifies eligible families and youth. PHA processes applications following standard HCV procedures. For VASH: VAMC (VA Medical Center) or DSP (Department of Social Services) screens homeless veterans and refers eligible families to PHA. Initial voucher search term is 120 calendar days. For Mainstream and NED: Applications submitted through standard HCV process. Special eligibility screening for disability status conducted. For SVP (Maryland Statewide Voucher Program): Applicants selected from existing HCV waiting list. Automatically restored to HCV waiting list six months before SVP voucher expiration.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides transportation services for Medical Assistance (Medicaid) recipients in Baltimore County and statewide who need to access medically necessary medical services. Offers multiple transportation modes based on clinical necessity including ambulatory/paratransit, wheelchair van, sedan/cab, or ambulance (BLS, ALS, or specialized care levels). Services include transportation to medical appointments, treatments, and facility transfers/discharges for eligible recipients with no other means of transportation available. Transportation is provided using the least expensive method suitable to the recipient's needs. Regular service operates Monday through Saturday from 5 a.m. to 8 p.m., with emergency medical facility discharges and transfers available 24/7.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free shared-ride transportation services to and from medically necessary medical appointments and medical facility discharges or transfers. Transportation modes include paratransit vehicle, public transit system, cab/sedan, wheelchair van, or ambulance (BLS, ALS, SCT/P, SCT/N, or Neo-natal) based on clinical assessment and medical necessity. Regular service operates Monday through Saturday from 5 a.m. to 8 p.m., with emergency medical facility discharges and transfers available 24/7. Rides must be scheduled 1 to 7 days in advance with at least 24 hours' notice; same-day transportation is not provided except under extreme circumstances. The Maryland Medical Assistance Program covers all costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County and Maryland statewide residents with eligible Medical Assistance (Medicaid) who have no other means of transportation available to access medically necessary services. Includes Medical Assistance eligible participants requiring transportation for medical treatment, Medicare recipients, and other insured individuals for out-of-area services, as well as patients being discharged or transferred from medical facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to and from medically necessary medical appointments, medical facility discharges, transfers, and out-of-area medical providers when services are unavailable locally or medically necessary at a distant facility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County and Maryland statewide. Baltimore County residents receive priority for in-area services. Local Health Department MA Transportation Units handle requests. Service is a safety net program available only to eligible recipients with no other means of transportation.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County or Maryland resident with active and eligible Medical Assistance
Must have a valid 11-digit Medical Assistance number or Social Security number
Must have underlying medical diagnosis requiring transportation
Must have no other means of transportation available; screening is performed initially and quarterly to confirm no other transportation resources are available

Must obtain medical certification from physician, PA, CRNP, or dentist on a Maryland Statewide Medical Assistance Transportation Certification Form or Baltimore County Certificate for Medical Transportation form stating the patient cannot use public transportation due to a specific medical condition
Medical certification must be renewed at least annually (form valid for one year from certification date)
Must pre-schedule all transportation requests 1 to 7 days in advance with at least 24 hours' notice
Must be ready and waiting at the designated pickup location at the assigned ready time
Failure to cancel at least 30 minutes before scheduled pickup time counts as a no-show; multiple no-shows can result in advance confirmation requirements or suspension
For wheelchair and stretcher transports with Hart to Heart, diagnosis must support medical necessity of the mode of transport
For TransDev ambulatory service, physician must certify inability to use public or ADA transportation
For ambulance transport: patient must be bed-confined OR require continuous monitoring/medical interventions
Clients using Mobility program may not use Medical Assistance Transportation except under extreme circumstances
Proper conduct required; conduct jeopardizing safety of passengers or driver can result in suspension
For stretcher transports to doctor's offices, medical facility must verify accommodation prior to scheduling
For out-of-area services: services must be unavailable at closer facility; priority given to closest appropriate provider, not necessarily patient's preferred provider
For facility discharges/transfers: facility must complete transfer/discharge form with provider certification from Physician, PA, CRNP, Discharge Nurse, or Social Worker
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain a Maryland Statewide Medical Assistance Transportation Certification Form or Baltimore County Certificate for Medical Transportation form, or for transfers/discharges, a Maryland Statewide Medical Assistance Transportation Transfer/Discharge Form. 2. Have your physician, PA, CRNP, dentist, discharge nurse, or social worker complete and certify medical necessity, including determination of appropriate transportation mode based on clinical assessment. 3. Submit the completed certification form to the Baltimore County Department of Health or local Health Department MA Transportation Unit. 4. Once approved by the Health Department, contact the appropriate transportation vendor to schedule rides. For Hart to Heart wheelchair and ambulance transports, call the County at 410-887-2828 to schedule. For TransDev ambulatory service, call TransDev directly at 410-783-2465. 5. Schedule rides 1 to 7 days in advance, providing required information including recipient details, underlying medical diagnosis, Medical Assistance number, pickup and destination addresses with specific building/room numbers, physician name, appointment time, and transport type needed. 6. Be ready for pickup at your assigned ready time (90 minutes before appointment for TransDev; 1 hour for Hart to Heart). 7. After your appointment, be at the designated return pickup location at the scheduled return time.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Historical Restorations and Rehabilitations
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that encourages owners of historic properties in Baltimore County to restore and rehabilitate their properties. Residential owner-occupied dwellings receive a 20 percent county property tax credit for eligible rehabilitation work, which can be extended for up to 10 years. Commercial properties receive a 10-year tax freeze when rehabilitation work results in an increased assessment.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential owner-occupied dwellings qualify for a 20 percent county property tax credit for eligible rehabilitation work, extendable for up to 10 years. Eligible rehabilitation work includes exterior repairs such as roof repair, window repair or replacement, painting, stucco work, and interior work such as painting, upgrading electrical and plumbing systems, heating and air conditioning. The total cost of rehabilitation work must exceed $1,000 and must conform to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards. For commercial properties, a 10-year tax freeze is provided when rehabilitation work results in an increased assessment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties in Baltimore County, including residential owner-occupied dwellings and commercial income-producing properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration and rehabilitation work on historic properties, including exterior repairs (roof repair, window repair or replacement, painting, stucco work) and interior work (painting, upgrading electrical and plumbing systems, heating and air conditioning).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland. Properties must be designated as historic, either as a contributing structure in a County Historic District, a contributing structure in a National Register Historic District, or individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places or on the Final Landmarks List.

Property must be either a contributing structure in a County Historic District, a contributing structure in a National Register Historic District, or individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places or on the Final Landmarks List

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available to owners who make qualified improvements to mobile home parks, senior housing developments, or commercially zoned properties located in designated commercial revitalization districts in Baltimore County. The credit reduces County real property tax obligations based on the value and location of improvements. Tax credits equal 100 percent of the increase in County taxes for senior housing in revitalization districts, 50 percent for senior housing outside districts, 100 percent of County property taxes for other commercial property in designated districts, and 100 percent of the tax increase for mobile home parks. Credits run for five years, or ten years if improvements exceed $10 million.

Credits run for five years, or ten years if improvements exceed $10 million. Qualified improvements must have a full cash value of $100,000 or more. The credit reduces the Baltimore County real property tax obligation for the improved property.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free reforestation program that converts lawn or grass areas to forest by planting approximately 200 native trees per acre on private land in Baltimore County. The program provides tree planting services to landowners with at least one acre of open space available for reforestation. Services include site preparation, tree planting in staggered rows, deer protection shelters and stakes, and three years of maintenance with a 90 percent tree survival warranty. The program provides native canopy, midstory, and understory trees selected from species native to the Piedmont and Coastal Plain regions of Maryland. The program is part of the Phase II Chesapeake Bay Watershed Implementation Plan.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free reforestation services at no cost to the landowner. The County plants approximately 200 native trees per acre on qualifying properties, selected from native canopy, midstory, and understory species found in Maryland's Piedmont and Coastal Plain regions. Typical reforestation composition includes 80%-90% canopy and midstory trees with 10%-20% understory trees. Trees are spaced 15 feet apart in staggered rows and equipped with stakes and shelters for deer and pest protection. Services include a site visit and consultation, development of a planting plan, site preparation, installation of trees and deer protection shelters, and three years of maintenance and monitoring including seasonal mowing, vine and invasive species management, shelter upkeep, and yearly inspections. Trees are warranted to have at least 90 percent survival rate each year for three years. Final species selection is determined by Forest Management staff and is subject to local nursery availability, though other native trees may be considered upon request.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County landowners and residents with at least one acre of open space (lawn or grass) available for reforestation, away from utility easements, Forest Conservation Easements, septic systems and septic reserves.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reforestation of open space on residential and other properties in Baltimore County to reduce stormwater runoff and support watershed improvement through native tree species acquisition and planting. Funds cover site preparation, tree planting, deer protection measures, and three-year maintenance and establishment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland, specifically rural areas within the Piedmont and Coastal Plain regions. Properties must have one acre or more of open lawn or grass space away from utility easements, Forest Conservation Easements, septic systems, and septic reserves.
requirements_list: Landowner must have at least one acre or more of open space available for reforestation
Property must be in Baltimore County
Landowner or group of landowners must own the property
Open space must be lawn or grass
Open space must be away from utility easements
Open space must be away from Forest Conservation Easements
Open space must be away from septic systems and septic reserves
Final species selection determined by Forest Management staff
Subject to local nursery availability of tree species
Other native trees may be considered upon request
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Reforestation Property Form with information about your property and the area to be reforested to the Forest Sustainability Program. EPS staff will review your submission and contact you to schedule a site visit. If you qualify, staff will meet with you on your property to discuss planting details, prepare a planting plan, and coordinate with contractors to complete the reforestation project. Forest Management will determine final tree species selection. Property owners will be responsible for maintaining the trees and reporting their survival to EPS.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free program that provides spaying, neutering, vaccinations, and other veterinary services for community cats living outdoors in Baltimore County. The program aims to humanely reduce the unowned cat population by preventing breeding, improving cat health and quality of life, and reducing nuisance behaviors. The program also provides trap loans, registration as a Feral Cat Caregiver, and support for managing community cat colonies. Participants register to be considered in good standing with Baltimore County Animal Services' TNR Program as required by Baltimore County Code Section 12-1-115.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free spay or neuter surgery, rabies vaccine, FVRCP vaccine, left ear-tipping, abdominal tattoo, microchipping, flea treatment, and veterinary exam while sedated. There is no cost to participants for the surgical package. Trap loans are also available free of charge to eligible participants for one month at a time. Equipment includes humane traps ($90 replacement value) and dividers ($25 replacement value). Registration as a Feral Cat Caregiver provides legal protection and authorization to maintain and care for community cat colonies with food, water, shelter, and sustenance. Mediation program referrals and humane trapping instructions are also provided. Health summaries and rabies vaccine certificates are provided at pick-up. Post-operative care and evaluation by veterinarian is included before release.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual residents of Baltimore County who care for or wish to humanely manage community cats living outdoors, including caregivers, trappers, transporters, and community members managing community cat colonies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are provided to cover the cost of spaying or neutering surgery, vaccinations (rabies and FVRCP), microchipping, ear-tipping, tattoos, flea treatment, and veterinary examination for unowned community cats. Equipment loans for traps and dividers are available to assist with humane trapping.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available in Baltimore County, Maryland. Cats must be living outdoors at an address within Baltimore County to be eligible. Property owner permission is required before trapping if the participant is not the property owner. Cats must be returned to the same location where they were found or an approved alternative location.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tree planting program that provides landscape-style tree plantings and larger shade trees for managed grounds such as homeowners associations, apartment complexes, and businesses to maintain and increase tree canopy in densely populated urban areas. Urban tree plantings come with an initial one year of maintenance and 100 percent survival guarantee, including watering, pruning, and shelter upkeep. EPS conducts two inspections during the initial maintenance period and continues to monitor plantings for at least 10 years.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Association Restoration, Planning and Implementation Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore County Department of Environmental Protection and Sustainability awards annual grants to locally-based watershed associations and nonprofit organizations to identify and implement restoration projects and educational activities that help meet water quality requirements and support the health of local watersheds and the Chesapeake Bay. Grant funding of up to $30,000 is available (in some cases, grants exceeding $30,000 may be awarded to established organizations with exemplary track records). Activities span multiple watersheds including Back River, Deer Creek, Gwynns Falls, Jones Falls, Baltimore Harbor, Liberty Reservoir, Lower and Little Gunpowder Falls, Tidal Gunpowder/Middle River/Bird River, Loch Raven Reservoir, Patapsco River, and Prettyboy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding of up to $30,000 is available (in some cases, grants exceeding $30,000 may be awarded to established organizations with exemplary track records). Funds cover staff salaries and hours dedicated to environmental restoration activities and public awareness. Fringe benefits up to 30 percent of salary and indirect costs up to 10 percent of combined salary and fringe may be included. Materials and equipment are not funded. The grant term runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, February 6, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Locally-based watershed associations and community groups with active membership in Baltimore County that are registered as 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), or 501(c)(6) nonprofit organizations in good standing with the State of Maryland and have a demonstrated history of successfully conducting resident-based and community restoration projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff salaries and hours for conducting restoration planning and implementation, watershed education and outreach. Eligible activities include tree plantings and maintenance, stormwater best management practices (BMPs) design and maintenance, downspout disconnections, rain gardens, rain barrels, stream cleanups, Stream Watch programs, conservation landscapes, invasive plant removal, and storm drain marking. Materials and equipment are not funded.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All grant-funded activities must be implemented in Baltimore County. Organizations must be locally-based with active membership in Baltimore County. Activities span multiple watersheds including Back River, Deer Creek, Gwynns Falls, Jones Falls, Baltimore Harbor, Liberty Reservoir, Lower and Little Gunpowder Falls, Tidal Gunpowder/Middle River/Bird River, Loch Raven Reservoir, Patapsco River, and Prettyboy.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications have three key steps: (1) Complete the DEPS Watershed Grant Application Questions addressing organization eligibility, restoration and stewardship activities, grant deliverables by quarter, Stream Watch participation, watershed planning involvement, connection of actions to watershed plans, education and outreach, capacity building, project guidance and inspections, and past year accomplishments. (2) Complete the standard Baltimore County Application for Financial Assistance (AFA form). (3) Submit all materials including supporting documents such as proof of 501(c)(3/4/6) good standing status, budget proposal, financial statements, and any additional attachments as separate PDF files via email to Erin Watts. The application must be signed by the Executive Director or President of the Board. Applicants will be notified of their status in May.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides financing to small, minority, woman, and veteran-owned businesses operating in leased commercial space in Baltimore County using revenue from Maryland's video lottery terminals. The program supports key job-creating industries by offering business owners $50,000 to $250,000 in financing with reduced down payment requirements and interest rates set at or below current market rates. Loans have a maximum 20-year term and customized payment plans to help businesses maintain cash flow. Funds can be used for start-up funding, gap funding, building improvements, equipment acquisition, lease improvements, business acquisition, working capital, and commercial real estate acquisition. To date, Boost has approved over $6 million in loans.

structured_extraction.program_name: Grocery Store Personal Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City offers a personal property tax credit to grocery stores and supermarkets that are locating in or making significant renovations within targeted Food Desert Retail Incentive Areas in the city. The program was created by enabling legislation passed at the state level in 2015, with City Council support, and went into effect on January 31st, 2016. It was amended in 2018. The credit recognizes that access to healthy food choices is important for community health and that quality supermarkets drive economic development. Personal property tax credits are provided to supermarkets and grocery stores that locate or renovate in designated Food Desert Retail Incentive Areas and meet specific requirements for the amount and variety of healthy food they provide. The credit is a 10-year, 80 percent credit against personal property tax covering furniture, fixtures and equipment.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-year, 80 percent credit against personal property tax for supermarkets and grocery stores locating in or making significant improvements in targeted grocery store incentive areas. The credit covers personal property, which typically includes furniture, fixtures and equipment. Personal property tax credits are provided to supermarkets and grocery stores that locate or renovate in designated Food Desert Retail Incentive Areas and meet specific requirements for the amount and variety of healthy food they provide. The credit is based on expenditures on new personal property.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal property investment in grocery stores, including furniture, fixtures and equipment used for grocery retail operations. Tax credits to support supermarkets and grocery stores locating or renovating in food desert areas to provide healthy food options.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in a designated grocery store incentive area or Food Desert Retail Incentive Area in Baltimore City. Applicants can verify eligibility by visiting CityView and entering their address.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Fill out and submit a pre-qualification form to determine if the location is in a grocery store incentive area; allow 30 days for processing. Complete the downloadable pre-qualification form, print and sign in blue ink, scan and email to info@baltimoredevelopment.com with store concept and rendering. Step 2: Once pre-qualified, proceed with construction or renovation; upon completion, download the fillable initial application form, complete and print, sign in blue ink, scan and email to tax.credits@baltimorecity.gov with pre-qualification letter and invoices/receipts; allow 60 days for processing. This must be received by October 1 to be considered for the tax year beginning January 1 of the next calendar year. Step 3: Once a tax credit is granted, download the continuing eligibility form and submit each year by November 30 of the prior year to maintain eligibility for the full 10-year period. Print with blue ink signature and email to info@baltimoredevelopment.com. Applicants should contact the Baltimore Development Corporation for application procedures and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: BGE Energizing Small Business Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to help eligible small businesses in Maryland succeed and recover by providing grants of up to $20,000 per eligible business. The program is presented in partnership with Hello Alice and the Global Entrepreneurship Network (GEN). Originally launched to support COVID-19 relief and recovery, the program has evolved into an ongoing initiative that supports business operations and serves customers with a focus on those operated by historically underrepresented groups, minority-owned businesses, and woman-owned businesses. The program is part of BGE's comprehensive customer relief and economic recovery initiative. During the first year, $3.5 million was distributed to 176 diverse small business owners across Maryland, with $15 million total distributed across multiple application rounds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $20,000 per eligible business. The program has offered multiple rounds of funding, with $15 million total distributed across application cycles in 2021 and 2022, with $3.5 million distributed to 176 diverse small business owners in the first year. The program continues with recurring application rounds. Applicants from previous rounds who were not selected may reapply with new information.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Multiple rounds including: January 20 – March 3, 2021; May 5 – June 16, 2021; September 1 – October 13, 2021; August 26, 2022; and June 13, 2025 at 6 p.m. ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses with 25 or fewer full-time employees and annual gross revenues under $7 million, located in Maryland and existing BGE electric and/or gas customers in good standing. Priority given to companies owned by historically underrepresented groups, minority-owned businesses, and woman-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: COVID-19 relief and recovery support; to support business operations and serve customers as determined by demonstrated need for funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-wide; applicant must be an existing BGE electric and/or gas customer in BGE's service area.

Annual gross revenues of less than $7 million USD

Demonstrated need of funding to support business and serve customers
Preference given to minority-owned and woman-owned businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications through the BGE website or Hello Alice portal. Multiple application rounds are available. Applications are evaluated based on eligibility criteria and demonstrated need. Applicants from previous rounds who were not selected may reapply with new information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The BGE Green Grants program provides grants to nonprofit organizations and government agencies for environmental stewardship, energy efficiency, pollution prevention, and community engagement initiatives within Baltimore Gas and Electric Company's service territory. The program supports local initiatives that advance environmental protection and sustainability. Grants of up to $10,000 are available for projects focused on clean air and water, fighting the effects of climate change, innovative use and promotion of alternative energy sources, conservation, education, and other environmental initiatives. The program is in its 13th year of operation, having awarded more than $2.6 million to hundreds of community-based projects since its launch in 2013, with more than $251,000 awarded to nonprofit organizations in 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Calvert County Homeowner Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A county supplement to Maryland's State Homeowners Property Tax Credit Program for primary residence homeowners of all ages in Calvert County with gross household income less than $60,000. This tax credit reduces property tax liability on the principal residence. Eligible applicants complete the HTC-60 application with required documentation and submit to the Maryland State Assessments and Taxation office. Upon approval, the homeowner receives a revised tax bill from the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit against county property taxes for primary residence homeowners. Applicants must have gross household income less than $60,000 and file the HTC-60 application. One application covers both state and county credits. Eligible applicants download the HTC-60 form, complete it with required documentation, and submit to the Maryland State Assessments and Taxation office for processing. Once approved, the homeowner receives a revised tax bill from the county.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than September 1 each year (often extended to October 31)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Primary residence homeowners in Calvert County of all ages with gross household income less than $60,000

Homeowner status
Primary residence homeowner

Complete application with copy of federal income tax return and submit by September 1 each year (deadline often extended to October 31). Download the HTC-60 form from the SDAT website, complete the application with required documentation, and mail the signed application and documentation to Maryland State Assessments and Taxation, 301 W Preston Street, 9th Floor, Room 900, Baltimore, Maryland 21201. Contact the SDAT office at 800-944-7403 to check application status. One application serves for both state and county credits. Upon approval, a revised tax bill is issued by the county.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides free native tree seedlings to property owners in Calvert County's Chesapeake Bay Critical Area who want to replant areas on their property to help maintain forest cover. The program is funded by fees collected when on-site forest replacement is not possible. Species availability varies by year, and applicants can choose substitute species if their preferred species is unavailable or reapply the following year.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free native tree seedlings are provided to eligible property owners in the Critical Area for reforestation efforts on their property. Species availability varies by year, and applicants can choose substitute species if their preferred species is unavailable or reapply the following year.

Only native species listed on the Calvert County Native Plant List for the Critical Area Reforestation Program can be used

Applicants are notified of decisions and can choose substitute species if preferred species are unavailable. Contact the Planning & Zoning Department for more information on the application process and eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that help high-hazard properties reduce risk through mitigation projects. The program covers up to 75% of project costs, with homeowners responsible for the remaining 25% and any cost overruns. Projects may include acquisition and demolition of high-risk structures or elevation of flood-prone properties.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants covering up to 75% of eligible project costs. Homeowners are responsible for the remaining 25% of costs and any cost overruns. Funding is allocated through FEMA after the subapplication review process, typically released in late summer.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not later than July 1st for Pre-Screening Questionnaire submission; August 31st for final application materials submission
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with high-hazard properties at risk from flooding, cliff erosion, or other natural hazards. Priority given to NFIP Repetitive Loss and Severe Repetitive Loss properties, and high-risk cliff properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property acquisition and demolition, or elevation of structures above the Base Flood Elevation for flood-prone properties. Funds support new foundation construction, re-attachment of structures, and related mitigation work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to properties in Calvert County, Maryland. Priority consideration for properties along cliffs or properties with NFIP Repetitive Loss or Severe Repetitive Loss designation.
requirements_list: Property must be high-hazard and eligible for mitigation

For acquisition and demolition: property appraisal, plat survey, color photos, and itemized cost estimate required; flood projects require NFIP insurance copy and flood event documentation; cliff projects require certified imminent threat letter from engineer

For elevation (flood only): plat survey, color photos, NFIP insurance documentation, past flood event documentation, elevation certificate, certified structural stability letter from engineer, and itemized cost estimate
Homeowners responsible for 25% of project costs and any cost overruns
Documentation must be submitted by established deadlines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Pre-Screening Questionnaire by July 1st; Division of Emergency Management will contact resident with additional information. Submit complete application materials by August 31st using the provided homeowner guides. CCDEM develops subapplication by mid-November. Final subapplication submitted to FEMA by late January. FEMA releases funding decisions in late summer. Funding allocated to states and project begins in mid-spring. Process typically takes up to two years from initiation to funding awards.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners of Agricultural Preservation Districts can apply to certify TDRs. The TDRs can be sold privately to buyers who use them to increase density on receiving area properties.

structured_extraction.program_name: Caroline County Small Business Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A revolving loan fund that provides financing to small businesses and agriculture-based businesses in Caroline County to help them start up, expand, scale operations, and close funding gaps after arranging traditional financing. The program assists with working capital, equipment purchases, inventory purchases, processing, packaging, commercial real estate acquisition, new construction, building improvements, and other capital investments that typically cannot be fully financed through traditional lenders. Maximum loan amount is $20,000, though exceptions may be made for large projects creating substantial new jobs; most loans are for less than $10,000. Interest rate is typically prime rate plus 1% at the discretion of the CCED Loan Committee, with loan terms of 5-7 years based on risk level and quarterly or monthly payment options. Funds are disbursed only after all loan documents are signed by all parties. Loans cannot be used to finance existing debt, reimburse owners or equity partners, buy out partners, pay delinquent federal, state, or local taxes, or finance non-owner occupied real estate investment.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: A revolving loan fund that provides loans with a maximum loan amount of $20,000 (though exceptions may be made for large projects creating substantial new jobs; most loans are for less than $10,000) to help businesses close funding gaps after arranging traditional financing or to support business startup, expansion, and growth. Applicants request a specific loan amount and repayment term. Interest rate is typically prime rate plus 1% at the discretion of the CCED Loan Committee. Loan term is 5-7 years based on risk level, with quarterly or monthly payment options available. Funds are disbursed only after all loan documents are signed by all parties. Loan repayment is required regardless of business standing. Applicants must sign a promissory note to the County Commissioners. Funds can be used for working capital, equipment purchases, inventory purchases, commercial real estate acquisition, new construction, building improvements, processing, packaging, business start-up costs, and up to 12 months of operating capital. Loans cannot be used to finance existing debt, reimburse owners or equity partners, buy out partners, pay delinquent federal, state, or local taxes, or finance non-owner occupied real estate investment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Edge: The Caroline County Business Academy
structured_extraction.program_description: A free 8-week business training and education program for small business owners in Caroline County that equips entrepreneurs with tools, resources, and support to grow and manage their businesses. The program is particularly encouraging to minority and women-owned businesses. The curriculum covers organizational infrastructure, leadership, marketing, accounting, financial management, human resources, legal structure, taxes, insurance, and access to capital. The program includes classroom instruction via Zoom on Tuesday evenings (6-9 p.m.), one-on-one mentoring sessions with business coaches, weekly assignments, and culminates in a final 15-minute PowerPoint presentation. Participants learn to increase revenue and sales, manage and hire staff, create sustainable business models, manage expenses, improve financial reports, develop growth budgets, create plans to attract new clients, and prepare to access capital from lenders and investors. No tuition cost; funded through a partnership with the Mid-Shore Regional Council using a grant from the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund.

Participants receive one-on-one mentoring sessions with business coaches, complete weekly assignments including cash flow projections, and deliver a final 15-minute PowerPoint presentation about their business. Participants who complete all requirements receive a Certificate of Completion. Space is limited to 15 participants. structured_extraction.program_description: A tax incentive program offering real property tax credits and state income tax credits to businesses in designated enterprise zones (including Federalsburg, Ridgely, Greensboro, and Goldsboro) in Caroline County that invest in capital improvements or hire new full-time employees. The program is designed to grow existing businesses, create jobs, revitalize communities, and spur development in economically disadvantaged areas. It is part of a partnership between the State of Maryland, which provides reimbursement of the benefits, and the County and Towns. The real property tax credit provides credits against county and municipal property taxes on incremental increased assessed value, with 80% of increased value for the first five years, then decreasing 10% annually (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, and 30%) for subsequent five years. The state income tax credit provides up to $1,000 per qualified new employee hired after certification. The state reimburses 50% of uncollected tax revenue to local jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of tax credits are available: (1) Real Property Tax Credits for businesses investing at least $100,000 in capital improvements, receiving tiered reductions on county and municipal property taxes on newly assessed value with 80% of increased value for the first five years, then decreasing 10% annually (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, and 30%) for subsequent five years, and (2) State Income Tax Credits for businesses hiring at least one net new employee working a minimum of 35 hours per week and paid at least 150% of federal minimum wage (currently at least $10.88 per hour), with up to $1,000 per qualified job in state income tax credit available. Employees must be hired after the business entity receives certification. Tax reductions apply only to the increased property value from improvements, not existing property value. structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps businesses, residential-based businesses, and Internet Service Providers invest in broadband infrastructure and gain access to high-speed internet in Carroll County. The program provides matching reimbursement for construction, acquisition, or leasing of facilities, wireless spectrum, land, towers, or buildings used to deploy broadband service, and also funds last-mile connections to fiber optic networks in underserved or unserved areas through the Fiber Network Enterprise Fund. The program supports ISPs and qualified business enterprises seeking to expand broadband service options or add redundancy to their internet connections. Broadband Internet Access is defined as 25 Mbps downstream/3 Mbps upstream with latency of 100ms or less.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 50% matching reimbursement of qualified project expenses for construction, acquisition, or leasing of facilities or wireless spectrum, land, towers, or buildings used to deploy broadband service, with a cap of $25,000 per approved project and $100,000 per entity or service provider per fiscal year. Additionally, the program earmarks $200,000 to assist qualified business enterprises and Internet Service Providers in gaining access to higher internet speeds through last-mile connections, with Carroll County leasing available fiber to ISPs or businesses directly through the Fiber Network Enterprise Fund. Funds support capital investment in broadband infrastructure including equipment, construction, and fiber laterals. All allocations are subject to approval by the Carroll County Board of Commissioners. Project costs must be paid within 30 days after project period ends. Invoices must include: project name, vendor invoice, and copy of paid check with number, date, and amount.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted immediately with no specified deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, residential-based businesses, Internet Service Providers, and business enterprises located within Carroll County, Maryland with limited access to high-speed internet or seeking to deploy broadband infrastructure; applicants must be in good business standing with federal, state and local authorities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, acquisition, or leasing of facilities or wireless spectrum, land, towers, or buildings used to deploy broadband service; last-mile connections to fiber optic networks in underserved or unserved areas; improved internet connection speeds through fiber network access; and capital investment in broadband infrastructure including equipment and fiber laterals for business and residentially-based businesses located within Carroll County. Project must deliver broadband speeds of 25 Mbps downstream/3 Mbps upstream with latency of 100ms or less.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland, with priority given to unserved or underserved areas of the county. Unserved areas lack access to fixed internet with speeds of 25 Mbps download/3 Mbps upload. Underserved areas lack access to fixed internet with speeds of 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload from two or more providers.

structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency grant program that provides grants to Carroll County small businesses, including sole proprietors and home-based businesses, affected by COVID-19 disruptions to their operations. The program offers $1,000-$1,250 grants intended to provide interim working capital relief to support payroll, rent, mortgage payments, utility expenses, and other ordinary business expenses while businesses coordinate with their banks, business interruption insurance, financial institutions, and federal and state partners. The program was implemented in multiple phases: Phase 1 provided $500,000, Phase 2 provided $250,000 (with $50,000 designated for remaining Phase 1 applicants and $200,000 specifically for sole proprietors and home-based businesses), and Phase 3 made available $93,000 in grant funds, reaching a total fund of $843,000 to support approximately 674 Carroll County small businesses.

structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest loan program that helps new and existing small businesses and individuals, including start-ups, acquire land, buildings, equipment, inventory, and other business needs. The program provides funding to creditworthy businesses and individuals who have difficulty obtaining financing through traditional sources due to limited equity, collateral requirements, or marginal cash flow issues. The program is designed to promote job growth and economic development in Cecil County.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $5,000 to a maximum of $75,000 (may be increased with Loan Review Committee approval and County Executive approval for amounts exceeding $75,000; such increases must meet capitalization requirements). Interest rate is Prime Rate plus 2% fixed for up to 5 years, with rate adjustment for loans exceeding 5-year repayment. Loans may be unsecured or secured at the Loan Review Committee's discretion. All loans require personal guaranty from business principal(s) or owner(s), except limited partners in a limited liability partnership. Repayment terms vary by use: real estate up to 10 years with 20-year amortization and balloon payment at month 120; equipment 3 to 10 years depending on useful life; working capital 1 year interest-only with balloon payment at month 12 and option to extend two additional 1-year periods; physical improvements to real property 5-year maximum. One-time non-refundable application fee of $100 due at submission; closing costs including title searches, lien searches, recordation fees, taxes, and legal fees due at settlement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil Grown Micro Ag Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides small but impactful grants to support the growth, diversification, and long-term sustainability of existing agricultural businesses physically located in Cecil County, Maryland. Funding supports capital improvements, value-added production, agritourism infrastructure, strategic marketing, technology adoption, research, and other investments that strengthen Cecil County's agricultural economy.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Total of $74,666 in available funding offered in three tiers: Seed Grants up to $2,500 for small-scale projects and pilot initiatives; Growth Grants up to $5,000 for operational upgrades, infrastructure improvements, and agritourism enhancements; and Impact Grants of $7,500 to $10,000 for higher-impact projects. All awards are cost-reimbursable, meaning awardees must pay project expenses up front, submit required receipts and documentation, and then receive reimbursement. Reimbursement requests must be submitted no later than June 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 27, 2026 at 12 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing agricultural businesses and farmers physically located in Cecil County, Maryland, including farms, producers, and agricultural enterprises looking to start or grow their operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Production equipment and capital improvements, value-added processing and product development, agritourism and farm experience infrastructure, strategic marketing and market development, technology innovation and implementation, research and education and pilot projects, climate resiliency and conservation improvements, animal welfare improvements, and business diversification or new enterprise. Funds may not be used for debt repayment, general operating expenses, salaries or wages for existing staff, vehicles or trailers, land or real estate purchases, expenses outside the approved project period, or projects outside Cecil County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Agricultural business must be physically located in Cecil County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Operate an existing agricultural business (not conceptual or idea-stage project)
Be physically located in Cecil County, Maryland
Be actively producing agricultural goods or services
Be able to cover project costs up front and request reimbursement
Be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Submit a complete application through the County's OpenGov portal by the stated deadline
All funded projects must be fully completed by May 30, 2026
Submit reimbursement requests with all receipts and required documentation no later than June 15, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete application through the County's OpenGov portal with a detailed project budget including vendor information and cost estimates. Quotes, estimates, or screenshots are required for all major purchases. Applicants must certify eligibility through mandatory attestations. Applications will be reviewed by Cecil County Office of Economic Development staff and external reviewers using a standardized scoring rubric evaluating eligibility and completeness, project impact and feasibility, alignment with program priorities, budget clarity and readiness, and overall quality of the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax deferral program that allows eligible elderly or permanently disabled residential property owners in Cecil County to postpone payment of a portion of their county property taxes. The deferred amount is the increase in county property taxes from year to year (calculated as the difference between the current year's county property taxes and the previous year's county property taxes, after deducting any Homeowner's Tax Credit), up to a maximum of 50% of the assessed property value at the time of initial application. No interest is charged on deferred taxes. Deferred taxes are recorded as a lien against the property and must be repaid if the homeowner sells the property, moves or ceases to occupy it as principal residence, dies, fails to reapply annually, if household income exceeds $60,000, if the property becomes subject to tax sale, or if the base property taxes are not paid. Upon the homeowner's death, deferred taxes must be repaid by the estate or co-owners. A recording fee applies. The deferral applies only to the Cecil County portion of property taxes, not state or town portions.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible homeowners can defer the annual increase in Cecil County property taxes (the amount by which this year's taxes exceed last year's taxes, after deducting any Homeowner's Tax Credit). The maximum total deferral is limited to 50% of the assessed property value at the time of initial application. No interest accrues on the deferred amount. The deferred taxes are recorded as a lien against the property and must be repaid if the homeowner sells the property, moves or ceases to occupy it as principal residence, dies, fails to reapply annually, if household income exceeds $60,000, if the property becomes subject to tax sale, or if the base property taxes are not paid. Upon the homeowner's death, deferred taxes must be repaid by the estate or co-owners. A recording fee applies. Early payment discounts are not considered in deferral calculations; if a discount was granted, it will not be included in the deferral amount calculation. This program defers payment of property taxes only; funds are not provided to recipients but rather tax payment is postponed. The deferral applies only to county property taxes, not state or town portions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: For first-time applicants, by September 1. For consecutive year applicants, application by May 1 and signed Deferral Agreement by June 1 to be included in the July tax bill, but must be received no later than September 1 to be eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Cecil County residential property owners who are at least 65 years old, permanently disabled, or meet other disability criteria, have owned and occupied their home for at least 5 years, and have combined household income not exceeding $60,000.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax deferral only; funds cannot be used for other purposes. The deferral applies only to the Cecil County portion of property taxes, not state or town portions. Deferred taxes must eventually be repaid when the homeowner sells the property, ceases to occupy it as a principal residence, dies, becomes subject to tax sale, or fails to reapply.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County only. The program applies only to the Cecil County portion of property taxes, not state or town tax portions. Applicants must have resided at their property for at least 5 years.
requirements_list: Own residential property for at least 5 years and currently occupy it as principal residence

Be at least 65 years old, OR be permanently disabled and receive benefits from Social Security, Railroad Retirement, Armed Forces, or other federal retirement program, OR be permanently disabled as certified by a physician
Have combined gross income of all household members not exceeding $60,000
Provide proof of age and/or disability
Provide proof of income
Reapply each year to continue participation
If property is co-owned, all owners must sign the application
Pay the base amount of taxes each year (non-deferred portion)
Maintain the property as principal residence
Remain the property owner
Not exceed the 50% of assessed value cap on total deferred taxes
Early payment discounts are not considered in deferral calculations; if a discount was granted, it will not be included in the deferral amount calculation
All property owners must sign the application even if not living in the home
Deferred taxes are recorded as a lien against the property and recording fees apply
Must maintain ownership of the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application form from the Cecil County website in PDF format, pick it up at the Cecil County Finance Office (200 Chesapeake Boulevard, Suite 1100, Elkton, MD 21921), or call 410-996-5385 to request the form by mail. Complete the application and provide required documentation proving age, disability status, and income. Submit the application to the Finance Office by the deadline (September 1 for first-time applicants; May 1 for consecutive year applicants applying for consecutive years to be included in the July tax bill). For returning applicants, the signed Deferral Agreement must be submitted by June 1. All applications must be received by September 1 of any tax year to be eligible. The Cecil County Finance Office will review the application and calculate the deferral amount.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that assists very low-income families, elderly individuals, and people with disabilities to afford decent, safe, and sanitary housing in the private market. Participants receive rental assistance to help pay a portion of monthly rent and can find their own housing including single-family homes, townhouses, and apartments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance provided on behalf of families or individuals to help afford housing or pay a portion of monthly rent. Assistance is provided based on family income meeting federal income guidelines. Families can use vouchers to rent single-family homes, townhouses, and apartments in the private market.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very low-income families, elderly individuals, and people with disabilities who meet federal income guidelines. Preference given to Cecil County residents first, then Maryland residents, then all others.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance to help families afford housing or pay a portion of monthly rent for safe, decent housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland. Families with vouchers may use portability to find housing in other Maryland jurisdictions or elsewhere if a Housing Choice Voucher Program exists in that jurisdiction.
requirements_list: Family income must meet federal income guidelines
Applicant must complete preliminary application
Family must find housing within 120 days that meets HUD Housing Quality Standards
Housing must be within allowable rent limits
Landlord must agree to lease terms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete and submit preliminary application (available as PDF download or by request via email or mail) and family name is placed on waiting list. 2. Selection based on application date and time with preference to Cecil County residents. 3. Wait on list (current wait time approximately 3 years for Cecil County residents). 4. When name reaches top of waiting list, enrollment interview is scheduled and eligibility is determined. 5. If eligible, family attends briefing session. 6. Family finds housing within 120 days meeting HUD standards. 7. Family and landlord agree on lease terms. 8. Housing Agency reviews lease and inspects dwelling. 9. Housing Agency approves or disapproves lease and unit. 10. Upon approval, Housing Agency and landlord enter contract on behalf of family.

Funds are generated from settlements reached with certain manufacturers and distributors of prescription opioid pharmaceutical products and are distributed in accordance with Legislative Provisions set by the State of Maryland. Maximum grant amount is $100,000 per application, with organizations eligible to submit up to two applications addressing different legislative provisions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant funding distributed in spring for the following fiscal year. Maximum amount of each request is $100,000. Organizations may submit no more than two applications, each addressing a different legislative provision. Funds address substance use prevention, overdose response, treatment, and recovery support services per state requirements.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects addressing substance use prevention, overdose response, treatment, and recovery support services for substance use and opioid addiction as prescribed by Maryland state legislation.

Project must address substance use prevention, overdose, treatment, or recovery support services per state requirements
Aligned with Legislative Provisions detailed in the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA)

Organizations may submit no more than two applications, each addressing a different legislative provision
