structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to businesses and organizations in Cecil County to improve the exterior visual appearance and function of properties along the Route 40 corridor. The program aims to enhance the visual appearance of businesses visible from Route 40 and increase community utilization of these businesses, supporting economic growth and community revitalization. Grant funding assists businesses and organizations located along Route 40 corridor in Cecil County to improve exterior appearance and functionality of their facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $25,000 for revitalization projects or up to $50,000 for blight removal projects. Applicants must provide matching funds equal to the grant amount requested, except for blight removal applications which require no matching funds. Funds are distributed on a reimbursement basis after project completion and submission of invoices and proof of expenditures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit businesses and organizations located in Cecil County with a Route 40/Pulaski Highway address seeking to improve their exterior appearance and visibility from Route 40.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds must be used to improve the exterior visual appearance and function of businesses and organizations along Route 40. Eligible activities include signage, lighting, siding, painting, entrance improvements, porch/deck work, fencing, landscaping, hardscaping, sidewalks, driveways, parking, ADA ramps, demolition, and removal of blight. Up to 20% of grant funds may be used for related interior improvements with prior approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Cecil County, Maryland, along the Route 40 corridor with a Route 40/Pulaski Highway address. The property must be on Route 40 and visible from Route 40.
requirements_list: Property must have a Route 40/Pulaski Highway address
Property must be on Route 40 and visible from Route 40
Applicant must be in good standing with the IRS, State of Maryland, and Cecil County
Applicant must provide matching funds equal to the amount requested (except for blight removal applications)
Improvements must be Route 40-front facing or easily visible from Route 40
Projects must improve the exterior facade of the business or organization
Project designs must be approved by Cecil County Government
One application per address
If applicant is a tenant, written authorization from the property owner is required
Existing businesses with residential accommodations must be clearly identified as primarily a business with regular, publicized operating hours
Projects must be completed by June 30, 2026
Grant funds cannot be used to pay off debt from prior projects
Reimbursement only after project completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the Grant Administrator to discuss your project. 2. Read the Route 40 Revitalization Grant Notice of Funding Opportunity. 3. Complete the application online through OpenGov, download and print the PDF application, or request a mailed copy. 4. Gather all required supporting documents including tax returns, proof of good standing, property photos from Route 40, design and cost estimates, documentation of matching funds, proof of insurance, and site control evidence. 5. Submit the completed application and all documents online, by email, by mail, or in person. 6. The Grant Review Committee will evaluate applications on a rolling basis and notify applicants by email of the decision.

Properties zoned SR (Standard Residential) and DR (Development Residential) can act as receiving areas to purchase development rights and achieve higher densities, provided they meet minimum criteria and have adequate water and sewer facilities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles County Small Local Business Enterprise (SLBE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A certification program that gives local, small for-profit businesses based in Charles County exclusive access to certain county government contracts and competitive advantages in bidding on others, through preferences in formal procurements and exclusive reserved procurement opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified SLBE vendors receive exclusive access to county procurements under $50,000 as long as at least three qualified SLBE firms exist. For formal procurements between $50,000 and $500,000, SLBE firms receive competitive preferences: up to 10% cost advantage on Invitations to Bid and Requests for Quotation, and up to 10 points on Requests for Proposals, prorated based on documented SLBE firm participation. If fewer than three SLBE firms are available for informal procurements, SLBE bidders receive an advantage over non-SLBE bidders.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses headquartered in Charles County that meet Maryland Small Business Reserve program thresholds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to county government procurement opportunities for goods and services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have headquarters located in Charles County, or have a branch or satellite office in Charles County that generates at least 50% of the company's annual gross sales or has 50% of its full-time equivalent employees residing in Charles County.
requirements_list: Be a for-profit business and independently owned (no brokers or subsidiaries)

Have headquarters located in Charles County, or have a branch or satellite office in Charles County that generates at least 50% of the company's annual gross sales or has 50% of its full-time equivalent employees residing in Charles County
Meet Maryland SBR (Small Business Reserve) industry-specific thresholds for gross sales and employees
Be certified in Maryland's Small Business Reserve Program
Be registered with eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must first become certified in the State of Maryland's Small Business Reserve Program, then register with eMaryland Marketplace Advantage. Submit a Charles County SLBE application with supporting documentation to demonstrate eligibility. The program is race and gender neutral.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rental assistance program designed to help low-income persons afford decent, safe, and sanitary housing. The Housing Authority issues vouchers to eligible applicants, giving them 60 days to locate suitable housing. Once a suitable unit is found and approved, the Housing Authority makes monthly Housing Assistance Payments directly to the landlord on behalf of the participant, with the tenant paying a portion based on household income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly Housing Assistance Payments made directly to the landlord on behalf of the participant. The tenant's portion of rent is determined by household income and can range from a percentage of income to a subsidized amount. The Housing Authority covers the difference between the tenant's payment and the approved rent amount.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Waiting list currently closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families seeking affordable rental housing in Charles County. Applicants must meet household income limits established by HUD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly rent and utility assistance through subsidy payments to landlords. Funds help participants afford decent, safe, and sanitary rental housing including single-family homes, duplexes, apartments, townhouses, and other rental properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland. Voucher holders may request to move anywhere in the United States where the Housing Choice Voucher Program is administered, though transfers to higher-cost areas may be denied under certain budget conditions.
requirements_list: Household income must not exceed established HUD limits (ranging from $57,400 for 1 person to $108,200 for 8 persons)
Applicants must be on the waiting list and selected when a voucher becomes available
Upon enrollment, applicants have 60 days to locate suitable housing
Housing unit must meet HUD Housing Quality Standards (decent, safe, and sanitary)
Rent must be determined as reasonable by the Housing Authority
Tenant cannot rent from a family member (defined as parents, children, sisters, brothers, grandparents, or grandchildren)
Applicants must complete enrollment interview with an Occupancy Specialist to determine income-based rent contribution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must first get on the waiting list. Once their name nears the top of the waiting list, the Housing Authority will notify them and schedule an enrollment interview with an Occupancy Specialist. At the interview, the Specialist reviews household income to determine the tenant's monthly rent contribution. Once approved, the applicant receives a voucher and has 60 days to locate suitable housing. The tenant then submits a Request for Tenancy Approval to the Housing Authority. The Housing Authority reviews the request and inspects the unit to ensure it meets Housing Quality Standards and rent reasonableness. If approved, contracts are executed between the tenant and Housing Authority and between the Housing Authority and the landlord. The tenant is then authorized to move into the unit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A nine-month educational program for county executives and leaders that deepens understanding of the Southern Maryland region and ecosystem through immersion with other leaders. The program includes an orientation retreat, nine monthly sessions, travel within Southern Maryland, and a volunteer commitment.

Participants must complete a 25-hour volunteer commitment or project by March 1 to graduate.

The developers can then build at higher densities in designated growth areas, while the original property is permanently restricted to agricultural, forestry, and open space uses.

Transferring development rights restricts the property to agricultural, forestry, and open space uses through recorded covenants. The program has been in operation since 1992.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Revenue from the sale of development rights goes to the property owner. The rights allow developers to build at higher densities in designated growth areas.

requirements_list: Property must be in a rural area eligible for the TDR program

Price is negotiated between willing buyer and willing seller

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides tuition reimbursement to Charles County Government employees to support their continued professional development through job-related education and degree programs.

Reimbursement covers up to 12 credit hours per year, with a maximum amount determined through the annual County budgetary process. Textbook costs are also reimbursed with receipt submission. Undergraduates must earn a grade of C or better, and graduate students must earn a grade of B or better to qualify for reimbursement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time and full-time reduced hour Charles County Government employees who have worked for the County for a minimum of one year and are non-probationary.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and textbook costs for credit courses that are job-related or part of a degree program related to the employee's current position or a County position the employee may reasonably expect to progress into.

Courses must be job-related or part of a degree related to current or reasonably expected future County position
Undergraduates must earn a grade of C or better
Graduate students must earn a grade of B or better
Employees must reimburse the County on a pro-rata basis if they separate from County employment within one year following course completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employees must submit course information for approval, complete the course, submit the final grade report showing successful completion, and submit textbook receipts for reimbursement. structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program providing support services to family caregivers and relatives caring for older adults, people with Alzheimer's disease, people with disabilities, and grandchildren. Services include education, training, information and referrals, counseling, support groups, respite care, adult day center referrals, in-home aide services, home modifications, escorted transportation, legal and financial assistance, hospice services, geriatric care management, and skill development training. The program provides financial assistance for supplemental services such as supplies, durable medical equipment, and prescription assistance. The program helps alleviate the emotional and financial burdens of informal caregiving by filling gaps in care and providing temporary relief from caregiving responsibilities.
structured_extraction.agency: Charles County, Montgomery County, and Frederick County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance may be available for respite care to provide temporary relief from caregiving responsibilities and supplemental services such as one-time or short-term supplies, durable medical equipment, prescription assistance, and similar services. In Frederick County, up to $800 per year in assistance is available toward respite care with no income requirements. The program provides respite care (short-term breaks for caregivers provided inside or outside the home), in-home aide services with help for bathing, dressing, housekeeping, and personal care, referrals to adult day centers for social, recreational, and health services, support groups offered in-person, by telephone, or online, practical guidance and emotional support, home modifications and devices for safety and independence, escorted transportation, legal and financial assistance including power of attorney and healthcare planning, hospice services with symptom management and grief counseling, geriatric care management, and skill development training on assisting with daily tasks safely. Caregiver training includes information on caregiving skills, self-care, employment laws, and when to seek professional help. Services are provided at no cost to eligible recipients where applicable. Priority for funded services is given to financially needy persons where applicable. Education and training coordination with local organizations, information and referrals to local agencies and services, and resource materials are also provided.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jordan Cox, Caregiver Program Coordinator; Sayira Ball, Caregiver Program Coordinator
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers of any age who meet eligibility criteria, including those caring for frail older adults and people with disabilities, caregivers of persons age 60 or older, caregivers age 55 or older caring for children under 18, grandparents and relative caregivers aged 55 and older caring for children aged 18 or under or adult children with disabilities aged 19-59, caregivers of persons with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders of any age, non-related caregivers, and adults providing assistance to family members with physical or cognitive disabilities. One out of four adults in Montgomery County provide care to family members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Respite care for temporary relief from caregiving responsibilities and providing assistance toward respite care costs, adult day center referrals, supplemental services including supplies, durable medical equipment, prescription assistance, and similar one-time or short-term services. In-home aide services with help for bathing, dressing, housekeeping, and personal care. Home modifications and devices for safety and independence, escorted transportation, legal and financial assistance, hospice services, geriatric care management. Non-financial assistance includes training on caregiving skills, information about available services, counseling, support groups, practical guidance, emotional support, education and training coordination with local organizations, information and referrals to local agencies and services, resource materials, and connection with skilled providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Montgomery County, and Frederick County, Maryland. The person cared for must be a resident of Charles County, Montgomery County, or Frederick County. If the caregiver is caring for children, the caregiver must be a resident of Charles County age 55 or older, or a grandparent/relative caregiver age 55 or older in Frederick County.
requirements_list: The person cared for is a resident of the eligible county and at least 60 years old, OR
The caregiver is a resident of the eligible county who is at least 55 years old and is the primary caregiver for children under the age of 18, OR
The caregiver provides care for a person with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder regardless of age
Grandparents and relative caregivers must be age 55 or older caring for children age 18 or under or adult children with disabilities aged 19-59 and cannot be the child's natural or adoptive parent
Priority given to persons who are financially needy
No income requirements in Frederick County
Eligibility requirements vary by specific service or program component; eligibility screenings conducted by staff
A W-9 form is required for Frederick County applicants
Caring for another adult with physical or cognitive disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Caregivers can contact the Aging Division or call the Aging and Disability Resource Unit at 240-777-3000 to get information and assistance. Staff will conduct eligibility screenings, help complete applications, and advise on required documentation. For respite care specifically, contact Arc Montgomery County Respite Services Program at 301-816-9647 or call 240-777-3000 to have an application mailed. Support groups meet at 2:00 p.m. on the last Wednesday of each month at the Richard R. Clark Senior Center in La Plata. In Frederick County, applicants complete the appropriate respite care application (for those caring for someone 60 or older with early onset dementia, or for grandparent/relative caregivers). A W-9 form is required. Submit applications to the Division of Aging and Independence. Caregivers can also contact Holy Cross Caregiver Resource Center for referrals to specific services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program component that allows eligible Housing Choice Voucher participants to use their rental assistance to purchase a home. The program converts Housing Choice Voucher rental subsidies into homeownership assistance, helping first-time homeowners purchase their own home using voucher funds. Provides financial assistance to first-time home buyers and current voucher program participants to help them transition from rental assistance to homeownership. A monthly assistance subsidy is paid towards the mortgage on the participant's home, with the subsidy amount based on household income and approved mortgage payment. The program provides pre-eligibility determination and support for transitioning from renting to homeownership.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly assistance subsidy paid towards the mortgage on the participant's home. The subsidy amount is based on the participant's household income and the approved mortgage payment. The program converts a Housing Choice Voucher rental subsidy to help eligible first-time homeowners purchase a home. Voucher funds that previously paid rent to a landlord are now applied to homeownership assistance. The program provides pre-eligibility determination and support for transitioning from renting to homeownership.

Applicants must obtain independent financing through a participating lender. Upon approval, monthly assistance subsidies are paid towards the mortgage.

requirements_list: Must be age 18-25 at the start of the program
Must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident alien, or have documentation confirming permission to work in the U.S. during the year-long term of service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website and should indicate during the application process if they are interested in working with the City of Annapolis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Trust Water Quality Improvement Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to fund the design of new stormwater treatment facilities and construction of new facilities. Projects can treat currently untreated runoff and improve drainage in communities. Design grants may fund engineering firms to design stormwater facilities, conduct public outreach meetings, and assist in gathering maintenance agreements. Construction grants fund permitting and implementation of stormwater projects.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants available for stormwater treatment facility design and construction. Design grants fund engineering firms to design stormwater facilities, host public outreach meetings, and assist in gathering long-term maintenance agreements. Construction grants fund permitting and implementation of projects. Projects are typically publicly bid to ensure fair pricing. As-builts or plans showing the as-constructed survey of new stormwater facilities are delivered to the City upon project completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Usually applications are due in the Spring
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities and property owners in Anne Arundel County seeking to improve stormwater management and water quality
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design of new stormwater treatment facilities, construction of new facilities, engineering services, public outreach meetings, maintenance agreements, permitting, and project implementation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, including the City of Annapolis
requirements_list: Project must involve stormwater treatment or drainage improvement
Design projects may require public outreach meetings
Long-term maintenance agreements must be gathered
Construction projects typically must be publicly bid
As-builts or plans showing as-constructed survey must be delivered to the City upon completion
Stormwater facilities must be inspected by the City every three years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted annually, typically due in Spring. Projects are evaluated and approved through the City's partnership with Anne Arundel County and the Chesapeake Bay Trust. Once a project is designed, funding for construction can be sought in subsequent grant cycles.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis Owner Occupied Housing Rehabilitation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Eligible Annapolis homeowners can apply for forgiveness loans to make home improvements. The assistance covers the cost of home improvement work performed by a licensed contractor. There are no monetary loans involved—the work is done at no cost to the homeowner unless the home is sold, rented, or transferred within 15 years.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Forgiveness loan for home improvements. The City provides up to $30,000 in home improvement work at no cost to the homeowner. If the home is sold, rented, or transferred within 15 years, the homeowner must repay the full amount within 11 years. After the 11th year, the loan is reduced by 20% per year for the last five years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Annapolis with household income less than 60% of Area Median Income
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home improvements including roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, kitchen and bathroom remodeling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis, Maryland only
requirements_list: Homeowner in Annapolis, MD
Combined household income less than 60% of Area Median Income
Property must be the resident's sole and principal residence
Proof of income for all people living in the home
Proof of homeownership
Proof of homeowners insurance
Proof that mortgage payments are up to date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Property Rehabilitation Program pre-application and mail it to Arundel Community Development Services at 2666 Riva Road, Suite 210, Annapolis, MD 21401. Applications can be submitted by mail or fax.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis Rental Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to help eligible low and moderate-income households pay rent, security deposits, and unpaid utility bills to stabilize housing situations, prevent eviction, prevent utility shutoffs, and provide security deposit assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct payment assistance to landlords or utility companies on behalf of eligible renters. The approved funding amount is based on the applicant's qualifications. Account balances must not be more than 60 days past due. Application processing takes up to 4-6 weeks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate-income renters living in the City of Annapolis who are at risk of homelessness or housing instability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent payments, security deposits, and unpaid utility bills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be living in the City of Annapolis and renting in a household with a current and valid City rental license.
requirements_list: Must live in the City of Annapolis
Income must be at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) as defined by HUD
Household must demonstrate risk of homelessness or housing instability through past due utility or rent notice, eviction notice, or other evidence
Must hold a lease or sublease in applicant's name or demonstrate ability to hold a lease for security deposit assistance
Must be employed or show employment within the last 90 days, or be retired
Must rent in a household with current and valid City rental license
Account balances must not be more than 60 days past due
Must provide verification of household income (W-2, pay stubs, tax returns, bank statements, proof of retirement)
Must provide rental/lease agreement or sublease
Must provide photo identification for all adult household members
Must provide at least one of the following: eviction notice, judgment, landlord correspondence indicating arrears and amount owed, unpaid utility bill, or utility shut-off notice
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application through the provided survey form or apply in person. Provide information about your household and income. Submit supporting documentation including income verification, lease agreement, photo identification, and evidence of housing instability. Once all documentation is received, a rental associate will review for eligibility. Approved payments are made directly to the landlord or utility company. Applicants can also walk in to apply at the Robinwood Community Services office at 1453 Tyler Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21403 or call to schedule an appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers low-interest loans to help property owners in the downtown Historic District pay for installing automatic fire sprinkler systems in their buildings.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five-year loans at 1% annual percentage rate with a maximum loan amount of $25,000. Funds are available until the annual allocation of the fund is exhausted. Priority is given to applicants proposing residential use in upper floors and those utilizing a certified minority contractor. Once the loan application is approved and building permits are issued, the payment is disbursed as a check to the applicant.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline specified; available until annual allocation is exhausted
structured_extraction.contact_name: Adam Strott, Economic Development Manager; Bud Zapata, Captain of the Fire Marshal's Office
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in the Annapolis Historic District on Main Street and Francis Street who are required to install fire sprinkler systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financing the cost of retrofitting buildings with automatic fire sprinkler systems that meet National Fire Protection Association Standard 13.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Restricted to buildings on Main Street and Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District that have a dedicated City water line for sprinkler system connection.
requirements_list: Must own property on Main Street or Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District
Must have a dedicated City water line available for sprinkler system connection
Must have a licensed contractor create a plan for the sprinkler retrofit
Must be required to comply with Annapolis City ordinance O-1-22 requiring fire sprinkler installation
Building permits must be obtained before work begins
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an online loan application by scanning the QR code provided or using the keyword 'sprinkler loan' at www.annapolis.gov. The Finance Office reviews the application and shares it with the Fire Marshal, who coordinates with the permit office and provides approval. The City of Annapolis Office of Law then prepares a contract. Once the contract is finalized and building permits are issued, the loan disbursement is made as a check to the applicant.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis partners with the Arbor Day Foundation to distribute free trees to residents. The program includes a research-based, easy-to-use online mapping tool that helps identify the best location to plant trees in a yard. By entering information about a home and yard, the tool calculates where to strategically plant trees for the greatest cooling, energy, and money-saving benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free trees distributed to residents who register for the program. Registration includes access to an online mapping tool to help determine optimal planting locations for maximum cooling and energy savings benefits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration begins on September 15
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis residents interested in planting free trees on their property with guidance on optimal placement for energy and cooling benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free trees for planting on residential property to increase urban forest canopy and maximize cooling and energy-saving benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis area. Registration tool helps identify best planting locations in individual yards based on home and yard characteristics.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online beginning September 15 using the Arbor Day Foundation registration link. Use the online mapping tool to enter information about your home and yard to identify the best planting locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis distributes federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development to support community development projects and provide assistance to low and moderate-income residents. The program aims to develop viable urban communities by providing decent housing and suitable living environments, expanding economic opportunities, and funding social services, primarily for low and moderate-income persons and households. Funds support capital projects involving physical infrastructure, construction, housing rehabilitation, homeownership opportunities, home repairs for low-income homeowners, and support for community and social service organizations.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Annapolis receives approximately $278,182 in CDBG entitlement funds annually (FY 2027). Funds are allocated for capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction, housing rehabilitation, homeownership opportunities, home repairs for low-income homeowners, and support for community and social service organizations that benefit low and moderate-income individuals and households. Public service projects are no longer funded through this program. The city distributes these grants to eligible community organizations and individuals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 4:30 PM on Friday, March 6, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations and low-income homeowners in the City of Annapolis, particularly those serving or supporting low and moderate-income residents. Families with children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects involving physical infrastructure, construction, housing rehabilitation, homeownership opportunities, home repairs for low-income homeowners, and support for human service and social service organizations. Public service projects are no longer funded through this program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis only. Activities and projects must be located within the City and benefit low and moderate-income individuals and households.
requirements_list: All proposed activities and projects must benefit low and moderate-income individuals and households
Proposed projects must be capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction
Applications must be submitted to the Planning and Zoning Department by the stated deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community organizations and low-income homeowners submit applications to the Planning and Zoning Department by the deadline. The City's Community Development Division reviews applications. A public hearing is held to allow for public comment. The Affordable Housing and Community Equity Development Commission provides oversight and recommends funding. The City Council approves all CDBG-funded projects, which then become part of the CDBG Action Plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: A low-cost do-it-yourself home energy audit option that allows homeowners to assess their home's energy efficiency without professional assistance. This self-directed home energy audit tool is accessible online and allows homeowners to identify energy efficiency opportunities at a low cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A self-directed home energy audit tool accessible online that homeowners can use to identify energy efficiency opportunities at a low cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners seeking an affordable self-guided energy audit
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; this is a technical assistance tool for identifying energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in the BGE service territory
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Access the DIY home audit tool online through the provided website link.

structured_extraction.program_name: Electric Leaf Blower Rebate Program (City of Annapolis)
structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program that helps residents and landscape businesses transition from gas-powered leaf blowers to electric models. Residents receive up to $100 and businesses receive up to $1,500 to offset the cost of purchasing electric leaf blowers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates up to $100 for residents and up to $1,500 for lawn care and landscape businesses to purchase electric leaf blowers. Applicants must fill out an application, provide proof of residency, and proof of purchase.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis residents and lawn care and landscape businesses operating in Annapolis
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of electric leaf blowers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and businesses operating within the City of Annapolis limits
requirements_list: Proof of residency
Proof of purchase of electric leaf blower
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants fill out an application online and provide proof of residency and proof of purchase.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis provides operating and capital grants to non-profit organizations. Operating grants support day-to-day costs of running the organization. Capital grants support the purchase of property, construction, remodeling, expansion of facilities, or purchase of equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Operating grants provide support for day-to-day costs of running a non-profit organization. Capital grants provide support for the purchase of property, construction, remodeling, or expansion of a facility, or the purchase of equipment. Award amounts and specific terms are determined through the annual budget process based on committee recommendations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, April 1st, 2026, by 4:30 PM
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations serving Annapolis residents that provide services sustaining and empowering youth, families and individuals; preserve and enhance community character; contribute to a vibrant economy; or are integral to community revitalization, economic development and environmental sustainability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating grants support day-to-day costs of running a non-profit organization. Capital grants support purchase of property, construction, remodeling or expansion of facilities, or purchase of equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis. Organizations must demonstrate that seventy-five percent of programming and work benefits and engages City residents.
requirements_list: Applicant must have administrative and financial capacity to carry out the project successfully
Applicant must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Project must help meet one of the four grant priorities
Applicant must demonstrate that the proposed activity provides maximum public benefit in relation to cost
Applicant must demonstrate ability to leverage additional funds
Organization must clearly demonstrate one or more of the four priorities
Organization should show strong collaboration with community members, local churches, schools, and or other organizations that share similar objectives
At least seventy-five percent of programming and work must benefit and engage City residents
Organization should have diverse funding sources outside city funding, such as in-kind donations, fundraising and donation efforts, and federal grants
Past Community Grant recipients must show consistency with grant reporting
Must include copy of last audit or financial statements, or most recent IRS Form 990 tax return
Must include current year organizational budget with income and expenses
Must include Board of Directors list with addresses and phone numbers
Must include copy of current IRS determination letter indicating 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status
Must include Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must include most recent annual report if applicable
If request includes partner organizations, must provide Memorandum of Understanding, support letters, or signed description of roles and responsibilities
Must include summary of City support over previous year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed FY 2027 Community Grant Application with all required supporting documents by Wednesday, April 1st, 2026 at 4:30 PM. Applications received after this deadline will not be considered and no extensions will be permitted. A committee consisting of the Mayor's designated staff person, the Finance Director's designated staff person, and two at-large staff persons will review and evaluate applications. The committee makes recommendations to the Finance Committee for consideration as part of the annual budget process.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Annapolis Children and Families Success Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds community-based organizations to open, expand, and enhance child care and youth development programs in Annapolis. Funded programs provide structured activities for youth with adult oversight at a physical location that develop physical, emotional, social, behavioral, and intellectual capacities. Eligible programs include recreation, sports, arts, science and technology, youth development, learning and education, enrichment, crafts, life skills, and wellness projects. The program supports organizations serving low-income families while preventing adverse childhood experiences and prioritizing equity and inclusion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $10,000 per organization. A minimum of five organizations will be funded. Funding covers program costs for the implementation and evaluation of the project, not general operational expenses. First 75 percent of funds disburse during the week of August 25th upon return of signed contract.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 25th at 4:30pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) status or businesses providing scholarships or free programs serving low-income youth and families in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports opening, expanding, and enhancing child care and youth development programs that provide structured activities including recreation, sports, arts, science and technology, youth development, learning and education, enrichment, crafts, life skills building, and wellness projects for youth in Annapolis. Programs must serve low-income families, prevent adverse childhood experiences, and prioritize equity and inclusion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be located within the City of Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Organization must have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status or be a business that will use funding for scholarships or free programs
Program must provide structured youth activities with adult oversight at a physical location in Annapolis
Program must develop youth physical, emotional, social, behavioral, and/or intellectual capacities
Programs should demonstrate focus on serving low-income families and communities
Programs that accept Maryland Child Care subsidy participants are encouraged
Projects addressing after-school and summer programming, especially 2pm-7pm activities, are preferred
Grantees must submit mid-program and final reports
Grantees must participate in three meetings with Office of Community Services staff
Funding covers program implementation and evaluation, not general operational expenses beyond what is necessary for project success
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through an online application portal at arcg.is/1H0TTj1 or through the Survey123 form-based application portal. Organizations unable to submit online may contact Iesha Young for approval to submit a paper application at City Hall (160 Duke of Gloucester Street, Annapolis, MD 21401) or via email to communityservices@annapolis.gov. All parts and questions must be completed or the application will not be deemed fundable. A review panel evaluates applications based on alignment with grant objectives, community need and impact, innovation and equity, organizational capacity, partnerships, budget justification, technical compliance, and performance measurement. Grant decisions are made by August 8th, and award letters are sent by August 13th.

structured_extraction.program_description: Food Friday is a weekly food distribution program designed to combat food insecurity in Annapolis by providing food-insecure individuals and families with fresh produce, fruits, vegetables, frozen meat, rice, pasta, and other nutritious foods. The program connects recipients with local resources and support networks to promote long-term food security.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each week, eligible Annapolis residents receive a box filled with fresh and canned fruits and vegetables, frozen meat, rice, pasta, and other non-perishable foods. Boxes can be customized for vegan or vegetarian dietary needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Food-insecure individuals and families living in the City of Annapolis who are currently facing hardship and need assistance with food.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fresh produce, fruits, vegetables, frozen meat, rice, pasta, and other non-perishable foods for eligible recipients.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is available only to residents of the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Must live in the City of Annapolis
Must be currently facing hardship and need assistance with food
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals can sign up for a Food Friday box through the online application form available on the city website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Front Yard and Street Tree Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis provides free trees to residents and property owners to plant in front yards or in the public right-of-way (the strip between sidewalk and curb). City contractors plant the trees at no cost. The program aims to grow the urban forest, improve air quality, provide shade, reduce stormwater runoff, and make streets more beautiful and livable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free trees provided and planted by city contractors at no cost to the recipient. Recipient must agree to water and care for the tree for the first 3 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis residents and property owners interested in planting trees in their front yards or in the public right-of-way.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Trees for planting in front yards or the public right-of-way to increase urban forest canopy, improve air quality, provide shade, reduce stormwater runoff, and enhance neighborhood beautification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis only. Planting location must be in the public right-of-way (typically the strip between sidewalk and curb) or in the front yard.
requirements_list: Be a City of Annapolis resident or property owner
Have a suitable planting location in the public right-of-way or in the front yard
Agree to water and care for the tree for the first 3 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Free Tree Application web form available on the city website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive home energy audit program that assesses a home's energy efficiency and provides a list of recommended upgrades and improvements tailored to that specific home.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A home energy audit conducted by a BGE contractor for a $100 fee (valued at $400) that identifies energy efficiency improvements and provides information for accessing rebates.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners seeking a professional energy efficiency assessment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The audit identifies home-specific energy efficiency upgrades and improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in the BGE service territory
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact BGE to schedule a Home Performance audit with an Energy Star contractor.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Repair - Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.program_description: Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County provides home repairs for qualifying county homeowners in need. The program can assist with most types of repair needs and offers up to $10,000 worth of home repairs at no cost to the homeowner.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $10,000 worth of home repairs at no cost to the homeowner. Repairs are performed by Rebuilding Together volunteers and staff.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Annapolis with household income less than 50% of Area Median Income who demonstrate a legitimate need for repairs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs including roof, plumbing, electrical, heating and cooling, and other maintenance and structural issues
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, with focus on Annapolis
requirements_list: Homeowner in Annapolis, MD
All persons on deed must reside in the home needing repair
Combined household income less than 50% of Area Median Income
Demonstrate a legitimate need
Unable to perform the work themselves
Owned home for more than 2 years
Plan to reside in the home for at least two years after repairs
Proof of income for all people living in the home
Proof of homeownership
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Home Repairs and mail it to Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County at 819 Ritchie Hwy, Suite 2000, Severna Park, MD 21146. Applications can also be submitted by email or fax.

structured_extraction.program_name: Installation of Fire Sprinkler System Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for property owners who install fire sprinkler systems in Annapolis.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit available to property owners who install fire sprinkler systems on their property in Annapolis. Specific credit amounts and terms are detailed in the application form.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Annapolis installing fire sprinkler systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of fire sprinkler systems. Tax credit to reduce tax liability for fire sprinkler system installation costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Annapolis, Maryland
requirements_list: Property owner must install a fire sprinkler system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Installation of Fire Sprinkler System Tax Credit Application form.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides financial assistance to homebuyers who need help paying down payment and closing costs when purchasing a Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) home in the City of Annapolis.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $10,000 as a zero percent interest loan. No payments are required during ownership. Repayment is only due upon sale or transfer of the property, or at the end of 10 years, whichever comes first. A lien is placed on the property through a Deed of Trust. The loan amount is determined by MPDU staff in conjunction with the borrower's lender. The borrower must contribute a minimum of one percent of the sales price from their own funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebuyers purchasing a Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit in the City of Annapolis
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing costs for the purchase of an MPDU home
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis
requirements_list: Have an MPDU Certificate of Eligibility
Be a graduate of a HUD-certified Homeownership Counseling Program
Be prequalified by a lender listed in the program or go to a lender of your choice
Contribute a minimum of one percent of the sales price from own funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MPDU Eligibility Certificate Holders will receive this information in their Home Buyer Packet when the city notifies them of available MPDUs for sale. Applicants may also call the program office at 410-263-7961, ext. 7727 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Fish and Wildlife Chesapeake Bay Stewardship Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Small watershed grants for both design and project implementation of stormwater treatment and water quality improvement projects in the Chesapeake Bay region
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Small grants available for watershed project design and implementation. Grants can fund engineering design services and on-the-ground project implementation for stormwater and water quality improvements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are usually due in Spring
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities and organizations in the Chesapeake Bay watershed seeking to improve water quality and stormwater management
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and implementation of watershed restoration projects, stormwater treatment facilities, and water quality improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Chesapeake Bay watershed, including Anne Arundel County and the City of Annapolis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are typically submitted in Spring. Projects are evaluated based on water quality and watershed restoration benefits.

structured_extraction.program_description: A no-cost home energy audit program that helps homeowners assess their home's energy efficiency, safety, and comfort to identify ways to reduce energy costs and carbon footprint.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free home energy audit that identifies energy efficiency opportunities specific to the homeowner's residence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in the BGE service area
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; this is a technical assistance program that provides an audit and recommendations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in the BGE service territory
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact BGE through their website to schedule a quick home energy check up.

structured_extraction.program_description: A city-funded tree planting program designed to restore the City of Annapolis's forest canopy and help achieve 50% urban tree canopy by 2050. The program plants trees at homes, congregations, businesses, and schools through community tree planting projects. The program relies on volunteer community leaders trained through the Tree Trooper program to help find places that need trees and oversee tree planting projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free tree planting services and volunteer support. Community leaders receive free training through the Tree Trooper program consisting of 4 virtual sessions and one in-person planting event. Trees are planted at no cost to eligible properties including homes, congregations, businesses, and schools. The city-funded program provides direct tree planting support and services to communities in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and managers in Annapolis including homeowners, congregations, businesses, and schools who want to participate in tree planting, as well as community leaders interested in becoming Tree Troopers and communities seeking tree planting support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting at residential properties, congregations, businesses, and schools throughout the City of Annapolis to restore and increase urban forest canopy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis only.
requirements_list: Property located within the City of Annapolis
Interest in participating in tree planting program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To become a Tree Trooper and participate in the program, visit the website at aawsa.org/tree-trooper and fill out the interest form located under Become a Tree Trooper section.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides rehabilitation assistance and financing to eligible low and moderate income homeowners in the City of Annapolis to address major systems deficiencies, correct hazardous conditions, and ensure their homes are safe, healthy, and habitable. Loans are budgeted by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and available to eligible homeowners to address conditions that endanger the health and welfare of occupants.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides rehabilitation assistance funds and loans budgeted by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to eligible low and moderate income homeowners for home repairs, improvements, and addressing major systems deficiencies and hazardous or health-endangering conditions to ensure homes are safe, healthy, and habitable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate income homeowners in the City of Annapolis with single-family homes seeking to rehabilitate their primary residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home rehabilitation, repairs, improvements, and addressing major systems deficiencies and hazardous or health-endangering conditions to ensure homes are safe, healthy, and habitable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis only (Anne Arundel County); contact Arundel Community Development Services, Inc. for specific eligibility details.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner
Must be eligible based on program criteria
Property must have major systems deficiencies or hazardous conditions
Low to moderate income
Must meet eligibility requirements determined by Arundel Community Development Services, Inc.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of Community Development or Arundel Community Development Services, Inc. at 410-260-2200 Ext. 7727 or 410-222-7600 to determine eligibility and begin the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Fire Department program providing smoke alarm assessment and installation of smoke and carbon monoxide alarms for residential properties in Annapolis. The program has been operating for 15 years and aims to reduce fire deaths by ensuring homes have working smoke and carbon monoxide detection. The program includes assessment of current smoke alarm situations, guidance on replacing alarms with hard-wired smoke detectors, and referral to local hardware stores for replacement detectors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free installation of smoke and carbon monoxide alarms for residents who request them or cannot afford to purchase alarms. The program includes assessment of current smoke alarm situation, guidance on replacing alarms with hard-wired smoke detectors, and referral to local hardware stores for replacement detectors. Residents can call to request installation or fill out a Smoke Alarm Assessment Form.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of City of Annapolis, both renters and homeowners, who need smoke or carbon monoxide alarms or cannot afford to purchase them.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assessment and guidance for smoke alarm installation, and installation of smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms in residential homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis only. Must be a City of Annapolis address.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the City of Annapolis
Must need an alarm or be unable to afford one
Must be located within City of Annapolis
Residences with battery-operated or no smoke alarms must upgrade to hard-wired detectors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Smoke Alarm Assessment Form with preferred and alternate dates, provide property address and contact information, and indicate current smoke alarm type. Alternatively, call the Annapolis City Fire Department to request installation of a smoke or carbon monoxide alarm.

structured_extraction.program_name: Volunteers in At-Risk Communities: Adopt a Community FY 2024 Building Resilient Communities Together Boots on the Ground Community Engagement Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program funding community-based organizations to develop hands-on outreach and engagement programs that build resilient, empowered communities in Annapolis. The program supports organizations working directly with residents in designated at-risk neighborhoods through trauma-informed programming, mentorship, and community relationship building.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $200,000 in total one-time grant awards available. Maximum of $20,000 per organization. Only one organization will be funded per neighborhood. Funds support community engagement, relationship building, and trauma-informed programming from September 2023 through June 30, 2024. Eligible use of funds includes electronic items (laptops, computers, tablets - max $1,200 limit), travel expenses at GSA rates, meals and incidental expenses (M&IE) per GSA rates, incentive/stipend costs for volunteers providing essential services, and incidental expenses (transportation, supplies) for volunteers.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis until funds are used
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations with 501c-3 nonprofit status serving at-risk neighborhoods in Annapolis
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mentorship programs, mental health services or counseling, trauma-informed programming, community engagement activities, neighborhood-targeted outreach, programs that build community ownership and resilience, electronic equipment (laptops, computers, tablets with max $1,200 limit), travel expenses at GSA rates, meals and incidental expenses per GSA rates, incentive/stipend costs for volunteers providing essential services, and incidental expenses (transportation, supplies) for volunteers. Cannot fund one-time events or projects outside Annapolis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be located in designated at-risk Annapolis neighborhoods: Bay Ridge Gardens, Harbour House/Eastport Terrace, Madison Apartments, Bywater, Robinwood, Annapolis Gardens, Admiral Oaks, Clay Street/Obery Court/College Creek Apartments, Woodside, Parole, Allen Apartments, Admiral Farragut, Quiet Waters, or Watergate Village. Only one organization per neighborhood.
requirements_list: Must have 501c-3 nonprofit status
Must focus on one specific Annapolis neighborhood
Must include one-on-one contact with residents
Must develop practical work plan and timeline with SMARTIE goals and objectives
Must include performance measures and expected outcomes
Must submit itemized budget proposal with maximum 10% overhead costs
Must attend quarterly meetings with Office of Community Services
Must submit progress reports twice during grant period
Must use trauma-informed approaches
Must have long-term relationship building strategy, not one-time events
Electronic equipment costs must align with staff Level of Effort (LOE) percentage
Equipment costs must be proportionally requested based on project involvement
Incentive/stipend costs must be directly tied to program outcomes
Stipends must include justification of recipients and frequency of payment
Costs must comply with GSA per diem rates for travel and M&IE
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete all parts and questions in the online application portal at https://arcg.is/1XSnbT. Alternatively, organizations unable to submit online may contact communityservices@annapolis.gov for approval to submit paper applications at City Hall (160 Duke of Gloucester Street, Annapolis, MD 21401) or via email. Submit itemized budget proposal and work plan with application. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until funds are exhausted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The AU Scholarship Fund helps offset the cost of program registration fees for eligible participants in the Abilities Unlimited adaptive and inclusive recreation programs offered by the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The scholarship covers either 100% or 50% of program registration fees depending on income level. Families with adjusted gross income at or below 300% of the federal poverty line receive 100% coverage. Families with adjusted gross income between 301% and 600% of the federal poverty line receive 50% coverage. Funds are distributed as available and are not guaranteed for all programs at all times.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible participants in Abilities Unlimited adaptive and inclusive recreation programs offered by the City of Frederick who meet income requirements and need assistance paying program registration fees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program registration fees for Abilities Unlimited adaptive and inclusive recreation programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have a rectrac account set up through www.playfrederick.com
Must complete the Participant Questionnaire including accommodation information
Must provide adjusted gross income (AGI) documentation from the most recent tax year
For 100% coverage: AGI must be 300% or less of the federal poverty line
For 50% coverage: AGI must be between 301% and 600% of the federal poverty line
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested participants must set up a rectrac account by visiting www.playfrederick.com and clicking 'register for programs' to create a new account. Then participants must complete the Participant Questionnaire with accommodation information and provide adjusted gross income documentation from their most recent tax year to verify eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to nonprofit charitable and civic organizations to create or enhance services benefiting City of Frederick residents. The program awards grants to support community promotion activities and events that positively impact the greatest number of City residents. Partial funding may be awarded in lieu of a full award, and multiple applications can be submitted for different types of activities. Funds are distributed after July 1 of each year following completion of a letter of agreement between the City and the organization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City Council awards funding to nonprofit charitable and civic organizations to support community promotion activities and events. Partial funding may be awarded in lieu of a full award. Funds are distributed after July 1 of each year following completion of a letter of agreement between the City and the organization. Multiple applications can be submitted for different types of activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling applications accepted; FY2027 cycle opens November 3, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit charitable and civic organizations serving City of Frederick residents and organizations seeking to promote community events and activities in Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating or enhancing services and community promotion activities and events that benefit City of Frederick residents
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Organization must be a nonprofit charitable or civic organization
A letter of agreement between the City and the organization must be completed before funds are distributed
All applicants must attend one of two virtual information sessions
All reporting must be up to date if previous funding has been granted
Interim report due January 31 of the year following funding
Final report due July 31 of the year following funding
Separate application required for each specific type of community promotion activity
Separate applications may be submitted for each specific type of activity or event
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Program Overview. 2. Ensure all reporting is up to date if previous funding has been granted. 3. Attend one of two required virtual information sessions. 4. Complete the online application through Foundant. Applications can also be submitted by email, mail, or hand delivery to City Hall. A scorecard will be available for review.

structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency weatherization program for homeowners and renters currently without a working heating or cooling system, providing HVAC upgrades and tune-ups during the months when those systems are most needed.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, grant-funded emergency HVAC repairs or replacements for homeowners and renters without working heating or cooling systems. Heating funding is available during winter months and cooling funding is available during summer months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties who currently lack a functioning heating or cooling system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: HVAC system upgrades and tune-ups to restore functioning heating or cooling capability in the home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties in Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below the threshold for household size (ranging from $68,500 for 1 person to $129,100 for 8 people)
Homeowner or renter must currently lack a working heating or cooling system
For renters, only the tenant needs to income qualify and landlord permission is required
Homeowners must own the property or have landlord permission if renting
Landlords must sign a building owner agreement and provide proof of ownership if applicable
Applicant must provide name, address, email, and phone number
Applicant must disclose current assistance programs received (OHEP, SSI, SNAP, TANF, Medicaid, DHCD Rehab Program)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a crisis application form available online. Submit supporting documentation showing household income. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development will review and approve all applications. Heating assistance is provided during winter months and cooling assistance during summer months. Applicants can create an account to save progress and auto-populate fields, or request an email copy of the form.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-to-one financial coaching available to anyone wanting to stabilize and improve their financial well-being. No income limits. Service area is Frederick County.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial coaching including goal-setting, credit repair, budgeting, and income and savings management

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Financial Coaching Client Intake Packet and contact Steven Rose at (301) 600-2077 or srose@cityoffrederickmd.gov to schedule an appointment. No cost.

Must want assistance with the mediation process

structured_extraction.program_description: Free monthly workshops for first-time homebuyers that teach financial management, credit, and homeownership basics. Participants must attend two sessions and a credit and budgeting consultation to earn a certificate required for most down-payment assistance programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free monthly homebuyer education workshops held on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Participants must attend both sessions plus an individual credit and budgeting consultation to receive a certificate. Class size is limited to 40 participants.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational training in budgeting, credit management, and homeownership preparation

Must attend both workshop sessions
Must complete individual credit and budgeting consultation
Must provide completed budget worksheet at individual consultation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application online at frederickmd.gov/homebuyers. No income limits. Register on the registration page which has limited capacity of 40 participants per class.

Counselors may recommend clients seek legal advice when appropriate. No income limits.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational counseling on landlord-tenant rights and responsibilities, lease issues, and rental law

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time reduction to water and sewer charges for residential customers who experience excessive bills resulting from an interior or exterior leak on their property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a one-time bill adjustment reducing water and sewer charges. Eligibility requires a bill that is at least 2 times normal usage based on the average of the last three billing cycles. After the leak is repaired and normal usage is confirmed through two readings by the Water Department, the bill is adjusted from the first service day of the protested bill to the first normal reading. The resident continues to make payments based on the average of the last three billing cycles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential customers of the City of Frederick who experience excessive water and sewer bills due to leaks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water and sewer bill reduction for leaks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residential properties served by the City of Frederick water system. Not offered to apartments, condominiums, or any multi-family structure served by one meter.
requirements_list: Must be a residential customer
Water and Sewer bill must be at least 2 times normal usage based on average of last three billing cycles
Leak must be repaired
Water Department must perform two readings to confirm usage has returned to normal
Not available to apartments, condominiums, or multi-family structures served by one meter
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Utility Billing to discuss the excessive bill. The Water and Sewer Finance Team will instruct the resident to have the leak repaired and coordinate with the Water Department for property inspection. After repair, the Water Department performs two readings to ensure usage has returned to normal. Once normal usage is confirmed, the bill is adjusted.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Consultation and guidance on mortgage delinquency resolution options

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Mortgage Default Client Intake Packet and contact the office for assistance. No cost.

Submit an event budget and project budget
Submit a final report by December 31, 2026
Apply through the online portal only; requests via email, phone, or direct mail will not be reviewed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted through the online grant portal. The application deadline is May 1, 2026. Award recipients must submit a final report by December 31, 2026. Funds will be distributed after July 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual appointment-based HUD-required comprehensive reverse mortgage counseling for seniors age 62 or older. Cost is $100, with fee waiver available based on income. Service area is all of Maryland.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling on reverse mortgage options and alternatives to decrease monthly expenses or increase cash flow
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service area is all of Maryland

Must be a homeowner
