structured_extraction.program_name: SECURE Initiative (Supporting Emergency Capacity, Urgency, Resiliency, and Equity)
structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency relief program that provides one-time, flexible bridge funding to eligible local nonprofits that sustain critical services and serve the city's most vulnerable residents. The program addresses funding disruptions affecting nonprofits delivering essential services like food access, housing support, healthcare, youth development, and mental health care.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time, non-renewable bridge grants of up to $50,000 per organization. Total program funding is $700,000. Funds are flexible and can be used to address disruptions caused by loss of state or federal funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Closes March 31, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations in good standing (501(c)(3) or other nonprofit classifications) that operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flexible bridge funding to address program disruptions caused by loss of state or federally funded grants and subgrants, or loss of previously reliable funding sources due to non-renewal, reduced awards, or policy changes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization in good standing (501(c)(3), other nonprofit classifications, or fiscally sponsored projects)
Must operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents
Must deliver programs that support community needs or essential services
Must have experienced a loss in state or federally funded grants and/or subgrants that disrupted program timelines or operations
Must have lost a previously reliable funding source due to non-renewal, reduced awards, or policy changes
Must demonstrate an increased demand for services compared to the same time period last year due to specific federal cuts within a similar or adjacent service
All reporting must be up to date if previous funding has been granted by the City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create or log into an account on the City's application portal at grantinterface.com. Ensure all prior reporting is current if the organization has previously received City funding. Starting October 15, 2025, submit applications through the online portal on a rolling basis until the March 31, 2026 deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A local property tax credit supplement for eligible seniors who own their primary residence in the City of Frederick. The credit is administered by the State of Maryland as part of the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit supplement administered by the State of Maryland. Eligible City taxpayers who file for the State credit are automatically evaluated for the City supplement. If qualified, the State processes both the State credit and City supplemental credit together.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior homeowners age 70 and older who own their primary residence in the City of Frederick and meet income and net worth requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied to the homeowner's property tax obligation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the City of Frederick, Maryland. The property must be the taxpayer's principal residence where they live at least six months of the year, including July 1, unless they are a recent home purchaser or unable to due to health or special care needs.
requirements_list: Be at least 70 years old as of the end of the calendar year preceding the taxable year for which the credit is sought
Have combined gross household income of $40,000 or less (City requirement); $60,000 or less (State requirement)
Own or have a legal interest in the property

The dwelling must be your principal residence where you live at least six months of the year, including July 1, unless you are a recent home purchaser or unable to do so due to health or special care needs
Net worth, not including the value of the property on which you are seeking the credit or any qualified retirement savings or Individual Retirement Accounts, must be less than $200,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program. The State will determine if you are eligible for both the State credit and the City supplement. If eligible, the State will process both credits together.

structured_extraction.program_description: A down payment and closing cost assistance program funded by the City of Frederick's Community Development Block Grant. Provides affordable homeownership access for first-time homebuyers with low to moderate income by offering interest-free loans up to $25,000 for down payment and closing costs with no payments due until the property is sold, refinanced, or is no longer the primary residence. Loan amounts vary based on Area Median Income (AMI): $25,000 at 50% AMI, $15,000 at 51%-69% AMI, and $10,000 at 70%-80% AMI.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interest-free loan up to $25,000 for down payment and closing cost assistance. Loan amount based on Area Median Income (AMI): $25,000 (50% AMI), $15,000 (51%-69% AMI), $10,000 (70%-80% AMI). No payments required until the property is sold, refinanced, or is no longer the primary residence of the borrower. Funded by City of Frederick's Community Development Block Grant from HUD.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers with low to moderate income in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing cost assistance for primary residence purchase
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Home must be located in The City of Frederick, Maryland. Mortgage lender must have physical office in Frederick County, Maryland. Settlement company must have physical office in Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the City of Frederick
Must be a first-time homebuyer
Home must be buyer's primary residence
Must be income, assets, and credit eligible
Must complete homebuyer education requirements
Home must be located within The City of Frederick
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Housing Counseling Office at (301) 600-1506 or HCO@cityoffrederickmd.gov for application details. Homebuyer education class registration available through DHHS Housing Counselors at (301) 600-2077. Contact the Housing Counseling Office for application details and eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A residential tree planting program that provides a 50/50 cost share for containerized trees in the spring. The program encourages residents to plant trees to increase tree canopy, improve air and water quality, and reduce energy costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides a 50/50 cost share for containerized native trees. Trees are pre-discounted to reflect the cost share. Each resident may purchase up to 5 trees in one transaction.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Trees available from February 1st until all trees sell out. Pickup event on March 28th.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of the City of Frederick who own or rent property with landlord permission.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of containerized native trees for planting in residential yards (front or back yards).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to residents of the City of Frederick, Maryland only. Not available to residents outside the city limits.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Frederick resident
Maximum of 5 trees per resident per season
Trees must be ordered and purchased together in one transaction
Renters must have landlord permission
Trees must be planted in an appropriate location on residential property (front or back yard)
May not be a repeat purchase if purchased in prior year under certain conditions (though the FAQ indicates repeat purchases are allowed if still a city resident)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Enter your address on the Tree Frederick online storefront to verify city residency. Step 2: Select trees from available options, considering yard size. Step 3: Pay for trees through the online storefront at the discounted price. Step 4: Pick up trees on the designated pickup event date at Harry Grove Stadium.

structured_extraction.program_description: Financial assistance program administered by the Office of Home Energy Programs aimed at helping income-eligible households pay utility bills and make utility expenses more affordable, protecting against utility-related crises.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help income-eligible households pay utility bills and protect against utility-related crises.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible households in Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Utility bills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick City, Maryland
requirements_list: Income-eligible

structured_extraction.program_description: A weatherization program that audits homes for a full range of energy efficiency improvements, including air sealing, insulation, ventilation upgrades, lighting replacements, and appliance replacements to reduce heating, cooling, and electricity costs by up to 30%. Free, grant-funded weatherization work is completed at no cost to eligible homeowners and renters, with average savings of $372 or more per year on energy bills.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, grant-funded weatherization work on homes including air sealing, insulation, ventilation upgrades, lighting replacements, and appliance replacements. All work is completed at no cost to eligible homeowners and renters. Average savings are $372 or more per year on energy bills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters, as well as nonprofits serving income-eligible clients in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Air sealing, insulation improvements, heating and cooling system upgrades, energy-efficient lighting, health and safety work including combustion appliance venting and mechanical ventilation, and thermostat installation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties in Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below the threshold for household size (ranging from $68,500 for 1 person to $129,100 for 8 people)
Homeowners must own the property or have landlord permission if renting
Landlords must sign a building owner agreement and provide proof of ownership
For renters, only the tenant needs to income qualify
Buildings must be residential (landlords of commercial spaces are not eligible)
Apartment buildings may contain up to 4 units per building for state weatherization funds (more than 4 units reviewed case-by-case)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an application form available online. Submit supporting documentation showing household income. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development will review and approve all applications. Once approved, a qualified professional will audit the home to determine which weatherization work will provide the greatest energy savings.

structured_extraction.program_name: Winning That Government Contracting Award Series
structured_extraction.program_description: A four-session training series designed to equip entrepreneurs with essential knowledge and skills to successfully navigate the federal procurement process. Presented by Ali Paskun, Owner of ABIL Solutions with 40 years of experience in business development. Participants learn about the business development lifecycle, team roles and responsibilities, decoding Federal Government Request for Proposals (RFPs), and proposal writing fundamentals. Registration deadline: 4/27/2026 5:00 PM EDT

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown is allocating $600,000 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding to eligible nonprofit organizations for projects that address community needs including children and families, seniors, education, economic recovery, mental health, health and health disparities, and transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nonprofit organizations can receive grants up to a maximum of $50,000 per eligible project category (Children & Families, Seniors, Education, Economic Recovery, Mental Health, Health/Health Disparities, or Transportation). A total of $600,000 is available for distribution.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1, 2023 at 4:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) tax-exempt status located in or serving Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must fall under one or more of the following categories: Children & Families, Seniors, Education, Economic Recovery, Mental Health, Health/Health Disparities, or Transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must serve the City of Hagerstown or its residents.
requirements_list: Must hold valid 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) nonprofit tax-exempt status

Questions must be submitted by 4:00 p.m. on August 25, 2023.

Homeowner status

structured_extraction.program_description: A Community Development Block Grant funded microenterprise assistance program that provides grants to small for-profit businesses in Hagerstown to support business growth, job creation, and employment opportunities for low-to-moderate income residents. The program aims to help with business stabilization, expansion, and revitalization of vacant commercial spaces.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $2,500 to $5,000 with no private match required. Funding is administered as a reimbursement upon submission of approved receipts. Eligible uses include acquisition of business equipment, purchase of inventory, fixed assets like machinery and IT equipment, professional services including marketing, technological infrastructure upgrades, entrepreneurial training, and operational expenses such as payroll, utilities, and commercial rent or mortgage.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis with no fixed deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit microenterprise business owners located in Hagerstown with five or fewer employees and household income at or below HUD-established limits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of business equipment, purchase of inventory, necessary fixed assets such as machinery and IT equipment, professional services including marketing and business promotion, technological infrastructure and upgrades, entrepreneurial training, and operational expenses including payroll, utilities, rent or mortgage for commercial locations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located within the corporate boundaries of the City of Hagerstown. Roving businesses must document that at least two-thirds of their business occurs within Hagerstown boundaries and must have been in operation for at least six months.
requirements_list: Business must be located in the corporate boundaries of the City of Hagerstown
Business must have five or fewer total employees including owner(s)
Business must be a private, for-profit business
Business and owner(s) must be in good standing with the City and State of Maryland
Business and owner(s) must be in compliance with all applicable City regulations including the Land Management Code
Business must be established and operating for at least 12 months at time of application, except new businesses which may apply with a business plan and business counseling documentation
Owner must have household income at or below HUD-established limits based on household size
Business cannot be a business that restricts access for minors, rental/property investment business, or cannabis-based business
Priority given to first-time applicants; previous awardees must wait three years to reapply; not more than two grants per household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a pre-screening questionnaire to confirm business qualifies. After confirmation, City staff will provide an application form. Submit the application with all required documents including business income tax returns, business bank statements, vendor paperwork, lease agreement or home business permit, business plan if applicable, profit and loss statement, and income verification documents. Funding is administered as reimbursement upon submission of approved receipts.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides child safety seats to families in Washington County through multiple programs. Includes loaner programs at no cost or low cost with optional deposit and partial refund upon return, and free distribution programs for income-qualified families and those receiving public assistance. Seats include specialized models for children with special needs as well as infant, convertible, toddler convertible, and booster seats. All participants must attend short instruction sessions.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Center Vacant Storefront Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to revitalize vacant storefronts in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District. It helps bring first-floor commercial spaces up to current code standards, reduce blight, preserve structures, and create jobs while incentivizing the reuse and activation of vacant storefronts in the City Center area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to a maximum of $50,000 with no minimum amount. Funds are disbursed only after staff verification that all work has been completed to code, including site inspection approvals, and final receipts have been provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners and developers seeking to revitalize vacant storefronts in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation and upgrades to bring vacant first-floor commercial spaces up to current code standards in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) Zoning District, which is part of the City's Sustainable Communities Area in Hagerstown
requirements_list: Project must be located in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District
All projects must comply with federal, state, and local codes, laws, and ordinances
All upgrades must be performed to City Code
A development plan outlining the renovation schedule and major components must accompany the application
All work must be completed to Code with required site inspection approvals
Final receipts must be provided before funds are disbursed

Applications are reviewed based on economic impact, proximity to Public Square (with priority to Main Street), renovation budget, square footage being revitalized, building condition and code violations, and length of prior vacancy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application form with an accompanying development plan outlining the renovation schedule and major project components. A cross-department Review Committee will evaluate applications based on established criteria. Approved applications receive a Letter of Commitment from the City which may be used to assist in financing. Funds are disbursed only after staff verification that all work is completed to Code with required site inspection approvals and final receipts are provided.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Center and City-Wide Redevelopment Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program to support redevelopment projects in the City Center and throughout Hagerstown. The program offers two tiers of funding: grants of $150,000 to $250,000 for larger City Center projects (typically $450,000 to $750,000 or more when combined with developer matching funds), and grants of $5,000 to $25,000 for city-wide projects (typically $15,000 to $75,000 or more when combined with developer matching funds). All developers must provide a minimum 2:1 match of their own funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $5,000 to $250,000 maximum depending on project scope, requiring a minimum 2:1 match from the developer. City Center projects receive $150,000 to $250,000 and typically range from $450,000 to $750,000 or more. City-wide projects receive $5,000 to $25,000 and typically range from $15,000 to $75,000 or more.

requirements_list: Minimum 2:1 match from the developer
Compliance with complete program guidelines

For façade projects, grants range from a minimum of $2,500 to a maximum of $7,500, also requiring a 1:1 match from the applicant (total project cost $5,000 to $15,000).

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that develops viable urban communities by providing decent housing, public facilities and improvements, public services, suitable living environments, and expanding economic opportunities specifically for low- and moderate-income individuals and families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Hagerstown, as an entitlement grantee, receives an annual allocation of funds from HUD. The city prepares a five-year Consolidated Plan supported by annual action plans. CDBG activities are implemented by city staff or community partners who are subrecipients of CDBG funds. Funded projects have included park improvements, accessibility ramps, pedestrian bridges, surveillance systems, skate parks, and dwelling rehabilitations.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community development projects including park improvements, accessibility infrastructure, public facilities, public services, housing rehabilitation, and economic development activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The City of Hagerstown is the only regional entitlement community and lead agency under the CDBG program for the region.

Activities must be outlined in the Annual Action Plan

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The City of Hagerstown's Department of Community and Economic Development (DCED) prepares the Consolidated Plan and annual action plans. CDBG activities are implemented by city staff or community partners designated as subrecipients.

structured_extraction.program_name: Crime-Free Housing Training and Multi-Housing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive program designed to help owners and managers of rental properties reduce drugs and other illegal activity on their properties. The program consists of three phases: management training, premises security assessments, and resident training. It includes a voluntary 4-hour training course that introduces landlords, property owners, and managers to best practices for maintaining crime-free rental properties, providing tools and techniques to promote safe communities and reduce criminal activity. The program educates property owners and residents to improve neighborhood livability by reducing crime. Some property owners and managers may be required to attend if their property receives a certain number of notices from the city.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is free of charge with no obligation to continue. It consists of three phases: management training, premises security assessments, and resident training. The management training is a voluntary 4-hour training program held at the Washington County Free Library, Room 334. Some property owners and managers may be required to attend if their property receives a certain number of notices from the city. The training teaches best practices for achieving crime-free properties and meets the Excessive Use of City Services training requirements under the city ordinance. Services are provided by the Hagerstown Police Department located at 50 N. Burhans Blvd, Hagerstown, MD 21740. Classes with no registrations 48 hours before the start date will be cancelled.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: TBA
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and managers of rental properties in Hagerstown seeking to reduce crime, drug activity, and improve neighborhood livability and tenant quality
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training for property owners and managers on crime prevention and property management best practices, security assessments of rental properties, and training for residents on crime prevention
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown, Maryland rental properties
requirements_list: Owner or manager of a rental property
Some attendees may be required to complete training if their property receives a certain number of city notices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Lt. John Lehman at 301-797-6408 or jlehman@hagerstownpd.org to register or enroll. Download the registration form. The program is voluntary and free to join. Classes are held at Washington County Free Library, Room 334. Classes with no registrations 48 hours before the start date will be cancelled.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax incentive program that provides real property tax credits, income tax credits, and personal property tax credits to businesses and developers that make construction or rehabilitation investments or create new jobs within the designated Enterprise Zone area in Hagerstown, comprising approximately 4,000 acres in the City of Hagerstown and Washington County. The program designates a specific economic incentive area to encourage businesses to locate or expand within the zone boundaries and is designed to stimulate economic development by providing economic incentives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three components: (1) Real Property Tax Credits - a ten-year credit against local real property taxes on the value of real property improvements, starting at 80% of the change in assessed value in years 1-5 and declining from 70% to 30% in years 6-10. Properties in the City receive credits on both City and County property taxes. The State reimburses each jurisdiction 50% of lost revenue. (2) Income Tax Credit (Job Creation) - $1,000 per non-disadvantaged new employee (one-time credit) or $3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, and $1,000 third year for economically disadvantaged employees. (3) Commercial Building Excise Tax Exemption - No commercial building excise taxes on new construction in the Enterprise Zone. Personal property tax credits are also available in Focus Area locations based on personal property assessment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing businesses expanding through capital investments and/or job creation, property developers and owners, and employers creating new jobs located within the designated Enterprise Zone in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building and land acquisition, new construction, rehabilitation and property improvements, new machinery and equipment, and tax credits against real property taxes and income taxes for wages paid to new employees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located within the designated Enterprise Zone in Hagerstown, Maryland, comprising approximately 4,000 acres in the City of Hagerstown and Washington County. Different investment and job creation minimums apply inside City Center (CC-MU zoning area) versus outside City Center. Personal property tax credits require project or business location in the Focus Area.
requirements_list: Located within the designated Enterprise Zone
Minimum construction or rehabilitation investment of $5,000 (in City Center) or $50,000 (outside City Center), OR create 1 new job (in City Center) or 5 new jobs (outside City Center)
Machinery and equipment purchases do not count toward investment requirement
New jobs must be full-time permanent positions (35+ hours per week)
New jobs must pay 150% of federal minimum wage
New employees must be employed for at least 6 months before claiming credit
New jobs must not have previously existed in Washington County
Business must be in an eligible industry type: Manufacturing, Warehousing, Research & Development, Corporate/Regional Offices, Service Industries, or Mercantile/Retail (if in City Center)
Property tax credit applications must be submitted before project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits
Property owner must concur with application if developer/company applies on their behalf
Qualified employees must meet Maryland Department of Commerce requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Washington County Department of Business Development (Linda Spence) to begin the application process. Complete applicable sections based on credit type sought (property tax credit, employment tax credit, and/or personal property tax credit) and submit to Linda Spence. Complete application and program guidelines are available. Property tax credit applications must be submitted before project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program to support installation or improvement of fire suppression systems in buildings. The program contributes to the cost of installing lifesaving fire suppression systems and lowers financial barriers associated with installing water service and fire lines, meter vaults, water meters, and other public utility infrastructure directly associated with adding or upgrading fire suppression systems that meet National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants range from a minimum of $7,500 to a maximum of $50,000. Applicants must match the grant amount 1:1 from their own resources. For example, a $25,000 grant requires a $25,000 applicant match for a total project investment of $50,000. Matching costs can include all work related to fire suppression system installation, both interior and exterior. The program operates on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding availability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified; first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of residential, commercial, professional office, retail, and mixed-use buildings in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for any expenses directly associated with installing or upgrading NFPA-compliant fire suppression systems required to meet current Code standards, including automatic sprinkler system installation, water service or fire line increases, meter vault installation or upgrade, installation or replacement of sprinkler heads and piping, and replacement of mains and backflow devices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the City of Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area. Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be for a fully residential, commercial, professional office, retail, or mixed-use building
Project must be located within the City's Sustainable Communities Area
Applicant must be in good standing with the City of Hagerstown
Total project cost must demonstrate a minimum 1:1 match from the applicant

Application must be aligned with the City of Hagerstown's overall vision for the city

Complete program guidelines and application instructions are available through the provided links. Questions can be directed to the Planning & Economic Development Department.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must live in a one to three family dwelling
One detector available for each living level of the home
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a smoke detector request through the online form or contact the Hagerstown Fire Department by phone at (301) 790-2476.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program designating certain areas as Historically Underutilized Business Zones, offering assistance to small businesses in those zones. HUBZone-certified small businesses receive preferential access to federal contracts and subcontracting opportunities, including competitive and sole source contracting eligibility, and a 10% price evaluation preference in full and open contract competitions. The federal government has a goal of awarding 3% of all federal prime contract dollars to HUBZone-certified small business concerns. The program helps small businesses in urban and rural communities gain preferential access to federal procurement opportunities through the Small Business Administration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HUBZone-certified small businesses receive preferential access to federal contracts and subcontracting opportunities. Benefits include competitive and sole source contracting eligibility, and a 10% price evaluation preference in full and open contract competitions and subcontracting opportunities. The federal government has a goal of awarding 3% of all federal prime contract dollars to HUBZone-certified small business concerns.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses located in historically underutilized business zones in urban and rural communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to federal procurement and contracting opportunities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses located in HUBZone-qualified census tracts and non-metropolitan counties. Hagerstown, Maryland contains designated HUBZone areas.
requirements_list: Business must be a small business concern
Business must be located in a qualified HUBZone area

structured_extraction.program_description: The Tenant Advocacy program works to ensure Maryland renters are living in safe and healthy housing. Tenant advocates advance housing justice in Maryland through direct service, research, and advocacy. Services include assistance with landlord-tenant issues and tenants' rights information and education. The program provides an educational guide covering tenant rights, lease agreements, security deposits, maintenance issues, eviction procedures, harassment protections, fair housing laws, and landlord-tenant dispute resolution. Services include lease reviews, eviction notification and procedure guidance, information on nonpayment of rent, code enforcement assistance, guidance on substandard or unsafe housing, security deposit information, rent escrow information, and lead paint information. Guidance also provided on affordability assessment, property searches, landlord research, application processes, quiet enjoyment rights, harassment protection, and retaliation protections.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides Maryland tenants statewide with free information about tenant rights and responsibilities. Services include lease reviews, eviction notification and procedure guidance, information on nonpayment of rent, code enforcement assistance, guidance on substandard or unsafe housing, security deposit information, rent escrow information, and lead paint information. They also provide referrals to legal service providers and other agencies that could assist Maryland renters. Services are delivered through an online intake form, hotline, downloadable one-page fact sheets, a comprehensive tenant guide, and fair housing fact sheets.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Information and assistance with landlord-tenant issues, tenant rights education, lease reviews, eviction procedures, code enforcement, unsafe housing concerns, security deposits, rent escrow, lead paint issues, affordability assessment, property searches, landlord research, and fair housing protections

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Use the online intake form at econaction.org/tenant-advocacy-intake-form/ to request assistance (response within 24-48 hours). Alternatively, call the tenant hotline at 443-447-7336 (Tuesday-Friday, 10 AM-2 PM) for direct assistance. Contact District Court Self-Help Center at 410-260-1392 (Monday-Friday, 8:30 AM-8:00 PM). Fair Housing program available at 410-709-8429.

structured_extraction.program_description: Commissions, purchases, or accepts donations of site-specific public art works to be installed on property owned by the City of Rockville. Works reference historical, cultural, or socially relevant themes and reflect the city's diversity and dynamism. The program aims to nurture, inspire, and expand citizens' awareness and educational experience with visual arts.

Funding commissions artists to create and install public art on city-owned property.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides and installs basic, inverted-U style bicycle racks for free at business locations that lack bicycle parking near their shop or office. Racks are installed either in public rights-of-way or on private property with a signed agreement and are available for public use on a first-come, first-served basis.

Installation occurs in public rights-of-way or on private property with a signed agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps City of Rockville residents who own homes and properties take steps to prevent damage from future flooding events. The program reimburses residents up to 50% of money paid for approved flood-proofing improvements, up to a total of $5,000. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement for approved flood mitigation improvements, covering up to 50% of total costs with a maximum of $5,000 per applicant. Approved flood-proofing measures include: gutters and downspouts maintenance, grading, protective flood walls, French drain systems, window and door flood protection equipment, basement waterproofing, utility protection, sandbags, flood socks, permanent flood doors, earthen berms, floodgates, sump pumps, drain tiles, waterproofing materials, and flood alert systems. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Applicants must keep all itemized receipts and invoices for reimbursement submission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Rockville residents who own homes and properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flood-proofing and flood mitigation improvements on residential properties, including yard drainage improvements (swales, berms, French drains, grading), foundation waterproofing (impermeable materials, sealers), basement protection (window wells, floodgates, flood panels), interior drainage (sump pumps, drain tiles), flood detection and response (flood alarms, portable pumps), and permits and professional consultation fees.

structured_extraction.program_description: Amendment to the Montgomery County Heritage Area Management Plan that promotes heritage tourism, preservation, and education in Rockville, Maryland. The program provides eligibility for grants and loan assistance for acquisition, development, public interpretation, and programming of heritage properties. It also offers tax incentives for the rehabilitation of non-designated historic buildings and non-historic buildings in active tourism use. The program focuses on late 18th-mid-20th century historic resources and includes funding for capital projects, infrastructure improvements, signage, heritage interpretation and education programming, and community events centered on historic preservation and cultural heritage.

list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

Grants and loan assistance available for acquisition, development, public interpretation, and programming of heritage properties. Sustainable Communities Rehabilitation Tax Credits available for National Register-listed or eligible properties and tax incentives for rehabilitation of non-designated historic buildings and non-historic buildings in active tourism use. Support includes funding for historic property maintenance and renovation, park improvements, signage and wayfinding, heritage education programming, festivals, interpretive materials, walking/cycling tours, and infrastructure development. Bonding Authority of $5,000,000 available for major initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Heritage tourism visitors, local residents, private property owners with historic properties, non-profit organizations, schools and educational groups, cultural organizations, civic associations, businesses, and diverse populations including low-income residents, seniors, and people with disabilities. Businesses and organizations in Rockville's Heritage Enterprise Zone eligible to pursue acquisition, development, and programming of historic properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heritage preservation and adaptive reuse of historic buildings; conservation of natural areas and greenways; heritage interpretation and education programming; tourist amenities development; exhibits and educational products; signage and wayfinding; park restoration and improvements; historic district documentation; walking, cycling, and driving tours; heritage festivals and community events; curriculum development and teacher training; ADA accommodations; infrastructure and building maintenance at historic sites including roof repairs, brick repointing, and restoration work at farmsteads and historic homes. Acquisition, development, public interpretation, and programming of heritage properties. Rehabilitation of non-designated historic buildings and non-historic buildings in active tourism use.

Includes access to identified greenways (Watts Branch and Rock Creek) and major public historical parks (Dawson Farm Park and Glenview Farm).

structured_extraction.program_name: Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit Homeownership Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides access to affordable homes by requiring some for-sale properties in Rockville to be available to residents at prices below market-rate. First-time homebuyers who meet eligibility requirements can purchase homes and must maintain ownership for 30 years. The program establishes affordability requirements, pricing controls, and resale methodologies for designated units in residential developments. Resale prices are calculated by adding inflation allowance and home improvement credits (capped at 10% of original purchase price) to the original purchase price.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible first-time homebuyers can purchase moderately priced dwelling units priced below market-rate. Buyers must qualify for a minimum mortgage of $150,000 and meet household income limits based on Area Median Income (AMI) levels ranging from 50% to 80% AMI. Income limits vary by household size, ranging from $57,400 to $141,610 annually. The program provides access to affordable homeownership with a 30-year deed restriction on resale. Resale prices are calculated by adding inflation allowance and home improvement credits (capped at 10% of original purchase price) to the original purchase price. Home improvements must be permanent, add market value, and be documented with receipts.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Rockville with household income at or below specified AMI levels who are committed to owner-occupancy. Priority is given to MPDU homeowners seeking to resale or refinance their homes, and to households with members who currently live or work in Rockville, have a household member over 55 years old, or have a larger household size.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a moderately priced dwelling unit to be used as the buyer's primary residence. Credits available for documented permanent home improvements that add market value.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program applicants must be Rockville residents within the City of Rockville, Maryland. Priority is given to households with members who currently live or work in Rockville, have a household member over 55 years old, or have a larger household size. Program applies to residential developments in specific zoning districts.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Attend a First-Time Homebuyer Class conducted by the Housing Initiative Partnership or another HUD-approved counseling agency and obtain a completion certificate. Step 2: Obtain a mortgage pre-approval letter from your bank lender (letter must be on lender letterhead and notarized; valid for one year). Step 3: Complete the MPDU Homeownership Program Application online or request a hard copy by emailing rockvillempdu@rockvillemd.gov. Once the application is received, an MPDU certificate will be sent by email within three to four weeks. The household is then placed on the city's MPDU waiting list. When MPDU homes become available, sellers or developers will contact households on the waiting list. The application must be renewed every two years. For resale or refinance requests, submit the request form indicating purpose with documentation of improvements and HUD-1 settlement sheet to: MPDU Program, City of Rockville, 111 Maryland Avenue, Rockville, MD 20850. For improvement credits, submit written request with readable receipts showing payment and itemized costs; MPDU Office may inspect property to verify improvements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit Rental Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville offers affordable rental units through its Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Program. MPDU rentals are available in a number of properties throughout the city at reduced rates for income-eligible households.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides rental units at below-market rates. As of July 1, 2025, MPDU rental rates for buildings initially leased before 2024 range from $1,322 per month for a studio to $1,890 per month for a three-bedroom unit. For buildings initially leased 2024 and later, rates range from $1,400 per month for a studio to $1,999 per month for a three-bedroom unit. Household income must not exceed the maximum limits (for example, $68,840 for a one-person household in FY 2026) and must meet a minimum of 2.5 times the MPDU rent. Housing Choice Vouchers can be used to supplement rental payments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families with moderate incomes seeking affordable rental housing in Rockville.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental of residential units in approved properties throughout the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is limited to Rockville, Maryland. Housing Choice Vouchers must be issued by Rockville Housing Enterprises to be used in Rockville, though vouchers from the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County or other agencies can be ported into Rockville Housing Enterprises.

Applicants must submit MPDU applications through the rental properties

Developers may fulfill requirements through installing art on-site, presenting visual/literary/performing arts on-site, providing arts spaces, providing arts-based infrastructure, or contributing to the City's Art in Public Places Program. The program promotes community welfare by incorporating works of art in private development to preserve character, improve quality of life, reduce the impact of urbanization, and support economic vitality.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program administered through a partnership with Chesapeake Bay Trust that helps Rockville residents and nonprofits reduce stormwater pollution and flooding by installing small-scale stormwater management and water conservation projects on their properties. Eligible improvements include rain gardens, permeable pavers, rain barrels, cisterns, native plantings, tree canopy, green roofs, and impervious pavement removal. The program also provides free educational workshops on stormwater management and free on-site stormwater runoff evaluations.

Green roof: $9 per square foot. Maximum lifetime rebate per property is $5,000. Additionally, free educational workshops on stormwater management and free on-site stormwater runoff evaluations are provided.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program offered by the City of Salisbury to assist businesses within the Main Street District that have been negatively impacted by COVID-19. Each business is eligible for up to $20,000 as a one-time grant award with no repayment required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $20,000 per business as a one-time grant award with no repayment required. Eligible uses include paying employee sick leave for those affected by coronavirus, maintaining payroll during business disruptions, covering increased material costs due to supply chain interruptions, paying past due or future rent or mortgage payments, repaying past due or future obligations, purchasing PPE or safety measures, making building improvements to reduce COVID-19 spread, and purchasing business equipment to expand services in response to COVID-19.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 28 at 11:45 PM
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered businesses in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury that have a physical location in the designated Main Street area of Salisbury and have been negatively impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for providing paid sick leave to employees affected by coronavirus, maintaining payroll and retaining employees during business disruptions, meeting increased costs for materials due to supply chain interruptions, making rent or mortgage payments that are past due or future payments at risk, repaying past due or future obligations, purchasing personal protective equipment or implementing safety measures to reduce COVID-19 spread, making building improvements to reduce COVID-19 spread, purchasing business equipment to expand services in response to COVID-19, or other uses demonstrating how COVID has impacted the business and how funds would support recovery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury within the designated Main Street area. Contact the city to verify if your address is in the approved area.
requirements_list: Must be a registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury
Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury within the designated Main Street area
Must have no pre-existing tax liens or legal judgements prior to March 5
Home-based businesses are not eligible
Churches are not eligible
Banks and financial institutions are not eligible
Investment real-estate entities are not eligible unless applying for payments for a business located in the Main Street area or COVID-related investments on a Main Street property
Food trucks are not eligible
Government agencies are not eligible
Contractors, construction, and service repair-based businesses are not eligible unless applying for COVID-related investments on a Main Street property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application during the open period. Applications will be graded by a committee based on the degree the business has been negatively impacted by COVID-19, how the funds would help the business recover from the negative impacts of COVID-19, and the degree the business contributes to the vitality of the designated Main Street area. Applicants will be notified of award status, and funded businesses must submit proof of receipts and use of funds narrative by the end of April.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant program providing $2,300 to small businesses in Salisbury that were impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and related State Executive Orders. Funds were donated by Delmarva Power and from the City's Revolving Loan Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant award of $2,300 with no repayment due. Award selected through lottery system. Tier 1 applicants (businesses mandated to fully close) receive first priority. If funds remain, Tier 2 applicants (businesses mandated to partially close) enter the lottery. Recipients must complete a disbursement form and provide receipts within 60 days of City approval.
structured_extraction.contact_name: City of Salisbury Office of Business Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in Salisbury with no more than 25 full-time employees that were regulated or impacted by COVID-19 State of Emergency orders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing paid sick leave to employees unable to work due to COVID-19; maintaining payroll and retaining employees during business disruptions or shutdowns; meeting increased costs to obtain materials due to supply chain interruptions; making rent or mortgage payments; repaying obligations that cannot be met due to revenue losses; purchasing personal protective equipment or spending on safety measures to reduce COVID-19 spread.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury within the Revolving Loan Boundary map. Businesses outside the Revolving Loan area that meet other criteria are eligible for lottery funding from Delmarva Power donations.
requirements_list: Registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury
Physical establishment in the City of Salisbury within the Revolving Loan Boundary map
No more than 25 full-time employees as of March 5, 2020
Engaged in activities regulated or impacted by COVID-19 Maryland State of Emergency with required license or permit showing mandated closure
No pre-existing tax liens or legal judgements prior to March 5, 2020

Not a home-based business, church, medical service provider, non-profit, bank, financial institution, investment real estate entity, food truck, national franchise, government agency, or contractor/construction/service repair business
Must demonstrate tangible and immediate need for funding
Must certify funds will be used for stated need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online or by email to the City of Salisbury Office of Business Development. Applications are reviewed by the Director of Business Development, a Finance Department officer, and the Deputy City Administrator for completeness and to verify tangible need. Approved applicants are classified as Tier 1 (mandated fully closed) or Tier 2 (mandated partially closed). Tier 1 applicants enter the lottery first. If funds remain, Tier 2 applicants enter the lottery. Selected awardees receive grant checks via mail and must complete a disbursement form and provide receipts within 60 days.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Conversion from Rental to Homeowner-Occupied Dwelling Tax Abatement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Tax abatement program for residential real property converted from rental use to owner-occupied family residence. The City of Salisbury offers an incentive program for the purchase of rental properties and their conversion to owner-occupied dwellings. City property taxes are fully abated for the first five years, then gradually phased in over subsequent years until the tenth year when full taxes are due. This program helps property owners save money when converting a rental property into their primary residence. Property owners must convert a rental property into their primary residence, resulting in substantial tax savings.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Years 1-5: 100% exemption from city property tax. Year 6: 20% of prevailing residential tax rate. Year 7: 40% of prevailing residential tax rate. Year 8: 60% of prevailing residential tax rate. Year 9: 80% of prevailing residential tax rate. Year 10 and beyond: Full prevailing residential tax rate. Applicant must maintain owner-occupied use for the entire 9-year abatement period or pay back all abated taxes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 annually for annual certification of qualification
structured_extraction.contact_name: Director of Internal Services, City of Salisbury
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual homeowners purchasing rental properties for conversion to owner-occupied family residences within Salisbury city limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction for converted owner-occupied residences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located within corporate limits of City of Salisbury, Maryland, in Wicomico County.
requirements_list: Property must be located within City limits
Property must have been used exclusively as a rental property for at least 3 years immediately prior to conversion
Applicant must purchase with intent to convert to owner-occupied family residence
Applicant must occupy within one year of purchase
Property must be the principal residence of the homeowner
Applicant must maintain owner-occupied status for full 9 years or pay back all abated taxes
Annual certification of qualification required by April 1
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application forms to Director of Internal Services. File certificate of qualification annually by April 1. Maintain agreement obligations throughout 9-year participation.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Owner-Occupied Housing Repair Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury partners with non-profit organizations to provide grants for critical repairs to owner-occupied homes within the city limits. The program helps bring homes into compliance with city codes through repairs to mechanical, electrical, plumbing systems, building components, energy conservation improvements, and lead paint hazard reduction.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $20,000 per property to cover eligible repair costs. A 5-year notice of lien is recorded on the property. After receiving a grant, applicants are not eligible again until the 5-year lien term expires.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-546-1551 (Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County) or 410-543-4626 (Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners living in owner-occupied homes within the City of Salisbury corporate limits with household incomes below 80% of Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for repairs that bring the house into compliance with city codes, including repair or replacement of defective mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems; defective building components and surfaces; energy conservation activities; lead paint hazard reduction; accessibility improvements for disabled persons; and general property improvements of a non-luxury nature.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be within the City of Salisbury corporate limits. Properties located in a floodway are not eligible.
requirements_list: Household gross income must be below 80% of Area Median Income based on household size
Applicant must own the property in fee simple, as joint tenants, or tenants by their entireties (not tenants in common)
At least one owner on the deed must reside in the property
All mortgage payments must be current for the previous three months
All property taxes and city-issued invoices must be current
Applicant must be free of tax liens or judgments
Any bankruptcies must have been discharged for a minimum of 2 years
Property must have clear title
Applicant must insure the property for the entire loan term
Properties in the 100-year flood plain must have flood insurance
Owner-occupants must not own any other house and must not have substantial assets enabling them to secure rehabilitation funds elsewhere
A 5-year Notice of Lien must be signed and recorded
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact either Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County or Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services for application information and to discuss eligibility. Both organizations administer the application and award process on behalf of the City of Salisbury.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Summer Youth Employment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A paid 8-week summer employment opportunity for high school students in Salisbury (entering grades 10-12) to work in various City of Salisbury departments while gaining workforce readiness and career-specific skills. The program combines structured employment with on-the-job training, mentoring from Junior Achievement volunteers, resume development, and soft skills training. Participants work up to 28 hours per week and earn wages while gaining practical job experience and career knowledge.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive paid employment working up to 28 hours per week for 8 weeks (June 22 - August 14, 2026). Program includes on-the-job training, mentoring, resume writing assistance, and soft skills development through collaboration with Junior Achievement volunteers. Participants earn wages while gaining work experience and career-specific skills in City departments.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for Summer 2026 are now closed. Applications for Summer 2027 will open in January
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students entering grades 10-12 for the 2026/2027 academic year enrolled in Wicomico County school district seeking summer employment and career development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants gain work experience, job skills training, resume writing, soft skills development, and career guidance through paid employment in City of Salisbury departments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must be currently enrolled in the Wicomico County school district. Residency in the City of Salisbury is preferred but not required. Program serves Salisbury and surrounding areas in Wicomico County.
requirements_list: Students must be entering 10th-12th grade for the 2026/2027 academic year
Must be currently enrolled in the Wicomico County school district

Must provide 2 forms of updated identification (birth certificate, social security card, current student ID or state-issued ID)

Applicants must provide required identification documents and obtain a work permit by the specified deadline. Contact the City of Salisbury Community Relations Division at 410-341-9550 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) – Entitlement Communities
structured_extraction.program_description: The CDBG Program provides annual grants to entitled metropolitan cities and urban counties to fund community and economic development activities directed toward neighborhood revitalization, economic development, and improved community facilities and services. The program supports activities that benefit low and moderate income persons, prevent or eliminate slums and blight, or meet other urgent community development needs. Local communities determine which activities to fund based on their own needs and priorities, as long as activities meet national objectives and eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual formula-based grants to entitled cities and counties. For program year 2021, the City of Salisbury received $399,903 in total CDBG funds, with $70,000 for administrative costs and $329,903 for program and project funds. No more than 20 percent of the grant can be spent for planning and administrative costs, and no more than 15 percent can be spent for public service activities. The maximum amount any applicant may seek in any competitive funding round is $150,000. Funds are awarded on a reimbursement basis only.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entitled metropolitan cities and urban counties; non-profit organizations registered as 501(c)(3) entities; government agencies; low and moderate income persons; local communities seeking to implement neighborhood revitalization, economic development, and community facility improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and clearance of real property; public improvements and facilities such as senior centers, recreation centers, and day care centers; public services including child care, health care, job training, education programs, recreation, drug abuse counseling, and services for the homeless; relocation assistance; rehabilitation of residential, commercial, industrial, and nonprofit buildings; historic preservation; lead-based paint hazard evaluation and reduction; code enforcement; assistance to micro-enterprises; homeownership assistance; urban renewal completion; technical assistance to increase capacity of public and private nonprofit organizations; assistance to institutions of higher education; and program administration costs related to planning and execution of CDBG-funded activities. Activities must benefit persons of low and moderate income, aid in prevention or elimination of slums and blight, or meet other community development needs of particular urgency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Salisbury, Maryland and other entitled metropolitan cities and urban counties.
requirements_list: Each activity must be eligible under CDBG guidelines

Each activity must meet one of the following national objectives: benefit to persons of low and moderate income; aid in the prevention or elimination of slums and blight; or meet other community development needs of a particular urgency
Non-profit subrecipients must be registered 501(c)(3) organizations and must provide supporting documentation confirming this status
Any capital project proposed on property not held by the subrecipient must include written approval by the property owner
Subrecipients requesting funds for community services must be either developing a new public service or proposing a quantifiable increase in service for an existing program
No more than 20 percent of the grant (plus program income) can be spent for planning and administrative costs
No more than 15 percent of the grant (plus program income received during the preceding program year) can be spent for public service activities
The maximum amount any applicant may seek in any competitive funding round is $150,000
Applicants must have sufficient operating funds available to expend on project expenses before reimbursement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Activities are initiated and developed at the local level based on community perception of local needs and priorities. Eligible non-profit community groups or organizations may apply for either a public service or a capital grant. All applicants must submit supporting documentation confirming 501(c)(3) status and provide copies of paid invoices, cancelled checks, and any other requested documentation. Funds are awarded on a reimbursement basis, so applicants must expend funds on project expenses, provide documentation to the City, and then wait to be reimbursed for those expenditures. Each entitlement grantee receiving CDBG funds determines which activities to fund as long as certain eligibility requirements and national objectives are met.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides property tax credits and state income tax credits to businesses that locate, expand, or substantially improve properties within the designated Salisbury Enterprise Zone area in Wicomico County. The property tax credit reduces local property taxes for qualifying commercial real estate improvements over ten years, starting at 80% for the first five years then decreasing by 10% annually to 30% in the tenth year. The income tax credit is based on hiring new employees, offering a one-time $1,000 credit per non-disadvantaged employee or up to $3,000 for economically disadvantaged employees in the first year, $2,000 in the second year, and $1,000 in the third year of employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Real Property Credit provides a ten-year credit against local property taxes, equaling 80% of the difference between base property value and newly assessed value after improvements. Credit is 80% for the first five years, then declines 10% annually (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%). Minimum capital investment of $50,000 required. The State Income Tax Credit is based on new employees hired: non-disadvantaged employees qualify for a one-time $1,000 credit per employee; economically disadvantaged employees can receive up to $3,000 in the first year, $2,000 in the second year, and $1,000 in the third year of employment. Personal property tax credit available only in Focus Area Zones. Tax credits automatically apply to property tax bills or are claimed when filing business entity tax returns.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 31st (for property tax credit eligibility to take effect following tax year beginning July 1)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, developers, and property owners that are locating, expanding, or substantially improving commercial properties within the Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements to commercial real estate property, including new construction, rehabilitation, and machinery and equipment. Funds support the hiring of new employees. Reduces property and state income taxes for businesses in the enterprise zone.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must have property located within the designated Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone eligible area in Wicomico County, Maryland. Specifically includes the Salisbury Enterprise Zone. The Enterprise Zone was established December 15, 1982 and covers the Salisbury city area and portions of Wicomico County. A zone map is available to identify eligible areas.
requirements_list: Locate or expand within an eligible enterprise zone
Apply and receive approval
Business property must be located in the designated Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone
For Real Property Credit: minimum capital investment of $50,000 required
For Real Property Credit: only commercial properties qualify; no residential use portions may receive credit
For Real Property Credit: applicant must obtain base assessment before commencing work
For Real Property Credit: application must be submitted prior to project completion and issuance of occupancy permits
For Real Property Credit: local Zone Administrator must certify eligibility by December 31st for credit to apply to next taxable year beginning July 1
For Income Tax Credit: business must hire two or more qualifying new employees
For Income Tax Credit: employees must be hired after Enterprise Zone designation date or business relocation date, whichever is later
For Income Tax Credit: employees must work at least 35 hours per week for at least six months
For Income Tax Credit: employees must be paid at least 150% of federal minimum wage
For Income Tax Credit: employees must spend at least half working hours in the Enterprise Zone or on activities directly resulting from business location in zone
For Income Tax Credit: employees must be new hires or rehired after more than one year of layoff
Completed Enterprise Zone Application
Meet program eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download and submit the Enterprise Zone Application or apply through the online application portal. Complete the application form and submit to the Business Development Specialist. You will receive a letter acknowledging receipt of your application. 2. The Zone Administrator reviews the application and forwards it to appropriate State entities for approval. 3. If eligible, you will receive a letter confirming Enterprise Zone certification from the City of Salisbury. Keep this letter as proof of certification. 4. For Real Property Tax Credit, the tax credit automatically appears on your property tax bill either at the start of the next fiscal year or after the next assessment cycle. For State Income Tax Credits, claim them when filing your business entity tax returns. Review Enterprise Zone Benefits document for specific tax credit details and eligibility criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps property owners in Downtown Salisbury connect to Maryland Broadband's high-speed fiber internet service that runs along Main Street. The program reimburses eligible construction costs for bringing fiber into private properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available in amounts not to exceed $2,500 and are made on a reimbursement basis only. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis until funds run out for the fiscal year. The program is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and tenants (with owner approval) located in Downtown Salisbury within the eligible historic district area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction costs of bringing high-speed fiber into the private property and ending at the termination point where the modem will be located.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The property must be located within Downtown Salisbury, specifically in the Salisbury Historic District, using existing conduits that have been abutted to buildings as part of the Main Street project. The City of Salisbury historic district boundaries are shown on the attached map. The eligible area encompasses specific neighborhoods and streets within Salisbury city limits as identified on the historic district map.

Applicant must use a licensed contractor to perform the work
Approval from the Historic District is required if necessary

Grant amount does not exceed $2,500
Construction costs cannot be passed along to those using the service

If the project has already been completed, submit copies of all receipts and paid invoices. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax exemption program that provides relief from personal property taxes for machinery, equipment, and tools used in manufacturing or research and development operations in Salisbury. Eligible businesses that locate, expand, or develop new products in the city can apply for exemptions lasting up to five years.

The exemption is granted for a specific year in which equipment was purchased and can be for a term up to a maximum of five years. Exemptions must be approved by the City of Salisbury Council. structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that own and operate manufacturing or research and development facilities in Salisbury, or those expanding operations or developing new products in the city
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The exemption applies to personal property taxes on machinery, equipment, and tools used in manufacturing or research and development operations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Salisbury, Maryland (Wicomico County). Equipment must be used at a manufacturing or research and development operation located in Salisbury.
requirements_list: Equipment must be owned and operated by a facility that either locates in Salisbury, expands operations in Salisbury, or develops a new product or industrial process in Salisbury
To qualify for the maximum five-year exemption term, the application must be received within two years from December 31st of the calendar year in which the equipment was purchased
Exemption approval requires City of Salisbury Council approval; exemption from Wicomico County does not automatically grant exemption from the City of Salisbury

Mail applications to Finance Department, 125 North Division Street, Salisbury, MD 21801-4940. All exemptions require approval by the City of Salisbury Council.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for public safety officers (firefighters, paramedics, police officers, and volunteers) and those with service-related disabilities who own residential property in Salisbury. The credit reduces the City's real property tax on the primary residence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit of up to $2,500 applied to the City real property tax on a primary residence. The credit may not exceed the amount of real property tax imposed on the dwelling. The credit is available for one taxable year and must be renewed annually by reapplying before April 1.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought. Applications filed after April 1 are treated as applications for the next succeeding taxable year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time firefighters, paramedics, and police officers employed by the City of Salisbury Fire Department or Police Department with at least one year of employment; active volunteer firefighters meeting service requirements; individuals with service-related disabilities; retired public safety officers in good standing; and volunteer firefighters with more than 20 years of active service who are lifetime members.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Salisbury, Maryland. The property must be the primary residence of the applicant.
requirements_list: Must be employed full-time as a firefighter, paramedic, or police officer by the City of Salisbury with at least one year of employment, OR be an active volunteer firefighter meeting service requirements, OR have a service-related disability, OR be retired in good standing, OR be a volunteer firefighter with more than 20 years of active service and lifetime membership status
Must own the property to which the credit will be applied
