Must provide supporting documentation such as current paystub, letter of retirement or separation, or letter evidencing volunteer status
Must not have received a real property tax credit under Title 9 of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland for the same property
Must file application on or before April 1 of the year immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Public Safety Tax Credit Application form providing property information, applicant details, and public safety officer designation. Select the applicable officer category (full-time firefighter/EMT, full-time paramedic, full-time police officer, active volunteer firefighter, service-related disability, retired, or 20+ year volunteer) and submit supporting documentation. Certify under penalties of perjury that all information is true and complete. File the application with the City of Salisbury Finance Department on or before April 1 of the year immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit program that allows restaurants to set up temporary outdoor dining areas to serve customers during limited indoor capacity periods. The program provides approval for extended outdoor service spaces under state guidelines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city provides approval for restaurants to establish temporary outdoor dining areas at no application fee. structured_extraction.program_description: A revolving loan fund program designed to aid in the revitalization of Downtown Salisbury by fostering the growth of new businesses and assisting expanding businesses. The program provides financing to eligible businesses, entrepreneurs, and organizations located within designated areas of Salisbury to support business development, growth, new business startups, and expansion and renovation projects. The program aims to improve the physical appearance of commercial and mixed-use buildings, increase the tax base, provide goods and services to residents, preserve historically significant structures, and address code deficiencies. Revolving loans of up to $100,000 are offered for professional engineering/architectural assistance, renovation of building exteriors and interiors, and purchase/renovation of equipment or machinery within the designated Revolving Loan Fund boundary area and other eligible zones in Salisbury.

Loans cannot be used for start-up costs, working capital, refinancing fees, access streets/roads, parking areas, utility extensions, or activities inconsistent with historic district guidelines. Applicants must demonstrate personal financial investment in the project, provide evidence of committed financing, and show how the business will benefit the city. Applicants must submit a Revolving Loan Fund Application, Personal Financial Statement, and meet program requirements as outlined in the guidelines. Specific loan terms, interest rates, and repayment schedules are detailed in the program guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water Incentive Program provides financial assistance to eligible households to help pay their water and sewer bills. Eligible households may receive one payment per year in an amount up to $2,000 towards their water and/or sewer bills (or up to $1,000 if the property has a leak). Households not receiving these benefits must have total household income not exceeding 60% of State Median Income.

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County offers property tax credits to businesses that create at least ten full-time jobs locally or are new to the county and operating in targeted industries. The credits apply to both real and personal property and are granted for five to ten years depending on the number of jobs created. Companies can receive up to $100,000 in total tax credits based on job creation levels. The credit is based on the number of jobs created: for 10-15 jobs, $5,000 per year for 5 years ($25,000 total); for 16-25 jobs, $8,000 per year for 8 years ($64,000 total); for 26 or more jobs, $10,000 per year for 10 years ($100,000 total). The credit applies to existing structures and can also provide a 50% reduction on county property taxes for new capital investments. If a business leases rather than owns its building, the credit goes to the building owner with an agreement to pass savings to the tenant creating the jobs. The program supports private businesses starting or growing in St. Mary's County, with particular focus on targeted industries, specific locations, and underserved areas.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps homeowners ages 55 and older make accessibility improvements to their homes to support aging in place. Improvements include widening doorways for wheelchairs, adding grab bars in bathrooms, installing first-floor bathrooms and showers, adding ramps, changing door and sink hardware to lever-style handles, and adding bedrooms and bathrooms on the main level to allow seniors to remain safely in their own homes. The program also supports low and moderate-income families with home rehabilitation, energy conservation, and lead hazard reduction. Essential home repairs may also be funded if the homeowner does not qualify for the accessibility-focused program. The program provides zero percent interest deferred loans with no payments for 30 years for eligible seniors, and loans with interest rates based on household income for low and moderate-income families. Average loans are anticipated to be around $10,000 to $15,000 with no set loan limit. Upon the end of the 30-year term, if the homeowner is unable to repay, the State can extend the deferral period. The loan becomes payable only when the house is sold or transferred. If transferred to a family member and the original owner still resides there as their primary residence, repayment is not triggered. If the spouse continues to live there after the original borrower's death, deferral continues. If a child occupies the home as their principal residence after the original borrower's death, the loan does not become due at that time, though the interest rate may increase if the child's income exceeds certain limits. If the property is refinanced with cash out, the loan must be repaid in full. If refinancing with no cash out, immediate repayment is not required. It is available through all 19 local Area Offices on Aging statewide in Maryland and the Frederick County Division of Housing.

If the property is refinanced with cash out, the loan must be repaid in full. If refinancing with no cash out, immediate repayment is not required. Loans can be extended beyond the 30-year term if the homeowner is unable to repay. Payments may be structured as a lump sum at the end of the deferral period or as monthly payments at the homeowner's request.

structured_extraction.program_name: Helping Empower Area Resources Together (HEART) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant program designed to help nonprofit organizations in Frederick County that have been impacted by the federal government shutdown. The program provides emergency funding to support organizations that deliver essential services and resources to vulnerable populations in the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $50,000 to eligible nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations. Award amounts are based on 10% of the nonprofit organization's annual operating budget for fiscal year 2026, not to exceed $50,000. Funds are provided as a lump sum after grant agreements are executed. Awards can be used for operational expenses resulting from revenue gaps or service increases, or to expand essential direct services to Frederick County residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations serving Frederick County residents that have been impacted by the federal government shutdown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operational expenses resulting from revenue gaps or shortfalls caused by the shutdown, operational expenses resulting from increased demand for services, or expansion of essential direct services to Frederick County residents. Costs must be reasonable and incurred during the grant period and not reimbursed by other County, State, or Federal grants or restricted donations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must have a physical location in Frederick County and serve a majority (over 51%) of Frederick County residents.
requirements_list: Has a physical location or address in Frederick County and serves over 51% of Frederick County residents
Is in good standing with the Internal Revenue Service, the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation's Personal Property Tax Division, and Frederick County Government
Was established prior to July 1, 2022 and plans to continue operating through at least June 30, 2026
Is a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization (not under an umbrella or fiscal sponsor)
Is not a church, religious organization, fraternal or civic organization, homeowner's association, labor union, private/political/public foundation, cemetery, or volunteer fire department
Can demonstrate impact from the federal government shutdown such as decreased revenue, increased costs, or financial insecurity
Delivers direct services and resources to Frederick County residents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Foundant online grant portal. Applicants must provide a finalized budget with actual revenue and expenditures for the last two fiscal years and year-to-date current fiscal year, proof of good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, IRS Nonprofit Designation Letter, financial statements for the immediate past year, and the most recent IRS Form 990 or E-Postcard. A review committee evaluates applications based on completeness, organizational need, community benefit, and budget size, then recommends awards to the County Executive for final approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Choice Voucher Program provides rental assistance to eligible low-income households to enable them to afford housing in the private rental market. Qualified families receive long-term individual vouchers for federally funded rental housing assistance to rent private market properties. The program provides variable rent subsidies to qualified tenants based on their family income. Families pay approximately 30% to 40% of their income towards rent and utilities, and the monthly subsidy portion is paid directly to the landlord on behalf of the tenant. Units are inspected and families are recertified annually.

The housing agency pays the monthly subsidy portion of the contract rent directly to the landlord on behalf of the tenant. structured_extraction.program_description: A free energy assessment and home improvement program for low- to moderate-income households in Frederick County. The program provides a professional energy audit performed by a certified contractor to identify energy-saving opportunities and performs weatherization and efficiency upgrades at no cost to homeowners. Eligible improvements include air sealing, insulation, window and door weatherization, duct sealing, energy-efficient lighting, heat pump water heater replacements, HVAC system tune-ups or upgrades, and up to $1,500 for necessary health and safety repairs related to implementing energy improvements.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a free energy audit performed by a certified contractor and funds eligible home energy-saving improvements at no cost to the homeowner. Eligible projects include air sealing and insulation, window and door weatherization, duct sealing, energy-efficient lighting, heat pump water heater replacements, HVAC system tune-ups or upgrades, and up to $1,500 for necessary health and safety repairs related to implementing energy improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income Frederick County residents who own single-family homes, condominiums, mobile homes, or rental properties and are registered participants in Frederick County's Green Homes Challenge.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-saving home improvements including air sealing, insulation, weatherization, HVAC upgrades, water heater replacements, and necessary health and safety repairs related to energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland. Applicants must be Frederick County residents.
requirements_list: Applicant must be Frederick County resident
Applicant must be low- or moderate-income
Must be registered in Frederick County's Green Homes Challenge
Gross household income must be less than 85% of median income for Frederick County based on family size (ranging from $68,500 for 1 person to $129,100 for 8 people)
Homeowners in condominiums, mobile homes, and rental properties should contact the PSR Coordinator to discuss eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application through the county website (preferred) or request a print application by calling 301-600-1416 or emailing PSR@FrederickCountyMD.gov. Applications are reviewed for eligibility. If approved, a certified contractor schedules an energy audit appointment. A list of approved projects is reviewed with the homeowner before work begins. Home improvements are then performed.

The tax credit applies to property taxes based on rehabilitation and reconstruction improvements to vacant commercial structures, with the tax credit applied to property tax bills for qualified improvements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 30th (for tax credit to be applied on following Fiscal Year's tax bill mailed July 1)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners of vacant commercial structures in Frederick County and City of Frederick, Maryland.

Services include gap filling service dollars for eligible individuals and in-home aide services to assist with activities of daily living. In-home aides provide services such as bathing, dressing, meal preparation, chore services, and homemaker services. A case manager helps locate, arrange, and ensure individuals receive needed services at the right time.

A case manager helps locate and arrange for services and ensures individuals receive needed services at the right time. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Use a licensed pumping company from the permitted haulers list. 2. Complete an application using either the online application (preferred) or a printable application submitted by email or postal service. 5. Include required documentation: an invoice from a licensed pumping company and proof of payment.

Participants receive a monthly allotment of taxi funds loaded onto a reloadable card with photo ID, and pay a discounted zip code-based fare while the county covers the remainder.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly taxi fare subsidy provided through a reloadable swipe card. In zip codes 21701, 21702, and 21703, the county pays $60 monthly (customer pays $10). In all other Frederick County zip codes, the county pays $120 monthly (customer pays $20). Up to three months of funds can be stored on the card. Participants can draw funds in $5 or $10 increments for flexibility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors age 60 and older and people with disabilities who are registered with the Transit-plus program and have scheduled or attempted to schedule at least three Transit-plus rides within a month.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Taxi transportation services within Frederick County on weekdays and weekends based on taxi availability.

Once qualified and after meeting the three-ride requirement, eligible users receive a reloadable swipe card with photo ID. Funds are loaded monthly based on home zip code. To load fare online, visit the TAP fare website at eztransport.net/fred/members/.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial subsidy program that helps new vanpools get started by covering the cost of empty seats during their first year of operation. Eligible vanpools receive monthly subsidies based on vehicle size and the number of unfilled seats, with higher subsidies in months 1-6 and reduced subsidies in months 7-12. The subsidy amount decreases as more people join the vanpool. The program is designed for employees who commute 30 miles or more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly financial subsidy for unfilled vanpool seats during the first 12 months of operation. Subsidy amounts vary by vehicle size and operating period. For months 1-6: 15-passenger van up to $500/month, 13-passenger van up to $450/month, 12-passenger van up to $433/month, 10-passenger van up to $377/month, 9-passenger van up to $338/month, 8-passenger van up to $300/month, 7-passenger van up to $263/month. For months 7-12: amounts reduced to $300, $270, $260, $226, $200, $180, and $158 respectively. Per-seat subsidy calculated by dividing total eligible operating expenses (lease cost and gasoline) by available seating positions (excluding driver), then multiplied by number of unfilled seats. The subsidy decreases as more people join the vanpool.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and vanpool operators in Frederick County who commute 30 miles or more and are interested in forming new vanpools or joining existing vanpool routes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly subsidy to help vanpools cover operating expenses (lease costs and gasoline) for empty seats during the first year of operation while the vanpool fills up.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Vanpools starting in Frederick County with routes serving Frederick County and surrounding areas including Washington DC, Maryland suburbs (Bethesda, Rockville, Gaithersburg), and Virginia destinations (Fort Belvoir, Manassas).
requirements_list: Vanpool must be in first 12 months of operation
Eligible vanpools include owner-operated vans, third-party vendor vans, and employer-provided vans
Subsidy based on actual unfilled seats in the vanpool vehicle
Subsidy limited to months 1-6 and months 7-12 with different maximum amounts
Must commute 30 miles or more
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Frederick County Transit Services to inquire about vanpool formation assistance and eligibility for the incentive program. Transit Services will assist new and existing vanpools in finding riders and can explain the financial subsidy application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Commercial & Industrial Business Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A ten-year real property tax credit for businesses conducting manufacturing, fabricating, or assembling operations with a total new investment of at least $5 million and at least 25 new jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage. The credit is applied to reduce the amount of property tax owed on the value of new improvements, with County Council approval required if the average credit over 10 years exceeds 60% of the new tax amount.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: A ten-year real property tax credit for qualifying manufacturing, fabricating, or assembling operations. The credit is a percentage of the new property tax that results from building or expanding a facility. County Council must approve if the average credit over 10 years exceeds 60% of the new tax amount.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to real property taxes on new improvements.

Total new investment of at least $5 million
Create at least 25 new permanent jobs
Pay wages at least 150% of the federal minimum wage
New positions may not be transferred from another location in Frederick County

Next, you must apply with the County Treasurer by October 1 of the first tax year your facility is eligible. structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A twelve-year tax credit for businesses that expand by at least 250,000 square feet and create a minimum number of new jobs. The credit applies to property tax increases on the new or expanded premises and substantially renovated adjoining or neighboring real property. This program is for businesses that are already in Frederick County or are moving to the county from outside of Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A twelve-year credit equal to 58.5% of the property tax imposed on the increase in assessment of the new or expanded premises and any substantially renovated adjoining or neighboring real property (where renovation is at least 50% of each building).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses undertaking large-scale expansion projects in Frederick County, including businesses already established in the county or relocating from outside Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to property taxes on the new or expanded premises and substantially renovated adjacent properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland, specifically in Priority Funding Areas.
requirements_list: Expand by at least 250,000 square feet
Create a minimum number of new jobs
Property renovation must involve complete renovation of at least 50% of each building on the property
Must be established in Frederick County or relocate to the county from outside Maryland

Must create at least 1,250 full-time permanent jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage, or alternatively create at least 2,500 full-time jobs and add 500 more positions, all paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage
Must inform the County's Director of Finance about your plan to claim the credit before you begin the expansion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the Frederick County Office of Economic Development. Then, you must notify the County's Director of Finance that you intend to claim the credit before your expansion begins.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County New Jobs Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a tax credit on real property to businesses that construct or expand by at least 5,000 square feet in a priority funding area and create at least 25 full-time jobs within the first two years of expansion. The tax credit on the increased value of real property decreases over six years: 52% for years one and two, 39% for years three and four, and 26% for years five and six.

The credit applies to real property taxes related to the new or expanded premises.

Create at least 25 full-time jobs within first two years of expansion
Locate in a priority funding area
Undertake new construction only
Must be established in Frederick County or relocate to the county from outside Maryland
Must maintain the 25 full-time permanent positions for three years after each year a tax credit is allowed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the Frederick County Office of Economic Development. Before you expand, you must notify the County's Director of Finance of your intent to claim the credit.

Application must be filed on or before October 1 of the first eligible tax year; annual reapplication required

structured_extraction.program_description: A cooperative group buying program that leverages collective purchasing power to reduce costs for residents and small business owners installing solar panels, battery storage, electric vehicle chargers, or heat pumps. The program is available in multiple Maryland jurisdictions including Frederick County, Rockville, Montgomery County, and the City of Annapolis, and is part of the broader MD-VA-DC regional cooperative purchasing network. Participants can purchase or lease rooftop solar systems and renewable energy components at discounted cooperative pricing approximately 20% lower than typical market rates. A typical solar project is expected to save at least $6,500 on purchase and installation. The program conducts reverse auctions with pre-vetted contractors to secure group discounts. Participants register for free without obligation and can place a 100% refundable deposit to lock in contracts. Leasing and financing options are available for all income levels. Low- to moderate-income households may qualify for the Maryland Solar Access Grant Program offering up to $7,500 per system.

structured_extraction.program_description: Garrett County Government offers subsidies for bringing broadband service to difficult-to-serve addresses in Garrett County. The program helps residents whose quoted price to receive broadband service to their home is out of their budget. The program provides subsidies to pay a portion or all of the customer contribution requested by an internet service provider for broadband connection to underserved addresses. All payments are made directly to the internet service provider. Customers may be asked to contribute up to 10 percent of the requested subsidy amount if possible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides subsidies to pay a portion or all of the customer contribution requested by an internet service provider for broadband connection to underserved addresses. All payments are made directly to the internet service provider. Customers may be asked to contribute up to 10 percent of the requested subsidy amount if possible. Program funding and funding per project are limited. Internet service providers must also contribute to each project and participate in the Affordable Connectivity Program to qualify. Only valid expenses directly related to connecting a customer to broadband service are eligible. Direct customer expenses cannot be paid or reimbursed.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Business Property Tax Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for new and expanding businesses in Garrett County that make improvements to business property. The program provides a tax credit against the county's portion of real property tax on improvements for five years, starting at 50% of the assessed value of improvements and decreasing by 10% each year to 10% in the final year. Businesses that locate or expand facilities in Garrett County can reduce their county real estate tax burden through this property tax incentive. The credit is calculated on the net assessment increase from qualifying improvements and applies only to County real estate tax, not State or municipal property tax levies. Credits cannot be combined with enterprise zone credits to exceed 100% total relief.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that enables local jurisdictions to implement or support an established Day Reporting Center providing highly structured, non-residential community-based services and treatment to non-violent individuals under pretrial, probation, or parole supervision, or as an alternative to incarceration. Participants live at home and report to the center regularly, often daily. Services include counseling, cognitive behavioral therapy, drug treatment, educational remediation, job training, workforce development, job placement, behavioral healthcare, and intensive supervision. The program aims to reduce recidivism, jail and prison populations, and corrections-related costs by offering structured community-based alternatives to incarceration.

Award period: July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. No match required. Funds are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded grant program administered by Maryland's Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy that provides funding to protect the lives of law enforcement officers through procurement of protective body armor and stab-resistant vests. The program assists local law enforcement agencies in procuring protective body armor and stab resistant vests for their officers, and allows replacement of protective body armor if testing or age indicates a need for replacement. structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding to purchase and procure body armor and stab resistant vests conforming to National Institute of Justice (NIJ) standards for sworn law enforcement officers only; not for civilian personnel or anticipated new hires. structured_extraction.program_name: Child Sex Trafficking Screening and Services Act Regional Navigator Program (RGNV)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that expands regional navigator services to help identify and assist child victims of sex trafficking and labor trafficking. Regional navigators provide screening and services to comply with Maryland's Child Sex Trafficking Screening and Services Act of 2019, which requires law enforcement and local Departments of Social Services to notify a Regional Navigator when they have reason to believe a child is a victim of sex trafficking or labor trafficking. Grantees must coordinate and/or provide services for suspected child sex or labor trafficking victims until the child reaches age 24. The program provides funding to support regional navigator services through contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, supplies, training, and other eligible costs to help establish resources throughout eligible jurisdictions to assist victims in achieving self-sufficiency, improving victim safety, and ensuring victims are aware of their rights and resources.

Up to $1,750,000 in total RNPG-State grant funding available for up to eight awards ranging from $50,000 to $200,000 (single jurisdiction) or up to $500,000 (multiple jurisdictions). Continuation funding available at SFY 2024 levels for previously funded programs. Funds support personnel costs, operating expenses, contractual services, equipment, training and professional development, direct victim services (medical accompaniment, mental health assistance, legal assistance, forensic interviews, family engagement activities, educational opportunities, drug abuse assistance/rehabilitation programs), public awareness activities, and coordination activities.

structured_extraction.program_description: COAP provides funding to support comprehensive opioid, stimulant, and substance use interventions at specific service sites and through broader initiatives. The program responds to illicit substance use and misuse, reduces overdose deaths, promotes public safety, and supports access to prevention, harm-reduction, treatment, and recovery services. The program supports implementation of the Law Enforcement Assisted Diversion (LEAD) program, which works with law enforcement to provide diversion options for low-level offenses among people with mental illness or substance use disorders. COAP focuses on short-term funding for expansion of existing programs rather than development of new programs. The program aims to reduce opioid overdose deaths while increasing access to care and treatment through police and detention-based referrals, utilizing harm reduction approaches and collaboration between public safety and public health agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding is provided to support comprehensive opioid, stimulant, and substance use site-based interventions, including implementation and expansion of substance use disorder treatment, harm reduction, prevention, recovery services, and Law Enforcement Assisted Diversion programs. Up to $894,500 total available for FY 2026 with up to 8 awards anticipated. Minimum request: $50,000. Maximum request: $150,000. Funds can be used for personnel (salaries, case managers, peer specialists, treatment providers, data analysts, fringe benefits), operating expenses (rent, communication, postage), travel (program-related meetings, trainings, mileage), contractual services (behavioral health, case management, substance use treatment), equipment (mobile response units, telehealth infrastructure, jail-based medical equipment with unit cost ≥$10,000), and other eligible costs (Naloxone, medications, laptops, tablets, software licensure with unit cost <$10,000). Reimbursement is quarterly based on actual expenditures. Fringe benefits may not exceed 30% of salary costs without prior approval. Indirect costs may use negotiated rate or 15% de minimis rate if eligible. Services include case management and care coordination, medication-assisted treatment (MAT), behavioral health enrollment, medical insurance connection, housing and transportation assistance, mental and physical health support, peer support, reentry support and planning, financial assistance vouchers, courtroom support/advocacy, ID paperwork assistance, hygiene kits, insurance assistance, wound care, overdose prevention training, naloxone distribution, and community outreach.

Target populations include individuals with opioid/substance use disorders, justice-involved individuals, individuals at risk of arrest for diversion-eligible offenses, historically underserved and marginalized populations, women, children, families, LGBTQ+ communities, racial and ethnic minorities, homeless individuals, youth, and individuals self-referring for help.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Specific programs currently operate in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Calvert, Carroll, Harford, and St. Mary's Counties, with statewide coverage through the Maryland Office of the Public Defender. Additional coverage includes Baltimore City, Cecil, Frederick, and Washington Counties through various local implementations.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) is released in August with applications due in September. Interested government agencies and other eligible applicants should register for the Grant Management System (GMS) and submit applications online according to the NOFA requirements. Signed certified assurances and documentation must be uploaded to GMS by the program-specific NOFA due date. Applications must include organizational information, problem statement/needs justification, project design and implementation strategy, goals and objectives, data collection plan, qualifications of implementing agency and key personnel, organizational chart, and required certifications. Referrals for participants are initiated by public defenders, judges, law enforcement, or community providers, with screening conducted by case managers. Draft narrative in word processing program, transfer to Grants Management System (GMS), and submit through GMS portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A remedial program that provides financial assistance to innocent victims of crime in Maryland. The program compensates victims for injuries and losses resulting from criminal acts and serves as the payer of last resort. Compensation covers medical expenses related to physical injury, psychological counseling expenses from certain offenses, loss of earnings directly related to inability to work following the crime, bereavement leave up to 2 weeks or $2,000, total or partial permanent or temporary disability, funeral expenses in the case of homicide, loss of support or dependency when a homicide victim was providing support to the claimant, up to 30 days in lost wages for a parent or guardian caring for a child injured by crime, crime scene cleanup, and other board-approved expenses.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses eligible crime victims for medical and dental expenses related to physical injury, expenses for psychological injury and counseling from certain offenses, loss of earnings directly related to inability to work following the crime, bereavement leave up to 2 weeks or $2,000, total or partial permanent or temporary disability, funeral expenses in the case of homicide, loss of support or dependency when a homicide victim was providing support to the claimant, up to 30 days in lost wages for a parent or guardian caring for a child injured by crime, crime scene cleanup, and other expenses as approved by the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board. Victims must have incurred at least $100 in reimbursable expenses or lost wages to qualify. The Board is the payer of last resort and all other reimbursements must be used before a possible award. To receive lost wages, claimant must have lost at least two continuous weeks' earnings or support, or have more than $100 in other unreimbursed eligible costs. The program does not cover property losses, mileage, lock changes, relocation, childcare, or emotional distress compensation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within three (3) years from the date of the crime or discovery of the crime. Crime must be reported to authorities within 48 hours unless good cause is shown. In cases of child abuse, must file within three years of the date the claimant knew or should have known of the abuse. Exceptions may apply for terrorist acts.

Applicant must be at least 18 years of age to apply.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Victims submit an Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions. structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides law enforcement with resources to meet District and Circuit Court guidelines for efficient and timely domestic violence response and serving of protective orders. It is designed to reduce or minimize the time between the issuance of interim and temporary protective orders and their entry into MILES/NCIC databases. The program helps local law enforcement agencies enhance existing service efforts and comply with Family Law Article sections 4-504.1(g) and 4-505(b). It is an institutionalized program that has continued since 2002 despite original statutory termination.

structured_extraction.program_name: Edward J. Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (BJAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program from the United States Department of Justice, Office of Justice Programs, that provides funding to states and local government units for criminal justice initiatives. Funds help reduce gaps in services that impact violent crime, crime victims, enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, and rehabilitation. The program supports a broad range of state and local criminal justice initiatives critical to effective criminal justice, including law enforcement programs, prosecution and court programs, prevention and education programs, corrections and community corrections programs, drug treatment and enforcement programs, planning/evaluation/technology improvement programs, crime victim and witness programs, and mental health programs and related law enforcement and corrections programs. The program aims to improve sentencing and correction policies, reduce crime, provide public safety, protect victims, track DNA, and train local law enforcement. Funds may be used for personnel, training, equipment, contractual support, technologies, and other approved criminal justice purposes. Funds are distributed to eligible organizations through a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) based on BJAG-developed formulas that account for population and crime statistics.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants support various criminal justice initiatives including contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, training, technologies, and other approved uses. Three funding allocations available: General BJAG Formula Funds ($911,378, up to 18 awards of $20,000-$100,000), Local BJAG Formula Funds ($989,469, up to 20 awards of $20,000-$100,000), and Small Jurisdiction BJAG Formula Funds ($99,153, up to 7 awards of $10,000-$40,000), with total funding up to $2,000,000. Funding allocations are based on BJAG-developed formulas that account for population and crime statistics. Funds are distributed to eligible organizations through a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA). Funds are provided on a quarterly reimbursement basis following submission of fiscal and programmatic reports. Specific award amounts and terms are detailed in the NOFA documentation. Permissible expenses include salaries, fringe benefits, overtime, training and technical assistance, equipment (over $10,000 per unit with useful life exceeding one year), contractual services, operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications), travel (mileage, lodging, meals per state rates), technology and operational improvements, data collection and performance measurement, and consultant services (capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day). Funds must supplement existing budget and cannot supplant or replace existing funds.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The agency releases a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) typically in August. Interested applicants should request access to the Grant Management System (GMS) and review application materials and guidelines provided. Applicants must obtain a User ID by August 29, 2025. Applicants submit applications through GMS per guidance issued by BJA, with applications typically due in September by 11:59 PM. The application process includes: completing the Face Sheet with implementing/applicant agency personnel and authorized representative information; submitting a Project Summary (≤100 words); submitting detailed Narrative sections with specific word limits addressing alignment with federal purpose areas and state priorities in outline format with numerical/lettering structure; designating a Fiscal Officer and Civil Rights Contact; identifying service sites with addresses and 9-digit zip codes or statewide/countywide designation; uploading organizational chart and letters of support if applicable; and providing all required certifications and documentation including SAM.gov registration, W-9, and civil rights compliance materials. County governments may authorize the County Executive or designated official to submit applications to the United States Department of Justice, Office of Justice Programs. Applications are reviewed through a three-tier review process including internal staff and external independent reviewers, with final selections based on eligibility, relevance, and merit. Funding is distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis following submission of fiscal and programmatic reports.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides temporary shelter environments and supportive services through a network of local domestic violence services programs. It offers comprehensive services to meet the needs of domestic violence victims and their families, including prevention of family violence, domestic violence, and dating violence; immediate shelter and supportive services for victims and their dependents; and specialized services for children exposed to violence, underserved populations, and victims from racial and ethnic minority populations. Services are delivered locally to increase likelihood that victims will benefit and ensure appropriate linkages to other community-based services, fostering a coordinated community approach that includes partnerships with law enforcement, courts, hospitals, local departments of social services, and other related support agencies.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funds support local law enforcement agencies and prosecutors in developing and implementing strategies specifically intended to reduce gun-related crime in Maryland. The program directly supports the goal of removing illegal firearms from Maryland communities and reinforcing prevention, disruption, and prosecution strategies, addressing the rise of gun violence, illegal distribution, manufacturing, and seizures of firearms. Funded categories include contractual services, equipment (including ballistic technology and gunshot detection systems), personnel, travel, and other expenses related to gun violence reduction initiatives.

Grant funds support contractual services, equipment (including ballistic technology and gunshot detection systems), personnel (salaries, overtime for law enforcement, crime analysts, prosecutors), travel (conferences, training, workshops, per diem), and other expenses related to gun violence reduction initiatives including crime analysis, focused deterrence, targeted enforcement, and firearm-related prosecutions. Operating expenses such as rental space, printing, and communications are also eligible. No cost-share required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to local law enforcement agencies, state law enforcement, and designated child advocacy centers for salaries, training, equipment, and other costs used to investigate and prosecute Internet crimes against children. The program supports the ongoing operations of the Maryland Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force and funds internet crimes against children prevention and prosecution initiatives statewide. The program aims to reduce victimization of Maryland's children by protecting them from abuse or neglect, and addresses Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) and childhood trauma. At least $2 million annually goes to local law enforcement agencies and the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, with up to 25% of funds available for designated child advocacy centers.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to support access to specialized investigative and law enforcement training for criminal justice professionals across Maryland. Advances coordinated criminal justice strategies rooted in collaboration, information sharing, and knowledge transfer. Provides funding for specialized investigative and law enforcement training courses and seminars, including crime scene investigation, laboratory procedures, crime lab certification, data-driven policing strategies, law enforcement information sharing, victim services, witness protection, and investigative techniques. Provides up to $5,000 per recipient to support specialized law enforcement training. Grant funds may be used for non-degree courses and to cover related expenses, including travel, lodging, registration fees, training materials, and in certain cases, bringing trainers directly to a law enforcement agency.

structured_extraction.program_name: Legal Services for Crime Victims Fund (LSCV)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Legal Services for Crime Victims Fund is a grant program authorized by Criminal Procedure Article §11-919 and administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy through the State Board of Victim Services that provides annual funding for legal services to Maryland crime victims. The fund uses money from unclaimed restitution collected by the Division of Parole and Probation and Department of Juvenile Services to award grants that provide legal counsel (defined as legal advice, consultation, or representation by licensed attorneys) to victims of crime and delinquent acts to protect their rights as provided by law. Funding supports contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other eligible categories. Grants are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis, with the total funding amount changing each year based on unclaimed restitution collected. Grants must start on the first day of a month and end on the last day of a month, with a maximum project period of 12 months.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants to provide legal counsel to victims of crimes and delinquent acts. Maximum award not to exceed $75,000 per grant, with total of two (2) awards anticipated for total anticipated funding of $150,000 for statewide legal counsel. Legal counsel defined as legal advice, consultation, or representation provided by a licensed attorney. Funding can support staff attorney and director salaries, fringe benefits (not to exceed 30% of salary without prior approval), operating expenses (rent, communications, postage, printing), travel (mileage, transportation, meals, lodging per Maryland reimbursement rates), contractual services (consultant contracts for training and evaluation at rates capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day unless prior approval obtained), equipment (items with useful life >1 year and cost ≥$10,000), other costs (registration fees, office supplies, indirect costs, equipment <$10,000), supplies and technology systems. Funds are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis. The total funding amount changes each year based on how much unclaimed restitution is collected. Grants must start on the first day of a month and end on the last day of a month, with a maximum project period of 12 months.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Warrant Apprehension & Absconding Grant Program (WAAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program supports law enforcement agencies across Maryland with reducing the number of open warrants, especially warrants for violent crimes, and the apprehension of individuals who have absconded from a court-ordered drug and/or alcohol treatment facility. The program supports improving quality of life and creating safer communities through reduction in violent crime by apprehending wanted individuals, and develops coordinated criminal justice strategies and increases availability of data to support data-driven decisions.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding to eligible local law enforcement agencies on a reimbursable quarterly basis. Total funding anticipated: $1,000,000 for SFY 2026 with up to 30 awards. Individual award amounts: $10,000-$75,000 based on agency size (Small agencies ≤50 sworn officers: up to $30,000; Medium agencies 51-300 sworn officers: up to $50,000; Large agencies >300 sworn officers: up to $75,000). Funded categories include officer overtime to serve warrants and conduct targeted warrant operations; analyst overtime to identify and track wanted or absconded individuals emphasizing violent crime warrants; program administration overtime to support oversight and management of warrant apprehension programs; extradition costs for travel expenses related to execution of extradition warrants; equipment procurement for essential items for safe warrant arrests such as shackles, handcuffs, and protective face masks; contractual services; and other operating expenses including supplies and travel.

structured_extraction.program_name: Markell Hendricks Youth Crime Prevention and Diversion Parole Grant Program (YCPD)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant assistance to local law enforcement agencies for diversion programs or youth engagement programs in high-crime areas throughout Maryland. Focuses on creating outreach and programming designed to divert youth who have committed threshold offenses from formal processing into the juvenile justice system, including youth involved in school-based offenses. Goal is to reduce the number of youth entering the juvenile justice system by providing supportive services within their communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $50,000 available for SFY 2026 with one award anticipated. Intent for two additional years of level funding (SFY 2027-2028) if program is in good standing with positive outcomes. Funds are reimbursed quarterly based on actual expenditures. No cost-sharing requirement. Eligible expenses include personnel (salaries and fringe benefits), operating expenses (rent, communications, postage), travel at State of Maryland rates, contractual services (maximum $81.25/hour or $650/day for consultants), equipment (unit cost $10,000 or more), and supplies and equipment under $10,000. Categories of eligible expenses also include training and education programs, case management services, crisis intervention, group therapy, evidence-based alternatives to incarceration, victim services, and educational opportunities for youth upon re-entry. Indirect costs allowed with negotiated agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-agency coalition of criminal justice agencies that collaborates and coordinates tactics, resources, and intelligence through data sharing and cross-jurisdictional partnerships to identify, disrupt, and dismantle criminal organizations involved in guns, gangs, drugs, and human trafficking. The program develops robust information-sharing infrastructures enabling cross-jurisdictional sharing of accurate and actionable intelligence, supports identification and dismantling of violent criminal networks, and includes initiatives to decrease fatal and non-fatal overdoses stemming from substance use. The program supports improved intelligence infrastructure, data collection strategies, subject matter experts trained to investigate criminal networks, and expert prosecutors to prosecute violent criminals at federal and state levels.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding available to support criminal intelligence network coordination and overdose reduction initiatives. MCIN provides up to 14 awards ranging from $100,000 to $700,000. ODAC provides up to 25 coordinator positions (one per Maryland jurisdiction plus one statewide) with awards ranging from $40,000 to $110,000. Total anticipated funding: $6,623,865. Funds may support personnel salaries for Coordinators, Intelligence/Crime Analysts, MCIN-designated Prosecutors, and ODAC positions; contractual services; equipment; software; travel for conferences, workshops, regional task force meetings, and training; law enforcement overtime for investigative and prosecutorial operations; and other approved expenses. Reimbursement occurs on a quarterly basis. Applicants must register with the Grants Management System to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program that prevents incidents of family violence, domestic violence, and dating violence and meets the needs of all victims and their dependents, including those in underserved communities. The program makes temporary shelter environments and supportive services available through a network of local domestic violence services programs. It provides comprehensive services to meet specific needs of domestic violence victims and their families, and supports establishment, maintenance, and expansion of programs to prevent violence, provide immediate shelter and supportive services, and provide specialized services for children exposed to violence and underserved populations. The program fosters a coordinated community approach that includes partnerships with law enforcement, courts, hospitals, local departments of social services, and other support agencies.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Victims of Crime Fund provides advocacy and support services to victims of crime through the creation of new ideas and the enhancement of existing programs in Maryland. It ensures implementation of the Declaration of Crime Victims' Rights Amendment to the Maryland Constitution and the Federal Guidelines for treatment of and assistance to crime victims and witnesses. State funding is administered by the State Board of Victim Services to provide financial assistance and services to crime victims. The fund was created by the Maryland General Assembly in 1991 to implement Article 47 of Maryland Declaration of Rights and supports child advocacy centers. Grants support contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs related to victim services delivery.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program assists community organizations, nonprofit organizations, and local governments to fund security operations during times of high pedestrian traffic in entertainment districts where a higher than average number of calls for police assistance in response to reported crimes are placed. The program aims to strengthen security in Maryland's entertainment districts through collaborative efforts among local governments, community organizations, and law enforcement by supporting enhanced security and crime prevention activities.

Local governments can request up to $50,000; community organizations and nonprofits can request up to $30,000. Funding is reimbursed quarterly, with monthly reimbursement available for nonprofits with awards over $50,000. Eligible budget categories include contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Performance Incentive Grant Fund provides grants from savings generated by Maryland's Justice Reinvestment Act reforms. The program funds evidence-based strategies to safely reduce the prison population, improve reentry outcomes, reduce impacts of incarceration on communities, provide resources to victims of crime, and connect nonviolent offenders with behavioral health needs to community treatment and support. The program supports a data-driven approach to reduce Maryland's state and local incarcerated population through appropriate diversion, deflection, service provision, and recidivism reduction resources.

structured_extraction.program_name: Police Accountability, Community, and Transparency Grant (PACT)
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant supports law enforcement agencies across Maryland with developing effective accountability procedures to achieve lawfulness and legitimacy while enhancing community relations and transparency. Funds help increase safety and training for law enforcement, promote safe communities, and encourage community engagement between law enforcement and the communities they serve. The program provides support for law enforcement agencies with the development of effective practices related to police accountability, community engagement, and transparency. The program supports three categories: Core Priorities (Accountability, Training, Transparency); High Impact Support Initiatives (Officer Wellness and Community Engagement); and Innovation and Research Initiatives (Emerging Needs and Best Practices). The program was developed to ensure law enforcement agencies can comply with the Maryland Police Accountability Act of 2021 (House Bill 670/Chapter 59, 2021) by July 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide up to 50 awards ranging from $20,000 to $300,000 with anticipated total funding of $4 million. Funds support contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other eligible expenses to support law enforcement agency compliance with Maryland Police Accountability Act requirements and development of effective practices for police accountability, community engagement, and transparency. Funding is reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Eligible uses include hiring staff, training programs, equipment purchases (including body-worn cameras, weapon/holster detection systems, VR simulators), software systems (Early Intervention Systems, Misconduct Databases), mental health services, community engagement initiatives, and research and evaluation efforts.

structured_extraction.program_name: Police Recruitment and Retention Grant Program (PRAR)
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports Maryland law enforcement agencies in developing, implementing, and sustaining evidence-informed strategies to address recruitment and retention challenges for sworn officers. Funds support recruitment modernization (mobile platforms, marketing), retention efforts (bonuses, referral bonuses, service bonuses, degree bonuses, training, health club memberships, uniform allowance, tuition reimbursement, dependent care), personnel costs, equipment, contractual services, and travel. Focuses on modernizing recruitment practices, strengthening workforce pipelines, improving organizational culture and officer wellness, and increasing long-term retention with measurable outcomes and sustainability beyond the grant period.

structured_extraction.program_name: Program for Preventing Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Infection for Rape Victims
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program that provides victims of rape, sexual assault, or child sexual abuse with a full course of non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) treatment and follow-up care to prevent HIV infection. The program covers HIV exposure assessment, nPEP medication regimen, laboratory services, medications, vaccines, sexual assault forensic exam services, and follow-up care. Physicians, qualified healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies are reimbursed through the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund for providing this treatment and care.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses physicians, qualified healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies for providing a full 28-day course of non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) medication, HIV exposure assessment, laboratory services (HIV testing, pregnancy tests, blood panels, STI testing, toxicology), medications (antibiotics, emergency contraception), vaccines, sexual assault forensic exam services, and follow-up care. Medication must begin within 72 hours of the sexual assault. Follow-up care is covered within 180 days of the sexual assault. The total amount paid statewide may not exceed $750,000 annually. The Governor's Office has partnered with Terrapin Pharmacy to provide medication via mail delivery or courier when hospitals cannot provide the full 28-day medication supply. Reimbursement claims must be submitted within 90 days from date of service.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 90 days of the exam or service date

structured_extraction.program_name: Residential Substance Abuse Treatment (RSAT) for State Prisoners Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The RSAT program helps states, local, and tribal governments develop and implement substance use disorder treatment programs in state and local correctional and detention facilities. It targets pre-trial defendants, individuals in correctional facilities, and citizens in need of post-incarceration treatment and community reintegration assistance. The program funds residential treatment services lasting at least 6 months in facilities separate from general prison/jail populations, evidence-based group substance use treatment with trauma-informed approach, integrated treatment for co-occurring substance use disorder and mental health disorders, and Medication Assisted Treatment (MAT) as part of comprehensive treatment strategy. It also provides aftercare services and community reintegration support to help offenders transition after release from incarceration. The goal is to reduce demand for, use, and trafficking of illegal drugs and break the cycle of drugs and violence by providing evidence-based treatment practices.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to states, local, and tribal governments and correctional agencies to develop and implement residential substance abuse treatment programs within correctional facilities. Funds are reimbursed quarterly and may be used for personnel (salaries, wages, fringe benefits up to 30%), contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, training, and other costs. Equipment items with useful life greater than one year and cost of $10,000 or more per unit require special documentation. Consultant rates are capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day unless pre-approved. Applications involving partnerships with community-based substance abuse treatment programs receive priority consideration. A 25% non-federal cost share (cash or in-kind) is required. Funds cannot support unmanned aerial systems/vehicles, motor vehicles, construction/renovation, prizes/entertainment, lobbying, food/beverage, or supplanting state/local funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive statewide program addressing law enforcement, prosecution, victim services, courts, and discretionary initiatives to respond to domestic violence, sexual assault, dating violence, stalking, strangulation, and sex-trafficking. The STOP VAWA Program encourages the development and strengthening of effective, victim-centered law enforcement, prosecution, and court strategies to combat violent crimes against women in Maryland. Administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, the program distributes funds among victim-centered law enforcement, prosecution, courts, and nonprofit victim service providers to support services, training, and enforcement related to violence against women, and helps criminal justice entities hold offenders accountable.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula grant program that distributes funds according to statutory requirements: 25% to law enforcement, 25% to prosecution, 30% to nonprofit victim services, and 5% to courts, with up to 15% at the state's discretion. Additionally, 10% of victim service allocation must be distributed to linguistically and culturally specific community-based organizations. Twenty percent of total funds across allocations must meaningfully address sexual assault. Funds can be used for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, training and retraining programs, specialized personnel (advocates, bilingual officers, investigators), policy development, technology infrastructure, coordinated community response initiatives, and other approved expenses to support victim-centered strategies against violent crimes against women. Does not include forensic exams requiring insurance reimbursement, lobbying, construction, or fundraising activities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Sexual Assault Kit Testing Grant Program (SAKT)
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program to support sexual assault kit testing initiatives and related victim services. The program provides grant funding to the Maryland State Police and local law enforcement agencies, as well as nonprofit organizations serving sexual assault victims, forensic service providers, hospitals and medical facilities, and crime victim service providers to pay for the testing of sexual assault evidence collection kits by forensic laboratories. Funding also supports a statewide victim notification hotline and related support services, and peer-to-peer telehealth providers for forensic evidence collection. Funding supports criminal investigation of untested sexual assault evidence collection kits, personnel (investigators, victim notification advocates, forensic nurse examiners), victim services, training related to sexual assault kit testing, and related expenses. Agencies can request funding for in-house personnel and supplies for testing, outsourcing of testing, or equipment purchases or upgrades if they have an in-house forensic laboratory. Anticipated funding of $450,400 in total with up to 3 anticipated awards. Requests should be based on the current number of eligible, untested kits plus the annual average number of kits collected by the applicant agency. Funding is limited to testing of sexual assault kits collected since May 1, 2018. The program coordinates criminal justice strategies at local, state, and federal levels to improve victim services for Maryland residents.

Requests should be reasonable and directly align with anticipated cases and should be based on the current number of eligible, untested kits plus the annual average number of kits collected by the applicant agency. Eligible expenses include: personnel (salaries and fringe benefits not exceeding 30% unless pre-approved, consultant rates capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day), operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications), travel expenses (mileage, lodging, meals per state rates), contractual services (consultant contracts for training/evaluation), equipment ($10,000+ per unit requires Property Inventory Report Form), and other approved costs including supplies, registration fees, and equipment under $10,000. Indirect costs available at negotiated rate or 15% de minimis rate. Applicants with in-house forensic laboratories may request additional funds for equipment purchases or upgrades. No cost-share required.

structured_extraction.program_description: SARU provides reimbursement to physicians, hospitals, pharmacies, and laboratories for medical examinations, evidence collection, emergency treatment, and follow-up care for victims of rape, sexual assault, or child sexual abuse. The program aims to prevent re-victimization and help victims and families focus on healing by covering the costs of forensic medical exams and related medical services. SARU reimburses healthcare facilities for sexual assault forensic medical examinations (SAFE) and related medical services, and also covers drug-facilitated sexual assault (DFSA) testing.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement is made directly to medical providers on behalf of victims. Physicians receive reimbursement up to $80 for rape or sexual offense exams, or up to $80 per hour (maximum 5 hours) for child sexual abuse exams. Hospitals receive reimbursement at rates established by the Health Services Cost Review Commission for emergency room, outpatient clinic, and in-hospital care. Laboratories receive established rates for necessary tests. Pharmacies receive established rates for HIV prophylaxis medication. Services covered include emergency room treatment, in-hospital treatment, follow-up medical testing within 90 days, screening for pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections, diagnostic tests, laboratory tests, toxicology screening, medications for pain and other assault-related conditions, postcoital and prophylactic medications, medical screening exams, forensic exams, laboratory services (STI testing, toxicology screening, pregnancy tests, HIV testing), medications (antibiotics, emergency contraception, antiretrovirals/nPEP, pain medications), vaccines, radiology, and surgical consultations related to sexual assault cases. Drug-facilitated sexual assault (DFSA) testing is covered for urine and blood sample testing when collected within specified timeframes (blood within 24 hours, urine within 120 hours of suspected ingestion) and submitted to qualified forensic toxicology laboratories with Maryland Department of Health Forensic Laboratory License.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 90 days of the exam

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for physical examinations, evidence collection, emergency treatment, in-hospital care, follow-up medical testing within 90 days, screening for pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections, diagnostic and laboratory tests, toxicology screening, pain and antiemetic medications, postcoital medications, prophylactic medications for sexually transmitted infections and tetanus, HIV prophylaxis medication, medical evaluation and treatment for sexual assault, forensic evidence collection and examination, laboratory and toxicology testing, medications and vaccines, HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP), and drug-facilitated sexual assault (DFSA) testing (urine and blood samples)—all directly related to alleged rape, sexual assault, or child sexual abuse.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Medical providers must be licensed to practice in Maryland to receive reimbursement. If a victim is assaulted outside Maryland but receives treatment in Maryland, services are covered if all other eligibility criteria are met. Drug-facilitated sexual assault testing must be submitted to qualified forensic toxicology laboratories with Maryland Department of Health Forensic Laboratory License.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Aid for Police Protection Fund (SAPP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A formula-driven funding program that supplements resources for police protection in local communities throughout Maryland. The program provides financial assistance to counties and qualifying municipalities to help offset costs associated with local law enforcement services. State funds ensure residents throughout the State have access to adequate police protection regardless of jurisdiction's tax base or fiscal capacity. Funds are distributed based on a statutory formula considering population, number of police officers in the agency, total jurisdictional taxable income, and crime rates. The program has two components: Formula Funds (statutory allocation based on the formula) and Enhancement Funds (based on violent crime reporting). Annual fund distributions are calculated according to the previous year's operations costs.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula-driven grant funding allocation for annual fund distributions calculated according to the previous year's operations costs. Funds are distributed based on a formula derived through a subdivision's population, number of police officers in the agency, and the total jurisdictional taxable income. Assistance includes reimbursement for police protection expenditures including salaries and wages for officers and civilian employees, capital outlay (equipment, vehicles, radios, etc.), debt service related to police activities, communications, travel, fuel, utilities, contractual services, supplies and materials, fixed charges (rent, insurance), motor vehicle operation and maintenance, retirement and social security contributions, traffic control costs, and central alarm system costs. Grants are reimbursed quarterly unless otherwise stated.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to assist State's Attorney's Offices (SAOs) in establishing or enhancing automated case management systems to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of case management processes through advanced technology solutions. The program reflects a commitment to modernizing prosecutorial operations and supporting data-driven decision-making within Maryland's criminal justice system. It helps modernize case management using advanced technology, improve data accuracy and efficiency in case tracking and decision-making, and support fairness and equity by tracking key data on defendants and victims.

Eligible costs include contractual services (system development, customization, technical support, consultant fees), equipment (hardware and software), personnel (salaries and fringe benefits), operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications), travel (mileage, meals, lodging), and other expenditures. structured_extraction.program_name: Title II Juvenile Justice Delinquency Prevention Formula Grant (JJAC)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal formula grant funding to support reform in Maryland's juvenile justice system through initiatives and strategies based on a Developmental Approach to Juvenile Justice Reform. The approach emphasizes accountability without criminalization, alternatives to justice system involvement, individualized response based on assessment of needs and risks, confinement only when necessary for public safety, fairness, sensitivity to disparate treatment, family engagement, and juvenile delinquency prevention. The program focuses on improving outcomes for children and youth by increasing and strengthening programs in the areas of aftercare and reentry, alternatives to detention, diversion, and probation. The program supports community-based programs and services, expands community-based alternatives to confinement, and brings the state into compliance with federal limitations on holding youth in adult jails or lock-ups. A developmentally appropriate and trauma-informed framework is required. The program is authorized under Sections 221–223 of the Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention Act of 1974, as amended in 2002.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that improves the treatment of victims of crime by providing assistance and services necessary to aid their restoration after a violent criminal act and support them through the criminal justice process. Services include crisis intervention, counseling, emergency transportation to court, temporary housing, and criminal justice support and advocacy. The program helps crime victims and their families recover and receive information about and assistance in filing for Crime Victim Compensation. Supports critical needs of crime victims throughout Maryland by funding victim services programs with proven track records of service. Funding is supported by criminal fines, forfeited bail bonds, penalty fees, and special assessments collected by U.S. Attorney's Offices, U.S. Courts, and the Bureau of Prisons from offenders convicted of Federal crimes.

Funds can support contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel (with administrative positions limited to 30% of salary and fringe), and travel. The Crime Victims Fund is supported by criminal fines, forfeited bail bonds, penalty fees, and special assessments collected by U.S. Attorney's Offices, U.S. Courts, and the Bureau of Prisons from offenders convicted of Federal crimes. Grants are reimbursable on a quarterly basis. Total anticipated funding approximately $60 million with approximately 150 awards expected. Minimum request is $50,000.
