structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports effective violence reduction strategies, specifically gun violence, through evidence-based and evidence-informed health programs. The program funds hospital-based violence intervention programs and other public health initiatives designed to prevent gun violence, supporting academic institutions, governmental entities, community-based organizations, and independent researchers working on violence intervention and prevention. The program evaluates the efficacy of funded programs through independent, third-party researchers and is established by §4–902 of the Public Safety Article. Funded through House Bill 432, approved by Governor Hogan in 2018.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding of up to $2,600,000 total anticipated availability with up to 20 awards not to exceed $300,000 each (continuation applicants may request up to 10% less than current SFY26 award). Funds are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis for actual expenditures, with monthly reimbursement available for nonprofit entities with awards over $50,000. Funded categories include: personnel (salaries, wages, fringe benefits up to 30% of salary), operating expenses (rental space, communications, printing), travel (training, meetings, field work), contractual services (behavioral healthcare providers, clinical providers, training providers), equipment (per unit cost $10,000 or more with useful life of one year or more), and other eligible expenses (program/office supplies, technology equipment under $10,000, client support, indirect costs). Consultant rates capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day. Requires 33% cash or in-kind cost share (match). Funding period: July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Academic institutions, governmental entities, independent researchers, community-based organizations, local governments, and nonprofit organizations working on violence intervention and prevention programs. Specific focus on serving individuals in communities disproportionately impacted by firearm violence and target populations served by community violence intervention programs, including gun violence survivors, families affected by domestic violence, at-risk youth, trauma center patients, residents of affected communities, survivors of violent injury, people at high risk for involvement in violence, African American males ages 18-50, young men of color ages 18-34, individuals experiencing depression and trauma, families of violence victims, high-risk youth aged 14-25 years, families experiencing early-stage domestic violence, and community residents in targeted violence hotspots.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel (staff salaries, wages, fringe benefits for program directors, violence interrupters, outreach workers, case managers, victim advocates, clinicians, evaluation staff), operating expenses (rental space, communications, printing directly related to VIPP project), travel (training, VIPP meetings, field work), contractual services (behavioral healthcare providers, clinical providers, education/training providers, evaluation services), equipment (items with cost $10,000 or more and useful life of one year or more), and other approved expenses (program/office supplies, technology equipment under $10,000, client support on case-by-case basis, indirect costs) for violence intervention and prevention programs that address gun violence through evidence-based or evidence-informed health programs. Includes support for hospital-based violence intervention programs, street outreach and violence interruption, group or individual risk-focused intervention, crisis response and stabilization services, case management, mentoring, advocacy services, mediation and conflict resolution, and referral to supportive services. Additionally supports community events, bedside assessments, prevention/education activities, workforce development and job placement services, mental health and substance abuse counseling, peer support and mentoring, trauma recovery assistance, emergency supplies for participants, housing and food assistance, database development and data management systems, telehealth and virtual service capabilities, community partnership development, and social media and outreach efforts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Specific service sites and catchment areas are defined by zip codes at applicant's discretion. Program includes focus on 27 ENOUGH-eligible communities with high concentrated child poverty. Targeted focus areas include Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Prince George's County, West Baltimore/Park Heights areas, and Southern Maryland. Applicants may define project geography as local (specific county), multijurisdictional (multiple counties), or statewide.

structured_extraction.program_name: Protecting Against Hate Crimes Program (PAHC) / Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive state and federal grant program providing financial assistance to nonprofit organizations, including faith-based organizations, houses of worship, and schools, to enhance security measures and implement hate crime prevention and counter-extremism initiatives for facilities at risk of hate crimes, terrorist attacks, or other extremist violence. The program supports physical security enhancements, community engagement and education, emergency preparedness, and integration with broader state and local preparedness efforts. Funding supports security equipment, systems, training, threat assessments, and emergency response planning to help protect individuals belonging to protected classes including religion, race, color, sexual orientation, gender, disability, national origin, and homelessness. The program supports the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy's objective of developing criminal justice and victim services strategies through collaboration, information sharing, and knowledge transfer between law enforcement, victim services, and communities targeted for hate crimes. The PAHC component was established in 2020 to address documented and recent risks of hate crime victimization.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy; Maryland Emergency Management Agency
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding provided on a quarterly reimbursement basis. Maximum of $200,000 per location for NSGP; organizations can apply for up to six locations total per nonprofit organization with no more than three locations in either NSGP-UA (Urban Area) or NSGP-S (State funding), not to exceed $600,000 total per state. For FY2025, there is no cost share requirement. Funds support personnel (hiring for facility security, staff attending safety/crime prevention training; fringe benefits capped at 30% of salary without prior approval), equipment (surveillance cameras, alarm systems, hardened doors/windows, security fences, improved lighting, cybersecurity systems, communication towers; items ≥$10,000 require inventory records), contractual services (external security services, risk assessments, training, consultants capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day unless pre-approved), travel (mileage, lodging, meals, ground transportation), and other direct security enhancements. Physical security enhancements, community engagement and education initiatives (anti-hate awareness campaigns, cultural competency workshops, bystander intervention training), emergency preparedness activities (emergency response plans, active threat drills), classroom-based training, exercises, and purchase of mobile and portable equipment are supported. Projects under $250,000 are exempt from Buy America domestic content procurement preference requirements. Excludes: alcoholic beverages, bonuses, construction (except modifications/renovations for NSGP), corporate formation, fundraising, lobbying, meals (except pre-approved client food), debt obligations, trinkets, and covered foreign unmanned aircraft systems per the American Security Drone Act and Executive Order 14305.

Excludes: alcoholic beverages, bonuses, construction, corporate formation, fundraising, lobbying, meals (except pre-approved client food), debt obligations, trinkets, covered foreign unmanned aircraft systems per the American Security Drone Act and Executive Order 14305.

Applicants must demonstrate local and state statistics showing documented or current events/trends indicating their facility serves members of protected classes facing substantial threat of hate crimes or other extremist attacks.

The Investment Justification is the principal application document and must be supported by the organization's Mission Statement and Vulnerability Assessment. structured_extraction.program_description: A procurement program that provides Certified Small Businesses (CSBs) with a designated price preference in state procurements. The base price preference is up to 5% of the total contract value, with additional preferences available for veteran-owned small businesses (up to 7% total with an additional 2% preference) and disabled-veteran-owned small businesses (up to 8% total with an additional 3% preference). The program expands procurement opportunities for CSBs by allowing them to submit bids that can exceed the lowest bid within specified percentage thresholds. Certified Small Businesses automatically receive the small business preference when bidding on eligible state procurements, with the preference applied during the procurement agency's bid evaluation process.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified Small Businesses receive a designated price preference up to 5% of total contract value in procurements where the SBP Program applies. Veteran-owned small businesses may receive an additional 2% preference (7% total), and disabled-veteran-owned small businesses may receive an additional 3% preference (8% total). The procurement agency will accept the most favorable responsive bid from a responsible certified small business if the bid does not exceed the most favorable responsive bid from a non-small business by the specified percentages. CSBs use the price preference to make their bids more competitive on designated state contracts.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - apply at any time; no specific deadline. CSB certification is valid for three years; must recertify within 30-day window before expiration.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CSBs interested in the SBP Program must first obtain CSB certification through the eMMA platform. To apply: Register in eMMA system, navigate to General Info > Company Profile, select "Yes" for CSB Certification application, navigate to Documents tab, click plus icon to add CSB Application (only once), read and agree to CSB Disclaimer, and complete all required fields. Once certified, CSBs are automatically eligible to receive price preferences on procurements where the SBP Program applies. Specific bidding instructions are provided in individual solicitations that include the SBP Program. No separate application is required beyond CSB certification. CSB certification is valid for three years and must be recertified within a 30-day window before expiration.

structured_extraction.program_description: A procurement program that reserves state-funded contracting opportunities exclusively for Certified Small Businesses (CSBs), allowing small businesses to compete as prime contractors against other small businesses rather than larger, more established companies. The program establishes a unique marketplace where small businesses compete only against other small businesses instead of larger, more established companies. Approximately 20% of all open state-funded solicitations advertised on Maryland's online procurement platform are designated as SBR, meaning awards can only be made to certified small businesses. Participating state agencies direct a portion of their fiscal year procurement expenditures to certified SBR businesses. This is a socioeconomic program delivered through certification and reserved contracting opportunities with no cost to become certified. CSB certification is valid for three years and requires recertification within 30 days before the expiration date.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The SBR Program provides certified small businesses with access to state procurement opportunities where they compete only against other small businesses as prime contractors. Participating agencies designate approximately 20% of their open solicitations as SBR, creating a reserved marketplace for eligible small businesses. Awards can only be made to CSBs on designated SBR procurements. There is no cost to become certified. This is a procurement access program, not a direct funding program. CSBs use their certification to bid on state contracts designated as SBR solicitations, and funds are earned through winning designated procurements. CSB certification is valid for three years with expiration date and requires recertification within 30-day window before expiration date; failure to recertify by expiration date results in automatic removal of certification.

structured_extraction.program_name: T.I.P.S. (Training & Insights for Procurement Success) Small Business Webinar Series
structured_extraction.program_description: A free monthly webinar series offered by the Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs that helps small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses learn how to compete for state contracts and improve core competencies. The program offers two complementary series: T.I.P.S. webinars covering topics such as state procurement processes, minority business enterprise rights and responsibilities, solicitation anatomy, contracting requirements, bid preparation, and federal contracting opportunities; and Small Biz Resource Connections webinars featuring presentations from various Maryland state agencies and organizations on topics including employment law, non-discrimination policies, business lending, accessibility compliance, and labor standards. Sessions are conducted virtually via Zoom approximately twice monthly at 10 a.m. and are recorded for future reference.

Participants register online to receive a unique Zoom participation link. Session materials, slide presentations, and video recordings are provided post-session for future reference. structured_extraction.program_name: Technical Training Classroom & T.I.P.S. (Training & Insights for Procurement Success) and Small Biz Resource Connections Webinar Series
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive free training program offered by the Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs to help small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses learn about government contracting and general business operations. The program combines multiple components: (1) Technical Training Classroom & T.I.P.S. Small Business Webinar Series, featuring in-person monthly classroom sessions (fourth Tuesday of each month except December) at the Governor's Coordinating Offices at 100 Community Place in Crownsville with morning sessions at 10 a.m. and afternoon sessions at 2 p.m., plus twice-monthly virtual webinars via Zoom at 10 a.m. covering state and federal procurement processes, e-Procurement platform navigation, small business prime contracting opportunities, subcontractor rights and responsibilities, proposal writing, capabilities statements, buyers' behaviors, contract price analysis, cash flow management, business planning, pricing and negotiations, prevailing wage and living wage laws, financial capacity building, business communication, networking, and contracting strategies; and (2) Small Biz Resource Connections Webinar Series, featuring periodic presentations from various Maryland state agencies and organizations on topics such as employment law, non-discrimination policies, business lending, contracting resources, accessibility compliance, labor standards, and negotiation strategies. All training is free and requires advance registration with limited seating for classroom sessions. Participants receive access to instructor slide decks, video recordings, and session materials post-session for use as resource materials.

No cost to attend any format, but advance registration is required with limited seating for classroom sessions. Webinar registration opens three weeks in advance of each session. Registration can be completed through Eventbrite or the program website at goMDsmallbiz.maryland.gov. Participants receive access to instructor slide decks, video recordings, and session materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: Monthly in-person workshops for certification and re-certification in the Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise (VSBE), Certified Small Business (CSB)/Small Business Reserve (SBR), and Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) socio-economic procurement programs. Workshops are held across multiple Maryland counties to help businesses obtain or renew their certifications and learn about accessing state contracting opportunities through 70+ purchasing units.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free monthly in-person workshops held in various counties across Maryland (Charles, Montgomery, Anne Arundel, Frederick, Baltimore City, Prince George's, Dorchester, Howard, Calvert, St. Mary's, and other counties). Workshops provide certification and re-certification training for VSBE, SBR, CSB, and MBE programs. Topics include program eligibility standards, prime and subcontracting opportunities, UNSPSC codes, NAICS codes, eMMA registration, procurement data mining, and access to 70+ state purchasing units. structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland socioeconomic procurement program that provides greater economic opportunities to veteran-owned small businesses through certification and preferential contracting opportunities on state-funded procurements. Designated state agencies and departments are directed to spend at least 3% of the dollar value of their procurement contracts with certified VSBE firms. Certified VSBE firms can work as prime contractors or subcontractors on state-funded procurements. The program certifies veteran-owned small businesses to participate in state procurement contracts and gain access to contracting opportunities. The program enhances opportunities for veteran-owned small businesses to perform within the state contracting arena with over 50 state agencies participating. As of FY2023, over 750 certified firms received $141M in payments across 322 VSBEs that received contracts.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides certification that allows veteran-owned small businesses to be counted toward VSBE contracting goals on state-funded procurements. Certified VSBE firms can work as prime contractors or subcontractors. Certification is free and must be renewed every 3 years effective September 1st, 2025. Firms must register as a vendor on the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) e-Procurement platform, complete veteran verification through either the Maryland Department of Veterans & Military Families or the SBA's Federal Veteran Small Business Verification Program, and submit a VSBE certification application. Vendors registered in eMMA may receive email notices of procurement opportunities from state agencies valued over $15,000, as well as county and local government procurements. Solicitations with established VSBE contract participation goals are noted in eMMA.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Danielle Davis (Veterans Services Specialist / VSBE Program Compliance Manager)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veteran-owned small businesses seeking contracting opportunities on state-funded procurements. Eligible businesses must meet size standards set by the United States Small Business Administration and be at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more veterans. Program serves veterans, transitioning service members, National Guard and Reserve members, women veterans, and military spouses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a certification and contracting program, not a direct financial assistance program. Certified businesses gain access to state procurement opportunities valued at a higher percentage of contract dollars and use their VSBE certification to bid on and perform state-funded procurement contracts across over 50 state agencies and departments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Vendors registered in eMMA may receive email notices of procurement opportunities from state agencies valued over $15,000, as well as county and local government procurements. All 52+ state agencies and departments participate.
requirements_list: Must meet size standards adopted by the United States Small Business Administration in 13 C.F.R. 121.201
Must be at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more individuals who are veterans

A veteran must be verified as having served on active duty in the Uniformed Services of the United States (other than for training) and was discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable
Must be a for-profit business
Must be in Good Standing
Must register as a vendor on the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) platform
Must complete veteran verification through either the Maryland Department of Veterans & Military Families or the SBA's Federal Veteran Small Business Verification Program
Must submit a VSBE certification application in eMMA

Regulations found in COMAR 21.11.14
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The certification process requires three steps. Step 1: Register as a vendor on the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) e-Procurement platform at no cost. When registering, indicate that you would like to apply to the VSBE Program. Log into your account and complete the Certifications section by selecting 'Add Certifications' and choosing 'Certification/VSBE Application'. Step 2: Verify your veteran status by submitting required documents (such as DD Form 214, DD215, NGB22, NGB23, DD Form 5016, Order Memo, Certificate of Release, Discharge Papers, VA Rating Decision, or Federal Benefit Letter) to either the Maryland Department of Veterans & Military Families using the VSBE Veteran Verification Form or through the SBA's Federal Veteran Small Business Verification Program. Step 3: Complete the VSBE certification application in eMMA by logging into your account, selecting the Company Profile tab, and under Procurement Programs and State Programs, selecting 'Yes' to enroll in the VSBE Program. Enter your veteran verification number (a combination of letters and numbers from the state, or the SAM UEI number if certified through the SBA) and save your changes. Upon approval, you will receive a VSBE Certification Number (VBXX-XXXXXX). Self-certification is available with same-day certification possible.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME)
structured_extraction.program_description: HUD entitlement grants that Harford County receives annually to support housing, infrastructure, revitalization, and services for low- to moderate-income citizens. The program funds projects that provide decent housing, a suitable living environment, and expand economic opportunities for low- to moderate-income persons. The county uses funds for capital projects that benefit low- to moderate-income persons or households, or to reduce slum and blight, including affordable housing, services to vulnerable residents, job creation, and business opportunities expansion. Funds are dispersed annually to nonprofit organizations and eligible entities throughout Harford County and are not available to individuals directly.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HUD entitlement grants distributed annually based on a pre-determined HUD formula. Harford County receives an annual entitlement allocation from HUD. Funding can be spent on housing, infrastructure, revitalization, and services for low- to moderate-income citizens. Funds are primarily used for capital projects that benefit low- to moderate-income persons or households, or to reduce slum and blight. Funds are dispersed annually to various nonprofit organizations and in some cases for-profit entities throughout Harford County and are not available to individuals directly. Projects and activities must be submitted to and approved by HUD through a 5-year Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan. All selected programs and projects are subject to availability of funding and the county's budget review process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typical application period runs during January/February
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private nonprofit organizations with IRS 501(c)(3) status, for-profit entities in some cases, and public entities serving Harford County's low- to moderate-income citizens. Community development organizations and housing organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing, infrastructure, revitalization, services, public facility improvements, nonprofit services, tenant-based rental assistance, low-mod income housing construction, first-time homebuyer support, critical repairs, projects providing decent housing, suitable living environment, expansion of economic opportunities for low- to moderate-income persons, and reducing slum and blight. Community development activities and housing investments.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds renovation and new construction projects to improve business exteriors along designated stretches of U.S. Route 40 (Pulaski Highway) and MD-755 (Edgewood Road) in the Edgewood Sustainable Community Area. The program aims to transform business exteriors to generate economic development and increase investment in a historically underserved community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grant for eligible facade improvement projects. Projects costing up to $10,000 receive 100% reimbursement with zero match required. Projects exceeding $10,000 receive reimbursement up to 80% of approved costs over the first $10,000, with the business owner required to provide a 20% match for costs above $10,000. Funds are used for project reimbursement only.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within the designated eligibility area bordering U.S. Route 40 (Pulaski Highway) or MD-755 (Edgewood Road) located in the Edgewood Sustainable Community Area overlay in Harford County.

Project will be subject to final inspection and site visit upon completion before reimbursement funds are paid

The application will be reviewed by the county and must receive approval from the Maryland Historical Trust. Once approved and project is completed, a final inspection and site visit will be conducted before reimbursement is paid.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax incentive program that encourages business investment, retention, expansion, and job creation in designated Enterprise Zones in Harford County, particularly in the Aberdeen and Havre de Grace areas. Businesses located within the zones receive tax credits for capital improvements and job creation to support business operations, expansion, and development of underutilized properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of tax credits are available. Real property tax credits provide up to 80% credit on increases in assessed value of real property for the first five years, decreasing by 10% annually for the next five years, for a total of up to 10 years. Job creation tax credits include a one-time $1,000 tax credit per new job created submitted with annual tax filing, and an additional $6,000 total per eligible economically-disadvantaged employee distributed over three years. Tax credits are provided to qualified businesses located within designated Enterprise Zones in Aberdeen, Havre de Grace, Edgewood, and Joppa.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1st
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in designated Enterprise Zones including Aberdeen, Havre de Grace, Edgewood, and Joppa in Harford County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital investments in construction and renovation of real property, job creation with payroll meeting specified wage requirements, business operations, expansion, and development of underutilized properties in Enterprise Zones
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties within the 9,738-acre Aberdeen and Havre de Grace Enterprise Zone, including areas along U.S. Route 40, Aberdeen and Havre de Grace municipalities, portions of Aberdeen Proving Ground, Belcamp, Perryman, and the HEAT Center area. Includes specified business parks: 40 East Industrial Park, Aberdeen Industrial Center, Advantage Business Center, Chesapeake Industrial Park, Cranberry Run Business Park, Enterprise Business Park, Hardee's Industrial Park, Harford Gateway, Hickory Ridge Industrial Park, North Gate Business Park, Perryman Industrial Park, Rock Glenn Business Park, CONVERGE, and Water's Edge Corporate Campus.

Minimum job creation of 2 new jobs for businesses with 10 or fewer employees, or 5 new jobs for businesses with 11 or more employees
New jobs must involve working 35 hours per week or more
Hourly pay must be 150% of minimum wage
Half of work time must be within the Enterprise Zone
Real property tax credits require the building to be occupied to receive credit
Enterprise Zone Administrator must be contacted prior to construction
Submit itemized cost breakdown for construction and renovation with application
Submit site plan showing any changes to interior/exterior of buildings
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Enterprise Zone Administrator prior to construction to discuss timeline for real property tax credits. Submit completed application with itemized construction costs, site plan, and required documentation by October 1st. For job creation tax credits, submit Maryland Form 500 CR with annual tax filing.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that helps Harford County households become economically independent by learning to take control of their lives and achieve financial independence within five years through goal-setting, obstacle removal, and support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FSS participants receive support services including childcare, transportation, education, job search and job retention skills, financial planning, credit repair, and home-ownership counseling. Participants also receive an interest-bearing escrow savings account that accrues as the household's portion of rent increases due to earned income growth. The escrow account and accrued interest are paid to the participant upon successful completion of the five-year contract. Escrow payments are nontaxable according to Internal Revenue Service rules.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with Section 8/Housing Choice Vouchers who are current Harford County residents with employment goals and wish to achieve financial independence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program helps participants achieve financial independence through goal-setting, career planning, financial planning, and support services. Participants build savings through an escrow account funded by increases in their earned income portion of rent.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County only
requirements_list: Currently participating in Harford County Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) program
Must currently have a Section 8/Housing Choice Voucher
Must be residing in Harford County
Have employment goals
Wish to achieve financial independence
Complete and sign a contract
Have a current signed training plan
Maintain contact with FSS specialist
Complete all activities on the contract and training plan within up to five years to access escrow savings
Be free of Maryland Temporary Cash Assistance welfare benefits at time of graduation
Be employed at time of graduation
Must know current Housing Choice Voucher Analyst name
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To make an appointment and learn more about FSS, complete and submit the interest form available on the website or call 410-638-3045. Complete and submit online form providing name, address, contact information, Section 8 voucher status, residency status, and current voucher analyst name. Interested participants work with an FSS specialist to define and choose career and financial goals, then develop a contract and training plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Fast Track 2.0 is an expedited permitting program that enables businesses and industrial users to establish an accelerated schedule for permit and license issuance. The program provides prioritized reviews and processing, a dedicated Harford County Business Navigator/liaison to support projects through completion, online progress tracking, and assistance meeting project deadlines. structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Agricultural Land Preservation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program protects productive agricultural land and woodland to support continued food and fiber production and maintains agriculture's vital role in the local economy. Through the Agricultural Preservation District, landowners commit to limiting subdivision of their parcel for a minimum of five years in exchange for a tax credit of $50 per acre that can offset up to 50% of the property's annual Harford County property tax. After the initial five-year term expires, the agreement and tax credit remain in effect indefinitely until the owner requests termination. Landowners can also receive payment for selling development rights to the state or county. Following purchase of development rights, the farm is subject to an easement that prohibits future development.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners receive a tax credit of $50 per acre that can offset up to 50% of the property's annual Harford County property tax through the Agricultural Preservation District commitment program. The tax credit applies for the initial five-year commitment period and then continues indefinitely unless the owner requests termination. Upon termination, all accrued property tax credits must be refunded to the county. Landowners can also receive payment for selling development rights to the state or county. Following purchase of development rights, the farm is subject to an easement that prohibits future development.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Historic Preservation Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: A county tax credit program that provides financial incentives for owners of Harford County Historic Landmarks who undertake qualified historic rehabilitation and restoration work. Tax credits reduce county real property tax based on the increase in property assessment from the work and provide an additional credit equal to 10% of qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses, capped at $7,500. All work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Rehabilitation and the Harford County Historic Preservation Design Guidelines.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners may reduce their county real property tax by a tax credit based on the amount their assessment increased due to rehabilitation or restoration, plus a tax credit equal to 10% of qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses, capped at $7,500 (based on qualified expenses of $75,000). Applicants must submit a Certificate of Appropriateness before work begins and a Certification of Completed Work after the project is finished, along with an itemized expense sheet documenting all rehabilitation costs. There is no limit on the number of tax credits granted, but a previous tax credit amount must be exhausted before another can be granted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of Harford County Historic Landmarks seeking to rehabilitate or restore their historic properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses for historic properties, including materials, labor, and other project costs that meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland. Properties must be designated as Harford County Historic Landmarks by the County Council or located within designated historic districts in Harford County.

Work must meet the Harford County Historic Preservation Design Guidelines

Applicant must provide an itemized expense sheet detailing all rehabilitation costs

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Part 1: Submit an Application for Certificate of Appropriateness to the Harford County Historic Preservation Commission for approval of rehabilitation plans before beginning work to ensure the proposed rehabilitation meets historic preservation standards. Part 2: Upon project completion, submit a Certification of Completed Work Application and an Itemized Expenses spreadsheet. A staff site visit and review by the Historic Preservation Commission at their monthly public meeting will occur prior to approval. Applications must follow the provided instructions and may reference the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and local Design Guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Community Impact Grant (Tourism Funding Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to support individual nonprofits or municipalities with creating, expanding, or enhancing events that drive tourism and economic growth in Harford County. This includes festivals, events, exhibits, and other programming that attract individuals to either overnight stays or day trips. The program is funded through Harford County's 6% hotel tax. Funds not used by the Partnership Grant program are set aside for this Community Impact Grant program. The program provides grants to help fund events and activities that attract visitors to the county.
structured_extraction.agency: Harford County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds support individual nonprofits or municipalities with creating, expanding, or enhancing tourism-related events and programming. Funds may cover direct tourism-related marketing costs, non-marketing event expenses, and up to 75 percent of salaries for key employees in the first year (with decreasing percentages in subsequent years: 50 percent year two, 25 percent year three, and 0 percent thereafter). Funds may not be used for daily operating costs, capital improvements, property acquisition, building projects, or debt reduction. For the 2026 fiscal year, a total of $770,000 is available for all awards through both the Partnership Fund and Community Impact Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications will open on Monday, February 23, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual nonprofits and Harford County municipalities seeking to develop creative and innovative approaches to increase tourism in the county with emphasis on attracting out-of-county visitors. Eligible non-profits must have a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) status and a primary focus on tourism.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct tourism-related marketing costs for festivals, events, exhibits, and programming; non-marketing expenses for events that attract local or out-of-county visitors; internal operational expenses including up to 75 percent of key employee salaries in the first year (decreasing in subsequent years); festival or event programming that enhances community culture and quality of life. Funds cannot be used for daily operating costs, capital improvements, property acquisition, building projects, debt reduction, or general office equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County organizations only. Organizations must be registered in Harford County with the State of Maryland to be eligible. Only organizations registered with the State of Maryland at an address in Harford County are eligible to apply.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) nonprofit organization or Harford County municipality
Must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessment and Taxation
Must be in good standing with Maryland Office of the Secretary of State, Charitable Organization Division
Must demonstrate ability to capture data and measure success of initiatives
Must demonstrate efforts to pursue additional funding sources outside Harford County Government
Must not have history of non-compliance with past Harford County grant programs
If applying for operational funding, organization must demonstrate ability to work towards self-sustainability
The organization's mission must be tourism-related, meaning its activities primarily attract visitors from outside Harford County for overnight stays
Applicants to the Partnership Fund must collaborate with at least one other organization
Applicants must submit all required documentation, which includes financial statements, proof of non-profit status, and letters of support from partners
Must complete and upload Tourism Budget and Expense Report
Must complete and upload Quarterly Narrative Activity Report (QNAR) with summary tab and program/event overview and objectives at time of application
Must provide payment information, bank account information, and W-9 (Supplier Package)
Must set up account via eCivis portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Qualified nonprofits and municipalities submit applications through the online eCivis portal beginning February 23, 2026. Applicants must download and complete the Tourism Budget and Expense Report and Quarterly Narrative Activity Report (QNAR) forms, set up a portal account, and submit all required documentation including board member lists, staff information, good standing certificates, 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) documentation, Form 990, balance sheets and income statements for fiscal years 2023 and 2024, payment information, bank account information, and W-9. A review committee evaluates the applications and makes funding recommendations to the County Executive for final award decisions. Forms will be used for ongoing reporting if award is granted.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides funding to small businesses in Harford County to support their overall growth through capital investment, job creation, retention, and economic development. structured_extraction.agency: Harford County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans provide funding up to $200,000 through flexible terms. Eligible uses include building and land purchases, renovations, technology upgrades, and equipment purchases. Loans can be used in conjunction with other lending institutions through gap financing and partnerships. Collateral is required, though exceptions may be made for loans less than $10,000. structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program designed to support transformational development and revitalization efforts along the Route 1 corridor in Howard County, providing financial incentives for properties and businesses located in the Route 1 corridor area to encourage economic development and revitalization. The program offers tax credits to owners of commercial and industrial properties to support visible improvements to properties along the Route 1 corridor. The program provides a tax credit up to a maximum of $100,000 per property. Applicants may be eligible for up to 125% of approved expenses if costs exceed the initial estimate, not to exceed the $100,000 cap. The full credit is available over five years if the property's taxes are high enough. The credit stays with the property, not the owner, if it is sold. The program has a total annual allocation of $250,000.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial and industrial properties along the Route 1 corridor in Howard County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include: exterior renovations or cleaning; structural improvements to the facade; replacing false facades; restoring architectural features; adding streetscape items like landscaping, walkways, or lighting; repairing doors and windows; new signs, canopies, or awnings; visible roof repairs; screening for utility or trash areas; enhanced exterior lighting; fencing that does not hide the building; sidewalks; new construction that improves the property's appearance; and necessary interior structural work.

requirements_list: You must be current on property taxes.
The property must have no outstanding violations for zoning, licensing, permits, or fire codes.
Proposed improvements must comply with the Route 1 Manual and county development standards.
Approval for the tax credit does not replace the need for any required building or sign permits.
The program has a total annual allocation of $250,000.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the agency to discuss your proposed project. If you decide to apply, submit an application with contractor cost estimates and photos of the property's current condition. County staff review the application to ensure you meet all requirements. An inter-departmental committee then votes to approve or deny the project. You must not begin any work until you receive a Certificate of Eligibility. After completing the work, submit a final application with a maintenance agreement and invoices by April 1st. A county representative will inspect the site to verify the work was completed as approved.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Howard County initiative that provides grants to nonprofit, for-profit, and government organizations to create free, accessible, and supportive programs promoting youth engagement and activities outside of traditional school hours. The program supports underserved youth ages 14-25, including those with psychiatric and developmental disabilities, LGBTQIA+ youth and allies, and high school students with opportunities for social-emotional learning, mental health and wellness resources, career exploration, academic and career readiness, leadership development, and community connections. YEP! grants fund specific programming including Gender Sexuality Alliance (GSA) clubs, mentorship programs, writing initiatives like Navigating the Margins, career transition services, internships, job placement, job coaching, and retention support to help youth build skills, confidence, and prepare for employment and adulthood. Programming also includes field and sports days, environmental groups, community service activities, gardening programs, and seminars on academic and career readiness and mental health and wellness resources.

structured_extraction.program_name: Agribusiness Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest agricultural loan program designed to fund equipment purchases and provide working capital for Maryland's agribusiness and rural business sector. The program helps rural businesses innovate, diversify, and take advantage of emerging market opportunities, particularly for those who cannot obtain commercial financing from traditional lenders like banks or farm credit associations. MARBIDCO provides additional loan proceeds ranging from 20% to 40% of total commercial financing required, working with commercial banks and public sector lenders. The program serves established Agricultural/Resource-Based Industry firms and producers throughout Maryland. Loans support innovation, diversification, and emerging market opportunities for rural businesses, including value-added food processing, agri-tourism and rural recreation, timber growing or harvesting, primary or secondary wood processing, environmental or water quality projects, and biomass or energy production.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $15,000 to $100,000 for equipment purchases and working capital. Equipment loans have terms of 3 to 8 years (with up to 12 months interest-only possible). Operating loans have terms of 1 to 2 years (with up to 6 months interest-only possible). Interest rates are 4.75% with a public sector lender partner or 6.75% without. A 1% loan origination fee applies. Typically 10% equity contribution is required. All loans to business entities must be personally guaranteed by owners. MARBIDCO provides additional loan proceeds ranging from 20% to 40% of total commercial financing required, working with commercial banks and public sector lenders. Loans support innovation, diversification, and emerging market opportunities for rural businesses, including value-added food processing, agri-tourism and rural recreation, timber growing or harvesting, primary or secondary wood processing, environmental or water quality projects, and biomass or energy production.

structured_extraction.program_name: Forestry Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program established by MARBIDCO to meet the unique financing needs of Maryland's forest products businesses. Provides low-interest loans for equipment purchases and working capital, designed to help forest products-related businesses and timber operations access affordable financing, innovate, and exploit emerging market opportunities. The program complements private commercial lenders through cooperative arrangements with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, and USDA Farm Service Agency to make rural business financing available and affordable.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $15,000 to $150,000 for equipment purchases (3 to 6 year terms) or working capital (1 to 2 year terms). Interest rates are established on a case-by-case basis with a minimum fixed rate of 6.25%. A 1% loan origination fee applies. Borrowers typically need to provide 5-10% equity contribution. Commercial lender participation is required through cooperative arrangements with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, and USDA Farm Service Agency. More liberal underwriting guidelines than normal commercial lending, including a minimum cash flow coverage ratio of 1.0/1.0 and partially relaxed collateral security requirements where appropriate. Maximum outstanding aggregate portfolio balance under this program is $400,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland forest products businesses, forest products-related businesses, forestry operations, and rural forest-related businesses seeking financing for equipment purchases or working capital needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases, machinery, working capital, value-added secondary wood processing, timber growing or harvesting, environmental and water quality projects, and biomass/energy products for forest products-related businesses and timber operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program serving both Eastern Shore and Western Shore forest products businesses. The Upper Shore Regional Council offers an additional equity incentive grant for eligible loans in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Government Agriculture & Resource-Based Industry Project Cost Share Program
structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO matches rural business development investments made by local governments and rural regional development councils to support agricultural and resource-based businesses in Maryland. This ongoing grant program provides cost-sharing assistance for projects that help retain and grow existing and emerging farms, forestry operations, and seafood businesses. Projects may include agritourism activities, food production, soil or water-based goods, packaging, value-added processing and marketing, and water or air quality improvements that contribute to business sustainability.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MARBIDCO provides matching grants to local governments and regional development councils for agricultural and resource-based business projects. Maximum grant amounts are $10,000 (standard projects), $5,000 (Food Safety Modernization Act matching grants), and $3,000 (deer fences and farm operation solar or generator systems). There is a $25,000 annual cap per government jurisdiction and a $15,000 lifetime maximum for individual farmers or business owners.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that assist Maryland's farming, forestry, or seafood industries, including agritourism activities, food production, soil or water-based goods, packaging, value-added processing and marketing, water or air quality improvements that contribute to business sustainability, young and beginning farmer support, timber growing or harvesting, primary and secondary wood processing, biomass and energy production, niche market production, aquaculture and fishing operations, farm operation solar systems or generators, deer fences, and Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) compliance. Equipment and facilities for these purposes are also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide program. Program partners include Anne Arundel, Cecil, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Queen Anne, Salisbury-Wicomico (Wicomico County), Worcester counties, and the Town of Mount Airy.
requirements_list: Applications must be submitted by a local or regional economic development office
Government entity's funds must be own-source (not pass-through)
Project must fit within MARBIDCO's statutorily established economic development profile

The program provides low and moderate-cost loans and grants designed to help farmers, watermen, aquaculture businesses, seafood processors, wood processors, vineyards, and veterinarians secure affordable capital and credit for equipment, commercial facilities, real estate purchases, and business operations. Services support retention of existing resource-based industry production and commerce, promote rural entrepreneurship, and nurture emerging or expanding agricultural enterprises.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) Rural Business Energy Efficiency Improvement Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan and grant program that provides financing to help rural agricultural businesses and food and fiber processing operations improve energy efficiency. MARBIDCO offers low-interest loans ranging from $5,000 to $30,000 at a fixed interest rate of 4.50%, with a grant incentive of 10% of the loan amount (not to exceed $1,000). The program finances projects based on recommendations from qualified third-party energy auditors to help farmers and agricultural businesses reduce energy consumption and increase profitability.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans range from $5,000 to $30,000 at a fixed interest rate of 4.50% with loan terms of 2 to 7 years, tied to anticipated energy savings payback period. A grant incentive of up to 10% of the loan amount (not to exceed $1,000) is provided for borrowers in good standing. Loan origination fee of $75 is required at closing. Loans are unsecured and fully amortized with at least a 1.0:1.0 ratio on annual energy savings payback. Loan advances cannot exceed the total project cost minus any other grant incentive funding received from State, Federal Government, EnSave, or MARBIDCO. No collateral required; personal guarantee required for borrowers and business entities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline stated; ongoing program with rolling applications processed in order received

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of equipment or technology related to lowering business-related energy consumption, based on recommendations from a qualified third-party energy auditor. Loan amounts cannot exceed total project cost less any grant funding from State, Federal Government, EnSave, or MARBIDCO. Energy efficiency improvements in buildings and operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide availability in rural Maryland. The Upper Shore Regional Council (USRC) offers an additional equity incentive targeting farmers in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties to help meet down-payment requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides low-cost financing to help eligible applicants start up or expand small- and medium-sized USDA-inspected livestock processing facilities in Maryland for processing meat, poultry, seafood, and blue catfish. Established by MARBIDCO to complement USDA's Meat and Poultry Intermediary Lending Program, it aims to increase processing capacity in the state. The program offers loans ranging from $250,000 to $2,500,000 at a fixed interest rate of 4.00% with a 0.25% loan origination fee (maximum $5,000). Financing is provided through standalone MARBIDCO loans or cooperative arrangements with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, and USDA Farm Service Agency. Large-sized meat and poultry processing companies are not eligible.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $250,000 to $2,500,000 at a fixed interest rate of 4.00% with a 0.25% loan origination fee (maximum $5,000). Veteran interest rate reduction available: 0.25% reduction for qualifying veterans. Loan proceeds can be used to purchase real estate, construct new or expand existing livestock processing facilities, and purchase equipment. Loan terms correspond to the useful life of assets with an initial interest-only period of up to 12 months. Borrowers must provide at least 7.5% equity contribution, and MARBIDCO will match on a dollar-for-dollar basis up to 10% of project costs (capped at $250,000). Applicants constructing new facilities must demonstrate minimum working capital of 10% of project cost. Personal guarantees are required unless borrower provides 20% equity contribution. Financing is provided through cooperative arrangements with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, and USDA Farm Service Agency.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Oyster Shucking House Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program established by MARBIDCO through 2022 legislation (Senate Bill 830) to help finance the cost of eligible seafood processing projects, including historic oyster shucking facilities, and to increase the amount of oyster shells retained in the state and returned to the Chesapeake Bay. Low-cost financing is provided specifically for oyster shucking house operations and related seafood processing infrastructure through cooperative arrangements with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, and USDA Farm Service Agency. Loans up to $250,000 are available for qualifying oyster processing business projects. The program is funded with $1 million.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from a minimum of $25,000 to a maximum of $250,000, with the loan amount capped at $25,000 for each full-time or seasonal full-time job created or retained. Fixed interest rate of 3.25% with no origination fee. Loan terms correspond to the useful life of the assets being financed, following an initial interest-only period of up to 6 months. An equity contribution of at least 3% of the project's total cost is required from the borrower. In Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties, MARBIDCO will match the equity contribution on a dollar-for-dollar basis, up to 5% of the project cost with a cap of $12,500. Working capital requirements must be demonstrated: 15% of project cost for new facility construction or 10% for other applicants. Low-cost financing is provided through cooperative arrangements with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, and USDA Farm Service Agency. Loans can be standalone or combined with other MARBIDCO programs. Potential debt forgiveness may be available based on oyster shell returned to DNR.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Remote Setting Shellfish Aquaculture Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides affordable, subsidized financing to commercial watermen, individuals, and businesses who want to start or expand shellfish remote-setting aquaculture operations, such as raising oysters or clams in tanks. Remote setting is a process for growers to produce cost-effective seed oysters for aquaculture. The program covers equipment and supplies including seed (larvae), shell substrate, tanks, pumps, blowers, valves, and heaters needed for the operation.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $5,000 to $30,000 with a term of 5 years for loans $5,000–$15,000 and 6 years for loans $15,001–$30,000. Borrowers pay interest only during the first year, then make regular amortizing payments in subsequent years. The final year of loan repayments is forgiven for borrowers in good standing, effectively providing a subsidy of between 22% and 27% of the principal. The interest rate is 5.25% with no application fee. Borrowers must contribute at least 10% equity as a cash contribution. Equipment and supplies eligible for funding include seed (larvae), shell substrate, tanks, pumps, blowers, valves, tank heaters, advertising, workboat expenses, vehicle expenses, salaries and wages, labor hired, consultants, consumable equipment, repairs and maintenance, freight and trucking, gasoline and fuel, insurance, rent of machinery and equipment, rent of farm/pasture, storage and warehousing, utilities, and other business expenses related to commercial remote setting aquaculture projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest loan program providing gap financing to agricultural and resource-based industry enterprises, including poultry operations, farming ventures, forestry, seafood businesses, equine and horticulture operations, and food/fiber processing projects. Established by MARBIDCO to meet unique financing needs of Maryland farm, forestry, and seafood businesses, focusing on entrepreneurship and business innovation to help agricultural and resource-based businesses innovate, diversify, and exploit emerging market opportunities. MARBIDCO offers below-market-rate financing through direct loan or participation loan options, taking a junior collateral lien position behind commercial lenders to help reduce borrower costs and improve debt service coverage ratios. Available as either a Direct Lending program where MARBIDCO provides supplemental loan proceeds in collaboration with a commercial bank, or a Participation Loan program where MARBIDCO partners with lenders like Horizon Farm Credit and Colonial Farm Credit. MARBIDCO takes the junior collateral lien position behind the commercial lender in participation loans and aims to graduate borrowers to conventional commercial financing over several years. The participation loan program uses a 'First Lien / Last Out' structure where MARBIDCO purchases up to 49% interest in the first priority promissory note. Direct loans are available up to $600,000 for real estate and poultry house construction, $300,000 for equipment and fixed assets, or $1,000,000 for large-scale food and fiber processing projects. Participation loans are available up to $700,000 for real estate and poultry construction, $350,000 for equipment, or $1,000,000 for processing projects. Funds can be used for purchasing land and capital equipment necessary for production and processing activities, business operations, expansion, environmental or water-quality enhancement projects, on-farm and off-farm value-added processing, niche product development, agri-tourism, and renewable energy projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct loans up to $600,000 for real estate and poultry house construction, $300,000 for equipment and fixed assets, or $1,000,000 for large-scale food and fiber processing projects (not more than 25% of project cost). Participation loans up to $700,000 for real estate and poultry construction, $350,000 for equipment, or $1,000,000 for processing projects. MARBIDCO provides 20% to 40% of total commercial financing needed in direct loans, supplementing commercial bank or public-sector lender financing, with MARBIDCO's share in participation loans ranging from 30% to 49%. Direct loan interest rates: 4.75% for first 3 years, 5.25% for next 3 years, 5.75% for remaining term, plus 1% origination fee. Participation loan rates: 4.25% with optional lender servicing fee up to 0.75% (5% maximum total). Veteran rate reduction of -0.25% available under Hometown Heroes incentive. Direct loan terms are 5 to 7 years; land loans 10 to 30 years typically with 10-year balloon. Participation loan terms align with partnering lender terms, including mandatory 15-year MARBIDCO balloon payment. MARBIDCO takes a junior collateral lien position behind the commercial lender in participation loans. No MARBIDCO application or origination fees charged for participation loans. Loans can also support environmental or water-quality enhancement projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: A subsidized loan program partnership between the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) providing affordable financing to commercial watermen, individuals, and businesses who want to start or expand shellfish aquaculture operations for oysters, clams, and other shellfish in the Chesapeake and Coastal Bays of Maryland. MARBIDCO offers affordable, subsidized loans for substrate, seed, and capital equipment needed for oyster and other shellfish farming, including oyster-growing cages, harvesting equipment, and refrigeration units. The program includes principal forgiveness components and can be used in conjunction with NRCS EQIP or Chesapeake Bay Watershed Initiative Grants. University of Maryland Extension provides training and business planning assistance.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans range from $5,000 to $100,000, with subsidized interest rates starting at 3.00% (first one to three years, interest-only period) up to a maximum of 5.25%. Loan terms vary by purchase type: substrate and seed up to 5 years, capital equipment up to 7 years, blended purchases up to 6 years. First-time borrowers receive 40% principal forgiveness (up to $100,000). Existing borrowers in good standing receive 25% principal forgiveness on loans between $100,001 and $300,000. No loan origination fees. Minimum 10% equity contribution required from borrower. Up to $2.2 million available statewide for aquaculture projects. Financing available for seed, equipment, and facility infrastructure including oyster-growing cages, harvesting equipment, and refrigeration units. Grant funds can be assigned to reduce loan balance, with principal forgiveness calculated on remaining balance after grants applied. Quarterly repayment required.

structured_extraction.program_description: An affordable loan program that helps Maryland landowners and agribusinesses establish or expand vineyards, orchards, and hop yards, and develop wineries by providing low-cost financing in partnership with private commercial lenders, Farm Credit Associations, and USDA Farm Service Agency. The program is designed to meet the unique financing needs of Maryland's rural landowners and agricultural entrepreneurs. Addresses the 3-4 year production timeline before vines produce their first commercial crop. Loans range from $15,000 to $100,000 with two repayment options: Option 1 offers 5.00% interest for the first three years, then 6.25% thereafter with adjustable principal payments; Option 2 offers a fixed 6.25% rate with the option to make interest-only payments for the first three years. A 1% loan origination fee applies. The program aims to increase acreage of viable commercial vineyards and tree fruit orchards in Maryland. Home Town Heroes Interest Rate Reduction of 0.25% (25 basis points) is available for U.S. military veterans with honorable discharge.

Designed to assist both generational and beginner commercial watermen in obtaining necessary equipment or workboats for seafood harvesting operations. The revolving loan fund was established by MARBIDCO to provide affordable commercial capital and credit to Maryland watermen, with support especially for those who faced challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic. Loan amounts range from $7,000 to $40,000 depending on the type of purchase.

Lifetime aggregate limit of $40,000. Repayment includes a 6-month interest-only period followed by 4 to 6 years of quarterly amortizing payments (principal and interest). Loan forgiveness is available for the final 25% of payments if all payments are made on time. No collateral is required. Commercial watermen may purchase tangible equipment including boats, motors, and harvesting gear. Seafood processors may purchase only seafood processing equipment. All equipment purchased must have a useful lifespan of at least 7 years.

structured_extraction.program_name: Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program (Next Gen) / Small Acreage Next Generation Program (SANG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Agricultural Resource-Based Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) that provides down payment assistance and financing to young, beginning, or first-time farmers purchasing agricultural properties. The program includes both a general Next Gen track for farmland typically over 50 acres and a Small Acreage Next Generation Program (SANG) track for properties between 10 and 49 acres. Next Gen provides assistance representing up to 51% of fair market value (capped at $500,000), while SANG provides down payment assistance representing 30% to 60% of fair market value (capped at $500,000 or $6,000 per acre). Assistance covers the land-only fair market value in exchange for a permanent agricultural conservation easement. The program helps overcome high farmland costs and limited access to capital by collaborating with commercial or farm credit lenders. After settlement, landowners must enroll in an Agricultural District program and maintain a permanent easement through an approved program. If no permanent easement is procured within the specified timeframe (4 years if county is default easement holder, 7 years if MARBIDCO designates easement holder), MARBIDCO ensures permanent preservation through an easement. The SANG track in Washington County provides automatic permanent preservation at the time of settlement without requiring pursuit of a permanent easement after settlement. The program preserves agricultural land from future development by temporarily relinquishing development rights to support eventual permanent preservation. SANG operates in partnership with the Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission (SMADC) for five Southern Maryland counties (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, and St. Mary's).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Under Next Gen, MARBIDCO pays up to 48% to 51% of the fair market value of farmland only, with a maximum of $500,000 per applicant. A $2,500 closing transaction fee is collected at settlement. The farmer then has either 4 years (if county is default easement holder) or 7 years (if MARBIDCO designates easement holder) to sell a permanent conservation easement to a rural land preservation program and repays MARBIDCO the original option purchase amount plus a 3% administrative fee. Under SANG, MARBIDCO provides down payment assistance representing 30% to 60% of the fair market value of the land, capped at $500,000 or $6,000 per acre, along with financing assistance provided in collaboration with commercial or farm credit lenders. A commercial lender must be involved in all transactions. If a farmer cannot sell a permanent easement within the specified timeframe, MARBIDCO exercises the option at no additional cost and a third-party default easement holder (county agricultural land program or private land trust) holds the permanent easement. SANG is funded through MARBIDCO and also operates in partnership with the Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission (SMADC) for five Southern Maryland counties (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, and St. Mary's) with $1 million in SMADC State funding. Development rights are temporarily relinquished to support eventual permanent preservation of the land.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Young, beginning, and first-time farmers seeking to purchase agricultural properties and working farmland, including small acreage parcels between 10 and 49 acres, as well as larger farmland typically over 50 acres, who want to preserve agricultural land from future development and face challenges entering agriculture due to high farmland costs and limited access to financial capital. Beginner farmers are defined as those not owning a farm or ranch (or owning less than 9 acres for SANG; less than 20 acres for Next Gen) and not having operated a farm or ranch as a principal operator for more than 10 years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of agricultural land between 10 to 49 acres (SANG) or typically over 50 acres (Next Gen) for long-term agricultural use and preservation with permanent agricultural conservation easement requirements. Properties must qualify for county Agricultural District programs or SANG/Next Gen program and be working farms with agricultural production. Properties should be at least 90% cropland/forage land.

Properties located within designated Priority Preservation Areas, Rural Legacy Areas, or MALPF-eligible areas receive priority consideration. Applicants must contact their county agricultural preservation program office in the county where the farmland is located at least one month before submission. Washington County applicants work with the County's Land Preservation Office. SANG operates in partnership with the Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission (SMADC) for five Southern Maryland counties: Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, and St. Mary's. Talbot County and Queen Anne's County have been identified as areas with successful program recipients.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your county agricultural preservation program office at least one month before submission to discuss suitability of the farm for permanent preservation. Work with the county's agricultural land preservation program office to verify property eligibility and complete the application. Ensure required seller paperwork (Form 1) is received at the county office no later than one month in advance of application submission. Applicant completes Form 2 with required financial documentation including Applicant Statement describing agricultural experience/education, college transcripts or farm training certifications, tax returns (if available), Balance Sheet, Income Statements (past 2 years and Pro Forma), and Debt Repayment Schedule. Farm property seller must complete Form 1. County Program Administrator completes Form 3. Permanent easement holder must be identified from approved holders (county agricultural land program, private land trust, Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation, or local land conservation programs). Develop a detailed farm business plan and negotiate a ratified contract of sale. Contact a commercial lender to understand financing requirements. Submit completed application with all required forms and attachments by 4:00 p.m. on the last business day of each month to the MARBIDCO office in Annapolis. In Washington County, buyers work with the County's Land Preservation Office to complete the application. Applications are evaluated using a point-based scoring system (maximum 160 points with bonus) evaluated on property characteristics, applicant farmer characteristics, and farm business plan quality. Requests are made on a competitive basis. MARBIDCO's Review Committee ranks applications and makes recommendations to the MARBIDCO Board of Directors. After approval, submit a loan commitment letter from your commercial lender. Contact Allison Roe at (410) 267-6807 or aroe@marbidco.org with questions or to submit applications, or contact Washington County at 240-313-2430 or planzone@washco-md.net. The process typically takes approximately 6 to 8 months from submission to completion.

structured_extraction.program_name: Southern Maryland Revolving Loan Fund for Agriculture
structured_extraction.program_description: A revolving loan fund that provides subsidized low-cost financing to agricultural producers in Southern Maryland for smaller agricultural projects that typical commercial lenders might not finance. Loans range from $10,000 to $20,000 with no collateral security pledge required, at a fixed interest rate of 4.50% with loan terms of one to four years following an initial interest-only period. No loan origination fee is charged. Borrowers in good standing receive approximately 20-25% loan forgiveness at the end of the loan term by foregoing the final quarter of amortizing loan payments. Established by Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission (SMADC) and Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO).
