structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For grant applications: Applications are submitted during the designated application window, which typically opens in early January and closes in early April. Applications are posted on the Request for Proposals (RFP) on the Program webpage. The Program Coordinator completes due diligence from April-May. The Spay and Neuter Advisory Board reviews and scores applications from May-July. In August, the SNAB meets to determine funding recommendations and sends them to the Maryland Secretary of Agriculture. Once approved, the Program Coordinator notifies applicants and prepares the Grant Contract (typically mid-to-late September). Applicants sign the contract in September-October. First funding allocation typically arrives mid-to-late December. Grantees must submit Quarterly Grant Progress Reports and a Final Report. For direct services to low-income families and feral cat programs: Contact the MDA-funded organization listed for your county to verify eligibility and apply for services. Check the list of active projects by county to find an organization serving your area. Applicants submit the Maryland Spay/Neuter Grant Application and required documents to their local program location, and applicants will be contacted for scheduling of services. Individuals can download and complete the Spay Neuter Grant application form. Applicants should visit the Maryland Department of Agriculture website or contact their local program location for application details and eligibility requirements. County-level programs may also be accessed by downloading and completing application forms available through local county resources. Separate applications are required for Pet Focused Grants and Feral Cat Focused Grants. Complete applications must include all supporting documents required by the specific grant type instructions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides farmers and landowners with incentive payments to plant streamside buffers on farmland to improve local stream health and Chesapeake Bay water quality. Farmers can establish forest buffers, grass buffers, or watercourse access control areas adjacent to cropland or pastures. The program supports the establishment of conservation buffers that filter water runoff and protect water quality. Farmers can receive up to $4,500 per acre to install a riparian forest buffer with pasture fencing, with a one-time bonus payment of $1,000 per acre for new riparian forest buffers. Payment rates range from $500 per acre for an existing grass buffer to a maximum of $4,500 per acre. Farmers receive 75% of project costs upfront and 25% after verification of planting. Annual maintenance payments of up to $330 per acre per year are available for forest buffers during the first five years after planting. Contracts are for 5 or 10 years.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Farmers receive payment for installing and maintaining conservation buffers. Payment rates range from $500 per acre for an existing grass buffer to a maximum of $4,500 per acre to install a riparian forest buffer with pasture fencing. Farmers receive 75% of project costs upfront and 25% after verification of planting. An additional one-time tree bonus payment of $1,000 per acre is available for forest buffers. Annual maintenance payments of up to $330 per acre per year are available for forest buffers during the first five years after planting. Contracts are for 5 or 10 years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual open enrollment period from November 1, 2025 through April 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers, rural landowners, and landowners responsible for managing eligible lands who want to improve water quality while utilizing marginal farmland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to establish and maintain conservation buffers (forest, grass, or watercourse access control areas) on eligible agricultural land adjacent to streams, ditches, or pastures to improve stream and Chesapeake Bay health.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program available in all counties. Eligible land must be cropland or pasture adjacent to a stream, ditch, or watercourse, with highly erodible or hydric soils as determined by the local soil conservation district.
requirements_list: Farmers and landowners must be responsible for management of eligible lands
Leased land requires certification of active lease for buffer contract term or landowner agreement
Must be in good standing with USDA and state cost-share programs
Current Nutrient Management Plan Certification required and must be submitted with application
Eligible land must have established cropping history in pasture, commodity crops, or hay
Land with highly erodible or hydric soils as determined by soil conservation district
Existing buffers or lands enrolled in state or federal programs or mandated by easement are not eligible
Field ditches are not eligible for woody conservation buffers
Buffer must be planted within 1 year of signed agreement
Mowing and hay harvesting allowed; nutrient applications not allowed
Landowner must install riparian forest buffer with pasture fencing
Land must be suitable for streamside buffer planting
Applicants must be farmers
Buffer width: 10-100 feet depending on practice type
All landowners on property deed must sign agreement
Map depicting buffer location and estimated acres required
Compliance with state nutrient management requirements (MD Agric. Code Ann. §§8-801-8-806 and COMAR 15.20.06-08)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district to apply during the annual open enrollment period (November 1, 2025 through April 30, 2026). Submit the completed 2025-26 Buffer Application form along with a map showing buffer location and acreage, signed Nutrient Management Plan Certification Form, and signed IRS Form W-9. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. Soil conservation districts provide free technical assistance. After verification of planting, submit a Claim for Payment form to receive remaining funds. SCD conducts eligibility review and MDA determines eligibility and approves.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides financial assistance to Maryland farmers and organizations working with farmers to implement innovative soil health conservation practices. The program supports practices that minimize soil disturbance, maximize soil cover, enhance biodiversity, and increase the presence of living roots. Selected applicants receive up to $50,000 to support 3 years of enhanced soil health practices, including agroforestry practices such as alley cropping, hedgerow planting, windbreak/shelterbelt establishment, silvopasture, and tree and shrub establishment to improve soil health and build climate resilience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Selected applicants receive up to $50,000 to support 3 years of enhanced soil health practices. Grant recipients receive up to 30% of funds distributed upfront, with the remainder distributed annually in spring following verification of progress (4 payments total). Funds may be used to support implementation of conservation practices including equipment purchase, project staff and administrative time, and research costs. Labor must be directly related to project implementation. Ineligible uses include overhead, livestock, imported feed, soil fertility inputs, liming, and startup/operating funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 9, 2026 at 5:00 pm EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual farmers, groups of farmers operating in Maryland, and individuals or organizations working with farmers in Maryland whose agricultural operations have a gross annual income of $2,500 or more (or $2,500 or more of donated agricultural products if a non-profit) and/or manage 8 or more animal units. Farmers and landowners in Maryland with agroforestry projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of conservation practices including cover crops, conservation tillage, pasture and hay planting, conservation cover, critical area planting, conservation crop rotation, nutrient management, integrated pest management, prescribed grazing, soil carbon amendment, and agroforestry practices such as alley cropping, hedgerow planting, windbreak/shelterbelt establishment, silvopasture, and tree and shrub establishment. Funds may be used for equipment purchase (with preference for rental, used, or leveraging matching funds), project staff and administrative time, and research costs. Eligible uses also include establishment of annual or perennial grass and/or forbs for pasture, hay, or cover, and woody plant establishment for tree and shrub planting projects. Ineligible uses include overhead, livestock, imported feed, soil fertility inputs, liming, and startup/operating funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to agricultural operations operating in Maryland statewide with no minimum or maximum acreage requirements.
requirements_list: Agricultural operation(s) must have gross annual income of $2,500 or more (or $2,500 or more of donated agricultural products if a non-profit entity) and/or manage 8 or more animal units (8,000 pounds of live animal weight)
Applicants must provide proof of compliance with Maryland's nutrient management requirements at time of application by submitting a Current Nutrient Management Plan Certification Form

Project must focus on soil health practices
Agroforestry practices eligible
For grazing projects: completion of grazing plan template or existing NRCS grazing plan with maps detailing current and proposed paddock division
For tree and shrub planting projects: applicants must detail planting plans and submit templates with species selection and planting timeframes/methods
For grass and forb planting projects: applicants must complete the Grass and Forb Planting Template with species selection and planting information
Must answer all narrative questions (10-page limit, not including images)
Must submit project narrative via email as Word/PDF attachment or print and mail
Must include separate project budget
Must demonstrate soil health goals and proposed conservation practice changes
Must provide three-year implementation timeline
Must include soil health outcome measurements and tracking plan
Must describe technical assistance/expertise being leveraged
Must address carbon sequestration and/or GHG emission reduction benefits
Must describe post-grant maintenance and expansion plans
Must describe experience with local Soil Conservation District (SCD) or NRCS
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a competitive proposal including project narrative (answering 9 questions with 10-page limit), budget, and appropriate templates for conservation practices during the program's open enrollment period. For specific practices, applicants download applicable templates (Grazing Plan, Tree and Shrub Planting, Grass and Forb Planting, or Cover Crop), complete them with project details and supporting documentation, and submit via email as Word or PDF attachment or printed and mailed to the MDA. Grant award recipients will be contacted by March 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Training course that enables farmers to comply with Maryland's nutrient management requirements. Farmers who apply nutrients to 10 acres or more must complete a 2-hour training course every three years. Free in-person and online 2-hour training sessions are offered multiple times throughout the year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person and online 2-hour training sessions offered multiple times throughout the year to help farmers meet state nutrient management compliance requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing through April 9, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers who apply nutrients to 10 acres or more
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training to understand nutrient management requirements and best practices
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide (Maryland)
requirements_list: Apply nutrients to 10 acres or more
Complete 2-hour training course every three years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for available in-person or online training sessions through University of Maryland Extension website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Organic Certification Cost Share Program (OCCSP) provides reimbursement to producers and handlers certified by USDA-accredited certifiers to help cover the costs of organic certification. Funding comes from the Farm Bill and is subject to annual USDA appropriations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Producers and handlers certified by USDA accredited certifiers receive reimbursement for 75% of certification fees, up to a maximum of $750 per scope. Reimbursement cannot be issued until the producer is issued a certificate.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: As of August 2025, USDA has not yet announced funding for 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Producers and handlers certified by USDA accredited certifiers in Maryland seeking reimbursement for organic certification costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement covers 75% of organic certification fees, up to $750 per scope.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland producers must submit to MDA. Non-MDA certified producers must be in Maryland to receive reimbursement.
requirements_list: Must be certified by a USDA accredited certifier
Maryland producers must submit Cost Share Application to MDA Organic Certification Program
Non-MDA certified producers must submit a copy of their certification fees invoice with their cost share application
Reimbursement cannot be issued until the producer is issued a certificate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Producers submit the Cost Share Application to the MDA Organic Certification Program. Non-MDA certified producers must include a copy of their certification fees invoice. Reimbursement is provided after certification is issued.

structured_extraction.program_description: An optional registration program for producers who gross $5,000 or less annually in organic agricultural sales. Registered exempt operations are listed on MDA's website as compliant with National Organic Program regulations. Exempt from certification but must comply with National Organic Program (NOP) standards for production, handling, and labeling. Allows small-scale organic producers to represent products as "organic" without full certification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exempt producers may voluntarily register with MDA to be listed as a registered exempt operation on MDA's website. The registration fee is $30. Exempt registrations must be updated annually to maintain listing on MDA's website. Exempt producers must still comply with all National Organic Program regulations, including recordkeeping requirements. Allows small-scale organic producers to represent products as "organic" without full certification. Must maintain listing on MDA's website and in MDA Brochure through annual filing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual filing requirement
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small-scale organic agricultural producers in Maryland with gross organic agricultural sales of $5,000 or less annually who choose to register as exempt operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registration provides public listing on MDA's website as a compliant exempt operation. Application fee: $30.00.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Operations must be located in Maryland. Statewide program.
requirements_list: Gross organic agricultural sales must total $5,000 or less annually

No prohibited substances applied to fields for last 3 years
No ionizing radiation, GMOs, or sewage sludge in production
Maintain buffer zones around organic production areas

Registration must be renewed annually to remain listed on MDA's website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free service that collects and safely disposes of unusable, unwanted, banned, or expired pesticides from current or retired farmers and agricultural producers. The program collects any EPA or USDA-registered pesticide products and other identifiable pesticide materials, with unknown materials sampled and tested by the Maryland Department of Agriculture before collection to ensure safe disposal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is a free service funded by licensing, certification, and registration fees collected from pesticide businesses, certified applicators, and pesticide manufacturers. MDA contracts a licensed hazardous waste hauler to collect pesticide materials directly from storage sites and transports them to an EPA-approved disposal facility (incinerator or hazardous waste landfill) at no cost to the participant.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 15, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current or retired farmers and agricultural producers, including orchardists, nurserymen, greenhouse operators, and Christmas tree growers. Not available to homeowners with household pesticides or pesticide dealers/commercial applicators unless approved by MDA.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Collection, transportation, and safe disposal of unusable, unwanted, banned, or expired pesticide materials
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available throughout Maryland (all 23 counties and Baltimore City); specific service areas determined by MDA review
requirements_list: Must be a current or retired farmer or agricultural producer
Must complete and submit the registration form with grower name, address, county, contact person, and site address
Must provide accurate pesticide inventory with brand name, active ingredient, EPA/USDA registration number, formulation, container type, quantity, size, and condition
Must provide directions and map to pesticide storage site
Storage site must be accessible for MDA inspector verification and hazardous waste hauler collection
Samples may be collected for unknown or unlabeled pesticides for testing
Submit completed form by January 15, 2025
Pesticides must have EPA or USDA registration number or be identifiable as pesticide
Exclude: fertilizers, antifreeze, motor oil, household pesticides
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the fillable registration form listing name and amount of each pesticide and submit via email to pest.reg@maryland.gov or mail to the Pesticide Regulation Section by January 15, 2025. An MDA inspector will contact the applicant to schedule a site visit to verify information and pesticide materials. Once MDA has a complete inventory of materials needing disposal, a licensed hazardous waste hauler collects the pesticides and transports them to an EPA-approved disposal facility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Poultry and Rabbit On-Farm Processing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary certification program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture that allows FSIS inspection exempt producers to slaughter and process poultry (less than 20,000 per year) and rabbits for intrastate sale to restaurants, retailers, and farmers markets. Certified producers can sell whole or parts (but not ground meat) anywhere within Maryland. The program includes training, label approval, and compliance with federal, state, and local regulations. Producers may also store meat from USDA inspected facilities on-farm under MDA inspection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides online and in-person training (~6 hours) and certification that allows producers to legally slaughter and process poultry and rabbit meat intrastate to retail and food service establishments. Participation requires attendance at MDA required training, passing an exam with 80% or better score, paying a $75 annual certification fee, and complying with program requirements including facility inspections, label approval, and water testing. The program includes follow-up support, guidance on non-compliances, label review and approval, and ongoing annual certification renewal.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: DUE JUNE 30, 2025 for annual renewal; no deadline for initial training registration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small-scale poultry and rabbit producers who want to slaughter and process their own animals for intrastate sale to restaurants, retailers, and farmers markets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; this is a certification and training program rather than a funding program. An annual $75 certification fee is required to maintain certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Intrastate sales only. Applicants must be FSIS inspection exempt producers.

One person from each facility must attend MDA required training and achieve 80% or better on exam

Allow MDA access to conduct inspections
Meat cannot be ground; only whole or parts allowed

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested producers register for the online training course (continuous enrollment, ~6 hours) through University of Maryland Extension or contact Molly Gillingham. After completing self-paced online training and passing exam with 80% or better score, producers receive a training certificate. Producers then complete the On-Farm Rabbit/Poultry Processing Application, submit product labels for approval, pay the $75 annual certification fee, and obtain MDA certification. Annual renewal applications are required by June 30 with updated information, wastewater compliance method, product labels, and the $75 fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cooperative agreement between the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) and USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) that builds resilience in the middle of the food supply chain, provides more and better markets to small farms and food businesses, supports the development of value-added products for consumers, encourages fair prices and fair wages, and establishes new and safe job opportunities. The program supports expanded capacity for aggregation, processing, manufacturing, storing, transporting, wholesaling, and distribution of locally and regionally produced food products.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of grants available: (1) Infrastructure Grants ranging from $100,000 to $3 million for projects related to aggregation, processing, storing, transporting, wholesaling, and distribution of local food products including specialty crops, dairy, grains for human consumption, aquaculture, and other food products excluding meat, poultry, and wild-caught seafood. Projects run for three years. Grant applicants must contribute 50% of total proposed project cost as a match to federal funding. For historically underserved farmers and ranchers and small businesses that qualify under the Small Business Administration including small disadvantaged businesses, women-owned small businesses, and veteran-owned small businesses, the required match is reduced to 25% of total proposed project cost. (2) Simplified Equipment-Only Grants ranging from $10,000 to $100,000 for purchase of special-purpose equipment directly related to project activities, with no cost-sharing required. Eligible uses include cold storage equipment, expanding capacity for processing, aggregation, and distribution, supporting construction of new facilities, improving operations through employee training, modernizing manufacturing, tracking, storage, and information technology systems, and food safety improvements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2024 at 11:59 pm EST
structured_extraction.contact_name: Karen Fedor, Grant Administrator; Martin Proulx, State-Led Supply Chain Coordinator
structured_extraction.program_audience: Underserved farmers and ranchers, new and beginning farmers and ranchers, veteran producers, small and mid-size agricultural producers and food businesses, food processors, local and regional food system stakeholders, small disadvantaged businesses, women-owned small businesses, and other eligible entities operating middle-of-the-supply-chain activities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cold storage equipment, expanding capacity for processing, aggregation, and distribution, supporting construction of new facilities and expansion of existing structures, improving operations through employee training, modernizing manufacturing, tracking, storage, and information technology systems, purchase of special-purpose equipment and special-purpose vehicles (including refrigerated trucks), facility construction and installation, personnel and labor costs, food safety modernization and HACCP training, climate-smart equipment installation that reduces emissions and water consumption, energy-efficient machinery, renewable energy sources, and value-added product development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Facilities must be physically located within Maryland. Majority of agricultural food products must be sourced from Maryland. MDA has a cooperative agreement with USDA Agricultural Marketing Service for $3.8 million dollars to implement this grant program.
requirements_list: Applicants must apply for a minimum award of $100,000 and a maximum award of $3 million for Infrastructure Grants, or $10,000 to $100,000 for Equipment-Only Grants
Infrastructure projects are for three years

Equipment-Only Grants require no cost-sharing

Applicants must be agricultural producers or processors, nonprofit organizations, for-profit entities meeting SBA small business size standards, local government entities, tribal governments, or institutions such as schools, universities, or hospitals operating middle-of-the-supply-chain activities

Projects must comply with all applicable Federal, State, and local regulatory requirements, good engineering practices, construction best management practices, and applicable stormwater pollution prevention controls
Projects must comply with National Historic Preservation Act, Clean Water Act, and environmental justice considerations
Floodplain development permits required when projects impact floodplains
USACE permits required for facility upgrades within wetland areas

Must obtain proper permitting and demonstrate no significant environmental impacts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit the Infrastructure Equipment Grant application or Equipment Grant ONLY application along with the USDA Applicant Environmental Questionnaire, Match Verification Template Letter (for Infrastructure Grants), and Evidence of Critical Resources and Infrastructure Template Letter. A RFSI Budget-Match Worksheet is provided to assist with calculations. Groups of producers must provide letters of support. Applications must include information on Maryland county(ies) benefiting from the project. AMS staff review and request additional environmental compliance information via questionnaire; AMS conducts environmental screening and compliance evaluation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to urban and small-scale producers who want to plant cover crops but do not qualify for traditional cover crop grant programs geared toward larger farm operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $1,500 per grower per year for planting cover crops on less than 10 acres. Growers are reimbursed based on paid receipts for eligible cover crop seed and planting activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 24, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual growers, organized for-profit agricultural businesses, and non-profit organizations that produce farm products generating a minimum of $1,000 in sales or donations annually and operate in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting cover crops on less than 10 acres, including single cereal grains or cover crop seed mixes in open plots/fields, raised beds, or high tunnels.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Operations must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Operation must produce a farm product generating a minimum of $1,000 in sales or donations annually
Farm product must be grown or raised in Maryland
Must comply with all local, state, and federal regulations
Must secure required permits necessary for the agricultural operation
Cover crops must be planted on less than 10 acres
Eligible species include single cereal grains or cover crop seed mixes
Cover crops may be planted in open plots/fields, raised beds, or high tunnels
Maximum payment per grower is $1,500 per year
Reimbursement based on paid receipts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants download the 2026 Small Acreage Cover Crop Program Application and Instructions form, complete it, and submit during the enrollment period. Growers follow cover crop planting recommendations from the seed manufacturer or University of Maryland Extension for eligible species. After planting, they submit paid receipts for reimbursement. They must also download and sign the Requirements and Agreement form before participating.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Farm and Urban Agriculture Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides financial assistance to support small-scale agricultural operations located in urban, peri-urban, rural, and suburban areas. It aims to increase community access to healthy foods by helping farmers improve their management of natural resources by adopting Bay-friendly and climate-smart farming practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers Small Acreage Cover Crop Grants in the spring and fall, and Water and Power Grants for qualifying operations located in urban areas. Specific grant amounts and terms are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, organized for-profit agricultural businesses, or non-profit organizations that operate small-scale farms in urban, peri-urban, rural, or suburban areas and produce a farm product that generates a minimum of $1,000 of sales or donations annually.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support small-scale agricultural operations and help farmers improve their management of natural resources by adopting Bay-friendly and climate-smart farming practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The farm product must be grown or raised in the state of Maryland.
requirements_list: The operation must produce a farm product that generates a minimum of $1,000 of sales or donations annually
The grantee is responsible for all local, state, or federal regulations and permits necessary for the agricultural operation
The farm product must be grown or raised in the state of Maryland

Eligible farm products include agricultural, horticultural, vegetable, or fruit products; livestock, meats, marine food products, poultry, eggs, or dairy products; equine operations; wool, hides, feathers, or honey; or any product of farm, forest, orchard, garden, or water
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Program Administrator for application procedures. Specific application steps are not detailed on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that enhances the competitiveness of Maryland specialty crops including fruits and vegetables, culinary herbs and spices, honey, hops, grapes, maple syrup, Christmas trees and nursery crops. Funding is awarded through a competitive review process guided by industry, nonprofit and government stakeholders. Projects must demonstrate broader impact for a group of similar producers or industry segment, not just benefit a single organization or individual. Grant funding supports specialty crop production and market development initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDA anticipates that approximately $400,000 in funding may be available under this annual competitive grant program. Funds are awarded through a competitive review process. Grant funds will not be awarded for projects that only benefit or provide profit to a single organization, business, institution or individual. Projects must demonstrate potential impact for a broader group of similar producers or industry segment. Allowable costs include: supplies and materials (at actual prices, net of applicable credits), computing devices essential and allocable to the Federal award (under $5,000), training related to project objectives and Federal grants management, and domestic and foreign travel (when in approved budget or with prior written approval and aligned with program purpose). Unallowable costs include: sponsorships, event naming rights/logos, trade show attendance/displays, meeting room reservations, and exhibits not aligned with grant purpose.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual specialty crop producers, nonprofit organizations, and government entities working with specialty crops in Maryland. Projects must benefit a broader group of similar producers or industry segment, not just a single entity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that enhance the competitiveness of specialty crops including fruits and vegetables, culinary herbs and spices, honey, hops, grapes, maple syrup, Christmas trees and nursery crops. Funding supports specialty crop production and market development initiatives. Allowable costs include: supplies and materials (at actual prices, net of applicable credits), computing devices essential and allocable to the Federal award (under $5,000), training related to project objectives and Federal grants management, and domestic and foreign travel (when in approved budget or with prior written approval and aligned with program purpose). Unallowable costs include: sponsorships, event naming rights/logos, trade show attendance/displays, meeting room reservations, and exhibits not aligned with grant purpose.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Funding received by MDA is based on specialty crop acreage and production value on an annual basis.

Must specify project start and end dates

Approved applications forwarded to USDA for final review

Must provide Applicant Certification affirming information completeness and accuracy
Failure to comply may preclude organization from receiving award

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register/login to OneStop portal. Search for Maryland Specialty Crop Block Grant Application. Complete 4-page application form. Download and complete SCBGP Project Profile Template. Upload completed template. Complete Grant Program Accounting System and Financial Capability Questionnaire with organizational and financial information. Review entire application. Submit application. Receive confirmation. Applications are reviewed competitively by industry, nonprofit and government stakeholders.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal-state partnership and state programs offering payments to farmers and landowners to plant trees for environmental, agronomic, and wildlife benefits. The umbrella program includes five distinct programs: CREP, Conservation Buffer Initiative, Healthy Soils Competitive Fund, Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program, and related practices. The program aims to help Maryland achieve its tree-planting goals to capture greenhouse gas emissions and address climate change. Eligible farmers receive $2 for each new tree planted as part of an approved conservation practice, in addition to the regular cost-share rate for the qualifying practice.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple program components offering different assistance: CREP provides land rental payments for 10-15 years with $1,000/acre bonus for riparian forest buffers (new enrollments only). structured_extraction.program_name: Turfgrass Professional Fertilizer Applicator Recertification Training

Participants stay current on nutrient management practices for turf and landscape applications. Also includes certification examination required by the Fertilizer Use Act of 2011 for individuals applying fertilizer to turf on non-agricultural land.

Fee of $105 for in-person Green Industry Professional Pesticide and Fertilizer Applicator Re-certification Seminar in February 2026. Recorded webinars available anytime for self-study. Certification examination with $100 certification fee and $50 business license fee (waived for government employees/agencies) required to pass 50-question multiple choice exam with 70% or better score. structured_extraction.program_name: USDA GAP/GHP Audit and Harmonized Audit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A cooperative program between MDA and USDA/Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) that audits fruit and vegetable producers and handlers for compliance with USDA Good Agricultural Practices and Good Handling Practices standards and Pre Harvest and Post Harvest Harmonized standards. The program verifies compliance with national food safety standards and provides national recognition for producers and handlers meeting audit requirements. Audits cover field operations, harvesting, post-harvest, storage, transportation, and food defense.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDA currently has USDA Specialty Crop grant money available to assist Maryland producers in offsetting USDA audit costs. MDA conducts audits through a cooperative agreement with USDA/AMS to verify compliance with USDA GAP/GHP standards and Pre Harvest and Post Harvest Harmonized standards. Producers that are USDA certified receive national recognition. Audit costs cover food safety standards addressing water quality, sanitation, pest control, worker health and hygiene, field sanitation, packing facility operations, storage, transportation, food security, and trace-back. Initial audit requests must be made no later than two weeks prior to the end of the growing/harvesting/packing season.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland producers and handlers of fruits and vegetables, including farms, packinghouses, greenhouses, wholesale distribution centers, and repacking operations seeking national certification and recognition for compliance with USDA good agricultural and handling practices standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds offset the costs of USDA GAP/GHP and Harmonized audits to verify compliance with national food safety standards for produce production and handling, including water quality, sanitation, pest control, worker health and hygiene, field sanitation, packing facility operations, storage, transportation, food security, and trace-back.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state program created in 1975 (previously known as the circuit breaker credit) that allows homeowners to receive credits against their property tax bill if property taxes exceed a fixed percentage of their gross household income. The program sets a limit on the amount of property taxes homeowners must pay based on their income level. Credits are calculated based on the amount by which property taxes exceed a percentage of household income using a formula that applies 0% of the first $8,000 of combined household income, 4% of the next $4,000, 6.5% of the next $4,000, and 9% of all income above $16,000. Only taxes resulting from the first $300,000 of assessed valuation are covered. The program provides property tax credits for low-income, blind, and disabled veteran homeowners and their surviving spouses to help reduce their tax burden. Originally created to provide assistance for the elderly, the program is now available to people of all ages based on income requirements. Credits are displayed on tax bills and reduce the amount due. If credit is issued after taxes are paid, a refund is issued to the taxpayer. Available statewide through county offices and the Maryland One-Stop Portal, with local supplement programs in Baltimore County, St. Mary's County, Queen Anne's County, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Charles, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, and Washington counties that provide additional credits to homeowners whose property taxes exceed specified limits tied to household income. Combined State of Maryland and Montgomery County credits averaged $1,276 for eligible senior residents. Taxpayers age 70 and older may file retroactively for up to three years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual tax credit granted based on household income in relation to property tax obligation. The credit is calculated based on the amount by which property taxes exceed a percentage of household income. The formula applies 0% of the first $8,000 of combined household income, 4% of the next $4,000, 6.5% of the next $4,000, and 9% of all income above $16,000. Only taxes resulting from the first $300,000 of assessed valuation are covered. Credits reduce property tax liability and are displayed on tax bills. If credit is issued after taxes are paid, a refund is issued to the taxpayer. Credits are applied directly to real property tax bills of qualified homeowners to reduce their annual tax obligation. Property tax credits are also provided for low-income, blind, and disabled veteran homeowners and their surviving spouses. Homeowners who file and qualify by April 15 receive the credit deducted from their initial July tax bill. Those filing after April 15 but by October 1 receive a revised tax bill or refund check. Approved credits for applications received after May 1 will be refunded. For Baltimore County, property taxes eligible for this credit do not include metropolitan charges, buildings or portions used for business purposes, taxes for excess land acreage, or other buildings. The County Supplemental Credit applies to county property taxes only. St. Mary's County residents age 70 and over can receive an additional credit equal to or up to the amount of the remaining tax bill, less the Bay Restoration Fund fee. Baltimore County offers a Supplemental Credit that applies to county property taxes only and is granted one time only to homeowners who qualify for the State HOTC and have a documented hardship on the property. Applications available online through the Maryland One-Stop Portal, via the Online Tax Credit Application at https://www.taxcredits.sdat.maryland.gov, or at local county tax offices.

The exemption applies to personal property such as manufacturing equipment and machinery used directly in the manufacturing or R&D process. Leased equipment may also qualify if used for manufacturing or research and development purposes. The exemption covers equipment categories including lease number, lessor information, acquisition and installation dates, cost, lease terms, and equipment description.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state property tax relief program providing direct payments to qualified renters with incomes below specified limits. The program recognizes that renters indirectly pay property taxes as part of their rent and deserve similar relief as homeowners. Eligible renters can receive an annual rent reimbursement or credit of up to $1,000 based on the relationship between rent and income, calculated using a formula that assumes 15% of annual occupancy rent (excluding utilities and other fees) goes toward payment of property taxes. The credit is calculated based on the difference between 15% of annual rent and a tax threshold determined by income. Montgomery County provides an additional supplement equal to 50% of the State credit to all renters who receive the State credit. The program is designed to help reduce housing costs and provide tax liability relief to qualifying individuals and is administered statewide through the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, with local availability through county resources.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit or annual rent reimbursement of up to $1,000 paid as a direct check from the State of Maryland. The credit amount is calculated based on the relationship between rent and income. The plan assumes that 15% of occupancy rent (excluding utilities and other fees) goes toward payment of property taxes. Credits are calculated using a formula that compares 15% of annual occupancy rent against a tax limit based on combined household income. The credit is the difference between 15% of annual rent and a tax threshold determined by income. Reimbursements are provided to residents who qualify based on gross household income in relationship to fixed amount of rent charged. Montgomery County provides an additional County Supplement equal to 50% of the State credit; there is no separate application for the County Supplement—the County automatically calculates and sends it directly to the renter as a check.

Seeking tax relief and housing cost assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit or reimbursement is applied to property taxes that renters indirectly pay as part of their rent or towards rent paid on the renter's primary residence. The dwelling must be the renter's principal residence in Maryland. To help reduce housing costs and lower tax liability.

Applications must be mailed to the State Department of Assessments & Taxation in Baltimore. Montgomery County residents who receive the State credit also receive an additional County Supplement.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Property Tax Exemptions for Veterans with 100% Service-Connected Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax exemption available to disabled veterans with a disability determined by the Veterans Administration to be 100% service-connected, permanently, and totally disabling, or 100% permanently unemployable. Eligible veterans, disabled active duty service members, certain un-remarried surviving spouses, and surviving spouses of military personnel killed in the line of duty may receive a complete exemption from real property taxes on their principal dwelling house, surrounding yard, lot or curtilage, and structures necessary to use the property as a residence, such as a garage or utility shed. An Attorney General's Opinion provides that the exemption may also be granted where the rating is less than 100% disability if the Veterans' Administration finds that the veteran is permanently unemployable.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: A complete exemption from property taxes on the disabled veteran's principal residence dwelling, including the lot or curtilage and necessary structures such as garages or utility sheds. The exemption covers the dwelling house and surrounding yard for eligible veterans with permanent, total service-connected disabilities or permanent, total unemployable service-connected disabilities as determined by the Veterans Administration. The disabled veteran must own the dwelling and it must be their principal residence. Applications can be submitted at any time without meeting the September 1 filing deadline. Surviving spouses of eligible veterans may also be eligible for full property tax exemption on their primary residence. Surviving spouses of active duty military personnel who died in the line of duty are eligible for exemption on their dwelling house. Refunds of previously paid property taxes may be available under Tax Property Article 7-208.

Contact the DVMF service program office for assistance with VA disability verification. Disabled veterans and surviving spouses may apply at any time and do not have to meet the September 1 filing deadline. Applications can be filed for refunds of previously paid taxes.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complete exemption from real property taxes on the dwelling house, lot, and surrounding yard (including necessary structures such as garages or utility sheds) for eligible veterans with permanent, total service-connected disabilities determined by the Veterans Administration to be 100% service connected, or 100% permanently unemployable. Eligible veterans and surviving spouses may have their qualifying dwelling house and surrounding yard exempted from real property taxation. In Baltimore County, eligible individuals may also receive a refund of property taxes paid for up to three years before the exemption takes effect. The disabled veteran must own the dwelling and it must be their principal residence. An Attorney General's Opinion provides that the exemption may also be granted where the rating is less than 100% disability if the Veterans' Administration finds that the veteran is permanently unemployable. Applications can be submitted to the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, through local county assessor offices, or to the Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families. Disabled veterans may apply at any time and do not have to meet the September 1 filing deadline.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline; veterans and surviving spouses may apply at any time. Standard deadline is by September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year, but disabled veterans do not have to meet this deadline.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland State Department of Assessments & Taxation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are veterans with 100% service-connected disability ratings from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs; also includes disabled active duty service members, certain un-remarried surviving spouses, and surviving spouses of military personnel killed in the line of duty.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Principal residence dwelling, lot, surrounding yard, and associated structures such as garages or utility sheds. In Baltimore County, eligible individuals may also receive a refund of property taxes paid for up to three years prior to receiving the exemption.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties: Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. The property must be located in Maryland. Contact your local Maryland assessment office for specific eligibility details for your county.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out and submit the appropriate exemption application form based on your eligibility category (disabled veteran, active duty service member, surviving spouse of veteran, or surviving spouse of military casualty) to your local Maryland assessment office or the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. Include required documentation such as the DD-214 form, most recent VA rating notification packet, and proof of Maryland residency. For active duty service members, obtain medical certification from a physician and active duty certification from your Commanding Officer. Contact the DVMF service program office for assistance with VA disability verification. For a refund in Baltimore County, first file for and receive an exemption from SDAT, then submit a copy of the approved exemption to the Baltimore County Council along with a letter requesting the refund. Applications can be submitted at any time, and disabled veterans do not have to meet the September 1 filing deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouse of Military Casualty Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax exemption for the principal residence of a surviving spouse of an individual who died in the line of duty while in active military service. The exemption provides a complete exemption from property taxes on the principal residence of a surviving spouse of a military casualty, provided the dwelling is owned by the surviving spouse and meets specific criteria regarding ownership or acquisition timing. The dwelling must be owned by the surviving spouse and meet one of the following criteria: it was owned by the individual who died in the line of duty at the time of death, it was acquired by the surviving spouse within 2 years of the death if either the individual or surviving spouse was domiciled in Maryland as of the date of death, or it was acquired after qualifying for the exemption on a former dwelling. The surviving spouse must be unremarried.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation that helps homeowners of limited income avoid tax sale of their home by diverting vulnerable homeowners from the tax sale process into an alternative loan program. The program provides protection for at least three years, removes eligible homeowners from the tax sale process, connects them with resources and support services, and assists with paying delinquent property taxes owed. It minimizes tax collection costs and allows homeowners to remain in their homes and retain their principal residence. The program includes county-level loan programs such as the Calvert County and Talbot County Homeowner Protection Programs to help homeowners protect their properties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation; Calvert County; Talbot County
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program helps homeowners pay delinquent property taxes owed and protects their home from tax sale for at least three years by removing eligible homeowners from the tax sale process into an alternative tax lien repayment loan program. Assistance includes connection to resources and support services to help homeowners retain their principal residence, provided they meet income and asset limits. County-level loan programs provide additional property protection assistance to eligible homeowners. Applications must be filed at least four weeks prior to the county's tax sale date to be considered before the sale, but applications may be submitted during any phase of the tax sale process throughout the year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: At least four weeks prior to the county's tax sale date to be considered prior to the sale; applications accepted during any phase of tax sale process throughout the year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited-income homeowners whose home is their principal residence and who are in tax sale or at risk of tax sale, including those age 60 or older, those receiving disability benefits from Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income, those whose home has been their principal residence for 10 or more years, and homeowners in Calvert County and Talbot County seeking property protection assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paying delinquent property taxes, property tax payment, removal from tax sale process, protection from tax sale to maintain principal residence, and property protection.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland with all Maryland counties eligible; applicants must be on their county's tax sale list or in the tax sale foreclosure process. Additional county-level programs available in Calvert County and Talbot County.
requirements_list: Dwelling must be the applicant homeowner's principal residence
Home must be in tax sale or at risk of tax sale
Assessed value must not exceed $300,000
Combined annual household income must not exceed $60,000
Total value of assets must not exceed $200,000, excluding the home's value
Limited income as defined by the program
Homeowner status
Property owed to county/city must be $7,000 or less
Will reside in property July 1, 2026 and for 6 or more months thereafter
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online through a recommended form or submit a paper application. Online applications are processed faster. Applications must be filed at least four weeks prior to the county's tax sale date to be considered before the sale, but applications may be submitted during any phase of the tax sale process throughout the year. Applicants can check their home's current assessment on the SDAT website to verify eligibility before applying. Priority enrollment is given to homeowners aged 60 or older, those receiving disability benefits from Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income, or those whose home has been their principal residence for 10 or more years. Enrollment is limited and eligibility does not guarantee enrollment. Calvert County applicants should submit the 2025 Homeowner Protection Program Loan Application. Applicants can contact the State Tax Sale Ombudsman via phone, email, or website to inquire about the program and apply. County-specific loan applications may be available.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides Maryland income tax credits to investors who make qualified investments in certified biotechnology companies headquartered in Maryland. The credit equals 33% of an eligible investment up to $250,000, or 50% up to $500,000 for companies in certain counties. Enhanced credits of 65% up to $575,000 (Level 1) or 75% up to $750,000 (Level 2) are available for investments in Opportunity Zone funds, and 50% up to $500,000 for RISE Zone investments. The credit is refundable if the investor has no Maryland income tax liability. Program supports investment in seed and early-stage biotech companies to promote growth of the biotech industry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors receive an income tax credit equal to 33% of a qualified investment in a Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Company (QMBC) up to $250,000 in credits, or 50% up to $500,000 if the QMBC is located in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset County. Enhanced credits of 65% up to $575,000 (Level 1) or 75% up to $750,000 (Level 2) are available for Opportunity Zone fund investors. RISE Zone enhancement provides 50% credit up to $500,000. The credit is refundable if the investor has no Maryland income tax liability. Investors must make a minimum investment of $25,000. Maximum credit per investor: $250k/year; Maximum credit per company: $1.2M/year, $7M total.

Form A Investor applications: September 15, 2025 at 11:59 p.m. EST. Online Electronic Queue Investor Registration: September 16, 2025 at 9:00 a.m. EST. Program authority ends June 30, 2028.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equity investments in qualified Maryland biotechnology companies. Funds support research and development activities, biological materials and related technology development, and commercial biological or biomolecular product development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Companies must be headquartered and have their base of operations in Maryland. Enhanced credits available for companies in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, and Somerset Counties, and for companies located in Opportunity Zones and RISE Zones. Montgomery County investors may receive supplemental payments from the county program in addition to state credits.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. QMBC submits Form B application through online system beginning August 19, 2025 (ongoing, first-come, first-served) with comprehensive documentation including articles of incorporation, certificates of status, financial statements, business plan, employee records, and IP documentation. 2. Investor submits Form A application through online system September 2-15, 2025 at 11:59 p.m. EST to be eligible for electronic queue registration. 3. Investor receives five-letter username and six-digit reference number via email. 4. Beginning September 16, 2025 at 9:00 a.m. EST, investor registers through Online Electronic Queue Investor Registration using username and reference number. 5. Commerce reviews applications in submission order and issues Initial Certificate of Approval if approved. 6. Investor must make investment within 30 days of certificate issuance and provide proof within 10 days. 7. Commerce issues Final Certificate of Approval and awards tax credit. 8. Investor claims credit on Maryland Tax Return with copy of Final Certificate.

structured_extraction.program_name: Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program supports the development of innovation infrastructure in high-growth industries such as advanced manufacturing, aerospace, agriculture, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, blue technology, cybersecurity, defense, energy and sustainability, life sciences, quantum, sensors and robotics, and clean technology. Launched under the Governor's Innovation Economy Infrastructure Act of 2023, the program reflects Maryland's commitment to economic growth, job creation, and inclusive prosperity. Grants may be used to acquire, construct, rehabilitate, install, improve, or equip eligible innovation infrastructure projects, including labs, manufacturing facilities, equipment, and training programs. The program provides grants to private companies, nonprofit entities, local governments, and colleges and universities. Grant awards range from $333,333 to $2 million based on project scope. Applicants must provide matching funds: 200% for grants up to $1 million and 400% for grants between $1 million and $2 million. Funds from other State grant programs do not count toward the matching requirement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive matching grants ranging from $333,333 to $2 million to support infrastructure development in critical innovation sectors. Applicants must provide matching funds equal to at least 200% of the grant amount for grants up to $1 million, and 400% of the grant amount for grants between $1 million and $2 million. Funds from other State grant programs do not count toward the matching requirement. Grants defray the cost of acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, installation, improvement, or equipment of eligible innovation infrastructure projects including wet laboratories, cyber ranges, specialized training spaces, manufacturing facilities, pilot production facilities, integrated end-to-end manufacturing operations, labs, equipment, and training programs. A single organization cannot receive more than $2 million in one fiscal year. Colleges and universities cannot receive more than 50% of the total funds available in a fiscal year. Grant funds must be spent within two years of the agreement date, and the project must be fully operational within two years of the agreement date.

Cannot use grant funds for indirect costs like salaries or management fees.

structured_extraction.program_description: An income tax credit providing 50% of the purchase price for Maryland companies with fewer than 50 employees that purchase cybersecurity goods, products, or services from Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Sellers. The program supports small businesses in protecting their information systems and data while supporting the state's cybersecurity industry. The maximum credit is $50,000 per year, covering up to $100,000 in purchases, with $4 million available annually ($3 million for technology purchases and $1 million for service purchases). Technologies must be proprietary products designed to protect information systems and data, and services must align with the most recent National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Commerce runs the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund, which provides grants and loans to small businesses, including those owned by minorities and women, entering the adult-use cannabis industry. The fund also offers grants to Historically Black Colleges and Universities for cannabis-related programs and to business development organizations to train and assist licensed small businesses. Current funding is available for Social Equity Applicants with a conditional cannabis license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants and loans to small businesses entering the adult-use cannabis industry. A specific grant for Social Equity licensees offers funding based on license type: a standard dispensary can receive up to $131,250, a processor up to $183,750, and a grower up to $525,000. Businesses with micro-licenses receive smaller amounts. The grant is paid in four tranches as the business meets specific milestones. Funds can support license application fees, operating costs, capital expenses, and targeted training.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application portal opened on June 3, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses entering the adult-use cannabis industry, with a focus on minority-owned and women-owned companies. Also supports Historically Black Colleges and Universities and business development organizations that train cannabis entrepreneurs. Current funding targets Social Equity Applicants with a conditional cannabis license.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can support license application fees, operating costs, capital expenses, and targeted training to support participation in the adult-use cannabis industry.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through the Maryland Department of Commerce.

Must be at least 51% owned by individuals with a personal net worth not exceeding $1.7 million
Must meet the minimum Adequate Capital Requirement set by the Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA)
Must be an existing business in Good Standing with the State of Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for access to the application portal on the Maryland Department of Commerce website. Required documents include your lottery number, conditional license letter, personal net worth information for all owners, a W-9 form, and proof that your business is in Good Standing with Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A no-interest revolving loan program that provides financing for capital expenses to licensed child care providers who participate in the State Department of Education's Child Care Scholarship Program. The program supports acquisition, expansion, renovation, and new construction of child care facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-interest revolving loans for capital expenses related to child care facilities. Loans up to $50,000 do not require collateral if the applicant owns property. Loans over $50,000 require collateral in the form of owned property. Loans must be repaid within five years after receiving loan proceeds. No prepayment penalties. Applicants must attest to project completion via signed document and are subject to random audits requiring proof of completion and receipts.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application period closed January 30, 2026. Please revisit this webpage for updates on when the next round of funding will occur this calendar year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers in Maryland who participate in the State Department of Education's Child Care Scholarship Program and need financing for capital improvements to their facilities, including existing providers seeking to expand to additional locations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital expenses for child care facilities including acquisition (purchase of existing facilities), expansion (construction or purchase of additional space), renovation (repairs, upgrades), and new construction. Eligible uses include facility improvements, parking lot/driveway expansion (if justified by limited parking), outdoor play space (decks, patios, fences, playgrounds), and furniture for child care facilities. Cannot be used for vehicles, outstanding taxes, existing loan payoff, credit card debt, working capital, or operational expenses such as marketing, payroll, lease or rent expense, supplies, utilities, or to refinance existing debt.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland. Loan proceeds must be used for a child care facility location operating in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Employer Security Clearance Costs (ESCC) Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides income tax credits to businesses for expenses related to federal security clearance costs, construction or renovation of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs), and first-year leasing costs for qualified small businesses performing security-based contract work in Maryland. The program offers three categories of qualified expenses: Security Clearance Administrative Expenses (up to $200,000 per taxable year), SCIF Costs (50% of construction or renovation costs up to $200,000 for a single facility or up to $500,000 per calendar year for multiple facilities), and First Year Leasing Costs for Qualified Small Businesses (up to $200,000 for rental payments during the first year of a lease). Total credits for all businesses are capped at $2 million per calendar year, with pro-rata distribution if applications exceed this cap. Excess credits may be carried forward until fully used.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses may receive income tax credits for three categories of qualified expenses: (1) Security Clearance Administrative Expenses: up to $200,000 per taxable year for costs related to processing security clearance applications, maintaining or upgrading computer systems required for clearances, and training employees to administer the clearance process; (2) Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) Costs: 50% of construction or renovation costs for a single SCIF up to $200,000, or up to $500,000 per calendar year for multiple SCIFs; (3) First Year Leasing Costs for Qualified Small Business: up to $200,000 for rental payments during the first year of a lease for spaces used for security-based contracting work. Total credits for all businesses are capped at $2 million per calendar year, with pro-rata distribution if applications exceed this cap. Excess credits may be carried forward until fully used.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides real property, personal property, and state income tax credits to businesses located in a Maryland enterprise zone or focus area in return for job creation and investments. The program was created in 1982 to encourage revitalization and economic development through commercial development in economically distressed areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: General Income Tax Credit: $1,000 one-time tax credit for each qualified new employee in an enterprise zone, or $1,500 in a focus area. Income Tax Credit for Economically Disadvantaged Employees: $6,000-$9,000 over three years ($6,000-$3,000 per year in enterprise zones, or $9,000-$4,500-$1,500 per year in focus areas). Real Property Tax Credit: Ten-year credit covering 80% of eligible assessment for first 5 years, then decreasing 10% annually to 30% in year 10 in regular zones; steady 80% in focus areas. Personal Property Tax Credit (focus areas only): Ten-year credit covering 80% of eligible assessment for new investment in personal property. State reimburses local jurisdictions 50% of revenue lost from property tax credits (subject to annual budget approval).

structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in Maryland enterprise zones or focus areas seeking to create jobs and make capital investments. County and municipal governments seeking to designate economic development areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits applied against state income tax liability, real property taxes, or personal property taxes. Credits support businesses making capital improvements, hiring new employees, or investing in personal property. Funds used as tax relief incentives for economic development.

Zones must meet at least one of four economic distress criteria: average unemployment rate at least 150% of state or national average, low-income poverty area with family poverty rate at least 1.25 times national proportion, at least 70% of families with incomes less than 80% of median family income, or other qualifying criteria. Specific zones and their expiration dates are listed on the program page.
