structured_extraction.program_description: A state and local tax credit program established in 1982 that encourages business investment, job creation, expansion, and development of underutilized properties within designated enterprise zones across Maryland. The program provides real property, personal property, and state income tax credits for businesses located in one of 34 Enterprise Zones in 19 Maryland jurisdictions or one of designated Focus Areas in return for job creation and capital investments. The program encourages revitalization and economic development through commercial and industrial expansion in economically distressed areas. Businesses receive state income tax credits of $1,000 per new employee or $6,000 per economically disadvantaged employee (spread over 3 years: $3,000 year 1, $2,000 year 2, $1,000 year 3) in standard Enterprise Zones, with enhanced credits in Focus Areas ($1,500 per new employee or $9,000 per economically disadvantaged employee: $4,500 year 1, $3,000 year 2, $1,500 year 3). Local property tax credits provide 80% of eligible assessment for the first 5 years, then decrease by 10% annually for years 6-10 (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%) in standard zones, or 80% for the full 10-year period in Focus Areas on both real and personal property. Businesses in Focus Areas may qualify for personal property tax credits on new investment and enhanced income tax credits for creating new jobs. Special provisions apply for newly constructed mixed office and retail properties, providing 13-year credits. The program helps businesses in designated areas stay and grow, promotes the use of empty or underused properties, and supports county efforts to improve older office and industrial areas. It is a local economic development program established by the Maryland General Assembly that gives local governments legal authority to offer economic incentives, with the state reimbursing local jurisdictions 50% of revenue lost from offering property tax credits (subject to annual budget approval).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses receive state income tax credits and real and personal property tax credits. General income tax credit is $1,000 per qualified new employee in an enterprise zone or $1,500 in a focus area. Income tax credit for economically disadvantaged employees is $3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, and $1,000 third year in an enterprise zone; $4,500, $3,000, and $1,500 respectively in a focus area. Real property tax credits provide 80% of eligible assessment for 10 years (declining 10% annually after year 5 in standard zones, or 80% for full 10 years in focus areas). Personal property tax credits (focus areas only) provide 80% of eligible assessment for 10 years. Real property county and city tax credits based on increase in real property tax assessments from commercial capital investment, decreasing over 10 years. Income tax credits can carry forward for up to 5 years. Tax credits apply to state income tax liability and can be used for general business operations and expansion. Special provisions apply for newly constructed mixed office and retail properties, providing 13-year credits. Additionally, the program may include exemptions from Commercial Building Excise Tax in certain jurisdictions. State reimburses local jurisdictions 50% of revenue lost from property tax credits (subject to annual budget approval). Credits are non-refundable and excess credits can be carried forward up to 5 years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 15 and October 15 each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying new and existing for-profit businesses, individuals, non-profits, government entities, and proprietorships, partnerships, and corporations that make job creation and capital investments in designated Enterprise Zones or Focus Areas in Maryland. This includes businesses in Manufacturing, Warehousing, Research and Development, Corporate/Regional Headquarters, and Service Industries. Also includes property owners, end-user businesses, development companies, commercial enterprises, hospitality operators, and food service/distribution companies. County and municipal governments and local economic development entities are also eligible to establish enterprise zones. In FY 2024, 6,639 companies were certified.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property improvements, personal property improvements, job creation, state income tax credits, and local real property and personal property tax credits for business investment and expansion within enterprise zones and focus areas. Capital investments in construction and renovation of real property, new construction, rehabilitation projects, and new machinery and equipment. Job creation with payroll meeting specified wage requirements. General business operations and expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in one of 34 Enterprise Zones in 19 Maryland jurisdictions or one of designated Focus Areas. Zones must meet at least one of four economic distress criteria: average unemployment rate at least 150% of state or national average, low-income poverty area with family poverty rate at least 1.25 times national proportion, at least 70% of families with incomes less than 80% of median family income, or other qualifying criteria. Anne Arundel County's designated 1,572-acre Enterprise Zone is located in the Brooklyn Park area. In Harford County, the Havre de Grace Enterprise Zone includes the 9,738-acre Aberdeen and Havre de Grace Enterprise Zone, including areas along U.S. Route 40, Aberdeen and Havre de Grace municipalities, portions of Aberdeen Proving Ground, Belcamp, Perryman, and the HEAT Center area, as well as specified business parks. Additional designated zones are located in Edgewood and Joppa. Garrett County has two Enterprise Zones: the Southern Garrett Enterprise Zone (comprising the Southern Garrett Industrial Park and Southern Garrett Business & Technology Park) and the Northern Garrett Enterprise Zone (comprising the Northern Garrett Industrial Park). Baltimore County maintains three Enterprise Zones: North Point, Southwest, and Federal Center at Woodlawn, with Federal Center at Woodlawn bounded by Security Boulevard, Windsor Mill Road, Rolling Road, and nearby landmarks including Security Square Mall, Woodlawn High School, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, and Social Security Administration. Washington County maintains approximately 5,910 acres across two state-designated Enterprise Zones: the Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,410 acres in City of Hagerstown) and the Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres surrounding the Town of Hancock). Baltimore City and Prince George's County operate Focus Areas with distinct tax credit benefits. Not every business in an Enterprise Zone, Sustainable Community, or Opportunity Zone is automatically eligible; certification by the local enterprise zone administrator is required. Use the Enterprise Zone interactive map to verify if an address is within a zone. Applicants can use the My Neighborhood Interactive Map to determine if a property is within an Enterprise Zone. Enterprise zones total approximately 68,893 acres across Maryland with varying expiration dates ranging from 12/14/2022 to 1/3/2030.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax credit program that encourages eligible businesses to expand or relocate in Maryland and to hire qualified veterans, with special provisions for manufacturers. The program promotes manufacturing growth by providing tax incentives for manufacturers that create new jobs, encourages investment in new equipment through accelerated and bonus depreciation, and funds job training and apprenticeship programs. In 2019, the program was expanded to include non-manufacturers locating or expanding in Opportunity Zones. Businesses that create a minimum number of net new full-time positions receive an income tax credit for each newly created job. Manufacturers creating at least 5 new full-time jobs receive a 10-year tax credit equal to 5.75% of wages per eligible position, and businesses employing eligible apprentices receive additional $1,000 credits per apprentice. The credit is equal to $3,000 per new job, increasing to $5,000 per new job if the business locates or expands in a revitalization area (state enterprise zone, federal empowerment zone, DHCD Sustainable Community, or Tier 1 County). The credit increases to $4,000 per job if filled by a qualified veteran employee, or $6,000 per job if filled by a qualified veteran employee in a revitalization area. Small businesses that hire at least one qualified veteran employee receive $2,500 for each qualified veteran employee who has filled the position for at least one year, with a maximum of five qualified veteran employees per credit year. For warehousing and distribution facilities located in Priority Funding Areas, the credit granted is the lesser of $1,000 or 2.5% of annual wages for each new employee in a qualified position. A business may not earn more than $1 million in a credit year, and the program is capped at $4 million in tax credits in a calendar year. Unused credits may be carried forward through the fifth taxable year following the credit year. This includes the More Jobs for Marylanders-Manufacturing Tax Credit, which provides new and existing manufacturers with refundable income tax credits tied to job creation for a 10-year period and encourages additional investment in new equipment through accelerated and bonus depreciation.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits available to new and existing manufacturers that create new manufacturing jobs. The credit is equal to $3,000 per new job. The credit increases to $5,000 per new job if the business locates or expands in a revitalization area (state enterprise zone, federal empowerment zone, DHCD Sustainable Community, or Tier 1 County). The credit increases to $4,000 per job if filled by a qualified veteran employee, or $6,000 per job if filled by a qualified veteran employee in a revitalization area. Small businesses that hire at least one qualified veteran employee receive $2,500 for each qualified veteran employee who has filled the position for at least one year, with a maximum of five qualified veteran employees per credit year. For manufacturers, a 10-year state income tax credit equal to 5.75% of the wages per eligible new position is available for those creating at least 5 new full-time jobs. Additionally, businesses employing eligible apprentices receive a $1,000 tax credit per apprentice. For warehousing and distribution facilities located in Priority Funding Areas, the credit granted is the lesser of $1,000 or 2.5% of annual wages for each new employee in a qualified position. A business may not earn more than $1 million in a credit year. The program is capped at $4 million in tax credits in a calendar year. Unused credits may be carried forward through the fifth taxable year following the credit year. New businesses locating in Tier 1 counties like Garrett County may be eligible for: (1) a refundable credit against the State's income tax; (2) a credit against the State's portion of real property tax; (3) a refund of sales and use tax; and (4) a waiver of fees charged by the State Department of Assessment and Taxation. Existing businesses may be eligible for a refundable credit against the State's income tax. Job training and apprenticeship programs are also supported. A refundable income tax credit for job creation tied to manufacturing activity over 10 years is available, plus accelerated and bonus depreciation for new equipment investment.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible businesses that locate or expand in Maryland and create a minimum number of net new full-time positions, including manufacturing businesses creating new full-time jobs, small businesses that hire qualified veteran employees or apprentices, and non-manufacturers locating or expanding in Opportunity Zones; particularly businesses in targeted regions and Tier 1 counties. New and existing manufacturers are eligible. For-profit businesses creating jobs in Maryland. structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Income tax credit for businesses that create new jobs, hire qualified veteran employees, or employ apprentices; wage expenses for manufacturers; equipment investment; job training and apprenticeship programs. structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties are eligible. Priority Funding Areas include state enterprise zones, federal empowerment zones, DHCD sustainable communities, Baltimore City, incorporated municipalities, the area between I-495 beltway and Washington D.C., the area between I-695 beltway and Baltimore City, and any area in a county designated by the county as a priority funding area. Revitalization areas include state enterprise zones, federal enterprise zones, federal empowerment zones, DHCD sustainable communities, and Tier 1 Counties (Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester). Caroline County requires a minimum of 10 new qualifying positions. Garrett County is a Tier 1 county. Non-manufacturers must locate or expand in Opportunity Zones to be eligible. Warehousing and distribution facilities must be located within a Priority Funding Area as defined by the Job Creation Tax Credit statute. Companies locating to Anne Arundel County are eligible. Program is available statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit enhancement program that helps small businesses access financing by enabling participating lenders to establish a loan loss reserve fund. Based on Maryland Economic Development Article, § 5-1702, the program provides loss reserve accounts for participating financial institutions to support qualified loans. The program provides up to 100% coverage to participating lenders on losses from certain loan defaults, allowing lenders to offer more favorable loan terms to qualifying small business borrowers. The program supports business growth and success in Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland by making it easier for lenders to approve loans that fall slightly outside their normal credit guidelines. Loan amounts range from $10,000 to $1,000,000. Contributions to the reserve account typically come from the lender, borrower, and the State of Maryland, with contributions totaling approximately 6 percent of the loan amount.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A participating lender enrolls a qualifying loan for a small business. The lender, borrower, and the program each contribute to a reserve account. Contribution percentages typically include lender contribution of 1.5% to 2.0%, borrower contribution of 1.0% to 1.5%, matched by the program for a total reserve fund of up to 6% of the original loan amount. Enrolled loan amounts range from $10,000 to $1,000,000. Loans can have terms up to 10 years with fixed or variable interest rates, and can be secured or unsecured. If a loan defaults, the reserve fund covers losses up to 100% of the loss. The program leverages State funds to develop small business loans. The State deposits funds into Loss Reserve Accounts for participating lenders. Loans can be used for lines of credit or term loans and may be combined with other loan programs. Financial institutions receive loss reserve accounts to support lending; state liability is limited to funds in the Loss Reserve Account.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Financial institutions (credit unions, banks, community development financial institutions) with lending operations in Maryland that support small businesses. Small businesses, including nonprofit organizations, that have difficulty obtaining financing and are located in Maryland, particularly those located in Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business financing for start-up, expansion, working capital, or projects located in Priority Funding Areas. Excluded uses include passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, community facilities like fire stations or hospitals, adult entertainment facilities, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, gun shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, and sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide with lending branches in Maryland. Projects in Priority Funding Areas are encouraged. Most Maryland small businesses are eligible statewide. Projects financed must be located in a Priority Funding Area as approved by the Maryland Department of Planning. Applicants must have Maryland lending branches.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For participating financial institutions: Complete application form (new or amended) and submit via email to fpaaworkflowcoordinator.commerce@maryland.gov. The Department reviews and approves enrollment. For small business borrowers: Small business applies to a participating lender. The lender underwrites and determines if the loan is appropriate for enrollment in the program. If approved, the lender, borrower, and program each contribute to a reserve account based on a contribution schedule (typically lender contributes minimum 1.5-2.0%, borrower contributes 1.0-1.5%, and the program matches the combined amount for a total of approximately 6%). The lender submits a one-page Loan enrollment form with summary information to MD CAP via email. If a loan defaults and the lender has completed normal collection methods, at charge-off the lender files a one-page claim form for payment from the reserve account.

Grants provide up to 50% reimbursement of qualified project costs, with a minimum grant award of $10,000 (requiring a total project cost of at least $20,000) and a maximum of $200,000 per year. The program helps increase worker skills for new technologies and production processes, improve employee productivity, and increase employment stability.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A flexible and broad-based state fund that provides conditional grants, loans, and equity investments to assist economic development initiatives. The program supports business attraction and retention, infrastructure development, brownfield redevelopment, arts and entertainment districts, daycare facilities, revolving loan funds, and local strategic planning. It includes five financing capabilities: Strategic Economic Development Opportunities for significant statewide or regional projects, Local Economic Development Opportunities where businesses provide valuable economic development to their local jurisdiction and are a priority of the local governing body, Direct Assistance to local jurisdictions or MEDCO, Regional or Local Revolving Loan Funds, and Special Purpose Programs targeting brownfield revitalization, seafood and aquaculture, animal waste, arts and entertainment, and child care center development. Projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas and support eligible industry sectors. Awards are made on a competitive basis. Assistance is conditional based on the company's commitment to job creation and capital expenditures. The program supports extraordinary economic development opportunities that create and retain employment as well as create significant capital investments. The Economic Development Opportunities Fund (Sunny Day Fund) component promotes Maryland's participation in extraordinary economic development opportunities providing significant returns through job creation and retention and capital investment in priority funding areas, with participants required to provide a minimum capital investment of at least five times the amount of the Sunny Day assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers five financing capabilities: Strategic Economic Development Opportunities with loans not exceeding the lesser of $10 million or 20 percent of the current fund balance (capped at 70 percent of project costs), Local Economic Development Opportunities with loans up to $5 million or conditional loans and grants up to $2 million (assistance cannot exceed 70 percent of total project costs), Direct Assistance to local jurisdictions or MEDCO with total assistance not exceeding $3 million unless the jurisdiction is a qualified distressed county (funds may be used for land acquisition, infrastructure improvements, acquisition of fixed assets, leasehold improvements, up to 70 percent of feasibility study costs, and up to 50 percent of local economic development plan preparation), Regional or Local Revolving Loan Funds, and Special Purpose Programs including loans for brownfield revitalization, seafood and aquaculture, animal waste management, arts and entertainment, and child care center development. For Local Economic Development Opportunities, the local jurisdiction must sponsor the business and participate with a guarantee, direct loan, or grant equal to at least 10 percent of the state's financial assistance. The Economic Development Opportunities Fund (Sunny Day Fund) provides financial assistance for extraordinary economic development opportunities, with participants required to provide a minimum capital investment of at least five times the amount of the Sunny Day assistance. Conditional loans of various amounts are approved for eligible business expansion projects. Assistance is conditional based on the company's commitment to job creation and capital expenditures. $3.5 million was restored to the Fund in Fiscal Year 2014 budget.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Global Gateway Soft Landing Program for Foreign Companies
structured_extraction.program_description: A physical soft landing program that allows foreign companies to establish operations in Maryland by locating staff in partner incubators and accelerators across the state for a consecutive six-month period. Participating companies receive grant funding, office and facility access, business facilities, resources, advisors, networking events, mentoring services, programming, and assistance with business registration and state regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible companies receive a $10,000 grant awarded upon signing an agreement with a Global Gateway partner organization. Funding is provided directly to the partner organization on behalf of the company upon landing. Soft landing program partners provide access to business facilities for up to six months with amenities such as internet and conference space. Services include educational programs and training on business topics, networking events, strategic partnerships, and access to mentors and advisors. Eligible expenses covered by the grant include: rent, utilities, facility access, administrative and program fees, networking events, industry memberships, marketing services, business registration fees, and professional consultations (immigration, accounting, regulatory; maximum $5,000). Companies participate in at least five targeted matchmaking meetings with Maryland companies and organizations. Funds cannot be used for religious aspects, matching other state funds, flights, accommodations, or food.

structured_extraction.program_description: MIDFA promotes private sector investment in economic development projects by providing access to long-term capital markets and reducing lender risk through multiple mechanisms. The program issues private activity revenue bonds (both taxable and tax-exempt) for fixed asset financing and projects including land acquisition, building acquisition, construction, infrastructure, machinery and equipment, and eligible soft costs. MIDFA also provides credit insurance through the Conventional Program (insuring up to 80 percent of financing transactions, up to 90 percent for export transactions, not to exceed $2.5 million) and a Bond Program (insuring bonds up to 100 percent, not to exceed $7.5 million). The program encourages private sector investments and supports small- and medium-sized businesses, historically disadvantaged businesses, manufacturers, not-for-profit entities, day care providers, and businesses in rural areas, with priority for projects located in Priority Funding Areas.

Bonds provide access to long-term capital markets for fixed asset financing including land and building acquisition, construction, infrastructure, machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, leasehold improvements, and certain eligible soft costs.

structured_extraction.program_description: MIDFA promotes private sector investment in economic development projects by providing access to long-term capital markets through taxable and tax-exempt industrial revenue bonds, loan guaranties, and linked deposit programs. The program provides greater access to capital for small- and medium-sized businesses and supports historically disadvantaged businesses and businesses in rural areas through private activity revenue bonds, credit insurance in the form of loan guaranties, and below-market rate loans funded through certificates of deposit. Uses include land acquisition, building acquisition, construction costs, machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, leasehold improvements, eligible soft costs, energy-related projects, and working capital. The Conventional Program insures up to 80% of a transaction, not to exceed $2.5 million (90% for export transactions). The Bond Program insures bonds up to 100%, not to exceed $7.5 million of taxable or tax-exempt bonds. The linked deposit program provides certificates of deposit to lenders as funding sources and pricing incentives to provide below-market rate loans for small businesses in rural areas with high unemployment.

Grants range from $25,000 to $500,000, covering up to 75% of eligible costs for small manufacturers (3-50 employees) and up to 50% for mid-sized manufacturers (51-250 employees). Eligible investments include machinery, equipment, software, training, advanced sensors, data analytics, cloud computing, cybersecurity, and systems integration projects.

Eligible costs include machinery, equipment, software, training, advanced sensors, AI, data analytics, cloud computing, cybersecurity, ERP systems, robots, and systems integration projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Sales and Use Tax Exemption Incentive Program for Data Centers
structured_extraction.program_description: Sales and use tax exemption on qualifying data center personal property purchased or leased for use in data centers located in Maryland. Provided under Senate Bill 397 (2020). Businesses must create new full-time jobs and meet minimum investment thresholds to qualify. Tax exemption incentive for businesses locating or expanding in Maryland as a qualified data center and creating new full-time positions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exemption from Maryland sales and use tax on the purchase or lease of qualified data center personal property including servers, mainframes, network infrastructure, data storage hardware, cabling, switches, wiring, cabinets, battery racks, cable trays, power generation and distribution equipment, radiators, exhaust fans, fuel storage tanks, batteries, cogeneration equipment, and monitoring equipment. The benefit period is 10 years for businesses meeting minimum investment and job creation requirements within 3 years. The benefit period expands to 20 years if the business invests at least $250 million within 10 years. Benefits are subject to annual renewal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA)
structured_extraction.program_description: MSBDFA promotes the viability and expansion of all small businesses in Maryland, with a focus on businesses owned by economically and socially disadvantaged entrepreneurs. The program provides financing and equity investments for working capital, supplies and materials, machinery and equipment acquisition, real estate acquisition, leasehold improvements, business purchase, contract financing, and expansion and growth. The program can also provide bid, payment, and performance bonds. Loans and equity investments range from $25,000 to $1,000,000 and require a minimum 1:1 private capital match with the lender maintaining 20% at risk in debt financing. The program received $45 million in State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) federal funds for distribution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSBDFA provides financing and equity investments through several components managed by a private contractor (Meridian Management Group). The program offers working capital loans, equipment financing, real estate acquisition financing, contract financing, surety bonds, and equity investments in the form of preferred stock, common stock, warrants, partnership interests, and other equity-like structures. Loans and equity investments range from $25,000 to $1,000,000. Financing and investments require a minimum 1:1 private capital match and the lender must have 20% at risk for debt financing.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Randy Croxton, Chief Investment Officer (general information); Robin Harris (application assistance); Les Hall

structured_extraction.program_description: A refundable credit against Maryland state income tax equal to 25% of qualified production costs incurred within Maryland by theatrical production entities. The credit supports National Touring Productions and Pre-Broadway Productions that meet specific performance and staging requirements.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A refundable tax credit of 25% of qualified production costs incurred in Maryland. The minimum production cost threshold is $100,000 to qualify. The maximum tax credit award cannot exceed $2 million for a single theatrical production. Eligible costs include set design and operation, special and visual effects, wardrobe, makeup, sound, lighting, lodging, vehicle leasing, salaries for work performed in Maryland, and travel expenses to bring cast and crew to the state. Qualified direct costs also include production insurance, advertising and public relations, professional fees from Maryland-licensed providers, office expenses, IT services, and completion bonds. General expenses such as opening night galas and contingency costs allocated to qualified direct expenses are eligible. Individual compensation cannot exceed $100,000 per week.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application for Qualification must be submitted before beginning any work on the theatrical production in Maryland. Application Addendum must be submitted before the first rehearsal. Application for Final Tax Credit Certification must be submitted within 180 days of production completion.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Robin Bailey, Director of Policy and Program Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit theatrical production entities producing National Touring Productions or Pre-Broadway Productions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Production costs including set design and operation, special and visual effects, wardrobe, makeup, sound, lighting, lodging, vehicle leasing, salaries and wages for work performed in Maryland, advertising and public relations, rental of facilities and equipment, travel expenses to bring cast and crew to Maryland, production insurance, professional fees from Maryland-licensed providers (legal, accounting, auditing), office expenses, IT services, completion bonds, and opening night galas. Excludes salary/wages for writers, directors, and producers (except technical roles), entertainment, gifts, gratuities, vehicle personal use, taxes, penalties, and fines to other jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All costs must be incurred within Maryland or be clearly and demonstrably allocable to Maryland production time. The production must take place in a qualified theatrical production facility (theater) in the state. Advertising and public relations expenses must be within Maryland only. Shipping must be into or within Maryland only. Travel expenses must be into or within Maryland only. National Touring Productions must perform for four weeks or more in at least four cities outside Maryland after the final performance in the state. Pre-Broadway Productions must be prepared for presentation in the Broadway theater district within twelve months after final performance in Maryland.

Pre-Broadway Production must have at least eight public performances, be in original or adaptive version, not have been performed or only have limited performance in the preceding five years, and be prepared for presentation in the Broadway theater district within twelve months after final performance in Maryland
Estimated total direct production costs incurred in Maryland must exceed $100,000
All statutory requirements must be met
Application for Qualification must be complete and signed with completed Application Addendum
Qualified Theatrical Production Entity must demonstrate financing
No salary, wages, or other compensation for individuals receiving more than $100,000 per week in connection with the production
Writers, directors, and producers' compensation not eligible (except technical roles like Lighting Director)
Cannot claim refundable security deposits or purchase of real estate or vehicles as authorized costs

Production company must be approved by Secretary of Commerce

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Before beginning any work on the theatrical production in Maryland, submit a complete Application for Qualification to the Department via email with all required attachments, including Good Standing Certificates and proof of financing. The Department will review applications in the order received and issue a Letter of Qualification within 30 days confirming qualification and maximum credit amount. Before the first rehearsal, submit the Application Addendum with required documentation including insurance certificates, unemployment insurance account number, chief internal accountant information, payroll service information, and production accountant information. After completing all required performances, within 180 days submit an Application for Final Tax Credit Certification with all final documentation including payroll reports, general ledger, vendor and accounts payable lists, employee lists, Maryland resident employee lists, Maryland business vendor lists, expenditure report, production schedule, crew list, and an independent auditor's report (if total authorized costs exceed $250,000) performing Agreed Upon Procedures. The Department reviews the application and issues a Tax Credit Certificate not exceeding the amount in the original Letter of Qualification. To claim the credit, file the applicable Maryland state income tax return, complete Form 500CR, and include a copy of the Tax Credit Certificate. The credit is only available with electronically filed returns.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive program that promotes economic development and environmental improvement by encouraging the cleanup and reuse of contaminated or potentially contaminated properties (brownfields), especially in distressed urban areas and densely populated urban centers. The program identifies and redeploys underutilized properties by providing financial incentives to help organize and assess brownfield properties, perform environmental evaluations, and conduct cleanup work. Property owners and operators who clean up qualified brownfield sites can receive low-interest loans or grants for Phase I and Phase II environmental assessments, site remediation activities, and property tax credits. Property owners who successfully remediate qualified brownfield sites can receive real property tax credits of 50% to 70% of the property tax attributable to the increase in assessed value of the site for a 5-year period, with potential extension to 10 years in designated enterprise zones. Additional credits of up to 20% may be available for properties in enterprise zones, designated commercial revitalization areas, or when cleanup costs exceed $1,000,000.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides three types of financial incentives: (1) low-interest loans or grants for Phase I and Phase II environmental assessments; (2) property tax credits of 50% to 70% of the property tax attributable to the increase in assessed value of the site granted for a 5-year period, with potential extension to 10 years in designated enterprise zones or opportunity zones, with combined credits not exceeding 100% of the tax on the increased value, plus additional discretionary credits up to 20% for properties in enterprise zones, designated commercial revitalization areas, or where cleanup costs exceed $1,000,000; and (3) low-interest loans or grants for site remediation. Additionally, 30% of the increased tax liability from participating jurisdictions contributes to the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Fund. These incentives are designed to stimulate redevelopment in areas where cleanup will have significant environmental, economic development, and urban revitalization benefits. Competitive grant and loan funding applications are managed through the Maryland Department of Commerce Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF). For grant and loan information, visit the Advantage Maryland website.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, operators, prospective purchasers, innocent purchasers, and developers of brownfield sites located in participating Maryland jurisdictions who are seeking to remediate and redevelop industrial or commercial sites in densely populated urban centers and Enterprise Zones. Applicants must be 'inculpable persons,' meaning they are not responsible for the contamination.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Phase I and Phase II environmental assessments, site remediation activities, property redevelopment, organizing and assessing brownfield properties, performing environmental evaluations, property tax credits on the increased assessed value of remediated brownfield properties, environmental cleanup and remediation costs, new construction on remediated sites, and county contributions of 30% of increased property tax liability to State BRIP for loans and grants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The site must be located in a participating jurisdiction in densely populated urban centers or designated incentive areas. Participating counties are Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, and Worcester. Participating municipalities include Colmar Manor, Cumberland, Frederick, Salisbury, and Taneytown. Sites must generally be industrial or commercial in nature and substantially underutilized. Additional benefits are available for properties in Enterprise Zones, designated commercial revitalization areas, Opportunity Zones, and other incentive zones. Properties may extend to designated commercial revitalization areas. The brownfield property must be located within a participating jurisdiction that has enacted BRIP legislation.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed General Application and BRIP addendum to the Department of Commerce along with copies of MDE letters showing VCP acceptance, inculpable person status, and a closure document, plus a copy of the building permit. Once approved, the Department issues a letter that the property owner takes to the local jurisdiction to apply for the tax credit. Competitive grant and loan funding applications are managed through the Maryland Department of Commerce Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF). The taxing jurisdiction must elect participation through legislation and notify the Department of Commerce. Credit applies automatically to qualifying sites in that jurisdiction. For additional application information and program details, contact the Maryland Department of Commerce or visit the Advantage Maryland website for grant and loan information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Military Personnel and Veteran-Owned Small Business Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland program that provides no-interest loans from $1,000 to $100,000 to military personnel, veterans, Reservists, and National Guard personnel, as well as small businesses with 50 or fewer employees that employ such persons. For businesses with owners called to active duty, funds can cover general business expenses caused by deployment. For businesses involving service-disabled veterans, funds can help make a home, vehicle, or workplace accessible. Loans are available for 1 to 8 years, with repayment periods typically matching the useful life of equipment purchased. The program supports business establishment, development, and operations.

structured_extraction.program_name: More Jobs for Marylanders – Manufacturing Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that provides tax incentives to new and existing manufacturers and non-manufacturers locating or expanding in Opportunity Zones that create new full-time jobs and employ apprentices in Maryland. The program offers a refundable income tax credit equal to 5.75% of wages per eligible new position for manufacturers creating at least 5 new full-time jobs (or at least 10 jobs in Tier 1 areas, 20 in Tier 2 areas), a $1,000 tax credit for businesses employing eligible apprentices, and encourages additional investment in new equipment through accelerated and bonus depreciation. Tax credits are available for a 10-year period in Tier 1 areas and 5 years in Tier 2 areas. The program was expanded in 2019 to include non-manufacturers locating or expanding in Opportunity Zones, particularly in Tier 1 counties like Garrett County, which may be eligible for additional incentives including real property tax credits, sales and use tax refunds, and fee waivers. The program stopped accepting new applicants on June 1, 2024; only companies that enrolled before that date can participate. State sets application period after July 1 each year for returning participants.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A refundable state income tax credit for eligible businesses. Manufacturers receive a refundable 10-year income tax credit equal to 5.75% of wages per eligible new position for creating at least 5 new full-time jobs (at least 10 jobs required in Tier 1 areas, 20 in Tier 2 areas). The credit is available for 10 years in Tier 1 areas and 5 years in Tier 2 areas. Businesses also receive a $1,000 tax credit for employing eligible apprentices. The program encourages additional investment in new equipment through accelerated and bonus depreciation. Businesses locating in Tier 1 counties (such as Garrett County) may be eligible for additional incentives including credits against the State's portion of real property tax, refunds of sales and use tax, and waivers of fees charged by the State Department of Assessment and Taxation. Qualified jobs must pay at least 150% of state minimum wage for manufacturers and at least $50,000 per year for non-manufacturers.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program stopped accepting new applicants on June 1, 2024. Only companies enrolled before that date can participate. Application period set after July 1 each year for returning participants.

Program is closed to new applicants as of June 1, 2024.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits for wage expenses, apprentice employment, job creation initiatives, equipment depreciation incentives, and job training and apprenticeship programs

Non-manufacturers must locate or expand in Opportunity Zones to be eligible. Tier 1 areas receive more favorable credit terms (10 years) and lower job creation thresholds (10 jobs) compared to Tier 2 areas (5 years, 20 jobs).

Businesses should notify Maryland Department of Commerce of intent prior to hiring new employees.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax credit program for businesses that invest in economic development projects and create qualified jobs in Maryland. The credit amount depends on the number of jobs created and qualified project costs incurred. Businesses making capital investments and creating new qualified positions in Tier 1 Counties and Priority Funding Areas receive state income tax credits as incentives. The program provides credits up to $5 million based on job creation levels and eligible project costs. The amount of income tax credit a business qualifies for depends on the amount of capital investment made in the project and the number of new qualified jobs created within a 24-month period.
list_of_eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit for businesses making capital investments and creating qualified jobs. Credit amounts depend on job creation and eligible project costs incurred within a 24-month period. For businesses creating 10-24 qualified positions with at least $500,000 to $1 million in eligible project costs, the maximum credit is $1 million. For businesses creating 25-49 qualified positions with at least $2.5 million in costs, the maximum credit is $2.5 million. For businesses creating at least 50 qualified positions with at least $5 million in costs, the maximum credit is $5 million. The credit can be carried forward for up to 10 years after the certified credit year. Beginning the fourth year after the credit year, the business may apply the credit against its state income tax liability and request a refund limited to payroll withholding attributable to the qualified positions. Eligible project costs include land acquisition, performance and contract bonds and insurance, architectural and engineering services, environmental mitigation, utility installation, interest costs prior to and during acquisition and construction and for two years after completion, legal and accounting fees, fixed telecommunication equipment, office furniture and equipment, and costs related to moving a business from outside Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses, including for-profit and non-profit organizations, that invest in economic development projects and create new qualified jobs, particularly those in Tier 1 Counties and Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible project costs include land acquisition, performance and contract bonds and insurance, architectural and engineering services, environmental mitigation, utility installation, interest costs prior to and during acquisition and construction and for two years after completion, legal and accounting fees, fixed telecommunication equipment, office furniture and equipment, and costs related to moving a business from outside Maryland. Tax credits for capital investment and job creation projects. Minimum eligible costs must be at least $500,000.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) or qualified opportunity zone in a Tier 1 County. As of December 2025, Tier 1 Counties are Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester (Worcester remains eligible through September 2026 under the 24-month look back provision). PFAs include state enterprise zones, federal empowerment zones, Department of Housing and Community Development Sustainable Communities, incorporated municipalities, areas between the I-495 beltway and Washington D.C. and the I-695 beltway and Baltimore City, and growth areas designated by each county. Qualified Opportunity Zones are also eligible in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Notice of Intent letter to Maryland Commerce. Register for an account in Commerce's online system and login to complete your application. Submit a Preliminary Application and Employment Affidavit showing projected job and wage data and the number of jobs at the facility prior to creating new jobs. Commerce will issue a Preliminary Certificate of Eligibility if the business is projected to qualify. Once the project has incurred eligible project costs, created at least 10 qualified jobs, and those jobs have been filled for 12 months, the business may apply for final certification by submitting a Final Application with a list of qualified positions and employees, list of eligible costs, and documentation confirming expenditures for a sample of costs. Commerce will issue a Final Certificate showing the amount of credit for which the business qualifies, which the business attaches to its tax return.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Research and Development Tax Credit program provides income tax credits to businesses that invest in research and development in Maryland. The program fosters increased research activities and expenditures in Maryland by offering a tax credit against state income tax for qualified R&D expenses. Businesses with qualified R&D expenditures in Maryland may qualify for a tax credit equal to ten percent of eligible R&D expenses incurred during the taxable year in excess of the Maryland Base Amount. The program offers both a Basic R&D Tax Credit and a Growth R&D Tax Credit, with total credits granted capped at $12 million in a fiscal year, or pro-rated if exceeded.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit is equal to ten percent (10%) of eligible R&D expenses incurred during the taxable year in excess of the Maryland Base Amount. The total statutory cap is $12 million with a small business set-aside of $3.5 million and $8.5 million reserved for non-small businesses. A single applicant may not receive a tax credit exceeding $250,000. If total credits applied for exceed the statutory caps, the business's R&D tax credit is prorated. R&D tax credits certified after December 15, 2012 are refundable for small businesses (defined as for-profit entities with net book value assets less than $5 million) to the extent that the tax credits exceed the income tax liability for that taxable year. Unused credits may be carried forward for 7 years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 15 of the calendar year following the end of the taxable year in which expenses were incurred
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses conducting research and development in Maryland, including small businesses, corporations, limited liability companies, partnerships, sole proprietorships, S corporations, and larger corporations. Small businesses are defined as having net book value assets less than $5,000,000.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Maryland qualified research and development expenses as defined by Section 41(b) of the Internal Revenue Code incurred in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Qualified research and development must be conducted in Maryland. Gross receipts must be reasonably attributable to Maryland business operations. The program applies statewide.

Research and development must be conducted in Maryland

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A business must submit an application to the Maryland Department of Commerce by November 15 of the calendar year following the tax year in which the Maryland Qualified Research and Development expenses were incurred. Small businesses must also submit documentation showing net book value assets less than $5 million. Commerce will issue a tax credit certificate with the approved credit amount by February 15 of the calendar year following the end of the year in which a business submits an application. After receiving certification, the business may file an amended tax return for the year it is certified or it may claim the credit on an income tax return filed for any of the following 7 tax years. The business must attach a copy of the Department's certification to its tax return.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account - Video Lottery Terminal Fund (VLT)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state fund that uses proceeds from video lottery terminals to provide below-market-rate loans to small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses for business expansion, real estate acquisition, equipment purchase, and working capital. At least 50 percent of allocations go to targeted businesses within 10 miles of Maryland's six casinos (Maryland Live! in Anne Arundel County, Hollywood Casino Perryville in Cecil County, Rocky Gap Casino in Allegany County, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City, and National Harbor in Prince George's County), with the remaining 50 percent available statewide to eligible businesses throughout Maryland. Loans range from $10,000 to $500,000 and are priced at or below current market interest rates. A specialized FLEX Fund component offers $2 million in flexible financing with expedited approval (two-week turnaround) and reduced underwriting requirements, specifically designed for small, minority, and veteran-owned businesses in Prince George's County. Additional loan products administered through regional partners such as Tri-County Council for Western Maryland provide financing up to $1,000,000 with interest rates tied to Prime Rate plus 1 percent, terms up to 5 years for working capital and 15 years for fixed assets, and targeted support for Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties. The program supports hiring and business expansion objectives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below-market-rate loans ranging from $10,000 to $1,000,000 are available to small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses for business acquisition and expansion, owner-occupied commercial real estate, equipment purchase, leasehold improvements, working capital, start-up costs, hiring new employees, professional and technical assistance, and refinancing of existing debt under certain circumstances. Funds are distributed through regional fund managers who provide loans to eligible businesses. At least 50 percent of allocations go to targeted businesses within 10 miles of the six Maryland casinos, with 50 percent available to targeted businesses throughout Maryland. A specialized FLEX Fund component offers $2 million in flexible financing with expedited two-week approval turnaround and reduced underwriting requirements. Standard underwriting practices consider repayment capacity, financial strength, industry and management experience, and collateral protection. Interest rates are competitively priced at or below market rates; some programs offer Prime Rate plus 1 percent. Terms of up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets. A standard 5-year term with interest-only first year, then principal and interest; terms up to 30 years available based on collateral and purpose. Application fees of $250 (non-refundable) for loans over $25,000, or $25 for loans between $10,000-$25,000 may apply. Approved borrowers pay a 1 percent loan origination fee at closing. Loan processing time is 30-90 days. Settlement is facilitated with the assistance of outside attorneys.

Primary focus on Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties for select loan products. Startup entrepreneurs and business owners located in or relocating to Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business and commercial real estate acquisition and expansion, leasehold improvements, equipment, working capital, hiring new employees, start-up costs, professional and technical assistance, refinancing of existing debt under certain circumstances, building improvements, business purchase (limited to $250,000), and general business financing and operations.

Also available statewide to eligible businesses throughout Maryland. Businesses must be located within 10 miles of any of Maryland's casinos or elsewhere in Maryland. The FLEX Fund component is available specifically in Prince George's County. Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties are designated as primary target areas for select loan products. Businesses must be located in or relocating to Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program (WVEDG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state program providing tax credits and grants to support capital improvements at existing wineries and vineyards, as well as assist new entities looking to establish wine production operations in Maryland. The program offers an income tax credit or grant equal to 25% of qualified capital expenses. For tax credits, the total may not exceed $500,000 in a single tax year; if applications exceed this amount, credits are prorated among qualified applicants. A total of $1 million is available for grants. Eligible capital expenses include barrels, bins, canopy management machines, fermenters or other recognized fermentation devices, fruit harvesters, irrigation equipment, presses, seeders, tanks, bottling equipment, tractors, and other related equipment. A qualified winery must hold a Class 3 or Class 4 winery license from the Comptroller of Maryland, and a qualified vineyard must be at least one continuous acre of agricultural land in Maryland used only for growing grapes for a licensed Maryland winery.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides either an income tax credit or grant equal to 25% of qualified capital expenses incurred to start a new winery or vineyard, or to improve and expand an existing winery or vineyard. For tax credits, total credits may not exceed $500,000 for a single tax year; if applications exceed this amount, credits are prorated among qualified applicants. For grants, $1 million is available for the program. Eligible expenses include barrels, bins, canopy management machines, fermenters or other recognized fermentation devices, fruit harvesters, irrigation equipment, presses, seeders, tanks, bottling equipment, tractors, and other related equipment. The grant does not cover the cost of constructing buildings, utilities, labor, or general supplies.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements and equipment purchases including barrels, bins, canopy management machines, fermenters, fruit harvesters, irrigation equipment, presses, seeders, tanks, bottling equipment, tractors, and other related equipment for starting, improving, expanding, or enhancing wineries or vineyards. Funds cannot be used for constructing buildings, utilities, labor, or general supplies.

structured_extraction.program_description: A refundable tax credit against Maryland state income tax for film production entities that incur qualifying costs in Maryland. The credit covers up to 28% of authorized direct costs (or 30% for series), with a maximum of $10 million per project for standard productions or $125,000 for Maryland Small Films. This program supports feature films, television series, commercials, documentaries, music videos, and other qualified production types with national distribution.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Commerce, Maryland Film Office
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified film production entities receive a refundable income tax credit of up to 28% of total authorized direct costs of a film production activity, or 30% for series projects with a maximum tax credit of $10,000,000 per project. Maryland Small Films may receive up to 28% of authorized direct costs with a maximum of $125,000 per project. The credit is claimed against state income tax on Form 500CR of the Maryland state income tax return and may result in a refund if the credit exceeds tax liability. Authorized direct costs include production personnel, equipment rentals, set construction, facilities, materials, pre-production, production, and post-production expenses incurred directly in Maryland or provided by qualified vendors.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on first come, first served basis while funding available; must be submitted before beginning any film production activity in Maryland. Final Tax Credit Certification must be submitted no later than 180 days after completion of all film production in the State.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorized direct costs incurred in Maryland necessary to carry out a film production activity, including qualified production personnel (writers, producers, directors, cast, crew), equipment rentals, set construction, travel into Maryland, accommodation, facilities, materials and supplies, transportation within Maryland, pre-production, production, and post-production expenses. Costs must be directly incurred by the film production entity or provided by a qualified vendor, and used in Maryland only. Specific eligible costs are outlined in the Authorized Direct Costs list. For materials and goods with initial cost greater than $1,000, the direct cost equals initial cost minus resale value upon completion.

Costs are limited to those directly incurred in Maryland and pro-rated for time spent in Maryland only. Washington, DC does not qualify. Applicants must have a Maryland business address or register to do business in Maryland before beginning production.

Step 2: Within 30 days of receiving a complete application, the Department issues a Letter of Qualification confirming maximum tax credits available or notifies applicant of ineligibility. structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program established in 1982 that provides real property, personal property, and state income tax credits for businesses located in a Maryland enterprise zone or focus area in return for job creation and capital investments. The program encourages revitalization and economic development through commercial and industrial expansion in economically distressed areas. Businesses in focus areas may qualify for enhanced credits including personal property tax credits on new investment and enhanced income tax credits for creating new jobs. Three types of tax credits are available: (1) General Income Tax Credit – one-time $1,000 credit per qualified new employee in an enterprise zone, or $1,500 in a focus area. (2) Income Tax Credit for Economically Disadvantaged Employees – three-year credits totaling $6,000 ($3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, $1,000 third year) in an enterprise zone; or $9,000 total ($4,500, $3,000, $1,500 respectively) in a focus area. (3) Real Property Tax Credit – ten-year credit at 80% of eligible assessment for first 5 years, declining 10% annually thereafter (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%); focus area real property credit maintains 80% for all ten years. Personal Property Tax Credit in focus areas – ten-year credit at 80% of eligible assessment for entire ten-year period. Special provisions apply for newly constructed mixed office and retail properties, providing 13-year credits. State reimburses local jurisdictions 50% of foregone local property tax revenue from real property tax credits (subject to annual budget approval). The program has grown from 2 zones to 34 zones across Maryland, helping businesses in designated areas stay and grow, promotes the use of empty or underused properties, and supports county efforts to improve older office and industrial areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Finance Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three types of tax credits available: (1) Real property tax credit offering 80 percent reduction on property taxes from real property improvements for 10 years (decreasing 10 percent annually in years 6-10 in enterprise zones, or full 10 years at 80% in focus areas), (2) Personal property tax credit in focus areas providing 80 percent of eligible assessment for 10 years, and (3) Employment credit with state income tax credits ranging from $1,000 per new employee ($1,500 in Focus Areas) to $6,000 per economically disadvantaged employee over three years ($9,000 in Focus Areas, spread as $3,000-$2,000-$1,000 in standard zones or $4,500-$3,000-$1,500 in focus areas), with credits carrying forward for up to 5 years. In standard Enterprise Zones, local property tax credits are 80% of eligible assessment for the first 5 years, then decrease by 10% annually for the next 5 years (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%). In Enterprise Zone Focus Areas, local property tax credits on real and personal property are 80% of eligible assessments for the full 10-year period. Special provisions apply for newly constructed mixed office and retail properties, providing 13-year credits. Tax credits apply to state income tax liability and real and personal property taxes for businesses making capital improvements or hiring new employees in designated Enterprise Zones and Focus Areas. Both County and Maryland tax credits are available to eligible businesses. State reimburses local jurisdictions 50% of foregone local property tax revenue from real property tax credits (subject to annual budget approval). Additionally, the program may include exemptions from Commercial Building Excise Tax in certain jurisdictions.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying new and existing for-profit businesses, individuals, non-profits, and government entities that make job creation and capital investments in designated Enterprise Zones or Focus Areas in Maryland. Includes businesses located in or relocating to enterprise zones across eligible counties, property owners, end-user businesses, development companies, commercial enterprises, hospitality operators, food service/distribution companies, manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, corporate/regional headquarters, and service industries. Also includes proprietorships, partnerships, and corporations. County governments, municipal governments, and local economic development entities are eligible to establish enterprise zones. Political subdivisions seeking enterprise zone designations. Businesses establishing operations in the enterprise zone.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits applied against state income tax liability and local property taxes for businesses making qualifying investments in real property expansion, renovation, capital improvements, equipment purchases, facility expansions, new construction, rehabilitation projects, or creating new qualified jobs. Includes economically disadvantaged employee hiring initiatives and new machinery and equipment investment. Capital investment in enterprise zone; job creation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located within one of 34 designated enterprise zones across 19 Maryland jurisdictions or within designated focus areas to qualify. Areas must be designated by the Secretary as meeting at least one economic distress criterion (unemployment rate at least 150% of state or U.S. average, low-income poverty area, crime rates, substandard housing, or commercial vacancy rates 20%+) and be within a State Priority Funding Area or meet an exception. Enterprise zones have varying expiration dates ranging from 2022-2032. Certification by the local enterprise zone administrator is required before claiming any credits. Anne Arundel County's Enterprise Zone covers over 1,572 acres in the Brooklyn Park area. Businesses must be located in designated Enterprise Zone or Enterprise Zone Focus Area in Prince George's County. Only properties located within one of Baltimore County's three Enterprise Zones are eligible: North Point, Southwest, or Federal Center at Woodlawn. Federal Center at Woodlawn Enterprise Zone (Woodlawn area, Baltimore County) includes area bounded by major roads including Security Boulevard, Windsor Mill Road, Rolling Road, and nearby landmarks such as Security Square Mall, Woodlawn High School, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, and Social Security Administration. Washington County maintains approximately 5,910 acres across two state-designated Enterprise Zones: the Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,410 acres in City of Hagerstown) and the Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres surrounding the Town of Hancock). Garrett County has two Enterprise Zones: the Southern Garrett Enterprise Zone (comprising the Southern Garrett Industrial Park and Southern Garrett Business & Technology Park) and the Northern Garrett Enterprise Zone (comprising the Northern Garrett Industrial Park). Applicants can use the My Neighborhood Interactive Map or Maryland Enterprise Zone Map to determine if a property is within an Enterprise Zone. Baltimore City and Prince George's County also operate Focus Areas with distinct tax credit benefits.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Verify the eligibility of an address using the interactive Maryland Enterprise Zone Map. Check if the location is in an Enterprise Zone or Focus Area. Download detailed maps of specific enterprise zones. Apply to the local enterprise zone administrator for certification. Complete and submit an enterprise zone application form with applicable sections (C for property tax credits, D for employment tax credits, and/or E for personal property credits) based on credit type sought. Applicant and property owner must sign and date application. Applications must be received on April 15 and October 15 each year. Once certified, business can claim income tax credits on Maryland Tax Form 500CR included with state tax return. Credits apply to state income tax only, not county income tax add-ons. Contact the appropriate local enterprise zone coordinator or the Department of Commerce for additional application procedures and county-specific requirements. For property tax credits: Complete the application and send it to the local Enterprise Zone Administrator by the application deadline to receive a property tax credit on the next tax bill. After the department reviews your application, you will get a letter confirming if you are eligible. For the property tax credit, the county will automatically notify the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. To claim the income tax credit, you must submit Maryland Tax Form 500CR with your annual tax return. If you hire a disadvantaged employee to receive a higher credit, you must get that employee certified by Maryland Department of Labor. For Washington County: Contact Linda Spence at edcinfo@washco-md.net or 240-313-2280 for application materials and requirements. For Anne Arundel County, contact the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation at 410-222-7410 for assistance with the application process. For Prince George's County, contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist. For Baltimore County, download the eligibility application form and complete it. Send the completed application to the Enterprise Zone Coordinator at the Baltimore County Department of Economic Development, Historic Courthouse Suite 100, 400 Washington Avenue, Towson, Maryland 21204. You can also contact them by phone at 410-887-8030, fax at 410-887-8017, or email at businesshelp@baltimorecountymd.gov. Political subdivisions submit zone designation requests with supporting economic statistics to the Secretary of Commerce by April 15 or October 15 each year for evaluation against distress criteria. Annual reporting required post-designation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The State of Maryland provides enhancements to several of its economic development tax credit programs for businesses located in Maryland Opportunity Zones. Businesses can apply for Level 1 or Level 2 Enhancements to receive higher tax credits through the Job Creation Tax Credit, One Maryland Tax Credit, More Jobs for Marylanders Income Tax Credit, Enterprise Zone Income Tax Credit, Enterprise Zone Focus Area Income Tax Credit, and Biotechnology Investor Incentive Tax Credit programs. The program also extends benefits to historic revitalization projects and qualified workforce housing in opportunity zones.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Finance Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses located in Maryland Opportunity Zones receive enhanced tax credits instead of standard credits from underlying tax credit programs. Level 1 enhancements provide moderate increases (for example, $3,075 per qualified job creation position versus $3,000 standard rate). Level 2 enhancements provide higher increases ($3,300 per qualified job creation position). Specific credit amounts vary by program: Job Creation Tax Credit offers $3,075-$5,500 per position; One Maryland offers up to $5,125,000-$5,500,000; More Jobs for Marylanders offers 6%-6.25% of wages; Enterprise Zone offers $1,025-$1,200 per job; Enterprise Zone Focus Area offers $1,540-$1,750 per job; Biotechnology Investor Incentive Tax Credit offers 65%-75% of investment up to $575,000-$750,000. Historic revitalization projects receive 20% credit on qualified rehabilitation expenditures, with additional 5% for high performance buildings or Tier Level 1 projects, and 7.5% for Tier Level 2 projects. Workforce housing tax credits provide up to $4,000,000 maximum aggregate annually. Property tax credits range from 90% (Tier 1) to 100% (Tier 2) of property taxes on qualified business property. Sales and use tax refunds available for qualified purchases.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Certificates cannot be issued on or after June 1, 2025 for certain programs; Historic Revitalization Tax Credit program sunset June 30, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in Maryland Opportunity Zones that meet the qualifications of underlying tax credit programs and have received investment from a Qualified Opportunity Fund; property owners and developers undertaking rehabilitations; workforce housing developers; community development organizations; small businesses and microenterprises.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital expenditures and job creation within Opportunity Zones; qualified rehabilitation expenditures on certified historic structures; qualified workforce housing projects; business property acquisition and development; equipment and service purchases for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Federally designated Opportunity Zones in Maryland as defined by federal opportunity zone designations under IRC § 1400Z-1 (specific census tracts confirmed via Department of Housing and Community Development's Incentive Lookup Interactive Map). Priority areas include Allegany County, Garrett County, Somerset County, and Wicomico County. Limitation: not more than 60% of total historic revitalization credit amounts may be issued for projects in a single county or Baltimore City. Cybersecurity investment incentive excludes Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, and Somerset Counties.
requirements_list: Must be located in a Maryland Opportunity Zone designated under IRC § 1400Z-1
Must meet specific criteria for relevant tax credit program (job creation, enterprise zone, biotechnology, or innovation)
Business must first meet qualifications of the underlying tax credit program

For Job Creation, One Maryland, More Jobs for Marylanders, Enterprise Zone and Enterprise Zone Focus Area credits: business must be a Qualified Opportunity Zone Business as defined in Internal Revenue Code Section 1400Z-2 and have received investment from a Qualified Opportunity Fund

For Biotechnology Investor Incentive Tax Credit: investor must be a Qualified Opportunity Fund and the Maryland Biotechnology or Technology Company receiving investment must be located in an Opportunity Zone
Current on all state and local tax obligations
Must not be in default under state or local contracts
Must be in good standing and authorized/registered to do business in Maryland

Level 1 Enhancement requires: investment from Qualified Opportunity Fund; copy of Federal Form 8996 filed with IRS; documentation of capital expenditures, job creation, and zone resident hiring; investment date, amount, and total project/business investment
Level 2 Enhancement requires all Level 1 requirements plus: community board representation by zone residents OR Community Benefits Agreement; must obtain county/municipal approval

For historic rehabilitations: structure must qualify as certified historic structure; rehabilitation must be completed within 30 months of initial credit certificate issuance (extendable for reasonable cause); work must begin within 18 months of certificate issuance

For workforce housing: project must be placed in service during or after fiscal year of credit allocation; project must meet Housing and Community Development Article § 4-2501 et seq. requirements; maintain project eligibility for at least 30 years from first taxable year credit claimed
For manufacturing and processing: minimum 5 positions in Tier I areas; 10 in Tier II areas
Qualified Opportunity Zone Business: trade or business with substantially all tangible property used being qualified Maryland opportunity zone business property
Qualified Opportunity Fund: organized as corporation or partnership, holding at least 90% of assets in qualified Maryland opportunity zone property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attach an Opportunity Zone Enhancement program application to your application for the specific tax credit program. For Level 1, provide investment information, copy of QOF's Federal Form 8996, and documentation of capital expenditures, job creation, and zone resident hiring. For Level 2, provide all Level 1 information plus documentation of community board representation or a community benefits agreement, and municipal or county approval. For historic rehabilitations, submit documentation including address/census tract, NAICS code, impact report with qualitative and quantitative data, and certification documentation. For workforce housing, notify Secretary when project is placed in service and certify project meets qualified workforce housing requirements. Submit copy of final credit certificate with tax return.
