structured_extraction.program_name: Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation's Affordable Rental Housing Opportunities Initiative for Persons with Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation and the State of Maryland to provide affordable rental housing options for persons with disabilities. The program designates units in rental housing developments for occupancy at affordable rents specifically for very low-income persons with disabilities, commonly referred to as Weinberg Apartments. The program provides both rental assistance subsidies for individuals and capital grants as an incentive for owners of eligible rental housing developments with non-profit involvement. Weinberg-funded units house non-elderly, disabled persons at 10-30 percent of Area Gross Median Income (AGMI), with tenants paying 30 percent of their income for rent and utilities. Total funding includes $7 million in grants from The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation and financial assistance from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development through its Multifamily Rental Housing Programs.

Total funding includes $7 million in grants from The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation and financial assistance from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development through its Multifamily Rental Housing Programs. Rental assistance helps low-income people with disabilities afford housing in their community.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides Maryland residents age 3 or older with free assistive telecommunications equipment to independently make or receive phone calls. Offers custom solutions based on individual needs for people with difficulty using standard telephones due to vision loss, hearing loss, speech difficulty, memory loss, cognitive limitations, or mobility limitations, as well as those who are deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind, blind, or low vision. Equipment includes text telephones (TTYs), Braille TTYs, Hearing Carry-Over (HCO) phones, Voice Carry-Over (VCO) phones, phones with large buttons, picture phones, hands-free phones, captioned telephones, amplified phones, tablets, and wheelchair pad phone switches. All equipment is provided on long-term loan and remains property of the State of Maryland. Braille TTYs include a keyboard for typing and a Braille display for reading responses, with personalized text pacing adjustable in five-word increments from ten to forty-five words per minute. Equipment is mailed 4-6 weeks after completion of an evaluation that determines which equipment options best meet the applicant's needs. Equipment repair and maintenance services for normal wear and tear are provided at MAT office discretion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free, one-on-one evaluations by MAT specialists to determine the right assistive telecommunications solution for each applicant. Qualified applicants receive assistive equipment shipped to their home at no cost via UPS or available for pickup at MAT program location, with delivery 4-6 weeks after evaluation completion. Equipment types include text telephones (TTYs), Braille TTYs, Hearing Carry-Over (HCO) phones, Voice Carry-Over (VCO) phones, phones with large buttons, picture phones, hands-free phones, captioned telephones, amplified phones, tablets, and wheelchair pad phone switches. Initial training is provided during evaluation, with detailed instructions included in equipment shipment. Additional free training from MAT evaluators is available. The Talk, Text, Train (TTT) program offers up to 2 one-on-one sessions with trainers for low vision and blind customers. For Braille TTYs, users can dial 711 or 800-735-2258 to connect with a Maryland Relay Operator who voices their typed messages and types spoken responses for the user to read on the Braille display. Personalized text pacing is available with typing speeds adjustable in five-word increments from ten to forty-five words per minute. Equipment repair and maintenance services for normal wear and tear are provided at MAT office discretion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 3 or older who are deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind, blind, low vision, or have cognitive, mobility, speech-related, or other difficulties and have difficulty using a standard telephone. structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest loan program that helps Maryland residents with disabilities and their families obtain financing to purchase assistive technology equipment, devices, adapted and non-adapted vehicles, accessibility modifications to homes and vehicles, and other supports to enable independent living, work, learning, and employment goals. The program offers loans with fixed rates below market rates and extended repayment terms, ranging from $500 to $70,000 depending on equipment type and creditworthiness.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans with fixed rates below market rates and extended repayment terms. Loan amounts range from $500 to $70,000 depending on equipment type: unsecured AT loans up to $10,000; unsecured vehicle and home modification loans up to $20,000; non-adapted vehicles up to $40,000; and adapted vehicles up to $70,000. Interest rates are discounted based on creditworthiness and disclosed at application processing and approval. Lenient lending parameters include flexible income thresholds and extended repayment terms. In 2021, 25 loans were approved from 68 applications, with a total loan value of $644,719.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anyone who intends to use the loan to buy assistive technology for a Maryland resident with a disability, including people with disabilities, family members, and friends.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of assistive technology equipment including home modifications, adapted and non-adapted vehicles, scooters and wheelchairs, Braille equipment, hearing and vision aids, augmentative communication devices, environmental control units, computers and adaptive peripherals, smart home technology, and many other assistive technology devices to help with living, working, and learning independently.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; available to all Maryland residents with disabilities

Applicant or family member must have a disability
Must intend to use the loan to buy assistive technology for a Maryland resident with a disability

Income documentation required (pay stubs, SSI, SSDI award letters, pension statements, or tax forms)
Applicants must demonstrate adequate income compared to debt

Good likelihood of loan repayment required for approval
Program criteria are less stringent than traditional bank lending standards
Can apply as independent borrower or with co-applicant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the ATLP application online through the One Stop portal by creating a OneStop account, uploading photo ID, and submitting the application with supporting documents. Alternatively, download the ATLP application form and email the completed application with supporting documents to mdtap.general@maryland.gov. MDOD reviews the application, then the lender reviews for approval. If the lender declines, the application may go to the ATLP Board for review. An appeals process is available. Lender decision expected within 30 days (unless loan guarantee required). Applicants can also contact MDTAP or a regional office to begin the application process, where the program director guides applicants through the application steps. Financial counseling and coaching available through partnership with CASH Campaign of MD.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland High-Tech Assistive Technology Reuse (MATR) Center
structured_extraction.program_description: The state's high-tech assistive technology reuse center that accepts donations of assistive technology devices, refurbishes them, and provides them at no cost to Marylanders with disabilities in need. The program collects gently used assistive technology devices through donations, sanitizes and refurbishes them, and provides them for free to individuals who cannot afford new equipment. Offers innovative resources paired with training and support to help users integrate technology into daily life. Available devices include CCTVs and video magnifiers, iDevices, adapted computer keyboards and mice, switches, speech communication devices, personal sound amplifiers, amplified telephones, and eye-gaze systems. In 2021, 236 devices were refurbished or repaired, and consumers saved a total of $556,441.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free high-tech assistive technology equipment provided at no cost to eligible individuals with disabilities. Available devices include CCTVs and video magnifiers, iDevices, adapted computer keyboards and mice, switches, speech communication devices, personal sound amplifiers, amplified telephones, and eye-gaze systems. Equipment is sanitized and refurbished before distribution. Available for pickup at the MATR Center location (7125 Riverwood Drive, Suite D1, Columbia, Maryland 21046) or through community partners and AT libraries throughout Maryland. Individuals apply online, are contacted for a consultation, and can schedule a pickup or consultation appointment.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Refurbished assistive technology devices including CCTVs, video magnifiers, iDevices, adapted computer peripherals, switches, speech communication devices, personal sound amplifiers, amplified telephones, and eye-gaze systems for home, school, and work use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. The reuse center is located at 7125 Riverwood Drive, Suite D1, Columbia, Maryland 21046. Equipment also available through community partners and AT libraries.

structured_extraction.program_name: Assistance in Community Integration Services (ACIS) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The ACIS Program is a Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) program authorized by CMS under Maryland's Section 1115 Waiver (HealthChoice) that delivers housing-related case management services and tenancy-based supports to eligible Medicaid-enrolled individuals who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless. Operating from January 13, 2025 through December 31, 2026, the program helps eligible individuals live safely and independently in their homes and communities. Services include community integration assessments, person-centered housing plans and planning with measurable goals, connection to social services, landlord accommodation discussions and communication assistance, home management training and support, and housing support and crisis management coordination. Services are provided through local health departments and county governments as Lead Entities, with participation by public and non-profit (501(c)(3)) and private for-profit entities as Participating Entities. The program is capped at 2,140 participant spaces and became effective July 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) funded through Maryland Medicaid HealthChoice. Lead Entities receive reimbursement at $725 per member per month (PMPM) for delivering a minimum of three qualified services per member per month, plus $100 per member per year for compliance activities and Housing Support Care Plan (HSCP) completion. Funding is split 50% State General Funds and 50% Federal Funds. Services include community integration assessments, person-centered community integration planning with measurable goals, housing support and crisis management coordination, assistance connecting individuals with social and supportive services, communication assistance with property managers or landlords regarding accommodation needs, and training and resource support related to tenancy, housing stability, and household management. The program does not cover room and board or rental costs. Lead Entities must enroll as Maryland Medicaid providers (Type GH) with a separate NPI (Taxonomy 251B00000X) for ACIS billing and must deliver services through the conflict-free case management model.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Letter of Intent due by 5 p.m. on March 13, 2026; Request for Responses/Application due by 5 p.m. on March 27, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local health departments, county governments, and other local governmental entities (Lead Entities) applying to become ACIS providers and deliver services within their jurisdiction; also eligible are consortiums of entities serving a county or multiple counties, public and non-profit entities organized under section 501(c)(3), and private for-profit entities as Participating Entities. Individual participants are Medicaid-enrolled individuals experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness who have serious mental illness, substance use disorders, chronic medical conditions, and meet specific health and housing criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing and tenancy-based case management services for individuals experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless, including community integration assessments, person-centered planning, housing support coordination, connection to social services, landlord coordination, and home management training and support. Reimbursement to Lead Entities for staffing and operations for ACIS program delivery, administrative costs, data systems and tracking, and compliance activities. Does not include room and board or rental costs. Funding cannot be used to duplicate or supplant existing federal programs (e.g., PATH program).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is authorized statewide for all Maryland counties to apply for provider status. Participant services are currently available in Baltimore City, Cecil County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County, with statewide expansion authorized as of January 2025. Services are delivered within provider's jurisdiction by enrolled Medicaid providers.
requirements_list: For Providers/Lead Entities: Must be a local health department, county government entity, or consortium of such entities serving a county or region
For Providers/Lead Entities: May include public and non-profit entities (501(c)(3)) and private for-profit entities as Participating Entities
For Providers: Must enroll as Maryland Medicaid provider (Type GH) with separate NPI number (Taxonomy 251B00000X) for ACIS services
For Providers: Must create ePREP business account for Medicaid billing
For Providers: Must enter data-sharing agreements compliant with HIPAA
For Providers: Must provide minimum of three qualified services per month for each member to receive monthly reimbursement
For Providers: Must comply with 42 CFR 441.700-441.745
For Providers: Must implement conflict-free case management model with separation of assessment, treatment planning, and service provision functions
For Providers: Must submit timely quarterly and annual reports to MDH
For Providers: Must respond to state inquiries within one business day

For Individuals: Choose to participate in the ACIS program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Providers: Step 1 - Request the mandatory Letter of Intent (LOI) template and instructions by emailing mdh.medicaidacis@maryland.gov. Step 2 - Submit completed LOI by 5 p.m. on March 13, 2026. Step 3 - Submit the Request for Responses/Application by 5 p.m. on March 27, 2026. MDH will review applications March 27-April 24, notify award recipients via email by May 1, and begin program onboarding by May 18. Successful applicants receive an ACIS Award Letter with onboarding details. structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-year fund established by the Maryland legislature through Senate Bill 283 (Chapter 286) and House Bill 418 (Chapter 287) in 2023 to address critical behavioral health workforce shortages in Maryland. The fund supports training, education, placement, and retention of behavioral health professionals and paraprofessionals across multiple occupations including peer recovery specialists, addiction counselors, social workers, professional counselors, nurses, nurse practitioners, and psychiatrists. It includes seven core programs: Certified Peer Recovery Training and Placement Grants, Alcohol and Drug Counselor Registered Apprenticeship, Social Worker Residency Program, Loan Repayment Programs, Community BH Talent Attraction and Retention Grants, Community BH Nursing Apprenticeship, and Nurse Practitioner/Psychiatry Fellowship Programs. The fund provides a total $148.5M investment over 5 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides multiple forms of assistance with a total $148.5M investment over 5 years. Assistance includes grants to employers for talent attraction and retention ($100,000-$1,000,000), paid internships and fellowships, apprenticeship programs, loan repayment assistance (average $40,000 per professional), residency program support, tuition assistance and scholarships, training stipends, retention bonuses, supervision and mentorship expansion, and career and technical education pathway development. Specific programs include: (1) Certified Peer Recovery Training and Placement Grants covering course fees, stipends, and wage subsidies; (2) Alcohol and Drug Counselor Registered Apprenticeships; (3) Social Worker Residency Programs; (4) Expanding Loan Repayment Programs for Social Workers and Professional Counselors requiring 2-year service commitments in underserved areas; (5) Community BH Nursing Apprenticeships ($15,000 per trainee for 965 LPN/RN degrees); (6) Child/Adolescent Nurse Practitioner Community Psychiatry Fellowship Programs (12-month fellowships at $100,000 per fellow per year); and (7) Community Psychiatry Residency Expansion (10 additional slots at $150,000 per resident per year).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prospective and current behavioral health professionals including peer recovery specialists, addiction counselors, social workers, professional counselors, nurses, nurse practitioners, and psychiatrists; employers in community-based behavioral health settings; educational institutions training behavioral health professionals; individuals from diverse backgrounds and underrepresented communities; low-income and underrepresented populations; rural providers and professionals; adult learners and second-career professionals; school-age youth (K-12).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid internships and fellowships; tuition assistance and scholarships; training course fees; registered peer supervisor compensation; trainee stipends; supportive services; employer wage subsidies for full-time positions; educational loan repayment and forgiveness; retention bonuses; flexible or hybrid work schedules; supervision and mentorship expansion; apprenticeship support and wages; release time for training; licensing and certification support; career awareness programs; job quality improvements for community-based providers; clinical rotations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; all counties eligible. Priority focus areas include Eastern Shore, Western Maryland (rural areas), and specific counties designated as Mental Health Professional Shortage Areas (MHPSAs) including Frederick, Garrett, Washington, Somerset, Dorchester, Wicomico, Worcester, Caroline, Kent, Queen Anne's, and Talbot. Also focuses on Calvert, Charles, and St. Mary's counties which have significant workforce shortages. Emphasis on community-based programs and settings where high levels of uninsured and underinsured residents access care.
requirements_list: Must target behavioral health occupations with demonstrated workforce gaps
Performance benchmarks for peer recovery training: 57%-62.5% pass Certified Peer Recovery Specialist (CPRS) certification exam; 76%-80% employment 90 days post-training
Organizations must provide comprehensive training including all required courses (for peer recovery program)
Programs must support placement in paid roles with community-based organizations
For loan repayment: minimum 2-year service commitment in community-based or school settings in Health Professional Shortage Areas (HPSAs) or medically underserved areas/populations (MUA/Ps)
Grounded in three core principles: Equity, Collaboration, and Outcomes
Must increase providers in community-based settings
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of Healthcare Access and Workforce Development for program details and application information. structured_extraction.program_name: Childhood Lead Poisoning Prevention and Environmental Case Management Program (Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program removes lead hazards from homes and provides in-home case management services to reduce exposures to lead and asthma triggers for families with children exposed to lead, at no cost to eligible families. The program helps families reduce lead exposure in homes built before 1978 by covering lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed. Services include in-home visits and environmental services provided by county health departments. Environmental assessments address dust, pests, mold, pets, and tobacco smoke. The program provides technical assistance to eligible families with children who have elevated blood lead levels.

Environmental assessments address dust, pests, mold, pets, and tobacco smoke. Services are provided by county health departments in participating counties.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Health Worker Certification and Training Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive accredited Community Health Worker training and certification program offered by the Maryland Department of Health through partnerships with local community colleges and organizations. The program trains individuals to provide health education and support services in their communities through accredited training available in English and Spanish at multiple statewide locations including Salisbury, Brentwood, CCBC Essex campus, Columbia (Howard County), Largo (Prince George's County), Frederick, La Plata, Arbutus, Silver Spring, and through partner organizations like The Healthy Church in Columbia, the Asian American Center of Frederick, College of Southern Maryland Foundation, The E-See Seeds LLC, Prince George's Community College, and Fenote Training Academy. Training opportunities with scholarship and stipend support are available throughout the state, with specific scholarship and stipend programs through the College of Southern Maryland Foundation in the Southern Maryland region (Calvert, Charles, and St. Mary's counties). Upon completion of an accredited CHW training program, individuals can obtain state certification valid for two years at no cost. Certification requires applicants to be at least 18 years old, hold a high school diploma or GED equivalent, and provide documentation of successful completion from an accredited training program.

Scholarship and stipend opportunities are available through various institutional partners, with specific programs available through the College of Southern Maryland Foundation for eligible students in the Southern Maryland region. Certification is issued at no charge and requires submission of documentation from the accredited training program including program name, address, accreditation number, completion date, and authorized signature, along with verification of age and a high school diploma or GED equivalent. structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid 1915(c) Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) waiver program that provides support services to help individuals with developmental disabilities live more independently at home and in their communities. The program offers a variety of meaningful day services (employment services, supported employment, employment discovery and customization, career exploration, community development services, day habilitation, medical day care), support services (assistive technology, behavior support, environmental modifications, family mentoring, housing support, nursing support, respite care, transportation, vehicle modifications, and other supports), and residential services (supported living, shared living, group homes, and community living with enhanced supports). Services are available through both self-directed and traditional agency-based models as an alternative to institutional care.

Services are available through self-directed or traditional agency-based models. structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid buy-in program that allows workers with disabilities to maintain Medicaid coverage even when their earnings would normally make them ineligible by purchasing coverage based on a sliding scale premium. Participants ages 16 to 64 can maintain Medicaid coverage while employed or self-employed. Premiums effective January 1, 2026 range from $0 for individuals earning less than $15,960 annually to 7.5% of monthly countable income for those earning $95,760 or more, with specific monthly rates of $25, $40, or $55 for intermediate income brackets. Married couples have higher income thresholds. Asset limit is $10,000. Hardship exemptions are available for those temporarily unable to pay premiums for up to 6 months.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly Medicaid health insurance coverage with sliding scale premiums based on income. Premiums effective January 1, 2026: individuals earning less than $15,960 annually pay $0; $15,960-$31,920 pay $25/month; $31,920-$39,900 pay $40/month; $39,900-$47,880 pay $55/month; $47,880-$71,820 pay 4% of monthly income; $71,820-$95,760 pay 5% of monthly income; $95,760+ pay 7.5% of monthly income. Asset limit is $10,000. Participants pay the monthly premium to maintain Medicaid eligibility while working. For those unable to pay premiums, a Claim of Hardship Exemption is available for up to 6 months.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the EID Program application with blue or black ink or use fillable PDF online, sign and date it, gather and include all supporting documents including pay stubs (4 weekly, 2 bi-weekly, or 3 monthly), bank statements with first day of application month, Schedule C if self-employed or business ledger, and life insurance/funeral plans/burial fund documentation if applicable. Maryland Department of Health will provide eligibility determination within 30 days of receipt.

structured_extraction.program_name: Food System Aggregation and Hubs + Local Foods Purchasing Strategies
structured_extraction.program_description: A funding opportunity to support food system aggregation, food hubs, and local foods purchasing strategies in rural Maryland to increase access to locally produced foods. This program is part of Maryland's Rural Health Transformation Program funded by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) under a cooperative agreement.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal financial assistance in the form of a cooperative agreement providing funding for food system aggregation infrastructure, food hub development, and local foods purchasing strategies in rural Maryland. Funds support implementation of approved initiatives from December 29, 2025 through October 30, 2030 across five budget periods. Funding amounts are allocated annually based on technical score and performance metrics. Allowable uses include personnel costs, equipment, minor renovations/alterations (capped at 20% of award), and provider payments for clinical services. Administrative costs are capped at 10% of total budget.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Awards announced by December 31, 2025
structured_extraction.contact_name: Project Officer (PO) and Grants Management Specialist (GMS)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Food system organizations, aggregators, food hubs, and entities supporting local foods purchasing in rural Maryland. Rural healthcare providers and communities. State health departments and organizations implementing rural health transformation initiatives.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food system aggregation infrastructure, food hub development, and local foods purchasing strategies and programs. Minor renovations and alterations (capped at 20% of total award). Personnel and project-related costs (fully itemized and justified). Equipment acquisition (nonexpendable personal property with acquisition cost of $10,000 or more). Provider payments for clinical services. EMR/EHR system upgrades. Telehealth equipment and infrastructure. Training and education programs. Evaluation and needs assessment activities. Administrative costs (capped at 10%). NOT ALLOWED: New construction or major building expansions, meals for community meetings, demolition, lobbying activities, pre-award costs, clinician salaries with non-compete clauses, duplicate payments for services reimbursable by insurance, perpetual funding-dependent expenses, international clinical worker recruitment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rural areas and rural communities within Maryland as defined by the State in its application. Funds must broadly benefit rural areas and rural residents.
requirements_list: Must be partner or subawardee of Maryland's RHTP cooperative agreement with CMS
Must comply with RHTP terms and conditions
Non-supplanting requirement: funds cannot replace current federal, State, or local funding
Minimum 5-year service commitment required for clinical workforce recruitment/retention initiatives
Administrative costs limited to 10% of total budget
Minor alterations and renovations capped at 20% of total award
Sustainability plan required for initiatives to be sustainable after program funding ends in October 2030
Submit revised budget by January 30, 2026
Submit quarterly reports with specific due dates
Submit annual Expenditure Federal Financial Report (FFR) within 90 days of budget period end
Submit final FFR within 120 days of performance period end
Finalize State policy actions by December 31, 2027 or 2028 for specific policies
Use funds only for approved applications and NOFO purposes
Maintain HIPAA-compliant privacy and security safeguards
Maintain current SAM.gov registration with UEI
Subaward reporting for amounts ≥$40,000 within 30 days
CMS review and approval of publications, presentations, and communications (30 days prior)
Press releases and media materials (7 days prior)
Annual property inventory reporting
Patent and invention reporting (Form HHS 568 within 120 days of project end)
Audit reporting if expending $1,000,000+ in federal awards annually
SAM.gov debarment checks for all subrecipients and contractors
Provision of NPI, Tax ID, and EIN for key personnel and entities within 30 days of award start
Data submission and documentation as requested by CMS
Return of CMS-provided data at project conclusion
Subaward monitoring and compliance
Records retention per 2 CFR 200.334
No changes to initiatives may be implemented prior to receiving explicit written approval from CMS
Coordinate with assigned Project Officers regarding initiative performance concerns
Cannot unilaterally modify, suspend, or cancel initiatives
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This is a post-award program for which Maryland Department of Health has already received a cooperative agreement. Application details for subrecipients or additional funding requests should be directed to the Project Officer and Grants Management Specialist. Applicants should check the RHTP procurement page for updates on any additional opportunities or subrecipient application processes.

structured_extraction.program_description: A special category of eligibility and priority for developmental disability services designed to help students ages 21 to 22 transition from school to adult services and employment. The program funds supported employment services, day services, and targeted case management for eligible graduating students who otherwise may not have received services or would have been placed on a lengthy waiting list. Services are provided through person-centered planning to identify desired services and support needs. This is a collaboration between the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) and Maryland's Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) to help youth and families navigate a path toward a 'good life' as adults.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The DDA earmarks funds in its budget to provide supported employment services, day services, and targeted case management for eligible transitioning youth. Funding comes from federal waiver programs including Community Pathways, Family Supports, and Community Supports. Services are delivered through care management by Coordinators of Community Services (CCS) agencies and person-centered planning to identify desired services and support needs. Day services include career discovery, exploration, and skill-building. Employment support services are aligned with Employment First principles.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 30 of the eligibility year
structured_extraction.contact_name: Beryl Parker (Central Maryland), Jim Sullivan (Eastern Shore), Nicole Sheppard (Southern Maryland), Brenda Sperow (Western Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth with developmental disabilities ages 21 to 22 transitioning from high school, families of transitioning youth, and Maryland residents who meet developmental disability eligibility requirements. Eligibility begins at the individual's 21st birthday and continues until their 22nd birthday, or for one year after graduation if graduation occurs after the 21st birthday.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supported employment services, day services, targeted case management, care coordination, person-centered planning, career discovery, exploration, skill-building, and services to obtain and maintain community employment. Funding from federal waiver programs (Community Pathways, Family Supports, Community Supports) and DDA budget earmarks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in the State of Maryland. Statewide across all Maryland counties, with regional offices serving Central Maryland (Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford, Howard), Southern Maryland (Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's), Western Maryland (Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Washington), and Eastern Shore (Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester).
requirements_list: Must be found fully eligible as developmentally disabled
Must have a severe chronic disability attributable to a physical or mental impairment (other than sole diagnosis of mental illness) or combination of mental and physical impairments
Disability must be manifested before age 22
Disability must be likely to continue indefinitely
Must result in inability to live independently without external support or continuing and regular assistance
Must reflect need for a combination and sequence of special, interdisciplinary or generic care, treatment, or other services that are individually planned and coordinated
Must be ages 21 to 22 years old (or one year after graduation if graduation occurs after 21st birthday)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for DDA services through the Division of Developmental Disabilities and the standard eligibility process. Once determined to be eligible for DDA services as developmentally disabled, individuals in the transitioning youth age range receive priority and access to the Governor's Transitioning Youth Initiative. Applications must be submitted by June 30 of the eligibility year. A Coordinator of Community Services assists with accessing services and developing a person-centered plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant programs administered by the Maryland Department of Health Behavioral Health Administration Office of Harm Reduction that support local implementation of harm reduction programs and ensure statewide access to resources for harm reduction activities, including naloxone and syringe service programs. ACCESS stands for Advancing Cross-Cutting Engagement and Service Strategies for People Who Use Drugs. The program provides funding to support harm reduction activities aligned with the strategic goal of reducing substance-related morbidity and mortality by optimizing services for people who use drugs. The program currently provides funding to 50 organizations (28 nonprofits and 22 Local Health Departments).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support local implementation of harm reduction programs and ensure statewide access to resources for harm reduction activities, including naloxone distribution and syringe service programs. Currently provides funding to 50 organizations (28 nonprofits and 22 Local Health Departments) to conduct harm reduction activities aligned with Office of Harm Reduction strategic goals. Funding covers personnel costs (salaries, FICA, retirement, health insurance, workers' compensation, unemployment insurance), consultants and special payments, travel (in-state and out-of-state), training, supplies (educational, medical, office, other), postage, advertising, gas/oil, human service contracts, medicine, drugs and chemicals, and indirect costs (10%). Syringe Service Programs must submit quarterly reports

structured_extraction.program_description: A 5-year grant program providing $41,550,000 in funding to twelve grantees supporting new and expanded clinical interventions and social determinants of health support for marginalized populations across Maryland. Programs address health disparities and improve health outcomes in areas including cardiovascular disease, diabetes, mental health, social isolation, maternal and child health, substance abuse disorder, obesity, childhood vaccination, sickle cell disease, and elder care. The program provides free clinical services and social services support including transportation, food assistance, and housing. No one will be turned away. Services include nurse-managed health centers, mobile health, remote patient monitoring, care coordination, health screenings, preventive care, disease-specific interventions, insurance enrollment, and primary care access. Implementation period runs from July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2029.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 5-year implementation grants totaling $41,550,000 awarded to twelve selected grantees to support new and expanded clinical interventions and social determinants of health support programs for marginalized populations. Grantees include healthcare systems, hospitals, Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), university schools of nursing and medicine, county health departments, community-based organizations, faith-based organizations, and community health centers/clinics. Funds support direct primary care services, community health worker programs, mobile health programs, nurse-managed health centers, telehealth services, social determinants of health linkages and support (housing, transportation, food assistance, insurance enrollment, job placement), health education and screening events, and care coordination and case management. Implementation period runs from July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2029.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income residents, residents living below poverty level, frail and elderly residents, people experiencing homelessness, African American and Haitian communities, Latina/Latinx women and communities, Hispanic women and children, rural residents, patients with chronic diseases (cardiovascular disease, diabetes, hypertension, obesity, substance use disorder, sickle cell disease), pregnant women and mothers, infants, and children across Maryland experiencing health disparities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct clinical services including nurse-managed health centers, mobile health programs, remote patient monitoring, primary care access, health screenings and preventive care, mental health services, substance use disorder services, chronic disease management, maternal and infant health services, disease-specific interventions (hypertension, diabetes, maternal health, substance use disorder, sickle cell disease). Social determinants of health support including housing assistance, food assistance, transportation assistance, insurance enrollment and coverage, care coordination and case management, community health worker programs, telehealth services, health education and community outreach, and job placement services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Implementation across ten specific counties: Baltimore City, St. Mary's County, Wicomico County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Somerset County, Talbot County, Allegany County, Garrett County, and Washington County. Twelve HERC grantees are implementing programs across these areas.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The HERC Programs are open for enrollment. Eligible individuals can enroll directly with HERC grantees. For enrollment information and program services descriptions, contact the program through the provided enrollment information link.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Babies - Pregnancy and Postpartum Coverage
structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid program that provides free health care coverage to pregnant individuals and continues coverage for up to four months after childbirth, regardless of citizenship status. The program also provides one year of coverage for children born to mothers on this program. Coverage includes pregnancy-related medical expenses including prenatal care, hospital delivery, postpartum care, dental care, lab work and tests, prescription drugs, mental health care, behavioral health services, and non-emergency medical transportation for those who meet income limits. Medicaid may also help pay for health care received in the three months before application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid covers healthcare costs including doctor visits, prenatal visits, hospital care and delivery, dental care, lab work and tests, prescription drugs, mental health care, behavioral health services, and non-emergency medical transportation. Coverage begins upon approval and continues through pregnancy and up to four months after the baby is born. Children born to mothers on this program receive one year of coverage. Medicaid may also help pay for health care received in the three months before application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive lead hazard reduction and healthy homes program that helps families with pregnant women, children under age 6, or children with elevated blood lead levels or moderate to severe asthma identify and reduce lead hazards in homes built before 1978. The program provides at no cost to eligible families: lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed; window replacement, door replacement, wall stabilization, and minimal structural repairs; lead-based paint risk assessments; healthy homes housing assessments and interventions; in-home case management and visiting services to reduce exposures to lead and asthma triggers; and outreach and education. Environmental assessments address dust, pests, mold, pets, and tobacco smoke. Services are provided by county health departments in participating counties statewide, with additional HUD-funded grant assistance available through Baltimore City for qualifying low to moderate income households and landlords. The Baltimore City program runs from April 1, 2026 to April 1, 2030 with $4,100,000 in HUD grant funding ($3,600,000 for Lead-Based Paint Hazard Control and $500,000 for Healthy Homes Supplemental Program) plus $1,516,000 in local match funds.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed, provided at no cost to eligible families in most counties. Interventions including window replacement, door replacement, wall stabilization, and minimal structural repairs. Lead-based paint risk assessments, healthy homes housing assessments, and healthy homes interventions to address environmental and safety hazards including dust, pests, mold, pets, and tobacco smoke. In-home case management, visiting services, outreach and education sessions provided to families with eligible children to help reduce lead exposure and asthma triggers and improve asthma outcomes. In Baltimore City, HUD grant funding of $4,100,000 total ($3,600,000 for Lead-Based Paint Hazard Control and $500,000 for Healthy Homes Supplemental Program) with $1,516,000 in local match funds is available for April 1, 2026 through April 1, 2030. Services include lead risk assessments, lead hazard reduction, healthy homes assessments and interventions, outreach and education sessions, and post-remediation home visits. Services are delivered by county health departments and Baltimore City in participating counties at no cost to eligible families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland families with pregnant women or children under age 6, or children 18 years old or younger who have elevated blood lead levels (3.5 ug/dL or higher in most counties, 5 ug/dL and above in Baltimore City), moderate to severe asthma, or both, and live in homes built before 1978 in eligible counties. Children must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland's Children's Health Program (MCHP). Low to moderate income households with children under age six who have elevated blood lead levels in Baltimore City. Homeowners and landlords with children spending at least 3 hours a day on two separate days a week and a total of 60 hours per year at the property also qualify.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed. Window replacement, door replacement, wall stabilization, and minimal structural repairs. Lead-based paint risk assessments, lead hazard reduction activities, paint stabilization and dust wipe clearance testing. Healthy homes housing rating system assessments and interventions to address environmental and safety hazards including dust, pests, mold, pets, and tobacco smoke. In-home visits, environmental case management, exposure reduction services, outreach and education sessions. Services to improve asthma outcomes for eligible children and post-remediation home visits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland with home visiting services available in Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, and Wicomico counties. Additional grant and loan funding available in Baltimore City for dwellings constructed prior to 1978.

Child must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland Children's Insurance Program (MCHP)
Child must spend 10 hours or more per week in the location where the lead exposure occurred (home, apartment, or day care)
Family must have a child exposed to lead or with moderate to severe asthma
Pregnant woman or child under age 6 living in the house, or a child spending 3 hours a day on two separate days a week and a total of 60 hours per year at the property
Income must not exceed guidelines based on household size and occupancy type (homeowner or renter occupied)
Household must be low to moderate income (Baltimore City)
At least one household member must have elevated blood lead levels
Homeowners and landlords may apply; landlords must contribute a portion of costs
Dwelling must have been constructed prior to 1978
Family resides in one of the eligible counties

For Baltimore City residents, apply online through the portal or complete a pre-application form and send it to the LIGHT Intake & Assessment Unit at 417 East Fayette Street, Suite 1125, Baltimore, MD 21202. structured_extraction.program_name: Home & Community Based Options Waiver Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state medical assistance program that provides services to enable adults 18 and older whose care needs meet the requirements for nursing home placement to live in a community setting instead of a long-term care facility. The program allows Medicaid to cover services typically only available in nursing homes when provided in participants' own homes or assisted living facilities. Qualified individuals can use waivers for either assisted living or in-home care services. The State pays for covered services through Medicaid to enable eligible clients to remain in the community rather than move to a nursing facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State pays for covered services through Medicaid to enable eligible clients to remain in the community rather than move to a nursing facility. Services are provided in participants' own homes or assisted living facilities, covering community-based care services for qualified individuals who meet medical and financial criteria. Financial assistance is available for either assisted living or in-home care services.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports and enhances the ability of hospitals and health care systems to provide effective care and save lives during emergencies and disasters that exceed normal day-to-day capacity. structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Health receives annual federal funding from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response (ASPR) and awards these funds in the form of grants to health care system partners across the state, including hospitals, free-standing emergency departments, community health centers, state-managed facilities, poison control centers, emergency medical services, home care and hospice agencies, and regional health care preparedness coalitions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hospitals, health care systems, community health centers, state-managed facilities, poison control centers, emergency medical services, home care and hospice agencies, and regional health care preparedness coalitions across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhance ability to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters and other emergencies that pose a threat to the health and safety of the community. Funds support development of regional health care coalitions, joint training and exercise opportunities, access to shared assets and equipment, and coordinated preparedness planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. structured_extraction.program_description: Hospitals can immediately determine Medicaid eligibility for certain individuals who are likely to be eligible, allowing temporary but immediate access to coverage for up to 60 days. This ensures the hospital will be reimbursed for services provided during this temporary coverage period, even if Medicaid later finds the individual ineligible, and provides individuals an opportunity to connect to longer-term coverage options. HPE provides temporary Medicaid coverage authorization that allows immediate enrollment without waiting for full application processing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hospitals receive reimbursement for services provided to individuals determined eligible under HPE during the temporary 60-day coverage period. HPE provides coverage for up to 60 days maximum, ensuring hospital reimbursement for services provided during the temporary coverage period even if the individual is later found ineligible for full Medicaid coverage. Eligible individuals receive immediate access to Medicaid coverage without waiting for full application processing, allowing immediate enrollment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland hospitals that are participating Medicaid providers in good standing seeking to become qualified HPE entities, and individuals likely to be eligible for Medicaid
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hospitals use HPE determinations to immediately enroll eligible individuals in temporary Medicaid coverage for health care services. Coverage of health care services provided by participating Maryland Medicaid hospitals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; all Maryland counties
requirements_list: Hospital must be a participating Maryland Medicaid provider in good standing
Hospital must complete and submit the MDH HPE Application and Agreement
Hospital must apply to become a qualified HPE entity and be approved
Hospital employees making HPE determinations must attend required training
Staff must pass HPE certification test prior to making HPE determinations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the MDH HPE Application and Agreement. Submit the application to become a qualified entity. Once approved, designate an HPE primary contact who will email the Maryland Department of Health to request staff training. Hospital employees must attend the required training and pass the HPE certification test before they can make presumptive eligibility determinations. To request training, the hospital's HPE primary contact emails the Maryland Department of Health with a list of attendees.

The program offers reduced-cost car seat purchases for financially eligible families, in-person technical assistance through Child Passenger Safety 101 presentations and checkup events, virtual education through monthly webinars, training for child transporters and agency staff, and an information clearinghouse with a helpline and email support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides reduced-cost car seat and booster seat purchases for financially eligible families. It also offers free technical assistance including in-person child passenger safety presentations, training for child transporters and agency staff, car seat checkup events, virtual webinars offered monthly, and an information clearinghouse with a helpline and email support answering questions about car seat selection, usage, installation, and local assistance resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Caregivers, families, and child providers or transporters in Maryland who want to properly select, install, and use car seats and booster seats for children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduced-cost car seat and booster seat purchases for financially eligible families. Technical assistance, training, and educational materials on child passenger safety, car seat selection, installation, and usage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Financial eligibility required for reduced-cost car seat purchase program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the KISS program through the helpline at 800-370-SEAT, email at mdkiss@maryland.gov, or visit www.mdkiss.org to inquire about car seat assistance, schedule a checkup or video call, book a presentation or training, or obtain educational materials. Monthly webinars are available through registration links provided on the program website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The LISS Program serves children living at home with their family and adults with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities living in their own home in the community who are not receiving any support services from the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), as well as people on the DDA waiting list. The program provides limited funding (up to $1,000 per eligible child or adult) to help eligible individuals and families purchase eligible services and items from approved vendors including personal and attendant care, respite care, adaptive items, assistive technology, childcare, community integration and recreational services, educational services, home modifications, identification services, summer camps, transportation, and wellness services to address their needs, enhance quality of life, promote independence, productivity, and support community integration across their lifespan. Participants are randomly selected from qualified applicants and must provide documentation to verify identity, disability, residency, and eligible services delivered by approved vendors. The program aims to help eligible individuals live happy, healthy, independent lives while being integrated into their communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides up to $1,000 per applicant for FY 2026 to assist eligible children and adults with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities with purchasing eligible services and/or items from approved vendors to address their needs and maximize independence, productivity, and integration within the community. Services may include adaptive items, assistive technology, attendant/personal care, childcare, community integration and recreational services, educational services, home modification and barrier removal, identification services, respite care, summer camps, transportation, and wellness services. Applicants are randomly selected from those with eligible diagnoses. Selected applicants must provide documentation verifying identity, disability, Maryland residency, and that services are delivered by an eligible vendor.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Round 1 closes September 15, 2025

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing eligible services and/or items from approved vendors including adaptive items, assistive technology, attendant/personal care, childcare, community integration and recreational services, educational services, home modification and barrier removal, identification services, respite care, summer camps, transportation, and wellness services to address the needs of children and adults with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities that enhance quality of life, promote independence, productivity, and support community integration. Penn-Mar Human Services serves Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard and Washington counties. Applicants must be residents of the state of Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative providing free recommended vaccines to uninsured and underinsured adults age 19 and older to expand immunization access and reduce barriers to vaccination. Vaccines are available through local health departments across Maryland and include COVID-19, influenza, measles, pneumonia, respiratory syncytial virus, shingles, tetanus/diphtheria/pertussis, hepatitis A and B, polio, measles/mumps/rubella, varicella, rotavirus, haemophilus influenzae type B, human papillomavirus, meningitis, and rabies (in specific circumstances). The program is state-funded with $2.8 million allocated in partnership with the Maryland General Assembly and helps reduce the spread of vaccine-preventable diseases. No one will be turned away due to inability to pay.

All vaccines are fully subsidized with no cost to recipients. The program is funded through $2.8 million allocated in partnership with the Maryland General Assembly.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Breast and Cervical Cancer Program (BCCP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides education, screening, diagnosis, and treatment services for breast and cervical cancers to low-income, uninsured, and underinsured Maryland residents. The program has two main components: (1) early detection screening services delivered through local health departments, health systems, and hospitals; and (2) reimbursement to healthcare providers for diagnosis and treatment services delivered to eligible program participants. Services include clinical breast exams, mammograms, ultrasounds, biopsies, Pap and HPV tests, colposcopy, follow-up testing, patient navigation assistance, appointment scheduling, transportation assistance, and interpretation services. The program provides grants to local health departments and health systems to support cancer screening, diagnosis, patient navigation, outreach, and education services. Works with local health departments, health systems, hospitals, physicians, physician assistants, pharmacies, medical laboratories, and other healthcare providers to improve screening rates among medically-underserved populations and provide comprehensive care support. Particularly focuses on early detection through no-cost screenings on Maryland's Eastern Shore where treatment is most effective when cancer is caught early. Funded by the Centers for Disease Prevention and Control (CDC) and the Maryland Cigarette Restitution Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides project grants to local health departments, hospitals, and health systems to support cancer screening, diagnosis, patient navigation, outreach, and education services. Grant funds support the provision of breast and cervical cancer screenings including outreach, education, and follow-up services. Funds can hire community health outreach workers and contract with private physicians, radiologists, surgeons, and medical laboratories. Free or no-cost screening, diagnostic, treatment, and patient navigation services for eligible residents provided through local programs including local health departments, health systems, and hospitals. Services include clinical breast exams, mammograms, ultrasounds, biopsies, Pap and HPV tests, colposcopy, follow-up testing, appointment scheduling, transportation assistance, interpretation services, and linkage to treatment. The program reimburses qualified healthcare providers including hospitals, physicians, physician assistants, pharmacies, medical laboratories, medical item suppliers, nurse practitioners, nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, physical and occupational therapists, and home health agencies for diagnosis and treatment services delivered to program participants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state and federally funded health insurance program that provides full health benefits to eligible uninsured children under age 19 and pregnant women of any age whose family income is too low to afford private health insurance but may exceed Medicaid limits. The program covers children whose family income exceeds Medicaid limits but is insufficient to afford private health insurance, as well as pregnant women. Coverage is provided through Maryland's nine HealthChoice managed care organizations. Benefits include dental care, doctor visits for well and sick care, hospital care, immunizations, lab work and tests, mental health services, prescription medicine, substance abuse treatment, transportation to medical care, and vision care. Eligibility is based on family income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, or up to 300% with a premium.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MCHP provides full health benefits coverage to eligible children and pregnant women at no or low cost through one of Maryland's HealthChoice managed care organizations. Children under age 19 with countable income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level receive full coverage at no cost. Pregnant women of any age with income at or below 200% of federal poverty level receive full coverage. Coverage up to 300% of the federal poverty level is available with a premium. Benefits include behavioral health/mental health services, dental care, doctor visits for well and sick care, emergency services, family planning, home health, hospital care, immunizations, lab work and tests, mental health services, prenatal/postpartum care, prescription medicine, substance abuse treatment, transportation to medical care, urgent care, vision exams and glasses for children under 21, and no copays for children under 21 and pregnant women. Families select their preferred managed care organization. Approved applicants receive an enrollment packet in the mail.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC) Annual Request for Applications (RFA)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC) awards competitive grants to expand access to affordable, high-quality health care services in underserved communities across Maryland. The program helps communities address barriers to accessing health care through funding for various health initiatives including hospital-community partnerships, primary care, chronic disease prevention and management, dental care, behavioral health and substance use disorder services, maternal and child health promotion, support for medically vulnerable populations, reduction of infant mortality, and facilitation of health information technology adoption among safety net providers. Applicants address two strategic priorities: advancing health equity by addressing health disparities and social determinants of health through community partnerships, and supporting safety net providers and community-based organizations to align with state health initiatives. Community health resources must offer primary health care services or access services using a sliding fee schedule, providing free or nominal fees to individuals below 100% of federal poverty guidelines and free or reduced-price services to those at 100-200% of federal poverty guidelines. The Commission is an independent entity within the Maryland Department of Health, authorized by the Community Health Care Access and Safety Net Act of 2005 and re-authorized by the Maryland General Assembly in 2024 until June 2035. Since its inception in 2005, the CHRC has awarded 985 grants totaling $396 million, serving more than 912,000 Marylanders, enabling grantees to leverage $54 million in additional federal and private/non-profit resources, and achieving program sustainability rates of approximately 75% one or more years after initial funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The CHRC makes approximately $7 million in grant funding available annually through a competitive Call for Proposals process to help communities address barriers to accessing health care. Grants are awarded for up to three years with individual grant amounts anticipated between $300,000 and $750,000. Funding is distributed across six areas of focus with allocation ranges of approximately $1,000,000 to $1,500,000 per area. Grants are evaluated competitively by independent subject matter experts based on use of evidence-based practices, ability to collect and report outcome data, demonstration of community need, program sustainability, and likelihood of overall program success. Applicants can apply for funding in six areas of focus: hospital-community partnerships, support for medically vulnerable populations including older adults and individuals with disabilities, chronic disease prevention and management, maternal and child health, dental health, and behavioral health for adults including mental health and substance use disorder services. Additional preference (5 points) given to proposals serving ENOUGH initiative census tracts. Awards are expected to be announced in late June 2026. Permitted uses of funds include salaries and employment benefits for project staff, subcontracting and consultant fees, data collection and analysis, project-related travel, conference calls, and meetings, office supplies and indirect costs (up to 15% of direct costs or higher if federally approved), limited essential equipment, minor infrastructure improvements, staff training and development, and program marketing. Prohibited uses include major equipment purchase or lease, construction projects, clinical trials, unapproved medical devices or drugs, and lobbying activities. Fringe benefits are limited to 25% of total salaries. Funding covers activities not currently covered by insurance or other sources and supports clinical health services, non-medical social determinants of health interventions, workforce development, technology investments, mobile clinics, case management, peer recovery specialist programs, harm reduction initiatives, telehealth services, transportation assistance, and dental prostheses. All funds must be used in compliance with the Department's Standard Grant Agreement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Letter of Intent due March 30, 2026 by 3:00 PM EDT; Full proposals due April 23, 2026 by 3:00 PM EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, for-profit entities, government agencies, higher education institutions, community-based organizations, hospitals, safety net providers, federally qualified health centers (FQHCs), local health departments, substance use treatment providers, outpatient mental health clinics, school-based health centers, and other eligible provider types serving underserved communities throughout Maryland seeking to expand access to health care services and address barriers to health care access, health disparities, and social determinants of health. Priority populations include low-income individuals, vulnerable populations in underserved rural and urban communities, medically vulnerable populations including older adults and individuals with disabilities, individuals with multiple chronic diseases, individuals aged 18+ for behavioral health services, and individuals with annual family income below 200% of federal poverty guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects addressing health disparities and social determinants of health such as food security, transportation, health insurance coverage, and other non-medical barriers to care. Six designated areas of focus: (1) hospital-community partnerships, (2) support for medically vulnerable populations including older adults and individuals with disabilities, (3) primary care and chronic disease prevention and management (diabetes, hypertension, heart disease), (4) maternal and child health promotion and reduction of infant mortality, (5) dental care supporting Maryland Medicaid Dental Benefit, and (6) behavioral health for adults including mental health and substance use disorder services and support for opioid crisis. Permitted use of funds includes clinical health services, non-medical social determinants of health interventions including transportation to services, food assistance, and case management; workforce development and training programs; technology investments including telehealth services; equipment and IT/telecom infrastructure (limited essential equipment and minor infrastructure improvements, not major capital); supplies; staff salaries and fringe benefits; contractual services; data collection and analysis; project-related travel, conference calls, and meetings; program marketing; and indirect costs. Community health resources must provide free or nominal fee services to individuals below 100% of federal poverty guidelines and free or reduced-price services to those at 100-200% of federal poverty guidelines. Funds may not be used for major capital expenses, construction, clinical trials, unapproved medical devices or drugs, lobbying, or activities that duplicate other funding sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout all jurisdictions in Maryland. Priority consideration given to applicants serving high-need populations in underserved areas of the state and the 116 census tracts eligible under the ENOUGH initiative. Applicants must address the totality of medical and non-medical needs in their communities through innovative and sustainable community partnerships. Service sites must be located within Maryland and services provided primarily to Maryland residents.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program and framework that expands access to comprehensive behavioral health services for Maryland students. The program addresses behavioral health challenges through prevention, behavioral health screenings, counseling, addiction treatment, family support, crisis planning and services, telehealth services, support groups, and wraparound services. In the first round, the program provided 127 grants totaling $110 million. The second round (contract period July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026) supports programs in all 24 jurisdictions, with grantees planning to serve more than 165,000 students statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants to support behavioral health services in schools across Maryland. The first round supported 127 grants totaling $110 million. The second round (contract period July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026) supports programs in all 24 jurisdictions, with grantees planning to serve more than 165,000 students statewide. Funds support hiring of practitioners and delivery of prevention, screening, counseling, addiction treatment, family support, crisis planning, telehealth, and wraparound services. Notable example: Anne Arundel County's Community Supports Partnership brings together 13 service providers and is expected to serve approximately 12,000 students over the next year.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland schools, students, and their families seeking behavioral health services and related support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Behavioral health services including prevention, screenings, counseling, addiction treatment, family support, crisis planning, telehealth services, support groups, and wraparound services for students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; programs support services in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Anne Arundel County has one of the first Community Supports Partnership Programs in the state.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Dent-Care Loan Assistance Repayment Program (MDC-LARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A student loan repayment program that provides financial assistance to dentists and dental hygienists who agree to treat Maryland Medical Assistance Program (MMAP) recipients. The program aims to increase access to oral health care services for Maryland's most vulnerable populations by offering loan repayment assistance to healthcare providers who commit to serving low-income patients in underserved Maryland areas. Dentists may receive up to $50,000 per year for up to 3 years of obligated service. Dental hygienists may receive up to $10,000 per year for up to 2 years of obligated service. Participating providers must treat a minimum of 30% MMAP recipients as part of their total patient population per year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full-time dentists receive up to $50,000 per year for a three-year commitment (total up to $150,000). Part-time dentists (20-39 hours per week with at least 80% clinical hours) receive up to $25,000 per year for a three-year commitment (total up to $75,000). Full-time dental hygienists receive up to $10,000 per year for a two-year commitment (total up to $20,000). Part-time dental hygienists receive up to $5,000 per year for a two-year commitment (total up to $10,000). The number of recipients per award is determined based on available funding. Participating providers must treat a minimum of 30% MMAP recipients as part of their total patient population per year. Dentists can renew for up to two additional years after the initial year, totaling 3 years maximum. Dental hygienists can renew for up to one additional year after the initial year, totaling 2 years maximum.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application cycle opens in March and closes in July
structured_extraction.contact_name: Stacy Costello, MPH, CHES, Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed dentists and dental hygienists in Maryland who are willing to commit to treating Maryland Medical Assistance Program (MMAP) recipients in underserved areas and have outstanding student loan debt.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Student loan repayment assistance for eligible higher education loans for dentists and dental hygienists.

Applicant must be practicing in Maryland and treat Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients in Maryland. Must have received degree from Maryland institution or accredited U.S. dental school.

The program supports community education, trauma-informed approaches, and linkages to behavioral health services. Training and technical assistance are delivered through in-person and online learning opportunities. The program is transitioning to new leadership with Health HIV starting July 1, 2025.
