structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Repayment Program for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded loan repayment assistance program administered by the Maryland Department of Health that helps nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, and nursing support staff repay their education loans in exchange for a service obligation to work at an eligible practice site in Maryland that serves underserved populations or areas experiencing healthcare professional shortages. The program offers tiered maximum awards based on credential level and employment status, with service obligations ranging from 1-2 years. Participants must commit to practicing in areas of Maryland experiencing health professional shortages, with funding through state-level resources. The Maryland Department of Health pays verified education loan holders directly on behalf of eligible participants. Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (CRNP, CNM, CRNA, CNS) receive up to $100,000 for full-time work or $50,000 for part-time work with a 2-year service obligation. Registered nurses and licensed practical nurses receive up to $50,000 for full-time or $25,000 for part-time with a 2-year obligation. Nursing support staff (CMT, CMA, CNA, GNA) receive up to $5,000 for full-time or $2,500 for part-time with a 1-year obligation. Full-time means 40 or more hours per week; part-time means 20-39 hours per week. Established in 2022 via Senate Bill 696/House Bill 975, with expansion to for-profit employment as of 2025 via HB 0019/SB 216.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Health repays verified education loans held by eligible participants through direct payment to loan holders. Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (CRNP, CNM, CRNA, CNS) receive up to $100,000 for full-time work or $50,000 for part-time work with a 2-year service obligation. Registered nurses and licensed practical nurses receive up to $50,000 for full-time or $25,000 for part-time with a 2-year obligation. Nursing support staff (CMT, CMA, CNA, GNA) receive up to $5,000 for full-time or $2,500 for part-time with a 1-year obligation. Full-time means 40 or more hours per week; part-time means 20-39 hours per week. Participants must work part-time (20-39 hours per week) or full-time (40+ hours per week) at an approved eligible practice site, with at least 80 percent of work hours dedicated to direct patient care (50 percent for Certified Nurse Midwives in ambulatory care). Award amounts vary based on technical scoring and available funding, and participants may receive less than the maximum award if funding is limited. Participants may receive up to two MLRP service obligations during their lifetime. Loan repayment funds are paid directly to the verified education loan holder. The program is based on a service obligation model, meaning participants agree to work at eligible sites in exchange for loan repayment assistance. Two full payments are made over a 2-year service obligation period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Approximately March 1 through April 15 (11:59 p.m., EST)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nurses (RN, LPN), Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (CRNP, CNM, CRNA, CNS), and Nursing Support Staff (CMT, CMA, CNA, GNA) who are U.S. citizens or nationals with active and valid licenses, education loan debt, and employment at an eligible Maryland practice site willing to work in areas experiencing healthcare professional shortages.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of education loans obtained for tuition, educational expenses, or living expenses for undergraduate or graduate study leading to practice as an advanced practice registered nurse, nurse, or nursing support staff. Repayment cannot exceed the current outstanding education loan debt balance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Throughout Maryland, with priority for areas experiencing health professional shortages. Health Professional Shortage Areas (HPSA) and medically underserved areas/populations receive priority. Rural areas and outpatient services are prioritized. Participants must be employed at a practice site that is physically located in Maryland. For-profit sites must be located in areas of the state identified by the Department as having a health care workforce shortage or public health need. Public and non-profit sites exempt under Internal Revenue Code sections 501(c)(3) or (c)(4) are eligible statewide.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted annually from approximately March 1 through April 15 (11:59 p.m., EST). Practice sites must be approved by MLRP at the time of application. An employment contract with an eligible practice site must be in effect by July 1 following the application cycle. Applicants submit required documents including promissory notes and service obligations. Successful applicants must demonstrate compliance with eligibility criteria and meet monitoring requirements throughout the awarded service obligation. Service obligations commence July 1 following the application cycle. MLRP funds are paid directly to verified education loan holders by the Maryland Department of Health. Year 1 requires offer acceptance documentation including promissory note, service obligation agreement, lender verification form, and debarment affirmation. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Repayment Programs - Physicians, Physician Assistants, and Other Health Professionals
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive state loan repayment program that helps physicians, physician assistants, final year medical residents, nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, and nursing support staff repay qualifying education loans in exchange for a service obligation at an approved Maryland practice site. The program includes both a state-administered component (MLARP) and a federal State Loan Repayment Program (SLRP) component. Participants commit to working part-time or full-time at eligible practice sites that serve patients regardless of ability to pay, including health professional shortage areas (HPSA), medically underserved areas (MUA), or state-designated health professional shortage areas. The program is administered through the Maryland Department of Health's State Loan Repayment Program (SLRP) and the Maryland Loan Repayment Assistance Program (MLARP). The program provides varying award amounts based on credential type and employment status: physicians and physician assistants up to $100,000 full-time or $50,000 part-time per year; advanced practice registered nurses up to $100,000 full-time or $50,000 part-time; RN and LPN up to $50,000 full-time or $25,000 part-time; nursing support staff up to $5,000 full-time or $2,500 part-time. Service obligations range from 1 to 3 years depending on credential and commitment level. The program provides education loan repayment assistance by paying funds directly to verified education loan holders to repay qualifying education loans incurred for undergraduate or graduate study. The program aims to improve recruitment and retention of the health professional workforce, especially in areas experiencing health professional shortages. Participants may receive up to two service obligations per lifetime, with 2-year service obligation periods and two loan repayment payments distributed over the period (one per year).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan repayment assistance for qualifying education loans obtained for undergraduate or graduate study leading to practice as a physician, physician assistant, nurse, or other eligible health professional. Award amounts vary by credential: physicians and physician assistants up to $100,000 full-time or $50,000 part-time per year with maximum total award of $200,000 or two 2-year obligations; final year medical residents up to $100,000 full-time or $50,000 part-time with 3-year service obligation (1 year residency plus 2 years post-residency); advanced practice registered nurses up to $100,000 full-time or $50,000 part-time; RN and LPN up to $50,000 full-time or $25,000 part-time; nursing support staff up to $5,000 full-time or $2,500 part-time. For the federal SLRP component, up to $50,000 per year for a 2-year service obligation in a HPSA or MUA, with a maximum total award of $200,000 or two 2-year obligations. Participants must have a valid employment contract at an approved Maryland practice site located in a health professional shortage area (HPSA), medically underserved area (MUA), or state-designated health professional shortage area, or serving all patients regardless of ability to pay. The Maryland Department of Health pays loan repayment funds directly to verified education loan holders. Direct payments are made to lenders/loan servicers with two full payments distributed over the 2-year service obligation (one per year). Full-time participants work 40 or more hours per week, and part-time participants work 20-39 hours per week. Service obligations range from 1 to 3 years depending on credential type. Award amounts may vary; participants may receive less than the maximum depending on scoring bracket. Participants may receive up to two service obligations per lifetime.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application Enrollment Opens: approximately March 1; Application Deadline: approximately April 15 (11:59 p.m., EST)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Physicians (MD and DO), physician assistants, final year medical residents, nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, nursing support staff, and other health professionals who owe education loans and are willing to work at approved Maryland practice sites in health professional shortage areas, medically underserved areas, or state-designated health professional shortage areas. Primary care specialties prioritized: family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics, geriatrics, obstetrics/gynecology, mental health, clinical substance use disorder treatment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of qualifying education loans obtained for undergraduate or graduate study leading to practice as a physician, physician assistant, nurse, advanced practice registered nurse, or other eligible health professional. Loans must have been obtained for tuition, educational expenses, or living expenses. Loans obtained after licensure are not eligible. Loans may be private, federal, or other types.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Practice sites must be physically located in Maryland in health professional shortage areas (HPSA), medically underserved areas (MUA), or state-designated health professional shortage areas. For the state program, applicants must practice at an approved practice site serving all patients regardless of ability to pay. For the federal SLRP component, applicants must practice at an eligible practice site located in a health professional shortage area (HPSA) or medically underserved area (MUA). The program serves all Maryland counties with focus on areas experiencing healthcare professional shortages and rural areas. Primary care is prioritized. HPSA designation receives priority in technical scoring but is not a requirement. Practice sites may include primary care practices, specialty care practices, community clinics, governmental facilities, hospitals, private or group practices, long-term care facilities, hospice, academic centers/schools, school-based health centers, and correctional facilities. Eligible practice sites must be public, non-profit (501(c)(3) or (c)(4)), or for-profit entities in areas with health workforce shortage or public health need. For nurses/nursing support staff: eligible employers must be public or non-profit (501(c)(3) or (4)) OR for-profit in designated shortage areas.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Maternal Opioid Misuse (MOM) Case Management Services
structured_extraction.program_description: Enhanced case management services for pregnant individuals and new parents with opioid use disorder who are Medicaid participants. A case manager meets with participants at least monthly to develop a personalized, person-centered care plan and help connect them with prenatal care, medication-assisted treatment, postpartum checkups, mental and physical health services, overdose prevention education, and other health and social support services. Services are available during pregnancy and up to one year after birth. The program aims to improve maternal and infant health outcomes by addressing social determinants of health and coordinating care through the statewide health information exchange (CRISP). Services are provided through nine managed care organizations across Maryland. Care plans are shared with providers serving MOM participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free enhanced case management services provided by nine managed care organizations. A case manager meets with participants at least monthly to develop a personalized, person-centered care plan and connect them with medication-assisted treatment, prenatal and postpartum care, behavioral health services, mental and physical health services, overdose prevention education, and social support services. Services include screenings for depression and anxiety, social determinants of health assessment, goal-setting, and care coordination through the statewide health information exchange (CRISP).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant individuals and new parents with opioid use disorder who are covered by Maryland Medicaid
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management services to coordinate prenatal care, medication-assisted treatment, postpartum care, mental and physical health services, overdose prevention education, social support services, and connections to local resources. Services address social determinants of health and improve maternal and infant health outcomes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through nine managed care organizations to Maryland Medicaid members
requirements_list: Have health insurance through Maryland Medicaid
Be pregnant or postpartum
Use or have used opioids or be diagnosed with opioid use disorder
Diagnosed with opioid use disorder or history of opioid use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible individuals can enroll through the online enrollment portal at https://health.maryland.gov/EnrollMOM or by contacting their health care provider or health care plan for assistance. Referrals can also be made by health care providers and community partners. Enrollment is available at any time as this is an ongoing program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Statewide program providing free naloxone and overdose education through multiple service delivery models including fixed sites, vending machines, and mobile outreach. Services include naloxone distribution, overdose education, drug testing strips (fentanyl, xylazine, benzodiazepine, medetomidine), and comprehensive harm reduction services. The program authorizes government agencies and community-based organizations to provide overdose education and dispense naloxone, fentanyl test strips, and xylazine test strips to the community. Additional services vary by location but may include: HCV/HIV testing, housing assistance, medication for opioid use disorder, syringe services, wound care, food access, mental health services, and substance use disorder counseling/treatment. Free naloxone and overdose prevention supplies are distributed to residents in person at Overdose Response Programs throughout Maryland, with certain counties also offering naloxone delivery by mail to eligible residents' homes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Authorization and support for eligible agencies and organizations to provide overdose education and distribute naloxone, fentanyl test strips, xylazine test strips, and additional testing strips (benzodiazepine, medetomidine) to their communities. Free naloxone kits and overdose prevention supplies are distributed to residents in person at Overdose Response Programs throughout Maryland, with certain counties also offering naloxone delivery by mail to eligible residents' homes. Multiple access points available including fixed sites, 24/7 vending machines, on-site programs, off-site/referral services, and backpack outreach. Comprehensive harm reduction services also available including personal protective equipment, syringe services and disposal, wound care, HCV and HIV testing, medication for opioid use disorder access, substance use disorder counseling and treatment referrals, housing assistance referrals, food access resources, mental health services, safe storage devices, gun locks, medication disposal kits, telehealth services, and transportation assistance.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Department of Health Center for Harm Reduction Services
structured_extraction.program_audience: Government agencies, community-based organizations, people at risk of opioid overdose, people with substance use disorders, individuals experiencing homelessness, LGBTQ individuals, and Maryland residents seeking free naloxone and overdose prevention supplies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Naloxone kits, test strips (fentanyl, xylazine, benzodiazepine, medetomidine), overdose education supplies, harm reduction supplies, wound care materials, personal protective equipment, condoms, personal care kits, safe storage devices, gun locks, medication disposal kits, and overdose prevention materials for overdose prevention and response.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available through public Overdose Response Programs throughout Maryland with locations in multiple Maryland counties including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Interactive map and PDF list available on website. Certain Maryland counties offer mail delivery of naloxone to eligible residents.
requirements_list: No prescription required
No proof of certification or training required
Residents of certain Maryland counties eligible for mail delivery
Individuals at risk of opioid overdose eligible for services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For organizations: Contact the Office of Overdose Prevention & Education to apply for authorization. For residents: Find an Overdose Response Program near you using the interactive map or PDF list provided on the website. Visit the program in person to receive naloxone, test strips, and overdose education for free. Multiple access points available including fixed sites, vending machines (24/7 access at select locations), and mobile outreach. Alternatively, contact an Overdose Response Program to inquire about naloxone by mail delivery if you reside in an eligible county. No application required—walk-in services available.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides competitive grants for pediatric cancer research conducted by physicians, hospitals, laboratories, educational institutions, and other organizations and persons. The Maryland Pediatric Cancer Research Commission oversees the review, evaluation, and award of these grants according to criteria, standards, and procedures it develops.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants are awarded from the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Research Fund to support pediatric cancer research. The Commission oversees the review, evaluation, and award of these grants according to criteria, standards, procedures, and guidelines it develops. The specific grant amounts, terms, and mechanics are available through the Commission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Physicians, hospitals, laboratories, educational institutions, and other organizations and persons conducting pediatric cancer research.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pediatric cancer research.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide.
requirements_list: Applicants must be conducting pediatric cancer research
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications for pediatric cancer research grants are reviewed and evaluated by the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Research Commission according to criteria, standards, procedures, and guidelines established by the Commission. The Commission ensures each application is complete and satisfies the established requirements. Complete details about the application process are available through the Commission.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program connects humanitarian immigrants—including refugees, asylees, parolees, and victims of trafficking—with culturally and linguistically appropriate mental health services. It helps individuals process trauma, adjust to their new circumstances, and access support services after arriving in Maryland. The program serves approximately 2,000 humanitarian immigrants per year who have been welcomed to Maryland from around the world.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides mental health services and counseling that are culturally and linguistically appropriate for humanitarian immigrants, including refugees, asylees, parolees, and victims of trafficking, to help them process trauma and adjust to their new circumstances in Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Humanitarian immigrants, including refugees, asylees, parolees, and victims of trafficking who have been welcomed to Maryland. The program serves approximately 2,000 humanitarian immigrants per year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health counseling and support services to help with adjustment and trauma processing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. The program serves approximately 2,000 humanitarian immigrants per year who are welcomed to Maryland from around the world.
requirements_list: Must be a humanitarian immigrant, including a refugee, asylee, parolee, or victim of trafficking
Must have arrived in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Not specified on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides comprehensive primary, acute, and preventative health services including chronic condition management to students, families, and communities through clinics located on school campuses. The program aims to increase access to health services for students in underserved communities and improve both health and educational outcomes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides support for opening and operating school-based health centers on school campuses. Organizations receive technical assistance and support for establishing clinics that deliver comprehensive primary, acute, and preventative health services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications typically accepted in July and November
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations interested in opening new school-based health centers to serve students, families, and communities in underserved areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing and operating comprehensive primary, acute, and preventative health service clinics on school campuses, including chronic condition management services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program currently operates 91 active school-based health centers across 16 jurisdictions in Maryland. New centers can be established statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified organization type (non-profit, for-profit, higher education institution, or government)
Must have collaboration with local stakeholders
Must have an appropriate school campus building structure for the clinic
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in opening a new school-based health center should email md.sbhcprogram@maryland.gov for further information and tailored support. The process differs based on the type of organization applying, extent of collaboration with local stakeholders, and building structure of the desired site. Applications are typically accepted in July and November.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free, confidential tobacco cessation program available to all Maryland residents over 13 years old that helps people quit any form of tobacco. The program provides trained quit coaches, personalized quit plans, and support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week via phone, web, and text message in multiple languages including English and Spanish. Services include one-on-one coaching, coping strategies for managing cravings, free nicotine replacement therapy products (patches and gum while supplies last), and referrals to local resources for in-person cessation classes or counseling. Specialized intensive programs are available for youth ages 13-17, pregnant individuals, expectant parents, and those in recovery from substance use disorders. Pregnant and new parents can enroll in a specialized incentive program to receive gift cards for participation while supplies last. Non-smokers can call for information to help a family member, friend, or patient. Healthcare providers can become Fax to Assist providers to refer patients. Youth can also access the Live Vape Free program for help with quitting vaping.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free quit coaching services available by phone, web, and text message in English, Spanish, and other languages. Participants receive trained quit coaches who help develop personalized quit plans, manage cravings, and provide ongoing support and encouragement. Free nicotine patches and/or gum are provided while supplies last. Intensive multi-call programs are available for youth ages 13-17 and pregnant women. Services are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week with calls typically lasting 15-25 minutes. Pregnant participants can enroll in a specialized incentive program to receive gift cards for participation. The program also provides printed and web-based self-help materials and may refer participants to local resources like health departments for in-person cessation classes or counseling. Non-smokers can call for information to help a family member, friend, or patient. Healthcare providers can participate as Fax to Assist providers to make patient referrals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents over 13 years old who want to quit any form of tobacco, including youth ages 13-17, pregnant individuals, expectant parents, new parents, those in recovery from substance abuse, healthcare providers with patients ready to quit, and adults seeking cessation support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tobacco cessation support and services including one-on-one coaching, nicotine replacement therapy products, educational materials, medicine consultation support, incentive rewards for participation, and referrals to local cessation classes or counseling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be at least 13 years old
Must be a Maryland resident
Must be willing to participate in coaching sessions
Must be willing to work with trained coaches on tobacco addiction
Medicine options must be approved by the participant's doctor
Pregnant individuals interested in the incentive program must register during enrollment in the Maryland Tobacco Quitline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 1-800-QUIT-NOW (1-800-784-8669), visit the web portal at quitnow.net/maryland, or text READY to 34191 to enroll. Teens ages 13-17 can also enroll online in the Live Vape Free program by texting VAPEFREE to 873-373. Upon enrollment, receive free confidential one-on-one counseling from trained coaches, develop a personalized quit plan with a quit date, receive follow-up help and encouragement, access web and phone services, and receive a free supply of nicotine replacement therapy products. Pregnant participants can register for the specialized incentive program during enrollment to receive gift cards for participation. Healthcare providers can become Fax to Assist providers to refer patients or make referrals via email.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded entitlement program administered by the Maryland Department of Health and CDC that provides vaccines at no cost to children who might not otherwise be vaccinated due to inability to pay. The program supplies routine childhood vaccines recommended by ACIP and influenza vaccine during influenza season to enrolled physicians and healthcare providers for eligible children ages 18 and younger. Eligible beneficiaries include children who are Maryland Medicaid eligible, uninsured, Native American or Alaskan Native, or underinsured (have health insurance that does not cover immunization). The program removes cost as a barrier to vaccination and aims to increase vaccination rates and protect public health by ensuring all eligible children receive recommended vaccinations to prevent serious diseases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enrolled physicians and healthcare providers receive routine childhood vaccines recommended by ACIP and influenza vaccine during influenza season at no cost to administer to eligible children. Vaccines are shipped directly from McKesson Specialty distributor. The program covers vaccines for children who are Maryland Medicaid eligible, uninsured, underinsured (have health insurance that does not cover immunization), or Native American or Alaskan Native. Providers enrolled in the program receive free vaccines for eligible beneficiaries and place subsequent vaccine orders through the ImmuNet system on a bi-monthly basis. Once enrolled, providers receive updates on immunization issues.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children ages 18 and younger who are Maryland Medicaid recipients, uninsured, underinsured (no vaccine coverage), or American Indian or Alaskan Native, and medical practices/offices with enrolled physicians and responsible physicians holding Maryland State licenses who want to offer free vaccines to eligible children in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Routine childhood vaccines recommended by ACIP and influenza vaccine during influenza season for eligible children ages 18 and younger who are Maryland Medicaid eligible, uninsured, underinsured, or Native American or Alaskan Native to prevent vaccine-preventable diseases. Healthcare providers can use the vaccines to administer to qualifying patients.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Physician or healthcare provider must enroll by completing and returning the Vaccines for Children enrollment package
Medical practice or office with responsible physician holding Maryland State License
EHR/EMR system required for newly enrolled providers to submit vaccine administration data
Practice/office contact and backup contact must complete annual educational training
Continuous monitoring digital data logger (DDL) with valid calibration certificate required for each vaccine storage unit
At least one backup digital data logger (DDL) required
Stand-alone or pharmaceutical-grade vaccine storage units required
Vaccine administration data reporting to ImmuNet within seven days
Must offer all medically appropriate ACIP-recommended vaccines to VFC-eligible patients
Site review required before vaccine shipment begins
Practice or clinic must comply with federal law regarding vaccine documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Healthcare providers can enroll in the VFC program by submitting a letter of interest on business letterhead with specified information to mdh.izinfo@maryland.gov or by completing and returning the Vaccines for Children enrollment package. VFC staff will send enrollment documents via email. A site reviewer will contact the practice or clinic to provide necessary training on vaccine storage, handling, and federal compliance requirements. Upon approval, the provider places an initial vaccine order, and subsequent orders are placed through the ImmuNet system on a bi-monthly basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland's Mouths Matter Fluoride Varnish and Oral Health Screening Program for Kids
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides fluoride varnish application and oral health screening services for children in Maryland to promote dental health and prevent tooth decay through participating providers and community health settings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fluoride varnish application and oral health screening services provided to eligible children through participating providers and community health settings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dental fluoride varnish treatment and oral health screening services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all of Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A group-based prenatal and postpartum care program for pregnant women who are Maryland Medicaid members. Participants meet in groups of eight to ten people with the same due date for 90-minute to two-hour visits that include clinical exams with healthcare providers, education, and peer support. Topics covered include pregnancy side effects, labor and delivery, breastfeeding, baby care, stress management, and healthy nutrition. The program provides care, support, and learning in a group setting before and after birth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free group-based prenatal and postpartum care for eligible Maryland Medicaid members. Participants receive individual clinical exams with healthcare providers and group sessions of 90 minutes to two hours focusing on pregnancy education, labor preparation, postpartum support, and peer support. No cost to participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant women who are Maryland Medicaid members
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Group-based prenatal and postpartum care, including provider clinical exams, group education sessions, peer support, and health education on pregnancy, labor, delivery, breastfeeding, baby care, and stress management
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through Medicaid Managed Care Organizations
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Medicaid member
Must be pregnant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO), which is your Medicaid insurance plan. You can find the MCO phone number on your insurance card. The MCO will help you find a CenteringPregnancy provider near you and enroll.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides free doula or birth worker services to eligible Maryland Medicaid members. Doulas are trained professionals who offer physical, emotional, and informational support to pregnant people and birthing parents before, during, and after birth. Services include prenatal visits (typically in the birthing parent's home), attendance at birth, and postpartum visits. Prenatal and postpartum services cover topics such as labor anatomy, medical procedures, comfort measures, mental health, self-advocacy, breastfeeding, and community resources. During birth, doulas provide emotional and physical support including positioning assistance, communication help with medical teams, and breathing techniques.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free doula and birth worker services are provided at no cost to eligible Medicaid members. Services include prenatal visits (typically in the birthing parent's home), attendance during labor and birth, and postpartum visits. The doula provides emotional, physical, and informational support covering topics such as labor anatomy, medical procedures, comfort measures, mental health, self-advocacy, breastfeeding, and community resources. During birth, doulas provide emotional and physical support including positioning assistance, communication help with medical teams, and breathing techniques.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant Maryland Medicaid members or those who have been pregnant within the last 180 days.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Doula and birth worker services including prenatal visits, birth attendance, and postpartum support covering labor support, communication assistance, comfort measures, mental health support, breastfeeding guidance, and connection to community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland for all Medicaid members. Eligible individuals should contact their Medicaid HealthChoice Managed Care Organization (MCO) to access services.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland Medicaid member
Be pregnant or have been pregnant within the last 180 days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Medicaid HealthChoice Managed Care Organization (MCO), which is the healthcare organization that provides your Medicaid coverage. Your MCO will help connect you to a doula as soon as one is available and provide information about the services. You can also contact your health care provider for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: An income-based, limited benefits plan that provides free family planning services and birth control to eligible Maryland residents who do not qualify for full Medicaid coverage. The program offers no premiums, deductibles, or copays for covered services. Services include exams and birth control advice, prescription and over-the-counter birth control, IUDs, implants, emergency contraception, screening tests for sexually transmitted infections, hepatitis and HIV, cervical and breast cancer screening and diagnosis, and HPV vaccination. Tubal ligation and vasectomy services are also available through providers for applicants at least 21 years old. Eligible individuals receive a Medicaid Family Planning Program card to use with participating providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free family planning services and birth control with no premiums, deductibles, or copays. Services include exams and advice about birth control, prescription and over-the-counter birth control, IUDs, implants, emergency contraception, screening tests for sexually transmitted infections, hepatitis and HIV, cervical and breast cancer screening and diagnosis, and HPV vaccination. Tubal ligation and vasectomy services are available through providers for applicants at least 21 years old. Eligible individuals receive a Medicaid Family Planning Program card to use with participating providers. Does not cover prenatal care, infertility services, or non-emergency medical transportation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Apply any time
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-800-456-8900 (Pregnancy and Family Planning Helpline) or 1-855-642-8572 (Maryland Health Connection for eligibility and application questions)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents of all ages who are U.S. citizens or qualified non-citizens and meet the income limit for family planning, but are not eligible for full Medicaid or other Medicaid programs, do not have Medicare, and are not pregnant or sterilized.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Family planning services including exams and counseling, prescription and over-the-counter birth control, IUDs, implants, emergency contraception, screening tests for sexually transmitted infections, hepatitis and HIV, cervical and breast cancer screening and diagnosis, HPV vaccination, and tubal ligation or vasectomy services for those at least 21 years old. Does not cover prenatal care, infertility services, or non-emergency medical transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident
Be a U.S. citizen or a qualified non-citizen
Meet the income limit for Family Planning
Not have or be eligible for full Medicaid coverage or another Medicaid program
Not have Medicare
Not have had a tubal ligation or vasectomy
Not be pregnant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply at any time through Maryland Health Connection online or by phone. If eligible, coverage can start immediately. For questions about eligibility or your application, contact Maryland Health Connection at 1-855-642-8572 or call the Pregnancy and Family Planning Helpline at 1-800-456-8900.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that adds a child development specialist to your child's pediatric care team to provide resources, screenings, support, and services for healthy growth during the first three years of life. The program helps track child development, provides parenting resources, and connects families to needed community services like housing or transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including child development specialist support at pediatric care visits, developmental tracking, parenting resources, breastfeeding support, mental health and stress management guidance, and connection to community resources for eligible families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and families with children newborn to age 3 who are enrolled in Maryland Medicaid
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services include child development support, parenting guidance, breastfeeding support, mental health resources, and referrals to community services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide through participating Medicaid Managed Care Organizations
requirements_list: Child must be a Maryland Medicaid member
Child must be newborn to their 4th birthday
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO), which is your Medicaid insurance plan. You can find their number on your insurance card. The MCO will help you find a HealthySteps provider.

structured_extraction.program_description: A support program that provides home-based services and parenting skill education to pregnant people and families with young children. Specially trained professionals or nurses visit families in their home to teach about child development, parenting skills, self-care, community resources, nutrition, and mental health support. Services continue from pregnancy through the child's second or third birthday, depending on the program selected. Two evidence-based models are offered: Healthy Families America and Nurse Family Partnership.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free home visiting services provided by specially trained professionals or nurses. Services are delivered in the home and include education on child development, parenting skills, self-care, community resources, nutrition, and mental health support. Two evidence-based models are offered: Healthy Families America and Nurse Family Partnership. Services continue from pregnancy through the child's second or third birthday depending on the program selected.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant people and families with young children who are Maryland Medicaid members
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services focus on education and support including child development information, parenting skills training, self-care, community resource navigation, nutrition and diet education, future planning, and mental health and stress management support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide for all Maryland Medicaid members
requirements_list: Be a Maryland Medicaid member
Be pregnant or have delivered a child within three months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Managed Care Organization (MCO) to enroll in Home Visiting Services. Your health care provider can also help you find the right home visiting program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides non-emergency transportation to and from medically necessary covered services for Maryland Medicaid recipients who have no other means of transportation. Transportation is available to covered medical services and MD Healthy Smiles Dental providers for recipients with full Medicaid coverage.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-emergency transportation services provided to Medicaid recipients for medically necessary covered services and MD Healthy Smiles Dental providers for those with full Medicaid coverage. Recipients must have no other means of transportation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid recipients in Queen Anne's County who have no other means of transportation and have scheduled appointments for covered medical services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Non-emergency transportation to and from medically necessary covered services and MD Healthy Smiles Dental providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County residents only. For transportation services in other Maryland jurisdictions, contact the Local Jurisdictions Contact List.
requirements_list: Be a resident of Queen Anne's County
Be an active Medical Assistance (Medicaid) recipient with qualifying coverage
Have no other means of transportation
Have a scheduled appointment for a covered medical service
Complete screening questions to determine final eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 443-262-4462 to schedule transportation. Hours of operation are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. (except holidays). All applicants must complete screening questions to determine final eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A home and community-based services Medicaid waiver that helps individuals receive medical care and support in a community-based setting as an alternative to nursing facility care. Provides medical day care and related services for people who need nursing facility level of care, including skilled nursing, nursing assessments, medication monitoring, meals, social work services, activity programs, daily living skills training, transportation, therapy, personal care, and nutrition services. Services are delivered by licensed medical day care providers and are available at least four hours a day up to seven days a week.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Covers all Medicaid-covered services and benefits plus waiver services including medical day care at least four hours a day up to seven days a week, activity programs, meals, medication monitoring, nutrition services, skilled nursing and nursing assessments, social work services, therapy, personal care, daily living skills training, and transportation, delivered by licensed medical day care providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 16 or older who need nursing facility level of care and have full Medicaid coverage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical day care services, skilled nursing, nursing assessments, medication monitoring, meals, nutrition services, social work services, activity programs, daily living skills training, therapy, personal care, and transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local health departments and Maryland Access Point in all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Be age 16 or older
Need nursing facility level of care
Have a medical order for medical day care
Not be in another waiver program at the same time
The cost of community-based services must not be more than institutional care
Must already have full Medicaid with a red and white card
Must qualify for Medicaid in the community
Must require the level of care necessary to qualify for nursing facility services
Meet all medical, technical, and financial eligibility rules
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request a medical assessment to determine if you meet the level of care requirement by contacting your local health department, Maryland Access Point at 844-627-5465, or the Maryland Department of Health to inquire about eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: Help paying Medicare Part A (Hospital Insurance) and Part B (Medical Insurance) premiums. The program may also pay Part A and Part B deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments for eligible beneficiaries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program pays Medicare Part A and Part B premiums. For qualifying beneficiaries, it may also pay Part A and Part B deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments. Which program you qualify for depends on your income and asset levels.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicare beneficiaries with income and assets below the program limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of Medicare Part A and Part B premiums, deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Income and assets must be below program limits
Must be a Medicare beneficiary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person or by mail to your local department of social services. Download the application form from the Department of Human Services website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A chronic disease prevention and health promotion program that provides grant funding to organizations delivering community-based education, preventative programming, community engagement, partnerships, outreach, technical assistance, and ongoing intervention services. The program focuses on seven health areas: asthma, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, obesity, diabetes and prediabetes, pregnancy and birth outcomes, and mental health. The program addresses health disparities in vulnerable and minority communities through prevention, education, outreach, and strategic partnerships.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided to organizations for delivering community-based health education and health promotion interventions. Up to 18 awards ranging from $25,000 to $75,000 each for a one-year agreement (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027) with optional continuation funding into a second year contingent on satisfactory year one performance. Funding supports staffing, program activities, training, materials, and resources. Grantees are monitored through monthly reports, quarterly progress reports, and performance measures throughout the funding period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 11, 2026, at 5 p.m. local time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations (classified as tax-exempt under IRS section 501(c)(3)), local government agencies, state government agencies, public colleges, and state universities serving racial and ethnic minority populations and communities with chronic disease prevention and health disparities in asthma, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, obesity, diabetes/prediabetes, pregnancy and birth outcomes, and mental health.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports personnel (salary and fringe), consultants, travel, contractual services, supplies, operating costs, community-based health education and health promotion activities, program materials and resources, and partnership and collaboration activities. Funds cannot be used for tax items or advance startup funding. Equipment may be purchased but must comply with procurement standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - open to organizations throughout Maryland with all jurisdictions eligible, including Baltimore City. Applicants must maintain an operational office within the proposed jurisdiction and submit jurisdiction-specific applications. For border communities or rural multi-jurisdiction areas, exceptions apply.
requirements_list: Organizations must be 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations with IRS Determination Letter OR local/state government agencies OR public colleges OR state universities
Must be registered and in good standing with Maryland Comptroller
Must provide community-based health education and health promotion interventions
Must utilize community engagement and partnerships, including letters of commitment from at least two program partners
Must partner with Local Health Departments
Must participate in Local Health Improvement Council (LHIC)
Must collaborate with other MOTA grantees and community-based or faith-based organizations
Must attend all quarterly MHHD/MOTA partnership meetings
Must provide health education using evidence-based curricula
Must stratify data and track performance by race and ethnicity
Must comply with Americans with Disabilities Act accessibility requirements
Must submit monthly reports by the 10th of each month
Must submit quarterly progress reports by specified dates
Must submit itemized expenditure statement within 60 days of grant period close
Must complete Attachment E (Performance Measures Table) with annual targets
Must complete Attachment F (Monthly Performance Measures Table) for FY 2027
Must submit Work Plan Table (Attachment C) organized by performance measures
Must submit Gantt Chart (Attachment D) with one-year timeline
Must submit Budget Narrative and Budget Forms (Exhibits B and C)
Must submit signed W-9 form with contact person names and phone numbers
Must retain bills of sale and property acquisition evidence for 3 years
Must comply with Maryland State Finance and Procurement Article requirements
All funds must be obligated and spent by specified dates
Grantees selected for FY27 funding may be considered for continuation funding in FY28 based on year one performance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations apply through eMMA (Maryland's grants management system) at https://emma.maryland.gov/ using Solicitation ID BPM055355. The FY27 RFA deadline is March 11, 2026 at 5 p.m. local time. Applicants must submit Volume 1 (Project Narrative/Technical Proposal) with all required attachments including performance measures tables, work plan, budget, and letters of commitment from partners. A pre-application webinar was held in February with recording and slides available for reference. Questions should be submitted at least seven days prior to the deadline. Selected grantees receive awards and enter into one-year agreements with optional continuation funding contingent on satisfactory performance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that brings skilled healthcare professionals directly to the homes of eligible residents to assess health needs, help reach personal health goals, and connect people with community resources at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free home visits by skilled healthcare professionals who review medical history and medications, conduct basic physical assessments, check home safety, provide personalized health education, discuss health goals, and refer residents to local support and community resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults ages 18 and older who are residents of Queen Anne's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home health visits including medical history review, physical assessments, home safety checks, health education, and referrals to community resources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County only
requirements_list: Must be 18 years or older

structured_extraction.program_description: A performance-based incentive program for nursing facilities that evaluates facilities on staffing measures, resident satisfaction, MDS outcomes, staff immunization rates, and year-over-year improvement to determine awards. One percent of the Program's nursing facility Medicaid budget is awarded each year to eligible facilities. The highest-performing facilities receive 85 percent of the total award amount, while facilities demonstrating improvement from the previous year receive 15 percent. Awards are distributed based on performance across multiple quality indicators including staffing levels, staff stability, resident care quality measures, family satisfaction, and staff immunization rates. Facilities are ranked and categorized as P4P (Pay-For-Performance) or P4I (Pay-For-Improvement), with awards distributed as per diem rate increases or bonus payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating nursing facilities receive a share of one percent of the Program's annual nursing facility Medicaid budget based on performance scoring across four main domains: staffing measures (35 points), MHCC resident satisfaction survey (30 points), MDS outcomes (30 points), and staff immunization (5 points). The highest-scoring facilities receive 85 percent of total awards; facilities demonstrating year-over-year improvement receive 15 percent. Financial awards are calculated as $/MA Day multiplied by total MA Days and distributed based on facility performance scores on staffing levels, staff stability, minimum dataset quality indicators, family satisfaction surveys, and staff immunization rates.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicaid-participating nursing facilities with 45 or more beds that meet quality and compliance standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Performance incentive payments and improvement incentive payments tied to quality metrics including staffing levels, staff retention, resident satisfaction, MDS clinical outcomes, and staff immunization rates.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland nursing facilities participating in Medicaid and meeting eligibility criteria.
requirements_list: Have 45 or more beds
Are not continuing care retirement centers (CCRCs) or continuing care retirement communities (CCRC)
Have not been identified as a federally-designated special focus facility in the previous year ending March 31
Have not had a denial of payment for new admissions (DPNA) by CMS in the previous year ending March 31
Have not been determined to have provided substandard quality of care as defined in federal Medicaid regulations in the previous year ending March 31
Achieve minimum score threshold to receive award
Submit cost reports, wage survey data, and MDS data
Provide staff immunization rate documentation
Cannot receive both P4P and P4I awards simultaneously
Maintain minimum staffing hours based on acuity (35 points possible)
Demonstrate staff retention with >2 years tenure (15 points)
Achieve resident satisfaction survey performance standards (30 points)
Meet MDS clinical outcome measures (30 points)
Maintain staff immunization rates >90% minimum for points (preferred >95%)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nursing facilities participating in Medicaid are automatically evaluated based on performance data collected throughout the scoring period. Scoring is based on payroll records, MHCC resident satisfaction survey results, MDS submissions, staff immunization documentation, and facility staffing levels using an automated scoring system. Facilities do not submit separate applications; they are assessed using data already reported through required Medicaid reporting channels including cost reports, wage surveys, MDS submissions, MHCC surveys, and immunization data. Awards are distributed based on performance rankings.

structured_extraction.program_name: Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Program (OADPOP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program (formerly known as Syringe Services Program) that provides a wide range of services to help people who use drugs, including infectious disease prevention and overdose prevention. The Maryland Department of Health authorizes organizations as OADPOPs to provide needle and syringe distribution and collection, substance use disorder counseling, treatment and recovery services, case management, HIV and hepatitis C testing, overdose prevention education, naloxone distribution, fentanyl and xylazine testing strips, wound care, PrEP/PEP, reproductive health education and services, and on-site housing and emergency shelter access at select sites.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Health authorizes and supports organizations to operate as OADPOPs. The Office of Overdose Prevention & Education reviews new applications, manages program reporting, issues program guidance, and provides technical assistance and support to approved programs. Services provided by OADPOPs include distribution and collection of needles and syringes, substance use disorder counseling, treatment and recovery service referrals, case management, HIV and hepatitis C testing, PrEP/PEP, reproductive health education and services, wound care, overdose prevention education and naloxone distribution, fentanyl and xylazine testing strips, and on-site housing and emergency shelter access at select sites. Programs may be fixed-site, mobile, backpack model, or combinations thereof.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing - no specific deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations and local health departments, including non-profits and government entities, seeking approval to operate as an opioid-associated disease prevention and outreach program to serve people who use drugs in their communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorization to operate as a program providing infectious disease prevention, overdose prevention, needle and syringe distribution and collection, counseling, testing, treatment referrals, case management, HIV and hepatitis C testing, PrEP/PEP, reproductive health education and services, wound care, naloxone distribution, fentanyl and xylazine testing strips, and related harm reduction services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Currently 30 authorized OADPOPs operate in 21 counties. Programs may apply for authorization in any Maryland county or multicounty jurisdictions. Applicants must obtain approval from local health officer in each county where operations are proposed. Multi-jurisdictional programs require approval from all involved local health officers.
requirements_list: Submit application through web form with all required documentation
Read and comply with OADPOP Application Guidance
Meet requirements under MD Health-General §24-901 - 909
Comply with regulations under COMAR 10.52.01.01-10.52.01.09
Comply with 42 CFR Part 2 (confidentiality regulations)
Approved programs must provide or refer for core services including needle and syringe distribution, counseling, treatment and recovery services, case management, and HIV/hepatitis C testing
Provide program operating procedures for needle/syringe distribution, collection, and disposal including security and accounting measures
Submit community outreach and education plan including needle litter cleanups and law enforcement engagement
Submit referral protocols with consent and release of information policies
Specify program model with service delivery details (fixed site, mobile, backpack, etc.)
Establish data collection and evaluation procedures compliant with Maryland regulations and submit quarterly data
Have departmental approval and local health officer approval in proposed jurisdiction(s)
Staff must have expertise in working with injection drug users, opioid-associated disease prevention, and harm reduction strategies, and receive Department-approved training
Maintain participant confidentiality per Health-General Article §24-906(b) and 42 CFR Part 2
Issue identification cards to participants
Provide comprehensive security protocols including infection control, sharps container management, and needlestick injury procedures
Allow participants to obtain and return needles/syringes at any time during program operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations seeking approval must apply using the web form linked on the MDH website. Programs may appeal revocation of approval to Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services in writing within 30 calendar days of notice postmark date; Deputy Secretary must grant or deny appeal and respond in writing within 60 days with explanation. For more information, email mdh.syringeservices@maryland.gov.

Funds support initiatives approved in the recipient state's application. Minor renovations or alterations directly linked to program goals are permitted up to 20% of total funding per budget period. Administrative costs are capped at 10% of total award. Funds cannot be used for new construction, major building expansions, pre-award costs, or to supplant existing federal, state, or local funding.

Permitted uses include minor renovations and alterations directly linked to program goals (up to 20% cap). Prohibited uses include pre-award costs, new construction, building expansion, significant retrofitting, cosmetic upgrades, supplanting existing funding, lobbying, and clinician salaries. All costs must be itemized, justified, and linked to program goals.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: States submit applications through Grants.gov with required SF-424A budget forms and narrative descriptions. Annual non-competing continuation (NCC) applications are used to update budgets and make minor changes for subsequent budget periods. Awardees must coordinate with assigned CMS Project Officers regarding changes. Change requests are evaluated on a case-by-case basis at CMS's sole discretion. Final OMB-approved reporting templates must be used for all submissions. Application details are announced periodically, and applicants should check the RHTP procurement page for updates.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Health that funds local health departments and community-based organizations to provide comprehensive women's health services and reduce infant mortality. The program supports 29 grantee organizations providing initiatives such as reproductive health care, prenatal and postnatal care, family planning, care coordination, patient navigation, health education, home visiting programs, screening and treatment for STIs, HIV, and substance use disorders, behavioral health services, smoking cessation services, and support for vulnerable populations including pregnant women, postpartum women, women with substance use disorders, low-income women, women of color, and underserved communities. Services include prenatal care, family planning services, care coordination, patient navigation, health education, home visiting, screening and treatment for STIs, HIV, and substance use disorders, behavioral health services, smoking cessation services, and linkages to social services such as health insurance enrollment, WIC, childcare resources, and job training.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds support staff salaries, operational and administrative costs, clinical services, care coordination services, patient navigation, prenatal and postnatal care, family planning services, home visiting programs, health education, screening and treatment for STIs, HIV, and substance use disorders, behavioral health services, smoking cessation services, linkages to health insurance enrollment, WIC, childcare resources, job training, and other social services for pregnant women and women of reproductive age.

structured_extraction.program_name: Promoting Food Security, Reducing Obesity, and Addressing Diabetes
structured_extraction.program_description: A collection of 45 grants supporting programs that address food security, obesity prevention, and diabetes management for vulnerable and underserved populations across Maryland. Programs expand access to care, screenings, and comprehensive interventions including community health worker services, diabetes self-management education, lifestyle interventions, medically-tailored meals, food pantry expansion, mobile health clinics, health screenings, care coordination, and wraparound services. Focus is on reducing health disparities among racial and ethnic minorities, low-income residents, and other underserved communities disproportionately impacted by diabetes and obesity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $25,000 to $1,600,000 provided to qualified grantee organizations including nonprofits, government agencies, healthcare institutions, and health care organizations to support programs addressing diabetes prevention, obesity reduction, and food security. Grants fund staff salaries including community health workers, certified diabetes educators, nurses, and care coordinators; medical equipment for home monitoring; diabetes education and prevention programs; medically-tailored meal delivery; food pantry expansion and mobile farmer's markets; health screenings and testing; case management and care coordination services; nutrition education and cooking classes; mobile health clinics and telehealth services; peer support groups; electronic health dashboard systems; community outreach and health education; and addressing social determinants of health including food insecurity, transportation barriers, and housing instability.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hiring community health workers, certified diabetes educators, nurses, and care coordinators; providing diabetes self-management education and prevention programs; delivering medically-tailored meals; funding mobile clinics and health screenings; supporting food pantries, mobile farmer's markets, and nutrition programs; purchasing home monitoring equipment and electronic health dashboard systems; conducting community outreach and health education; implementing evidence-based interventions; case management and care coordination services; nutrition education and cooking classes; telehealth services; peer support groups; and addressing social determinants of health including food security and transportation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Providing Dental Care for Low-income Children and Adults
structured_extraction.program_description: A grants program funded by the Maryland Department of Health that awards grants to various grantee organizations across Maryland to expand access to dental services for low-income, uninsured, and underinsured residents. The program supports the launch of new dental clinics, expansion of existing dental programs, and partnerships to address dental health professional shortages in underserved areas. Grants support opening new dental clinics, expanding existing dental programs, hiring dental staff, providing dental screenings and preventive care, offering subsidized or free dental services, and reducing dental-related emergency department visits. The program has awarded 51 grants to organizations serving vulnerable populations including children, adults, seniors, homeless individuals, and those with substance use disorders or mental illness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $10,000 to $745,000 support dental program operations, staff salaries, equipment purchases, dental supplies, patient transportation assistance, health insurance enrollment support, care coordination, and subsidized or free dental services for eligible low-income populations. Grants have varied terms, with most being 2-3 year awards. Some grants provide matching funds or seed money to establish new dental clinics or expand existing programs. Funding can be used to hire dentists, dental hygienists, dental assistants, community health workers, and support staff; purchase dental equipment and supplies; provide oral health education; conduct dental screenings; offer preventive services like fluoride and sealants; provide restorative and emergency dental care; cover facility costs; support patient transportation; and integrate dental services with primary and behavioral health care.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, uninsured, and underinsured children and adults in Maryland, including vulnerable populations such as homeless individuals, those in recovery from substance use disorders, individuals with mental illness, pregnant women, seniors, disabled adults, individuals on Medicaid or Medicare, individuals with chronic diseases, and Latino/Hispanic and other underserved racial and ethnic populations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support expansion and operation of dental care services including: opening new dental clinics; expanding capacity of existing dental programs; hiring dentists, dental hygienists, dental assistants, case managers, community health workers, and support staff; purchasing dental equipment and supplies; providing dental screenings, preventive care (fluoride, sealants), and restorative care; offering oral health education; providing patient transportation to appointments; covering medication costs; supporting enrollment in health insurance; care coordination and outreach; integration of dental services with primary and behavioral health care; facility costs; and providing subsidized or free dental services to low-income residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties and Baltimore City are eligible. Individual grantees serve specific jurisdictions including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, suburban Maryland (Prince George's County), Garrett County, Harford County, Allegany County, Washington County, Cecil County, Anne Arundel County, Charles County, St. Mary's County, Caroline County, Kent County, Howard County, Frederick County, Carroll County, Montgomery County, Wicomico County, Calvert County, and Southern Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: An internship program that introduces undergraduate juniors and seniors, graduate students, and recent graduates to public health careers and exposes them to different subject areas within the Maryland Department of Health. Students gain practical experience in areas including behavioral science, biostatistics, community health, epidemiology, health education, health informatics, health policy, healthcare administration, infectious disease, preparedness and response, public health accreditation, and public health communications to enhance their academic knowledge and prepare them for entry into the public health workforce. Specific internship positions include epidemiology roles focused on viral hepatitis data management and analysis, health education positions in nutrition and public health, health informatics roles in data modernization, health policy positions in research and strategic planning, healthcare administration opportunities, and infectious disease positions in surveillance and outbreak response.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid internship positions offering resume experience and practical training in public health. Undergraduate students are paid $17.15 per hour; graduate students are paid $20.15 per hour. The Summer 2026 cohort runs from June 3 to August 11, 2026. Specific internship roles include epidemiology positions working with data management and analysis (SAS, Tableau) for viral hepatitis surveillance and epidemiological profile development; health education positions in nutrition departments and public health functions (meal preparation, health education); health informatics roles in data modernization initiatives; health policy positions in research, policy analysis, and strategic planning; healthcare administration roles in program management, Medicaid compliance, healthcare licensing, fraud investigation, and accounting; and infectious disease positions in zoonotic/vector-borne disease surveillance and hepatitis case investigations. Hands-on training and experience in a public health environment for undergraduate juniors and seniors, graduate students, recent college graduates, and recent graduates with advanced degrees. Positions located across Maryland, including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll County, and Prince George's County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Queen Anne's County No-Cost Colorectal Cancer Screening Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Queen Anne's County Health Department, administered by the Maryland Department of Health, provides no-cost colorectal cancer screenings and patient navigation services to help low-income, uninsured, and underinsured residents get screened for colorectal cancer. The program helps detect colorectal cancer early and prevent the disease by finding and removing precancerous growths before they turn into cancer through screening methods including colonoscopy, stool-based tests (FIT/FOBT), and flexible sigmoidoscopy. Services are available to eligible residents age 45 and older, or younger individuals with increased risk factors such as family history of colorectal polyps or cancer.
