structured_extraction.program_name: Rare and Expensive Case Management (REM) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The REM program is a Maryland Medicaid program providing medical case management services and related medical services as an alternative to HealthChoice Managed Care Organization (MCO) for recipients with specified rare and expensive conditions. It is a voluntary program that helps case managers develop care plans, coordinate services, provide education and support, and help members access needed services. Case managers conduct needs assessments, develop individualized care plans, assist with service applications, monitor and adjust care plans as needed, and provide ongoing education and information.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides comprehensive case management services on a fee-for-service basis managed by registered nurses or licensed social workers, including needs assessment, care plan development, service coordination, home visits, patient education, family support, treatment plan development, and provider service coordination. Additional services include Certified Nursing Assistant services, Certified Medication Technician services, chiropractic services, Home Health Aide services, nutrition counseling and supplements, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, private duty nursing and shift nursing services. All standard Medicaid covered services and benefits are included. Services must be medically necessary and ordered by a health care provider.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicaid recipients eligible for HealthChoice managed care program who have at least one rare and expensive condition for their age group and choose to participate in or enroll in the REM program. Individuals must have a diagnosed condition on the REM Disease List with an approved ICD-10 code and meet age limits that vary by condition.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management services including service coordination, home visits, needs assessment, patient education, family support, treatment plan development, and provider service coordination. Additional covered services include Certified Nursing Assistant and Certified Medication Technician services, chiropractic services, home health aide services, nutrition counseling and supplements, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, and private duty or shift nursing services. All services must be medically necessary and ordered by a health care provider.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide for individuals eligible for HealthChoice managed care program across all Maryland counties.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals can be made by the Managed Care Organization, the recipient's doctor, any concerned person, or recipients can self-refer either at the time of diagnosis or later. A licensed health care provider must complete the REM Intake and Referral Form with all requested information, sign it, and date it. The completed form must be submitted with supporting clinical documentation via fax to 410-333-5426 or by email to mdh.remreferralfax@maryland.gov. The REM Intake Unit reviews the submission for completeness and clinical eligibility. A determination of approval or denial is issued. Upon approval, an REM case manager will be assigned to help develop a care plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: This is an umbrella program category that funds multiple community health initiatives across Maryland designed to reduce preventable emergency department visits and promote access to care in community settings. Specific grantees implement projects addressing chronic disease management, behavioral health, cultural and linguistic barriers, and mobile health services. One funded project targets individuals with chronic disease conditions who frequently utilize emergency departments in Baltimore City and promotes access to primary and preventative care services in the community. Grant funds support emergency department diversion teams, help residents enroll in public health care coverage, and provide health care system navigation support. Funded projects have included the Better Access to Care Program at the University of Maryland Department of Family Medicine, which reduced hospital emergency department visits using the Chronic Care Model for patients with diabetes, depression, and asthma. Grant funds are also used to support emergency department diversion teams deployed in hospitals in Baltimore City such as Sinai and Northwest Hospitals.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program supporting state-led rural health transformation initiatives through five-year cooperative agreements with CMS. The program funds comprehensive initiatives addressing rural health challenges including service expansion, health information technology advances, behavioral health expansion, innovative care delivery models, clinical workforce recruitment and retention, and policy changes to support rural healthcare transformation. Total funding: $50 billion over 5 fiscal years (FY 2026-FY 2030).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cooperative agreement funding from CMS providing up to $50 billion over five fiscal years (FY 2026-FY 2031) to support rural health transformation initiatives. States receive baseline funding plus workload-based allocations. Funds support: clinical workforce recruitment and retention with 5-year rural service commitments; workforce development and training programs including residency and GME expansion; rural healthcare infrastructure improvements and equipment; telehealth and technology solutions; policy implementation and regulatory changes; innovative care delivery models; chronic disease prevention and management; provider payments tied to outcomes (limited to 15% of total); minor renovations and alterations (limited to 20% per budget period); administrative costs (limited to 10%); subawards and contracts. Prohibited uses include: new construction, major building expansions, pre-award costs, lobbying, broadband infrastructure, replacement of currently billable services, clinician salaries with non-compete clauses, perpetual operating expenses, international visa sponsorship, and program duplication. States must invest in at least three permissible use categories. Rural Tech Catalyst Fund available for consumer-facing technology solutions (up to $20 million or 10% of state allocation, whichever is less).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 5, 2025, no later than 11:59 p.m. ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: State government agencies, rural healthcare providers and facilities, rural communities and residents, clinical workforce in rural areas, healthcare systems, hospitals, clinics, community mental health centers, Tribal Nations and Indian health organizations, rural populations and Medicaid beneficiaries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Clinical workforce recruitment and retention with minimum 5-year rural service commitments; workforce development, training and certification programs; residency program expansion; graduate medical education expansion for new populations; financial recruitment and retention incentives (relocation expenses, travel subsidies, childcare subsidies); rural healthcare service expansion and infrastructure improvements; equipment purchases including medical equipment and mobile clinics; health information technology implementation and upgrades; telehealth infrastructure and digital health solutions; innovative care delivery models and alternative payment models; substance use disorder and mental health services expansion; chronic disease prevention and management; provider payments tied to outcomes; policy implementation and legislative/regulatory actions; state personnel for program administration; minor renovations and alterations; subawards and contracts with partners; equipment for Critical Access Hospitals; Rural Tech Catalyst Fund for technology solutions. Cannot be used for: new construction, pre-award costs, lobbying, broadband infrastructure, clinician salaries with non-compete restrictions, replacement of currently billable services, international visa sponsorship, perpetual ongoing operating expenses, program duplication, major building expansions, endowments or investment funds, student loan repayment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all 50 U.S. states. Within Maryland, available to the state's 18 recognized rural counties: Allegany, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. Funds must benefit populations identified as rural by the state in its approved application. Clinicians must practice within the same state receiving funding. States must rank at or above the 90th percentile for land area metric to receive scoring points for that data-driven factor. Funds should benefit rural residents of the state; collaboration between rural and non-rural areas permitted (e.g., specialists in non-rural areas providing telehealth to rural areas).

structured_extraction.program_name: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal nutrition assistance program that provides supplemental foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and health referrals to eligible pregnant women, postpartum women, breastfeeding women, infants, and children up to age 5 who meet income and nutritional need requirements. WIC provides supplemental healthy foods through an electronic WIC benefits card (eWIC) or vouchers to purchase healthy foods including fruits, vegetables, whole grains, dairy, eggs, protein-rich foods, legumes, peanut butter, infant formula, and baby foods at authorized retail locations and farmers' markets. The program also offers nutrition education, counseling, breastfeeding support services, and referrals to other programs and health services to help participants develop healthy eating habits and receive proper nutrition. A Maryland WIC mobile app is available for participants on iOS and Android platforms, enabling them to locate authorized retail stores and WIC clinics, manage their WIC card with a personal identification number, check benefit balance, upload required documentation, and use a UPC barcode scanner to verify authorized WIC foods. The program helps ensure healthy pregnancies, improved birth outcomes, and better nutrition for vulnerable populations. Participants must live in Maryland, meet income guidelines (at or below 185 percent of the federal poverty line), and demonstrate a nutritional need. The program is available to individuals regardless of employment status, housing situation, or family structure.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides electronic WIC benefits (eWIC card) and food vouchers that can be used to purchase approved nutritious foods including fruits, vegetables, whole grains, legumes, dairy, eggs, peanut butter, protein-rich foods, infant formula, and baby foods at authorized retail locations and farmers' markets. Participants receive a WIC card with a personal identification number to access their food benefits. Participants also receive nutrition education, counseling, and breastfeeding support services, as well as referrals to health and social services. Specific benefit amounts and food packages are determined based on individual nutritional needs. Benefits are available through local county agencies and designated clinics statewide. Participants must live in Maryland, meet income guidelines (at or below 185 percent of the federal poverty line), and have a documented nutritional need.

structured_extraction.program_name: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC)
structured_extraction.program_description: WIC is a federal nutrition assistance program that provides supplemental healthy foods, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and referrals to other assistance programs for low-income pregnant women, nursing mothers, breastfeeding women, fathers, caregivers, and children under five years old. Participants receive food benefits via an electronic WIC card with a personal identification number to purchase authorized nutritious foods including fruits, vegetables, legumes, whole grains, dairy products, eggs, peanut butter, infant formula, and baby foods at authorized retail locations and farmers' markets. The program serves pregnant women, new mothers (up to six months after delivery), breastfeeding mothers (up to one year after delivery), infants, and children under age five who meet income guidelines (at or below 185 percent of the federal poverty line) and have nutritional needs. Services include nutrition education, breastfeeding support, health screenings including growth and weight assessments, and referrals to other assistance programs delivered through local county WIC agencies to support healthy development and proper nutrition, ensuring healthy pregnancies, improved birth outcomes, and better nutrition for vulnerable populations. A Maryland WIC mobile app is available for participants on iOS and Android platforms, enabling them to locate authorized retail stores and WIC clinics, manage their WIC card with a personal identification number, check benefit balance, upload required documentation, and use a UPC barcode scanner to verify authorized WIC foods.

Participants also receive breastfeeding support from lactation specialists, nutrition education and counseling, health screenings including growth and weight assessments, referrals to other health and social agencies, and participation in the annual WIC Farmers' Market Program. Services are delivered through local county WIC agencies to eligible pregnant women, new mothers (up to six months after delivery), breastfeeding mothers (up to one year after delivery), infants, and children under age five who meet income guidelines (at or below 185 percent of the federal poverty line) and nutritional risk criteria. The program is available statewide throughout Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: Expedited licensing and certification process for service members, veterans, military spouses, and surviving spouses in health occupations and other regulated professions in Maryland. This law helps active military personnel, veterans, and their spouses obtain professional licenses and certifications in Maryland more quickly if they already hold a valid license in good standing in another state. The program requires licensing units and boards to give credit for relevant military training, education, and experience, allows expedited temporary licenses, and requires the State Superintendent to expedite educator certification and the Maryland Higher Education Commission to develop guidelines for awarding academic credit for military training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides expedited licensing and certification for qualified individuals. Temporary licenses are valid up to 6 months or until permanent license decision. Expedited processing occurs within 15 business days for completed applications. An assigned board advisor assists applicants through the application process. The program helps identify education and training programs for unmet requirements. Credit is given for relevant military training, education, and experience toward years of practice requirements and training/education requirements if substantially equivalent. Penalties and fees are waived for deployed military members renewing licenses late. The program facilitates the expedited licensure, certification, and registration process for those who already hold valid professional licenses in other states. Temporary educator certificates are available for limited periods, and guidelines are developed for awarding academic credit for military training.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Veterans must apply within one year of discharge or separation; current service members may apply when assigned to a Maryland duty station; military spouses may apply when spouse is assigned to a Maryland duty station; surviving spouses must apply within one year of the service member's death or the veteran's discharge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Service members (active duty U.S. Armed Forces, Reserve components, National Guard), veterans (discharged within 1 year under honorable or non-dishonorable circumstances), and military spouses (including surviving spouses of veterans or service members who died within 1 year of application) who hold valid professional licenses, certificates, or registrations in other states and are seeking licensure in health occupations and other regulated professions in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program itself does not provide direct funding but facilitates the expedited licensure, certification, and registration process for eligible individuals, including assignment of board advisors, temporary licensing options, and credit for military training and experience. Professional licensure, certification, and registration fees apply.

Military spouses' spouse must be assigned to a duty station in Maryland or have established legal residence in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A USDA-funded nutrition grant program providing annual benefits to eligible WIC participants and low-resource senior participants to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables at authorized farmers' markets and farm stands. WIC recipients receive approximately $30.00 annually and senior participants receive $35.00 annually. Benefits are distributed during summer months (June through November) and can be redeemed through November 30th each year. The program operates statewide across Maryland, with over 100 farmers' markets participating. Benefits are distributed through WIC clinics for WIC participants, through the Healthy Together app for seniors, and through local Area Agencies on Aging. Authorized farmers and farm stands must use the Healthy Together app to process transactions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides monthly fruit and vegetable benefits to eligible WIC participants including children, pregnant women, and breastfeeding mothers. Benefits can be redeemed at WIC-authorized vendors including grocery stores, farm stands, and farmers' markets who accept eWIC benefits. Benefit amounts vary by participant type: children receive $26, pregnant women $47, and breastfeeding mothers $52 per month. The program also authorizes farmers to become WIC vendors to accept Farmers' Market Nutrition Program (FMNP) benefits and WIC Fruit and Vegetable Benefits from WIC participants. Farmers and authorized retailers can process electronic WIC fruit and vegetable benefits using the free S3 Merchant Link app (mobile app system for smartphones/tablets) with no set-up fees, transactional fees, cancellation fees, or additional equipment required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Wound Care and Comprehensive Care for People Who Use Drugs Training
structured_extraction.program_description: Free training program providing in-person or virtual wound care education for clinical staff and basic first aid and medical training for non-clinical staff working with people who use drugs. Includes materials on xylazine-associated wound care and comprehensive care approaches for healthcare providers and service providers delivering care to people who use drugs. Clinical staff receive specialized wound care training covering proper wound assessment, cleaning, dressing application and securement, infection prevention, and related care. Non-clinical staff access basic first aid and medical training. Training resources, videos, and reference materials are provided to support comprehensive care for people who use drugs with focus on wound care related to drug use complications. Also includes medical education and empowerment directly to people experiencing homelessness and support workers, focusing on infections, wounds, and other skin conditions including trenchfoot, eczema, hives, impetigo, frostbite, burns, skin ulcers, bites, lice, and scabies. Comprehensive instructional material covers wound care management, infection identification and treatment, prevention strategies, when to seek medical help, and coverage of topics including antibiotics, abscesses, cellulitis, severe infections, sepsis, endocarditis, necrotizing fasciitis, bone and joint infections, and foot conditions. Additionally includes resource toolkit for healthcare providers covering stimulant use, health risks, treatment options, harm reduction strategies, and clinical management of stimulant use disorder.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person or virtual wound care training for clinical staff covering proper wound assessment, cleaning, dressing application and securement, infection prevention, and related care including xylazine-associated wound care. Basic first aid and medical training available for non-clinical staff. Comprehensive care materials, technical assistance, training resources, videos, and reference materials included. Access to educational videos in English and Spanish, handouts, and training materials from partner organizations. Comprehensive instructional material on wound care management, infection identification and treatment, prevention strategies, when to seek medical help, and coverage of topics including antibiotics, abscesses, cellulitis, severe infections, sepsis, endocarditis, necrotizing fasciitis, bone and joint infections, and foot conditions. Also covers skin conditions including trenchfoot, eczema, hives, impetigo, frostbite, burns, skin ulcers, bites, lice, and scabies. Technical Assistance available through Opioid Response Network (ORN) for healthcare and service providers offering wound care and comprehensive care. Resource toolkit for healthcare providers covering stimulant use, health risks, treatment options, harm reduction strategies, and clinical management of stimulant use disorder with information on stimulant types, cardiovascular/pulmonary/oral/dermal health risks, screening and diagnostic tools, pharmacotherapeutic and non-pharmacotherapeutic treatment options, and overamping management and prevention.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Clinical and non-clinical staff at healthcare organizations, healthcare facilities, harm reduction organizations, and community-based organizations serving people who use drugs. Includes healthcare providers, harm reduction workers, and outreach workers. Also targets people who use drugs, people experiencing homelessness, support workers, street medicine groups, community health workers, first responders, and overdose responders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wound care training and technical assistance in comprehensive care for people who use drugs, including first aid and medical training materials, wound care management, xylazine-associated wound treatment, and educational resources. Covers wound assessment, management, and treatment with specialized training on xylazine-associated wounds. Educational materials and resources on wound management and comprehensive care. Educational and training resources for clinical practice including stimulant use screening, diagnosis, treatment options, and harm reduction strategies. Training related to basic supplies for wound care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Training available in-person or virtually across the state. Nationally applicable materials available (xylazine emerging nationally). Spanish-language materials available.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Options (CO) Waiver / Home and Community-Based Options Waiver and Community First Choice Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid waiver program providing services to older adults and individuals with physical disabilities who require nursing home level of care, enabling them to live at home instead of in a nursing facility. Services include assisted living, behavior consultation, case management, dietitian and nutritionist services, medical day care, Senior Center Plus, personal assistance, supports planning, nurse monitoring, personal emergency response systems, environmental assessments, accessibility adaptations, assistive devices, home delivered meals, family and consumer training, transitional cost assistance, and all other standard Medicaid services including Community First Choice. For applicants receiving Long Term Care Medicaid in a nursing home, the program provides assistance to develop a plan to safely transition to the community. The program allows Medicaid to cover services typically only available in nursing homes when provided in participants' own homes or assisted living facilities.

All standard Medicaid services including Community First Choice are covered. Services are provided based on assessed need. For applicants transitioning from nursing homes, assistance is provided to develop a plan to safely move to the community. The State pays for covered services through Medicaid to enable eligible clients to remain in the community rather than move to a nursing facility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program undertaken by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development in partnership with the Maryland Department of Aging that provides zero percent interest loans and grants to help seniors and low and moderate-income homeowners make accessibility improvements and essential home repairs to their homes. Improvements may include installation of grab bars and railings, widening of doorways, installation of ramps, wheelchair ramps, accessible showers, lever handles, first floor bathrooms, laundry rooms, energy conservation, plumbing, wells, sewer, and lead hazard reduction to enable seniors to remain independent in their homes and age in place. Senior homeowners age 55 and older receive zero percent interest loans with payments deferred for 30 years. Loans can be extended beyond the 30-year term if the homeowner is unable to repay and still occupies the home. The loan becomes payable when the house is sold or transferred, unless transferred to a family member who continues to occupy it as their primary residence, or if a spouse continues to reside there after the original borrower's death. Refinancing with cash-out triggers full repayment, but rate adjustments without cash-out do not. Payments may be structured as a lump sum at the end of the deferral period or as monthly payments at the homeowner's request. Grants up to $25,000 are available for applicants who do not qualify for loan funding.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent to 6 percent interest deferred loans for up to 30 years for senior homeowners ages 55 and older with payments deferred for 30 years. Interest rates range from 0% to 6.0% depending on household income level. Loans can be extended beyond the 30-year term if the homeowner is unable to repay and still occupies the home. The average loan amount is anticipated to be $10,000 to $15,000, with a maximum loan amount of 110 percent of the property value or up to 85 percent of the value of the property depending on program specifics. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a lien or mortgage on the property. All closing costs are included in the loan. The loan becomes payable when the house is sold or transferred, unless transferred to a family member who continues to occupy it as their primary residence, or if a spouse continues to reside there after the original borrower's death. Refinancing with cash-out triggers full repayment, but rate adjustments without cash-out do not. Payments may be structured as a lump sum at the end of the deferral period or as monthly payments at the homeowner's request. Borrowers with no repayment capability may be eligible for deferred principal and interest. Grants up to $25,000 are available for applicants who do not qualify for loan funding. Upon the original borrower's death, the loan may be deferred if the new owner occupies the home as their principal residence, though the interest rate could increase if income exceeds certain limits. The homeowner hires and pays contractors; DHCD or local government housing network inspectors authorize payments after work inspection. A two-party check made to both homeowner and contractor is sent to the homeowner, who signs and delivers it to the contractor.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 55 or older who own and occupy their home as their principal residence and need accessibility modifications to remain independent, as well as low and moderate-income homeowners and small rental property owners seeking home improvements to remain in their primary residence and age in place. Households at 80%, 60%, 50%, and 30% of Area Median Income (AMI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility improvements such as installation of grab bars and railings, widening doorways, installation of ramps, wheelchair ramps, accessible showers, lever handles, first floor bathrooms, laundry rooms, adding bedrooms and bathrooms on the main level, energy conservation, plumbing, wells, sewer, and lead hazard reduction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide with different income limits applying to Washington, DC PMSA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's Counties) versus the Rest of State. Applications are available at local County Housing Offices, Maryland Access Point Agencies, or through all 19 local Area Offices on Aging in Maryland. Baltimore County residents may also contact Senior Information and Assistance at 410-887-2594. Applications can be taken in the homeowner's home if necessary.

The program provides capital and operating funding to support housing, community, and economic development projects in Baltimore and surrounding neighborhoods based on regional strategic plans. The program focuses on areas where modest investment and coordinated strategy will have significant neighborhood revitalization impact.

structured_extraction.program_description: The BeSMART Home Energy Loan Program provides unsecured financing to help Maryland homeowners improve the energy efficiency and comfort of their homes by replacing and upgrading appliances, heating and cooling systems, and making whole house envelope improvements to save on utility bills. The program offers flexible loan terms with financing for energy efficiency measures including insulation, air sealing, ENERGY STAR equipment, windows and doors, lighting controls, programmable thermostats, geothermal and other heat pump systems, solar photovoltaic installation, and other improvements identified in certified energy audits. Licensed and insured contractors can participate by providing services to borrowers who are financing their projects through this program. Homeowners can select weatherization and energy efficiency professionals from a list of eligible providers whose qualifications have been reviewed by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unsecured loan offering flexible terms (less than 10 years available) with 6.99% APR and up to $30,000 in financing for energy efficiency measures. Minimum loan amount is $5,000. Uses a 2-party check system with 30% down payment at loan closing and 70% of remaining funds distributed upon project completion. Financing for solar photovoltaic installation is capped at 50% of total loan. Up to 25% of the cost of energy measures can be used for mold remediation, radon mitigation, and health and safety improvements necessary for the energy improvements. No prepayment penalties apply; early payoff avoids interest. Licensed and insured contractors provide the services and are paid through the program.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement and upgrading of appliances, heating, cooling and ventilation systems including heat pump systems, and whole house envelope improvements including insulation and air sealing, ENERGY STAR heating and cooling systems, ENERGY STAR hot water heating equipment, ENERGY STAR appliances (excluding stoves, ovens, and microwaves), windows and doors, lighting and controls, programmable and smart thermostats, ceiling fans and ventilation fans, geothermal heat pumps, solar photovoltaic installation (up to 50% of total loan), mold remediation and radon mitigation (up to 25% of total loan), and other improvements identified in certified energy audit. Cannot finance completed work or refinance completed energy improvements. Not eligible: stoves, ovens, microwave ovens, kitchen/bath remodeling, roof replacement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal funding program administered by the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA), U.S. Department of Commerce, to expand high-speed internet access by supporting broadband infrastructure deployment to unserved and underserved locations. The program aims to deploy broadband service to approximately 9,000 locations and 1,300 community anchor institutions in Maryland, focusing on the "last mile of the last mile." Service delivery methods include fiber-to-the-home (FTTH), hybrid-fiber coax (HFC/cable), low-earth orbit satellite, and fixed wireless. Maryland's State Plan establishes commitments and strategy to support broadband projects over the next five years to close the digital divide.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland was awarded $267,738,400.71 by the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) for the BEAD program. Subgrantees receive fixed amount subawards based on achievement of specific construction milestones for broadband infrastructure deployment and adoption projects. Funding supports fiber, hybrid-fiber coax, low-earth orbit satellite, and fixed wireless infrastructure deployment to unserved and underserved locations, as well as Community Anchor Institution (CAI) connectivity projects. Approximately 40% of projects utilize hybrid-fiber coax (HFC/cable), 38% utilize fiber-to-the-home (FTTH), and 22% utilize low-earth orbit satellite. The program involves a competitive application process with evaluation and selection of subgrantees. Low-cost broadband service options are required for the 10-year federal interest period. Reimbursements are issued on a quarterly basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 24, 2025 (full application window July 10-24, 2025); March 14, 2025 (prequalification deadline); Public comment deadline September 1, 2025 by 11:59 PM EDT
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ronnie Hammond, Director, Office of Statewide Broadband
structured_extraction.program_audience: Internet service providers, broadband service providers, electric cooperatives, electric utilities, units of local government, non-profit organizations, public-private partnerships, and Maryland jurisdictions and communities seeking to deploy broadband infrastructure and support digital adoption in unserved and underserved areas of Maryland. Eligible recipients include Community Anchor Institutions (CAIs) such as schools, libraries, and health care facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Broadband infrastructure deployment including fiber-optic, hybrid-fiber coax, satellite, and fixed wireless technologies. Funding supports capital costs for network construction, installation, and extension of broadband facilities, last-mile and middle-mile infrastructure, equipment, permitting, and deployment cost reduction. Low-cost broadband service options must be provided. Uses include: outside plant design and construction, network infrastructure deployment, permitting streamlining, pole/conduit access, construction techniques like microtrenching. Not permitted: operating expenses, maintenance costs, middle mile infrastructure (except as part of eligible deployment), spectrum licenses, personal equipment, or mobile phones.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide focus on unserved and underserved locations identified through the BEAD challenge process and FCC Fabric data in all Maryland counties. Coverage includes 18 of 24 Maryland counties with unserved/underserved areas; six counties are already fully served. Western Maryland (including Allegany, Garrett, Washington counties) is emphasized as having many unserved/underserved locations. Community Anchor Institutions (CAIs) are also eligible recipients. Final proposal includes 1,581 eligible CAI entries and approximately 9,000 unserved/underserved locations. No federally recognized tribal lands in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Boost Microgrant Program provides grants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 to support early-stage for-profit businesses seeking to start-up or expand within designated Sustainable Communities areas in Maryland. Administered through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) program, it gives preference to home-based businesses establishing their first commercial location outside of the home, minority and women-owned enterprises, innovative businesses driving technology advancements, businesses growing new industries, those leveraging existing regional strengths, and businesses partnering with education institutions. Up to $2,000,000 in total funding is available. Applicants must provide a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Microgrants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 provided directly to eligible small business owners for capital to support start-up or expansion opportunities. Total program funding is up to $2,000,000. Applicants must provide a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount. Businesses must be new or expanding and located in designated Sustainable Communities. Grants support capital and operating expenses including increased rent, increased payroll for new hires, new equipment, marketing, product development, and commercial real estate acquisition. Applicants must meet one or more priority impact attributes such as supporting minority and women-owned businesses, driving innovation or technology advancements, growing new industries, or leveraging existing regional strengths.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery Assistance - Hurricane Sandy
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal funding awarded to Maryland through the Disaster Relief Appropriations Act to support recovery activities from Hurricane Sandy in affected areas. The program provides assistance for necessary expenses related to disaster relief, long-term recovery, restoration of infrastructure and housing, and economic revitalization in areas impacted by Hurricane Sandy and other eligible events in calendar years 2011, 2012, and 2013. $8.6 million was awarded by Congress for recovery activities in Somerset County following Hurricane Sandy in October 2012, with Somerset County designated as the primary recovery area due to the most significant damage.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Somerset County, Maryland exclusively for primary recovery activities. Properties in floodplains require elevation to 2+ feet above base flood elevation. Properties along bodies of water (bay, river, creek) must meet specific elevation requirements. All recovery activities must be located in Somerset County, which was the most significantly impacted by Hurricane Sandy and is the designated recovery area for all $8.6 million in funding. Particularly City of Crisfield (593 of 889 impacted housing units).

Rental property assistance based on tenant income qualification
Properties in floodplains must be elevated to 2+ feet above base flood elevation

Promotion of sound, sustainable long-term recovery planning

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are reviewed and approved according to action plan amendments approved by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. Specific application procedures are outlined in the Action Plan documents. The state-level program requires Action Plan submission to HUD with public hearings at different program stages. For direct assistance, applicants must demonstrate unmet disaster-related needs and income qualification. Somerset County Department of Technical and Community Services administers as subgrantee. Housing Authority of Crisfield administers housing-related applications. Somerset County Economic Development Commission administers economic development applications. Citizen participation plan required with minimum 2 public hearings at different program stages.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant Special Projects
structured_extraction.program_description: A component of the Community Development Block Grant Program that funds special projects, planning initiatives, and other activities meeting criteria for special project designation. This federal program is designed to assist county and municipal governments with activities directed toward neighborhood revitalization, housing opportunities, economic development, and improved public facilities and services. The program provides public funds for activities meeting national objectives under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funds for special projects (up to $800,000), planning activities (up to $50,000), and economic development projects (up to $800,000). Supports housing rehabilitation, infrastructure improvements, public facilities, economic development initiatives, and services. Applications can be submitted at any time throughout the year after receiving written approval from the administering agency. Special Projects are processed on a first-come, first-serve basis once applications are complete. Housing rehabilitation grants have a maximum of $40,000 per single-family house. Assistance is available as grants and loans (revolving loan funds for housing rehabilitation).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for Special Projects and Planning can be submitted at any time throughout the year after a written approval has been received. Community Development competitive applications have a deadline of Friday, October 24th by 2:00 p.m. (annual deadline varies by funding cycle).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dona Sorce (Assistant Director); Kecia Campbell (Program Officer); Justin Fair (Program Officer); Charles Ansah (Project Manager); Cynthia Black (Project and Financial Manager)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties and non-entitlement cities and towns (population less than 200,000 for counties; less than 50,000 for cities/towns). Community Based Development Organizations (CBDOs) and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) certified by the State HOME Program. Non-profit organizations with IRS Section 501(c)(3) status. For-profit businesses in Good Standing (for economic development projects). Primary beneficiaries are low and moderate income (LMI) persons and households, including elderly persons, homeless persons, disabled persons, and communities with documented development needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning activities, economic development projects, housing acquisition and renovation, single-family owner-occupied housing rehabilitation, rental housing renovation, new construction in limited circumstances, public facilities, infrastructure improvements, water and sewer systems and connections, utility connections, preliminary engineering, economic development initiatives, job creation and retention assistance, downpayment and closing cost assistance, housing counseling assistance, broadband infrastructure installation (rental housing with 4+ units), generator installation (multi-family and public facilities), energy-saving materials, green and energy-efficient building materials and practices, fair housing improvements, homeless shelter operations and facilities, childcare center acquisition and renovation, health center facilities, training facilities, and commercial building renovation. Cannot be used for fire stations, police substations, or libraries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible units of general local government are in non-entitlement counties with population less than 200,000, excluding entitlement counties (Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's). Non-entitlement cities and towns with population less than 50,000 are eligible, excluding the cities of Annapolis, Baltimore, Bowie, Cumberland, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Hagerstown, and Salisbury. Projects cannot be located in special flood hazard areas, 100-year floodplains, or regulatory floodways, or coastal high hazard areas. Projects in 500-year floodplains are eligible with compliance conditions. Special consideration given to ENOUGH (Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, United, Generous, Helping) designated communities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that supports 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations by awarding allocations of state tax credits to benefit local projects and services in Priority Funding Areas and throughout Maryland. These tax credits serve as incentives to attract contributions from individuals and businesses for community revitalization, economic development, and local initiatives. Donors making contributions of $500 or more receive tax credits equal to 50% of the value of the money, goods, or real property contribution, which are in addition to federal and state tax deductions for charitable contributions. Tax credits can be used against taxes owed for the year in which the contribution was made and cannot be used retroactively for prior tax years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nonprofits receive allocations of state tax credits. Donors making contributions of $500 or more receive tax credits equal to 50% of the value of money, goods, or real property contributed. These tax credits can be used against taxes owed for the year in which the contribution was made and are in addition to Federal and State charitable deductions. Tax credits may not be used retroactively for prior tax years. Credits apply to Maryland state income tax liability for both individuals and businesses. Projects can include capital and/or operating expenses. State tax credit allocations support local projects and services for operating support and program delivery.

Projects can be capital and/or operating expenses.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state revitalization program that provides local governments, community development organizations, county councils, community development corporations, main street organizations, downtown partnerships, and groups of local governments with grants for capital projects with at least a 15-year shelf life aimed at strengthening communities through revitalization activities. The program supports neighborhood revitalization, housing, workforce development, and community development projects with a focus on vacant property reduction, homeownership, legacy resident investment, commercial and arts investment, and vibrant civic spaces. Approximately $8 million in capital funding is available annually for community improvement projects. Eligible project types include mixed-use development, business retention and attraction initiatives, streetscape improvements, homeownership increases, facade improvements, upper story redevelopment, adaptive reuse of vacant buildings, neighborhood parks, arts and cultural amenities, small business incubators, real estate acquisition, rehabilitation, or demolition, site development, construction of community facilities, building renovations and improvements, and community stabilization projects. Projects are most competitive when they explicitly connect to revitalization strategies and goals from a community's Sustainable Community Action Plan.

list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding through annual awards to designated Community Action Agencies and non-profit organizations to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization. Funds support direct services addressing employment, education, housing, nutrition, emergency services, and health for low-income individuals and families. The program distributes 90% of Maryland's allocated funds to designated Community Action Agencies, with the state using the remaining funds for discretionary funding and support activities. Funds may also support training, technical assistance, and coordination among Community Action Agencies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY23 Network Infrastructure Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program offering funding to local jurisdictions, their ISP partners, cooperatives, and other eligible organizations to construct new broadband networks serving unserved households and businesses. The program provides capital construction grants to build broadband infrastructure in areas where service is not currently available at specified speeds, with flexible matching requirements based on service area density. Up to $95 million is available for infrastructure projects deploying fiber optics, fixed wireless, or other technologies. Funds support equipment purchase and installation, construction of outside plant facilities, professional engineering services, fiber optic cable installation and testing, and related broadband service delivery infrastructure. Funded through the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Capital Projects Fund. The grant covers the majority of capital construction costs associated with providing service to unserved homes and businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $800,000 to $4.5 million covering 70% to 90% of capital construction costs for building new broadband networks serving unserved areas. Applicants must provide a match of 10% to 30% depending on service area density (households divided by route miles or towers). Up to $95 million total available. Eligible uses include electronic equipment (cabinets, switches, routers, wireless radios), outside plant materials (fiber, coaxial, copper), customer drops, customer premises equipment, engineering costs tied to funded capital assets, fiber optic cable installation and testing, labor (direct construction labor with employer taxes and benefits), materials (fiber optic cable, conduit, vaults, cabinets, CPE, splitters), equipment costs (operating or amortized hourly costs), travel expenses (lodging, mileage, meals), make-ready work, permits, software costs, and professional services (engineering, inspection, certification). Testing must include unidirectional and bi-directional attenuation testing at specified wavelengths per ANSI/TIA/EIA-568 standards with minimum 12 fiber strands tested per cable, end-to-end signature testing, splice testing, and OTDR testing. Ineligible uses include duplication of existing service, middle mile infrastructure (if alternative provider available), telephone/video service expenses, land/building purchases, operating expenses, pre-application costs, used or depreciated equipment, new tower construction (unless owned by applicant as match), and bandwidth costs. Projects must deliver broadband service at 100 Mbps download/100 Mbps upload speeds (or 100/20 Mbps under certain conditions) with maximum 50 millisecond latency. Reimbursement mechanism available for approved work performed by awardees.

Organizations conducting broadband infrastructure construction projects and awardees/grantees conducting broadband infrastructure projects. Applicants may not be individuals or partnerships.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband network infrastructure including electronic equipment (cabinets, switches, routers, wireless radios), outside plant materials (fiber, coaxial, copper), customer drops, customer premises equipment, engineering costs, labor (direct construction labor with employer taxes and benefits), materials (fiber optic cable, conduit, vaults, cabinets, CPE, splitters), equipment costs (operating or amortized hourly costs), travel expenses (lodging, mileage, meals), make-ready work, permits, software, professional services (engineering services, inspection, certification), fiber optic cable installation and testing, and related network infrastructure to serve unserved homes and businesses. Fiber optic outside plant infrastructure construction and installation costs are eligible. Broadband network infrastructure expansion and development. Only new materials and equipment are eligible unless OSB approves otherwise. Grant proceeds are ineligible for land purchases, tower construction (unless applicant-owned as match), building construction or renovation, bandwidth costs, and operating expenses. Middle mile infrastructure eligible if no alternative provider available. Customer connection costs reimbursable upon completion and operation.

Service area must be verified as unserved using documented methodology showing no locations receiving 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload speeds. Multi-state providers limited to Maryland service areas only.

structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive statewide income-qualified energy efficiency program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that serves limited-income households by providing free installation of energy conservation materials, home improvements, and energy efficiency and electrification assistance at no charge through a network of service providers including nonprofits, local governments, and for-profit contractors. The program includes five core sub-programs: Whole Home Efficiency, MEEHA (Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability Program), Base Efficiency, MEET (Maryland Energy Efficiency Tune-up), and Energy Kits. Services include weatherization, insulation, hot water system improvements, furnace and HVAC repair or replacement, renewable energy systems, heat pump installations, appliance installation, electrification measures, energy audits and personalized recommendations, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, refrigerator retrofits, and other health and safety enhancements. All services are provided at zero out-of-pocket expense to eligible participants. The program reduces energy usage by 16-23% and delivers approximately 94,350 tons of CO2 greenhouse gas savings. The program operates on a 2024-2026 cycle and is funded through the EmPOWER Maryland Act. The program is aligned with Standard Work Specifications (SWS) from the National Renewable Energy Laboratory. Services are coordinated with the DOE Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) and Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EmPOWER provides free energy efficiency upgrades to eligible limited-income homeowners and renters, including insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, refrigerator retrofits, HVAC repair or replacement, renewable energy systems, heat pump installations, appliance installation, electrification measures, and health and safety items. Services are provided at no charge to participants through an initial energy audit using DOE-approved methodology with diagnostic testing (blower door, combustion testing), personalized recommendations, contractor installation of improvements, and follow-up evaluation. The program operates through a statewide network of service providers including nonprofits, local governments, and for-profit contractors. Job cost caps: up to $16,000 per single-family job with health and safety up to $1,000 and incidental repairs up to 30% of total job cost. HVAC funding covers up to 85% of project cost. Energy kits include direct-install measures such as low-flow showerheads, smart power strips, outlet gaskets, pipe insulation, and faucet aerators. Multifamily projects receive grants and loans for energy conservation measures. Weatherization Readiness Fund provides up to $15,000 average per unit for addressing deferral conditions. Critical repairs are available separately, with maximum funding of $50,000 per project and maximum initial deposit of 33% of total project cost for homeowners. Nonprofits and local governments apply through a Request for Applications (RFA) process; for-profit contractors apply through a Request for Proposals (RFP) process. Competitive rounds are conducted at least every 3 years or more frequently to ensure statewide coverage. Training and Technical Assistance (T&TA) funding available with pre-approval required at least one week prior to training activities and reimbursement requests due within two weeks of completion. Technical guidance for energy efficiency retrofitting includes air sealing (attics, crawlspaces, subfloors, penetrations), insulation installation (attics, sidewalls, basements, manufactured homes), HVAC duct sealing and insulation, window and door installation/repair, domestic water heater and pipe insulation, low-flow plumbing fixtures, lead-safe weatherization practices, and ventilation improvements. Specific retrofitting work includes plenum insulation, water heater insulation, DHW pipe insulation, smoke alarms, CO detectors, LED lighting and controls, clothes dryer venting, exhaust fan installation, and appliance replacement. All work must comply with Standard Work Specifications (SWS) aligned with National Renewable Energy Laboratory standards.

Funding supports energy audits by Qualified Energy Auditors, purchase and installation of energy conservation measures, administrative costs for program implementation, staff training and certifications, technical assistance, equipment and vehicle purchases, health and safety repairs including asbestos remediation, biological hazard remediation, code compliance corrections, combustion appliance testing and replacement, fuel leak repairs, carbon monoxide and smoke detector installation, mold remediation, and ventilation system installation. Specific measures covered include: air sealing, attic improvements, weatherstripping, basement and crawlspace wall insulation, duct sealing and insulation, clothes dryer venting, exhaust fan installation, water heater and hot water pipe insulation, LED lighting upgrades and controls, smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, appliance metering, refrigerator replacement, window and door installation, and various other energy efficiency and health/safety measures. Critical repair funding available for homeowners covers structural repairs, electrical repairs, water leaks, lead remediation, and asbestos remediation. Minimum 80% of Program Income must be used for labor, materials, and program support; up to 10% may be used for Training and Technical Assistance (T&TA). Direct service costs, administrative costs, program operations, vehicle and equipment acquisition and maintenance, supplies and inventory (items valued at $1,000 or more per item), health and safety measures, transportation costs, liability insurance, and financial audit costs are allowable uses.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For homeowners and renters: Complete an easy online pre-application through the program website or submit a paper program application with required documents through DocuSign or the one-stop-shop energy programs application. Those currently approved for Energy Assistance payments from the Maryland Department of Human Services can contact the intake line. DHCD qualifies applicants for applicable funding sources and coordinates with all programs (Weatherization Assistance Program, Limited Income Energy Efficiency EmPOWER Program, and Maryland Energy Assistance Program). If eligible, applicants receive a letter with an assigned Network Partner contractor who contacts within 30 days to schedule an in-home comprehensive energy audit. Network Partners conduct comprehensive energy audits using DOE-approved methodology with diagnostic testing (blower door, combustion testing). Energy assessment agreement is signed before work begins; building owner agreement is required for rental properties. Network Partners identify all eligible measures and programs during the audit, develop written work scope documenting eligible work (distinguishing WAP-funded vs. other-funded work), and complete all recommended work at no cost through a single comprehensive retrofit project. Health and safety measures are prioritized and must be completed before energy efficiency measures proceed. Quality control inspections conducted after work completion. Data collection for refrigerators includes minimum 2-hour energy metering with data entered into Hancock system. Approximately 980 income-qualified applications are assigned monthly to Network Partners. Invoices submitted to energyinvoicing.dhcd@maryland.gov or appropriate reimbursement processes. For service providers: Nonprofits and local governments respond to periodic Request for Applications; for-profit contractors respond to Request for Proposals. Contractors can register on eMMA to receive notifications, or contact DHCD to be added to the vendor list. When a Request for Applications or Request for Proposals is posted (occurring at least every 3 years), eligible organizations submit competitive applications during the bidding round. For critical repairs: Submit completed application with all required documentation including income verification, property ownership documentation, bids from licensed Maryland contractors, and contractor cover page. Job classification includes Denial, Base Efficiency, and Whole Home Efficiency categories. Base Efficiency provides limited scope addressing health and safety concerns, exempt from full QC inspections. Whole Home Efficiency provides comprehensive retrofit with all eligible measures meeting program requirements. MEET (Maryland Energy Efficiency Tune-up) is a follow-up maintenance program for participants who received prior weatherization services, providing 1-2 hour home energy visits with assessment of energy consumption patterns, equipment evaluation, and direct installation of up to 15 energy-saving measures. Distribution of program updates to subgrantee network via email with overview of changes; conference calls scheduled with subgrantee network to review changes and Q&A; Q&A recordings distributed and posted on subgrantee website for reference.

structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Maryland Low Income Energy Efficiency Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide energy efficiency program established by the Maryland General Assembly through the EmPOWER Maryland Energy Efficiency Act (2008) to reduce per capita electricity and gas usage and peak demand, lower energy bills, reduce wholesale energy prices, and decrease greenhouse gas emissions. The program operates on multiple levels: (1) For limited-income homeowners and renters, EmPOWER provides free installation of energy conservation materials and home improvements including insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, refrigerator retrofits, major appliance replacements, weatherization, health and safety items, renewable energy systems, heat pump installations, and electrification measures. The program includes five core sub-programs: Whole Home Efficiency, MEEHA (Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability Program), Base Efficiency, MEET (Maryland Energy Efficiency Tune-up), and Energy Kits. Services include an initial energy audit using DOE-approved methodology with diagnostic testing, personalized recommendations, contractor installation of improvements, and a follow-up evaluation to confirm efficiency improvements, resulting in lower energy bills, improved comfort, and better indoor air quality. The program reduces energy usage by 16-23% and delivers approximately 94,350 tons of CO2 greenhouse gas savings. (2) For all Marylanders, the program promotes energy efficiency through utility-sponsored rebates and initiatives to help reduce electricity consumption, including incentives for switching from fossil fuel-powered heating and appliances to efficient electric alternatives. (3) For service providers, the program delivers energy efficiency services through a statewide network of nonprofits, local governments, and for-profit contractors who are competitively selected to serve limited-income households and businesses throughout Maryland in EmPOWER utility service territories. The program requires utility companies to achieve annual energy savings targets: 2.25% in 2025-2026 and 2.5% in 2027 and thereafter. DHCD requires energy savings of 0.53% in 2024, 0.72% in 2025, and 1% in 2026 for limited-income households. The program operates on a 2024-2026 cycle and is aligned with Standard Work Specifications (SWS) from the National Renewable Energy Laboratory. Services are coordinated with the DOE Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) and Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP).

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides multiple types of assistance: (1) For eligible limited-income homeowners and renters: free energy efficiency and electrification upgrades including insulation in attics, floors, crawlspaces, and walls, hot water system improvements and water heater replacement, lighting retrofits, furnace and HVAC repair, replacement, or tune-up services, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, refrigerator retrofits, major appliance replacements, renewable energy systems, heat pump installations including ductless heat pump units and heat pump water heaters, window and door replacement, weatherization, smart thermostats, electrical repairs and upgrades, and health and safety items. Services are provided at no charge to participants and include an initial comprehensive energy audit using DOE-approved methodology with diagnostic testing (blower door, combustion testing), personalized recommendations, contractor installation of improvements, and a follow-up evaluation to confirm efficiency improvements and monitor energy use reduction. Job cost caps: up to $16,000 per single-family job with health and safety up to $1,000 and incidental repairs up to 30% of total job cost; HVAC funding covers up to 85% of project cost. Energy kits include direct-install measures such as low-flow showerheads, smart power strips, outlet gaskets, pipe insulation, and faucet aerators. Multifamily projects receive grants and loans for energy conservation measures. Weatherization Readiness Fund provides up to $15,000 average per unit for addressing deferral conditions. Critical repairs are available separately, with maximum funding of $50,000 per project and maximum initial deposit of 33% of total project cost for homeowners. General Heat Waste budget up to $250 per home using DOE WAP funds. (2) For all utility customers: utility-sponsored rebate programs to promote energy efficiency and reduce electricity consumption, with incentives as of 2024 also supporting switching from fossil fuel-powered heating and appliances to efficient electric alternatives. Federal and state rebates, tax credits, and electricity rate offsets for residential customers are available. (3) For service providers: EmPOWER delivers energy efficiency services through a statewide network. Nonprofits and local governments apply through a Request for Applications (RFA) process; for-profit contractors apply through a Request for Proposals (RFP) process. Competitive rounds are conducted at least every 3 years or more frequently to ensure statewide coverage. Households are screened upon completion of the one-stop-shop energy programs application. Programs are managed by Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE), Potomac Edison Company (PE), Delmarva Power & Light (DPL), Potomac Electric Power Company (PEPCO), Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative (SMECO), Washington Gas Light Company (WGL), Choptank Electric Cooperative, and DHCD. Contractors must meet job quality requirements including 150% state minimum wage, paid leave, health insurance, and retirement benefits. Training and Technical Assistance (T&TA) funding available with pre-approval required at least one week prior to training activities and reimbursement requests due within two weeks of completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: When there is an active Request for Proposals or Request for Applications, notification will be posted on the program web page. Rolling/ongoing program; approximately 980 income-qualified applications assigned monthly to Network Partners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited-income Maryland households at or below 250% of Federal Poverty Level or 80% Area Median Income (whichever is higher), including both single-family and multifamily housing; limited-income households who are customers of one of six participating utility companies (BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas) and meet household income limits based on family size; homeowners and renters in utility service territories; residents of disadvantaged communities; approximately 450,000 limited-income households in Maryland (~21% of population); priority given to elderly persons (60+), families with children, persons with disabilities, high residential energy users, households with high energy burden, and at-risk occupants with documented medical conditions requiring air conditioning; also serves all individuals and businesses in Maryland using electricity seeking energy efficiency rebates; residential and commercial customers of participating utility companies; building owners, managers, and property developers; tenants in low-income housing; residents of group homes and shelters; multi-unit affordable housing residents; nonprofits, local governments, and for-profit home improvement contractors interested in becoming network partners to serve limited-income households; weatherization workers and contractors performing energy efficiency retrofits on residential properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency and electrification improvements including insulation in attics, floors, crawlspaces, and walls; hot water system improvements and water heater replacement; furnace and HVAC repair, replacement, or tune-up services; lighting retrofits; furnace cleaning, tuning, and safety repairs; refrigerator retrofits; major appliance replacement and recycling; renewable energy systems; heat pump installations including ductless heat pump units and heat pump water heaters; window and door replacement; smart thermostats; LED lighting; electrical repairs and upgrades; electrification readiness repairs; weatherization; health and safety items; breaker box upgrades; portable heating and cooling equipment; conservation services; and other health and safety enhancements. Rebates for energy efficiency improvements that reduce electricity usage. As of 2024, incentives also support switching from fossil fuel-powered heating and appliances to efficient electric alternatives and greenhouse gas emissions reductions. Funding supports energy audits by Qualified Energy Auditors, purchase and installation of energy conservation measures, administrative costs for program implementation, staff training and certifications, technical assistance, equipment and vehicle purchases, health and safety repairs including asbestos remediation, biological hazard remediation, code compliance corrections, combustion appliance testing and replacement, fuel leak repairs, carbon monoxide and smoke detector installation, mold remediation, and ventilation system installation. Critical repair funding available for homeowners covers structural repairs, electrical repairs, water leaks, lead remediation, and asbestos remediation. Minimum 80% of Program Income must be used for labor, materials, and program support; up to 10% may be used for Training and Technical Assistance (T&TA). Air sealing, duct sealing and insulation, crawlspace vapor retarder installation, clothes dryer venting, exhaust fan installation, and low-flow water conservation devices including low-flow showerheads and faucet aerators are also supported.

Certain areas have additional geographical eligibility criteria. Rebate programs are available to all Maryland utility customers. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For homeowners and renters: Applicants can complete an easy online pre-application through the program website or submit a paper program application with required documents through DocuSign or the one-stop-shop energy programs application. Those currently approved for Energy Assistance payments from the Maryland Department of Human Services can contact the intake line. DHCD qualifies applicants for applicable funding sources and coordinates with all programs (Weatherization Assistance Program, Limited Income Energy Efficiency EmPOWER Program, and Maryland Energy Assistance Program). If eligible, applicants receive a letter with an assigned Network Partner contractor who contacts within 30 days to schedule an in-home comprehensive energy audit. Network Partners conduct comprehensive energy audits using DOE-approved methodology with diagnostic testing (blower door, combustion testing). Energy assessment agreement is signed before work begins; building owner agreement is required for rental properties. Network Partners identify all eligible measures and programs during the audit, develop written work scope documenting eligible work (distinguishing WAP-funded vs. other-funded work), and complete all recommended work at no cost through a single comprehensive retrofit project. Health and safety measures are prioritized and must be completed before energy efficiency measures proceed. Quality control inspections conducted after work completion. Data collection for refrigerators includes minimum 2-hour energy metering with data entered into Hancock system. Approximately 980 income-qualified applications are assigned monthly to Network Partners. Invoices submitted to energyinvoicing.dhcd@maryland.gov or appropriate reimbursement processes. For rebate programs: Rebates are typically administered through utility companies. Participants can inquire with their local utility provider for available rebate programs. For service providers: Nonprofits and local governments respond to periodic Request for Applications; for-profit contractors respond to Request for Proposals. Contractors can register on eMMA to receive notifications, or contact DHCD to be added to the vendor list. When a Request for Applications or Request for Proposals is posted (occurring at least every 3 years), eligible organizations submit competitive applications during the bidding round. For critical repairs: Submit completed application with all required documentation including income verification, property ownership documentation, bids from licensed Maryland contractors, and contractor cover page. Job classification includes Denial, Base Efficiency, and Whole Home Efficiency categories. Base Efficiency provides limited scope addressing health and safety concerns, exempt from full QC inspections. Whole Home Efficiency provides comprehensive retrofit with all eligible measures meeting program requirements. MEET (Maryland Energy Efficiency Tune-up) is a follow-up maintenance program for participants who received prior weatherization services, providing 1-2 hour home energy visits with assessment of energy consumption patterns, equipment evaluation, and direct installation of up to 15 energy-saving measures. Baltimore County residents can contact the Department of Aging for application and eligibility verification. Households complete the one-stop-shop energy programs application and will be screened for all three programs (Weatherization Assistance Program, Limited Income Energy Efficiency EmPOWER Program, and Maryland Energy Assistance Program). Customers access EmPOWER programs through their utility provider or through DHCD for limited-income household programs. Companies report semi-annually to PSC on plan implementation and progress toward emissions reduction targets. Distribution of program updates to subgrantee network via email with overview of changes; conference calls scheduled with subgrantee network to review changes and Q&A; Q&A recordings distributed and posted on subgrantee website for reference.
