structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Home Stretch Program for Difficult to Serve Properties Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development program that provides financial assistance to help unserved and underserved households, county jurisdictions, and publicly supported housing gain access to high-speed, affordable internet. The program provides funding to county jurisdictions, individual homeowners, businesses, and public housing authorities to assist with capital construction costs for broadband service installation to premises that have difficulty obtaining service due to remoteness, distance from existing infrastructure, long driveways, or other geographic challenges. The program targets underserved areas with broadband speeds less than 25 Mbps and aims to close the digital divide through construction of wired and/or wireless broadband networks. In Fiscal Year 2024, $19.6 million in awards were made to provide internet access to approximately 2,400 unserved Maryland households in the first round.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $19.6 million in Fiscal Year 2024 awards available to county jurisdictions, homeowners, businesses, and public housing authorities. Maximum of $8,000 per location for difficult-to-serve properties. A 25% match of eligible project costs is required from county jurisdictions. Eligible uses include fiber optic extension, end-user facilities, internal wiring, wireless access points, building modifications, broadband networking equipment (hardware, software, modems, switches, routers, firewalls), low voltage contracting work, engineering and design services, and installation and provisioning labor. Minimum service speeds required: 100 Mbps download/100 Mbps upload with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds. Common area WiFi must meet minimum 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload. Funds help address distance from broadband infrastructure, long driveways, or other geographic issues that discourage service providers from delivering broadband service to underserved and difficult-to-serve areas. Funding source: American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Capital Projects Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: on or before December 22, 2023
structured_extraction.program_audience: County jurisdictions, public housing authorities, homeowners, businesses, and residents in hard-to-reach and difficult-to-serve areas lacking broadband infrastructure access. Particularly targets individuals living in households with income ≤150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, English learners, racial or ethnic minority group members, and residents of publicly owned housing developments and properties with inadequate broadband access in underserved areas with broadband speeds less than 25 Mbps.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for broadband service installation and extending broadband access to provide high-speed, affordable internet to difficult-to-serve, unserved, and underserved properties. Eligible uses include extension of fiber optic facilities, installation of interior wiring to individual units, wireless access points in public and common areas, broadband networking equipment (hardware, software, modems, switches, routers, firewalls), low voltage contracting work, engineering and design services, installation and provisioning labor, building modifications for broadband equipment installation, outreach and ACP registration assistance, and other construction necessary for internet service delivery to properties set far back from existing road infrastructure and publicly supported housing units. All equipment must be new and non-depreciated.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. All Maryland jurisdictions are eligible, including Somerset County and other underserved areas. Program focuses on publicly owned affordable housing units and properties lacking reliable connections meeting service requirements or with documented broadband access gaps. In the first round, 18 jurisdictions received awards and every jurisdiction that applied for the program received funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program designed to help Housing Choice Voucher Program and Public Housing participants achieve higher education, improve their employment status, and work toward economic self-sufficiency and reduced dependence on temporary cash assistance. The program evaluates skills and determines needs of families and individuals, providing guidance in financial literacy, job training, childcare, and other workforce success instruments. Participants work with FSS coordinators to develop individual family plans with short and long-term goals. Participants enter a contract (typically 5 years, extendable 2 years with good cause) and receive supportive services. When a family's income increases and they pay higher rent, the difference is credited to an interest-bearing escrow account.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides case management and supportive services including financial literacy training, job training and job retention support, childcare assistance, education support, employment counseling, health services referrals, homeownership guidance, and transportation assistance. Participants receive an interest-bearing escrow account where the increased rent portion (based on earned income increases above baseline wages) is credited and paid to the participant upon successful completion of the contract. FSS escrow payments are nontaxable per IRS ruling. Monthly escrow deposits accrue based on employment wage increases, with tax-free disbursement upon contract completion that can be used for any purpose including home down payment or other self-sufficiency goals. Early withdrawals from escrow are permitted for vehicle repair, testing fees, and pursuit of self-sufficiency goals.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education, job training, homeownership, entrepreneurship, childcare, transportation, financial literacy and employment counseling. Escrow account funds can be used for vehicle repair, testing fees, pursuit of self-sufficiency goals, and after contract completion for home down payment or any other purpose.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program created by the Maryland General Assembly in 2007 to help homeowners buy out (redeem) ground leases. Ground leases are long-term leases (usually 99 years) that are renewable forever and require periodic ground rent payments from the tenant to the lease holder. The program provides low-interest loans to homeowners to purchase ground lease redemptions and cover title search and loan closing costs. 0% interest, 30-year loans up to $3,500 including transactional costs up to $1,000 for lower income borrowers (60% AMI and below). Higher income borrowers (60-80% AMI) may receive loans at 4.5%-6.0% interest rates.

Higher income borrowers (60-80% AMI) may receive loans at 4.5%-6.0% interest rates. Funds used to redeem ground leases and cover title search and loan closing costs. A lien is recorded against the property for the loan amount. The program cannot provide grants for this purpose.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations construct, acquire, or modify existing housing to serve as group homes or assisted living units for people with special housing needs. Can also refinance mortgages on existing group homes. The program provides financing for group homes offering common, shared or independent living, dining, kitchen, and sleeping facilities with supportive services or supervisory personnel. Funds may support emergency and temporary housing facilities for homeless persons and victims of sex trafficking. Funded through state Group Home Financing Program funds, tax-exempt mortgage revenue bonds under the Special Housing Opportunities Program, and federal HOME Investment Partnerships Program funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans to finance newly constructed buildings, acquisition or acquisition and rehabilitation of existing residential buildings, or refinance mortgages on existing group homes. Interest rates vary from 0 to 7 percent depending on funding source and project cash flow. Maximum term is generally 30 years, with up to 40 years possible; construction term maximum 1 year. Maximum loan amounts vary by geographic location but cannot exceed appraised property value. Standard maximum loan amount is $125,000 per bedroom, with up to $143,750 per bedroom in high housing cost areas (Montgomery, Prince George's, and Howard Counties). Deferral provisions available for interest and/or principal, generally not more than 2 years. Nonprofit sponsors must contribute 5 percent equity; individual sponsors must contribute 10 percent equity. First lien position: up to 100% of appraised/after-rehabilitation value. Subordinate position: combined debt ≤95% of after-rehabilitation value. Current target interest rate 4%.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jack A. Daniels, Deputy Director CDA Special Loans Program, Single Family Housing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations that provide group homes to eligible residents including low-income persons, elderly individuals, developmentally or physically disabled persons, mentally disabled persons, juveniles in need of supervision, homeless persons, victims of sex trafficking, and persons with addictions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan funds may be used to refinance existing group home mortgages or for development costs including acquisition, closing costs, appraisal and inspection fees, architect and legal fees, surveys, and modification costs. Eligible modifications include repair or replacement of major systems (heating, roofing, electrical, plumbing), accessibility modifications (ramps, grab bars), lead paint abatement, general repairs and upgrades (painting, floor coverings), and minor improvements to meet state and local occupancy codes. Moderate rehabilitation, substantial rehabilitation, and turnkey new construction costs are eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: For Special Housing Opportunities Program financing, property must be located in a Priority Funding Area unless, for existing construction, a waiver is granted on an exceptional basis. For programs using federal HOME funds, property must be located in Maryland counties outside entitlement jurisdictions (excludes Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's Counties for HOME-funded component). Group homes must meet local government zoning codes. Montgomery, Prince George's, and Howard Counties classified as high housing cost areas with increased loan limits. Property must be in good repair and in compliance with applicable state and local housing and occupancy codes.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing financial assistance to help eligible Maryland homeowners identify, assess, and remediate health and safety hazards in their homes, including lead-based paint hazards in homes built before 1978. The program offers comprehensive assessments and remediation of critical issues including mold, gas leaks, roof damage, asbestos, combustion appliance problems, chimney damage, foundation waterproofing, radon, electrical hazards, plumbing issues, water and well repairs, window and door repairs, structural damage, building shell stabilization, and pest treatments. Grants up to $15,474.00 cover the actual cost of critical repair work on owner-occupied single-family homes and follow the Eight Principles of a Healthy Home to provide dry, clean, safe, well-ventilated, well-maintained, pest- and contaminant-free, thermally controlled homes. The program also addresses energy efficiency improvements to reduce utility bills and utility costs for homeowners.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides grants up to $15,474.00 to cover the actual cost of critical repair work on owner-occupied single-family homes. Maximum initial deposit is 33% of total project cost. Financial assistance covers comprehensive home assessments and hazard remediation including mold remediation, gas leak repair, roof repair and replacement, asbestos abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement, chimney repair, foundation and subspace waterproofing and drainage, radon mitigation, electrical hazard removal and service upgrades, plumbing repairs, water and well repairs, windows and doors for health and safety and water intrusion concerns, structural repairs, building shell stabilization, septic and sewer repairs, pest treatments, heating, cooling, and water heater system repairs or replacement. Flood insurance, hazard insurance, contamination assessment and remediation, and energy efficiency improvements are also eligible uses. Project costs cannot exceed 50% of property market value and cannot increase unit density or change land use from residential to non-residential.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 18, 2026 (comment submission deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes in eligible counties with household income at or below 80 percent of Area Median Income, with priority given to households with children under six years old. Maryland residents with primary residences.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical home repairs and hazard mitigation including mold remediation, gas leak repair, roof repair and replacement, asbestos abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement, chimney repair, foundation and subspace waterproofing and drainage, radon mitigation, electrical hazard removal and service upgrades, plumbing repairs, water and well repairs, windows and doors for health and safety and water intrusion concerns, structural repairs, building shell stabilization, septic and sewer repairs, pest treatments, heating, cooling, and water heater system repairs or replacement. Flood insurance, hazard insurance, contamination assessment and remediation, and energy efficiency improvements are also eligible uses.

Flood insurance is required for properties in 100-year floodplains. Property must be the applicant's primary residence with power to home.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: DHCD recommends starting with a free, in-home comprehensive assessment to identify repairs needed and enroll in appropriate programs. Applicant completes the Combined Energy Rehabilitation Application and submits it to DHCD for eligibility review along with all required documentation including income verification, home ownership proof, and contractor bid. Applicant selects one or more licensed contractors and obtains bids (not more than 60 days old) for the critical repairs. Applicant provides a work proposal with photos documenting the issues to DHCD's Healthy Homes Evaluator for review and possible property visit. Contractor provides required documentation including MHIC license, Certificate of Liability Insurance ($1M per occurrence minimum), Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 Form. Applicant signs the Grant Agreement, Rehabilitation Grant Agreement, and other closing documents which can be executed electronically via DocuSign. Contractor and owner sign the mutual Rehabilitation Agreement. Order to Proceed is issued after grant funds are encumbered and all necessary zoning and building permits are submitted. Contractor performs the work with on-site monitoring and inspections by the Healthy Homes Evaluator. Before final payment, owner signs the Certificate of Completion or final inspection form.

structured_extraction.program_description: Broadband infrastructure grant program for affordable housing developments that aims to close the digital divide and ensure covered populations have access to no-cost or low-cost internet access. The program assists municipal and nonprofit owners of public housing as well as internet service providers in providing broadband-capable wiring and infrastructure to individual dwelling units and common areas in affordable housing. The program addresses digital equity and accessibility gaps in affordable housing communities by enabling targeted housing units to leverage high-speed broadband services from existing Internet Service Providers. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Capital Projects Fund.

A 5% match of eligible project costs is required. Total of $26.9 million allocated. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Capital Projects Fund.

structured_extraction.program_description: A broadband grant program designed to assist in digital equity and inclusion efforts by providing broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units in low-income, publicly-owned housing. The program addresses the digital equity gap and fosters digital equity in Maryland by assisting local jurisdictions in implementing broadband delivery solutions to unserved residents in publicly supported housing. The initiative is transformative and comprehensive, covering network infrastructure, internal wiring, wireless access, and community engagement. The program reduces digital equity and inclusion issues for vulnerable populations, particularly addressing the strain on households caused by the COVID pandemic. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Capital Projects Fund. Minimum speeds required: 100 Mbps download/100 Mbps upload with maximum 50ms latency at dwelling units, and free WiFi in common areas with minimum 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload speeds.

list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Round 1: Grants ranging from $500,000 to $9,000,000 covering 95% of eligible project costs. Expanded Round (FY24 Affordable Housing): Grants of $250,000 to $5,000,000 covering 95% of eligible project costs. All applicants must provide a 5% match of eligible project costs (matching funds can be local, state, or federal). Funding covers broadband network infrastructure including fiber optic extension, end-user facilities, internal wiring, wireless access points, building modifications for equipment installation, engineering design services, community engagement and ACP registration assistance, and educational/technical assistance for adoption. Equipment must be new and non-depreciated. Non-capital administrative overhead capped at 1%. Funded through the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Capital Projects Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 31, 2025 (Affordable Housing); February 7, 2025 (Expanded Round)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of publicly supported housing developments and publicly owned low-income housing. Target populations include: aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers/English learners, individuals with low literacy levels, members of racial or ethnic minority groups, families with children, individuals with income ≤150% federal poverty level. Eligible applicants include local jurisdictions, public housing authorities, recognized jurisdictional housing authorities, entities that own and maintain stock of publicly supported housing, municipalities, non-profit organizations, Internet Service Providers, incorporated organizations recognized as partners by local jurisdictions, and cooperatives legally formed in Maryland and recognized as a partner by local jurisdiction. For Affordable Housing expansion round: applicants can also include cooperatives legally formed in Maryland and recognized as a partner by local jurisdiction. Partnerships and sole proprietors are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Extension of fiber optic facilities to individual dwelling units; installation of interior wiring to individual units; wireless access points and network equipment; end-user electronics and modems; low voltage contracting and cabling work; engineering design services tied to funded capital assets; installation and provisioning labor; community engagement and ACP registration assistance (capped at 3% of total project cost, not to exceed $15,000); broadband education and adoption support; building minor construction or renovation; customer premises equipment; electronic equipment (cabinets, switches, routers); outside plant materials (fiber, coaxial, copper); and related construction costs. Ineligible uses include middle mile infrastructure, telephone/video services, towers, operating expenses, bandwidth costs, new building construction, and depreciated equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program. Publicly owned housing developments identified as having need for broadband investment, particularly those lacking access to connections reliably meeting minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum 50ms latency. For Affordable Housing expansion round: multifamily dwelling units (MDUs) owned by municipalities or non-profit organizations. Properties must be publicly owned (not just publicly supported).

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide response to address homelessness in Maryland that provides over $15 million in annual federal and state funding to Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions. HSP provides technical support and funding to help communities across Maryland prevent and end homelessness by connecting people to housing programs, shelters, and other services. The program prioritizes funding for diversion, rapid housing connection, vulnerable populations, evidence-based practices, and equitable service delivery. HSP funds eligible homeless services activities including street outreach, emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, homeless prevention, permanent supportive housing case management, HMIS (Homeless Management Information System), and administrative costs. Leads the state's strategy, policy, and coordinated response effort to prevent and end homelessness, aligning Maryland efforts with federal priorities to make homelessness rare, brief, and non-recurring.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants totaling $15.2 million available (FFY2025 Emergency Solutions Grant: $1.2 million; SFY2026 State HSP Funds: $14 million; anticipated level funding or up to 30% increase depending on final state budget) provided to HUD-approved Collaborative Applicants/lead agencies of Maryland Continuums of Care and DHCD-approved lead agencies for Balance of State Local Homeless Coalitions to fund eight main activities: Homeless Prevention/Shelter Diversion, Emergency Shelter, Street Outreach, Rapid Re-Housing, Permanent Supportive Housing, HMIS, Special Events, and Administration Support Costs. Minimum $1 million allocated for unaccompanied youth projects. Funding supports rental assistance (short-term, medium-term, rental arrears), financial assistance (application fees, security deposits, utility deposits/payments, moving costs, furniture), case management, housing search and placement services, emergency shelter operations, street outreach engagement, and administrative costs (up to 10% of grant request). Federal and state funding and technical support coordinate resources and services across the state.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program created under the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 that helps Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic pay for critical repairs in their primary residences that could lead to displacement if not addressed. The program provides grants up to $10,000 per property, with exceptions up to $15,000 on a case-by-case basis with documentation of need. Eligible repairs include non-functioning heating/cooling systems, water heaters, electrical and plumbing/septic repairs, roof repair/replacement, mold/mildew remediation, lead paint/asbestos removal, and structural and maintenance issues. All work must be performed by licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractors.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $10,000 for critical home repairs; exceptions may be made for up to $15,000 on a case-by-case basis with documentation of need. Payment options: 33% deposit with 67% at completion OR 0% deposit with 100% at completion. Eligible repairs include non-functioning heating/cooling systems, water heaters, electrical and plumbing/septic repairs, roof repair/replacement, mold/mildew remediation, lead paint/asbestos removal, and structural and maintenance issues. All work must be performed by licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractors. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who experienced financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic and are facing critical home repair needs that could lead to displacement, with income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical health and safety repairs in primary residences that would cause involuntary displacement if unaddressed, including mold/mildew remediation, asbestos removal, HVAC repairs, electrical/plumbing/septic repairs, wells, roof repair/replacement, lead paint hazard reduction, structural/maintenance issues, and trip/slip hazards. All work must be performed by licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractors. Cannot be used for remodeling or non-essential repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All of Maryland, including all 24 counties. Applicants must reside in their primary residence in Maryland. Income limits vary by county and household size based on County Area Median Income (AMI).

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive funding program designed to support innovative multifamily housing development projects that meet Maryland's affordable housing needs. The program provides low- or no-interest loans to local housing authorities or county governments partnering with housing developers to increase housing production and reward innovative solutions to housing scarcity. The program also allows counties to purchase existing privately owned housing in conjunction with local housing authorities or housing developers. structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Grant and Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state and HUD-funded program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides grants or loans to help Maryland homeowners, landlords, and licensed residential childcare facility operators remove or reduce lead hazards in owner-occupied single family homes and rental properties. The program offers three funding mechanisms: grants (up to $25,000 per eligible property with $100,000 annual sponsor maximum available in certain target areas with no income limits; in other areas, income limit is 80% of Area Median Income), amortizing loans (0%-7%, 20 years), and deferred loans (0%, 20 years). Deferred principal and interest may be available for borrowers with no repayment capability at 50% and 30% AMI levels. Work must be performed by licensed and accredited lead abatement contractors. Services include education, lead risk-reduction, temporary relocation, and referrals to other programs. Eligible activities include treating doors and windows, treating floors, removing paint, stabilizing and repainting surfaces, encapsulating hazards, enclosing hazards, specialized cleaning, lead testing, architectural and legal fees, and other innovative approved lead hazard reduction methods to meet lead dust clearance standards. Match requirement: 20% for for-profit sponsors; 10% for nonprofit sponsors; 10% for owner-occupants with income above 80% of median; N/A for owner-occupants with limited incomes. Funding is available until April 1, 2029.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of counties, municipalities, and their agencies to finance public infrastructure projects that serve the community. The program provides long-term capital financing with favorable terms, reduces issuance costs through economies of scale and pooling local demand, and helps local governments navigate the complexities of tax-exempt bond financing. Local governments receive loans from the bond proceeds at market-based interest rates. The interest rate on local government loans is subject to market conditions at the time of bond sale based on the rate attained on the pooled bond issue. Local governments are responsible for repaying the debt and paying their pro-rata share of issuance costs. The loan term is set at the option of the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or thirty years, whichever is less. The program accommodates projects ranging from $150,000 to $10 million or more. Debt refinancing of existing debt for eligible projects is also available.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program governed by Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code that encourages private sector investment in the construction, rehabilitation, purchase, and preservation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis through funding rounds held once or twice annually to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors of eligible housing projects based on criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan. The tax credit equals the applicable percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building, with the applicable percentage determined by the IRS. Project sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return over a 10-year Credit Period. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for tax credits outside of the competitive process. Buildings must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years. The program requires compliance with income and rent restrictions, utility allowance calculations, tenant income certifications and annual recertifications.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal Low Income Housing Tax Credits are awarded on a competitive basis through funding rounds held once or twice annually. The tax credit equals the applicable percentage (4% or 9% depending on financing type) of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building. The applicable percentage is determined by the IRS. Tax credits are issued to developers and organizations and are claimed on the federal income tax return over a 10-year Credit Period. Project sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return. Projects must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. Buildings must comply with tenant income, maximum rent levels, and low-income occupancy requirements during the Compliance Period and Extended Use Period. Annual utility allowance reviews and calculations are required utilizing HUD Utility Schedule Model or Energy Consumption Model methodologies. Properties with Placed in Service (PIS) dates of April 24, 2019 or later must meet specified income limits (30%, 40%, 50%, or 60% of area median family income) and maximum rent restrictions based on qualified census tracts and difficult development areas. Income and rent limits are updated annually based on HUD Median Family Income data. Utility allowances must include all utilities except cable television, telephone, and internet. For sub-metered units, utility rates must match company rates charged to owner with administrative fees capped at $5/month per unit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing funding to local jurisdictions, 501(c) nonprofit entities, and community-based anchor institutions to further Maryland's digital inclusion efforts by enabling access to high-speed internet and expanding digital literacy. The program funds digital inclusion planning, implementation of digital inclusion programs, training, and operation of public access computing centers. Funded through the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 with $2 million allocated to address the digital divide exposed by COVID-19. Two grant tracks are available: Digital Inclusion Planning provides up to 50% of planning costs with a maximum of $30,000 and minimum of $5,000; Digital Inclusion Implementation provides up to 100% of implementation costs with a maximum of $75,000 and minimum of $10,000. Priority is given to underserved populations including low-income individuals (those in households with income ≤150% of federal poverty level), aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, English learners, individuals with low literacy, racial and ethnic minorities, and rural residents.

Total program funding: $2 million. Grant amounts may be reduced based on competitive review and applicant capacity. Funds support projects in the following areas: Access, Affordability, Literacy/Training, Planning, Adoption, and Other. Funding source: American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (ARPA) Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to help local jurisdictions, community-based organizations, nonprofits, and anchor institutions create and deploy broadband gap networks and community networks to address internet affordability challenges and provide low-cost or no-cost internet access to low and moderate income households and other underserved populations including individuals living in poverty, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers or low literacy, and members of racial or ethnic minority groups. The program supports the construction, deployment, expansion, or continuation of community-based gap networks and broadband networks using a technology-neutral approach. Funding is supported by the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds). Grants range from $25,000 to $250,000 covering up to 100 percent of project costs, with a total of $5 million available.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $25,000 and $250,000 for up to 100% of project costs for construction, deployment, expansion, or continuation of community-based gap networks and community networks. Total of $5 million available. Funds support equipment, networking capability, hardware, software, and digital network technology to provide broadband services at low or no cost to covered populations. Eligible equipment includes Optical Line Terminals (OLTs), Optical Network Terminals (ONTs), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and necessary equipment shelters. Projects must reliably provide a minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up. Funding source: American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development provides funding to assist Maryland's designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods in building capacity to achieve their community revitalization and economic development goals in designated Sustainable Community areas throughout the state. This Operating Assistance Grant Program provides vital support for community and economic revitalization efforts, enabling organizations to strengthen their operations and implement strategic initiatives aligned with their transformation strategies.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Operating assistance grants awarded to eligible Main Street communities. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities with full accreditation receive approximately $33,000 each; affiliate communities receive approximately $25,000 each; and Aspiring Communities receive approximately $12,000 each. Final amounts are contingent upon General Assembly approval during the FY2027 legislative session. Funds support operating expenses only, including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, consultant services, studies, branding, marketing, design work, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, and placemaking initiatives. Capital project costs are not supported. No matching funds are required, and all projects and activities must be completed within one year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Affordable Housing Trust makes affordable housing more available throughout Maryland by funding capital costs of rental and ownership housing, providing financial assistance for nonprofit developer capacity building, funding supportive services for occupants of affordable housing, and funding operating expenses of affordable housing developments. The program serves households earning less than 50% of area or statewide median income. The Trust also receives interest earnings from escrow accounts maintained by title insurance producers.

Pre-development awards are generally repayable. The Trust reserves the right to make funding available as interest-bearing loans. Financial assistance is available for operating assistance, property acquisition, pre-development costs, construction, and rehabilitation of residential properties.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides capital grants to improve the exteriors of commercial and mixed-use buildings located in Maryland designated revitalization areas including Sustainable Communities, Main Street Areas, RISE Zones, and Transit Oriented Development areas. Funding supports creation of consistent, attractive designs for commercial corridors to bolster economic vitality and stimulate private investments. Funding is available through local governments, groups of local governments, community development organizations, and directly to business owners and property owners in participating communities. Eligible improvements include painting, awnings, lighting, signage, masonry, door and window repairs, siding, shingles, rain gutters, porch repairs, storefront reconstruction, murals, roofs, and removal of unattractive finishes. Recipients may receive up to 50 percent matching funds for facade improvements. Approximately $5 million in capital funding is available in Fiscal Year 2025.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides capital grants to local governments, groups of local governments, community development organizations, and property owners to capitalize a grants fund for businesses and property owners to improve their building facades. Funds cover capital costs related to exterior facade improvements for business buildings and facilities including painting, awnings, lighting, signage, masonry, door and window repairs, siding, shingles, rain gutters, porch repairs, storefront reconstruction, murals, roofs, and removal of unattractive finishes. Individual business improvements range between $1,000-$50,000 per award cycle. Recipients may receive up to 50 percent matching funds. Improvements must be to primary elevations of commercial properties only. Ineligible uses include interior work, solar panels, electric charging stations, predevelopment or operating expenses, acquisitions, permitting, and architectural/design services. Approximately $5 million in capital funding is available in Fiscal Year 2025. Recent Kent County recipients included $50,000 to Main Street Historic Chestertown and $50,000 to the Town of Galena for façade improvements.

Improvements must be to primary elevations only. Ineligible uses include interior work, solar panels, electric charging stations, predevelopment or operating expenses, acquisitions, permitting, architectural/design services, and improvements under $1,000 or over $50,000. Historic windows and doors should be preserved or restored when possible rather than replaced.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program increases the construction and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes by providing tax-exempt bonds and notes for construction and permanent financing, leveraged with federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits. The program supports development and preservation of affordable rental housing through bond financing. Financing can be used for new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing rental housing with at least five units. Various bond structures are available with 17-40 year final maturity and mortgage amortization periods of 35-40 years. The program accepts a variety of financing structures with different terms, interest rates, and fees, including options paired with 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits with multiple credit enhancement structures available (FHA Risk Sharing, GNMA MBS, Freddie Mac TEL, FNMA MBS, Cash Collateral). Tax-exempt housing revenue bonds are issued as unrated private placements or rated bonds, with taxable GNMA loans featuring HUD/GNMA credit enhancement. This financing technique enables qualified multifamily rental housing developments to realize lower interest rates and minimize subsidies while maximizing leverage.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing for multifamily rental housing projects with a minimum of five units. Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years with various bond structures available with 17-40 year final maturity and mortgage amortization periods of 35-40 years. Permanent loan rates ranging from approximately 5.67% to 6.67% all-in rates. Interest rates are based on the Community Development Administration's bond rate. A first lien position is generally required. All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program including FHA Risk Sharing, GNMA MBS, Freddie Mac TEL, FNMA MBS, and Cash Collateral options. Projects must contain a minimum of five complete independent dwelling units. Loans may be provided to refinance existing high interest rate private loans if the refinance occurs with rehabilitation of the housing. Financing structures include 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits for projects complying with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan. Multiple bond program options available including Risk Sharing (HRB), GNMA Long Term (HRB), GNMA Tax/TE (Standalone), Freddie TEL (Standalone), Fannie Mae M.TEB (Standalone), and Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac Credit Enhanced Funds (Standalone). Taxable GNMA loans can be paired with tax-exempt bonds, with interest-only payments during construction (20-24 month construction period) and 40-year permanent loan amortization. Tax-exempt housing revenue bonds issued as unrated private placements or rated bonds. Upfront costs range from approximately $1.1M to $2.1M for $20M financing. Mortgage amounts up to $20,000,000. Multiple fee structures available including underwriter fees, bond counsel fees, financial advisor fees, trustee fees, CDA financing fees, and servicing fees.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability Program (MEEHA)
structured_extraction.program_description: MEEHA promotes energy efficiency and housing affordability in affordable multifamily rental housing developments through two funding pathways: EmPOWER and the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP). EmPOWER provides grants or low-interest loans (0% interest with deferred payments) to reduce electric or gas consumption, perform limited health and safety or incidental repairs, and support energy-saving measures, with funding totaling $134.9 million for calendar years 2024-2026. GHGRP provides grants to replace fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment and support building energy conservation and alternative energy systems, with $8.75 million in fiscal year 2024 and $5 million each in fiscal years 2025 and 2026. Eligible improvements include electric panel upgrades, replacement of fossil fuel-powered equipment and systems with electric equipment such as heat pumps, building energy conservation measures, alternative energy generating systems, solar photovoltaic installation, EV charging stations, building shell weatherization, HVAC replacement/upgrades, water heating systems, lighting, appliances, fenestration, and limited health and safety repairs. The program supports cost-effective energy efficiency and conservation upgrades for existing, major renovation, and new construction projects. GHGRP specifically funds multifamily projects to reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions through electrification and fossil fuel system replacement. Gas-reducing measures are available only in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territories.

Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP): $8.75 million in fiscal year 2024, and $5 million each fiscal years 2025 and 2026, offered as grants only. GHGRP provides up to $15,000 per dwelling unit with a project cap of $1.25 million. Funds are disbursed during construction as work is completed and verified, with DHCD inspecting a sample of installed measures. Payment processing typically takes 4-5 weeks after requisition approval. Funding supports energy efficiency improvements and housing affordability measures in multifamily rental housing, including electric panel upgrades, replacement of fossil fuel-powered equipment and systems with electric equipment such as heat pumps, and other energy efficiency upgrades. Projects must achieve at least 20% energy savings above minimum code and performance standards.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and operators of affordable multifamily rental housing developments, including for-profit and non-profit entities, seeking to improve energy efficiency, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and reduce housing costs for low-income renters. Projects of all building sizes and configurations are eligible, including single family units as group projects, individually metered buildings, or master metered buildings. Properties with 2 or more buildings or 35,000+ SF gross floor area are eligible. Grantees must have legal authority to execute agreements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements to reduce electric or gas consumption; replacement of fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment; building energy conservation measures; alternative energy generating systems; solar photovoltaic installation; EV charging station installation; HVAC system replacements and repairs; insulation improvements (attic, walls, basement, crawlspace, duct, pipe); lighting upgrades to LED; duct sealing and aeroseal; smart thermostats and variable frequency drives; electric panel upgrades; ventilation improvements; dehumidifiers; asbestos remediation; limited health and safety or incidental repairs in projects completing energy-reducing measures; domestic hot water system upgrades; fenestration/windows and doors; air sealing; appliance replacements; building electrification and decarbonization measures; water conservation measures; electric kitchen equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Gas-reducing measures under EmPOWER are limited to properties in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territories. GHGRP projects must be in existing buildings with 35,000 or more gross square feet of floor area (excluding parking garages), or two or more buildings with combined 35,000+ sf served by same meter/system.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Submit MEEHA application and supporting documents to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov. 2) Commission a Qualified Energy Professional from the approved Qualified Energy Professionals List to conduct an energy audit (rehabilitation projects) or energy certification review (new construction projects). 3) Qualified Energy Professional submits Funding Request to DHCD with project owner's supporting documents, including Building Information Notes, organized by meter affected (residential vs. commercial), with completed photo documentation and diagnostic testing reports as applicable. 4) DHCD reviews Funding Request, sends scope confirmation spreadsheet of approved measures and funding, and finalizes the request. 5) Project owner and DHCD execute funding agreement or grant agreement. 6) Project begins construction and submits requisitions with supporting documentation and required photo evidence as work is completed. 7) DHCD inspects sample of installed measures to verify compliance with specifications and processes payment (typically 4-5 weeks after requisition approval). 8) After construction, project enters affordability compliance period (monitored through Energy Star Portfolio Manager account and benchmarking). 9) Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) participation monitored through monthly payment reports with documentation of good faith efforts.

structured_extraction.program_description: A venture capital program dedicated to funding and growing early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential for job growth that have already raised equity and are seeking additional investment to reach the next funding milestone. The program provides venture debt investment with repayment in principal and interest, convertible note structures, or equity investment to support bridge financing and help businesses scale operations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Venture debt investment with repayment in principal and interest or a convertible note structure, as well as equity investment funding. SSBCI must be on at least a pari passu basis with private capital match, meaning equal priority with other investors. SSBCI funds must cause and result in the private capital match. Target SSBCI portion of venture debt is $500,000 to $2,500,000. Aggregate funding round less than $20,000,000. Minimum private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 1:1 required, with target match greater than 2:1. Typical bridge rounds exceed $2,000,000 and are designed for companies positioned to scale that need bridge financing to achieve milestones.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive funding program that provides capital and operating grants to support commercial and residential development activities and strategic economic development capital projects in targeted areas of the National Capital region designated for neighborhood revitalization in Prince George's and Montgomery Counties. The program focuses on areas where modest investment and coordinated strategy will have significant neighborhood revitalization impact and strengthen regional economic competitiveness. Assistance supports down payment assistance, property acquisition and rehabilitation, energy efficiency improvements, affordable housing development, mixed-use projects, community open space and public infrastructure enhancement, and strategic demolition.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal affordable housing production program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development to create, preserve, and increase the supply of safe, sanitary, and decent affordable rental housing for extremely low-income households earning 30% or less of the Area Median Income (or at the poverty line, whichever is greater). The program provides financing support for affordable rental housing development and preservation through funding for construction, rehabilitation, property acquisition, related soft costs, resident relocation costs, and limited operating costs or operating reserves for HTF-assisted units. HTF funds are often combined with other federal, state, and local housing resources to make affordable housing projects financially feasible. Projects must maintain affordability for 40 years from project completion. The program receives $3,000,000 in federal funding from HUD for FFY 2025 (October 1, 2025 - September 30, 2026).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HTF funds support acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury affordable rental housing, property acquisition, related soft costs, resident relocation costs, and limited operating costs or operating reserves for HTF-assisted units. Assistance may take the form of grants, equity investments, interest-bearing loans or advances, non-interest bearing loans or advances, or deferred payment loans. Approximately 90% of annual allocation supports housing activities including development hard costs, acquisition costs, soft costs, relocation costs, and operating/rental assistance (up to one-third of annual allocation, must be utilized within 5 years). The remaining 10% supports administrative and planning expenses. Operating expenses must be between $4,000-$8,000 per unit per year (excluding replacement reserves). Minimum $300 per unit per year in replacement reserve deposits required. Operating reserves must be maintained at 3-6 months of underwritten expenses. HTF funds cannot be used for refinancing existing debt or mandatory supportive services. Applications are accepted throughout the year. DHCD awards HTF funds to eligible projects on a competitive and non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis depending on fund availability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted throughout the year on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, for-profit developers, sponsors, and other qualified housing development entities with demonstrated financial capacity and experience seeking to develop or preserve affordable rental housing for extremely low-income (ELI) households, including families, seniors, persons with disabilities or special needs, homeless families, persons experiencing housing instability, veterans, and elderly individuals. Section 8 voucher holders and persons with other housing assistance are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury affordable rental housing. Funds may support development hard costs, acquisition costs, related soft costs, relocation costs, operating expenses, rental assistance, replacement reserves, and working capital. Projects must include energy efficiency improvements, accessibility enhancements, lead-based paint remediation, and health and safety corrections as applicable. Maximum per-unit development subsidy based on Maryland HOME Subsidy Limits (ranging from $181,488 for 0-bedroom to $359,263 for 4-bedroom units). Construction cost limits vary by building type ($173-$277 per square foot). HTF funds cannot be used for refinancing existing debt or mandatory supportive services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland with priority consideration in Priority Funding Areas (PFAs) for new construction, including incorporated municipalities, areas between Baltimore beltway and city limits, areas between Washington DC beltway and boundary, Sustainable Communities, Federal and State enterprise zones, county-designated PFAs, rural villages, and certified heritage areas. Rural areas include Allegany, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties, as well as any areas eligible under USDA Rural Development programs. Priority consideration for family projects in Communities of Opportunity and projects in Qualified Census Tracts (QCTs) or Difficult Development Areas (DDAs). Thompson v. HUD designated areas in Baltimore City and Baltimore County Conciliation Agreement designated tracts also eligible.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Administration issues bonds to fund loans for business projects located in priority funding areas and traditionally underserved areas defined as Sustainable Communities. The program serves as a gap lender for small businesses with flexible lending terms and can make senior or subordinate loans, or combinations of both. Projects can include acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed-use real estate, refinancing of stabilized commercial projects, and non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation, and new construction. The program has a long-standing history of over 20 years with a current portfolio of 158 loans exceeding $20 million in aggregate outstanding principal balance. Loans feature low LTV secured structures with debt service coverage ratio requirements of at least 1.25 for senior loan portfolios or 1.50 for CDA loans. Credit support and reinsurance mechanisms are available through the Maryland Housing Fund.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bond-funded loans for business projects located in priority funding areas or Sustainable Communities. Loans can be structured as senior or subordinate loans, or combinations of both. Loans finance acquisition, permanent financing, refinancing, and construction or rehabilitation of commercial and mixed-use real estate and non-profit facilities. The program uses industry-standard underwriting criteria with flexible lending terms designed to fill unmet marketplace demand. Debt service coverage ratio requirements: minimum 1.50 for CDA loans or 1.25 for senior loan portfolio. Low LTV secured lending structures available with top loss guarantees or shared risk coverage up to $5,000,000 for non-CDA lenders. Up to $10,000,000 in initial CDA loan capitalization; up to $2,000,000 in reinsurance support for debt securities; up to $3,000,000 in guarantees for co-senior loans and participations; approximately $5,000,000 annual state-appropriated capital for subordinate and higher-risk loans. Online application process available.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed-use real estate; refinancing of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects; construction financing; corporate headquarters acquisition; retail and office redevelopment; mixed-use housing, office, and retail projects; non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation, and new construction.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive federal Treasury-allocated loan participation program designed to assist small businesses and Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) with capital for working capital, owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, and relending through below-market-rate loans up to $5 million with flexible terms. The program includes direct lending to small businesses and a loan-to-lender component for CDFIs, working with community lending partners to provide financing. Priority is given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI) who own or operate Maryland-based small businesses. The Loan to Lender component provides loans to CDFIs for relending to small businesses combined with required private capital match, with targeted loans to small businesses of up to $350,000, focusing on businesses owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI), very small businesses (VSB), and CDFI investment areas. CDFI loans for relending range from $500,000 to $15,000,000 based on capacity. Designed to provide flexible financing for start-ups and new/existing business expansions with a focus on CDFI investment areas and emphasis on underserved entrepreneurs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or junior debt loans ranging from $350,000 to $5,000,000 for small businesses. SSBCI portion of loan is $350,000 to $5,000,000 with up to 30% program match. Interest rate based on underwriting analysis, maximum 18% for small business loans. Flexible loan terms up to 30 years depending on use and loan amount. SSBCI Loans to CDFIs: 0%-2% interest, up to 7-year term with annual renewal options, maximum $5,000,000 SSBCI funding per lender, maximum total financing $20,000,000. Individual small business loans from CDFIs: Up to $250,000-$350,000, maximum 18% interest, up to 5-year terms (longer for asset acquisition). Combined origination fee and points capped at 1%; application fee maximum $100-$250 and closing fee of $250. Requires flexible applicant cash contribution, personal guarantees, and collateral. Prepayment lockout period may apply. Proof of private capital match with target of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI/VSB or 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI/VSB required. Minimum required private capital to SSBCI funds match of 1:1. The Loan to Lender component provides loans to CDFIs ranging from $500,000 to $15,000,000 based on capacity for relending to small businesses combined with required private capital match. CDFIs must have 20% at risk. For non-SEDI businesses and those with 10 or more employees, goal of 4:1 private capital match. For SEDI businesses or those with fewer than 10 employees, targeted private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 2.3:1 (70-30). Applications processed on a first-come, first-served basis. The program provides loan participation funding through community lenders.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses operating in Maryland with fewer than 500 employees, particularly very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI), as well as Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) certified and in good standing seeking capital to relend to small businesses. Local governments are not eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses, machinery and equipment, working capital, relending to small businesses owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals and very small businesses, marketing, real estate down payments, equipment acquisition, business expansion costs, and other costs associated with sustaining or expanding a small business in manufacturing, service providers, retail, office or mixed-use sectors. Loans to eligible small businesses located in CDFI Investment Areas, rural communities, U.S. territories, communities undergoing economic transitions, and underserved communities.

Maryland-based small businesses. Statewide Maryland availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive federal Treasury-allocated loan program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development designed to assist small businesses, nonprofit organizations, and Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) with capital for working capital, owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, new construction, rehabilitation, expansion, and other business needs. The program operates through multiple complementary components: (1) Direct lending to small businesses and nonprofits with loans ranging from $350,000 to $5,000,000 with flexible repayment terms up to 30 years, (2) Loan-to-Lender component providing capital to CDFIs for relending to small businesses, particularly those owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI) and very small businesses (VSB) with fewer than 10 employees, with loan sizes ranging from $500,000 to $15,000,000 based on CDFI capacity, and (3) Loan Participation Program that works with community lending partners to provide financing to small businesses, including SEDI-owned enterprises. The program prioritizes very small businesses, SEDI-owned enterprises, projects in targeted geographic areas including Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, Opportunity Zones, Transit-Oriented Development areas, and BRNI Areas, and projects that strengthen community commercial districts, add or retain child care slots, provide fresh food access, or serve as seed investment in community revitalization. The program has been operating for over 20 years and currently manages 158 loans with over $20 million in outstanding principal balance with delinquency rates less than 1%. The program functions as a gap lender, typically serving as first money in or complementary financing. Works with banks, community development financial institutions (CDFIs), and mixed-use developers to provide financing options that help improve and revitalize existing commercial districts and town centers.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or junior debt loans for direct lending component ranging from $350,000 to $5,000,000 to small businesses and nonprofits with flexible repayment terms up to 30 years depending on use and loan amount. The Loan-to-Lender component provides loans to CDFIs with sizes ranging from $500,000 to $15,000,000 based on CDFI capacity for relending to small businesses with targeted loans up to $250,000-$350,000. The Loan Participation Program provides loan participation funding through community lenders. SSBCI portion supports up to 30% program match. Interest rates for SSBCI CDFI loans are 0%-2% with up to 7-year terms and annual renewal options. Interest rates for direct business lending are determined by underwriting analysis and market conditions. Applicants must provide cash contribution (target 10-20% depending on SEDI/VSB status, minimum 1:1 private to SSBCI match). Personal guarantees and collateral required. Fees include $250 application fee (maximum $100 for SSBCI), $250 closing fee, and 1% commitment fee. Combined origination fee and points capped at 1% for SSBCI. The CDA Loan Reserve provides up to $2,000,000 in reinsurance support and guarantees up to $3,000,000 in co-senior loans, while the non-CDA Loan Reserve provides up to $5,000,000 in top loss guarantees. DHCD provides up to $5,000,000 annually in subordinate loans and higher-risk financing. Prepayment lockout period may apply. Loans support working capital, owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, new construction, rehabilitation, expansion, machinery and equipment, and other costs associated with sustaining or expanding a small business or nonprofit project. CDFI lenders must combine loans with required private capital match. CDFIs must maintain 20% at risk. Maximum total financing $20,000,000 for SSBCI component. 34.46% of SSBCI funds must be expended on VSB and SEDI businesses combined. Small Business Loans (SBLs) made by lenders to businesses: maximum $250,000 (unless prior written approval), up to 18% interest, up to 5 years.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses with 500 or fewer employees (with priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals), nonprofit organizations seeking financing for commercial projects in targeted geographic areas, Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) seeking capital to relend to small businesses, Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI), and startups. Local governments are not eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, new construction, rehabilitation, expansion, mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses, machinery and equipment, working capital, real estate acquisition, leasehold improvements, nonprofit facility loans, market studies, planning or feasibility studies, business expansion costs, and other costs associated with opening, operating, sustaining or expanding a Maryland small business or nonprofit organization. For CDFIs, funds are used for relending to small businesses owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals, very small businesses, and businesses in CDFI Investment Areas. Funds support business growth and help improve and revitalize existing commercial districts and town centers.

Statewide Maryland eligibility.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can complete an initial consultation by filling out the Pre-Application Consultation Form and a member of the team will contact them. structured_extraction.program_description: The Neighborhood BusinessWorks program offers flexible financing to new or expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations for projects located in Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, Opportunity Zones, Transit-Oriented Development areas, or BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones. The program functions as a gap lender, typically serving as first money in or complementary financing. Eligible projects include acquisition, permanent financing, refinancing of commercial and mixed-use real estate, new construction, rehabilitation, expansion, machinery and equipment, working capital, leasehold improvements, and nonprofit facility loans. The program has been operating for over 20 years and currently manages 158 loans with over $20 million in outstanding principal balance with delinquency rates less than 1%.

A minimum 10% applicant cash contribution is required. The program provides senior or subordinate loans, or combinations of both. Bonds are issued to fund loans for business projects including acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed-use real estate, refinancing of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects, new construction, rehabilitation, expansion, machinery and equipment, working capital, real estate acquisition, leasehold improvements, and nonprofit facility loans. Fees include a $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% commitment fee. Personal guarantees and collateral are required. The CDA Loan Reserve provides up to $2,000,000 in reinsurance support, guarantees up to $3,000,000 in co-senior loans, while the non-CDA Loan Reserve provides up to $5,000,000 in top loss guarantees. DHCD provides up to $5,000,000 annually in subordinate loans and higher-risk financing.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas through capital construction projects. The program was funded through the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (Section 9901) via the U.S. Department of the Treasury to address economic consequences of COVID-19 pandemic by facilitating increased public investment in broadband infrastructure. The program provided funding between $50,000 and $500,000 to pay for 70% to 90% of capital construction costs, with a 10% to 30% match required. The program has now closed and is not accepting applications.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $50,000 and $500,000 paying for 70% to 90% of capital construction costs to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas. Cash or in-kind match of 10% to 30% required depending on household density. Either local jurisdiction or ISP may own the assets funded. Density determined by dividing households in service area by route miles. Funding provided on a reimbursement basis for actual, eligible capital project costs. Eligible uses include construction of facilities to deploy broadband service at minimum speeds of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum 50 milliseconds latency, middle-mile infrastructure directly necessary to provide service, electronics and equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless equipment, modems, equipment shelters), customer drops, customer premises equipment, outside plant infrastructure (fiber, coax, copper), and antennae. Match funds can support tower construction or improvements.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Partnership Rental Housing Program expands the supply of affordable rental housing for low-income households. It finances new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of rental housing through partnerships between state and local governments. The program also allows non-governmental entities to create housing for individuals with disabilities or special needs integrated within traditional rental housing developments. The program provides direct loans with deferred repayment for up to 40 years.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans for rental housing occupied by households with incomes at or below 50% of the statewide median income. Loan amounts are limited to $75,000 per unit for large projects and up to $2 million without a per unit cap for small projects (40 units or fewer). For individuals with disabilities or special needs units, eligible resident households must have gross income not exceeding 30% of the Area Median Income. Loan repayment is generally deferred for up to 40 years as long as the local government entity or borrower continues to own the housing and rents it to income-eligible households. Any profits from project sale must be used for other low-income housing purposes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project Creating Opportunities for Revitalization and Equity (Project C.O.R.E.) / Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative (BVRI)
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive multi-phase state program and partnership initiative between the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Maryland Stadium Authority, and Baltimore City designed to address vacant and blighted properties through demolition, deconstruction, stabilization, acquisition, and pre-development activities to catalyze neighborhood redevelopment, reinvestment, and stabilization in Baltimore City. Phase I focuses on demolishing city blocks of blight, with the state investing $75 million over four years plus $18.5 million from Baltimore City, with $50 million available in Fiscal Year 2025. The Maryland Stadium Authority serves as project manager responsible for site preparation including grading, seeding, and fencing. Baltimore City provides in-kind services valued at $0.25 for every $1 in state allocations. Phase II leverages an estimated $600 million through Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development programs to encourage new investment in revitalized communities. The program provides grant funding and loans to public and nonprofit partners for acquisition, stabilization, demolition and other pre-development activities, clearing the way for new green space, affordable housing and mixed-use developments. The program aims to improve economic opportunity and quality of life, support small business development and expansion, create jobs, increase green space, develop quality energy-efficient affordable housing for existing residents, and create safer neighborhoods. The initiative partners with local trade organizations, non-profit organizations, and state agencies to provide demolition opportunities, deconstruction work, redevelopment projects, training programs, and employment linkage services.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Project C.O.R.E. provides $75 million in state funding over four years, with $50 million available in Fiscal Year 2025, plus $18.5 million from Baltimore City for acquisition, demolition, deconstruction, stabilization, and redevelopment of blighted and vacant properties. Grant funding and loans are provided to public and nonprofit partners for pre-development activities. The Maryland Stadium Authority manages site preparation including grading, seeding, and fencing of demolished sites. Baltimore City provides in-kind services valued at $0.25 for every $1 in state allocations. FY17 awards ranged from $120,000 to $2,000,000 with total awards of $15,860,000 across 31 projects. The program includes workforce development and training programs, job placement services, and development opportunities for small businesses and affordable housing creation. Phase II leverages an estimated $600 million through Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development programs to encourage revitalization and new investment in redeveloped communities. Community relocation assistance is provided in accordance with the federal Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970. Funding supports redevelopment and stabilization projects including housing development, community facilities, vacant property rehabilitation, historic preservation, and park expansion.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Baltimore City Department of Housing identifies potential properties for demolition which are then reviewed by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development for final approval. First-time applicants should contact a regional project manager for eligibility determination. Application training available via webinar. Interested parties should monitor the Project C.O.R.E. website at dhcd.maryland.gov/projectcore for updates on opportunities, schedules, and participation options. structured_extraction.program_description: Project Restore provides financial support to Maryland's new or expanding businesses to help incentivize commercial investment in vacant retail and commercial properties. The program offers grants for businesses that plan on opening or expanding into previously vacant spaces, with assistance for rent payments and operating costs in their first year of operation to support business investment, job creation, and economic growth in Maryland communities.

The Business Operations Grant provides up to $250,000 per year for 1 or 2 years based on sales and use tax generated. Grant payments are made quarterly. Funds can be used for rent payments, staff costs, capital improvements, marketing, inventory and supplies, utilities and similar business operations, but cannot be used for executive salaries or bonuses.
