structured_extraction.program_description: A federal reimbursement program administered under the Other Needs Assistance (ONA) provision of the Individuals and Households Program (IHP) with 100 percent federal cost share that helps families and individuals pay for funeral expenses incurred for persons who died from COVID-19 or COVID-19-like symptoms. The program reimburses eligible expenses for deaths occurring after January 20, 2020, and requires documentation that COVID-19 or COVID-19-like symptoms caused or likely caused the death.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FEMA provides financial assistance for funeral services and interment or cremation expenses. Up to $9,000 per COVID-19 related funeral with up to $35,500 total ONA maximum award per fiscal year. FEMA reimburses eligible individuals for funeral expenses incurred after January 20, 2020, for a deceased person whose death was caused by or was likely a result of COVID-19 or COVID-19-like symptoms. Reimbursement covers eligible expenses including transportation to identify the deceased, transfer of remains, casket or urn, burial plot or cremation niche, marker or headstone, clergy or officiant services, funeral ceremony arrangement, funeral home equipment or staff use, cremation or interment costs, death certificate production and certification, and other expenses mandated by local or state government laws. Applicants must be U.S. citizens, legal residents, asylees, refugees, non-citizen nationals, or qualified aliens. Tribal members are eligible. FEMA will only award assistance once per deceased individual on a single application. Photocopied or scanned copies of death certificates are acceptable for the application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and households with COVID-19 related funeral expenses. U.S. citizens, non-citizen nationals, qualified aliens, refugees, asylees, and tribal members are eligible applicants. The deceased need not meet citizenship requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funeral services and interment or cremation expenses including transportation to identify the deceased, transfer of remains, casket or urn, burial plot or cremation niche, marker or headstone, clergy or officiant services, funeral ceremony arrangement, funeral home equipment or staff use, cremation or interment costs, death certificate production and certification, and expenses mandated by applicable local or state government laws or ordinances. Up to $9,000 per COVID-19 related funeral with up to $35,500 total Other Needs Assistance maximum award per fiscal year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the United States, including Maryland, U.S. territories and District of Columbia. Applicants must be in an area covered by a COVID-19 major disaster declaration with Individual Assistance. Deaths must have occurred in the state, territory, or tribe where declared. The program is administered nationally by FEMA.
requirements_list: Death certificate must indicate decedent died from COVID-19 or that COVID-19 was probable, presumed, suspected, or likely
Photocopied or scanned copy of death certificate is acceptable
Applicant or co-applicant must have incurred the funeral expenses
Applicant must be a U.S. citizen, legal resident, non-citizen national, qualified alien, asylee, or refugee
Funeral expenses must have been incurred after January 20, 2020

Cannot resubmit expenses already reimbursed through government agencies, voluntary agencies, non-profits, burial or funeral insurance, or life insurance policies (though life insurance reimbursement does not disqualify applicants from applying)
If applicant received outside assistance for certain funeral expenses, must document this assistance in the application
Tribal members are eligible applicants
Deaths must have occurred in the state, territory, or tribe where declared

If the death certificate does not list COVID-19 among the causes of death but COVID-19 is believed to be related, contact the medical certifier listed on the death certificate to request an amendment to the record
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the COVID-19 Funeral Assistance Line at 844-684-6333 (TTY: 800-462-7585) Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Central Time to begin the application process. Applicants must gather required documents including a copy of the death certificate indicating COVID-19 or COVID-19-like symptoms as the cause of death, and proof of funeral expenses incurred (such as receipts, funeral home contracts, or other documentation showing the applicant's name as the responsible person for the expense, the decedent's name, the amount of funeral expenses, and that expenses were incurred after January 20, 2020). If the death certificate does not list COVID-19 among the causes of death but COVID-19 is believed to be related, contact the medical certifier listed on the death certificate to request an amendment to the record. If multiple individuals contributed toward funeral expenses, they should register under a single application as applicant and co-applicant.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps low-income households pay off past-due natural gas bills (arrearages) to help them avoid utility service termination and reduce their debt. GARA provides grants to retire past-due gas balances with a minimum arrearage balance of $300 and maximum grant of $1,000. Households with vulnerable members (age 60 or older, under age 2, or medically fragile) may be eligible to receive the benefit again if the previously received benefit was less than $1,000 and the current past-due balance exceeds $300.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: GARA provides non-repayable grants to retire past-due gas balances. Minimum arrearage balance is $300. Maximum grant is $1,000 per household in a 5-year period. Households with vulnerable members (age 60 or older, under age 2, or medically fragile) may be eligible to receive the benefit again if the previously received benefit was less than $1,000 and the current past-due balance exceeds $300. Arrearage benefits can only be received once per five-year period for non-vulnerable households. The bill must be in the applicant's name.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing, applications accepted through the fiscal year

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of past-due natural gas utility bills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. Applications must be processed by the local office in the applicant's county to avoid delays.

Applications can be submitted online at MarylandBenefits.gov, by mail, through secure drop boxes at local offices, by telephone, or in-person. Local OHEP offices will automatically review completed applications to determine GARA eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Household Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to low-income households to help pay water and wastewater bills and prevent service shutoffs. Grants can be used to restore disconnected services, prevent disconnection, and pay arrearages and fees on water and wastewater accounts. Grants range from $100 to $2,000 and are based on household income, household size, and arrearage amount. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Human Services through local jurisdictions including Montgomery County, with applications processed first come, first served until funding is depleted.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct financial assistance paid to public water suppliers or wastewater treatment providers to help low-income households pay water and wastewater bills and prevent service disconnections. Grants range from $100 to $2,000 and are based on household income, household size, and arrearage amount (balance 30 or more days past due). Minimum arrearage of $100 is required to qualify. Benefits can pay toward arrearages, reconnection fees, and standard billing charges. Households may be categorically eligible if at least one member is receiving MEAP, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), SNAP, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), means-tested veterans benefits, or Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP). Applications are processed first come, first served in each local jurisdiction until funding is depleted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible renters, homeowners, and public housing residents in Maryland who have water and/or wastewater bills and are having difficulty paying or at risk of service disconnection.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water and wastewater utility bills, including restoration of services after disconnection, prevention of disconnection, arrearages (balance 30 or more days past due), reconnection fees, and standard billing fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Applications processed first come, first served in each local jurisdiction until funding is depleted.
requirements_list: Low-income household status
Must be a homeowner, renter, or public housing resident
Government-issued photo ID for identity verification
Social Security cards or federal government-issued documents (W-2, Social Security Benefits Notice) with name and Social Security number for all household members including children
Copy of water and/or wastewater utility bill or termination notice
Arrearage balance of at least $100 on account
Documentation of all household income for past 30 days (paystubs, Social Security award letters, pension statements, SNAP/TCA/TDAP award letters)
Proof of residence at service address
Proof of citizenship if applicable
Applicant must have at least one household member who is a legal resident with a Social Security number
Categorical eligibility available if household member receives MEAP, TCA, TDAP, SNAP, SSI, means-tested veterans benefits, or ERAP
Gross household income eligibility based on federal poverty guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications can be submitted online at mymdthink.maryland.gov or MyDHR, downloaded and mailed, dropped off in person at 1301 Piccard Drive, Suite 4200, Rockville, MD 20852, emailed to ohep@montgomerycountymd.gov, or faxed to 240-777-4099. Applications also available in English and Spanish. A phone appointment can be requested by calling 240-777-4450. Submit all documents with application for fastest processing. The office must review applications within 14 days of receiving a complete application and make a final determination within 45 days. Applicants can check application status at myohepstatus.org (allow 15 days for initial appearance), call the DHS call center at 1-800-332-6347, or contact the office directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state tax credit for working people with low to moderate income who qualify for the federal earned income tax credit. The Maryland credit equals 50% of the federal tax credit and reduces or eliminates state and local income tax owed. The program also provides free tax preparation and filing assistance for eligible Marylanders with income under $67,000 in 2024. Free tax preparation is available at certified sites by IRS-certified volunteers, or through free DIY tax software and Direct File tools. Tax refunds are provided via direct deposit and can be split into up to three separate bank accounts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For individuals who claim the federal earned income tax credit on their federal tax return, Maryland provides a state credit equal to 50% of the federal credit. The credit reduces or eliminates state and local income tax owed. IRS-certified volunteers prepare and electronically file taxes with direct deposit of refunds into bank accounts. Free DIY tax software is available at cashmd.org, and the Direct File tool is available for federal and state filing. Direct deposit refunds can be split into up to three separate bank accounts. Free tax preparation assistance is available through Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) programs and the CASH Campaign of Maryland at certified locations across Maryland.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-800-332-6347; IRS: 1-800-829-1040; Maryland Taxpayer Service: 1-800-638-2937; Tax Preparation: 800-492-0618
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and working individuals with income under $67,000 in 2024 who qualify for the federal earned income tax credit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces or eliminates state and local income tax liability for eligible working people. Tax refunds are provided via direct deposit and can be split into multiple accounts.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 800-492-0618 to locate the nearest tax preparation center. Visit cashmd.org for free DIY tax software or the Direct File tool. Individuals should first determine if they qualify for the federal EITC by using the IRS EITC Assistant or contacting the Internal Revenue Service at 1-800-829-1040. Those who qualify for the federal credit and claim it on their federal return can claim the Maryland EITC (50% of the federal credit) on their state tax return. IRS-certified volunteers will prepare and electronically file taxes with refunds deposited directly into bank accounts. For state credit information, contact Maryland Taxpayer Service at 1-800-638-2937.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide grant program that provides annual funding to non-profit and government-run feeding organizations to distribute emergency food assistance to individuals and families experiencing food insecurity throughout Maryland. Grants are allocated to all 24 Maryland jurisdictions based on available funding and demographic indicators of need such as population size, unemployment percentage, poverty rates, and SNAP recipients. Emergency food assistance is distributed through food banks, food pantries, soup kitchens, shelters, residential treatment programs, after-school programs, meal delivery programs, and weekend backpack programs at no charge to eligible individuals and families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are allocated to all 24 Maryland jurisdictions based on available funding and demographic indicators of need such as population size, unemployment percentage, and poverty rates. Maximum award: $50,000; Minimum award: $2,000. First-time grantees or those not receiving funding in the past 3 years are capped at $2,000. Total FY26 program allocation: $1,241,661. Emergency food assistance is provided to eligible individuals and families through contracted providers including food banks, food pantries, soup kitchens, shelters, residential treatment programs, after-school programs, meal delivery programs, and weekend backpack programs. Organizations distribute food at no charge to those in need. Funds may only be used for food purchases; prohibited expenses include cutlery, food storage containers, gift cards (unless food-only), paper products, and cleaning products. Locally-produced Maryland food and farmers market purchases are encouraged when feasible and cost-effective.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 5:00 PM on May 9, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and government-run feeding organizations and individuals and families experiencing food insecurity and emergency food needs, including disabled individuals, unemployed individuals, veterans, homeless individuals, seniors (60+), adults (18+), and children (0-17).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used only to purchase food for meals and/or groceries distributed at no cost to eligible individuals and families through food banks, food pantries, soup kitchens, shelters, residential treatment programs, after-school programs, meal delivery programs, and weekend backpack programs. Prohibited expenses include cutlery, food storage containers, gift cards (unless food-only), paper products, and cleaning products. Administrative costs and non-food expenses are prohibited. Locally-produced Maryland food and farmers market purchases are encouraged when feasible and cost-effective.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland jurisdictions are eligible. Funds are allocated to all jurisdictions using demographic factors including population size, unemployment, poverty rates, and SNAP recipients.

Operating for at least 3 years

Physical location providing related services such as community services, church outreach services, or housing services
Demonstration of community support through cash or food donations from outside entities

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) Energy Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: A year-round program administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services that helps low-income households and kinship caregivers pay their utility bills, heating fuel bills, and past due energy bills. OHEP provides grants and financial assistance to help customers afford electricity, gas, water, and other heating costs based on household income. The program also provides energy cost assistance through grants to repair or replace heating, cooling, and water heating systems at no cost, as well as limited assistance fixing broken furnaces. Work eligibility for system repairs is determined by a home assessment and funding availability. Residents do not need a turn-off notice to qualify for assistance. The program serves both general low-income households and informal kinship caregivers with children in their care. Specialists at local offices guide applicants through the energy assistance application process. Payments are made directly to fuel suppliers and utility companies on behalf of the customer. The program operates year-round and is federally funded. The program is currently placing applicants on a waitlist due to limited funding and high demand. Customers can receive benefits once per fiscal year (July-June). Arrearage Retirement Assistance provides grants up to $2,000 for past due electric bills and up to $1,000 for past due gas bills. Annual grants are also awarded to heating suppliers to assist with heating expenses for eligible households in participating counties. The Low-Income Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP) provides assistance with past due water and wastewater utility bills. Applications are available through local county Home Energy Program Offices and Washington County Community Action Council. Energy assistance will not reduce other public assistance benefits such as TCA or Food Stamps, nor will it reduce Social Security benefits. Grant amounts vary based on household income level and fuel type used. Income-based eligibility does not require a utility shut-off notice to qualify. Financial assistance is also provided to income-eligible households to help minimize energy-related crises and make utility, heating, and cooling expenses more affordable. The program includes the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) component, which provides one-time heating assistance grants to low-income households to help pay heating costs during the heating season, with grant amounts based on the type of fuel used, household income, and geographic location within the state. Direct grants are paid to gas companies or landlords to help pay heating bills, with each household receiving one benefit per program year. The program also includes the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) for electric bill assistance, the Critical Medical Needs Program, Utility Service Protection Program (USPP), and weatherization and home energy efficiency services.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Program provides utility grants and financial assistance to help eligible households pay their electric, gas, water, and heating fuel bills and prevent service shut-offs. Payments are made directly to fuel suppliers and utility companies on behalf of the customer. The program also provides grants and financial assistance to repair or replace heating, cooling, and water heating systems at no cost, with maximum funding of $50,000 for repair programs, and limited assistance fixing broken furnaces. Work eligibility for system repairs is determined by a home assessment and funding availability. Annual grants are awarded to heating suppliers to assist with heating expenses. Direct utility bill assistance is provided to qualifying low-income households and kinship caregivers. The Low-Income Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP) provides assistance with past due water and wastewater utility bills. Grants are determined based on household income and other factors. Customers can receive benefits once per fiscal year (July-June). Arrearage Retirement Assistance provides grants up to $2,000 for past due electric bills and Gas Arrearage Retirement Assistance (GARA) provides grants up to $1,000 for past due gas bills if the past due amount is $300 or greater. Customers may only receive an arrearage grant once every five years, with certain exceptions for grants received between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021. Residents do not need a turn-off notice to qualify. Energy assistance will not reduce other public assistance benefits such as TCA or Food Stamps, nor will it reduce Social Security benefits. Non-repayable grants help pay heating and electric bills. Grant amounts vary based on household income level and fuel type used. Program is administered through local county-based Home Energy Program Offices across Maryland. Home energy assistance is also provided to eligible informal kinship caregivers and children in their care. Applications are accepted year-round and can be submitted at any time during the year. One-time heating assistance grants are sent to heating suppliers per heating season based on fuel type, household income, and geographic location. If heat is included in rent, landlord may receive grant on behalf of household and deduct from rent owed. Grant covers part of heating costs only. Direct grant paid to gas companies, electric utilities, landlords, or directly to residents to help pay heating and electric bills, with benefits may also helping with past due bills and emergency assistance for those at risk of utility shut off. Eligible customers may be placed on budget billing plans to spread out annual utility bills into even monthly payments. Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) provides electric bill assistance grants with amounts determined by household income and electric use over the past 12 months; participants must enroll in budget billing with their utility company. Crisis season benefits available November 1 through March 31 for households with energy crises. Direct payments may be made to landlords to reduce tenant rent or utility charges for heating and electric costs included in rent or sub-metered billing; landlord must credit full benefit amount to tenant's account and cannot use benefits for security deposits or dwelling damage costs. Weatherization and home energy improvements are provided to eligible households. Energy efficiency improvements and installations are provided. Critical home repairs including structural, electrical, water leaks, lead, and asbestos remediation are funded with maximum repair program funding of $50,000. Eligibility is based on gross household income in the last 30 days. Each household can receive one benefit per program year (July 1 to June 30). Program provides energy usage data analysis and personalized energy savings estimates. Installation of energy-saving measures provided. Initial deposit maximum is 33% of total project cost.

Applications for heating assistance accepted between July - May each year in participating counties. Applications accepted year-round; you can apply at any time during the year. Crisis season: November 1 - March 31. FY2026 program year runs July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income and limited-income homeowners, renters, boarders, roomers, kinship caregivers, residents of public housing, sub-metered homes residents, and hard-working families in Maryland needing assistance with home repairs and utility bill payments. Eligible Maryland homeowners and residents with household income below 200% of the federal poverty level or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level based on last 30 days of income who have a non-functioning heating, cooling, and/or water heating system, or who need assistance paying home heating, electricity, water, and other utility bills. Home heating utility bills, including past due bills. Weatherization and home energy improvements. Utility bill payment assistance. Assistance helps prevent service disconnection. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov, https://mymdthink.maryland.gov/home/#/, https://myohepstatus.mymdthink.maryland.gov/, or MyDHR (http://mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us/), by mail, by phone, in-person at a local office, or by submitting a paper application to a secure drop box. Phone appointments can be requested by calling 240-777-4450, 1-800-332-6347, or 1-800-352-1446 to request a paper application. Baltimore City residents should drop applications at the nearest CAP Center. For Prince George's County, apply by email to pgcdss.energy@maryland.gov with completed application and supporting documentation, by mail/fax to Prince George's County Department of Social Services, Office of Home Energy Programs, 805 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785 (Fax: 301-909-6331), or in-person at 425 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785. Baltimore County applicants can apply at a District Office. St. Mary's County applications are available at all senior activity centers and are accepted between July and May each year through the Tri-County Community Action Committee. Frederick County: applications can be completed online at the Maryland OHEP status portal, printed from the Maryland Department of Human Services website, submitted as a PDF by email to ohep@cityoffrederickmd.gov, or dropped off in person. Paper applications can be mailed to PO Box 3929 Frederick, MD 21705. For Montgomery County, applications can be completed online at MyDHR, downloaded, or picked up in person. Submit completed applications by mail, in-person drop-off, email to ohep@montgomerycountymd.gov, or fax to the Office of Home Energy Programs at 1301 Piccard Drive, 4th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. Applicants can visit one of three walk-in centers in Silver Spring, Rockville, or Germantown. If at risk of shut off, call 240-777-4450 for emergency assistance. For Washington County, apply online at https://www.wccac.org/our-services/energy-assistance or schedule an appointment by visiting or calling the Washington County Community Action Council at 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740, (301) 797-4161. Contact the Community Action Agency's 24/7 hotline for more information. Documents can be submitted as clear photos with visible text or scanned copies. Kinship caregivers can submit an online application at Maryland Benefits website, apply in-person at local Department of Social Services, apply by phone at 1-833-373-5867, or request an application be mailed by calling local Department of Social Services. Applicants download and complete the Energy Assistance application form (DHS-FIA-9780-OHEP), gather required documents, and submit via their chosen method. Applications are processed on a rolling basis throughout the year. Dedicated specialists guide applicants through the process and at each office guide applicants through the energy assistance application process. Status of applications can be checked online at myohepstatus.maryland.gov or myohepstatus.org or by contacting the office. Submit completed application to local Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) office. Application is received, approved, and processed. Grant is then sent to heating supplier, electric company, or utility. Processing typically takes 45 days. For repair programs, once your household is determined eligible, a local agency will contact you to schedule a home assessment. The local agency will evaluate your service needs and determine how the program can increase your home's comfort. After discussing the assessment results, a contractor will be scheduled to complete the recommended work. Applicant qualifies for funding sources, receives letter with assigned contractor or financial assistance applied to utility bills. After assessment, contractor completes recommended work at no cost within 30 days. For crisis season assistance, submit DHS FIA 805 Crisis Season Declaration Form during November 1 - March 31 period. Proxy authorization available for applicants unable to apply in person using DHS-FIA-811 form; applicant must provide income documentation and proxy must be 18 years or older. Applicants with safety concerns may use DHS-FIA-804 Concern for Personal Safety/Privacy Form with third-party verification from authorized representatives (domestic violence service providers, legal representatives, medical professionals, law enforcement, or acquaintances). Landlords receiving payments must complete DHS-FIA-809 Landlord Agreement to credit full benefit to tenant account. Navigator signs confidentiality certification to gain access to applicant information for processing Critical Medical Needs Program applications. If you are currently approved to receive Energy Assistance payments from the Maryland Department of Human Services, you may contact the intake line at 1-855-583-8976. Submit complete application with required documentation to local DHS office. Energy usage data analysis and personalized energy savings estimates provided. For repair programs, submit application and documentation; home assessment will be scheduled; contractor bid reviewed; work completed at no cost within 30 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland SUN Bucks helps families with school-aged children buy groceries during the summer months when school is not in session. The program provides $120 per eligible child ($40 for June, July, and August) to support food and nutrition needs during the summer break when children lose access to free and reduced-price meals they receive during the school year. Benefits are issued in the last week of each month and loaded onto an Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card. Most eligible families are automatically enrolled with no action required; others can apply online or by paper application. The program implements the federal Summer EBT Program and builds on Maryland's existing Summer SNAP program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families receive $40 for each month (June, July, and August) for a total of $120 per eligible school-aged child. For families already receiving SNAP benefits, Maryland SUN Bucks is automatically applied to the head-of-household's Independence Card. If a child does not receive SNAP, a white Maryland SUN Bucks card is issued. Benefits are issued in the last week of each month and loaded onto an Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card. Benefits can be used to purchase food at stores and vendors that accept EBT, including most grocery stores, some farmers' markets, and some online retailers. Benefits expire 122 days after issuance. Benefits cannot be used for alcohol, cigarettes, tobacco, pet food, household supplies, vitamins, medicines, or prepared hot food.

Also includes children in Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) schools, Head Start-enrolled children, and children of migrant workers.

Benefits must be used for healthy, nutritious food including fruits, vegetables, meats, protein sources, whole grains, dairy, and other food products. Cannot be used for alcohol, cigarettes, tobacco, pet food, household supplies, vitamins, medicines, or prepared hot food.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Most eligible families (over 90%) receive benefits automatically if they meet eligibility criteria with no action required. Children not automatically enrolled can apply online at marylandbenefits.gov, submit a paper application, or apply in person at a local Department of Social Services office. structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program designed to help Maryland residents who live in nursing homes or require long-term care services pay for the cost of nursing home care, long-term care facility costs, waiver services, and other Medicaid-eligible medical services (including doctor, hospital, and other care) if they meet the program's financial, technical, and medical criteria. The program provides state and federal Medicaid funds to cover these costs for eligible low-income individuals and includes a review of resources from the five years prior to application to determine eligibility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State and federal Medicaid funds to cover the cost of nursing home care, long-term care facility costs, waiver services, and other Medicaid-eligible medical services including doctor and hospital care for eligible low-income individuals. The program reviews the applicant's resources from five years prior to application to determine eligibility. Applicants may be required to pay a portion of their income to the nursing home or care facility as determined by the program. No fees or payments are required to apply for or receive this program. Income and asset limits apply based on family size and program category. Covers medical bills incurred in the past 3 months and may include medical services provided in nursing facilities, state institutions, or community-based care providers. Some services such as dentistry, audiology, and vision may not be covered.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland residents who live in or require nursing home care or long-term care services, including those in nursing facilities, state institutions, or community-based care providers, and who meet program eligibility requirements, including financial, technical, and medical criteria. Includes U.S. citizens, lawfully admitted immigrants, veterans, and disabled widow(er)s and children of deceased veterans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nursing home care and long-term care facility costs, waiver services, doctor services, hospital services, medical bills incurred in the past 3 months, health insurance premiums including Medicare and other coverage, and other Medicaid-eligible medical care expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. The Office of Long Term Care (746 Frederick Road, Catonsville, Maryland 21228) serves applications from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County. Montgomery County is administered by the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services. Applications statewide can be filed online at https://marylandbenefits.gov or by mail to local health departments or local departments of social services. In- and out-of-state real property ownership is considered.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://marylandbenefits.gov or mail the application to your local health department or local department of social services. For Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County, mail to the Office of Long Term Care, 746 Frederick Road, Catonsville, Maryland 21228. For Montgomery County, call 240-777-3995 to request an application packet, pick up the packet in person at 401 Hungerford Drive, 4th floor, Rockville, Maryland 20850, mail or deliver the completed packet in person, or fax it to 240-777-1330. Submit completed DHS FIA 9709 form (or DHS FIA 9709R for redetermination) with supporting documentation including copies (not originals) of required financial documents. Provide proof of all income, assets, transfers, medical expenses, real property, and insurance. Submit tax returns for the last 5 years and other documentation available. Provide current statements for income and resources. Include Medicare/insurance cards and premium amounts. Applicant or authorized representative completes application with accurate financial and personal information and signs a declaration under penalty of perjury. Applicants are encouraged to apply promptly even if documentation is incomplete; additional documents may be requested and additional time provided to supply missing items. Department verifies information through Social Security number, employer contacts, banks, and local, state, and federal agencies. An authorized representative may file on behalf of applicant. Right to appeal or request hearing within 90 days of notice. Failure to complete redetermination results in cancellation of coverage.

structured_extraction.program_description: A joint state and federal program that provides comprehensive health insurance coverage to aged, blind, disabled, and low-income individuals and families. It is administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services using federal and state funds to cover medical expenses for eligible applicants. Coverage includes doctor visits, hospitalization, prescription medications, laboratory services, emergency dental, family planning, transportation to providers, home health services, physical therapy, personal care services, and Medicare premiums. Retroactive coverage for 3 months prior to application may be available if outstanding medical expenses exist, and a spend-down option is available for those exceeding income limits. Applicants can apply throughout the year at the Maryland Health Connection website, Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal, or in person at one of DHS's 24 local departments of social services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State and federal funds to pay medical bills and healthcare expenses for needy and low-income individuals. Eligible applicants have their medical bills, doctor visits, hospitalization, prescription medications, laboratory services, emergency dental, family planning, transportation to providers, home health services, physical therapy, personal care services, and Medicare premiums covered by the state Medicaid program. Retroactive coverage for up to 3 months prior to application may be available if outstanding medical expenses exist. A spend-down option is available for those exceeding income limits. Applications accepted year-round through Maryland Health Connection website, Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal, or in person at local departments of social services.

Children up to age 19 (MCHP), lawfully present immigrants (with some exceptions). All must be US citizens or meet alien status requirements and be Maryland residents.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at Maryland Health Connection (https://www.marylandhealthconnection.gov/how-to-enroll/medicaid/) for individuals under age 65, at Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal (https://marylandbenefits.gov) for individuals age 65 and older, disabled, or receiving Medicare, by phone, in person at one of DHS's 24 local departments of social services or District Office, or via mobile app (Enroll MHC). Free in-person assistance available. Processing typically takes 30 days; 7 days for expedited food supplement; 90+ days if disability determination required.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to protect low-income Medicare beneficiaries from the high costs of Medicare coverage by paying for out-of-pocket expenses like deductibles, co-payments, and Medicare Part B premiums. The program has two components: QMB (Qualified Medicare Beneficiary) which pays Medicare Part B premiums and cost-sharing amounts for those with income not exceeding 100% of federal poverty level, and SLMB (Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary) which pays Part B premiums for those with income between 100% and 120% of federal poverty level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: QMB Program: State Medicaid program pays Medicare Part B premiums and cost-sharing amounts (deductibles and co-payments) for individuals with modest assets (up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple) and combined income not exceeding 100% of federal poverty level. SLMB Program: Pays only the Part B premium for individuals with incomes between 100% and 120% of federal poverty level and assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Medicare beneficiaries in Maryland who meet asset and income limits and qualify for either QMB or SLMB assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medicare Part B premiums and out-of-pocket cost-sharing expenses including deductibles and copayments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Medicare beneficiary status
QMB: Combined income not over 100% of federal poverty level with modest assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple
SLMB: Income between 100% and 120% of federal poverty level with assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple
Must be a Medicare beneficiary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the QMB/SLMB application form and submit online at marylandbenefits.gov or in person to your local health department or local department of social services. Application form available for download.

structured_extraction.program_description: Re-Engaging Individuals through Successful Employment (RISE) is a program that helps unemployed and underemployed noncustodial parents (individuals owing child support) in the Mid-Shore Region secure and maintain unsubsidized, competitive employment through training, placement services, and support to remove barriers to employment. The program offers no-cost employment training and placement services, including hard skills training in in-demand industries such as healthcare, construction, welding, hospitality, warehousing, and biotechnology. Specific training programs include forklift training, flagger certification, ServSafe, HVAC, security training, commercial driver's license (CDL), bartending, and welding. Services also include soft skills training, job readiness, job search and placement, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, resolution of barriers to employment such as criminal record or suspended driver's license, and access to items needed for work such as clothing, tools, or textbooks. A personal career navigator and success coach provides ongoing support to help participants establish a pattern of regular child support payments.

structured_extraction.program_description: A supplemental employment services program for non-custodial parents owing child support that assists in obtaining and maintaining unsubsidized, competitive employment to establish a pattern of regular child support payments. The program uses a broad scope of resources to overcome barriers to employment and increase the likelihood that parents will be able to provide for themselves and their families. The program offers one-time financial support to help participants pay for identification, work boots, glasses, uniforms, interview attire, and transportation costs in connection with traveling to and from job interviews. Case managers work with participants to remove barriers to employment by potentially expunging criminal records or in other ways mitigating the negative impact of previous conduct. Training initiatives include GED and Driver Improvement courses, regional flagger certifications, work experience offerings for immediate employment, and CDL courses to advance employment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps noncustodial parents reduce or eliminate child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland by rewarding consistent on-time payments. Parents who pay as ordered for 12 consecutive months receive a 50% reduction in state arrears, and those who pay for 24 consecutive months have their state arrears reduced to zero. The program considers uninterrupted court-ordered payments made before joining and provides consideration for periods of unemployment due to seasonal work and no-fault job termination. Arrears owed directly to the family are not reduced.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Arrears reduction: 50% reduction of state arrears after 12 consecutive months of on-time payments, or full elimination of state arrears after 24 consecutive months of on-time payments. Credit is given for uninterrupted court-ordered payments made immediately before joining the program. Consideration is given for periods of unemployment due to seasonal work and no-fault job termination. Eligible parents must have income less than 225% of the Federal Poverty Level. Arrears owed directly to the family are not reduced.

This policy applies to the certification and licensure status of all Maryland prehospital providers (EMR, EMT-B, CRT, Paramedic and EMD) who are deployed or activated under military orders in the service of the United States Armed Forces. This also includes any reservist called to extended duty. Provides military EMS clinician status enabling service members to return to their established level of certification and function within one year of return to Maryland without jeopardizing their rights and privileges.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project Home, also known as the Certified Adult Residential Environment (C.A.R.E.) Program, is a supportive housing program for persons with mental illness or other disabilities. It offers an adult foster family model of care that provides a stable, family-like living arrangement in the community. Providers offer care in their own homes to one to four residents who have a disability. The program provides housing to adults who need supervision and assistance with activities of daily living and who are unable to live by themselves. It provides a more home-like and less costly alternative to nursing homes, psychiatric hospitals, and other institutional settings. Residents are provided with opportunities for growth, stimulation and change in the least restrictive environment. Case management services link each resident with appropriate community activities and supports.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Providers receive reimbursement for care based on resident's needs and level of care system; reimbursements are not taxable income. Providers are reimbursed at set rates for room, board, supervision and assistance. Most residents receive financial assistance through Public Assistance to Adults and Medical Assistance programs. Residents living in the program receive room, board, assistance with activities of daily living, recreational and social activities, medication supervision, and assistance with transportation to medical appointments. Residents contribute to cost of care.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provider reimbursement for resident care based on level of care needs, including room, board, assistance with activities of daily living, recreational and social activities, medication supervision, and assistance with transportation to medical appointments.

structured_extraction.program_description: PA2E is a workforce development program administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services that helps public assistance recipients and DHS customers start and expand their small businesses through free training and technical assistance. The program provides approximately 6 weeks of entrepreneurship training consisting of 8 comprehensive courses covering business fundamentals, business basics, marketing, financial planning, business plan development, social media engagement, and applying for business loans. Courses are held 1-2 times per week for approximately two hours each and are delivered through partnerships with Small Business Development Centers across Maryland. Training is available in virtual and/or classroom settings, offered in Spring and Fall cycles. Participants receive workforce development training credit, peer learning in a group setting, ongoing consulting and professional development support, and access to SBDC business consultants. The program helps eligible individuals transition from public assistance to self-employment by providing support for starting and growing their own businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides approximately 6 weeks of free business training consisting of 8 comprehensive courses, held 1-2 times per week for approximately two hours each. Classes cover business fundamentals, business basics, marketing, financial planning, business plan development, social media engagement, and applying for business loans. Training is delivered through the Small Business Development Center in virtual and/or classroom settings. Courses are offered in Spring and Fall cycles. Participants must attend all sessions and receive workforce development training credit, peer learning in a group setting, ongoing consulting and professional development support, and access to SBDC business consultants.
