structured_extraction.program_audience: Public assistance recipients and Department of Human Services customers, including individuals receiving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, Temporary Cash Assistance, non-custodial parents, foster youth, and veterans seeking to start or expand a small business.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business development, expansion, training, consulting, planning, and education to support business startup, self-employment, and entrepreneurship
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Departments of Social Services and partnerships with regional Small Business Development Centers. Currently offered in 12 jurisdictions, with programs emphasized in the Eastern Shore, Western Maryland, and Central Maryland regions including Frederick, Washington, Allegany, Somerset, Wicomico, Worcester, Dorchester, Caroline, Talbot, Kent, Queen Anne's, and Howard Counties.
requirements_list: Must be receiving or eligible for public assistance (SNAP, Temporary Cash Assistance, or other DHS assistance)
Must be a recipient of public assistance or a Department of Human Services customer
Must attend all eight business classes
Must have interest in starting a business or pursuing self-employment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can contact the family investment specialists, the Department of Social Services at their local county office, or the program directly to enroll in upcoming business training classes. Applicants may complete an online form through the application link. Classes are held in Spring and Fall cycles and are available in virtual and classroom formats. Marylanders receiving assistance from their local Department of Social Services can learn more and apply by visiting dhs.maryland.gov/PA2E or by calling 240-420-2507, 240-420-2559, or 1-800-332-6347.

structured_extraction.program_name: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB) Program / Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB) Program / Medicare Buy-In Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicare Savings Program that helps protect low-income Medicare beneficiaries from the costs of Medicare coverage, including premiums and out-of-pocket expenses. The program includes three components: QMB (Qualified Medicare Beneficiary) which pays full monthly Medicare premiums, co-payments, and deductibles for individuals with incomes up to 100% of federal poverty level; SLMB (Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary) which pays only the monthly Medicare Part B premium for those with incomes between 100 and 120% of poverty; and the Medicare Buy-In Program. If you qualify for QMB, you will receive a gray and white QMB card. If you qualify for SLMB, you will receive a notification letter.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: QMB covers full monthly Medicare premiums, Medicare co-payments, and deductibles for individuals with modest assets (up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple) and combined incomes not exceeding 100% of federal poverty level; recipients receive a gray and white QMB card. SLMB covers only the monthly Medicare Part B premium for those with incomes between 100 and 120% of poverty and similar asset limits; recipients receive a notification letter. Income and assets must be below the program's limits to qualify.
structured_extraction.contact_name: State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) Coordinator
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual Medicare beneficiaries or married couples who are U.S. citizens or lawfully admitted aliens and Maryland residents, eligible for Medicare Part A and Part B and meet asset and income limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medicare Part A and Part B premiums, Medicare co-payments, and Medicare deductibles (QMB); Medicare Part B premiums (SLMB).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents only. All 24 Maryland counties and Baltimore City are eligible. Apply through your local department of social services, health departments, or county State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) coordinator.
requirements_list: Must be a Medicare beneficiary or have applied for Medicare benefits
Must be a U.S. citizen or lawfully admitted alien with proof of immigration status
Must be a Maryland resident
Must be eligible for Medicare Part A and Part B
For QMB: Assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple; combined income not exceeding 100% of federal poverty level
For SLMB: Assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple; income between 100 and 120% of poverty
Income and assets must be below program limits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the QMB/SLMB/Medicare Buy-In application form and submit to your local health department, local department of social services, or county State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) coordinator. You can also apply in person, by mail, or online at marylandbenefits.gov. When you apply, the agency figures out which program you qualify for.

structured_extraction.program_description: Employment assistance programs designed to help refugees achieve economic self-sufficiency soon after arrival in the U.S. Services include job readiness training, resume writing, case management, job search assistance, vocational training, interview preparation, transportation assistance, interpretation during interviews, and post-placement support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employment assistance programs provide job readiness training, resume writing, case management to address employment barriers, job search assistance, vocational training, interview preparation, transportation assistance, interpretation services during interviews, and post-placement support. Services are provided through a network of grantee organizations in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area, Suburban Washington Area, and Frederick Area.
structured_extraction.contact_name: International Rescue Committee (IRC) Baltimore, Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area (LSSNCA), Ethiopian Community Development Council (ECDC)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees and asylees who are employable and seeking to achieve economic self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment services including job readiness training, resume writing, case management, job search assistance, vocational training, interview preparation, transportation assistance, interpretation services, and post-placement support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services available in Baltimore Metropolitan Area (including Baltimore City), Suburban Washington Area (Montgomery County area including Silver Spring and Greenbelt), and Frederick Area (Frederick County).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can enroll in employment programs at provider locations in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area, Suburban Washington Area, or Frederick Area. Contact information is provided for each location to register for services.

structured_extraction.program_description: RFEP addresses childcare barriers for refugee parents attending English language and occupational courses by providing simultaneous programming for young children ages 0-5 and their parents, including English classes and tutoring, childhood enrichment courses and playgroups, and support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Programming provided simultaneously for young children ages 0-5 and their parents, including English classes and tutoring, childhood enrichment courses and playgroups, and support services to address childcare barriers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible refugee parents and their children ages 0-5
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: English language instruction, childcare, tutoring, childhood enrichment activities, playgroups, and support services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Eligible parents and children must be ORR-eligible refugees
Children must be ages 0-5
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Solutions in Hometown Connections for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Health education and wellness services for eligible refugee clients. Provides opportunities to increase health literacy, coordinate and support navigation of health care, and organize wellness groups including mental wellness and peer support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Health education and wellness services including opportunities to increase health literacy, coordinate and support navigation of health care, and wellness groups for mental wellness and peer support. Services are provided in coordination with medical screenings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible refugee and asylee clients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health education services, health literacy support, health care navigation, and wellness groups.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through partnership with Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health.
requirements_list: Must be an eligible refugee or asylee client
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Clients interested in Refugee Health Promotion Program services may inquire during their medical screening appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Short-term medical coverage for refugee populations who are ineligible for Medicaid. Provides similar benefits to Medicaid for eligible refugees, asylees, humanitarian parolees, and victims of trafficking for up to 12 months after arrival in the U.S. or grant of asylum.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medical coverage providing access to healthcare services similar to Medicaid benefits. Available for 12 months after arrival in the U.S. or the grant of asylum, eligible humanitarian parole status, or victim of trafficking certification. Individuals under age 65 with no disabilities must first complete Medicaid application through Maryland Health Connection and be screened ineligible before applying for RMA through the MarylandBenefits portal.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees, asylees, individuals with eligible humanitarian parole status, and victims of trafficking who are ineligible for Medicaid.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical coverage for healthcare services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a refugee, asylee, individual with eligible humanitarian parole status, or victim of trafficking
Must be ineligible for Medicaid
Individuals under age 65 with no disabilities must complete Medicaid application requirements and be screened ineligible for MA through Maryland Health Connection before applying for RMA
Eligible for coverage for 12 months after arrival in the U.S. or grant of asylum, eligible humanitarian parole status, or victim of trafficking certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Means-tested individuals (those under age 65 with no disabilities) must first complete Medicaid application requirements to be screened for Medicaid eligibility through Maryland Health Connection. Upon being screened ineligible and over-scale income for Medicaid, clients may apply for RMA through the MarylandBenefits portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: Health assessment program providing comprehensive physical and mental health screenings for newly arrived refugees, asylees, parolees, and other eligible immigrants. Includes immunizations required for school enrollment and referrals to primary care physicians for preventive health and ongoing care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Comprehensive health assessment exams for newly arrived refugees and asylees. Screening appointments determine if new arrivals have medical conditions needing immediate attention. Services include physical and mental health screening, immunizations for school enrollment, and referrals to primary care physicians for preventive health and ongoing care. Goals include initiating health assessment within 90 days of U.S. arrival and completing within 180 days, preventing and controlling communicable diseases, and protecting public health.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Newly arrived refugees, asylees, parolees, and other eligible immigrants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health assessment exams, immunizations, and referrals to primary care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services available in Baltimore Metropolitan Area (Baltimore City and Baltimore County) through Baltimore Medical Systems, and in Suburban Washington Area (Montgomery and Prince George's Counties) through CCI Health Services.
requirements_list: Must be a newly arrived refugee, asylee, parolee, or eligible immigrant
Resettlement agencies are responsible for ensuring newly arrived refugees receive physical and mental health screening upon arrival
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals meeting eligibility requirements may visit their local Health Department and inquire about an initial health screening. Federally-qualified health clinics providing services are located in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area and Suburban Washington Area.

structured_extraction.program_description: RSIG supports school-aged refugee youth ages 0-18 to achieve academic success and provides support for public school systems to serve refugee populations. The program ensures students have access to academic support outside the classroom, parents are engaged in their children's education, and school personnel have cultural competence to address refugee needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support school-aged refugee youth through academic support outside the classroom, parent engagement in school activities, and cultural competency training for school personnel to provide effective, culturally-responsive education.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School-aged refugee youth ages 0-18 and public school systems serving refugee populations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic support outside the classroom, parent engagement programs, and professional development for school staff on cultural competency for refugee students
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; administered through International Rescue Committee offices in Silver Spring and Baltimore, and Baltimore City Community College
requirements_list: Youth must be school-aged, ages 0-18
Youth must be ORR-eligible refugees
School systems must be serving refugee populations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact International Rescue Committee Silver Spring, International Rescue Committee Baltimore, or Baltimore City Community College for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-administered and federally-funded temporary financial assistance program that provides cash support to eligible refugees and asylees until they can secure employment and become economically independent.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Temporary financial assistance provided as cash support to help refugees and asylees maintain basic living expenses while they work toward employment and economic independence. Benefits are available for up to 4 months after arrival to the United States or after an asylum grant, provided the recipient meets income eligibility guidelines and is not eligible for other cash assistance programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible refugees and asylees who have held documented immigration status in the United States for less than 4 months after arrival or after an asylum grant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary financial assistance to help clients maintain basic living expenses while securing employment and becoming economically independent.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Individuals in all Maryland counties may access Refugee Cash Assistance statewide through designated resettlement agencies, either remotely or in-person. Services are available through agencies in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area, Suburban Washington Area, and Frederick Area.
requirements_list: Have held an eligible and documented immigration status in the United States less than 4 months after arrival or after an asylum grant
Are ineligible for other cash assistance programs including TANF (Maryland TCA program for families with dependent children), SSI, OAA, AB, APTD, and AABD
Are not full-time students in institutions of higher education
Meet income eligibility guidelines
Must complete all required paperwork to be enrolled in RCA or RTCA, including providing proof of eligible immigration status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact one of the designated resettlement agencies serving their geographic area (Baltimore Metropolitan Area, Suburban Washington Area, or Frederick Area) to determine eligibility and apply for benefits. MORA administers the program in partnership with local resettlement agencies. Individuals can contact MORA for any difficulties accessing benefits.

structured_extraction.program_description: RYMP promotes positive civic and social engagement and supports academic and vocational achievement of refugee youth ages 15-24. The program provides grant funding to support academic achievement, vocational and career advancement, and social inclusion by matching eligible youth with mentors who provide personalized guidance, support, and nurturing to facilitate social integration and economic self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided to local resettlement agencies to support mentorship programs for refugee youth. Mentors provide personalized guidance and support to facilitate academic achievement, vocational advancement, social inclusion, and economic self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugee youth ages 15-24
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mentorship support services focused on academic achievement, vocational and career advancement, and social inclusion
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; administered through Ethiopian Community Development Council, International Rescue Committee Baltimore, International Rescue Committee Silver Spring, and Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area
requirements_list: Youth must be ages 15-24
Youth must be ORR-eligible refugees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Ethiopian Community Development Council, International Rescue Committee Baltimore, International Rescue Committee Silver Spring, or Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Respite Care Program provides financial reimbursement for short-term temporary care of children and adults with developmental or functional disabilities. This assistance gives family caregivers a period of rest and renewal by temporarily relieving them of caregiving responsibilities. Respite care is provided at planned intervals, during times of crisis, or on an as-needed basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement for short-term temporary care of children and adults with developmental or functional disabilities. Care is provided at planned intervals, in times of crisis, or on an as-needed basis to temporarily relieve family caregivers of caregiving responsibilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers of children and adults with developmental or functional disabilities. An informal family caregiver is an individual who routinely cares for someone with a developmental or functional disability and is not compensated for that care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Short-term temporary care of individuals with developmental or functional disabilities to provide relief and renewal for family caregivers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Department of Social Services offices.
requirements_list: Be an informal family caregiver (routinely care for an individual with developmental or functional disability without compensation)
Care for a child or adult with developmental or functional disabilities
Care must be provided at planned intervals, in times of crisis, or on an as-needed basis
Applicant must be an informal family caregiver (not compensated for care)
Individual receiving care must have a developmental or functional disability
Caregiver must routinely care for the individual with a disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Department of Social Services office to speak with a caseworker who will assist with understanding unique needs, next steps, eligibility determination, and the application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Responsible Parents Employment Network (RPEN) in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.program_description: An employment support program for noncustodial parents designed to engage, empower, and support them in obtaining and maintaining unsubsidized, competitive employment to help them secure jobs, increase their ability to pay child support, and establish a pattern of regular child support payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides employment training and support services to help noncustodial parents obtain and maintain unsubsidized, competitive employment, secure job placement assistance, and increase their capacity to meet child support obligations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment training and job placement services to help parents secure work and meet child support obligations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County only
requirements_list: Be a noncustodial parent
Be unemployed or underemployed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals should contact the Young Father's Coordinator for enrollment and participation details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Restaurant Meals Program allows eligible SNAP recipients to use their SNAP benefits to purchase prepared and hot food from participating restaurants and delis. SNAP recipients who are elderly (age 60 or older), disabled, or experiencing homelessness can use their Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card to purchase prepared meals directly from participating restaurants and delis. Homeless households can also purchase meals at a discounted price from contracted restaurants. Spouses of elderly or disabled individuals may also be eligible if they are the only participants on the SNAP case. The value of benefits used comes from the individual's existing SNAP benefit balance. SSI recipients and their spouses are also eligible. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services in coordination with the USDA Food and Nutrition Service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SNAP recipients who are elderly (age 60 or older), disabled, or experiencing homelessness can use their Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card to purchase prepared meals directly from participating restaurants and delis. The value of benefits used comes from the individual's existing SNAP benefit balance. Homeless households can also purchase meals at concessional (discounted) prices from contracted restaurants. SSI recipients and their spouses are also eligible. Meals are purchased using existing SNAP benefits at no additional cost to the recipient. Authorized meal service providers include private for-profit restaurants, drug and/or alcohol treatment programs, meal delivery services, communal dining facilities, homeless meal providers, shelters for battered women and children, group living arrangements (max 16 residents), and private for-profit senior citizens centers or residential buildings.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing program
structured_extraction.program_audience: SNAP recipients who are elderly (age 60 or older), disabled, or experiencing homelessness, including SSI recipients and their spouses. Spouses of elderly or disabled individuals may also be eligible if they are the only participants on the SNAP case. This program is also available to restaurant owners and other meal service providers seeking to participate as authorized meal service providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of prepared or hot meals from participating restaurants and delis. SNAP benefits can be redeemed for meals at authorized meal service locations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is currently available in select Maryland counties including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Calvert, Cecil, Charles, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, Prince Ageorgeś, St. Marys, and Washington. The program is expanding to additional jurisdictions. Eligible recipients can use benefits at participating restaurants in Maryland. Additionally, eligible Maryland RMP recipients can use their benefits at participating restaurants in other states that have authorized the Restaurant Meals Program.
requirements_list: Must be an active SNAP recipient or SSI recipient
Must meet one of the following criteria: (1) experiencing homelessness, (2) age 60 or older (includes spouses), or (3) disabled (includes spouse if only two participants on SNAP case)
Eligibility is reviewed at every SNAP recertification
Cannot purchase alcoholic beverages or non-food items
Use the meal purchase at a participating restaurant
Restaurants must submit a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with DHS
Restaurants must submit USDA FNS Form #FNS252-2 application for certification
Restaurants cannot be both a restaurant and traditional retailer simultaneously
Must comply with SNAP laws and regulations
Must prevent workers from trading cash for SNAP benefits
Must prevent unauthorized use of SNAP benefits
Must not use SNAP benefits for credit accounts or loans
Must not use SNAP benefits for non-eligible items
Must treat SNAP customers equally to other customers
Subject to disqualification for violations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For eligible SNAP recipients: Eligible SNAP recipients do not need to apply separately. Eligibility is determined during SNAP recertification. Recipients can then use their EBT card to purchase meals directly from participating restaurants listed on the DHS website. To use benefits: (1) locate a participating restaurant, (2) call 1-800-997-2222 or visit www.connectebt.com to confirm EBT card balance, (3) purchase a meal using the EBT card, (4) receive a receipt showing meal cost and remaining balance. For meal service providers seeking to participate: Submit a completed Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) and USDA FNS Form #FNS252-2 application to DHS. DHS reviews and elevates forms to FNS. FNS issues a certification number upon approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Roberta's House, Inc. Support Services Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grief counseling services provided to individuals and families whose lives have been impacted by violence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding supports grief counseling services to individuals and families impacted by violence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families impacted by violence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grief counseling

structured_extraction.program_name: STEP Up (Supporting, Training, and Employing Parents)
structured_extraction.program_description: A job-driven program that offers free job training and employment support services to help noncustodial parents overcome employment barriers and launch careers in in-demand industries. The program assists noncustodial parents in obtaining and maintaining unsubsidized, competitive employment through hard and soft skills development, job readiness, job search and placement, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, resolution of employment barriers, access to work items such as clothing, tools, or textbooks, and support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Participants train for careers in welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, hospitality, warehouse operations, culinary arts, retail customer service, administrative professional skills, building deconstruction, solar installation, brownfields remediation, and residential energy efficiency weatherization. Participants who successfully complete training can earn forgiveness of child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland and help establish a pattern of regular child support payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, no-cost job training including hard skills training in in-demand industries such as welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, hospitality, warehouse operations, biotechnology, and warehousing; soft skills training in communication and customer service; job readiness preparation; job search and placement assistance; industry-recognized certifications and credentialing; work experience; transportation assistance; referrals to community services; resolution of employment barriers such as criminal record issues, legal services, or driver's license suspensions; provision of items needed for work such as work clothing, tools, and textbooks; and ongoing support from a career navigator and success coach. Participants who successfully complete training can earn forgiveness for child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland. Training areas include welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, hospitality, warehousing, culinary arts, retail customer service, administrative professional skills, building deconstruction, solar installation, brownfields remediation, and residential energy efficiency weatherization.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline specified
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents with a Baltimore City child support case who can commit to working upon program completion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training and employment support services in industries including healthcare, construction, welding, hospitality, warehousing, biotechnology, green energy, building deconstruction, culinary arts, retail customer service, administrative professional skills, solar energy installation, brownfields remediation, and residential energy efficiency weatherization.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Initial program enrollment takes place at the Baltimore City Office of Child Support Services located at Mondawmin Mall, 2401 Liberty Heights Ave., Baltimore, MD 21215, Suite 4645.
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial party with a Baltimore City child support case
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must be able to commit to working upon program completion
Must reside in or be eligible to participate in Baltimore City
Have a Baltimore City child support case
Be a noncustodial parent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Start the enrollment process by calling (410) 844-7001 x 7144 or (800) 332-6347 to schedule an enrollment session. Initial program enrollment takes place at the Baltimore City Office of Child Support Services at Mondawmin Mall, 2401 Liberty Heights Ave., Baltimore, MD 21215, Suite 4645. Once enrolled, parents join a training program offered by one of the STEP Up employment program partners. Interested individuals can inform the intake coordinator of any specific training program preferences at their enrollment session.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Safe Haven Program aims to reduce newborn mortality and promote a healthy beginning for newborns by offering a safe alternative for a parent who is unable or unwilling to care for their child. The program allows a mother or responsible adult to surrender a newborn without the risk of arrest or prosecution. Once surrendered at a designated facility, the newborn receives necessary medical care and is placed with the Local Department of Social Services for permanent, stable family placement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a safe haven at designated facilities (hospitals, licensed medical providers, police departments, state police barracks, and insured fire companies) where a parent can surrender an unharmed newborn who is 2 months or younger without risk of arrest or prosecution. Once surrendered, the newborn receives necessary medical care and is placed with the Local Department of Social Services for permanent, stable family placement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Mothers or responsible adults who are unable or unwilling to care for a newborn 2 months or younger and in unharmed condition.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide financial assistance to applicants. It provides medical care for surrendered newborns and placement services. Newborns can be safely surrendered at designated facilities without legal consequences and are placed into permanent family care through the Local Department of Social Services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland at designated facilities in all 24 counties including hospitals, licensed medical providers, police departments, state police barracks, and insured fire companies (volunteer or professional).
requirements_list: Newborn must be 2 months or younger
Newborn must be unharmed (no evidence of physical injury or failure to provide proper care as determined by a licensed health care practitioner)
Surrender can only occur at designated facilities including hospitals, licensed medical providers, police departments, state police barracks, and insured fire companies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To surrender a newborn, call the DHS toll-free hotline at 1-800-917-7383 or call 2-1-1 to ask for the nearest Safe Haven location. The newborn can be surrendered at any designated facility. Once surrendered, the newborn receives necessary medical care before being placed with the Local Department of Social Services. If the parent changes their mind, they can contact the Local Department of Social Services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that gives foster youth the opportunity to practice living independently while being supervised by local departments of social services. Youth in SILA live in a variety of settings including renting a room, living in their own apartments, or staying on campus in a dorm. Each month, SILA youth receive a check from the department to help cover living expenses. Youth receive financial assistance to cover living costs while developing independent living skills in housing, health care, education, employment, financial literacy, and social and emotional well-being through support from the local department and provider agency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SILA youth receive a monthly check from their local department of social services to help cover living expenses for semi-independent living arrangements. Services include support from the local department and provider agency to help develop independent living skills in housing, health care, education, employment, financial literacy, and social and emotional well-being.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foster youth ages 16 to 21 in out-of-home placement who are sufficiently mature, can manage money, are continually enrolled and regularly attending school or vocational training, have a goal of self-sufficiency, maintain employment, and need help transitioning to self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Living expenses including rent, utilities, food, and other costs associated with semi-independent living arrangements, as well as assistance for housing, health care, education, employment, financial literacy, and social and emotional well-being.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through all 24 local departments of social services in Maryland, with specific programs in Baltimore City and other local jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Between 16-21 years old
Sufficiently mature
Demonstrate an ability to manage money
Continually enrolled in and regularly attending school or vocational training or working at least 80 hours per month
Agree to and maintain the terms of a service agreement
Able and willing to contribute to the cost of semi-independent living
Capable of contributing to the cost of living through earned income or income from scholarships, stipends, grants, work study, Social Security, or any combination
Needs help in transitioning to self-sufficiency
Youth with documented disability in living skills may be eligible with case plan accommodation
Have a goal of self-sufficiency
Maintain employment (where applicable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services to apply for SILA services. You can get a SILA application and information packet from your case worker, your attorney, or by calling the Ready by 21 program at 443-423-6120. Complete the application form and submit it along with the required documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Services Helping the Involvement of Non-Custodial Parents and Employment (SHINE)
structured_extraction.program_description: A free, comprehensive 12-month case management program designed for noncustodial parents obligated to pay child support in Allegany County. The program helps participants overcome barriers to employment, secure financial stability, and strengthen their relationships with their children. Services include job readiness and training, legal assistance and documentation support, parenting resources, health referrals, and basic needs support such as housing, transportation, and child care assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free 12-month case management including job readiness activities, resume development, interview skills training, occupational and vocational training access, GED classes, assistance obtaining vital documents and photo IDs, legal aid and expungement services, parenting skills training, mental health and substance abuse referrals, housing and shelter referrals, transportation resources, work clothing, and child care resource assistance. Employment services include skills assessment, employment barriers identification, education and training program referrals, and employment placement support.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing referral program; no stated deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents in Allegany County who are obligated to pay child support, have outstanding arrearages, or have been referred by a magistrate during a contempt hearing or by the Child Support Administration. Participants must seek stable employment and not have known physical or mental disabilities that prevent them from working.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program funds case management services, job training and readiness activities, assistance with documentation and legal services, parenting skill development, mental health and addiction treatment referrals, housing and transportation support, basic necessities such as work clothing and child care resources, education and certification programs, and employment placement assistance to help participants achieve stable employment and meet child support obligations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Allegany County, Maryland. Services are provided through the Allegany County Department of Social Services.
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial parent obligated to pay child support
Typically ordered by a magistrate during a contempt hearing for outstanding child support arrearages or referred by the Child Support Administration

structured_extraction.program_description: SNAP is the largest federal nutrition assistance program in the nation. It helps low-income households and individuals, including kinship caregivers and children in their care, purchase nutritious and essential food items by providing monthly benefits that increase their buying power based on the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Thrifty Food Plan. Eligible applicants receive benefits on an EBT card (Independence Card) that works like a bank ATM card and can be used to purchase eligible food items at authorized retailers. The program includes a Restaurant Meals Program for eligible elderly, disabled, and homeless individuals to purchase meals from participating restaurants. Some applicants with little or no money may qualify for Expedited SNAP benefits issued within 7 days after identity verification. Benefit amounts depend on household size, gross income, and allowable expenses, and benefits must be accessed no later than 30 days from when the office receives the application. Eligible foods include fruits, vegetables, meat, poultry, fish, dairy products, breads, and cereals. SNAP benefits cannot be used for hot or prepared foods, alcohol, tobacco, or non-food items. SNAP participants can also purchase fresh produce and groceries online from participating retailers including Amazon, Walmart, ShopRite, Food Lion, Giant of Maryland, Martin's, Aldi, Weis, and Safeway, with delivery to their homes or store pickup. Formerly known as Food Stamps.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SNAP provides monthly benefits deposited on an EBT card (Independence Card) to eligible low-income households to purchase food at authorized retailers. Benefit amount depends on household size, gross income, and allowable expenses. Financial assistance is provided based on the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Thrifty Food Plan standards and Maximum Allotment, adjusted annually for food prices. Maximum monthly benefits range from $339 for one person to $1,421 for eight people, with $136 per additional person for larger households. Benefits depend on household size and monthly gross income before taxes or deductions, with eligibility based on gross income under 130% of Federal Poverty Level and net income under 100% of Federal Poverty Level. Categorical eligibility at 200% FPL is available. Eligible foods include fruits, vegetables, meat, poultry, fish, dairy products, breads, and cereals. SNAP benefits cannot be used for hot or prepared foods (except through Restaurant Meals Program), alcohol, tobacco, or non-food items. Benefits typically cover only part of a household's food budget; recipients must spend some of their own cash along with benefits to buy enough food for a month. Benefits can also be used at participating restaurants through the Restaurant Meals Program for eligible elderly, disabled, and homeless individuals. Some applicants may qualify for Expedited SNAP benefits (less than $150 monthly income and $100 or less in cash/savings, or shelter costs exceeding income, or migrant/seasonal farm worker status), which are issued within 7 days after identity verification for those with little or no money. Benefits must be accessed no later than 30 days from when the office receives the application. Cash benefits can be accessed from ATMs. SNAP participants can also use their EBT card to shop online for fresh produce and groceries from participating retailers with delivery to their homes or store pickup.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households and individuals who need help buying food for good health, including those who work for low wages, are unemployed or work part time, receive Temporary Cash Assistance or other public assistance payments, are elderly or disabled and live on a small income, are homeless, or seeking assistance with food purchases. Also includes informal kinship caregivers and children in their care who meet income requirements, migrant/seasonal farm workers, and Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) ages 18-50. Eligible individuals include U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens. Those age 18 and older must register for work unless exempt. A household is defined as a group of people who live together, buy food, and prepare meals together. Applicants must meet financial and technical eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: SNAP benefits can be used to purchase eligible food and grocery items at authorized retailers to prepare nutritious meals, including in-store and online shopping with home delivery or store pickup from participating retailers such as Amazon, Walmart, ShopRite, Food Lion, Giant, Martin's, Aldi, Weis, and Safeway. Eligible foods include fruits, vegetables, meat, poultry, fish, dairy products, breads, and cereals. The program includes a Restaurant Meals Program for eligible elderly, disabled, and homeless individuals to purchase meals from participating restaurants. SNAP benefits cannot be used for hot or prepared foods (except through Restaurant Meals Program), alcohol, tobacco, non-food items, shipping, or delivery fees. SNAP is only part of the household's monthly food budget; households must spend some of their own cash along with benefits to buy enough food for the whole month. For online shopping, only SNAP EBT eligible labeled items can be purchased, and minimum purchase requirements may apply by retailer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland through local departments of social services including all Maryland counties, Baltimore County, and specific services available in Montgomery County. Online shopping available statewide with delivery areas varying by retailer and postal zones where perishable goods can be delivered. Applicants can apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov or through the Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal, in person at local departments of social services or Family Investment Division service centers, by phone, by mail, by fax, or through a Social Security district office if the applicant is receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits. Baltimore County residents and Montgomery County residents can apply by mail to any Office of Eligibility and Support Services location in Germantown, Rockville, or Silver Spring, or at three regional offices (MidCounty DHHS Building in Rockville, DHHS Silver Spring Center in Silver Spring, UpCounty Regional Services Center in Germantown). District Offices in Baltimore County are available for applications. Maryland residents only.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can file an application online at MarylandBenefits.gov, mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us, or through the Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal, download and submit a PDF application (Form DHS/FIA 9701), or apply in person, by phone, by mail, by fax, or through a Social Security district office if receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits. In Montgomery County, applicants are seen on a walk-in basis or by appointment at three regional offices (MidCounty DHHS Building in Rockville, DHHS Silver Spring Center in Silver Spring, UpCounty Regional Services Center in Germantown). In Baltimore County, applicants can apply at a District Office with paperwork required for application processing. The office will accept a signed application the same day it is submitted. Face-to-face interviews are available Monday through Thursday, with same-day processing available if applications are submitted by 11am. In Montgomery County, applicants can fax to the Germantown, Rockville, or Silver Spring office, email the application, or mail to any Office of Eligibility and Support Services location. Applications can be photographed by cell phone or scanned and emailed. Applicants must be interviewed and meet all financial and technical eligibility factors prior to benefit issuance. The application is reviewed the same day to determine initial eligibility, with formal eligibility determination within 7 days. A case manager will review the application, explain program rules, help complete any missing sections, and request proof of information provided. Expedited SNAP benefits are available within 7 days for eligible applicants who need only an interview and identity verification. Benefits should be accessible within 30 days of application submission. Maryland Hunger Solutions (866-821-5552, M-F 10AM-6PM) provides phone assistance for new applications. For online shopping, sign up through mydhrbenefit.dhr.state.md.us or call; select from participating online retailers to place orders and add eligible items to cart. For Restaurant Meals Program, restaurants must complete Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) and USDA FNS form #FNS-252-2 application for certification. For balance inquiries or card replacement, call 1-800-997-2222. Contact 1-800-221-5689 for USDA SNAP hotline (Spanish available) or 7-1-1 or 800-735-2258 for Maryland Relay for TTY calls.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Employment and Training (SNAP E&T)
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary employment and training program that connects SNAP recipients to free job-driven training programs lasting 12 to 16 weeks in industries including welding, construction, machine operation, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, and computer technology/IT. Participants receive job placement, retention, and support services including hard skills and soft skills training, job readiness, industry-recognized certifications and credentials, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, help resolving employment barriers, access to work-related supplies, and support from a personal career navigator and success coach to help them find and keep employment. The program is delivered through multiple third-party partner organizations including community colleges, workforce development organizations, non-profit organizations, and private training providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free industry-specific training programs lasting an average of 12 to 16 weeks in job-driven fields such as welding, construction, machine operation, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, and computer technology/IT. All programs include hard skills training in an in-demand industry, soft skills training in communication and customer service, job readiness, job search and placement assistance, industry-recognized certifications and credentials, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, help resolving employment barriers such as criminal records or legal issues, access to items needed for work such as clothing or tools, and support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Many programs also offer job placement and retention services. Supportive services include transportation vouchers or passes, work uniforms and interview clothing, tools and equipment, childcare support, certification and exam fees, digital equipment access, tuition assistance, legal services (such as expungement and employment-related support), mental health and crisis intervention support, and other wraparound services. Participants also receive career readiness training, financial literacy, numeracy and literacy instruction, mock interviews, and employer connections.

Participants receive hard skills and soft skills training, job readiness, job placement, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, help resolving employment barriers, access to work-related supplies, and support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Free industry-specific training programs lasting an average of 12 to 16 weeks in job-driven fields such as welding, construction, machine operation, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, and computer technology/IT. All programs include hard skills training in an in-demand industry, soft skills training in communication and customer service, job readiness, job search and placement assistance, industry-recognized certifications and credentials, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, help resolving employment barriers such as criminal records or legal issues, access to items needed for work such as clothing or tools, and support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Participants also receive career readiness training, financial literacy, numeracy and literacy instruction, mock interviews, and employer connections. Additional services include case management, assessment and orientation, vocational training in specializations such as CNA/GNA, HVAC, electrical, digital marketing, IT, ServSafe, ATSSA Flagger, DOT certifications, paid internships, on-the-job training, financial literacy and digital skills training, and job retention services with follow-up support (30, 60, 90-day and 12-month follow-ups).

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families authorized to receive cash assistance through Temporary Cash Assistance have current support payments assigned to the Department of Human Services. Pass Through payments are based on current support paid in the prior calendar month and are not available for support arrears payments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) / Maryland's Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) program that provides time-limited cash assistance to eligible families with dependent children and individuals when available resources do not fully address their needs and while promoting individual responsibility and self-sufficiency through work. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Human Services through local Departments of Social Services and county offices, including Prince George's County and Baltimore County. Families with minor children can receive assistance for a total of 60 months (5 years) over a lifetime. The program helps adults find employment through mandatory work activity participation and prepares program participants for independence through work. Cash benefits are issued through an Electronic Benefit Transfer card (Independence Card) and made available from the 2nd to the 4th of every month based on the first letter of the applicant's last name. In Montgomery County, specific services are available at three locations: Mid-County DHHS Building in Rockville, DHHS Silver Spring Center, and Up-County Regional Services Center in Germantown. In Baltimore County, services are available through District Offices. Recipients receive assistance through an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card called the Independence Card and participate in work program requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited monthly cash assistance payments provided to eligible families with dependent children and individuals to help meet their basic needs while they prepare for independence through work. Benefits are deposited directly through the MarylandBenefits system or issued through an Electronic Benefit Transfer card (Independence Card). The amount cannot exceed the benefit level paid for the assistance unit size. Funds can be withdrawn from ATMs or used to purchase items at participating stores. Families with minor children can receive assistance for a total of 60 months (5 years) over a lifetime. Families may also apply for assistance with child care costs. Recipients must assign child support rights to the State of Maryland where applicable. Program promotes individual responsibility and self-sufficiency through employment and employment support services. Cash assistance is provided to eligible families with children when other resources and services do not fully meet their needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible individuals and families with dependent children whose available resources do not fully address their needs and who are willing to participate in work activities and employment. Available to residents of all Maryland counties, including Prince George's County. Families must be U.S. citizens or have qualified immigrant status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash assistance for living expenses and basic needs while preparing for independence through work and employment support services. Funds can be withdrawn from ATMs or used to purchase items at participating stores.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland through local Departments of Social Services and county social services offices, including Prince George's County and Baltimore County. In Montgomery County, services are available at three locations: Mid-County DHHS Building in Rockville, DHHS Silver Spring Center, and Up-County Regional Services Center in Germantown. In Baltimore County, services are available through District Offices.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online through the MarylandBenefits website at https://MarylandBenefits.gov/home/#/ or through My DHR (Maryland Department of Human Resources), apply in person at a local Department of Social Services or county social services office, apply through a District Office in Baltimore County, or file an application by mail, fax, or other electronic means. Someone may drop off an application on behalf of the applicant. Interpretation services are available free of charge for customers with limited English proficiency. Applicants must complete a face-to-face interview and meet income requirements and specified work activity requirements before approval. Applications can be photographed by cell phone or scanned and emailed. For Montgomery County applicants: 1) View the DHHS Orientation video online, 2) Download the DHHS Orientation packet, 3) Submit the packet by email to HHS Employment Services or by fax to 240-777-4166, 4) After orientation and packet submission, you may be contacted if corrections or additional information is needed, 5) Complete Child Support application through the DHS online portal at benefits.maryland.gov, 6) Register with Equus for the Work Program by email or phone, 7) Bring required documents including proof of identity, Social Security number, proof of residence, proof of income, and proof of citizenship or immigration status. Interviews are held at one of three Montgomery County locations: Mid-County DHHS Building, DHHS Silver Spring Center, or Up-County Regional Services Center. Paperwork will be required for application processing. For Prince George's County applicants, submit Maryland Department of Human Resources Family Investment Administration Application for Assistance (DHR/FIA CARES 9701).

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded cash assistance program that provides time-limited monthly cash benefits to low-income disabled adults between ages 18 and 64 with no dependent children under age 18 living in the home. The program supports those whose disabilities prevent them from working and earning income, and assists while awaiting approval of federal disability support such as SSI or SSDI. Assistance is provided for up to 12 months within a 36-month period for basic living expenses and general needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited monthly cash benefits for low-income individuals with verified disabilities lasting at least 3 months that prevent workforce participation. Recipients may receive benefits for up to 12 months within a 36-month period unless they are pursuing Supplemental Security Income (SSI), in which case they may receive benefits for longer. Support is provided for basic living expenses and general needs while awaiting Supplemental Security Income approval. Income of a spouse in the household is used for eligibility determination, except SSI benefits. Individuals pursuing SSI may have different benefit terms applied.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income disabled adults between ages 18 and 64 in Maryland without dependent children under age 18 who need short-term cash assistance or support while awaiting federal disability approval.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash benefits for basic living expenses and general needs during temporary disability or while awaiting federal disability support approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local Department of Social Services offices; all counties eligible, including Baltimore County and Montgomery County.

The program operates statewide in partnership with the Maryland Food Bank and Capital Area Food Bank, providing federal surplus food for distribution and technical assistance to emergency food providers.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that provides 100% of tuition and mandatory fees for students pursuing credentials or degrees to work in targeted positions within the Maryland Department of Human Services. The program is designed to fast-track students' entry into human services careers and includes employment opportunities with the Department of Human Services. Recipients must fulfill a service obligation of 15 months of employment per academic year of scholarship received, within an 8-year window, and receive state employment benefits including pension, generous time off, and career advancement opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% of tuition and mandatory fees for eligible credential and degree programs at public higher education institutions in Maryland. Service obligation required: 15 months of employment per academic year of scholarship received, within an 8-year window. Employment is with the Maryland Department of Human Services in targeted positions. Recipients also receive state employment benefits including pension, generous time off, and career advancement opportunities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents or Maryland high school graduates who are rising high school seniors or currently enrolled students at public higher education institutions in Maryland and pursuing careers in targeted human services positions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees for credential and degree programs in targeted human services positions including Child Support Specialist, Family Investment Specialist, Family Support Worker, Family Services Caseworker, and Social Worker positions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents or Maryland high school graduates. Employment in targeted positions is available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Prince George's County, with additional opportunities through Local Departments of Social Services in other jurisdictions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Protects low-income families from utility service disconnections during the heating season. All customers eligible for the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) can participate in USPP. Participation requires year-round budget billing with equal monthly payments to spread annual utility bills into consistent monthly charges. The program provides financial assistance and protection from utility service disconnection year-round through budget billing. Failure to make consecutive payments may result in removal from the program. Customers should contact their local utility provider or the Public Service Commission at www.psc.state.md.us for specific eligibility and budget billing policies.

The program provides financial assistance and protection from utility service disconnection year-round. Failure to make consecutive budget billing payments may result in removal from the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Winning Fathers Program assists noncustodial parents, including incarcerated fathers, in obtaining and maintaining unsubsidized, competitive employment and developing skills for successful employment transition and family reconnection. The program provides job readiness training, resume writing, interviewing techniques, legal resources, and comprehensive support services to help participants transition from incarceration back into the community and establish a pattern of regular child support payments.

Training and technical assistance develop employment readiness and soft skills including resume writing, communication, self-confidence, social skills, time management, problem solving, and anger management. A full-time Job Developer and two full-time Social Workers assist participants throughout their transition.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment training, job placement services, and technical assistance to develop employment readiness and soft skills including resume writing, communication, self-confidence, social skills, time management, problem solving, and anger management.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Tuition Waiver for Foster Care Recipients
structured_extraction.program_description: A financial assistance program that waives tuition and mandatory fees for eligible foster care youth and former foster care youth pursuing higher education at Maryland public institutions. The waiver exempts eligible individuals from paying tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and other mandatory fees required for enrollment) at any Maryland public institution of higher education. The waiver covers all four terms: fall, winter, spring, and summer, and does not cover room, board, books, or transportation. Youth must be enrolled in school before age 25. Applicants must file FAFSA or MSFAA and contact their financial aid office to apply.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Human Services and Maryland Higher Education Commission
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver exempts eligible foster care and former foster care youth from paying tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and other mandatory fees required for enrollment) at any Maryland public institution of higher education. The waiver covers all four terms: fall, winter, spring, and summer. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation. Scholarships or grants awarded to a foster care recipient may not be applied to tuition since it is already waived. Each public institution determines its own tuition amount. Youth must be enrolled in school before age 25. Applicants must file FAFSA or MSFAA and contact their financial aid office to complete the application process.
