requirements_list: Employers must be impacted by COVID-19
Proposed program must include elements of Employee Support Programs or Payroll Incentives or both
Program must align with all funding limits, guidance, and policies for the Jobs that Build Employer Fund
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers submit a grant application identifying which benefits will be provided, how employees access and are approved for benefits, benefit amounts and allowances per employee. Applications should be designed with input from human resources, payroll, and accounting staff.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland 4th & Goal Program supports learners who have completed three GED tests with only one more to go on the way to a Maryland High School Diploma. It offers short-term assistance for classes, tutoring, and covering the costs of practice tests and the fourth and final exam.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term assistance for classes, tutoring, and covering the costs of practice tests and the fourth and final GED exam. The Maryland Subsidy Discount Code (MDGED2175) is available to all Maryland test takers, reducing the cost of the first attempt from $36.00 to $14.25 per module.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults in Maryland who have passed three of four GED tests and need assistance with the costs of practice tests and the final exam.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Classes, tutoring, practice tests, and exam fees for the fourth GED module.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must have passed three of four GED tests
Must need assistance with costs of practice tests and exam fees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the program website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Access to Banking Act - Assessment Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An assessment credit program for Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions that establish new branches or retain existing branches in low-to-moderate income communities. The assessment credit offsets annual regulatory fees charged to depository institutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides an assessment credit (offset to annual regulatory assessment fees) to incentivize Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions to establish new de novo branches or retain existing branches in low-to-moderate income communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assessment credit is applied as an offset to annual regulatory assessment fees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program applies to new or existing branches located in low-to-moderate income communities throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland state-chartered bank or credit union
Must establish a new de novo branch or retain an existing branch in a low-to-moderate income community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested institutions should subscribe to Office of Financial Regulation emails for updates on how to apply for and earn the assessment credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-seeded equity investment fund designed to invest in financial technology firms that develop innovative financial products to improve access to capital, funding, and financial services for small businesses in low-to-moderate income communities. The fund will deploy, test, and evaluate innovations and make them available to Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund will be initially seeded with up to $2,500,000 from the Office of Financial Regulation's Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund. Through June 30, 2028, the Commissioner of Financial Regulation may match any investment made by a Maryland state-chartered bank or credit union in the amount of the assessment credit earned by that institution. All investment returns or capital returns from the fund are credited back to the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fintech firms interested in developing financial products and innovations, and Maryland state-chartered depository institutions interested in participating in the fund
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in financial technology firms developing products and innovations that enhance access to capital, funding, and financial services for small businesses in low-to-moderate income communities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program focuses on serving low-to-moderate income communities throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a fintech firm or Maryland state-chartered bank or credit union
Proposed innovations must enhance access to capital, funding, and financial services for small businesses in LMI communities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested fintech firms or Maryland state-chartered depository institutions should subscribe to Office of Financial Regulation emails for updates regarding eligibility criteria and the application process. Applications should be sent via email to ofrmail@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A temporary financial assistance program providing up to 26 weeks of economic support to eligible workers who are unemployed through no fault of their own. Benefits consist of weekly cash payments ranging from $50 to $430 per week, calculated based on prior wages and individual circumstances. The program is administered statewide in Maryland and covers various categories of workers including private sector employees, federal civilian employees, military members, and union members. The program establishes rates and collects taxes from Maryland employers to finance benefits and conducts appeals when disputes arise between claimants and employers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides weekly cash payments ranging from $50 to $430 per week depending on prior wages, for up to 26 weeks of temporary financial assistance. The exact amount is calculated based on individual factors such as prior earnings and severance received. Claimants must meet eligibility requirements, register with the Maryland Workforce Exchange to document job search activities each week (minimum 3 activities per week), and complete weekly certification to receive benefits. Benefits are distributed based on individual circumstances.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applicant must file as soon as possible upon separation from employment
structured_extraction.program_audience: Workers who are unemployed through no fault of their own and meet eligibility requirements, including federal civilian employees, military members, union members, federal employees on furlough, and federal contractors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary economic assistance during unemployment while the claimant searches for a new job and works toward reemployment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Federal civilian employees must have their last official duty station in Maryland, be a Maryland resident with a duty station outside the United States, or be a Maryland resident separated from federal employment who then worked in non-federal employment in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be unemployed through no fault of their own
Must be ready to work hours normal for your job as soon as possible without restrictions
Must meet eligibility requirements (details available on the eligibility guide)
Have earned sufficient wages during the base period (18 months before applying): at least $1,176.01 during one quarter and a minimum of $1,800 over at least two quarters
Must register with the Maryland Workforce Exchange to document job search activities
Must record at least 3 job search activities per week showing you looked for work
Must complete weekly certification to receive benefits
Federal employees and federal contractors must verify their eligibility and complete an SF-8 or SF-50 form and 935 affidavit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check if you qualify using the eligibility guide and determine your eligibility. Step 2: Gather personal information including Social Security Number, address, employment history from the last 18 months, and dependent information if applicable. Step 3: Submit your claim online through the Maryland Unemployment Insurance Portal (BEACON) or by phone at 667-207-6520 (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.) or 410-949-0022 or 1-800-827-4839 (24/7). Step 4: Register with the Maryland Workforce Exchange to document job search activities each week, recording at least 3 activities per week. Step 5: Complete weekly certification starting each Sunday online or by phone to certify your claim and receive benefits. Federal employees must submit SF-8 or SF-50 form and 935 affidavit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A workforce training program that helps employers offset training costs for workers in Maryland. The program partners with local businesses to support employer strategies for retention, growth, expansion, and layoff aversion through skills training in in-demand occupations. Training funds are provided to businesses serious about increasing employee productivity and upgrading skills of current employees. Funds support classroom-based training, in-house staff training, apprenticeships, and other opportunities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides support to help employers offset the costs of workforce training. Training funds are provided for classroom-based training, in-house staff training, apprenticeships, and other skills training opportunities for current employees. There is a dollar-to-dollar match requirement. Maximum funding of $4,500 per trainee for a project or series of projects. Maximum request per year cannot exceed $40,000. Funds primarily targeted to small businesses with 250 employees or fewer and businesses facing potential layoffs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling applications
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers, particularly local and regional businesses, small businesses with 250 employees or fewer, and businesses facing potential layoffs seeking to train current workers and upgrade their skills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employee training and development, including classroom-based training, in-house staff training, apprenticeships, and other skills training opportunities for current employees in in-demand occupations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide, with focus on Baltimore City and local and regional businesses providing in-demand products or services.
requirements_list: Dollar-to-dollar match requirement
Maximum of $4,500 training cap per trainee
Maximum annual request of $40,000
Focus on in-demand occupations
Priority given to small businesses with 250 employees or fewer
Priority given to businesses facing potential layoffs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MOED Employer Services or the Maryland Department of Labor for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides part-time and on-the-job training opportunities for low-income men and women age 55 and older who are residents of Montgomery, Frederick, or Prince George's counties and have poor employment prospects or are unemployed. Trainees work at charities and government agencies while receiving minimum wage or stipends to build their skills and resumes while delivering valuable community service. The program includes personal and job-related counseling, job training, and job referral services to help older adults secure employment. SCSEP providers also educate employers about the benefits of hiring older workers. Veterans and eligible spouses are encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Labor; Montgomery County; Prince George's County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Part-time and full-time paid work opportunities at community service agencies combined with supportive services including personal counseling, job-related counseling, job training, and job referral assistance. Trainees receive minimum wage or stipends while working to build skills and resumes while delivering valuable community service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income men and women age 55 and older who are residents of Montgomery, Frederick, or Prince George's counties, are unemployed or have poor employment prospects, and are legally eligible to work in the U.S. Veterans and eligible spouses are encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Part-time and full-time paid work opportunities at charities and government agencies combined with job training, counseling, and employment support services to help older adults build skills, resumes, and secure employment while delivering community service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Restricted to residents of Montgomery, Frederick, or Prince George's counties, Maryland.
requirements_list: Age 55 or older
Low-income or have poor employment prospects
Resident of Montgomery, Frederick, or Prince George's counties, Maryland
Legally eligible to work in the U.S.
Unemployed or have limited employment prospects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program by phone at 240-395-0918 for Montgomery and Frederick counties, or 301-265-8450 for Prince George's County for application information. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding to help organizations cover the costs of butchering and processing donated deer that will be provided to programs serving low-income individuals and homeless people in Maryland. Grants up to $25,000 are available on a first-come, first-served basis, with a maximum allowable cost of $60 per deer when using grant funds. Funds may be split among multiple applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to a maximum of $25,000 are available on a first-come, first-served basis to cover butchering and processing costs for donated deer. The maximum amount a program can pay for butchering and processing is $60 per deer when grant funds are used. Funds may be split among multiple applicants. Applicants are responsible for identifying and contracting processors and coordinating distribution. Administrative costs are not eligible for reimbursement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be received electronically by 11:59 pm on Sunday, June 16, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: County governments, municipal corporations, and tax-exempt nonprofit organizations that operate programs providing nutritional support or food assistance to low-income individuals or homeless people in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Butchering and processing costs for donated deer hunted in compliance with Maryland hunting laws and regulations, with a dressed weight of at least 50 pounds. Administrative costs are not eligible for reimbursement. Applicants are responsible for identifying and contracting processors and coordinating distribution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Deer must be hunted in compliance with state hunting laws and regulations.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county government, municipal corporation, or 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization
Deer must be hunted in compliance with state hunting laws and regulations
Deer must be donated to a program administered by the applicant that provides nutritional support or food for low-income individuals or homeless people
Deer must have a dressed weight of at least 50 pounds
Maximum processing cost of $60 per deer when using grant funds
Grantees must submit quarterly reports including DNR hunting confirmation numbers, processor names and counts, costs per deer, pounds distributed, and recipient organizations
Applicants responsible for identifying and contracting processors and coordinating distribution
501(c)(3) organizations must provide tax exemption documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Venison Donation Grant Program Application form with all required fields and submit it electronically to Brian Eyler at brian.eyler@maryland.gov by the stated deadline. Attach supporting documentation including processor list, receiver list, and tax exemption proof if applicable.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit that allows the sampling, removal, or possession of aquatic organisms from Maryland waters for scientific research, educational projects, collections of display animals, ecological monitoring, or in-stream surveys. This permit covers activities that may not be permitted under commercial or recreational fishing licenses. The permit may not be used to collect animals for sale or personal use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual permit issued for a $10 fee payable by check, money order, or electronically through the online payment system. The permit allows sampling and removal of aquatic organisms from Maryland waters for authorized purposes. Permits are issued annually and require submission of maps of intended sampling locations and an annual activity report.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified - permits issued annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Researchers, scientists, and organizations conducting aquatic research in Maryland waters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The permit authorizes sampling, removal, and possession of aquatic organisms from Maryland waters for scientific research, educational projects, collection of display animals, ecological monitoring, and in-stream surveys. Cannot be used to collect animals for sale or personal use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland waters
requirements_list: $10 permit fee (online payment or check/money order)
Complete application with all information
Project proposal including reason for study, objectives, justification, species, and numbers
Specific collection location with maps
Identification of sampling gear to be used
List of all collectors beyond principal officer
Applicant certification of truthfulness
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application with required maps and fee to FISHCOLLECTION.DNR@MARYLAND.GOV or mail to Tamara O'Connell, Permit Coordinator. Application must include project proposal, specific collection locations with maps, identification of sampling gear, list of collectors, and applicant certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program funded by the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service Wildlife & Sport Fish Restoration Program that provides funding to public and private schools, environmental education centers, and other organizations for aquatic-based educational projects and angler education. The program aims to increase public understanding of water resources and associated aquatic life forms through angler education, outdoor ethics development, stewardship and conservation programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds provided to support angler education, outdoor ethics development, stewardship and conservation education programs that increase public understanding of the nation's water resources and associated aquatic life forms. Funds support aquatic-based educational projects in schools and environmental education centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private schools serving pre-K through 12th grade, environmental education centers that are part of the public school system, and organizations focused on outdoor environmental education related to aquatic resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Aquatic-based educational projects, angler education, outdoor ethics development, stewardship and conservation education programs, and aquatic resources education activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public or private school (pre-K through 12), an environmental education center that is part of the public school system, or an eligible non-profit or government organization.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Public and private schools, environmental education centers, and eligible organizations apply for funding to support aquatic-based educational projects through Maryland's Aquatic Resources Education Grants Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program designed to assist Maryland homeowners who have a waterway on or adjacent to their property to create a streamside buffer of native trees and shrubs. The program is particularly designed for homeowners with 5 acres or less of land and smaller landowners who are not eligible for agricultural cost-share programs. The program provides free native tree and shrub seedlings (typically 20-30 seedlings per bag, bare-root, approximately 1 to 2 feet in height) to homeowners for planting riparian forest buffers. Seedlings help filter stormwater runoff, stabilize stream banks, improve water quality, create wildlife habitat, reduce peak summer temperatures, prevent erosion, and reduce sediment, fertilizer, and toxic materials from entering streams. The program also provides technical assistance including fact sheets on tree species, planting techniques, proper maintenance, and additional learning resources. Each year, bags are available on a first-come, first-served basis with limited availability, typically reserved in March and picked up in time for spring planting season. County coordinators manage the program locally in each county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or subsidized buffer supplies containing native trees and shrub bare-root seedlings (typically 20-30 seedlings per bag, approximately 1 to 2 feet in height), along with fact sheets on tree species, planting techniques, proper maintenance, and additional learning resources. Technical assistance is provided to homeowners in establishing streamside buffers. A limited number of bags are available each year on a first-come, first-served basis. Reservations are typically taken in March, with bags available for pickup at designated local sites in time for spring planting season.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Reservations typically taken during the month of March
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners with 5 acres or less of land who have a drainage ditch, stream, creek, or river flowing through their property or live adjacent to such a waterway, particularly smaller landowners who are not eligible for agricultural cost-share programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Native tree and shrub seedlings for creating a streamside buffer to improve water quality, create wildlife habitat, reduce peak summer temperatures, stabilize streambanks, prevent erosion, and establish riparian forest buffers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland with county-specific coordinators, though funding is limited and the program may not be available in all counties at all times. Homeowners should contact their local Backyard Buffers County Coordinator to determine eligibility and availability.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland landowner
Own 5 acres of land or less
Must have a drainage ditch, stream, creek, or river flowing through property or live adjacent to such a waterway
Must be a smaller landowner not eligible for agricultural cost-share programs
Willingness to plant riparian buffer on property
Contact county coordinator to reserve seedlings during March signup period
Limited quantities available on first-come, first-served basis
Must be in a county where funding is available
Must register during the application period (typically March)
Must be a homeowner with property suitable for riparian buffer planting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Backyard Buffers County Coordinator to express interest and determine eligibility. Packet reservations are typically taken during the month of March. Bags are available for pickup at a designated local site in time for the spring planting season on a first-come, first-served basis with limited availability each year. Some counties have online registration forms available. Qualifying homeowners contact their local coordinator by phone or email.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants awarded to school groups, science and ecology clubs, and other nonprofit youth groups for proposed environmental education projects. Maximum grant amount is one thousand dollars.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to one thousand dollars for environmental education projects
structured_extraction.program_audience: School groups, science and ecology clubs, and nonprofit youth organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental education projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a school group, science club, ecology club, or nonprofit youth group

structured_extraction.program_description: A donation program that allows the public to contribute money to support largemouth bass and smallmouth bass management and conservation in Maryland. Donations are used for enhancing aquatic habitat, supplies for black bass tournament directors, and similar conservation efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The public can donate any amount of money to support black bass conservation. Donations can be made by check (for amounts of $1,000 or less, payable to Maryland Department of Natural Resources with 'Black Bass Conservation Fund' in the memo line, mailed to Martha Bruder, 580 Taylor Avenue, B-2, Annapolis, MD 21401; for amounts greater than $1,000, contact Martha Bruder directly) or through the Maryland Outdoors licensing portal under the Merchandise section. Donations are not tax-deductible. Funds support projects selected annually by the department and the Black Bass Advisory Committee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Members of the general public who wish to support black bass conservation in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to enhance aquatic habitat, provide supplies to black bass tournament directors, and support similar black bass conservation efforts in Maryland such as purchasing equipment for hatcheries to raise and stock largemouth bass.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Donors can contribute through two methods: (1) mail a check of $1,000 or less made payable to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources with 'Black Bass Conservation Fund' in the memo line to Martha Bruder, 580 Taylor Avenue, B-2, Annapolis, MD 21401; (2) for donations greater than $1,000, contact Martha Bruder at martha.bruder@maryland.gov; (3) donate online through the Maryland Outdoors licensing portal by logging in, going to the Merchandise section, and selecting the Black Bass Conservation Fund option.

structured_extraction.program_description: Permit/license allowing individuals to breed, possess, and/or commercially trade captive reptiles and amphibians. The permit protects and conserves native species while allowing educational and economic benefits from captive-bred animals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual permit fee of $10.00 (check payable to DNR). The permit is valid from the date of issuance until the following December 31. Permit holders may possess, breed, sell, offer for sale, trade, or barter native reptiles and amphibians according to specific possession limits outlined in Lists A and B. Unlimited numbers of captively-produced animals from Lists A and B may be possessed with proper documentation. Authorization to breed, possess, and/or commercially trade captive reptiles and amphibians.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and entities seeking to breed, possess, or commercially trade captive reptiles and amphibians.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The permit authorizes possession, breeding, and commercial trade of native reptiles and amphibians. Funds (the $10 fee) support permit administration and wildlife conservation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland (statewide); available in all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: $10 application fee
Proof of Workers' Compensation compliance (either employed by others, self-employed/family only, or exempt)
Workmen's Compensation Insurance or exemption documentation
List of related state and federal licenses/permits
Signature under penalty of perjury
Animals must be housed in humane, safe, and healthy conditions with appropriate lighting, temperature, humidity, and clean water
Enclosures must be kept in sanitary condition and good repair
Equipment must be available for proper waste storage and disposal
Effective measures must control infection, infestation, disease, and parasites
Animals taken from wild must not be released except at point of capture or with written DNR authorization

For List A: possess no more than 4 individuals of each reptile and salamander (only 4 taken from wild); possess no more than 4 adults and 25 eggs or tadpoles of each frog or toad (only 4 adults and 25 eggs/tadpoles from wild)
For List B: possess no more than 1 individual of each species (only 1 from wild, except no Wood Turtles, Spotted Turtles, or Diamond-backed Terrapins from wild)
No List C animals may be possessed, bred, or sold without Scientific Collection or Endangered Species permit
Venomous snakes may not be possessed
Turtles less than 4 inches cannot be sold in Maryland
Certificate of origin, bill of sale, or other documentation must be maintained proving legal acquisition
Transaction records must be kept and updated immediately after each transaction
Summary of reporting forms must be returned at permit renewal or by January 31 following permit expiration
Original forms must be retained for three years and made available for inspection
Permit holder must allow DNR inspection of premises and records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Print/type completed application and mail to Permits Coordinator at Tawes State Office Building, Annapolis, MD 21401. Include $10 fee (check payable to DNR). Applications can also be submitted by email to wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or by phone at 410-260-8540. Appointments are required at the Tawes State Office Building; walk-in customers not accepted without confirmed appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded grant program administered by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) that enables Maryland to provide resources for state programs and partners that improve water quality in the Chesapeake Bay Watershed. The program supports the goals and strategies developed under the 2014 Chesapeake Watershed Agreement, focusing on initiatives that reduce nonpoint source nutrient and sediment pollution, improve fisheries and habitats, address toxic contaminants, and enhance climate resiliency.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EPA-funded grants that provide resources for state programs, local governments, universities, and non-profit organizations focused on improving water quality in the Chesapeake Bay Watershed by reducing nonpoint source nutrient and sediment pollution. The program provides grant funding with a required 1:1 non-federal match for the funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants include state agencies, the University of Maryland system, local governments, and non-profit organizations working to restore and protect the Chesapeake Bay Watershed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support projects that help restore and protect the Chesapeake Bay. This includes efforts to reduce water pollution, improve fisheries and habitats, address toxic contaminants, and enhance climate resiliency in the Chesapeake Bay Watershed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Chesapeake Bay Watershed across Maryland
requirements_list: Requires a 1:1 non-federal match
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funds are provided by EPA to Maryland for administration through state programs and partnerships focused on water quality improvement and Chesapeake Bay restoration.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding to support environmental education and stewardship projects that improve student and community ability to take action benefiting Chesapeake and coastal ecosystems through professional development, training, curriculum expansion, outdoor learning, and stewardship activities. Funds transportation and facility fees, environmental engagement activities, educator professional development, community education programs, and supply costs for environmental investigations and stewardship projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant funding available through federal allocation. Maximum request of $75,000 per proposal, with up to $100,000 total available for CBIG annually. Funding varies year to year based on federal allocation. Supports transportation and facility fees, environmental engagement activities, educator professional development, community education programs, and supply costs for environmental investigations and stewardship projects. Funding becomes available September 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 12, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local non-governmental organizations, non-profits, local and state agencies, schools, school systems, and higher learning institutions working on environmental education and stewardship projects within Maryland's Chesapeake Bay Watershed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation and facility fees for student, teacher, or community access to natural areas; environmental engagement or stewardship activities; environmental educator professional development and training; community environmental education programs; supply costs for environmental investigations, field equipment, and stewardship projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All projects must be located within Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed. Projects can be located on public lands, in schoolyards, community property, or private property.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local non-governmental organization, non-profit, local or state agency, school, school system, or higher learning institution
Projects must be located within Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed

Track One projects must serve formal K-12 education systems and connect to curriculum standards such as Next Generation Science Standards, Maryland Environmental Literacy Standards, or Maryland Service-Learning Graduation Requirements
Track Two projects must serve communities or public education and connect to environmental or stewardship best practices
Both tracks must include proposals focused on local watershed and land-use issues
Projects must be based on sound environmental education principles
Projects should result from collaborative student/community-stakeholder planning oriented toward capacity building and civic engagement
Applicants must detail how they are supporting local communities and enhancing outreach to groups demonstrating need
Applicants must involve communities in their programming
Maximum request is $75,000 per proposal
Proposals scored on demographics/need, education and stewardship connections, program development, and budget feasibility
Required attachments vary by track but include transmittal letters, letters of support, and environmental literacy documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply through Grants Gateway Outcome 4. Submit proposals by the deadline with required attachments including transmittal letter on official letterhead signed by authorized executive, letters of support from leadership and partners, and evidence of environmental literacy programming or curriculum planning. Proposals are reviewed and scored on demographics and need, education and stewardship connections, program development, and budget feasibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve (CBNERR-MD)
structured_extraction.program_description: A place-based partnership program between NOAA and Maryland that provides funding, technical assistance, and national guidance to support natural resource management, research, and education at three estuarine locations in Maryland: Monie Bay in Somerset County, Otter Point Creek in Harford County, and Jug Bay in Prince George's and Anne Arundel Counties. The program addresses natural resource management issues including climate change impacts, nonpoint source pollution, habitat restoration, invasive species management, and provides living classrooms for learning and research.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NOAA provides funding, national guidance, and technical assistance for place-based programming at three estuarine reserve locations. The reserve is managed by lead state agencies or universities with input from local partners to support programming, research, education, and training. The program offers training to improve coastal resource management, supports research and education initiatives, provides research facilities and living classrooms for learning, and supports habitat restoration, invasive species management, and climate change adaptation initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local communities, regional groups, schools, universities, environmental education centers, and researchers working on coastal and estuarine resource management and education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Natural resource management initiatives including climate change impacts and adaptation, nonpoint source pollution reduction, habitat restoration, invasive species management, research facilities, education programs, research and training initiatives, and staff to support these activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Three reserve locations: Monie Bay in Somerset County, Otter Point Creek in Harford County, and Jug Bay in Prince George's and Anne Arundel Counties.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The reserve is managed by lead state agencies or universities with input from local partners. Reserve staff work with local communities and regional groups to develop and implement programs addressing natural resource management issues. NOAA provides ongoing funding, national guidance, and technical assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Trust Environmental Education Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to expand and enhance Chesapeake Bay environmental education programs for pre-kindergarten through grade 12 students in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available to support environmental education programs for students in Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Educators and schools seeking to expand Bay environmental education programs for pre-K through grade 12 students

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A long-standing state funding source administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources in collaboration with Chesapeake Bay Council agencies and a Scientific Advisory Panel. The program accelerates Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays restoration and protection by engaging local partners in achieving watershed goals. It focuses financial resources on the most efficient, cost-effective non-point source pollution control projects and ecological restoration initiatives identified in the State's Tributary Strategies and 2-Year Milestones. The fund supports stream and floodplain restoration, enhanced riparian buffers and forests, improved wetland ecosystems, comprehensive stormwater management, acquisition and construction projects, and advancement of innovative restoration technologies to achieve cleaner, safer water in the Bay watershed. The program incorporates updated science from the Comprehensive Evaluation of System Response (CSER) report and serves as a key funding source for the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership. The program incorporates co-benefits into project selection to promote holistic projects and seeks applications providing cost-effective and measurable nonpoint source pollution reductions along with co-benefits including restoration of aquatic resources, climate resilience, carbon sequestration, wildlife habitat creation, local employment opportunities, recreational opportunities, and environmental justice benefits. The program works with local and federal partners to leverage funds, target cost-effective locations and practices, engage the community, and ensure accountability.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants, cost-sharing/incentive payments, and technical assistance provided to support non-point source pollution control and ecological restoration projects. Specific funding mechanisms include: cover crop programs ($11.25M), agricultural technical assistance ($6.59M), grants to farmers ($3.01M), manure management program ($1.75M), competitive grant program ($34.64M), natural filters on public lands ($6M), Tree Solutions Now Act ($2.5M and $1.25M), water management permit expediters ($850K), field restoration specialists ($850K), strategic monitoring and assessment ($550K), innovative technology fund ($1M), restoration research grants ($300K), and Whole Watershed pilot program ($5M). Projects supported include stream restoration, floodplain restoration, riparian buffer enhancement, wetland ecosystem improvement, stormwater management, acquisition and construction projects focused on decreasing nutrient and sediment pollution, and innovative restoration technologies. Funds are geographically targeted to reduce the greatest amount of pollution entering the Bay. Applicants can apply through the Grants Gateway, and technical assistance is available to local governments and non-governmental organizations.

Top funded counties (FY09-FY24) include Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Cecil, Montgomery, Prince George's, Baltimore City, Harford, Howard, and Carroll. structured_extraction.program_description: A single point of entry for Maryland organizations seeking technical and financial assistance to restore local waterways, increase resilience to climate impacts, strengthen local economies, and develop the next generation of environmental stewards. The program supports comprehensive and integrated projects that achieve specific environmental outcomes related to Chesapeake Bay restoration, coastal protection, and natural resource management. Funds local stormwater management, flood planning, restoration projects, shoreline erosion control, and work that builds resilience to climate change by fostering healthy ecosystems, communities, and economies. Supports Chesapeake Bay and coastal education and conservation programs. Grants and loans are funded through the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund, the Coastal Resiliency Program, the Waterway Improvement Fund, the Shoreline Erosion Control Revolving Loan Fund, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the Environmental Protection Agency's Chesapeake Bay Program.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and loans provided through multiple funding sources including the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund, the Waterway Improvement Fund, the Shoreline Erosion Control Revolving Loan Fund, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the Environmental Protection Agency's Chesapeake Bay Program. Technical assistance and site visits are available upon request. Shoreline erosion control loans are available on a rolling basis with terms ranging from 5-20 years (determined by project type) and an administrative fee on a 10%-3% sliding scale. Living shoreline projects are eligible; structural projects such as bulkheads and stone revetments are ineligible for loans. Support available for projects that achieve at least one of the specified program outcomes and foster healthy ecosystems, communities, and economies resilient to climate change. Supports Chesapeake Bay and coastal education and restoration programs.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the WCS Grants Gateway Portal at https://webportalapp.com/sp/grants_gateway. First-time users must create an account by clicking 'Sign Up.' Technical assistance and site visits are available upon request through the deadline. Different outcomes have different application deadlines. Three-step application process: Step 1 (Common Application/Proposal with project narrative, goals, applicant profile, project need/problem, partner roles, outreach strategy, sustainability plan, site visit information, and contractor status); Step 2 (Site/Task Description for each site); Step 3 (Budget submission with template). Applications are reviewed January through March, projects are selected April through May, applicants are notified May through July, and project funding begins July through October. For shoreline loan applications: submit Common Application with linked applicant profile. For HOA/community projects: submit HOA/Community Property Project Authorization form documenting community approval through proper channels. For landowner agreement projects: Project Leader applies for Trust Fund grant and executes Landowner Agreement (Form A or Form B) with property owner. Five-step guidance process for sea level rise projects: assess project characteristics, identify action points, select tide gauge, determine flood risk tolerance, select RSLR estimate. For wet pond retrofits: create CAST profile and scenarios for pre/post restoration conditions, run comparative analysis, document results, and upload documentation to Grants Gateway.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland-focused initiative that supports forest-related goals for the Coastal Bays region, which face stresses similar to the Chesapeake Bay but are not covered by the Chesapeake Bay Agreement. The program provides technical assistance and funding for riparian forest buffer installation and forest management in the five watersheds of the Coastal Bays region. The initiative improves forest inventory information, identifies forest trends, presents pest defoliation data, and provides technical assistance for riparian forest buffers to improve water quality and forest habitat. The program supports increased buffer planting from less than 3 miles per year prior to the grant to over 14 miles (216 acres) in 2001, substantially exceeding the 10-mile goal. Technical assistance also addresses forest stewardship planning, urban forestry for stormwater management, afforestation, easement programs, and sustainable forest management.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program dedicated to assisting Maryland's coastal communities in addressing short- and long-term coastal hazards such as high tide flooding, storm surge, and sea level rise. The program connects local government staff and partners to essential information, tools, training, and financial assistance to build resilience in coastal communities. It provides financial assistance through Outcome 2 of the Chesapeake and Coastal Grants Gateway, technical assistance to local communities, training opportunities for local practitioners, and access to resources and supportive networks to help communities become more resilient to coastal threats. The program includes guidance for developing Nuisance Flood Plans and selecting Relative Sea Level Rise estimates for coastal projects, with step-by-step frameworks for assessing coastal flood risk and incorporating probabilistic sea level rise projections into planning and site-specific projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance is provided through Outcome 2 of the Chesapeake and Coastal Grants Gateway. The program also offers technical assistance to local communities and training opportunities for local practitioners. Communities receive access to essential information, tools, visualizations, and supportive networks. Technical guidance includes a 5-step worksheet process for selecting Relative Sea Level Rise estimates and support for developing Nuisance Flood Plans to address tidal and precipitation-induced flooding. Sea level rise projection data and mapping tools are available for seven tide gauge locations in Maryland and DC (Ocean City, Annapolis, Solomons Island, Cambridge, Baltimore, Tolchester Beach, and Washington DC).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should visit the Chesapeake and Coastal Grants Gateway, which provides a one-stop location for communities seeking technical and financial support for resilience projects, and apply through that portal. Projects are evaluated based on flood risk tolerance assessment, project characteristics (community value, replacement cost, adaptation likelihood, public safety implications, inundation sensitivity), and alignment with coastal resilience principles.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program funded by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) through the Coastal Zone Management Act of 1972 that provides Maryland with the means to administer and implement its Coastal Zone Management Program through the Office of Ocean and Coastal Resource Management (OCRM). The program supports partnerships with local and state entities to develop programs, plans, and strategies addressing specific coastal issues. Maryland currently receives approximately $2.5 million annually in federal funds, with total funds awarded ranging from $4.5 to $4.7 million per grant cycle including both federal funds and non-federal match. Section 306 funding requires a dollar-for-dollar match from non-federal fund sources. Grants are generally 18 months in duration, running from October 1 of one year to March 31 two years out. Funding supports acquisition and construction projects, coastal zone enhancement projects, creation of new enforceable coastal policies, reducing community vulnerability to sea level rise, and implementing the Coastal Nonpoint Source Pollution Program. Projects are reimbursed for funds expended once work is completed, typically within 12-month contract periods.

structured_extraction.program_name: Communicating About Climate Change with Confidence
structured_extraction.program_description: A training program that teaches teachers, park staff, nonprofit workers, and public-facing professionals communication techniques including values, metaphors, art, storytelling, and solutions-focused messaging to build confidence in addressing climate change and support collective behavior change for climate action. The program is offered in flexible formats ranging from minimum 90 minutes (with 3 hours preferred) to two-day in-person intensive training sessions. Instruction is provided by National Network for Ocean and Climate Change Interpretation (NNOCCI) facilitators on strategic framing and solutions-focused climate messaging. Participants learn a toolkit of communication techniques to address climate change in public interactions and receive vetted and reliable resources for productive climate conversations.
