Two-day programs are facilitated by National Network for Ocean and Climate Change Interpretation (NNOCCI) facilitators.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teachers, park staff, nonprofit workers, educators, communicators, and anyone who addresses climate in public interactions or seeks to improve climate change communication skills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in climate communication techniques focused on values, metaphors, art, storytelling, strategic framing, and solutions-focused messaging
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Coreen Weilminster at Coreen.weilminster@maryland.gov to learn more and arrange training, or contact the Maryland Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve or National Network for Ocean and Climate Change Interpretation (NNOCCI) to enroll in two-day programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Forestry Catalyst Fund (CF2) welcomes proposals that directly support tree planting projects or increase the capacity of organizations to scale up their tree planting and maintenance initiatives in overburdened, underserved communities across Maryland. The program aims to reduce barriers to tree planting and provide local partners with flexible access to funds that can be leveraged to secure additional resources without requiring matching funds. Grants are awarded through three tracks: Track A (Site Readiness) provides $5,000 to $50,000 for activities like stump removal, hazardous tree removal, vegetation removal, and concrete removal leading to tree planting; Track B (Implementation) provides $5,000 to $50,000 for tree planting projects with optional post-planting maintenance add-on; Track C (Capacity Building) provides $50,000 to $250,000 per year for activities like staff support, workforce development, pilot programming, and capacity expansion. Matching funds are waived for all eligible projects in disadvantaged communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided through three tracks: Track A (Site Readiness) provides $5,000 to $50,000 for site preparation activities including stump removal, hazardous tree removal, vegetation removal, and concrete removal. Track B (Tree Planting Implementation) provides $5,000 to $50,000 for tree planting projects with optional post-planting maintenance add-on. Track C (Capacity Building) provides $50,000 to $250,000 per year for enhancing organizational internal capacity including strategic planning, contractual support, and pilot programming. Matching funds are waived for all eligible projects in disadvantaged communities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monday, September 15, 2025 at 11:59 PM EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government entities, federally recognized tribes and tribal organizations, non-profit organizations, public and state-controlled institutions of higher education, and community-based organizations working in disadvantaged communities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must directly or indirectly result in trees being planted in disadvantaged communities. Eligible activities include stump removal, hazardous tree removal, vegetation removal, concrete removal, tree planting, post-planting maintenance planning, volunteer coordination, staff support, contractual support, workforce development, capacity expansion, and pilot programming for green jobs and forestry initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: 100 percent of work must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities identified in the Inflation Reduction Act Disadvantaged Communities Map (archived Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool).
requirements_list: Projects must be located within or serve disadvantaged communities identified in the IRA Disadvantaged Communities Map
100 percent of work must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities
Matching funds are waived for all eligible projects
Tree planting projects (Track B) require pre-application technical assistance from Maryland Forest Service or authorized representative from 5 Million Trees for Maryland partnership agencies
Applications under Track C cannot be combined with Tracks A or B
Tracks A and B may be submitted together
Project must result in trees being planted in disadvantaged communities
Executive Officer and Project Leader must be two separate individuals from organization (not contractors)
Two-year maintenance plan required addressing watering, mulching, pruning, pest/disease monitoring, climbing invasives management, leaf removal strategy, and care/mowing coordination
Project Leader email must match submission email in online system
Final report with receipts, invoices, and timesheets required (10% of award held until approved)
Organizations with outstanding reports ineligible for future grants
Partner commitment letters encouraged
Budget justification narrative required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through an online system managed by Chesapeake Bay Trust. The application system includes eligibility quiz, applicant information tabs, and other required sections. Applicants can contact the CBT Program Officer for questions about the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Community Parks and Playgrounds Program invests in the future of established communities by developing and revitalizing parks and playgrounds statewide. This grant funding program provides financial assistance to municipal corporations and Baltimore City to restore existing park and green space systems and create new ones. The program offers flexible grants to local governments to rehabilitate, expand or improve existing parks, create new parks, develop environmentally oriented parks and recreation projects, purchase and install playground equipment, develop or extend trails, create water recreation access points, and purchase land for new parks in older neighborhoods and intensely developed areas. Grants can fund up to 100 percent of the proposed project with no local matching funds required, though they are welcome. The program is reimbursable, meaning applicants must pay costs upfront before receiving reimbursement. Partial project reimbursements are permitted to help with cash flow. The program is funded primarily through State General Obligation Bonds. In FY'26, $5 million was approved to fund 26 projects. A total of $97.4 million has been approved so far for 908 parks and playground projects statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant program providing flexible capital funding to local governments for park and playground projects. Grants can fund up to 100 percent of the proposed project with no local matching funds required, though they are welcome. The program is reimbursable, meaning grant recipients pay costs upfront and receive reimbursement. Partial project reimbursements are permitted to help with cash flow. Applicants can request reimbursement for project costs up to the amount approved by the Board of Public Works. Eligible costs include design, construction, land acquisition, appraisals, surveys, title work, closing costs, playground surfacing materials, contract costs, direct purchases (supplies, materials, services, equipment rental), and force account/in-house labor and equipment costs. Grant funds are for capital projects with a minimum 20-year lifespan (or perpetuity for land acquisition). Funding levels have varied from $2.5 million to $5.5 million annually across fiscal years 2002-2026. In FY'26, $5 million was approved to fund 26 projects. A total of $97.4 million has been approved so far for 908 parks and playground projects statewide.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, August 20, 2025 by 3:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Tiffany DePaoli; Katelyn Mayberry; Michael McQuarrie; Local Grants Staff
structured_extraction.program_audience: Governing bodies of municipal corporations and Baltimore City that can demonstrate capacity to plan, implement, and maintain projects with sufficient and qualified staff or contractors, effective administrative procedures and systems, and evidence of past success. Maryland municipalities and local communities seeking to develop and revitalize parks and playgrounds in established communities. Nonprofit organizations are encouraged to partner with applicants in project sponsorship and implementation. General public—facilities must be open to all persons regardless of race, color, religion, sex, age, handicap, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, or national origin.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects for park facilities and elements including developing new parks, rehabilitating or improving existing parks, purchasing and installing playground equipment, developing environmentally oriented parks and recreation areas, developing or extending trails, creating water recreation access points, and purchasing land for new parks in older neighborhoods and intensely developed areas. Funds cannot be used for operating and maintenance costs, contingency costs, or reserves. Development projects must have a minimum 20-year lifespan and acquisition projects must be maintained in perpetuity. Eligible costs include design, construction, appraisals, surveys, title work, closing costs, playground surfacing materials, and low-impact development techniques. Playground surfacing materials must not exceed 90 ppm lead and must not contain added PFAS chemicals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within municipal corporation boundaries or Baltimore City in older neighborhoods and intensely developed areas throughout the state. Project location must be within blue areas shown on CPP eligibility map. The municipality must own the property or hold development rights through an easement, long-term lease with more than 20 years remaining with no termination for convenience clause, or a project-specific Joint Use Agreement. Projects must be open and available to all users. Project elements cannot have been funded by CPP, Program Open Space (POS) Local grants in the last 20 years, or Local Parks and Playgrounds Infrastructure (LPPI) grants in the last 15 years.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a governing body of a municipal corporation or Baltimore City
Applicant must be a local government

Applicants must demonstrate capacity to plan, implement, and maintain projects with sufficient and qualified staff or contractors, effective administrative procedures and systems, and evidence of past success
Must either have a deed to the property held by the project applicant or provide a joint use agreement signed by the property owner

If project is on non-municipal property, municipality must hold development rights through easement, long-term lease (more than 20 years remaining with no termination for convenience clause), or Joint Use Agreement
Projects must be open and available to all users, not limited to specific groups or interest groups
For property acquisition, costs must be supported by two independent appraisals
Development projects must have a minimum 20-year lifespan
Acquisition projects must be maintained for public use in perpetuity
Projects must be completed as proposed at the location stated in the application
Projects cannot have been started prior to grant award
For playground projects, inclusive playgrounds must have four characteristics: accessible, adaptive to different needs, welcoming to bring people together, and promote emotional well-being
Must complete all required fields in the fillable application PDF and submit with all necessary attachments

Projects replacing facilities previously funded by Program Open Space Local or CPP programs must wait 20 years after the previous grant requirements ended, or 15 years for projects previously funded with a Local Parks and Playgrounds Infrastructure (LPPI) grant
Contingency costs or reserves are not eligible
Compliance with all Local, State, and Federal statutes and regulations
Facilities must be open for public use at all reasonable hours
Compliance with Title VII Civil Rights Act and ADA requirements
Projects must be operated and maintained for 20 years from Board of Public Works approval
Projects must be maintained in attractive, safe, and sanitary condition
Local Government must indemnify the Department
Violation of agreement may result in project replacement obligation
Playground surfacing must not exceed 90 ppm lead and must not contain added PFAS chemicals
Playgrounds must comply with National Playground Safety Standards and ADA requirements

Inclusive playground design must incorporate seven principles of Universal Design: equitable use, flexibility in use, simple and intuitive use, perceptible information, tolerance for error, low physical effort, and size and space for approach and use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the fillable Community Parks and Playgrounds Application and Project Agreement PDF, save it on your desktop, and complete all required fields. Submit the completed form along with all necessary attachments including property documentation (either a deed or joint use agreement) and project cost details using the Reimbursement Request form. Applications are submitted in August of any calendar year. Local grants staff prepare and distribute application materials and conduct grant writing workshops if needed. Completed applications are evaluated by Program Open Space Local staff and DNR staff. Recommendations are provided to the Secretary of DNR for possible inclusion in the Governor's budget. Following a State Clearinghouse review, selected projects are submitted to the Board of Public Works (BPW) for approval. Applicants are notified by May of the following calendar year whether their project was selected for the upcoming fiscal year's budget. After BPW approval, grant recipients are notified of the grant award. Grantees must retain all support documents for three years after final reimbursement. Grantees must comply with local government procurement procedures and all applicable Local, State, and Federal statutes and regulations. Since the program is reimbursable, grant recipients pay costs upfront before receiving reimbursement. Project Coordinator or Fiscal Authority signature is required for Payment Certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to support schools, nonprofits, and community organizations that engage community members in environmental education and stewardship, eliminate local environmental problems, encourage environmental stewardship, and develop innovative solutions to environmental challenges through hands-on, project-based learning, particularly engaging children and young adults in community stewardship and environmental education or community use initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $5,000 are awarded annually to eligible organizations for environmental education projects, community engagement, neighborhood greening, stewardship projects, litter prevention, and local beautification activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools, nonprofits, and other community organizations whose missions center on directly engaging community members, especially children and young adults, in environmental education and stewardship.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental education projects, community engagement activities, neighborhood greening, eliminating local environmental problems, hands-on project-based learning, litter prevention, local stewardship and beautification, natural area preservation, identifying and eliminating root causes of local environmental issues, and community sense of place.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a school, nonprofit, or other community organization
Organization's mission must center on directly engaging community members in environmental education and stewardship
Projects should develop innovative solutions to local environmental problems
Projects should activate citizens and encourage stewardship through education and outreach
Projects should elevate awareness of local environmental problems and work to reduce them
Organization must demonstrate active engagement as a defender of the environment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted for the annual grant cycle, though specific application procedures and deadlines are not detailed on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A $5.46 million fund established through a Memorandum of Understanding between Maryland DNR and US Wind, Inc. to compensate commercial and charter vessel owners, operators, and crew for direct economic losses and impacts from the construction, operation, and decommissioning of the US Wind offshore wind energy project. The fund is divided into three phases: Construction ($1,546,864), Operations ($1,893,510), and Decommissioning ($2,014,757). Compensation is provided on a claims-made basis, with individual amounts determined using historical and current federal and state fishery landings data from the offshore project area, regardless of home port.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct compensation for economic losses during three project phases: Construction ($1,546,864), Operations ($1,893,510), and Decommissioning ($2,014,757). Total fund of $5.46 million. Individual compensation amounts are determined based on historical and current vessel revenue data from federal and state fishery landings in the offshore project area (Lease Area OCS-A 0490, approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, Maryland in federal waters).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Claims must be made no later than two calendar years after the end of the applicable Project Period during which loss occurred; may be extended up to five years after loss date if data unavailable or good cause shown.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial and charter fishing vessel owners, operators, and crew members from Maryland and Delaware with a demonstrated, documented history of fishing in or near Lease Area OCS-A 0490 (approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, Maryland in federal waters off the Atlantic coast).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct compensation for negative economic impacts and losses attributable to construction, operation, and decommissioning of the offshore wind farm.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to commercial and charter fishing vessels from Maryland and Delaware regardless of home port, provided they have a demonstrated history of fishing in or near Lease Area OCS-A 0490 (approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, Maryland) in federal waters off the Atlantic coast of Delaware and Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a commercial or charter vessel owner, operator, or crew member
Must have a demonstrated, documented history of fishing in or near Lease Area OCS-A 0490
Must experience and document a direct economic loss or impact from offshore wind project construction, operation, or decommissioning
Individual compensation amount determined based on past landings from the affected area
Compensation provided on claims-made basis
Claims must be submitted within specified timeframe (two years after applicable project period, extensible to five years with good cause)
Participation is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible fishers must document economic impacts experienced from the offshore wind project to receive compensation. Funds become available during each project phase (construction, operations, decommissioning). Claims must be filed within two calendar years after the end of the applicable Project Period, with possible extension to five years if data is unavailable or good cause is shown. A Regional Fund Administrator administers the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cost-share program available to private landowners providing financial assistance for conservation practices and environmental improvements on agricultural and forestry land.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share program providing financial assistance to private landowners for conservation practices and environmental improvements on agricultural and forestry land.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners with agricultural or forestry land
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Conservation practices and environmental improvements on agricultural and forestry land
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide

structured_extraction.program_name: Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP) - State Perpetual Easement
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program for the purchase of perpetual easements on Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) land. A written legal agreement between a landowner and the State of Maryland to install or maintain conservation practices that protect water quality and natural resources on agricultural land. Landowners with existing federal CREP or CRP contracts agree to keep their land in approved conservation practices permanently after the federal contract expires. The state acquires a permanent interest in the land, which passes to all future owners. Landowners can increase their easement acreage to maximize land preservation and easement value. The easement is filed with county land records and remains effective in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state purchases perpetual conservation easements on eligible properties. Compensation is provided for contract acres, match acres, and whole-farm easements based on a valuation system. The conservation easement is a permanent legal document filed with county land records that restricts land use and requires the land to be maintained in the vegetation type indicated in the conservation plan. The landowner retains ownership of the property but agrees to maintain it according to the conservation management plan or forest stewardship plan specified in the easement. No structures may be built on enrolled lands. The easement is conveyed to a government agency or nonprofit conservation organization qualified to hold and enforce easements. Easements remain effective in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners who have an existing federal Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP) or Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) contract and have installed the prescribed conservation practices seeking to make them permanent through easements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensation for contract acres, match acres, and whole-farm easements based on valuation system to install or maintain conservation practices that protect water quality and natural resources on agricultural land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties are eligible as of January 2024. The program is available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a landowner
Landowner must have an existing federal CREP or CRP contract
Landowner must have installed the prescribed CREP or CRP conservation practice(s)
Land must be maintained in the approved conservation practice as defined in a conservation management plan or forest stewardship plan in perpetuity
Must agree to keep the land in an approved conservation practice permanently after the federal contract expires
Landowner is responsible for maintenance, upkeep, and taxes on the property
Must notify easement holder of proposed property changes
Must allow annual monitoring visits
Must notify easement holder when selling or transferring property
Must comply with easement restrictions
No structures may be built on the enrolled lands
Conservation easement is conveyed to a government agency or nonprofit conservation organization qualified to hold and enforce easements
Property must qualify for conservation easement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners with existing or expiring federal contracts work with the state to establish a perpetual conservation easement. Upon approval, the easement becomes permanent and remains effective in perpetuity. The easement is documented in a legal agreement that is filed with county land records and applies to all current and future owners of the property. For specific application procedures and requirements, applicants should contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: Agreement between Maryland Environmental Trust (MET) and local land trusts to work cooperatively on land conservation. Enables land trusts to access benefits under Maryland law and MET's Land Trust Assistance Program. Facilitates communication and cooperation among Maryland's land conservation organizations. Provides access to the Land Trust Assistance Program including educational opportunities, stewardship assistance, and conservation initiatives. Eligible organizations gain access to state benefits including the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program, Land Trust Grant Fund, Program Open Space, Rural Legacy Program, Greenspace Equity Program, property tax exemptions, and other tax credits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Establishes a formal cooperative agreement that sets out the relationship between Maryland Environmental Trust and a land trust organization to clarify roles and establish common understanding for collaborative land conservation work. Provides access to the Land Trust Assistance Program including educational opportunities, stewardship assistance, and conservation initiatives. Enables land trusts to seek benefits including Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program, Land Trust Grant Fund, Program Open Space, Rural Legacy Program, Greenspace Equity Program, state property tax exemptions, and property tax credits. Provides Written Certification for property tax exemptions and credits on fee-owned land.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 30 days before Land Trust Outreach Committee meeting
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable land trusts incorporated in any state and operating in Maryland seeking to formalize partnerships with Maryland Environmental Trust
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing collaborative framework for land conservation and stewardship
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: State of Maryland; available to charitable land trusts with geographic focus areas within Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a charitable land trust incorporated in any state
Must be tax-exempt under IRC Section 501(c)(3)
Must be a 'qualified organization' under IRC Section 170(h)(3)
Must maintain 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status and 'qualified organization' status
Must be in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must adopt Land Trust Alliance's Land Trust Standards and Practices (2017)
Must have Records Policy for document retention and protection
New requests require review and approval by the Land Trust Outreach Committee and MET's Board of Trustees
Requests must be submitted at least 30 days in advance of an LTOC meeting
Must provide: IRS documentation, board resolution, Conflict of Interest Policy, Records Policy, Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, and project-selection criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a request for a Cooperative Agreement at least 30 days before an LTOC meeting for review and approval. Contact the Land Trust Assistance Manager for more information. Meeting dates are posted online.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit program that allows landowners, agricultural lessees, and designated employees to request DNR investigation of severe deer damage for population reduction purposes. The Wildlife and Heritage Service investigates legitimate damage to commercial farm crops, orchards, nurseries, and woodland areas with forest management or planting plans, and authorizes deer management activities on eligible properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DNR investigates severe deer damage and, if warranted, reduces deer population in the affected area. Permittees are authorized to take a specified number of antlerless deer (with limited exceptions for antlered deer). Deer must be utilized by the permittee/agents or donated to others, with donation to charitable food programs encouraged.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, agricultural lessees, designated employees, and woodland managers experiencing severe deer damage to commercial farm crops, orchards, nurseries, and managed forests.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deer must be utilized by the permittee/agents or donated to others, with encouragement for donation to charitable food programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program available in all counties. Specific regulations vary by county and Deer Management Region. County-specific staff contacts are provided for: Kent, Queen Anne's, Caroline, Wicomico, Somerset, Worcester, Dorchester, Talbot, Charles, Prince George's, Anne Arundel, Calvert, St. Mary's, Baltimore, Harford, Cecil, Carroll, Howard, Montgomery, Garrett, Allegany, Washington, and Frederick counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a landowner, agricultural lessee, or designated employee (W-2 form recipient)
Applicant must demonstrate severe deer damage and economic loss
Damage must be to commercial farm crops, orchards, nurseries, or woodland areas with forest management or planting plans
Landowner permission required for lessees and employees applying
Permittee and all agents must possess valid Maryland hunting license and firearm
Must meet Maryland Hunter Education and Safety Requirement
No Natural Resources violations within 2 years prior to application
DNRid numbers required for all agents
Background checks performed on all agents
Blaze orange required when using firearms or during deer seasons
Comply with distance requirements from buildings (150 yards/50-100 yards depending on county and weapon type)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Wildlife and Heritage Service staff responsible for your county during normal business hours. To schedule a wildlife permit appointment, email wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or call 410-260-8540. The Tawes State Office Building is open by appointment only.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit issued by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Wildlife and Heritage Service that allows the permittee to conduct deer carcass removal and handling operations on private land in Maryland. The permit fee is $100 and expires 1 year from the date of issuance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The permit allows the holder to conduct deer carcass removal and handling operations on private land. The permit fee is $100 and expires 1 year from the date of issuance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and organizations seeking to conduct deer carcass removal and handling operations on private land in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deer carcass removal and handling operations on private land. The applicant must specify the method they will use to dispose of a deer carcass at the time of application.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Private land in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must provide the Department with the method they will use to dispose of a deer carcass at the time of application
Permit is valid for 1 year from date of issuance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Deer Salvage Permit Application Form by email, phone, or mail to the Wildlife Permit Coordinator. Walk-in customers are not accepted without a confirmed appointment; schedule appointments by email at wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or by phone at 410-260-8540.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual award program that supports black bass fishing tournaments and recognizes youth conservation efforts by providing supplies and recognition to tournament directors who demonstrate commitment to bass conservation and watercraft safety.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Winners receive supplies (such as fish redistribution waiver, scales, rulers, cull clips, barbless tackle, thermometers, life jackets, aerators, ice, mesh bags, shade canopy, cattle tank, rubber nets, or weigh-in systems) with a maximum supply cost of up to $500, plus a Certificate of recognition. Up to two awards are given per year. Participants who complete the online Bass Class receive a Certificate of Completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: by May 1, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Black bass tournament organizers and co-organizers who are Maryland residents; Youth anglers ages 16 to 25; Tournament participants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment and supplies that promote fish survival and boater safety during tournaments, such as fish redistribution waiver, scales, rulers, cull clips, barbless tackle, thermometers, life jackets, aerators, ice, mesh bags, shade canopy, cattle tank, rubber nets, or weigh-in systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents who are tournament organizers or co-organizers.
requirements_list: Tournament organizer or co-organizer applicant must be a Maryland resident
All tournament participants must have a Maryland fishing license if required by law
Tournament may have at most 49 boats
At least 50% of angler participants must be between 16 and 25 years old, inclusive
Organizer or co-organizer must identify at least one best management practice when obtaining tournament permit from Fishing and Boating Services
All tournament participants must complete Fishing and Boating Services' online Bass Class including boater safety and conservation videos
Organizer or co-organizer must submit a 100-word narrative describing supply needs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application electronically to ryan.gary@maryland.gov by May 1, 2025. Applicants will be notified of their standing by June 1, 2025. Supplies will be purchased by the department on behalf of winners beginning July 1, 2025, and awards will be distributed by August 1, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provided grant funding to volunteer fire departments for the installation of dry fire hydrants in rural areas. Dry fire hydrants are non-pressurized pipe systems permanently installed in water sources such as lakes, streams, or ponds that allow firefighters to draft water for fire suppression operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding was provided to volunteer fire departments for the installation of dry fire hydrants. The program operated from 2003 to 2007 as part of a federal State Fire Assistance hazard mitigation grant and installed 114 new dry hydrants across the state.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Volunteer fire departments in rural areas of Maryland seeking to improve water availability for fire suppression.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of dry fire hydrants in water sources such as lakes, streams, and ponds to provide reliable water sources for fire suppression operations in areas without pressurized fire hydrant systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rural areas of Maryland without pressurized fire hydrant systems.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Forest Service provides financial assistance to public land managers, local governments, and conservation land managers for treating ash trees infested with Emerald Ash Borer. The program covers half the cost of effective trunk injection treatments with emamectin benzoate, a pesticide application that must be conducted by licensed pesticide applicators. The program also provides educational guidance for homeowners on protecting ash trees through insecticide treatment options, including information on identifying ash trees, recognizing infestation signs, treatment recommendations, insecticide options, application methods, environmental protection measures, and cost-benefit analysis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 50/50 cost share for trunk injection treatments with emamectin benzoate on public land. Treatments must be conducted by licensed pesticide applicators. The program covers half the cost of treatment expenses. The program also provides information on identifying ash trees, recognizing EAB infestation signs, treatment recommendations, insecticide options (soil drenches, trunk injections, bark sprays), application methods, environmental protection measures, and cost-benefit analysis. Trees must have less than 30% canopy loss for treatment success. Treatment timing varies by product (spring late April-late May or fall). Applications must avoid areas within 25 feet of water bodies and should not occur during heavy rainfall or when soil is frozen or saturated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public land managers, local governments, conservation land managers, and homeowners with ash trees in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Treatment of ash trees infested with Emerald Ash Borer using trunk injections, soil drenches, or bark sprays with insecticide applications. For public land managers and local governments, treatments must use emamectin benzoate applied by licensed applicators under a 50/50 cost share.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to public land managers, local governments, conservation lands, and homeowners throughout Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a public land manager, local government, conservation land manager, or homeowner
Must use licensed pesticide applicators for trunk injection treatments
Treatment must use trunk injections with emamectin benzoate for cost-share assistance
50/50 cost share structure for public land managers and local governments
Trees must have less than 30% canopy loss for treatment success
Treatment timing: spring (late April-late May) or fall for some products
Avoid application within 25 feet of water bodies
Do not apply when heavy rainfall expected within 24 hours
Do not apply when soil is frozen or saturated
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Forest Service for information on cost share programs. Homeowners should report infested trees to extension.umd.edu/hgic and consult with licensed professionals for treatment options.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit required for properly accredited persons of known scientific attainment to collect rare, threatened, or endangered species from the wild for scientific or educational purposes, or to capture, mark, and release such species. Public educational institutions also need this permit to salvage and maintain rare, threatened, or endangered specimens for educational purposes. The permit authorizes qualified individuals and public educational institutions to collect, capture, mark, release, salvage, and maintain rare, threatened, or endangered animal and plant species. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Wildlife and Heritage Service and relies on comprehensive lists of rare, threatened, and endangered animals and plants of Maryland to determine species eligibility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Issuance of a permit valid through December 31 of the issuing year, allowing collection, capture, marking, release, salvage, and maintenance of rare, threatened, or endangered animal and plant species for scientific or educational purposes. The permit also supports species identification, conservation status documentation, and guidance on rare species documentation and reporting for citizens submitting observations of rare, threatened, or endangered species. Applicants must pay a $10 fee (check or money order payable to Department of Natural Resources) and submit an annual report by December 31. Failure to submit an annual report may result in revocation of existing permits or rejection of future applications.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: (410) 260-8540, Toll-free in Maryland: 1-877-620-8DNR, TTY: Maryland Relay via 1-800-735-2258 or 711
structured_extraction.program_audience: Properly accredited persons of known scientific attainment seeking to collect rare, threatened, or endangered species for scientific or educational purposes; public educational institutions; scientists, naturalists, researchers, conservation partners; general public; individuals who observe rare species; conservation professionals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorization to collect, capture, mark, release, salvage, and maintain rare, threatened, or endangered animal and plant species from the wild for scientific or educational purposes. Also supports species monitoring and documentation, conservation status assessments, habitat protection, and species identification documentation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Rare, threatened, or endangered species are those with specific State Status designations on the List of Rare, Threatened, and Endangered Animals of Maryland (526 native species) or the List of Rare, Threatened, and Endangered Plants of Maryland (741 native species). These lists include species on the federal Endangered Species Act list, state Threatened and Endangered Species list, and species considered rare or under assessment.
requirements_list: Must be a properly accredited person of known scientific attainment
Must complete an Endangered Species permit application
Must pay a $10 fee (check or money order payable to Department of Natural Resources)
Must file an annual report by December 31 of the issuing year; failure to submit may result in revocation of existing permits or rejection of future applications
May need to obtain a federal permit from the United States Fish & Wildlife Service and/or United States Department of Agriculture for migratory birds or federally listed species
May need a Scientific Collection permit and/or an Aquatic (Fisheries) Scientific Collection permit depending on collection methodology and target species
Species must be listed on the Maryland rare, threatened, and endangered animals or plants list to be protected under permit/license requirements
GPS location details or precise written directions required for rare species reports
Photography and species description documentation required for rare species reports
Identification source documentation required for rare species reports
Habitat description required for rare species reports
Complete all pages of application
Provide project proposal with reason for study, objectives, and justification
Specify collection methods
List species by common and scientific names with numbers, age classes, and sex
Specify geographic areas and time period for collection
Specify final disposition of specimens
List all additional collectors beyond applicant
Provide personal information including SSN/Tax ID/FID
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an Endangered Species permit application form and submit it along with a $10 check or money order (payable to Department of Natural Resources) to the Permits Coordinator at MD DNR - Wildlife and Heritage Service, Tawes State Office Building, 580 Taylor Ave E-1, Annapolis MD 21401. Applications can also be submitted by email to wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or by phone at (410) 260-8540. The Tawes State Office Building is open by appointment only. Citizens can also submit information on rare, threatened, or endangered species observations via downloadable PDF form or online at dnr.maryland.gov/wildlife/Pages/plants_wildlife/rte_reportinginst.aspx.

structured_extraction.program_name: Explore the Patuxent Teen Leadership Paddle
structured_extraction.program_description: A week-long canoeing expedition for high school students that combines outdoor adventure with environmental education. Participants practice leadership and teamwork skills while navigating the Patuxent River, conducting water quality tests, studying plant communities, completing stewardship projects, and camping riverside. The program includes instruction in paddle safety, leadership skills, environmental science, and outdoor stewardship. The program culminates in a presentation to community leaders, families, and friends.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a subsidized environmental education and leadership training experience for high school students. Tiered pricing is available: Tier III at $200 (heavily subsidized), Tier II at $250 (partially subsidized), and Tier I at $300 (reflects full cost). Scholarships are available through Friends of Jug Bay for families needing additional assistance beyond Tier III pricing. The program includes instruction in paddle safety, leadership skills, water quality testing, environmental science, and outdoor stewardship. Tiered pricing subsidizes operational costs including staff, utilities, food, maintenance, and administrative expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, first come, first served basis; applications close when all spots are filled
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students interested in outdoor adventure, environmental education, and leadership development
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program participation covers the week-long canoeing expedition, meals, camping, instruction, water quality testing supplies, and educational programming. Activities include canoeing, leadership skill building, water quality testing, plant community study, stewardship project work, riverside camping, and meal preparation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Based at Patuxent River Park in the Patuxent River area in Prince George's County, Maryland. Statewide participation is accepted.
requirements_list: Must be a high school student
COVID-19 vaccination is recommended for all participants and staff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online via a Google Form at https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfTrwMkMEapIBnt6UIQ3TzA5J6ei4ydCKNbe-RDWKiI2qct5g/viewform?usp=dialog. Applications are reviewed on a rolling, first come, first served basis. Interested students should apply as soon as possible to secure their spot. For questions or scholarship inquiries, contact the program coordinator by email.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Estate Tax Benefit for Conservation Easements
structured_extraction.program_description: Landowners who donate a conservation easement can reduce their taxable estate since the easement limits development potential and lowers the appraised value of the land. Additionally, there is an estate tax exclusion of up to 40% of land value (maximum $500,000 per owner) for certain land subject to a donated easement, allowing the land to be partially shielded from estate taxes.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Conservation easements reduce the appraised value of land for estate tax purposes by limiting development potential. An estate tax exclusion of up to 40% of land value (maximum $500,000 per owner) is available for qualifying land subject to a donated easement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with estates who donate conservation easements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Estate tax reduction through lowered land valuation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies to land subject to conservation easements donated to qualifying organizations
requirements_list: Land must be subject to a donated conservation easement
Easement must meet federal requirements for estate tax purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Conservation easement donation affects estate valuation automatically upon the easement being recorded and approved.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Income Tax Deduction for Conservation Easement Donations
structured_extraction.program_description: Landowners who donate a conservation easement to a qualified organization can deduct the appraised value of the easement from their federal income taxes. The deduction may be taken in one year if the value is 50% or less of adjusted gross income, or spread over up to 15 years if greater. Qualified farmers or ranchers may deduct up to 100% of adjusted gross income. This federal tax benefit is governed by Internal Revenue Code Section 170(h) and 26 CFR § 1.170A–14, allowing donors to claim charitable income tax deductions for the fair market value of perpetual conservation easements donated to qualified organizations.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The easement value is determined by a qualified appraiser using a before-and-after valuation method, calculating the difference between the property's fair market value before the easement and after easement restrictions are imposed. If the value is 50% or less of adjusted gross income, it may be deducted entirely in one year. If greater, it may be deducted over up to 15 years. For qualified farmers or ranchers, the maximum deduction increases to 100% of adjusted gross income. The deduction is reduced if the donation increases the value of other property owned by the donor or related persons, and no deduction is allowed if the donor receives greater financial benefit than the general public.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 17, 2007 (for submission of comments on guidance)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual property owners and entities with qualified real property interests seeking federal income tax deductions for donations of conservation easements to qualified organizations including Maryland Environmental Trust, governmental units, and qualified 501(c)(3) charitable organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Conservation purposes as defined by the Internal Revenue Service, including outdoor recreation or education of the general public, protection of relatively natural habitat of fish, wildlife, plants or similar ecosystems, preservation of open space including farmland and forest land, and preservation of historically important land areas or certified historic structures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Real property must be located within United States jurisdictions. The easement must be conveyed to Maryland Environmental Trust, a governmental unit, or a qualified 501(c)(3) charitable organization with commitment and resources to enforce the easement. Conservation purposes must yield significant public benefit and further clearly delineated governmental policy.
requirements_list: Contribution must be of qualified real property interest (entire property interest, remainder interest, or perpetual use restrictions)
Easement must be donated exclusively for conservation purposes
Easement must be conveyed to a governmental unit or qualified 501(c)(3) charitable organization
Perpetual conservation restriction must be enforceable in perpetuity through legal restrictions
Qualified appraiser must establish the value of the easement using before-and-after valuation method
Written agreement between donor and donee is required
IRS Form 8283 must be attached to federal income tax return

Form 8283 must include a statement identifying conservation purposes, showing before and after property values, stating whether donation was required by contract or for permit approval, and describing any related property interests
If donation value exceeds $500,000, copy of appraisal must be provided to IRS
Property condition documentation including maps, photographs, and surveys required
Mortgagee must subordinate rights to donee organization's enforcement rights
Surface mining generally prohibited unless probability is negligible or pre-1976 separation exists
Donor must agree to notify donee before exercising reserved rights
Donee must have right to inspect property and enforce restrictions
For historic preservation: property must be certified historic structure or historically important land area with photographs and restriction descriptions required
No inconsistent uses that destroy other significant conservation interests (with limited exceptions)
Appraisals required for noncash charitable contributions exceeding $5,000
Appraiser must be qualified appraiser with relevant education and experience
Appraisal must comply with generally accepted appraisal standards (USPAP)
For real property: appraiser must be licensed/certified in the state where property is located
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain a qualified appraiser to determine the easement value using before-and-after valuation methodology. 2. Negotiate easement terms with qualified conservation organization. 3. Execute written agreement between donor and donee establishing conservation purposes and enforceability. 4. Complete IRS Form 8283 and required statement including property condition documentation, maps, photographs, and surveys. 5. Submit Form 8283 and statement to qualified organization for donee acknowledgement signature. 6. Qualified organization will return the form for submission to the IRS. 7. Attach completed Form 8283 to your federal income tax return. 8. Provide copy of appraisal to IRS if donation value exceeds $500,000.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration Boating Access Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration grant program that funds the construction and renovation of publicly owned boat ramps used by recreational trailered motorboats. The program is administered by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and implemented in Maryland by the Waterway Improvement and Infrastructure Program. Funding comes primarily from excise taxes on fishing equipment and motorboat and small engine fuels. Maryland receives approximately $500,000 per year in Sport Fish Restoration funding for boating access, with at least 15% of each state's apportionment required to go towards boating access projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants for construction and renovation of publicly owned boat ramps used by recreational trailered motorboats. Funding comes from excise taxes on fishing equipment and motorboat and small engine fuels. Maryland receives approximately $500,000 per year in Sport Fish Restoration funding for boating access, with at least 15% of each state's apportionment required to go towards boating access projects.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jennifer Jackson, Federal Boating Access Program Projects Lead
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public jurisdictions and government agencies in Maryland seeking to develop or improve public boating access through boat ramp construction and renovation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and renovation of publicly owned boat ramps used by recreational trailered motorboats.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a publicly owned entity
Projects must involve construction or renovation of boat ramps
Boat ramps must be for recreational trailered motorboats
Must serve recreational, trailered motorboats
Projects must involve publicly owned boat ramps
Projects must be for recreational, trailered motorboats
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Federal Boating Access Program Projects Lead for application information and procedures. Detailed information about Maryland's Boating Access Program and the application process is available through the program documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Permit program for operating fee fishing lakes/ponds in Maryland where the public pays to fish. A permit that grants permission to establish and operate a fee-fishing facility on privately-controlled ponds or lakes where paying customers can catch and keep fish without needing a Maryland Recreational Fishing License. Fish must be artificially propagated by commercial hatcheries or purchased from licensed sellers. The annual permit costs $25 and allows fish to be taken without regard to seasons, creel, or possession limits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Authorization to operate a fee fishing facility with regulated stocking and record-keeping requirements. An annual regulatory permit issued for $25 (payable by check, money order, or electronic payment through shopdnr.com) that authorizes the operation of a fee-fishing facility on privately-controlled ponds or lakes. The permit allows fish to be taken without regard to seasons, creel, or possession limits, and customers may fish without obtaining a Maryland Recreational Fishing License. Permits renew at the beginning of the calendar year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Permits renew at the beginning of the calendar year (February/March)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fee fishing facility operators, Rod & Gun Clubs, and private pond/lake operators seeking to offer public fee-based fishing services; fishing enthusiasts seeking public access for fee-based fishing on private ponds or lakes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The $25 annual permit fee authorizes operation of a fee-fishing facility where paying customers can fish without a Maryland Recreational Fishing License.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Applicants must own, lease, or control the pond or lake where fishing will occur.
requirements_list: $25 annual permit fee
Submit location map and directions from nearest major road
Submit facility description and sketch showing ponds, inflow, and effluent
Workmen's compensation certificate if employing staff
Fish must be artificially propagated by commercial hatcheries or purchased from licensed sellers
All fish removed must be identified by metal tag or bill of sale if transported by tank
Invasive or nonnative species listed in COMAR 08.02.19 must be euthanized onsite and not returned to any Maryland body of water
Maintain shipping and receiving records by species at the facility or other specified location
All fish received must be from an approved supplier
A fish stocking permit must be obtained prior to stocking additional fish
Notify the Department of Natural Resources immediately upon discovery of disease affecting fish at the facility
Submit annual activity report
Complete and timely compliance with all applicable conditions and state, federal, and local laws required
Must stock approved fish species
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Fee Fishing Lake Permit application form (available online or in PDF) with required documents including location map and directions from nearest major road, and facility description and sketch showing ponds, inflow, and effluent. Include workmen's compensation certificate if employing staff. Pay the $25 annual permit fee by check, money order, or through the online payment system at shopdnr.com. Mail application and supporting materials to: DNR Fishing and Boating Services B-2, 580 Taylor Ave., Annapolis MD 21401. Applications and inquiries may be sent to paylakes.dnr@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Training program that provides participants with the skills and knowledge to run beginner fishing lessons through their organization. Participants who complete the training qualify to borrow fishing gear from the state for extended use at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training program available Tuesday through Thursday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, November through April. Participants who complete the training develop skills and knowledge to conduct beginner fishing lessons. Upon completion, organizations qualify to borrow fishing equipment from the state at no cost for extended use in their fishing programs. Equipment must be reported on, maintained properly, and returned upon completion of lessons. Training must be scheduled in advance, with limited availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth organizations, schools, scout troops, parks, nature centers, 4-H clubs, libraries, summer camps, and community groups seeking to teach beginner fishing lessons.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training to develop skills and knowledge for running beginner fishing lessons. Borrowed fishing equipment for conducting fishing lessons in participating organizations' programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have at least 10 participants to request training
All participants must be 18 years of age or older
All participants must have or acquire a fishing license prior to the training
Must report on use of borrowed equipment
Must maintain all borrowed equipment
Must return any borrowed equipment upon completion of fishing lessons
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations should contact Chelsea Kenworthy to request and schedule a training session. Training must be scheduled far in advance due to limited availability and may require booking a year in advance for a particular date or time of year. Training is available Tuesday through Thursday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, November through April.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training program for educators that teaches bird education and conservation. Participants attend a 3-6 hour workshop with certified trainers and receive an activity guide called Flying WILD: An Educator's Guide to Celebrating Birds. The guide is provided free upon workshop completion, or can be purchased directly from the Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies online store.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Educators attend a 3-6 hour workshop conducted by certified trainers. Participants receive an activity guide titled Flying WILD: An Educator's Guide to Celebrating Birds, which focuses on bird education and conservation. The guide is provided free upon workshop completion, or can be purchased directly from the Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies online store.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Educators seeking bird education and conservation training
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and educational materials for teaching bird education and conservation activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Two training partners exist in Maryland: Ward Museum of Wildfowl Art in Salisbury and Black Hill Nature Programs in Boyds.
requirements_list: Must be an educator
Must attend a 3-6 hour workshop with certified trainers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of the two training partners in Maryland to inquire about training opportunities. The Ward Museum of Wildfowl Art is located in Salisbury, and Black Hill Nature Programs is located in Boyds. Attend the workshop to receive the activity guide.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that awards $500 and $1,000 scholarships to college and graduate students pursuing careers in natural resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarships in amounts of $500 and $1,000 awarded to college and graduate students pursuing careers in natural resources. Specific scholarships and requirements are detailed on the scholarship program website.
structured_extraction.program_audience: College and graduate students pursuing careers in natural resources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational support for students pursuing natural resource careers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - open to Maryland students
requirements_list: Must be a college or graduate student
Must be pursuing a career in natural resources
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application details and requirements can be found at http://www.marylandforestryboards.org/scholarship.cfm

structured_extraction.program_description: The Forest Conservation and Management Program provides landowners and developers with financial incentives and technical assistance to conserve and responsibly manage forestland by offering reduced and stabilized property tax assessments. This program minimizes the loss of Maryland's forest resources during land development by making the identification and protection of forests and other sensitive areas an integral part of the site planning process. Landowners agree to manage their forest land according to a management plan prepared for the property. Participants receive a forest management plan prepared by a forester and must commit to a legally binding agreement for a minimum of fifteen years. The agreement is recorded in county land records and the forestland receives a reduced property tax assessment, generally at the agricultural rate, which remains frozen for the life of the agreement. The program also provides technical assistance to identify and protect forest resources and create forest management plans for private property during land development. Open land recently planted with tree seedlings can be included after one growing season. This program helps landowners maintain forest cover and commit to long-term stewardship while protecting water quality, soils, fish and wildlife habitat, and supporting rural economies.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enrollment is established through a Forest Conservation and Management Agreement (FCMA) between the landowner and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. The agreement is legally binding, recorded in county land records, and guided by a forest management plan prepared specifically for the property by a forester. The minimum term of an agreement is fifteen years. During this period, the forestland included in the agreement receives a reduced property tax assessment, generally at the agricultural rate, which remains frozen for the life of the agreement. The program also provides technical assistance to identify and protect forest resources and create forest management plans for private property during land development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and property owners, including developers, with five or more contiguous acres of forestland who are committed to long-term stewardship and responsible forest management.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program supports conservation and responsible management of forestland, including forested tracts, newly reforested land, and Christmas tree plantations, through property tax reduction and technical assistance for forest identification, protection, and creation of private property forest management plans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Approximately 1,300 agreements are currently in place covering more than 84,000 acres of forestland. Eligible land includes forested tracts, newly reforested land once it has completed one growing season, and Christmas tree plantations if the trees are harvested at maturity. Areas such as house sites, crop fields, and other non-forest open land are not eligible for enrollment.
requirements_list: Own five or more contiguous acres of forestland
Agree to a legally binding Forest Conservation and Management Agreement recorded in county land records
Follow a forest management plan prepared for the property
Commit to a minimum fifteen-year agreement term
Eligible land includes forested tracts, newly reforested land once completed one growing season, and Christmas tree plantations harvested at maturity
House sites, crop land, and other non-forest open spaces not eligible
If agreement is broken, back taxes are assessed retroactively to the beginning of the agreement
Landowner must agree to manage forest land according to an approved management plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To begin the application process, contact your local Maryland Forest Service office. Forestry staff are available to answer questions, explain program requirements, prepare or review forest management plans, and guide landowners through enrollment. Eligible landowners apply through Maryland Forest Service to enroll in the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A licensing program for businesses engaged in forest products operations, including sawmills, pulpwood and logging contractors, firewood dealers, mulch suppliers, land clearing companies, tree removal companies, and lumber brokers. License issued by the Department of Natural Resources to persons qualified to engage in commercial trade of forest products, including harvesting, transporting, selling or re-selling of forest products (trees, logs, pulpwood, firewood, bark, chips, shavings, sawdust). License required for any person engaged in a forest products business in Maryland. Applies to every type of forest products manufacturing plant. 1-year term license. Forest harvest operations that disturb more than 5,000 square feet or 100 cubic yards of soil must have an approved erosion and sediment control plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program issues Forest Product Operator Licenses to forest product operators. A 1-year term license is required to legally operate a forest products business in Maryland. License displays qualifications to engage in commercial trade of forest products. Applicants must submit an application form with personal information, company information, business type, products, and workers' compensation documentation. The application fee is $20.00 annually. Applicants can submit online via Submittable (preferred method), via hardcopy by mail, or through the Submittable platform. Existing license holders can renew if information remains unchanged. License renewals for 2026 are effective January 1, 2026 - December 31, 2026. Renewal applications open November 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On-time renewal deadline: 12/31/2025; Renewal opens November 1, 2025
structured_extraction.contact_name: Thomas C. Bradshaw, Forest Industry Development Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Any person or business engaged in forest products operations, including sawmills, pulpwood and logging contractors, firewood dealers, mulch suppliers, land clearing companies, tree removal companies, and lumber brokers. Current forest product operators requiring license renewal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: License allows operators to legally conduct forest products business activities, including harvesting, transporting, selling or re-selling of forest products.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; Maryland (with specific provisions for Garrett, Allegany, Washington, and Frederick counties regarding road cut/fill requirements). Special regulations apply within Chesapeake Bay Critical Areas and areas with Nontidal Wetlands. Property owners are advised to contact their local Maryland Forest Service office to learn about permitting requirements specific to their area.
requirements_list: Must be engaged in a forest products business
Forest harvest operations disturbing more than 5,000 square feet or 100 cubic yards of soil must have an approved erosion and sediment control plan
Applicants must submit application on Department-provided form and pay $20.00 license fee
Must demonstrate compliance with Maryland Workers' Compensation Act (Title 9, Labor and Employment Article)
Must report location of manufacturing plant prior to erection or relocation
Must provide Certificate of Insurance for Workers' Compensation or certify as sole proprietor with no employees
Current license holders must renew annually; renewal required by December 31 for upcoming license year
Approved Erosion and Sediment Control Plan required (Standard or Custom Plan) for operations disturbing more than 5,000 sq ft or 100 cubic yards
Streamside Management Zone (SMZ) protection and planning required (minimum 50 feet width on both banks of blue line streams)
Three/Seven day stabilization requirement for perimeter controls and slopes
Responsible personnel must complete MDE-approved training
Plan certification by a Licensed Professional Forester required for Custom Plans
Haul road grades not exceeding 15 percent; skid trail grades not exceeding 20 percent
Road cuts/fills not exceeding 3 feet (5 feet in Garrett, Allegany, Washington, and Frederick counties)
Landings located on 3-10 percent slopes, 50+ feet from waters of the state
Stabilized harvest entrances at public road junctions
Waterway Construction Permit may be required for stream crossings
Pre-harvest planning with topographic maps and site review required
Site maps must identify access points, landings, haul roads, waters of the state, and SMZs
Notification to inspection agency 3 business days before operations commence
Timber Harvest Plan prepared by Maryland Licensed Forester for harvests of 1+ acre within 1-year intervals in Critical Areas
100-foot minimum buffer around waterways and tidal wetlands
25-foot buffer around nontidal wetlands (NTW)
Identification of Habitat Protection Areas required
Maintain 85% plant cover or replant deficient areas within one year
Apply fertilizer per Maryland nutrient management regulations and soil test recommendations
Comply with all erosion and sediment control standards
Maintain documentation of site visits, decisions, specifications, and certifications
Operating without a current license is prohibited under Maryland law (Md. Code, Natural Resources § 5-608)
Retain sales transaction documentation for one year
Disclose license number in all advertisements
Avoid false/misleading advertising
Cooperate with DNR investigations
Report address/phone changes within 30 days
Cannot trespass on adjacent property
Ensure safe equipment operation
Protect public safety and welfare
Complete Department form indicating forest products production during previous calendar year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To become a licensed Forest Product Operator or renew an existing license, complete the application form with personal information, company information, business type, products, and workers' compensation documentation. Select primary business type and indicate secondary business types if applicable. Provide products bought/sold information and identify top 3 counties where timber harvested. Submit your application and payment online via Submittable (preferred method), download the PDF application form and send it as a hardcopy along with a check for the $20.00 license fee to the Maryland Forest Service address, or mail check payment with completed application. Renewal applications open November 1, 2025, with an on-time renewal deadline of December 31, 2025 for the 2026 license year. Current license holders can renew if information unchanged.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit required for any person who wants to raise, breed, protect, or sell native game birds in Maryland. The permit specifies which game bird species may be bred, raised, protected, or sold and for what purpose, and includes requirements for fencing and other measures to protect native wildlife.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Authorization to hold and manage specified game species. Permit/license issued with a fee of $5.00 (check payable to DNR). Permit expires December 31st following issuance date and requires annual renewal.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and businesses/organizations seeking to hold and manage native game species in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable - this is a licensing program, not a financial assistance program
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must intend to raise, breed, protect, or sell native game birds
Native game bird species covered include bobwhite quail, ring-necked pheasant, wild turkey, ruffed grouse, and waterfowl species regulated by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
Species covered may only be sold live to a person with a State permit to possess that species or dead for human consumption
Live birds may be purchased without a permit if kept for less than 48 hours
Licensee must maintain a ledger of species raised or acquired, number killed, and number sold
Ledger entries must be made within 48 hours of occurrence
Bill of sale or similar document must be kept as long as animal remains in possession
Licensee must allow Department inspections at any reasonable hour
Game birds shipped within State must be accompanied by itemized bill of sale
Game birds shipped out-of-state must have bill of lading attached to shipping container
Compliance with Maryland's Workmen Compensation Act (Article 1-401)
Provide either insurance binder number or certificate of insurance, OR certify self-employment/family-only employment
List species to be held and source of acquisition
List related state and federal licenses/permits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application form with required information and submit with $5.00 fee (check payable to DNR) to Permits Coordinator by email at wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov, by phone at 410-260-8540, or by mail to Permits Coordinator, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife and Heritage Service, 580 Taylor Ave., E-1, Annapolis MD 21401. Appointments are required at the Tawes State Office Building.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cost-share program available to private landowners that provides financial incentives for sustainable forest management practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share program providing financial incentives for sustainable forest management.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sustainable forest management practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners should contact the Forest Service for program details and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: A lifetime pass that provides free day-use entry to all Maryland state parks that charge service fees for seniors age 62 and older. The pass also provides half-price camping Sunday through Thursday (excluding holidays) and waives boat launching fees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Golden Age Pass costs $10 as a one-time processing fee and is a lifetime, non-transferrable pass. It provides free day-use entry to state parks charging service fees for the cardholder (or free entry for all in a vehicle when per-vehicle fees apply). The pass provides half-price camping rates for one site Sunday through Thursday excluding holidays (includes campsites and mini-cabins, excludes full-service cabins and houses), and waives boat launching fees.
