structured_extraction.program_description: The Greenspace Equity Program provides competitive grant funding to eligible applicants for enhancing public health and livability in overburdened and underserved communities by implementing projects to preserve, create, and improve public greenspace. Established in 2023 through state legislation and funded by the state share of Program Open Space, the program works with community groups and local partners including Baltimore Green Space, Audubon Baltimore Chapter, Charles County Resilience Authority, and Mobilize Frederick to increase access to green space in overburdened communities through collaborative partnerships. Applicants may request funding to acquire land in fee simple or perpetual conservation easement, undertake stewardship activities to develop property for public use, or obtain independent appraisals in advance of submitting an acquisition application. The appraisal funding supports preparation for land acquisition projects in overburdened and underserved communities, with applicants able to request funding for up to two independent appraisals for property that meets the general requirements of the program. Appraisal reports must meet Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP) requirements.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants that support greenspace projects including acquisition, preservation, creation, and improvement of public greenspace in overburdened and underserved communities through collaborative partnerships with community organizations and local partners. Grant amounts vary by funding round. Applicants can acquire land in fee simple or perpetual conservation easement, undertake stewardship activities to develop property for public use, or obtain funding to cover the costs of up to two independent appraisals for properties proposed for acquisition from certified general real estate appraisers. Appraisal funding available up to $100,000 for the appraisal grant round with up to 100% of appraisal project cost covered. Eligible costs include acquisition costs (land purchase, appraisals, environmental assessments, surveys, title work), site clearing or development for community greenspace, administrative costs (up to 3% of grant amount), and program compliance costs for easement monitoring (up to 1.5% of grant amount). Funds are provided on a reimbursable basis, meaning applicants pay upfront and request reimbursement. Partial project reimbursements are permitted. Applicants selected and approved for appraisal funding must procure and complete appraisals in time to submit an acquisition application for the respective funding round. Funding is authorized from the state share of Program Open Space subject to annual budget actions. Grants provided on competitive basis up to 100% of project cost.

structured_extraction.program_name: Income Tax Modification for Reforestation and Timber Stand Improvement
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides income tax deductions for taxpayers conducting reforestation and timber stand improvement practices on commercial forestland in Maryland. Based on Article 81, Section 280 C Annotated Code of Maryland and Natural Resources Regulation 08.07.03.04. Eligible participants can deduct the cost of reforestation and timber stand improvement practices from their Maryland income tax return, minus any cost-share assistance received through other programs. For supplemental practices, the eligible costs are doubled for tax calculation purposes. Practices must be certified by a Maryland Registered Professional Forester and must remain in effect for at least 15 years from Final Certification. Periodic inspections occur at 5-year intervals. If practices are not maintained, the tax savings must be repaid.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax deduction for eligible forest management practice costs. Initial practices are deductible after Initial Certification. Supplemental practices are deductible after Final Certification, with costs doubled for tax calculation purposes. The deduction is calculated as the total eligible costs for approved practices, reduced by any cost-share assistance already received through other programs such as WIP or EQIP. Eligible costs include: tools, machinery, depreciation, labor, consultant fees, chemicals, seed, seedlings, and fertilizer. Practices must remain in effect for at least 15 years from Final Certification and are subject to inspections at 5-year intervals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Forest owners and lessees in Maryland with 3 to 1,000 acres of commercial forestland capable of growing 20 cubic feet of wood per acre per year for the primary purpose of growing and harvesting trees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reforestation and timber stand improvement practices including planting, thinning, pruning, and site preparation on eligible forest land. Christmas tree and ornamental tree operations are not eligible. Reforestation must result in 400 or more healthy sprouts or seedlings per acre.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible landowners contact the Supervisor of Forest Stewardship or their local Maryland Department of Natural Resources forester. The application involves: (1) completing DNR Form 393 with taxpayer and property information, listing all forest management practices with associated costs and acreage; (2) having the practices certified by a Maryland Registered Professional Forester who must affix their professional seal; (3) obtaining Initial Certification from the Maryland Forest Service; (4) completing the forest management practices; (5) obtaining Final Certification from the Maryland Forest Service within 2 years; (6) submitting four copies of the completed form (one with the Maryland income tax return, one retained by the taxpayer, one to the forester, and one to the Maryland Forest Service); and (7) reporting the deduction on the Maryland tax return as a subtraction from federal adjusted gross income.

structured_extraction.program_name: Innovative Technology Fund - Research and Development and Seed Capital Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: State financing to support advancement of knowledge in areas impacting Bay restoration programs, processes, and policies. Funding supports students, faculty, and staff from the University of Maryland System and Maryland-based companies in developing and commercializing innovative technologies that accelerate Chesapeake Bay restoration through the reduction of non-point source nutrients, sediment, and greenhouse gas emissions. In partnership with the University of Maryland's Maryland Industrial Partnership Program (MIPS), the state funds research and development projects focused on developing technologies that reduce nutrient and sediment pollution in the Chesapeake Bay. The program has two components: the Research and Development fund provides awards from $30,000 to $100,000 to University of Maryland System participants, while the Seed Capital Fund provides awards from $50,000 to $450,000 to Maryland-based companies for development and commercialization. The program is a partnership between the State of Maryland, University of Maryland, EPA, and Maryland's Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund.

Grants for University of Maryland System participants range from $30,000 to $100,000, while grants for Maryland-based companies range from $50,000 to $450,000 for development and commercialization. The program supports development of successful Maryland businesses, creates and retains green jobs, and identifies cost-effective and efficient technologies for Bay restoration. Total annual funding of $1 million is available ($500,000 for grants and $500,000 for investments).

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants help nonprofit groups, communities, land trusts, schools, and youth organizations in Maryland support environmental education projects, litter removal, citizen stewardship, and protect natural resources in urban and rural areas. The program includes multiple tracks: Community Stewardship grant (up to $5,000), Capacity Building for Land Trusts grant (up to $10,000), Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands grant (up to $50,000 for large-scale projects over 2 acres; up to $10,000 for small-scale projects under 2 acres), and Bill James Environmental Grant (up to $1,000 for school groups, science clubs, ecology clubs, and nonprofit youth groups). The combined partnership has provided over $1 million over three decades, focusing on engaging residents, increasing equitable access to green space, and advancing ecological health. Total awards of $205,134 were distributed in 2026. Funds are to be used from March 30, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided through multiple tracks: Community Stewardship (up to $5,000), Capacity Building for Land Trusts (up to $10,000), Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands (up to $50,000 for large-scale projects over 2 acres or up to $10,000 for small-scale projects under 2 acres), and Bill James Environmental Grant (up to $1,000). Funds support environmental education, litter removal, citizen stewardship, tree planting, reforestation, riparian buffer establishment, forest tract creation and enhancement, and organizational capacity building. Total awards of $205,134 were distributed in 2026 to community organizations. Funds are available from March 30, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Uses include personnel costs, supplies, contractor/subcontractor services, professional development and training, GIS software and equipment, technology for baseline documentation and monitoring, easement processing, and related conservation activities. Award winners are announced on March 20 (Keep Maryland Beautiful Day), and grant money is received by April 15.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to build sustainable land trusts statewide. The program supports organizational capacity building, community program development, standards and practices implementation, and public engagement for conservation and stewardship activities. Up to $10,000 is awarded to Maryland land trusts to increase organizational capacity, support programming and innovation, and foster stronger, better-connected land trusts that protect natural resources and enhance the lives of Maryland citizens. The program includes an annual recognition award (Aileen Hughes Award) of up to $5,000 presented to an individual representing a Maryland land trust who has demonstrated outstanding leadership, partnership, and innovation in land conservation or organizational development. Funding under the Aileen Hughes Award is awarded to the land trust on behalf of the recognized individual. All grants require a 100 percent match from the land trust of in-kind services and privately raised funds. Formerly known as the Janice Hollmann Grant, the program has awarded 177 grants totaling over $545,000 to 45 Maryland land trusts, with participating land trusts providing matching funds exceeding $775,000.

structured_extraction.program_name: Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides matching grants to state and local government entities to acquire land and develop or renovate public outdoor recreation amenities and facilities. The program was authorized by Congress in 1965 and is administered nationally by the U.S. Department of Interior, National Parks Service, with revenues generated from offshore oil and gas leases. LWCF funding requires a 1:1 match with non-federal funds, with acceptable matching sources including Recreational Trails Fund, Community Development Block Grants, Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration, Program Open Space, and Community Parks and Playground grants. Funds are reimbursement-based and issued after project completion. Maximum grant request is $3,000,000 (for a $6,000,000 total project) and minimum request is $50,000 (for a $100,000 total project), though exceptions may be granted by the Department. Projects must be completed within 3 years of the award date with possibility of a 2-year extension. Maryland qualifies to receive this funding through its approved Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan. The program has funded over 400 projects in Maryland since inception and is intended to create and maintain quality public outdoor recreational resources while stimulating non-federal investments.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based matching grants at a 1:1 ratio with non-federal funds. Maximum grant request is $3,000,000 (for a $6,000,000 project); minimum request is $50,000 (for a $100,000 project), though exceptions may be granted by the Department. Acceptable federal matching sources include Recreational Trails Fund, Community Development Block Grants, Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration, Program Open Space, and Community Parks and Playground grants. Funds are issued after the project is completed and NPS approval. Applicants must incur 100% of total project cost upfront, with reimbursement occurring after project completion. Projects must be completed within 3 years of the award date with possibility of a 2-year extension.

The entire park must be permanently protected and dedicated exclusively to recreational use. Design and construction work associated with improvements are eligible. Pre-award design and engineering costs may be eligible.

Projects must be accessible to the general public and cannot require memberships, exclude the public because of higher use fees, or include residential or elaborate lodging facilities. structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary land protection program that allows landowners to protect their property through a conservation easement—a legal agreement that restricts future development while allowing the owner to retain ownership, live on the property, farm it, sell it, and pass it to heirs. The easement is recorded in county land records and applies to all future owners. The program provides permanent protection of natural areas, farmland, forest, and historic property from development while allowing continued agricultural or forestry use by the owner. MET partners with local land trusts, governmental entities, and regional or national land trusts to hold and enforce conservation easements jointly as co-grantees.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who donate a conservation easement receive significant tax benefits including a federal income tax deduction for the appraised value of the easement as a charitable gift (value equals difference between fair market value before and after easement restriction), a state income tax credit, a 100% property tax credit for 15 years on unimproved land, lower estate and inheritance taxes due to reduced development potential, and potential federal estate tax exemptions. Maryland Environmental Trust provides long-term monitoring of the property to ensure easement terms are maintained. Available as a full gift (no money changes hands) or partial gift through bargain sale with appraisal value difference as charitable contribution. MET may reimburse donors for portion of certain costs in limited cases.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Form 8283, Required Statement, and appraisal must be submitted no less than 10 working days before tax return is due

Exceptional urban properties of all sizes, especially those providing public access, may also be considered. Farmers, ranchers, foresters, and property owners with appreciated property or existing mortgages/liens. Local land trusts and conservation organizations seeking to co-hold easements with MET.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program accepts donations of conservation easements on eligible properties to restrict future uses and protect natural areas, farmland, forest, and historic property from development while allowing continued agricultural or forestry use by the owner. Landowners receive tax benefits and long-term protection of their land. Conservation and stewardship of natural resources and landscapes. Properties may include dwelling units (with clustering requirements), accessory dwelling units, subdivisions, and other structures subject to restrictions. Properties 5+ acres may participate in ecosystem services marketing and mitigation banking opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located throughout Maryland from forested mountains and Garrett County to the shores of the Chesapeake Bay. All properties are considered statewide on a case-by-case basis. Coverage includes four regions: Central (Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Harford, Howard, Montgomery), Eastern (Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), Southern (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, St. Mary's), and Western (Allegany, Frederick, Garrett, Washington). Rural and urban settings throughout Maryland.

The program follows typical processing steps including evaluation, appraisal, negotiation of easement terms, and finalization of the Deed of Conservation Easement between the landowner and Maryland Environmental Trust. structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources provides reimbursement grants to marinas for the purchase, installation, operations, maintenance, upgrade, and replacement of marine sewage pumpout facilities. These facilities allow boaters to properly dispose of sewage and help protect Maryland waters. Reimbursement is up to $20,000 for initial installation and capital projects, up to $18,000 for upgrades or replacements, with annual grants also available to help marinas cover ongoing operational and maintenance costs of existing pumpout systems. Funding is provided through the Federal Clean Vessel Act/Sport Fish Restoration and Boating Trust Fund (75%) and the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund (25%).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants of up to $20,000 for new pumpout installations and up to $18,000 for upgrades or replacements of existing systems. Grants cover purchase of pumpout equipment, installation labor (contractor or in-house), plumbing and electrical work, permits and associated costs, and waste holding tanks if applicable. Marinas pay for equipment up-front and submit documentation including invoices with proof of payment and cancelled checks for reimbursement after final inspection. Annual grant funding is also available to help marinas pay for ongoing operations and maintenance of existing pumpout stations, with reimbursement up to $5,000 per marina for eligible expenses minus pumpout income. Eligible O&M expenses include log-keeping, staff labor, licensed plumber/electrician services, replacement parts, sewage hauling, winterization, and annual connection fees. Permit fees for first-time installations are also reimbursable. Must comply with Buy America provision for infrastructure materials.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; April 15, 2026 for operations and maintenance grants

Covers equipment purchase, installation labor, plumbing and electrical work, permits, waste holding tanks, and sewage hauling. Cannot be used for marina restroom sewage, bilge, power wash, or oily waste. Must comply with Buy America provision for infrastructure materials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties, statewide. Maryland law requires new and expanding marinas with more than 10 slips, and all marinas with 50 or more slips berthing boats over 22 feet, must have a pumpout facility.

Applicant owns and is responsible for pumpout; State/federal government assumes no liability
Installation must be completed within one year of application approval
Facility remains at location if marina is sold; new owner must comply with agreement
Facilities must serve the general public during reasonable business hours
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For capital projects: Step 1 - Download and complete the DNR Maryland Pumpout Grant Application. Step 2 - Submit the completed application with a project proposal including equipment specifications, minimum 3 competitive bids from Maryland-licensed contractors, and a drawing of the installation location. Step 3 - Complete the Coordinated Environmental Review Form Part I and submit to DNR, who will coordinate with local health department and Maryland Department of the Environment for approval. Step 4 - Complete the Watershed and Climate Services Risk Assessment Form. Step 5 - Obtain all local permits and forward copies to DNR. Step 6 - Ensure MDE approval is received for sewage disposal method. Once all approvals are received, DNR will approve the application and issue an approval letter. Step 7 - Purchase and install the pumpout facility according to the approved proposal. Step 8 - Submit the Pumpout Installation Reimbursement Invoice with receipts, proof of payment, cancelled checks, and W-9 form. Step 9 - DNR conducts final inspection and processes reimbursement. For operations and maintenance: Submit application using the annual Pumpout Operations and Maintenance Grant Application form (Google Form) prior to April 15 and maintain required pumpout logs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Abandoned Boat and Debris Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides reimbursable grants and expertise to authorized public agencies to remove abandoned boats and hazardous debris from Maryland state waterways. It aims to eliminate navigation hazards, protect the environment, and maintain safe recreational boating on Maryland waterways. Grants are 100% reimbursable up to $25,000 and are funded through the Waterway Improvement Fund generated by a 5% excise tax on boat purchases and titling in Maryland. The program provides both financial assistance and technical expertise to assist public agencies in removal efforts. Projects must expand or improve public boating access and enhance boating safety.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 100% reimbursable grants of up to $25,000 for the removal of abandoned vessels and hazardous debris from state waters. Reimbursement covers contractor costs, direct purchases, labor, and equipment. Reimbursement is contingent upon compliance with all terms and conditions of the grant, including proof of payment via invoices or requisitions with canceled checks or electronic fund transfer documentation, before and after photos, and proof of contractor selection via public bidding process. Funds come from the Waterway Improvement Fund generated by a 5% excise tax on boat purchases and titling in Maryland. Funds are obligated immediately upon approval. The program also offers expertise and technical assistance to public agencies.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted in July
structured_extraction.program_audience: Authorized public entities in Maryland such as counties, municipalities, and local governments with ownership, management, or jurisdiction over the aquatic lands where the vessel or hazardous debris is located.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Removal and disposal of abandoned boats and hazardous debris from state waters. Costs may include contractor services, materials, equipment rental, and in-house labor. Projects must expand or improve public boating access and enhance boating safety. Abandoned boats must be proven to be abandoned in accordance with Natural Resources Article §8-721. Debris that poses a hazard to navigation or limits access to a public boating access facility or shipping channel is eligible for removal.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland state waterways. Only authorized public entities in Maryland with ownership, management, or jurisdiction over the aquatic lands where the vessel or debris is located may apply.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an authorized public entity in Maryland (county, municipality, local government, etc.)
Entity must have ownership, management, or jurisdiction over the aquatic lands where the vessel or hazardous debris is located
Abandoned boats must be proven to be abandoned in accordance with Natural Resources Article §8-721
Debris must pose a hazard to navigation or limit access to a public boating access facility or shipping channel
Invoices or requisitions for payment with canceled checks or electronic fund transfer documentation required for reimbursement
Before and after photos of removal work required
Proof of contractor selection via public bidding process (lowest bidder) or existing Blanket Purchase Order Contract required
For in-house labor: staff list with hours and rates must be documented
Equipment usage documentation required if applicable
Three-year record retention for subcontractor contracts
Project must expand or improve public boating access and/or enhance boating safety
All federal, state, and local permits must be obtained before construction begins
Plans and specifications must be completed by Maryland Registered Professional Engineer (unless pre-approved otherwise)
Certify all costs are accurate and payments made per local procurement procedures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application (available in MS Word or Adobe PDF format) in July. Funds are obligated immediately upon approval. If approved, the grantee removes the vessel or debris and submits a Request for Reimbursement form (available in MS Word or Adobe PDF format) with required supporting documentation including invoices, proof of payment, before and after photos, and contractor selection proof to receive 100% reimbursement up to $25,000. Allow one month from date of receipt for processing. Reimbursement is contingent upon compliance with all grant terms and conditions. Forward completed request to Department of Natural Resources, Boating Services Unit, Abandoned Boat and Debris Program, 303 Marine Academy Drive, Stevensville, MD 21666. Fax: 410-643-2341.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Archery in the Schools Program (MD NASP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A training and certification program that equips teachers with archery instruction skills to teach basic archery safely to students in schools. Teachers attend a one-day training course (four to eight hours) and become certified instructors through the National Archery in the Schools Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-day training course lasting four to eight hours for teachers. Training covers safe range setup, determining dominant eye, making a string-bow, 11 steps to archery success, individual coaching skills development, safety orientation, practice on running the range, practice teaching, equipment nomenclature, operation, maintenance and repair. Each certified teacher receives a Basic Archery Instructor (BAI) kit containing a pocket guide, string for making a string bow, and NASP whistle. Training cost varies depending on the instructor and can range from $0 to $80. A test is given and the teacher becomes certified by the National Archery in the Schools Program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teachers in schools interested in participating in the Maryland NASP program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification for teachers to teach basic archery instruction to students
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland schools statewide. Training sessions are held regionally as needed and typically hosted in the gym of one of the teacher's schools.
requirements_list: Schools must send their teachers to a one-day training course
Teachers must pass a test to become certified by the National Archery in the Schools Program
A certified BAI must report their teaching hours annually by July 31st to maintain their archery certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Teachers attend a one-day training course lasting four to eight hours. The course covers safe archery instruction techniques and concepts. A test is given at the end and teachers become certified instructors. Training sessions are held regionally as needed. To find training sessions, use the NASP BAI class search tool at https://naspbai.org/classsearch.aspx

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Biological Stream Survey (MBSS) Certification Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive certification program offering six credentials in stream sampling and taxonomy for individuals who meet training, testing, and field audit requirements. The program includes spring certifications in benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, processing, and taxonomy, and summer certifications in physical habitat assessment, fish crew leadership, fish taxonomy, and mussel taxonomy. Training combines 4 days of in-person classroom instruction, laboratory work, and field protocol demonstrations held at Bowie State University. Certifications document competency in protocols required by some Maryland counties and state agencies. Six certification specialties are available: benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, benthic macroinvertebrate laboratory processing and subsampling, fish crew leader, fish taxonomy, mussel taxonomy, and physical habitat assessment. Participants may register for 1-2 days at $75 per day or for 3 or more days for $200. Training dates are held in May (May 26-29, 2026). Certifications are valid for 1-3 years (mussel taxonomy indefinite).
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Spring and summer training sessions at Bowie State University. Participants register for 1-2 days at $75/day or 3+ days for $200. Training consists of 4 days of in-person instruction covering classroom and laboratory instruction combined with field protocol demonstrations. Upon successful completion of training, written tests, and field audits, participants receive certification in one or more of six specialties: benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, benthic macroinvertebrate laboratory processing and subsampling, fish crew leader, fish taxonomy, mussel taxonomy, or physical habitat assessment. Certifications are valid for 1-3 years (mussel taxonomy indefinite). Certification fees are $300 per individual certification; $400 for combined certifications. Payments are made through the DNR Outdoor Store.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration is open now; training dates are May 26-29, 2026; field audits for benthic sampling must be scheduled before March 15; field audits for fish certifications must be scheduled before June 15; certification payment due one week from audit date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Professionals and non-professionals, including students, interns, seasonal employees, and volunteers seeking formal credentials and certification in stream biological monitoring protocols, taxonomy, and sampling methods required by some Maryland counties and state agencies. Individuals seeking certification and training in stream sampling protocols and taxonomic standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification in benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, laboratory processing and subsampling techniques, fish taxonomy, mussel taxonomy, physical habitat assessment protocols, and field demonstrations in stream sampling and biological assessment methods. Certification fees support quality assurance and field audit processes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program held at Bowie State University in Maryland. Certifications apply to Maryland streams and rivers with threatened and endangered mussel species. Certifications recognized by Maryland counties and state agencies. Open to participants statewide.
requirements_list: Individuals only; not firms, organizations, or agencies
Attendance at MBSS spring or summer training (except for laboratory processing certification)
Passing written tests
Passing field audits
Completion of quality assurance procedures (varies by certification type)

For benthic macroinvertebrate sampling: attend MBSS spring training annually, pass written test, complete one field audit in first season, maintain BIBI score difference ≤1.0 between personal and QC officer samples
For benthic macroinvertebrate laboratory processing: attend training at DNR office in Annapolis, pass written test, pass laboratory audit
For benthic macroinvertebrate taxonomy: individuals must be certified by the Society for Freshwater Science in both EPT East and North American Chironomidae

For fish crew leader: annual attendance at fish sampling protocol portion of summer training for 3 consecutive years; pass written test; complete field audit with MBSS Quality Control Officer in year 1; sample own site observed by MBSS Quality Control Officer

For fish taxonomy: score ≥90% (36/40) on taxonomy test at MBSS summer training for 3 consecutive years; on year 1, complete field audit identifying all fish from electrofishing pass(es) with ≥15 species richness and misidentifying no more than 1 individual; specimens smaller than 30mm not counted; preserve specimens that cannot be identified with confidence; document photographs; complete voucher labels with geographic coordinates

For mussel taxonomy: score ≥90% on mussel taxonomy test and 100% on threatened and endangered mussel species identification; no misidentification of any non-listed species as threatened/endangered; conduct at least 20 surveys within last 10 years OR 10 surveys within last 5 years; provide 2 letters of reference; annual continuing education handling 5 individuals of each threatened and endangered mussel species per year or 0.5 hours per species in reference collection; report annually to DNR by February 15
For physical habitat assessment: attendance at presentations and field demonstration; passing written test; passing field audit during training; pay registration fee in advance

For benthic sampling: required equipment includes D-net ≤600 micron, measuring tape, ethanol, waders without felt soles, and proper site setup (0m to 75m); must correctly determine productive habitat proportions; must follow MBSS Sampling Manual protocols; must use proper disinfection techniques

For fish crew leader: required equipment includes electrofishers, block nets, dip nets, mesh size specifications, scales, waders, decontamination solutions, permits; must follow electrofishing protocols with proper block nets, upstream sampling, habitat coverage, and fish mortality minimization; must process fish with certified taxonomy identification and proper data recording

For fish taxonomy: required equipment includes fish identification keys, formalin, voucher jars/containers, voucher labels, digital camera, state-listed species list, invasive/problematic species list, decontamination solution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online using the Google Form link provided on the website or through the DNR Outdoor Store. Pay registration fees ($75-$200) through the DNR Outdoor Store via credit card in advance; no walk-in registrants accepted. Attend MBSS training at Bowie State University during specified season (spring May 26-29, 2026, or summer). Take required written tests at training. If test is passed, pay certification fee. Complete field audit with MBSS Quality Control Officer or auditor using standardized checklist. Upon successful completion, name is listed in MBSS Registry of Certifications. For mussel taxonomy, submit annual reporting to DNR by February 15 with survey numbers, species handled, and training hours.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary certification and recognition program that celebrates environmental stewardship by marinas, boatyards, and yacht clubs. The program recognizes designated Clean Marinas as environmentally-responsible businesses and promotes the adoption of measures to reduce pollution from marinas and recreational boats. Participants commit to environmental stewardship by implementing best practices to protect water and air quality, keep Maryland's waterways free of harmful chemicals, excess nutrients, and debris, and educate boaters about their role as stewards of waterways.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance including an introductory workshop, access to the Maryland Clean Marina Guidebook and Award Checklist, informal site visits from Clean Marina staff with site-specific recommendations, ongoing support from mentors and Clean Marina staff, and formal confirmation visits to verify compliance with Award criteria. Resources and assistance help marina, boatyard, and yacht club operators minimize pollution and protect environmental resources. Certified facilities receive marketing benefits including use of the Clean Marina logo, an Award Certificate signed by the Governor, a burgee and flag, an aluminum sign, a free online business card, recognition in publications and advertisements in regional boating magazines, and news releases. Clean Marina Awards are presented to facilities meeting or exceeding minimum required scores across 8 operational areas: Vessel Maintenance & Repair (85%), Petroleum Control (80%), Emergency Planning (80%), Sewage Handling (80%), Waste Containment & Disposal (85%), Marina Management (80%), Stormwater Management (75%), and Marina Design & Maintenance (70%).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within one year of pledge date to implement practices and apply for certification
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marina, boatyard, and yacht club operators in Maryland; facility managers and recreational boating facilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide direct financial assistance. It is a certification and recognition program that helps marinas, boatyards, and yacht clubs implement environmental best practices to minimize pollution and protect water and air quality. Certified facilities receive marketing and recognition benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Sign the Clean Marina Pledge committing to keep Maryland's waterways free of harmful chemicals, excess nutrients, and debris
Control pollution from vessel maintenance and repair, petroleum storage and transfer, sewage disposal, solid/liquid/hazardous wastes, and stormwater runoff
Implement pollution prevention practices across all operational areas
Complete self-assessment using the Clean Marina Award Checklist and Maryland Clean Marina Guidebook
Implement recommended changes to meet Award criteria

Meet minimum passing scores on the Award Checklist in all 8 operational areas: Vessel Maintenance & Repair (85%), Petroleum Control (80%), Emergency Planning (80%), Sewage Handling (80%), Waste Containment & Disposal (85%), Marina Management (80%), Stormwater Management (75%), Marina Design & Maintenance (70%)
Schedule and pass a confirmation visit from Clean Marina staff and a certified Clean Marina operator
Comply with all applicable federal and state environmental laws and regulations
Annually sign and return an Affirmation of Good Standing
Participate in at least one reaffirmation meeting every three years
Apply to Maryland DNR for certification within one year of pledge date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, obtain program information by attending an introductory workshop (held each winter), downloading documents from the web page, or contacting the Clean Marina office. Second, sign the Clean Marina Pledge on behalf of the marina or boatyard, committing to pollution control measures, and return a photocopy while displaying the original publicly. Third, assess your facility using the Award Checklist and Guidebook to identify pollution control opportunities applicable to your operation, or request an informal site visit from Clean Marina staff. Fourth, implement appropriate pollution prevention practices at your own pace with support from Clean Marina staff or other certified operators. Fifth, apply to Maryland DNR for Clean Marina certification. Sixth, schedule a confirmation visit once you believe your facility meets the minimum passing scores in all 8 operational areas. A Clean Marina staff member and a certified Clean Marina operator will verify compliance. After the visit, the Clean Marina advisory committee reviews the findings. If you meet the Award criteria, you are certified as a Maryland Clean Marina. To maintain status, annually sign and return an Affirmation of Good Standing, and participate in reaffirmation meetings at least every three years.

structured_extraction.program_description: An award-winning AmeriCorps workforce development and public service program that engages young adults and veterans in extensive natural resource management and park conservation projects across Maryland. The program provides opportunities for service in the community and environment by preserving, protecting, enhancing, and restoring Maryland's natural resources while providing training, education, and career development opportunities. Members are employed to perform conservation work at Maryland state parks and natural resource management areas, including trail construction and maintenance, environmental education, forest management, invasive species removal, facility improvements, planting trees and native plants, restoring wildlife habitat, and supporting Chesapeake Bay improvement. Members work in crews of 5-7 on various projects and gain experience in diverse roles from operating chainsaws to leading educational programs. Participants undergo extensive skill development training including First Aid and CPR/AED certification, 40-hour Wildland Fire Fighting certification, Environmental Education and Interpretation, Chainsaw Skills and Safety, Leave No Trace ethics, trail maintenance training, canoe trip leading instruction, carpentry, animal care, and Foundation for Search Operations training. Members receive health care benefits, low-cost park housing, a completion award of $6,000, professional and networking opportunities, and a Conservation Steward Apprenticeship Certificate.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Young adults and veterans are employed to serve in AmeriCorps positions performing natural resource management, park conservation, restoration, and preservation work across Maryland. Members receive paid employment positions, on-the-job training, and work experience in conservation fields. Members gain experience in diverse conservation roles including trail construction, chainsaw use, invasive species management, carpentry, animal care, environmental education, planting trees and native plants, restoring wildlife habitat, and removing invasive species. Members receive health care benefits, low-cost park housing, a $6,000 completion award, professional and networking opportunities, valuable professional skills development, and a Conservation Steward Apprenticeship Certificate. Participants undergo extensive skill development training including First Aid and CPR/AED certification, 40-hour Wildland Fire Fighting certification, Environmental Education and Interpretation, Chainsaw Skills and Safety, Leave No Trace ethics, trail maintenance training, canoe trip leading instruction, and Foundation for Search Operations training.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Hiring target: August 19th; Program start date: September 9th; Interview scheduling begins in May
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults and veterans interested in conservation careers, environmental stewardship, and environmental service seeking to enter natural resource conservation or park operations and management careers, or individuals seeking paid employment and training in conservation work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment, training, and engagement in natural resource management, park conservation, restoration, and preservation work including trail maintenance, forest management, environmental education, park improvements, and ecological restoration projects. Completion award and certification prepare participants for careers in these fields. Members work in crews on projects including planting trees and native plants, building and maintaining trails, restoring wildlife habitat, removing invasive species, conducting educational programs, and supporting Chesapeake Bay improvement. Funds support participant wages, health care, housing, and skills training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide with projects at state parks and forests, the Chesapeake Bay, and coastal bays throughout the state. Locations available include Western Maryland (Garrett County), Central Maryland (Harford and Baltimore Counties), and Southern/Eastern Maryland (Prince George's County and Wicomico County). Members work together from all over the state on various public lands and conservation projects. Applicants specify preferred geographical location(s) for work placement within Maryland. Matching is based on applicant preferences and available positions.
requirements_list: Interest in working outdoors required
Specify preferred geographical work location(s)
Articulate specific interest in MCC program participation
Complete multi-step interview process including AI pre-screening questionnaire and virtual interview with MCC staff
Willingness to be placed at specified geographical location(s)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create an account on the BuildWithin portal and submit a Service Year application through the Department of Service and Civic Innovation website at https://dsci.maryland.gov/ indicating interest in outdoor work, preferred geographic location(s), and specific interest in MCC. Complete an AI pre-screening questionnaire. Participate in a virtual interview with MCC staff. Interviews are scheduled via the portal beginning in May. Interested individuals can register for webinar sessions to learn more about the program. After submitting your online application, it will be reviewed by Annalyn O'Grady, Conservation Corps Program Officer. Shadow crew opportunities are available October through early June to learn more before committing. Detailed application information is available on the How to Apply page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A summer employment and skills training program for youth ages 14-17 and veterans that combines hands-on outdoor conservation projects in Maryland State Parks with job and life skills training. Participants engage in habitat and facility restoration, environmental enrichment activities including fishing, archery, kayaking, and stream surveys, plus a camping experience. The program culminates in a graduation ceremony with certificates of achievement. Participants work Monday-Thursday on trail repair, tree planting, invasive species removal, and structure construction while receiving wages and career exploration opportunities. Fridays feature enrichment days with environmental education and recreational activities. The program emphasizes SPIRIT Principles: Stewardship, Professionalism, Initiative, Respect, Integrity, and Teamwork.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid summer employment combining job and life skills training with conservation work. Youth work 5 days per week for 5-6 weeks on habitat and facility restoration projects including trail repair, tree planting, invasive species removal, and structure construction. Monday-Thursday work schedule with Friday enrichment activities. Participants receive wages, meals (breakfast, morning snack, lunch, and afternoon snack), work uniforms (shirts, pants, belt, boots), transportation to and from work sites, environmental enrichment activities, optional three-day camping experience, performance evaluations, and career exploration opportunities. Training includes hand tools, equipment, landscaping, construction tasks, field skills, tool safety, and plant identification. Program emphasizes SPIRIT Principles: Stewardship, Professionalism, Initiative, Respect, Integrity, and Teamwork.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disadvantaged youth ages 14-17, young people and veterans interested in conservation employment and skills training through hands-on outdoor conservation projects. Priority given to ages 14-15 as first-time participants; ages 16-17 reserved for returning members. High school youth and those referred by Department of Juvenile Services. Youth with limited access to natural spaces. Primarily serves underserved and disadvantaged youth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Youth and staff wages, uniforms and safety equipment, transportation and meals, conservation project work including trail maintenance and construction, park infrastructure projects, invasive species removal, stream and environmental cleanup, native tree planting, facility improvements, signage installation, natural resource restoration, and park restoration activities within Maryland State Parks. Program supplies, tools, equipment, camping and enrichment activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Multiple Maryland State Parks and public lands statewide serving central, eastern, and western regions. Central region locations include Baltimore City, Susquehanna, Gwynns Falls Trail, Gunpowder Falls, Patapsco Valley, Lake Clifton Park, Cylburn Arboretum, Sandy Point, Merkle Wildlife Sanctuary, and Seneca Creek State Parks. Eastern region includes Assateague and Tuckahoe State Parks. Western region includes Rocky Gap and Cunningham State Parks. Primary service areas: Baltimore City, Harford County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Worcester County, and Anne Arundel County. Operates in 16 Maryland Parks and Complexes across multiple regions.

Strict attendance requirements and performance standards
Adherence to SPIRIT Principles (Stewardship, Professionalism, Initiative, Respect, Integrity, Teamwork)
Available to work Monday-Thursday during summer program
Participation in Friday enrichment activities

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Environmental Trust conserves, improves, stimulates, and perpetuates the aesthetic, natural, scenic, and cultural aspects of Maryland's environment. MET promotes conservation of open space and appreciation of the environment and its care through multiple programs including Land Conservation, Monitoring and Stewardship of conserved lands, Local Land Trust Assistance, and the Keep Maryland Beautiful Grants Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MET provides grants and technical assistance through multiple programs focused on land conservation, monitoring and stewardship of conserved lands, assistance to local land trusts, and keep maryland beautiful beautification grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, land trusts, local governments, community groups, government agencies, and the public focused on environmental conservation and beautification.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land conservation, environmental stewardship, monitoring of conserved lands, local land trust support, and beautification projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: Chesapeake Bay Foundation initiative providing free plant material, implementation, and three years of maintenance for streamside forest buffers and upland tree plantings. Program partners with agency programs for associated practices like stream bank fencing and livestock watering. Livestock producers interested in grazing can receive funding for conversion of row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, plus grazing mentors and technical assistance for farm economics and marketing. Expanded through Mountains to Bay Grazers Alliance for additional regional resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free plant material, implementation, and three years of maintenance for streamside forest buffers and upland tree plantings. Funding available for converting row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing. Technical assistance and grazing mentors available for farm economics and marketing through Maryland Grazers Network and Mountains to Bay Grazers Alliance. Program partners with agency programs for associated practices like stream bank fencing and livestock watering.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners and livestock producers interested in streamside forest buffers, upland tree plantings, or rotational grazing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Plant material, implementation, and maintenance for forest buffers and tree plantings. Conversion of row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing and grazing mentorship for livestock producers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland and Bay-wide region through Mountains to Bay Grazers Alliance
requirements_list: Participation in streamside forest buffers and upland tree plantings
Three years of maintenance required for recipients
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners and livestock producers contact the program or the Maryland Grazers Network for participation and receive assistance with implementation and maintenance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program run in partnership with states that protects environmentally important forests from conversion and development by purchasing conservation easements from willing private landowners. The program prevents forest fragmentation and maintains viable working forests and natural benefits while protecting public drinking water supply, fish and wildlife habitat, scenic resources, and cultural/historic values. The program provides up to 75 percent federal cost-share for the purchase of conservation easements, requiring a 25 percent non-federal match from the landowner or other sources. Conservation easements are legal agreements that restrict future activities on the land to protect its conservation values. Only private forests within designated Forest Legacy Areas are eligible. At least 75 percent of the area under easement must be forested, with the remaining 25 percent in compatible land uses such as agriculture. Properties are ranked at state and national levels for funding based on forest importance, threat of development, and strategic value to other protected lands or conservation initiatives.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Federal Government supplies up to 75% of the funding to purchase conservation easements at market value. At least 25% of funding comes from State, Local, NGO funds or can be donated by the landowner. Only private forests within designated Forest Legacy Areas are eligible. At least 75% of the area under easement must be forested, with the remaining 25% in compatible land uses such as agriculture. Conservation easements are legal agreements that restrict future activities on the land to protect its conservation values. Landowner must convey development and mineral rights as part of the easement, and may not reserve or withdraw building sites from eligible ownership. Landowner can sell development rights, public access rights, grazing rights, and/or farming rights. Requires written forest management plan approved by State, updated every 15 years. Third-party participation in acquisition, management, and monitoring possible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications evaluated on annual basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners in Maryland, particularly in designated Forest Legacy Areas who are willing to sell their development and mineral rights and protect their forests.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forest easement acquisitions and conservation of forest lands to protect forest conservation values, restrict future conversion to non-forest uses and development, and protect forest land from conversion to non-forest uses. Payment for conservation easement interests or deed acquisition. Landowner may accept below-market value payment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only in Forest Legacy Areas identified in Maryland's Forest Legacy Program Assessment of Need. Statewide program with local land use comprehensive plans and consistency with local conservation efforts required. Forest Legacy Areas are geographically defined areas determined to have high economic and environmental values for wildlife, wood products industry, water quality, and residents. At least 75% of the area put under easement must be forested; the remaining 25% must be in a compatible land use such as agriculture.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners apply on an annual basis. Applicants can contact the program administrator to discuss eligibility. Submit completed application package with required supporting documents. State Forest Stewardship Coordinating Committee reviews and scores using prioritization criteria. Property inspection and appraisal conducted. Applications are evaluated and ranked each year based on a point allocation system that considers forest importance, threat of development, strategic value to other protected lands or conservation initiatives, community support, adjacency to other Forest Legacy parcels, complementary federal investments, and donated or third-party funding. The highest ranked applications enter the national ranking process for funding. If selected for federal funding, the project enters negotiation and acquisition phase. If negotiations produce acceptable easement terms, the easement is purchased. Landowners whose projects do not receive federal funding or do not reach acceptable terms may reapply in future years.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Hunter Education Advanced Muzzleloader Hunter Course
structured_extraction.program_description: A training course that teaches safe and responsible muzzleloader hunting, including classroom instruction and supervised range sessions. Students learn muzzleloader history, equipment, loading techniques, and safety, and must pass an 80% test to receive certification that lasts a lifetime.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fully in-person training classes lasting 4 to 6 hours, provided by state certified instructors. Includes classroom sessions covering muzzleloader history, parts, blackpowder, loading techniques, hangfire and misfire procedures, cleaning, and Maryland-specific information. Students complete a supervised range session with loading procedures, proficiency shooting (marksmanship not evaluated), and minimum standard of 3 shots fired from a muzzleloading firearm. All training materials needed to pass evaluation are provided. Students must score 80% on a 25-question multiple choice test and demonstrate safe behavior to pass.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking muzzleloader hunting certification, including hunters who need specialty certification to hunt in other states or specific jurisdictions within Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification in muzzleloader hunting skills and safety.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Specialty courses are scheduled independently by training teams throughout the state.
requirements_list: Must demonstrate ability to behave in a mature and safe manner
Must score 80% on a 25-question multiple choice test
Must fire minimum 3 shots from a muzzleloading firearm during range session
Must pass equipment safety inspection
General safety violations may be grounds for course failure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for classes through the Advanced Hunter Education Courses registration link. Check the schedule for available courses near you. Attend the full in-person training including classroom and range session. Complete the required test and demonstrations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Hunter Education Advanced Specialty Courses
structured_extraction.program_description: Training courses that teach safe and responsible hunting with specialty equipment, including classroom instruction, field exercises, and supervised range sessions. Courses cover bow hunting, muzzleloader hunting, and tree stand safety, covering equipment, techniques, safety procedures, and state-specific hunting information. Students learn equipment operation, shot placement, tree stand safety (for bow hunting), loading techniques (for muzzleloader), and must pass an 80% test to receive lifetime certification. Courses are fully in-person, typically lasting 4 to 6 hours, and are taught by state-certified instructors. These courses are designed for hunters who need specialty certifications required by other states or specific jurisdictions within Maryland for organized hunting events or permitting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state provides fully in-person training classes scheduled independently by training teams across the state. Each specialty course (Bow Hunter, Muzzleloader Hunter, or Tree Stand Safety) includes classroom sessions with instruction and testing, field exercises or demonstrations, and range sessions. All instructional materials and information needed to pass evaluation are provided by state-certified instructors. Courses generally last 4 to 6 hours depending on student numbers and class participation. Students must achieve an 80% score on written tests and demonstrate safe behavior and proficiency standards. Bow Hunter Course includes supervised archery range sessions with equipment safety inspection and proficiency shooting.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hunters seeking advanced training and certification in specialized hunting disciplines. These courses are designed for hunters who need specialty certifications required by other states or specific jurisdictions within Maryland for organized hunting events or permitting.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training is provided in bow hunting, muzzleloader hunting, and tree stand safety. Courses cover equipment, techniques, safety procedures, and state-specific hunting information.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Courses are scheduled by training teams across Maryland. Classes are not generally required by the state of Maryland but may be required by other states and by some counties or municipalities within Maryland that organize hunting events or permitting.
requirements_list: Must demonstrate ability to behave in a mature and safe manner
Must score 80% on Bow Hunter Course written test (50-question multiple choice)
Must score 80% on Muzzleloader Hunter Course written test (25-question multiple choice)
Must score 80% on Tree Stand Safety Course written test (25-question multiple choice)
Bow Hunter Course: Minimum standard of 3 hits in vital 3-D deer target during range session
Muzzleloader Hunter Course: Minimum standard of 3 shots fired from a muzzleloading firearm
Must pass equipment safety inspection
General safety violations may be grounds for course failure
Students should have proper clothing for outdoor sessions and note any special facility requirements when registering
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective students check the class schedules posted on the DNR website and register through the Advanced Hunter Education Courses registration link. Training teams schedule courses independently across the state and post them on the DNR website. Attend the full in-person training including classroom, field exercises, and range session. Complete the required test and demonstrations. Students should plan ahead as demand for specialty courses is lower than basic hunter education classes and certification opportunities may be limited.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Hunter Education Advanced Tree Stand Safety Course
structured_extraction.program_description: A training course that teaches safe tree stand use and fall prevention, including classroom instruction and safety demonstrations. Students learn about tree stand types, harnesses, fall arrest systems, and fall recovery, and must pass an 80% test to receive certification that lasts a lifetime.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fully in-person training classes lasting 4 to 6 hours, provided by certified instructors. Includes classroom sessions covering tree stand manufacturer information, safety statistics, manufacturer instructions, types of stands (ladder stands, hang-on, climbing stands), climbing aids, fall arrest systems and harnesses, suspension trauma, life lines, fall recovery, and Maryland-specific information. Students participate in unscored demonstrations showing how to don a harness, set up tree stands, and perform fall recovery. All training materials needed to pass evaluation are provided. Students must score 80% on a 25-question multiple choice test and demonstrate safe behavior to pass.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking tree stand safety certification for hunting.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification in tree stand safety skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Specialty courses are scheduled independently by training teams throughout the state.
requirements_list: Must demonstrate ability to behave in a mature and safe manner
Must score 80% on a 25-question multiple choice test
Must participate in safety demonstrations
General safety violations may be grounds for course failure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for classes through the Advanced Hunter Education Courses registration link. Check the schedule for available courses near you. Attend the full in-person training including classroom and demonstrations. Complete the required test. Note any special instructions when registering as some facilities have special requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fully in-person, multi-day training event that teaches hunting safety, firearm handling, ethical hunting practices, and wildlife conservation. The course covers firearm equipment, shooting skills, tree-stand safety, hunting skills, ethics, survival skills, wildlife conservation, and Maryland-specific hunting regulations. Students complete classroom instruction, a trail walk practical demonstration, a written test, and a range session with live fire. Upon successful completion, students receive a Certificate of Competency required to purchase a Maryland hunting license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training provided by state-certified Hunter Safety Education Instructors. The classroom course typically lasts 12 to 16 hours spread over multiple days and includes classroom instruction on firearm equipment, shooting skills, tree-stand safety, hunting skills, ethics, survival skills, and wildlife conservation. Students must pass a 50-question multiple-choice test (requiring 80% score), complete a pass/fail trail walk demonstrating safe firearm handling and decision-making, and participate in a supervised range session with a minimum of two rounds of live fire. Upon successful completion, students receive a Certificate of Competency required to purchase a Maryland hunting license. There is no charge to students, though pre-registration is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who wish to hunt in Maryland and need to obtain a Certificate of Competency to purchase a hunting license.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and instruction in hunter safety, firearm handling, hunting skills, ethics, survival skills, and wildlife conservation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Classroom courses are scheduled independently by training teams throughout Maryland and posted on the DNR website. Students can find courses in their area through the registration website.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective students can pre-register through the link provided on the DNR website or at register-ed.com to view currently scheduled classroom courses in their area. Classes are scheduled independently by training teams across the state. Students should note any special instructions when registering and check individual class descriptions for specific requirements. Proper clothing for outdoor sessions is required.

structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer program that trains and certifies hunting safety instructors who teach novice hunters safe and responsible hunting practices. Instructors provide training in the knowledge, skills, and attitudes needed for safe and responsible hunting to approximately 7,000 new hunters each year. Sporting clubs are encouraged to develop instructor teams, and teams that commit to teaching a minimum of three classes per year may receive instructor training at their facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides instructor training at no cost to qualified volunteers. Teams that commit to teaching a minimum of three classes per year will receive instructor training at their facility. Volunteers are unpaid but receive instructor training and support to teach hunter education courses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with at least three years of hunting experience who have the ability to work with young people and a desire to provide quality hunting safety training. Sporting clubs are encouraged to develop instructor teams from interested members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Instructor training to teach Maryland Hunter Education Program courses in safe and responsible hunting practices. This program provides training for volunteer hunting safety instructors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available throughout Maryland.

Sporting clubs are encouraged to develop teams from interested members. Teams committing to teach at least three classes annually will have instructor training provided at their facility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A required educational program that trains individuals in trapper education and safety before they can trap furbearers in Maryland. The course covers trapping techniques, regulations, ethics, animal welfare, and safety practices. Developed by the Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies (AFWA), it teaches basic techniques with focus on responsible treatment of animals, legal methods, selectivity, and ethical trapper behavior. Topics include furbearer management, trapping regulations, best management practices, trap types, selective trapping techniques, water and land sets, cable devices, trapping safety, running a trapline, fur handling, furbearing animal species information, furbearer skinning, pelt processing, drying/freezing techniques, and responsible trapping ethics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training provided in two formats: an in-person instructor-led classroom course lasting 4 to 6 hours, or a test-out option where individuals complete a proctored exam. The course covers regulated trapping, Maryland furbearers, trapping laws and regulations, best management practices, safety, ethics, trap techniques, and animal welfare. Students must complete a workbook and pass a 50-question multiple choice test with an 80% score. All materials including the student manual and workbook are provided at no cost. Training covers topics including: introduction to trapper education, historical considerations, furbearer management, trapping regulations, best management practices, traps, trapping equipment, bait/lure/urine, selective trapping techniques, water sets, land sets, cable devices, trapping safety, running a trapline, using furbearers, handling fur, responsible trapping, disease and parasite management, trap identification and operation, fur processing techniques, furbearer species identification, pelt processing, drying/freezing techniques, and ethical decision-making scenarios.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-643-8502; (410) 260-8540; TTY users call via MD Relay
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time trappers and any person who wants to trap furbearers in Maryland. It is required effective August 1, 2007 unless the person held a Furbearer Permit during the 2006-2007 trapping season. Also relevant for hunters, wildlife conservation enthusiasts, landowners with furbearer control problems, and individuals seeking to become licensed trappers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in trapper education and certification to legally trap furbearers including muskrat, beaver, raccoon, fox, opossum, mink, skunk, river otter, fisher, long-tailed weasel, and coyote. Instruction covers responsible trapping practices, equipment selection, selective trapping techniques to avoid non-target animals, water and land sets, bait/lure use, best management practices for various furbearer species, humane dispatch of trapped animals, fur processing, pelt processing and handling techniques, drying/freezing techniques, and compliance with all trapping regulations. Completion of workbook before class/test; hands-on training with instructors; preparation for trapper certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Trapper Classroom Courses are scheduled independently by training teams throughout the state. References Maryland-specific regulations and trapping requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A series of comprehensive training courses designed for logging professionals covering best management practices, logging aesthetics, forest management, field practicum, logging safety and OSHA compliance, first aid and CPR, and continuing education. The program provides instruction in forest management principles, forest ecology, proper harvest design and layout, and life-saving skills. Attendance is voluntary, and upon completion of initial training covering five key areas, Master Loggers receive endorsement and must attend at least one continuing education course each year to maintain their designation. Most courses cost between $20 and $40.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a series of comprehensive training courses covering five initial areas: best management practices for timber harvest design and erosion prevention, logging aesthetics to improve visual appearance of harvests, forest management covering forestry science and ecology, field practicum where loggers apply principles on the ground, and logging safety including OSHA requirements, first aid and CPR training. After completion of initial training, Master Loggers must attend at least one continuing education course each year to maintain their designation. Most courses cost between $20 and $40. Periodic job site visits may be held to maintain Master Logger designation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Logging professionals, landowners, foresters, and all interested individuals who want to improve their forestry knowledge and practices. No prior experience required to attend classes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education in forestry and logging practices including best management practices, logging aesthetics, forest management, field application, safety procedures, first aid and CPR, and continuing education on topics such as log grading and marketing, environmental regulations, deed and title research, trucking safety, and timber estimation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer training program in environmental education, research, and stewardship that teaches interested participants about Maryland's ecosystems, wildlife, plants, ecology, and environmental science through classroom and field instruction. The program covers a broad range of topics including forestry, birds, wetlands, native plants, insects, ecology, Chesapeake Bay, and interpretation/teaching. Graduates become certified Master Naturalists who volunteer to share their knowledge with their communities through teaching, leading field trips, participating in citizen science research, and engaging in ecological awareness efforts. The program requires 40 hours of volunteer service within one year of training completion and 40 hours annually thereafter to maintain certification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides classroom and field-based training in environmental education, research, stewardship, and natural resource topics including forestry, birds, wetlands, native plants, insects, ecology, Chesapeake Bay, and interpretation/teaching. Classroom materials are provided online. Participants receive certification as a Master Naturalist upon successful completion. Participants who complete the training must commit to 40 hours of volunteer work within one year of training completion and 40 hours annually thereafter to maintain certification.

Classroom materials are provided online. Participants receive certification as a Master Naturalist upon completion. Participants receive no direct financial assistance but must commit to volunteer work (40 hours within one year of training completion, 40 hours annually thereafter).

Classes are held on Wednesdays from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m., with Saturday field days scheduled for hands-on practice. Program is available to Maryland residents. The program is managed statewide through University of Maryland Extension and may be available in other locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive mentorship program that pairs skilled veteran hunters with first-time or lapsed hunters to teach hunting skills, techniques, firearm safety, and hunting strategies. The program includes technical lectures covering firearm safety, hunting tips, techniques and strategies, plus range time to prepare mentees for hunting. Participants receive ongoing support through in-person meetings, text, calls, or email. The program offers general mentorship through the learnhunting.org platform and specialized 2.5-day mentored hunting events such as the National Deer Association Mentored Deer Hunt, an intensive muzzleloader hunting experience held in Accident, Maryland (Garrett County) that includes orientation, facility tours (including processing facilities), range time, meals, and most equipment provided at no cost. All participants receive support and training at no cost.

The program also offers specialized 2.5-day mentored hunting events (such as the National Deer Association Mentored Deer Hunt) that include orientation, facility tours (including processing facility tours), range time, meals, and equipment provided at no cost.
