structured_extraction.program_description: A $13.5 million fund providing resources to address impacts to fish landing facilities in West Ocean City and support harbor maintenance needs and associated fishing businesses affected by offshore wind development. The fund supports programs and projects ensuring availability of sustained, long-term commercial fisheries landing infrastructure and service solutions, and enables safe and profitable fishing through initiatives supporting fishing industry and local harbor area resilience. The fund has three components: Facility Displacement Component, West Ocean City Harbor Maintenance Component, and Programmatic Funds Component. Resources support bulkhead stabilization, temporary ice service support, business development, harbor maintenance, and support for new entrants to the local fishing industry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial support through three components: (1) Facility Displacement Component providing capital funds, bulkhead stabilization, business interruption funds, and shoreside services for displaced fishing facilities/operators; (2) West Ocean City Harbor Maintenance Component supporting dredging, dock and shore stabilization; (3) Programmatic Funds Component providing gear development, business development/marketing, vessel resilience fund, new entrant incentives, and charter fisher marketing support. The fund makes $13.5 million available for capital improvements to fish landing facilities, bulkhead stabilization, temporary ice service support, business development, harbor maintenance, and support for new entrants to the local fishing industry. Funding is based on displacement options with US Wind making monetary fund payments based on the extent of displacement of existing fishing facilities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Natural Resources Police Reserve Officer Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer program that recruits civic-minded individuals to serve as Reserve Officers supporting the Maryland Natural Resources Police mission. Reserve Officers are not sworn law enforcement and do not have arrest powers. They perform non-law enforcement assignments including community and public relations outreach, boating and hunting safety education, search and rescue operations, vessel maintenance, courtesy boat inspections, office administration, and children's programs. Reserve Officers receive training and equipment and may qualify for a Maryland state tax credit based on hours served. Volunteers commit to a minimum of 100 hours of non-compensated service annually.

Reserve Officers may qualify for a State of Maryland tax credit based on hours performed in a given tax year, subject to certain restrictions and eligibility provisions. Minimum commitment is 100 hours of non-compensated service annually. Volunteers can participate in public relations, search and rescue, outreach programs, vehicle and vessel maintenance, courtesy boat inspections, boating safety, office administration, hunting safety, and children's programs.

Volunteers are not financially compensated but may receive a state tax credit for hours served.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to support equitable access to outdoor recreation for communities that have been historically underserved. The program funds community-based projects that help Marylanders overcome social, geographic, cultural, physical, and economic barriers to the outdoors, including distance, transportation costs, equipment costs, lack of exposure, and feelings of not being welcome. These mini grants support recreation projects that increase outdoor recreation opportunities and access for underrepresented communities.

Funds may be used for program staff, materials, transportation, outreach, gear, event costs, or other eligible expenses that directly support project goals. Projects must be completed by September 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Property Tax Credit for Conservation Easements
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that encourages donation of conservation easements to the Maryland Environmental Trust or the Maryland Department of Natural Resources by providing participating landowners a property tax credit on unimproved land under easement. The state-level credit is effective for 15 consecutive years beginning July 1 following the easement donation, with the credit applied to 100% of the assessment on the unimproved and non-commercial portion of the property. Conservation easements must be perpetual and approved by the Board of Public Works after June 30, 1986. The program has been effective since the 1987-88 tax year. Landowners receive a 15-year property tax credit on land subject to a donated conservation easement, with no property tax owed on land under easement for 15 years from the date of donation. The credit offsets state income tax liability and does not apply to residential improvements or a minimum of one acre around improvements. After 15 years, unimproved land is assessed at the highest agricultural rate. Additionally, many Maryland counties offer their own property tax credit programs for conservation easements, with credit amounts and durations varying by county.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State-level: A 15-year property tax credit applied to 100% of the assessment on unimproved and non-commercial portions of property placed under a perpetual conservation easement. The credit is effective for 15 consecutive years beginning July 1 following the easement donation. The credit must be applied to state, county, municipal, and special district property taxes. No property tax is owed on land under easement for 15 years from the date of donation. The credit offsets state income tax liability and does not apply to residential improvements or a minimum of one acre around improvements. County-level programs also exist in select Maryland counties, with credit amounts ranging from $500/year to 100% of county property tax obligation and durations varying from annual to 5-year terms with renewal options.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before October 1 of the taxable year for which credit is sought (state program); varies by county for county-level programs, generally June 1 prior to the year for which credit is sought, except Prince George's County which uses October 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland property owners with land subject to perpetual conservation easements donated to the Maryland Environmental Trust or the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief/credit against state, county, municipal, and special district property taxes for land under conservation easement; conservation of unimproved land through easement donations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide for the state program. County-level programs are available in 10 counties: Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Calvert, Charles, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Queen Anne's counties offer programs with varying terms. Fourteen counties do not offer county programs: Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Kent, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. Credit only applies to unimproved and non-commercial portions of land and excludes residential improvements and a minimum of one acre around improvements.
requirements_list: Land must be unimproved and non-commercial
Perpetual conservation easement must be donated to Maryland Environmental Trust or Maryland Department of Natural Resources
Easement must be approved after June 30, 1986 by Board of Public Works
Easement must be donated prior to July 1 of taxable year to be eligible for that year's credit
Recorded Deed of Conservation Easement must be obtained
Original application must be submitted to local Assessment Office on or before October 1 of the taxable year
Board of Public Works approval letter must be obtained
Application must be filed with County Office of Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

For county programs: varies by county, some restrict credit to original grantor (Charles County) or exclude residential structures and improvements; Calvert County restricts land to improvements with sheds and barns only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Donate perpetual easement to Maryland Environmental Trust or Maryland Department of Natural Resources. 2. Obtain Board of Public Works approval (must occur after June 30, 1986). 3. Record the Deed of Conservation Easement. 4. Complete the Conservation Property Tax Credit Application. 5. Submit original application with copy of recorded deed and Board of Public Works approval letter to County Assessment Office or County Office of Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation on or before October 1 of the taxable year for which credit is sought. 6. Local Supervisor submits assessment credit worksheet annually to local government. 7. Master list submitted to each jurisdiction by October. Contact the Maryland Environmental Trust at 410-514-7900 or Ann Carlson at 410-697-9524 to discuss conservation easement options and tax credit eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A law requiring that forests cleared during construction activities that result in cutting or clearing 1 acre or more of forest be replaced on a one-to-one acre-for-acre basis within two years or three growing seasons of project completion. Applies to State and local government agencies and any entity using State funding for construction projects. Replacement occurs on public lands, prioritizing sites within the same county or watershed as the impacted area. If suitable replacement land is not available, the constructing agent may purchase credits from a forest mitigation bank or deposit funds into the Reforestation Fund at ten cents per square foot or $4,356 per acre, which the Maryland Department of Natural Resources uses to plant replacement trees on public and private lands and respond to forest health emergencies.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For construction projects using State funding that result in clearing 1 acre or more of forest, the law requires reforestation at a one-to-one ratio within two years or three growing seasons of project completion. Reforestation prioritizes sites within the same county or watershed as the impacted area. Constructing entities must reimburse the Reforestation Fund at ten cents per square foot of cleared forest area. The constructing agency may satisfy the requirement through on-site planting, public land reforestation, forest mitigation bank credits, or monetary contributions to the Reforestation Fund, which the Maryland Department of Natural Resources uses to fund tree planting on public and private lands, forest health emergency response, forest mitigation bank establishment and maintenance, and limited administrative costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Prior to construction start (before any removal occurs) and during project initial design stages
structured_extraction.contact_name: Daniel Coy, Urban & Community Forestry Supervisor
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local government agencies; private entities using State funding for construction activities involving forest clearing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting on public and private lands; forest health emergency prevention and response; forest mitigation bank establishment and maintenance; reforestation and replacement of forest cover cleared during construction; mitigation of forest loss due to construction impacts; tree replacement for agricultural pest treatment impacts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies statewide to all construction projects in Maryland using State funding that involve clearing 1 acre or more of forest. Prioritizes reforestation sites within the same county or watershed as the impacted area; secondary priority given to other counties or watersheds within the State; forest mitigation bank credits available as last resort in the construction activity watershed.
requirements_list: Construction project must result in clearing 1 acre or more of forest
Minimize tree cutting and clearing to only necessary amount
Consult with Maryland Department of Natural Resources before cutting and before locating reforestation area

Submit Reforestation site review form (Form UF 920) along with project construction plans to the appropriate regional Forest Service office during project initial design stages, prior to any tree removal
Highlight forest areas to be removed on plans with removal amounts noted
Provide estimated tree clearing and reforestation summary
Identify on-site replacement acreage or alternate public lands locations
Replacement must occur on an acre-for-acre, one-to-one ratio on public lands
Replacement must be accomplished within two years or three growing seasons of project completion
Reimbursement required at 10 cents per square foot of cleared forest area
If replacement land in same county or watershed is unavailable, constructing agent must purchase forest mitigation bank credits or deposit funds into the Reforestation Fund
Receive Forest Service approval before any payments accepted
Submit annual reports to legislative committees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The constructing agent submits a Reforestation site review form (Form UF 920) along with the project's construction plans, highlighting forest areas to be removed and providing an estimated tree clearing and reforestation summary, to the appropriate regional office of the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service during the project's initial design stages, prior to any tree removal. The form should identify on-site replacement acreage or alternate public lands locations. The DNR Regional Forest Service office conducts field review within 20 working days to verify cleared acreage and appropriate replacement planting, and provides approval before any reforestation or payments proceed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A public-private partnership program that allows qualified individuals and non-profit organizations to live in and restore historic houses located on Maryland state parkland and natural resource areas. Participants receive the right to lifetime tenancy in exchange for restoring and maintaining historically significant structures to preservation standards and periodically sharing them with the public. Curators become stewards of both historic and natural resources while preserving cultural heritage for public benefit. Curators enter into agreements with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to undertake restoration work on designated properties, developing a detailed restoration schedule with cost estimates covering up to seven years, with a minimum total restoration value of $150,000. Curators may contribute sweat equity (self-provided labor) as part of the restoration work, and all improvements become state property upon completion. The program seeks to restore, protect, and share properties that are important to local, state, and national history.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Curators receive the right to reside in a historic house on state land for their lifetime in exchange for funding and performing restoration and ongoing maintenance. The annual lease rate is $1.00 per year. Curators must develop a detailed restoration schedule with cost estimates covering up to seven years, with a minimum total restoration value of $150,000. Typical restoration costs range from $150,000 to $300,000 over five to seven years, though initial investments typically range from $200,000 to $250,000 or more, and some properties may require significantly greater investment. Curators are responsible for all restoration costs (funded by the curator), utilities, fees, and ongoing maintenance, and may contribute sweat equity (self-provided labor). The state provides the property and stewardship oversight. Curators do not pay rent to the state but may owe property taxes as determined by the county. All improvements and work completed by curators become state property. Curators receive a Right of Entry to conduct tests and stabilization work while the final agreement is drafted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline stated; properties offered unpredictably as they become available
structured_extraction.contact_name: Manager of Curatorships and Cultural Resources
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and non-profit organizations committed to historic preservation with the skills, knowledge, interest, and financial means to restore historic structures on state natural resource land, who have experience or qualifications in historic preservation. Non-profit organizations with missions aligned to the specific land unit (State Park, Forest, Wildlife Management Area, etc.) are given preference.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration of historic houses and associated structures to good condition meeting current building codes and standards, including structural repairs, electrical, plumbing, and heating system improvements; lead paint abatement; installation of smoke and carbon monoxide detectors; kitchens, bathrooms, and systems upgrades (heating, air conditioning); ongoing maintenance of the house, grounds, and outbuildings; utility payments; and property taxes if assessed by the county. Labor costs (contract and volunteer sweat equity), materials, and contractor fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Historic properties located on Maryland state parkland, forests, wildlife management areas, and other state natural resource properties throughout Maryland, from Western Maryland mountain regions to Assateague Island. The specific location of available properties varies and is determined by the Department of Natural Resources based on curatorship offerings. All properties must be located on Maryland state-owned park lands managed by the Department of Natural Resources. The program manages nearly 50 historic properties that have been fully restored or are under restoration on over 500,000 acres of state land.
requirements_list: Demonstrated commitment to historic preservation
Desire to live in a historic house on state natural resource land
Skills, knowledge, interest, and financial means to restore a historic property
Ability to spend an estimated $150,000 to $300,000 over five to seven years on restoration (some properties may require significantly greater investment)
Willingness to maintain professionalism and courtesy as a representative of the Department of Natural Resources and the specific land unit
Agreement to restore and maintain the property according to historic preservation standards using original materials whenever possible
Adherence to all building codes and standards, including compliance with current standard building codes
Adherence to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for preservation
Responsibility for all utilities, fees, property taxes (if assessed), and ongoing maintenance costs
Commitment to opening the house to the public 3 to 5 times per year or pursuing alternative public engagement methods such as maintaining a blog or providing virtual tour materials
Compliance with all terms of the Curatorship Agreement
Submission of a detailed proposal and cover letter
Minimum restoration value of $150,000
Restoration schedule not to exceed seven years
Detailed cost estimates for each phase of work
Resume demonstrating experience or qualifications in historic preservation
Personal Financial Statement disclosing all assets and liabilities
Demonstration of financial capability to undertake restoration work
Exterior appearance of building must remain substantially the same
All exterior and interior alterations require prior Department approval
Property may not be subleased or transferred to heirs
Annual accounting of expenses to Department
Obtain all necessary permits and licenses before beginning work
Meet lead-safe work practice requirements for disturbing painted surfaces
Maintain comprehensive personal liability insurance ($1 million minimum per occurrence, $2 million aggregate)
Maintain property coverage on personal property
Maintain renters insurance with State as co-insured
All plumbing, structural, electrical work must be performed by licensed master professionals
Comply with environmental impact review (30-day process)
Comply with environmental laws (federal, state, and local)
Permission required before ground disturbance or archaeological impact
No subletting or long-term caretakers without Department consultation
No hunting permitted on premises
Limited livestock allowed only with Nutrient Management Plan
Minors cannot be parties to curatorship agreement
Submit annual reports with documentation, photographs, and fund expenditure records
Obtain written Landlord approval before alterations or major improvements
Submit technical plans reviewed by certified professionals and Maryland Historical Trust
Provide two copies of keys to all structures and gates
Maintain premises in neat, clean, safe, structurally sound condition
Manage hazardous materials (including asbestos and friable materials) with written landlord approval
Keep comprehensive records for minimum 5 years post-lease termination
Annual inspections by Curator Program Manager
Comply with Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990
Comply with Occupational Safety and Health Standards
Comply with Maryland Building Performance Standards
Comply with non-discrimination provisions (Title VII, Title 19)
Comply with all applicable state and local building codes
Political contribution disclosure if contract value exceeds $100,000
Commercial nondiscrimination compliance
Pay annual rent of $1.00 per year
Timely payment of utility costs and property assessments
All work must comply with Secretary of Interior's Standards for Historic Preservation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested parties should contact the Manager of Curatorships and Cultural Resources to discuss the proposal process. Applicants submit a proposal package electronically or by mail (no faxes) that includes: a cover letter outlining restoration objectives, resume(s) highlighting historic preservation experience and qualifications (one per curator), a detailed Schedule of Restoration with task-by-task breakdown and cost estimates for each year, a Personal Financial Statement, and any corroborating evidence of financial capability. A committee or interagency panel (including the area manager, DNR regional engineer, a Maryland Historical Trust representative, and the Manager of Curatorships and Cultural Resources) reviews and scores proposals, which typically takes approximately three months. If selected, applicants receive a Right of Entry to conduct additional tests or stabilization work. Written requests for alterations or major ground improvements are evaluated within 40 days; environmental reviews are completed within 60 days; major land use changes require State Clearinghouse and Board of Public Works approval. The final selection is referred to the Board of Public Works (Governor, State Comptroller, and State Treasurer) for approval and signature of the Curatorship Agreement. The process from proposal to final approval by the Maryland Board of Public Works generally takes about six months. After approval and once the property passes lead paint testing (which may require complete repainting at the curator's expense) and any required inspections (electrical, plumbing, septic), the curator may take residence and begin restoration work, which must be completed within 7 years of lease commencement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A law requiring the maintenance and reproduction of pine resources on harvested forest land to provide recreational, aesthetic, wildlife, and environmental benefits while supporting the wood fiber industry. Eligible harvested areas must be regenerated to pine either through seed trees or pine seedlings according to an approved pine reforestation plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The law requires landowners with harvested forest areas of at least five acres that are at least 25% loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine prior to harvest to regenerate the land to pine. If using seed trees, at least 8 cone-bearing pine trees per acre must be left healthy, wind-firm, and well-distributed. Regeneration is successful when at least 400 seedlings per acre are present, well-distributed, and free to grow. Landowners must follow a pine reforestation plan.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dan Rider or local DNR forester
structured_extraction.program_audience: Forest landowners with harvestable pine timber on at least five-acre parcels.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide financial assistance. It requires landowners to comply with reforestation standards for harvested pine forest land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies to all forest land in Maryland subject to harvesting that meets the law's requirements.
requirements_list: Harvested area must be at least five acres in size
Area must be at least 25% loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine prior to harvest
Land will not be converted to non-forest use such as agricultural or residential
If using seed trees, at least 8 cone-bearing loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine per acre must be left
Seed trees must be healthy, wind-firm, and well-distributed
At least 400 loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine seedlings per acre must be established and free to grow
A pine reforestation plan must be followed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners should contact their local DNR forester or the Maryland DNR Forest Service to discuss their harvested forest land and obtain guidance on meeting the law's reforestation requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Estate Tax Benefit for Conservation Easements
structured_extraction.program_description: When land is subject to a conservation easement, the appraised value for Maryland estate tax purposes is reduced because the easement limits the amount of development that can occur, thus lowering the taxable estate. Conservation easements reduce the appraised value of land for Maryland estate tax purposes by limiting development potential, thus reducing the taxable estate passed to heirs.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Conservation easements reduce the appraised value of land for Maryland estate tax purposes by limiting development potential, thus reducing the taxable estate passed to heirs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners whose heirs will inherit property subject to a conservation easement in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; this is a tax benefit related to property valuation and estate planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Land must be subject to a conservation easement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Work with a tax attorney or estate planner to incorporate conservation easement into estate planning strategy. The easement reduces taxable estate value at time of death.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Income Tax Credit for Conservation Easement Donations
structured_extraction.program_description: State income tax credit for donations of perpetual conservation easements to Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation. The credit is based on the appraised value of the easement (the difference in fair market values before and after easement conveyance, reduced by any payments received). Maximum credit is $5,000 per year per individual or pass-through entity, with aggregate cap of $200,000 per year for pass-through entities. Unused credit may be carried forward for up to 15 years for a maximum total credit of $80,000. Credit is in addition to federal income tax deduction, estate tax savings, and Maryland property tax credit. Passed by Maryland General Assembly in 2001; further legislation in 2016 allows pass-through entities to claim the credit.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit equal to the difference in fair market values of property before and after easement conveyance, reduced by any payments received for the easement. Maximum credit is $5,000 per year per individual or pass-through entity (with aggregate cap of $200,000 per year for pass-through entities), or the amount of state income taxes owed, whichever is smaller. For joint owners, each is separately entitled to up to $5,000 per year based on percentage ownership. Unused credit may be carried forward for up to 15 years for a maximum total credit of $80,000. Additionally, property tax credit provides exemption for 15 years on unimproved land subject to the donated easement, and estate tax benefits through lowered land valuation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual landowners and pass-through entities that donate conservation easements to Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credit applied to state income tax liability for landowners and pass-through entities conserving their land through perpetual conservation easement donations to preserve open space, natural resources, agriculture, forest land, watersheds, ecosystems, viewsheds, or historic properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Easement must be perpetual, conveyed to Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation, and approved by the Board of Public Works.
requirements_list: Landowner must donate perpetual conservation easement to Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation
Easement must be perpetual
Easement must be approved by the Board of Public Works
Maximum credit is $5,000 per year per individual or pass-through entity (aggregate cap of $200,000 per year for pass-through entities)
Total credit cannot exceed appraised value of easement
Payment received for easement must be deducted from credit
Taxpayer may not claim both state income tax deduction and credit for the same easement
For joint owners, each calculates credit based on percentage ownership
Qualified appraiser must establish easement value; fair market value must be substantiated by certified real estate appraiser
Remainder of credit may be carried forward for up to 15 years for maximum total credit of $80,000
Easement must meet IRS criteria for federal deductions
Land must be subject to a Deed of Conservation Easement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain a certified real estate appraiser to determine fair market value of property before and after easement conveyance. 2. Donate the easement to an eligible organization and obtain Board of Public Works approval. 3. Complete Form 502CR (for individuals) or Form 500CR (for pass-through entities), including Part F. 4. Attach substantiation of property values from certified appraiser and fair market value difference calculation to your Maryland tax return. Interested landowners may also contact the Maryland Environmental Trust (410-514-7900), Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (410-841-5860), or Department of Natural Resources (410-260-8367) for additional application details and appraisal information. Consult tax advisor or attorney for guidance on individual tax implications.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Income Tax Deduction for Conservation Easement Donations
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland allows certain individuals who itemize deductions on their federal income tax return to also itemize deductions on their Maryland income tax return, including conservation easement donations, subject to limitations.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual taxpayers who itemize deductions on their federal income tax return may itemize deductions on their Maryland return, including conservation easement donations. However, a taxpayer cannot deduct a conservation easement donation if they claimed the Maryland income tax credit for donating the same conservation easement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who itemize deductions on their federal income tax return and donate a conservation easement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Conservation easement donations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must itemize deductions on federal income tax return
Cannot claim both state income tax deduction and state income tax credit for same easement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Claim deduction on Maryland tax return when itemizing deductions. Cannot be used if state income tax credit is claimed for the same easement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative supporting riparian forest buffers along streams and shorelines. The program coordinates efforts among state, local, federal, and nonprofit agencies to expand and maintain streamside and shoreline forests that reduce nutrients flowing to the Chesapeake Bay. The program establishes riparian forest buffers (minimum 35 feet wide) along watercourses through planting or natural regeneration, with focus on restoring and conserving forests for water quality improvement and ecological benefits. Maryland has planted over 1,300 miles of riparian forest buffers since 1996. The program includes long-term monitoring and assessment of riparian forest buffer effectiveness in improving water quality, stream morphology, bank stability, and benthic macroinvertebrate health.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides coordination and support for riparian forest buffer establishment and maintenance through multiple funding mechanisms. Landowners can participate through cost-share programs including: Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP) providing soil rental payments and establishment support (50% federal cost-share, 37.5% state through Maryland Agricultural Cost-Share/MACS; total up to 127% of establishment costs), signup incentive bonuses ($10/acre/year and $200 signing bonuses), practice incentive payments (40% of eligible establishment costs), and establishment cost reimbursement (87.5% total); Environmental Quality Incentive Program (EQIP) with 50% cost-share; Conservation Security Program with tiered payments; Forest Lands Enhancement Program (FLEP) with 50% cost-share; Watershed Implementation Plan (WIP) with 50% cost-share; and Buffer Incentive Program. CREP contracts average over $3,700 per acre for hardwood buffers over 15 years with annualized costs of approximately $206 per acre. Annual soil rental payments range from 100-200% of soil rental value depending on contract year. Technical assistance is provided by MD DNR Forest Service, NRCS, and partner agencies for planting plan preparation, site design, and maintenance recommendations. The program works to increase the rate of forest buffer establishment throughout the Chesapeake Bay Watershed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 1 (for fall planting) and July 1 (for spring planting)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, agricultural producers, and conservation organizations seeking to establish or maintain riparian forest buffers along streams and shorelines in the Chesapeake Bay Watershed. Includes private landowners, watershed organizations, land trusts, local governments, nonprofit organizations, volunteer groups, and community organizations. Particularly focused on landowners in rural watersheds and agricultural areas with stream frontage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Native, non-invasive woody trees and shrubs for riparian buffer establishment, planting and maintaining streamside and shoreline forests to reduce nutrient runoff to the Chesapeake Bay, improve wildlife habitat, aquatic conditions, air quality, streambank stability, carbon sequestration, and timber production. Funds can also support site preparation, weed control, tree protection, ongoing maintenance activities, tree shelters for browse protection, mowing between trees, herbicide application or weeding, and post-contract timber harvesting opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across all Maryland counties, with primary focus on the Chesapeake Bay Watershed. Maryland is accountable for establishing buffers in the state portion of the watershed. Program operates across Western, Central, Southern, and Eastern regions of Maryland with targeting based on 11-digit state subwatersheds (WRAS - Watershed Restoration Action Strategy). Priority areas include Chesapeake Bay Lowlands (Southern Maryland and Eastern Shore), specific coastal zone counties for certain programs, and watersheds selected through prioritization framework based on riparian forest buffer coverage, water quality, forested land use, agricultural soil productivity, and proximity to drinking water intakes. Focus watersheds include Monocacy, Catoctin, and Antietam watersheds in the Potomac Watershed Partnership region. Targeted regions include areas surrounding Washington, D.C. and Baltimore, Hagerstown Valley area, and Eastern Shore. All 134 8-digit watersheds in Maryland are eligible for participation.
requirements_list: Minimum 35 feet wide buffer on one side of watercourse (or 100 feet total/35-100 feet on each side if buffering both sides); buffers may average over 100 feet wide
Forest buffers must meet stocking level standards (greater than 200 trees per acre acceptable, 400 trees per acre preferred; well-stocked stand of trees required by 5 years post-establishment)
Must contain more than one species of trees or shrubs
Emphasis on native species only; no invasive species
Landowners must submit buffer reporting form to be included in statewide accounting
Site preparation and matching species to site conditions required
Active maintenance of growing conditions around planted trees for 3 to 5 years recommended
For CREP contracts: 10-15 year commitment period required (with renewal options); restrictions on mowing during nesting season; compliance with state harvesting rules
Buffers must maintain minimum 60 sq.ft./acre basal area in 50-foot streamside management zone per state harvesting BMPs where applicable
No commercial harvest allowed during CREP contract period; noncommercial thinning permitted under CREP contracts
Participation may be voluntary, required, or through mitigation banking arrangements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners interested in participating should submit the buffer reporting form (RFB Form 9) to the Chesapeake Watershed Forestry Coordinator. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with deadlines of January 1 (for fall planting) and July 1 (for spring planting). Participants can enroll through cost-share programs like CREP, EQIP, CSP, FLEP, or WIP which provide financial incentives for buffer establishment and maintenance. Technical assistance is provided by MD DNR Forest Service and NRCS for site design, planting coordination, and maintenance recommendations. Partner agencies and Technical Service Providers coordinate implementation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Council Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Council (MUCFC) provides funding to support community-based tree planting and forestry education projects that strengthen Maryland's urban and suburban forests. Grants support work on public lands such as parks, school campuses, streetscapes, town centers, and municipal properties that improves the urban tree canopy, engages citizens, and promotes long-term environmental stewardship. The program funds both tree planting projects and street tree maintenance initiatives in urban settings through the USDA Forest Service. Projects with matching funds or in-kind support are given priority. Funding aims to unite and encourage citizens to protect and enhance Maryland's community trees and forest ecosystems.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $1,000 are awarded to organizations for community tree planting projects, street tree planting and maintenance projects, and forestry education projects on public lands such as school grounds, parks, town centers, streetscapes, and municipal properties. Projects with matching funds or in-kind support are given priority. Projects that promote urban tree canopy and long-term maintenance receive preference. Grants are provided through Forestry Boards and the USDA Forest Service. Unused funds must be returned with the final report. Funding may be used for tree purchases (native species only, no invasive species), tree planting supplies, signage with MUCFC acknowledgement, and equipment for tree planting with detailed future use plans.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: by 11:59 p.m. on January 15 and July 15
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, government agencies, community organizations, volunteer groups, citizen volunteers, Master Gardeners, Boy Scouts, schools, civic organizations, and public facilities working on public lands to improve urban forests and educate the public about trees. Funding is only available to organizations, not individual applicants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports tree planting projects and street tree maintenance on public lands such as school grounds, parks, town centers, streetscapes, or municipal properties; educational and outreach projects that raise public awareness about the value of trees in urban environments; tree purchases (native species only, no invasive species); tree planting supplies; signage with MUCFC acknowledgement; and equipment for tree planting with detailed plans for post-project handling and future use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations statewide are eligible to apply. Projects must occur on public lands in towns and cities throughout Maryland with populations of 2,500 or more. All Maryland counties and Baltimore City are eligible. Work requires approval and signature from the local County Forestry Board in each county.
requirements_list: All funded projects must occur on public lands such as school grounds, parks, town centers, streetscapes, or municipal properties
Funding is only available to organizations, not individual applicants
Applications must be approved by the MUCFC and signed by your local County Forestry Board prior to starting the project
Local Forestry Board member original signature required on applications
Tree planting projects must include a clear site plan and project description
Tree planting projects must include a list of tree species and sizes with native, shade-providing trees preferred and invasive species will not be funded
Tree planting projects must include a maintenance plan describing watering, mulching, weeding, and long-term care
Projects should use reasonably priced plant materials and source trees from the John S. Ayton State Tree Nursery or TreeMendous Maryland when possible
Educational and outreach projects must raise public awareness about the value of trees and include draft content or images for signage or publications
Educational projects must describe target audience and distribution plan
Educational projects must explain how the project addresses an unmet informational need
Clear credit to MUCFC must appear on all printed materials and signage
Signage must display the MUCFC logo
Species list, planting location map, and signage mockup must be attached to application
Matching funds or in-kind support from other organizations is required
Volunteer involvement in projects is required
Multi-year maintenance plan required for tree planting projects
Project must involve volunteers
Final reports must be submitted one month after the proposed completion date
Any unused funds must be returned with the final report
Failure to submit a final report or return unused funds may disqualify applicants from future grants
Equipment requests require detailed plan for post-project handling and future use
Documentation of expenditures with receipts required
Tracking of volunteers and volunteer hours required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Grant Guidelines. Download and complete the Grant application form in Adobe Acrobat Reader. Submit a project application online or by email to the MUCFC Grants Chair by the deadline of 11:59 p.m. on January 15 or July 15. The application must be approved by the MUCFC and signed by your local County Forestry Board prior to starting the project. Complete the project. Submit a final report one month after the proposed completion date including expenditure accounting, volunteer information, and impact measurements. Any unused funds must be returned with the report. Contact Dan Coy at daniel.coy@maryland.gov or 410-531-5973 for application materials, deadlines, and more information. Additional information can be found at http://www.marylandforestryboards.org/mucfc.cfm

structured_extraction.program_description: A full-time, paid, year-round employment program that empowers veterans and engages them in conservation service work on Maryland's public lands. The program combines hands-on conservation work with professional development training to help veterans pursue careers in environmental stewardship, conservation service, and land management. Veterans receive training, certifications, and work experience in park operations, maintenance, and conservation projects.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full-time, paid, year-round employment positions with competitive wages and health insurance benefits. Members receive extensive training including Emergency Medical Responder certification, Wildland Fire Fighter certification, Chainsaw Use and Care, Environmental Education and Interpretation, trail construction and maintenance, Basic Tool Use and Safety, Basic Carpentry, and Small Craft Safety. Uniforms, work shirts, sweatshirts, pants, winter jacket, and $200 boot reimbursement are provided. Personal protective equipment including safety glasses, ear protection, gloves, hardhats, and chainsaw chaps are supplied when needed. Members work a standard 40-hour workweek, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with some projects involving overnight stays and weekend hours. Positions are for one year with the possibility of contract renewal.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ranger Sara Marcinak, Director of Conservation Corps
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. Military Veterans seeking training, certifications, and work experience in conservation and natural resource management careers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment and professional development in conservation work including park operations, recreation management, trail building and maintenance, facilities improvement projects, educational programs, volunteer coordination, special events assistance, forest enhancement, tree planting, stream and wetland restoration, habitat restoration, and invasive species removal.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is based out of Merkle Natural Resource Management Area in Upper Marlboro, Maryland (11704 Fenno Road, Upper Marlboro, MD 20772, Prince GeorgeAs County) and works regularly in the Southern Maryland Regional Complex that includes Calvert Cliffs State Park, Cedarville State Forest, Chapel Point State Park, Chapman State Park, Hallowing Point Waterfront Recreation Area, Rosaryville State Park, and Smallwood State Park.
requirements_list: Prior service in the U.S. Armed Forces
Education or experience in park operations, recreation, education, business, administration, forestry, social sciences, or natural resources related field is preferred
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds repeatedly and use hand tools including heavy tools like pulaskis, sledge hammers, and chainsaws
Ability to travel to and from park locations and various work sites
Commitment to service and interest in natural resources and outdoor recreation
Willingness to attend mandatory overnight trainings and projects for up to one week at a time
Willingness to work certain weekends
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Ranger Sara Marcinak, Director of Conservation Corps, at sara.marcinak@maryland.gov or 443-370-8246 for application information and inquiries.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax incentive program that provides technical assistance to private landowners for creating, developing, rehabilitating, and preserving waterfowl habitats on their lands through ten-year renewable license agreements. Expenditures made for approved projects are considered contributions to the state and may provide tax benefits.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners enter into ten-year renewable license agreements with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. The program provides technical assistance from a Wildlife and Heritage Service biologist to help prepare a Waterfowl Habitat Management Plan. Expenditures made for approved habitat projects are considered contributions to the state of Maryland for tax purposes. The department annually documents project status and provides a standard form to the licensee for tax documentation. Landowners are responsible for substantiating actual expenditure amounts if requested by the State Comptroller. Minimum project area is ten contiguous acres with at least one acre of semi-permanent water.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Richard Walls, Migratory Game Bird Habitat Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners interested in developing and managing waterfowl habitats on their property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating, developing, rehabilitating, and preserving waterfowl habitats including food and cover for ducks, nesting and resting habitat, semi-permanent water areas, and wetlands restoration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects are reviewed by the Regional Habitat Biologist for the county where the property is located. Mailing address: Wildlife & Heritage Service, PO Box 68, Wye Mills, MD 21679.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a landowner
Minimum of ten contiguous acres of habitat that will provide food or cover for ducks
At least one acre of semi-permanent water with nesting and resting habitat within or near the semi-permanent water
Project must include semi-permanent water or wetlands
Private lands used for commercial hunting enterprises are not eligible
Normal agricultural practices are permitted within the project area
Landowner must complete the application form and include telephone number
Landowner must provide property location and directions
Applicant must draw a map showing nearest town, access roads, and property location
Approval of Waterfowl Habitat Management Plan mutually agreed to by licensee and Wildlife and Heritage Service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the project eligibility rules to determine if your proposed project area qualifies. 2. Complete the Maryland Waterfowl Restoration Program Application Form, providing landowner information, project area size, acres of semi-permanent water/wetlands, and property location details with map showing nearest town, access roads, and property location. 3. Mail the application to Wildlife & Heritage Service, PO Box 68, Wye Mills, MD 21679, or call 410-827-8612 ext 103 for information. Include your telephone number(s). 4. The Regional Habitat Biologist for your county will review your application and contact you to arrange an inspection of your project area for eligibility. 5. Once accepted, you will receive an official information kit containing all program documents and related publications. 6. After entering the program, you enter into a ten-year license agreement with an approved Waterfowl Habitat Management Plan. Questions can be directed to your district Wildlife Manager or the Migratory Game Bird Habitat Manager.

structured_extraction.program_description: A citizen science program where waterfront property owners and community organizations grow young oysters in wire mesh cages suspended from private piers for approximately 9-10 months. Participants receive oyster spat (young oysters) and cages at no charge, care for them in their cages, and then the grown oysters are collected and planted on local sanctuaries closed to harvesting to enhance the oyster population and create living oyster reefs. The program runs September through May, with summer as downtime for spat production. Program launched September 2008 designed to foster stewardship of Chesapeake Bay and create living oyster reefs in sanctuaries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive oyster spat and wire mesh cages at no charge. Up to four cages containing approximately 500 oyster spat per cage are provided to each participant. Cages are 18 inches long by 1 foot wide and are supplied with rope for attachment to piers or wharfs. DNR provides guidance and advice for program implementation, selects sanctuary locations for oyster planting, and guides oyster planting in sanctuaries. Optional data collection training and forms are available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: by March 31
structured_extraction.program_audience: Waterfront property owners with existing piers or wharfs, community associations, non-profit organizations, RiverKeepers or similar groups, local government entities, and public schools interested in supporting Chesapeake Bay restoration and oyster population enhancement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants use the program to grow young oysters in wire mesh cages suspended from private piers. The oysters are grown for approximately 9 months and then collected for planting on sanctuaries. Participants are not permitted to harvest or eat the oysters. Areas around private piers are not routinely tested and approved for shellfish harvest due to risk of pollution from septic system failures, pet drainage, and other sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is active in tributaries with appropriate salinity levels in Maryland's Chesapeake Bay region. Participants must have a pier or wharf with at least four feet of water at low tide located in one of the tributaries selected for the program. Program is statewide with focus on Chesapeake Bay waters. Currently operating in 32 rivers with target of at least 100 cages per river (approximately 4 cages per pier).
requirements_list: Must have an existing pier or wharf with at least four feet of water at low tide
Pier or wharf must be located in one of the tributaries selected for the program with appropriate salinity levels
Must be willing to provide maintenance for up to four cages of oysters for up to 10 months
Must have interest in the welfare of the Chesapeake Bay and becoming a Bay and oyster steward
Must rinse oysters every one to two weeks by lifting the cage up and down out of the water or using a hose
Must keep cages clean and maintain them in winter to prevent freezing
Must attach cages to pier or wharf so cage hangs at least 6 inches off the bottom, away from sand and silt
Must keep oysters entirely in water even on very low winter tides
Must NOT eat oysters raised through oyster gardening at private piers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals and organizations interested in participating should register through the Oyster Gardening Registration form by March 31. After signing up, participants will receive notification from the local sponsor that cages containing oyster spat are ready for pickup. At pickup, participants receive a short briefing and information package on oyster care, then receive their oyster cages. Participants attach the cages to their pier or wharf and provide maintenance for approximately 9 months until collection.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tree planting program that provides coupons for eligible tree species. The program encourages environmental stewardship by offsetting the cost of trees with a retail value of at least $50. Eligible individuals can obtain and use coupons at Marylanders Plant Trees (MPT) participating nurseries to purchase native trees and recommended cultivars.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible individuals can receive a coupon worth $25 off the purchase of one new native tree or recommended cultivar from a participating MPT nursery. The tree must have a retail value of at least $50. Coupons are accepted only at Marylanders Plant Trees participating nurseries. Trees must be from the recommended tree list, cultivars of native species, or native species to Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents interested in planting native trees on their property or in their community
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of native trees and cultivars of native species from participating nurseries; trees must be from the recommended species list or native species to Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at participating nurseries across Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Maryland
Tree must be from the recommended tree list OR be native to Maryland OR be a cultivar of a native species
Tree must be purchased from an MPT participating nursery
Retail value of tree must be at least $50
Contact program if concerns about a particular species
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Print or obtain a $25 coupon from the program website. Step 2: Find a participating MPT nursery in your area. Step 3: Select an eligible tree from the recommended list or a native species/cultivar. Step 4: Purchase the eligible native tree and apply the coupon toward the purchase. Contact Ryan Mayenschein at 667-408-0000 with species concerns.

structured_extraction.program_name: NOAA Chesapeake Bay Watershed Education and Training (B-WET Chesapeake) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to support hands-on watershed education for students and teachers to foster stewardship of the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants support hands-on watershed education for students and teachers to foster stewardship of the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Educators and schools seeking to provide watershed education and foster Bay stewardship
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support hands-on watershed education for students and teachers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Chesapeake Bay region
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the NOAA Chesapeake Bay Watershed Education and Training program website to apply for grants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A seven-day annual educational camp for high school students interested in careers in natural resources. The camp features instruction from natural resource professionals and covers traditional forestry, GIS and GPS technology, urban forestry, wildlife habitat, fisheries, and watershed ecology. Students develop employment contacts while learning from industry professionals. Students aged 16 and older can earn two college credits from Allegany College of Maryland by completing the full week and passing an exam. The Forestry Boards provide partial scholarships to two students from each county. The curriculum is professionally developed in partnership with the state's Forestry Boards to prepare young people for careers in natural resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A seven-day residential camp with curriculum developed by natural resource professionals covering traditional forestry, GIS and GPS technology, urban forestry, wildlife habitat, fisheries, and watershed ecology. Students age 16 and older can earn two college credits from Allegany College of Maryland by completing the full week and passing an exam. The Forestry Boards provide partial scholarships to two students from each county.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students age 16 and older interested in pursuing careers in natural resources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational training and instruction in natural resources topics; workforce development in natural resources fields; opportunity to earn two college credits from Allegany College of Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - high school students recruited from all Maryland counties and Baltimore City through Forest Conservancy District Boards, with two students selected from each county.
