structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through Grants Gateway within Outcome 5. Once an applicant creates a user profile, applications can typically be submitted between July and September for the following fiscal year funding consideration; Small Project Grants can be submitted anytime throughout the fiscal year. Applicants submit completed forms appropriate to their project type (dredging, fire and rescue grants, reimbursement requests, or 25K applications). For Fire & Rescue Grants: Application submitted by authorized local government official with required signatures from local government and recipient officials. For 25K Grants: Submit completed application form with project details, schedule, site plans, drawings, photographs, and bid tabulation. DNR reviews and approves project plans and specifications. For Dredging/Navigation Projects: Submit Dredging/Navigation Needs & Benefits Form with supporting documentation including project descriptions, boat ramp impact documentation, boat type and service information, and satellite/photo maps. For Reimbursement: Submit completed reimbursement packet via email to Regional Administrator including transmittal letter, Request for Reimbursement Form, supporting invoices with payment evidence, labor/equipment documentation, grantee checklist, and photos for final reimbursement. For all WIF Grants: Grantees must follow structured project management checklist including engineering selection, bidding, permitting, construction, and inspections with DNR approvals at key stages. Grant balances not disbursed within one year are subject to reversion unless extension granted.

structured_extraction.program_description: A lottery-based, do-it-yourself hunting program offering access to public lands stocked with pheasants for apprentice license holders, junior hunters, first-time full season license buyers, and lapsed hunters. Selected participants receive permits and maps showing pheasant release areas. Hunters supply their own gear and firearms during established small game hunting hours. No check-in or guided services required and there is no cost to participate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Selected participants receive a permit letter and map showing the specific location where pheasants are stocked and the area where they can hunt. Participants supply their own gear and firearms and hunt during established small game hunting hours on designated dates (November 22-23, 2025). No check-in or guided services required and there is no cost to apply or participate.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 3, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth (junior) hunters, apprentice hunters, first-time full season license buyers, and lapsed hunters (those who have not purchased a hunting license in the past two seasons or any three of the last five years)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to stocked pheasant hunting on public lands. Participants provide their own equipment and firearms.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Public lands across Maryland on November 22-23, 2025. Specific locations are provided to selected participants via permit letter and map.
requirements_list: Must be a youth (junior) hunter, apprentice hunter, first-time full season license buyer, or lapsed hunter
Lapsed hunters must not have purchased a hunting license in the past two seasons
Must have current hunting license or Apprentice License
Must have completed Hunter Education
Must supply own gear and firearms
Must follow small game hunting regulations and shooting hours
Must participate on designated dates (November 22-23, 2025)
A lapsed hunter is defined as one who held a Maryland hunting license in the past but has not purchased a license in the past two seasons
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Log into your MD Outdoors account and enter the lottery between July 1 and October 3, 2025. Select first, second, and third location choices and one preferred hunting day. Random selection will be held after the deadline with winners notified by October 24, 2025, with final email confirmation by October 31, 2025. Selected participants receive a permit letter and map.

structured_extraction.program_description: An educational program where classroom teachers, environmental education centers, and nature centers raise hatchery-bred bluegill sunfish in aquariums during the school year (October through May) and then release them at approved sites. The program provides aquarium supplies, fish, food, instructional materials, and reimbursement for fish release trip costs to support aquatic resources education. Optional aquaponics materials and training are also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources provides aquarium supplies for starter and replacement kits (approximately $300 value per set, space limited, first-come-first-serve basis), hatchery-raised bluegill sunfish and fish food at no cost, a teacher's manual and data sheets, lesson plans and background information, training workshop on bluegill/sunfish care and aquaponics (optional), and reimbursement for fish release trip costs including 50% of total bus costs (maximum 3 buses) and 100% of substitute teacher costs (maximum 3 substitutes). Reimbursement requires itemized invoices with receipts and school principal certification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 15th (annual registration deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Classroom teachers, environmental education centers, nature centers, schools, and educational organizations in Maryland (including Title 1 schools, though not required) that want to provide aquatic resources education to students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Aquarium supplies, bluegill sunfish, fish food, instructional materials, optional aquaponics materials, and reimbursement for transportation (buses) and substitute teacher costs associated with fish release field trips. Approved expenses require itemized receipts and school principal certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program serving all 24 counties. Fish pickups available at multiple locations: Patapsco Valley State Park in Baltimore County, Gambrill State Park in Frederick County, William S. Schmidt Outdoor Education Center in Prince George's County, and Cedarville Fish Hatchery in Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Must be a classroom teacher, environmental education center, nature center, school, or non-formal educator
Participants must register every year by May 15th
Must be available for mandatory training workshop (held on 2nd Saturday of September for new participants; every 3 years for returning participants)
Must be available for one of the designated fish pickup days in early October (first and second Thursday)
Fish must be raised and lessons conducted between October and May
Fish must be released at an approved site no later than June 30th or request permission to keep longer
Reimbursement packages including invoices and proof of purchase must be submitted by June 30th
Participants must complete the ARE reporting form by July 31st
Failure to report will result in unenrollment from the program
Inventory materials upon receipt and report missing/broken items immediately
Return all equipment to Maryland DNR in Annapolis if not continuing program
Submit demographic form for grant reporting purposes; failure to submit results in ineligibility for following school year
School Principal signature and certification required for reimbursement
Federal ID # (9-digit EIN) required for reimbursement

Water quality monitoring required with specific parameters: Total Ammonia <2.5 ppm (Optimum: 0), Unionized Ammonia <0.12 ppm (Optimum: 0), Nitrite Optimum 0, Nitrate Optimum <40 ppm, pH Range 6.5-8.5, Temperature Range 65-80°F
Provide clean 5-gallon bucket for dechlorinating water
Provide panty hose for filter intake protection
Provide metric ruler for fish measurements
Hands must be soap-free during aquarium maintenance
Establish routine daily, weekly, and monthly maintenance schedule
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete online Google Form registration by May 15th each year (first-come-first-serve acceptance based on budget availability; decisions made after deadline). 2. Attend the mandatory teacher training workshop on the 2nd Saturday of September (required for new participants; every 3 years for returning participants). 3. Pick up fish and supplies on one of the designated October dates (first and second Thursday), or arrange pickup at alternative locations. 4. Raise fish and conduct lessons from October through May using provided instructional materials (20-gallon glass aquarium, canister filter, air pump, air stones, tubing, test kits, bacterial starter culture, water conditioner, thermometer, fish net, batteries, and fish food) and monitoring water quality parameters. 5. Release fish at an approved site by June 30th with available DNR staff support (request minimum 2 weeks in advance). 6. Submit reimbursement packages by June 30th with itemized invoices, receipts, and school principal certification. 7. Complete the ARE reporting form online by July 31st.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing fishing equipment to enjoy recreational fishing

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that helps Maryland residents and organizations restore tree cover on public land and community open space by providing affordable native trees for planting at schools, parks, local open space, and street locations. The program offers two main components: organizations can order native trees and shrubs at reduced cost with free delivery to three locations across the state each spring and fall (with additional fees available for direct delivery), and individuals can make gift contributions to plant trees in honor or memory of loved ones or for special occasions. Individual donors can purchase trees at $40 per tree or a grove of ten trees for $400, with framed certificates mailed to recipients within one week of order. Trees are planted on public lands and community spaces in areas of greatest need, typically in cities, towns, parks, playgrounds, schoolyards, and along creeks and streams. The program has assisted more than 3,000 towns and communities, parks, and schools.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tree-Mendous provides native trees at reduced cost to local governments, community groups, and individuals for planting on public land and open spaces. Individual donors can purchase trees at $40 per tree or a grove of ten trees for $400. Each contribution supports the planting and care of native trees. A framed certificate is mailed to the recipient within one week of order. Organizations can arrange free delivery to three locations across the state each spring and fall, with additional fees available for direct delivery to their site. Trees are planted during the next appropriate growing season (spring or fall) on public lands and community spaces in areas of greatest need. The program has assisted more than 3,000 towns and communities, parks, and schools.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Place orders at least one week before desired certificate arrival date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, community groups, schools, parks, organizations, and individuals seeking to plant trees and restore tree cover on public land in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing and planting native trees and shrubs on public land, schools, parks, local open space, street locations, and community open spaces
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland on public lands and open spaces. Trees are planted in the county where the certificate recipient lives, or based on project priorities and planting needs throughout Maryland. Planting occurs in cities and towns, parks, playgrounds, schoolyards, and along creeks and streams.
requirements_list: Organization must have permission from landowners to plant trees
Trees must be planted on public land or community open space, not private property
Order form is password protected and requires organization information and location verification
Donor must specify recipient of the gift certificate
Separate order form required for each recipient
Certificate must be ordered at least one week in advance for holiday delivery
Organization must complete the Tree-Mendous order form agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in ordering trees should send their organization's information and location to ryan.mayenschein@maryland.gov to request access to the password-protected Tree-Mendous order form at clearridgenursery.com. Individual donors complete a Gift of Trees order form specifying the recipient and can order trees at $40 per tree or $400 for a grove of ten trees. A certificate is issued and mailed within one week. Trees are delivered during spring and fall planting seasons based on project priorities and areas of greatest need.

structured_extraction.program_description: An educational program that provides classroom teachers, environmental education centers, and nature centers with financial aid, starter kits, fish eggs, food, training, and technical assistance to raise hatchery-bred rainbow trout in the classroom and conduct aquatic science lessons with students in grades 3-12. Students raise trout from eggs, learn about fish biology, aquatic ecosystems, and environmental stewardship, and participate in organized fish release events at approved sites. The program introduces youth to cold water conservation and nurtures conservation ethics in students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources provides financial aid to schools as the budget allows. New schools receive one starter kit (approximately $700) and one chiller. Returning schools receive one replacement kit (approximately $220). The program provides hatchery-raised rainbow trout eggs and fish food at no cost. Reimbursement is available for fish release trip costs: 50 percent of the total cost of buses (maximum of 3 buses) and 100 percent of the total cost for substitute teachers (maximum of 3 substitutes). Teacher training workshops are provided in fall, and schools receive access to lesson plans, background information on trout species, and reporting forms. DNR provides priority technical support for the first two years and emergency equipment access from a volunteer network for new participants. Optional annual replacement supplies kits are available. Water quality testing materials and tank maintenance supplies are also provided. Schools must purchase at their own cost: insulation board, surge power strip, bucket, measuring spoons, pipette, baking soda, safety glasses, turkey baster, and towel. No delivery services are provided.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens January 1 (deadline March 15); Invoice packages due June 30; Reporting form due July 31
structured_extraction.program_audience: Classroom teachers, environmental education centers, and nature centers serving grades 3-12 students in Maryland. Also includes school administrators, students, and program volunteers. K-12 schools, universities, government agencies, environmental educators, and community organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Starter kits and replacement kits for raising trout in classrooms, fish eggs and food, teacher training workshops, reimbursement for fish release trip transportation and substitute teacher costs, access to lesson plans and educational materials, water quality testing materials, tank maintenance supplies, and aquarium equipment and supplies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland including Washington D.C. Fish releases must occur at approved release sites per permit requirements. Program operates statewide across all Maryland counties, with trout stocked in more than 100 streams and lakes throughout the state. Program stocks over 500,000 trout annually.

Must register annually by March 15th
Must submit signed Memorandum of Intent (MOI) with registration
Must attend fall teacher training workshop hosted by Trout Unlimited volunteer coordinators
Must maintain an Aquatic Studies Permit issued by DNR
Must raise fish from October through May
Fish releases must occur at an approved release site
Must complete and submit reporting form by July 31st
Reimbursement packages must include invoices, proof of purchase, and updated W-9 form for the school or organization
Students must wear waders or rubber boots when wading; no wading above knees
No bare feet in stream
Hand washing and tick checks required after stream visits
Release sites must be checked for safety hazards
Sites must have accessible open area next to stream
Must adhere to state rules, policies, procedures, and reporting protocols
Must be flexible with pickup/delivery coordination
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register online by March 15th and submit signed Memorandum of Intent. 2. Attend fall teacher training workshop in late October or early November hosted by Trout Unlimited volunteer coordinators. 3. Receive aquatic studies permit from DNR in early December. 4. Receive fish eggs distributed in early December from Albert Powell Fish Hatchery. 5. Raise fish and conduct lessons from October through May. 6. Conduct fish releases in April or May at approved sites. 7. Submit reimbursement package by June 30th with invoices, proof of purchase, and W-9 form. 8. Complete reporting form by July 31st.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free lifetime pass that provides eligible individuals with disabilities and nonprofit groups free entrance to all public lands managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, including parks, state forests, and wildlife management areas. The pass covers the cardholder and one additional accompanying person. The pass does not require renewal and is non-transferable. It also allows eligible hunters with mobility impairments to hunt from a vehicle under the ADA/504 program when possessing a valid Maryland hunting license. A physician must certify applications for the hunting component. The pass does not cover automated gate entrance systems, camping fees, boat launches, rentals, bus parking, or other concessions and special charges.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free lifetime non-transferable pass providing free entrance to all public lands managed by the Department of Natural Resources, including parks, state forests, and wildlife management areas for the cardholder and one accompanying person. The pass does not require renewal. The pass does not cover automated gate entrance systems, camping fees, boat launches, rentals, bus parking, or other concessions and special charges. For hunting from a vehicle: a physician must certify the permit application. The vehicle must be at a complete stop with the motor turned off while shooting, aiming, or firing the weapon. All weapons must be unloaded while the vehicle is in motion. No loaded weapons are permitted in the vehicle on public roadways or road shoulders. Only the permit holder, other permit holders, and one non-hunting companion may be in the vehicle while hunting.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities (permanent or temporary) as defined by Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, including those with VA disability determinations, MVA disability parking certifications, or certifications from licensed health care professionals; nonprofit groups serving clients with disabilities; and hunters with mobility impairments seeking to hunt on public hunting lands in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free entrance to public lands managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, including parks, state forests, and wildlife management areas. Pass holder may also hunt from a vehicle on designated public hunting lands when possessing a valid Maryland hunting license and physician certification for the hunting provision.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide—all Maryland public lands managed by the Department of Natural Resources, including State Parks, State Forests, Wildlife Management Areas, and designated public hunting areas. Service centers located across six Maryland regions (Central, Eastern, Southern, Western).

Must provide one of the following: VA disability determination letter, MVA disability parking certification, or certification from licensed health care professional
Licensed health care provider must be physician, chiropractor, optometrist, podiatrist, or nurse practitioner

Health care provider certification must document impairment(s) that substantially limit one or more major life activities and include provider signature, specialty, address, phone, email, medical license number, issuing state, and expiration date
For nonprofit applications, must provide evidence of current non-profit status
For hunting, must possess a valid Maryland hunting license
For hunting from a vehicle, applicant must have a mobility impairment
For hunting from a vehicle, physician must certify the permit application
Permit holder must have the Universal Disability Pass on their person while hunting
Vehicle must be at a complete stop with motor turned off while shooting, aiming, or firing
Only the permit holder, other permit holders, and one non-hunting companion may be in the vehicle while hunting
All weapons must be unloaded while vehicle is in motion
No loaded weapons in vehicle on public roadways or road shoulders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Universal Disability Pass application form with name, phone number, and DNR ID, and submit to a local Maryland DNR Regional Service Center by appointment only. For individual applications, provide one of the following: VA disability determination letter, MVA disability parking certification, or certification from licensed health care professional. For nonprofit applications, include evidence of nonprofit status and disability certification from licensed health care provider. For the hunting provision, physician certification is required.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Volunteer Fire Assistance Grant Program provides financial, technical, and related assistance to rural volunteer fire departments to enhance their wildland fire suppression capabilities, improve firefighter safety, promote the use of wildland personal protective equipment, and provide basic wildland fire training classes for volunteer fire department members. The program supports fire department operations and community fire safety initiatives through grants, subsidies, and technical assistance to help departments acquire or maintain equipment and obtain training to better fight wildfires.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funds from USDA Forest Service reimburse up to 50 percent of eligible costs on a 50/50 cost-share basis. VFA sub-grants of up to $3,500 per department per year are awarded competitively based on a points system that prioritizes wildland firefighting equipment and training. Federal payment is capped at $3,500 maximum. Eligible uses include wildland personal protective equipment, power tools, firefighting equipment, pumping units, communications equipment, all-terrain vehicles, and wildland firefighting training. Financial, technical, and related assistance is available to rural volunteer fire departments and their communities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 15, 2025 at 4:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural volunteer fire departments serving communities with a population of 10,000 or less, or area fire departments whose service area includes a rural area or rural community with a population of 10,000 or less, and their communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wildland personal protective equipment (flame-resistant clothing, hard hats, eye protection, leather gloves, hearing protection, chainsaw chaps, fire shelters), wildland firefighting power tools (chainsaws, leaf blowers), wildland firefighting equipment (fire hose less than 2.5 inches, nozzles, adapters, bladder bags, chainsaw supplies), wildland fire engine and utility vehicle pumping units, rehabilitated wildland firefighting equipment from federal excess programs, fire communications equipment (pagers, radios), off-road ATVs and utility vehicles, equipment for ATVs and UTVs that support wildland firefighting, wildland firefighting training including tuition for National Wildfire Coordinating Group or chainsaw training, fire department operations, and community fire safety initiatives. Grants cannot be used for capital improvements, vehicle purchases, equipment solely for structural firefighting, hazardous material response or rescue, fire hose larger than 2.5 inches, medical equipment, or emergency medical services equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Rural volunteer fire departments or rural communities with population of 10,000 or less based on latest Census data.
requirements_list: Must be a rural volunteer fire department
A single fire department must serve a rural area or rural community with a population of 10,000 or less based on latest Census
Area fire departments may serve an aggregate population greater than 10,000 if their service area includes a rural area or rural community having a population of 10,000 or less
Departments must provide a 50/50 cost match
Equipment must have application to wildland firefighting
Equipment cannot be solely for structural firefighting, hazardous material response, rescue, or emergency medical services
Purchases must occur between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2025
Grants will not be approved for medical, rescue, or HAZMAT equipment, capital construction projects, or vehicle purchases
Fire hose must be less than 2.5 inches in diameter
Grants are awarded on a competitive basis using a points system
Supporting documentation including proof of purchase and payment must be submitted within specified timeframe
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a web-based application before September 15, 2025 at 4:00 p.m. Receive confirmation email with copy of responses. Notification of approval or denial by October 15, 2025. If awarded, receive supporting documentation including Memorandum of Understanding. Make purchases by December 31, 2025 and submit supporting documentation by January 15, 2026. Maryland Forest Service reimburses within 45 days of receiving necessary documentation based on 50/50 cost-share agreement (maximum $3,500).

structured_extraction.program_name: Warrior Hike Walk Off The War Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An outdoor therapy program supporting combat veterans transitioning from military service by thru-hiking America's three national scenic trails: the Appalachian Trail, Pacific Crest Trail, and Continental Divide Trail. The program addresses the gap in decompression time modern military personnel experience and responds to high PTSD rates among Iraq and Afghanistan veterans (over 20% affected). Participants receive equipment and supplies required to complete a thru-hike, trail town support coordinated with veteran and hiking organizations along the trails, and assistance with future employment opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Warrior Hike provides participants with equipment and supplies required to complete a thru-hike on one of America's three national scenic trails (Appalachian Trail, Pacific Crest Trail, or Continental Divide Trail). The program coordinates trail town support including food, transportation, and lodging with veteran and hiking organizations located along the trails, and assists with future employment opportunities through partnered companies and veteran hiring services. Participants also receive camaraderie and community support opportunities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Combat veterans honorably discharged from the U.S. military who seek to thru-hike a national scenic trail
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment and supplies for thru-hiking, trail support including food, transportation and lodging, and employment placement assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Veterans thru-hiking America's three national scenic trails: the Appalachian Trail (2,185 miles, 14 states from Georgia to Maine), Pacific Crest Trail (2,650 miles, 3 states from California to Washington), and Continental Divide Trail (3,100 miles, 4 states from New Mexico to Montana)
requirements_list: Must have served in a combat zone
Must be honorably discharged from the U.S. military
Must desire to thru-hike one of the three national scenic trails
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Warrior Hike website at warriorexpeditions.org/apply/

structured_extraction.program_description: Free water safety education programs designed for all age groups from pre-kindergarten through adult. Programs teach basic water safety concepts and boating safety information to help prevent drowning tragedies. Programs are simple, fun, customizable, and typically last 15 minutes to one hour.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free water safety training programs that can be scheduled for groups. Programs are customizable based on age group and needs. Participants need only provide a room full of interested students and possibly a VCR and TV. Program length ranges from 15 minutes to one hour depending on content selected.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students of all ages from pre-kindergarten through adult who want to learn water safety and boating safety.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education in water safety and boating safety concepts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Group of interested students willing to attend the program
Space to hold the program (such as a classroom or meeting room)
Possibly a VCR and TV depending on the program format
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Safety Education Section of the Maryland Natural Resources Police to schedule a program. Call 410-643-8502 or email Donna Seymour at donna.seymour@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A license that authorizes a person or business to conduct a waterfowl processing operation in Maryland. The license allows the holder to receive, process, and handle wild waterfowl that have been legally harvested and are properly tagged according to state and federal laws and regulations. Processors must maintain detailed logs of waterfowl processing activities, including species, harvest locations, delivery dates, and customer information.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A no-cost, no-fee license issued by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. The license is valid for one year and expires on June 30 following the date of issuance. Licensees must maintain detailed processing logs documenting all waterfowl processed, including species, harvest location, dates received and delivered, customer names and addresses, and processor book number. All books (used or unused) must be returned prior to March 1st annually. Licensees may renew by submitting a completed renewal application. Licensees must comply with Maryland Workmen's Compensation Act by providing a certificate of insurance, insurance binder number, or declaring self-employed or family-only employment status.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1st (for return of all books, used or unused)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and businesses that wish to conduct waterfowl processing operations in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The license permits the holder to receive, process, and handle wild waterfowl that has been legally harvested and properly tagged in accordance with state and federal laws.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must apply using a form supplied by the Department of Natural Resources
Applicant must not have been convicted of violating state game laws, regulations, federal game laws, or regulations
All waterfowl received must be properly tagged as required by state and federal laws and regulations

Licensee must maintain detailed records of all waterfowl processed, including species, location harvested, dates received and disposed of, and names and addresses of persons from whom waterfowl were received and to whom they were delivered
Licensee must submit annual record copies to the Department prior to March 1st of the permit year
Licensee must allow inspection of premises and records by Natural Resources Police officers or law enforcement at any reasonable hour
Licensee must not violate any provision of state wildlife laws, regulations, or federal game laws or regulations or face suspension or revocation of license
Licensee must record processor name and book number in processing logs
Licensee must log date received, customer name and address, species, number, location of harvest, and date delivered for each entry
Licensee must keep a copy of processing logs for records
Application fee is $0.00
Licensee must comply with Maryland Workmen's Compensation Act by providing a certificate of insurance, insurance binder number, or declaring self-employed or family-only employment status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain an application form from the Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife and Heritage Service. 2. Complete the Waterfowl Processing Operation Permit Application and print or type all pages. 3. Submit the application to the Permits Coordinator at Tawes State Office Building, 580 Taylor Ave E-1, Annapolis, MD 21401, by email to wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov, or by phone at 410-260-8538 or 410-260-8540. 4. Schedule an appointment if needed by emailing wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or calling 410-260-8540. 5. Contact the Permits Coordinator at 410-260-8538 to request processing log books. 6. Complete logs and return all books (used or unused) to the Wildlife and Heritage Service prior to March 1st annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: A collaborative program that connects and coordinates various resources and technical assistance available across the state to local communities and governments for watershed-related projects, watershed management, and environmental improvement activities. The program partners with The Environmental Finance Center, Chesapeake Bay Trust, and University of Maryland to provide grants for planning and designing water quality improvement projects, as well as technical assistance, project management, help with financing strategies, and training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Collaborative provides both technical assistance and financial assistance to eligible recipients for watershed-related projects, watershed management, and environmental improvement. Assistance includes project grants, technical help with project management, financing strategies, stakeholder outreach, and training for local governments and organizations. Resources are available year-round.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Year-round
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-profits, universities, and community groups in Maryland working on watershed protection, restoration projects, and environmental improvement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Watershed-related projects, watershed management, environmental improvement activities, design, watershed planning, program development, project management, financing strategies, and stakeholder outreach.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Youghiogheny watershed, or the Maryland Coastal Bays. Statewide resources available to Maryland communities and governments.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To get help, communities fill out a Request for Resources & Services Form. A separate Request for Proposals is available for the grant program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program managed by the Chesapeake Bay Trust that provides technical planning and design assistance for protection and restoration programs and projects that improve water quality in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed and the Maryland Coastal Bays. Planning projects include watershed characterization, survey, assessment, action plans, or financing plans. Design requests are accepted for the full suite of non-point source best management practices, including living shoreline and watershed restoration projects to reduce non-point source pollution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical planning and design assistance provided through grants. The program covers watershed characterization, survey, assessment, action plans, financing plans, and design for non-point source best management practices, including living shoreline and watershed restoration projects. The program works with local governments and non-profit organizations through the Chesapeake Bay Trust to fund planning efforts and design requests for best management practices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and non-profit organizations in Maryland seeking technical planning and design assistance for water quality improvement projects in the Chesapeake Bay watershed and Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning and design assistance for watershed protection and restoration projects, including watershed characterization, surveys, assessments, action plans, financing plans, and best management practice designs to reduce non-point source pollution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed and the Maryland Coastal Bays. Available statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should visit the Chesapeake Bay Trust website for grant details and to see a list of preferred contractors. Proposals are submitted through that partner organization.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Assistance – Two-Year Milestone Support Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development for protection and restoration programs and projects that lead to improved water quality in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding for design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development associated with protection and restoration programs and projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local communities, jurisdictions, and organizations undertaking comprehensive watershed protection and restoration activities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development for protection and restoration programs and projects that improve water quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves communities within the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities interested in undertaking comprehensive watershed protection and restoration activities should fill out the Request for Resources & Services Form or contact the Chesapeake & Coastal Service for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A five-year pilot program that provides collaborative, science-based funding and technical assistance to accelerate restoration of the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays and their watersheds. The program funds multi-faceted environmental actions including pollution reduction, habitat creation, aquatic resource improvements, equitable public access, carbon sequestration, and public health enhancements in five selected watersheds. The program combines existing funding sources and focuses on a coordinated approach involving multiple state agencies and local partners to achieve water quality improvements, habitat restoration, pollution reduction, and community benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Implementation Grants that cover up to 50 percent of project implementation costs (up to $2 million per watershed for FY2026), Operations Grants for project administration costs (including $20,000 for operational expenses per watershed), and Water Quality Monitoring Grants (totaling $1.25 million or $250,000 per watershed). Project sponsors must provide 50 percent matching funds from sources outside the Whole Watershed Fund. Matching funds can include cash or in-kind contributions and must be spent after July 1, 2025. Funds are distributed to the Project Sponsor quarterly based on reimbursement requests. Eligible restoration and conservation actions include urban tree plantings, riparian forest buffers, cattle stream exclusion fencing, row crop conversion to pasture, stormwater management, stream restoration, shoreline stabilization, habitat restoration, wetland restoration, wildlife habitat creation, septic and sewer improvements, and green infrastructure.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The original Request for Proposals (RFP) was issued October 1, 2024 and due on December 3, 2024. Awardees were selected in March 2025. The next RFP will be released by October 1, 2029.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipal, county, and regional agencies; nonprofit organizations; faith-based groups; homeowners associations; and soil and water conservation districts working on watershed restoration projects in eligible five-year pilot watersheds. The program prioritizes overburdened and underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, engineering of restoration and conservation projects; legal documents including permits and easements; maintenance; community outreach; implementation of best management practices; habitat restoration; stormwater management; water quality improvements; climate resilience actions; urban tree plantings; riparian forest buffers; cattle stream exclusion fencing; row crop conversion to pasture; shoreline stabilization; wetland restoration; wildlife habitat creation; septic and sewer improvements; green infrastructure; nature-based infrastructure; public access improvements; and water quality monitoring for a minimum of 5 years post-project completion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is currently in a five-year pilot phase with five selected watersheds: Antietam Creek (Washington County), Baltimore Harbor (Baltimore City), Upper Choptank River (Talbot and Caroline Counties), Newport Bay (Worcester County), and Severn River (Anne Arundel County). One watershed must be urban, one suburban, two agricultural, one with an adjoining state, and two with opportunities to engage overburdened or underserved communities. The program is organized by 8-digit watersheds within the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays and their tributaries.
requirements_list: Project must be located in one of the five selected pilot watersheds (Antietam Creek, Baltimore Harbor, Upper Choptank River, Newport Bay, Severn River)
Project must result in greatest improvements to shallow water habitat and living resources, achieve rapid de-listing of impaired streams, or generate rapidly improving ecosystem conditions
Project must emphasize cost-effective and measurable pollution reduction
Project must support land use policies, conservation programs, and restoration protocols at the local level that will sustain outcomes
Must document interest from affected property owners to allow restoration or conservation actions on their property
Project must minimize loss of trees and natural habitats
Must demonstrate opportunities to implement actions reducing environmental disparities in overburdened or underserved communities
Project must provide at least five co-benefits related to habitat, aquatic resources, carbon sequestration, climate resilience, employment, public health, or recreational access
One single project sponsor must be identified to administer the project, though partnerships and sub-awards to other entities are allowed
Project sponsor must hold at least 4 community meetings per year including local government representation
Must provide opportunity for public comment on preliminary designs of major or large-scale actions
Project sponsors must work with State Management Team to develop Implementation and Financing Plan

Outside matching funds must not be from Whole Watershed Fund sources (Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund, Bay Restoration Fund, Clean Water Commerce Act, Waterway Improvement Fund, Maryland Agricultural Cost Share Program, Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Fund)
Only projects implemented after July 1, 2025 are eligible for grant funding and match
Projects must be endorsed by each county and municipal corporation in which the project will occur
Project sponsor must provide 50 percent matching funds from non-Whole Watershed Fund sources
Matching funds must be spent after July 1, 2025
State Management Team approval required
State Management Team approval required by March 1, 2025 for current cycle; approval every 5 years thereafter
Stream restoration projects must use licensed stream restoration contractors
Water quality monitoring for minimum 5 years (may extend beyond 5 years if required by State Management Team)
Public notice required at 30% design completion
Public meeting required at 60% design completion (with exceptions for individual property owners)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit proposals through a Request for Proposals (RFP) process. The original RFP was issued October 1, 2024 with a December 3, 2024 deadline, with awardees selected in March 2025. The next RFP will be released October 1, 2029 with proposals due by March 1 of the following year. Proposals are evaluated by the State Management Team based on watershed selection criteria including water quality benefits, ecosystem improvements, cost-effectiveness, experience, ability to match state investment, environmental justice opportunities, innovation potential, and multiple co-benefits. Selected project sponsors work with the State Management Team to develop an Implementation and Financing Plan with measurable outcomes. Funds are distributed to the Project Sponsor quarterly based on reimbursement requests. The State Management Team includes representatives from the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Department of the Environment, and Maryland Department of Agriculture.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit that authorizes properly trained and accredited individuals to provide care and treatment for orphaned, sick, or injured wildlife and release them back to the wild. The permit is renewed on a two-year cycle and requires proof of adequate training, suitable facilities, and continuing education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is a regulatory permit/license, not a financial or technical assistance program. No financial assistance, grants, loans, tax credits, subsidies, or other qualifying assistance is provided.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-260-8540; Toll-free in Maryland: 1-877-620-8DNR; TTY: Maryland Relay via 1-800-735-2258 or 711
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals in Maryland who are properly accredited and wish to provide wildlife rehabilitation services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable - this is a permitting program, not a financial assistance program
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Proof of adequate training in the capture, handling, and care of wildlife
Facilities (owned or leased) of sufficient size and design to properly maintain permitted wildlife in captivity
Designation of species and numbers of wildlife authorized to be possessed at any given time
Continuing education credits required to maintain the permit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New applicants must submit an Application for Apprentice Wildlife Rehabilitation Permit, Statement of Veterinary Support, and Apprenticeship Agreement. For progression to Master level, submit an Availability Questionnaire for Wildlife Rehabilitator Permit and Sponsor's Checklist. Applications can be submitted by email, phone, or mail to the Wildlife Permit Coordinator.

structured_extraction.program_description: Educational program hosting events for land trust staff, board members, and volunteers to learn about land conservation and Maryland Environmental Trust's programming using nationally recognized land trust standards and practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Offers periodic workshops, Land Trust Roundtables, and volunteer monitoring trainings based on the Standards and Practices developed by the Land Trust Alliance, the nationally recognized authority on land trust actions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Land trust staff, board members, and volunteers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and training in land conservation practices and programming
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; workshops and trainings available to Maryland land trusts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check the Events page for information on upcoming workshops, trainings, Land Trust Roundtables, and volunteer monitoring trainings.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources partners with local community organizations to introduce children to fishing through youth fishing rodeos held at small ponds and lakes. The program provides fishing opportunities in a safe, controlled environment, teaches basic angling skills, helps children develop a stewardship ethic for the environment, and encourages fishing as a positive outdoor family activity. Support includes help with event planning, provision of fish for stocking events, assistance with obtaining rodeo permits, and coordination of programming. The program has a 60+ year history in Maryland and supports up to 70 rodeos annually with approximately 7,000 children participating each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The department provides support and assistance to community and non-profit organizations that sponsor youth fishing rodeo events. Support includes help with event planning, provision of fish for stocking events (trout stocked at 50 per surface acre, minimum 100 per event, or hybrid sunfish for warmer water events), assistance with obtaining rodeo permits, technical advice and information, website listing of events, and coordination of programming. Fish are stocked during the week preceding the event. Limited number of fish supplied; alternative support options available when fish cannot be provided, including referrals to commercial fish sources. Organizations must submit a post-event evaluation report within 30 days of the event. Failure to submit the required post-event report results in no rodeo permit or fish allocation for the following year. Information from post-event reports is used in annual grant reports to the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration Program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 15 each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community and non-profit organizations, including those serving individuals with physical or mental disabilities and veterans organizations serving those with service-connected disabilities, interested in sponsoring youth fishing events for children aged 3 to 15 years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for organizing and hosting youth fishing rodeo events, including assistance with event planning, fish provision for stocking, and rodeo permits. Participant fees should be disclosed for their intended use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Events are held throughout the state of Maryland between March and November. Events may be held at lakes, ponds, or streams with a maximum of 10 acres if on private property. Stocked area must be open to public fishing for at least 14 days after event.
requirements_list: Organizations must complete the Youth Fishing Rodeo Program Application
Coordinators are required to obtain a rodeo permit prior to the event
Organizations must submit a post-event evaluation report within 30 days of the event
Failure to submit post-event report results in no rodeo permit or fish allocation for the following year
Events must comply with the updated Youth Fishing Rodeo Policy
Minimum 25 youth anglers anticipated
Event must be open to all interested youth aged 3-15 (or provide description if restricted)
No fees collected for fish provided by program
Participants must be under 16 years old
Pond must be open for public fishing for at least 14 days after event (minimum 8 hours/day, consistent hours)
Organization must have submitted prior post-event report to be eligible for current year application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in sponsoring a youth rodeo event should complete the Youth Fishing Rodeo Program Application and submit it by January 15 each year to the Youth Fishing Rodeo Program Coordinator via mail, fax (301-791-4672), or email to Michael Anderson. Requests are prioritized based on information supplied and application receipt date. Post-event evaluation reports must be submitted within 30 days of the event via mail, fax (301-791-4672), or online at dnr.maryland.gov. Additional information about the program is available in the program information letter. Organizations must comply with current terms and conditions outlined in the updated policy.

structured_extraction.program_description: A biennial pass that provides non-commercial youth organizations with free day-use entry into Maryland State Parks on weekdays (excluding weekends and holidays from Memorial Day through Labor Day) and allows youth groups to reserve and camp in designated youth group camping areas subject to site availability. The pass is valid for two years and must be reapplied for upon expiration. Youth groups must maintain a minimum ratio of one adult supervisor for every five youth members aged 6 to 18 years old. The pass is non-transferrable and cannot be used until physically received. Reservation transaction fees and special facility charges for shelters, boat concessions, and special events are not covered by the pass.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The biennial pass (valid for two years) provides free day-use entry to Maryland State Parks on weekdays excluding weekends and holidays from Memorial Day through Labor Day. Youth groups can also reserve and camp in designated youth group camping areas at participating parks subject to site availability, though reservation transaction fees still apply. The pass requires a valid reservation and is non-transferrable. A minimum ratio of one adult supervisor for every five youth is required. Special facility charges for shelters, boat concessions, and special events are not covered by the pass. The pass cannot be used until physically received.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Park Service, Youth Group Coordinator
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-commercial youth organizations such as scout troops, schools, churches, religious groups, and other affiliated youth organizations with members between 6 and 18 years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free day-use access to Maryland State Parks on weekdays and the ability to reserve and camp in designated youth group camping areas at participating state parks and forests.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Youth group camping areas are located in Eastern, Central, Southern, and Western regions of Maryland at participating locations including Assateague State Park, Pocomoke River State Park, Tuckahoe State Park, Wye Island NRMA, Janes Island State Park, Sassafras NRMA, Elk Neck State Park, Gunpowder Falls State Park, Patapsco Valley State Park, Calvert Cliffs State Park, Cedarville State Forest, Newtowne Neck State Park, Sandy Point State Park, Smallwood State Park, Fort Frederick State Park, Greenbrier State Park, Green Ridge State Forest, Potomac-Garrett State Forest, Rocky Gap State Park, Swallow Falls State Park, and Washington Monument. Day-use entry excludes weekends and holidays from Memorial Day through Labor Day.
requirements_list: Non-commercial youth organization
Youth members must be between 6 and 18 years old
Organization must be a valid youth group
Must submit proof of tax exempt status (current tax exempt card or exemption certificate)

Must submit documentation confirming the organization is a current, valid youth group (scout troop charter certificates, registration documentation, institutional letterhead documentation, or group details with children's ages)
Minimum ratio of one adult supervisor for every five youth
Valid reservation required in addition to pass
Pass is non-transferrable and must be presented upon arrival
Application must include all required information
Application must be submitted by mail with supporting documentation
Applicants must apply for a pass before current pass expires
Sponsor/charter organization officer signature required on application
For camping, a valid pass and reservation are both required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Youth Group Pass application form or request it from the Maryland Park Service. Complete the application with all required information and submit it by mail along with two forms of supporting documentation: proof of tax exempt status and documentation confirming the organization is a valid youth group. Mail to: Maryland Park Service, Tawes State Office Building, 580 Taylor Avenue, E-3, Annapolis MD 21401, Attention: Youth Group Coordinator. Applications are processed in the order received and cannot be expedited. The application will be returned if it does not include all required information. Once approved and the pass is received, make a reservation by calling the park reservation service at 1-888-432-2267, online at parkreservations.maryland.gov, or by calling the specific state park office directly. The pass cannot be used until physically received.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal and state partnership program administered jointly by the Maryland Department of Agriculture, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, and Maryland Department of the Environment that helps Maryland landowners and farmers remove environmentally sensitive agricultural land, cropland, streamside property, highly erodible land, or wetlands out of production for 10-15 years and install conservation practices to protect water quality, streams, and create wildlife habitat. The program is a cooperative conservation effort between the USDA Farm Service Agency, USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, and Maryland Department of Agriculture, targeting enrollment of 100,000 acres of eligible cropland or marginal pastureland in the Chesapeake Bay watershed. The program offers attractive land rental rates with per-acre rental bonuses (100% bonus for planting forest buffers, 80% bonus for planting herbaceous buffers, retiring highly erodible land, or restoring wetlands), a one-time signing bonus of up to $1,000 per acre for riparian forest buffers and a $100 per acre state incentive payment, maintenance payments, and cost-share assistance (typically 50-100% of total cost) for streamside buffers, wetlands, watering systems, livestock fencing, forest improvement practices, and other conservation improvements. Landowners with existing Federal Farm Service Agency CREP or Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) Contracts can make them permanent through state-funded conservation easements, with the opportunity to increase easement acreage by up to ten times their CREP contract acreage to maximize land preservation and easement value. Perpetual conservation easements remain effective in perpetuity as a legal agreement between the landowner and the State of Maryland to maintain conservation practices that protect water quality and natural resources. After the federal contract expires, the landowner agrees to keep the land in an approved conservation practice forever. The easement is filed with county land records and passes to all future owners, permanently protecting the property. CREP buffers meet all Maryland setback requirements and can help finance required stream protection practices for livestock operations. Participants receive steady, dependable land rental income while helping protect local waterways and restoring wetlands and shallow water habitats.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Department of Agriculture, and Maryland Department of the Environment
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-time signing bonus of up to $1,000 per acre for new enrollments of riparian forest buffers through 2031, plus a one-time incentive payment of $100 per acre from the State of Maryland. Federal sign-up incentive payment (SIP) and practice incentive payment (PIP) available. Attractive annual rental and incentive payments provided throughout the contract term, with per-acre rental bonuses: 100% rental rate bonus for planting forest buffers, 80% rental rate bonus for planting herbaceous buffers, retiring highly erodible land, or restoring wetlands. Cost-share assistance available to install streamside buffers, watering systems, livestock fencing, forest improvement practices, and other conservation practices, typically reimbursing between 50% and 100% of the total cost (75-100% for some practices, up to 87.5% of eligible costs for establishment of conservation practices). Mid-contract management cost-share available (up to $50-$125 per acre depending on contract length). Cost-share for post-planting weed control within 12 months. Maintenance payments provided throughout contract. Landowners have the option to sell a permanent easement on their land to the State of Maryland. The program provides state-funded conservation easements to make existing Federal Farm Service Agency CREP or CRP Contracts permanent. Landowners can add up to ten times the amount of acreage in their CREP contract to their easement to maximize land preservation and easement value. Perpetual conservation easements provide the State of Maryland with a permanent interest in the land to ensure it remains in approved conservation practice indefinitely. The landowner retains property ownership but agrees to maintain it according to the conservation management plan or forest stewardship plan specified in the easement, with easements remaining effective in perpetuity and passing to all future owners. Compensation is provided for contract acres, match acres, and whole-farm easements based on a valuation system. Participants receive steady, dependable land rental income. Contracts last 10 to 15 years with yearly rental payments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Environmental Quality Incentive Program (EQIP) and Woodland Incentive Program (WIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal and state cost-share assistance program that offers financial, technical, and educational assistance to farmers, agricultural producers, forest landowners, and individuals engaged in livestock production or forestry management to implement conservation practices on eligible agricultural land and forestland. The program provides cost-share payments to install or implement structural and management practices, including forestry management practices on non-industrial private forestland, to address water quality and other environmental concerns. Assistance includes tree planting, site preparation, timber stand improvement, thinning, pruning, prescribed burning, crop tree release, herbicide treatments, nutrient management, manure management, integrated pest management, irrigation water management, wildlife habitat enhancement, and other land management practices. The Environmental Quality Incentive Program (EQIP) is a federal voluntary program providing incentives in the form of cost-share payments and grants to implement up to 200 conservation practices depending on location. The Woodland Incentive Program (WIP) is a state cost-share program available to private landowners that provides financial assistance for forest management and protection. Cost-share assistance is typically between 50% and 75% of total cost, with payments up to 50 percent of eligible practice costs for most participants and up to 90 percent for limited resource producers and beginning farmers and ranchers. WIP practices are funded at up to 65%. Payments are generally limited to $10,000 per person annually and $50,000 total over the 5 to 10 year life of the contract. Sixty percent of funding is earmarked for livestock production practices, including grazing. Landowners receive reimbursement upon approval by the local forester after submitting invoices and proof of payment. Approximately $100,000 is distributed annually through WIP to 75-100 landowners for management practices on 1,500-2,000 acres.

Sixty percent of the funding is earmarked for livestock production practices, including grazing. Landowners complete practices, pay for goods and services, and submit invoices and proof of payment for processing and reimbursement upon forester approval. Up to 200 conservation practices may be available depending on location. Participants are also eligible for incentive payments to encourage land management practices for up to 3 years.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County East Side Revitalization Community-Wide Assessment Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive grant program providing free Phase I and/or Phase II Environmental Site Assessments, community-wide assessment activities, and cost-free participation in the Maryland Department of Environment Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) and Technical Review Service (TRS) for brownfield properties and revitalization efforts located in the Baltimore County East Side target area. The program funds environmental site assessments and technical services to identify and evaluate brownfield contamination in Baltimore County's East Side communities including Sparrows Point, Bowleys Quarters, Lower Back River Neck Peninsula, North Point/Edgemere, Essex, Middle River, Perry Hall/White Marsh, and Dundalk. The program supports redevelopment by providing state authorization of environmental site conclusions and remedies, with participating property owners receiving a $6,000 VCP application fee waiver and approximately $500–$1,500 in TRS fees covered by the grant. Phase I ESAs identify recognized environmental conditions through document reviews, database searches, site inspections, and recommendations. Phase II ESAs include environmental sampling of soil, groundwater, and surface water with laboratory analysis and recommendations.

Participating property owners receive a $6,000 VCP application fee waiver and approximately $500–$1,500 in TRS fees covered by the grant. Participants engage in meaningful community service for a minimum of nine months at a minimum of 30 hours per week (up to 40 hours per week for full-time positions), earning at least $15 per hour at partner organizations such as nonprofits, for-profit businesses, government agencies, schools, universities, and school systems. Participants gain professional skills, civic engagement training, and potential apprenticeship credentials. Host organizations receive cost-reimbursement grants covering approximately two-thirds of member wages (up to $20,000 per year per full-time member working 40 hours per week), while organizations contribute the remaining one-third through cost-sharing of approximately $7,450 per year per member. Upon program completion, participants receive a $6,000 completion award. The program provides health insurance, on-the-job training, monthly professional development training, mentoring, networking opportunities, workforce development coaching, wraparound services (childcare, transportation, financial literacy), and professional development support, with the opportunity to enroll in a federally recognized registered apprenticeship pathway and earn Department of Labor credentials. Members serve in service positions across various sectors including climate, conservation, education, historic trades, health, information technology, public safety, public service, and arts. The program empowers residents to serve their communities while building professional skills in a supportive environment and fosters civic engagement and community development. This workforce development initiative strengthens Maryland's workforce and expands the state's employment opportunities. The program accepts applications for Members, Partner organizations, Host-Employers, and nominations on a rolling basis, with major application deadlines in April and May.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn at least $15 per hour for full-time service work (minimum 30 hours per week, up to 40 hours per week for full-time positions) lasting at least nine months. Upon completion of the program, participants receive a $6,000 taxable completion award. Participants also receive health insurance (self-only coverage or as needed), monthly professional development training, approximately 10 paid work hours per week for professional development activities, a dedicated service success coach, workforce development mentorship, networking opportunities, wraparound services (childcare, transportation, financial literacy assistance), and professional development support, and have the opportunity to enroll in a federally recognized registered apprenticeship credential and earn Department of Labor Registered Apprenticeship Certificate or trade credentials if eligible. Members serve in service positions with partner organizations across Maryland in roles across various sectors including climate, conservation, education, historic trades, health, information technology, public safety, public service, and arts. Host organizations receive cost-reimbursement grants providing up to $20,000 per year per full-time member working 40 hours per week at a minimum wage of at least $15 per hour. Organizations pay upfront for member wages, taxes, and benefits, then receive quarterly reimbursement from DSCI after submitting documentation. Organizations must contribute approximately $7,450 per year per member (about $180 per week) as their cost-share requirement, unless a cost-share waiver is awarded. DSCI provides training, coaching, and professional development directly to members. Members can apply directly, organizations can apply as Partners or Host-Employers, or individuals can be nominated as Members.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 18 years and older who reside in Maryland, including recent high school graduates from the classes of 2024, 2023, 2022, and 2021, seeking paid service opportunities and professional development. Service Year Option pathway is for ages 18-24 with high school diploma or equivalent (G.E.D. or Certificate of Completion). Maryland Corps pathway is open to all adults 18 and older with no education requirement, including individuals looking to pivot in their career or reenter the workforce. Organizations across Maryland including nonprofits, for-profits, government agencies, private schools, universities, and school systems seeking to hire young adults and adults for full-time positions with built-in professional development and service components.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full-time service in a community position matched with a host site employer in the participant's field of interest across various sectors including climate, conservation, education, historic trades, health, information technology, public safety, public service, and arts. Participants gain work experience, professional skills, and career development through service activities in Maryland communities while earning income and making community impact. Members use their earnings and $6,000 completion award to pay down debt, invest in education, save for the future, or other personal needs. Host organizations use grant reimbursement to offset member wages, payroll taxes, benefits, and health insurance costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland; open to Maryland residents and Maryland-based organizations. Members can serve in communities across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions from Western Maryland to the Eastern Shore. Maryland residency required for participants.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Members, organizations, or individuals can apply through DSCI's Application and Matching Portal or through BuildWithin at buildwithin.io or app.buildwithin.io, or email applytoserve@maryland.gov to schedule a virtual or in-person program overview. Apply as a Member, apply as a Partner (Host Site), or nominate a Member. DSCI reviews applications continuously on a rolling basis with major deadlines of April 1 (Round 1) and May 1 and may contact applicants with follow-up questions. Upon conditional acceptance, applicants explore positions and apply to Host Site Partner organizations through the portal. Interview with Host Site Partner organizations and accept an official offer. After acceptance, organizations must attend a required webinar covering program requirements and milestones. Before service begins, all Host Site Partners and Members attend required program orientation. Complete minimum 9-month service term at Host Site (program begins August/September). Upon graduation, receive $6,000 completion award and Department of Labor Registered Apprenticeship Certificate or trade credentials if eligible. After award is confirmed, host sites must review grant agreement, set up their grant management account, access required systems, review award documents, and understand their responsibilities. Individuals interested in the program should contact the Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: An employer commuter benefit program where employees choose between a paid parking space or a cash benefit. Commuters who carpool, vanpool, bike, walk, or take transit to work can receive a cash payment from their employer in exchange for surrendering their paid parking space. Employers who offer this program can realize significant savings while providing cash benefits to employees and can claim a tax credit of up to $100 per person. The program works best for employers that lease parking and is typically implemented at the time of a new lease or lease renewal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers provide a cash payment to employees who surrender their parking space. Employers who offer Cash in Lieu of Parking can claim a tax credit of up to or equal to $100 per person. Employers offer employees a choice between a paid parking space or a cash allowance, and can claim the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit of 50% of the cost of providing commuter benefits, up to $100 per employee per month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers offering free or subsidized parking to employees; employees who commute by carpooling, vanpooling, biking, walking, or taking transit
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash benefit payments to employees who opt for alternative commuting modes; parking lease costs; eligible for Maryland Commuter Tax Credit

structured_extraction.program_description: A web-based portal providing a centralized location for solicitation of transportation projects that incorporate climate benefits and reduce carbon emissions from the transportation sector. The program supports Maryland's Climate Solutions Now Act of 2022 and provides federal Carbon Reduction Program funding for projects that reduce surface transportation emissions and support climate resilience. The program is open to eligible applicants to submit climate-beneficial projects for implementation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal Carbon Reduction Program (CRP) sub-recipient funding for climate-focused transportation projects. Projects must include a minimum 20% cash match (80/20 federal/local split). Eligible project types include: adaptive traffic control systems, alternative fuel vehicles and infrastructure, bicycle-pedestrian and shared micro-mobility infrastructure, carpooling/vanpooling, congestion reduction, electric vehicles and EV charging infrastructure, freight modal shift, transit construction/operation/maintenance, sustainable pavements, fleet electrification, zero-emission vehicle purchase/lease, TSMO/ITS, congestion mitigation, VMT reduction, mode-shift initiatives, bike/pedestrian facilities, street lighting, diesel retrofits, port electrification, truck parking technology, and CAV technologies. Capital projects only; operating expenses and highway widening/expansion are NOT eligible.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects only (operating expenses not eligible) that reduce surface transportation emissions and build climate resilience, including: fleet electrification and zero-emission vehicle purchase/lease, EV charging infrastructure acquisition and installation, adaptive traffic control systems, alternative fuel infrastructure, bicycle-pedestrian and shared micro-mobility infrastructure, carpooling/vanpooling programs, congestion mitigation systems, transit construction/operation/maintenance, sustainable pavements, street lighting, diesel retrofits, port facility improvements and electrification, truck parking technology, connected and automated vehicle technologies, transportation demand management, rail and freight rail projects, and other transportation systems improvements that support decarbonization and emissions reduction.
