structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants register on the OneStop Portal at https://onestop.md.gov/, verify their email address, and access the Climate Focused Funding application portal. The application is structured in multiple sections: Project Components, Emissions Reduction Components, Resilience Components (optional), and Additional Details and Review. Application includes multi-section form with project point of contact, cost estimates, project schedule, emissions calculations, and narrative on surface transportation emissions reduction. Applicants submit with required attachments. MDOT provides weekly virtual office hours on Wednesdays from 3:00 pm to 4:00 pm during the solicitation window to answer questions and provide technical assistance. Application resources, guidance documents, and FAQs are available to support project identification and submission. Drafts auto-save for later completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free mobile app that helps commuters find and plan carpool, vanpool, transit, biking, and multimodal travel options. Users log their commute trips during peak hours on weekdays and earn points redeemable for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits as rewards for using alternative commuting methods. Points range from 10 to 100 depending on commute mode, with users able to earn up to $10 after completing 20 trips or save points for higher-tier rewards up to $90 in value, with a maximum of $600 per calendar year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Commuters earn points for logging eligible commute trips during peak commuting hours (6:30am–9:30am or 4:00pm–7:00pm on weekdays). Points range from 10 to 100 depending on commute mode, with alternative transportation modes (ridesharing, transit, biking, and walking) earning higher values than driving alone. Points are redeemable for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. Users can earn up to $10 after completing 20 trips or save points for higher-tier rewards up to $90 in value. Maximum earnings are $600 per calendar year.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Points earned can be redeemable for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits to support sustainable commuting options including carpool, vanpool, transit, biking, and walking.

Points are automatically awarded based on commute mode and trip details. Redeem accumulated points for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits through the app.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that targets intersections or corridors with a history of traffic fatalities or crashes to implement short-term, cost-effective solutions in collaboration with local jurisdictions. The program uses innovative, easy-to-implement measures on an accelerated timeline to improve traffic safety and test new products and solutions. Part of the Maryland Complete Streets Leadership Academy, it provides technical assistance and grant funding to deploy temporary demonstration projects that test new strategies to improve safety and access for pedestrians, bicyclists, and other users.

The program includes funding for project design, installation materials, data collection, community engagement, and offers an 8-week design-to-installation timeline. Technical assistance covers project design, performance measures, engagement planning, data collection, and storytelling.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Material procurement for quick-build demonstration projects including flex posts, speed cushions, planters, thermoplastic paint, markings, crosswalks, and signage. structured_extraction.program_description: A public-private partnership seeking a private operator for a 40-year lease to operate, maintain, and improve approximately 92 miles of freight rail corridors on Maryland's Eastern Shore and in Delaware. The partnership aims to modernize rail infrastructure, increase efficiency, attract new freight customers, reduce state subsidies, and generate revenue for improvements. The P3 covers four rail corridors: Chestertown Line (20 miles), Centreville Line (35 miles), Cambridge Line (30 miles), and Preston Track (6.5 miles), with approximately 56 miles currently in active use serving 15+ active shippers. The operator must provide capital improvements and asset maintenance to state of good repair (SOGR) standards. Federal Rail Administration (FRA) and Surface Transportation Board (STB) provide regulatory oversight.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 40-year concession lease agreement with a private partner (P3 Operator) to finance, improve, operate, maintain, and manage freight rail corridors. The private partner assumes operational risk and responsibility for capital improvements, maintenance, and business development while having the opportunity to retain revenues from freight services and property use agreements. The P3 Operator is responsible for all track inspection, maintenance, repair, and rehabilitation to bring corridors to state of good repair. MDOT retains ownership of real estate, track, structures, and bridges. The arrangement is a revenue-risk concession model where the operator assumes freight customer revenue collection risk. The operator must provide their own locomotives, cars, vehicles, and equipment. Minimum $5 million equity capital capacity and successfully financed capital projects of at least $30 million are required. Operator must comply with 49 CFR Parts 229 and 1033 (safety, inspection, testing standards).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Statement of Qualifications Due: August 11, 2025 at 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private companies, consortiums, joint ventures, partnerships, and limited liability companies with demonstrated operational and financial capabilities in freight railroad operations, infrastructure development, and financing. Requires entities capable of obtaining Surface Transportation Board (STB) regulatory approval, with Lead Rail Team Member currently approved by STB to perform operations associated with a railroad serving freight rail customers, and demonstrated experience in common carrier freight rail operations. Must be currently operating a railroad.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements and infrastructure rehabilitation of rail corridors to state of good repair standards, track maintenance (ties, rails, drainage), bridge and culvert maintenance, grade crossing maintenance, procurement of locomotives, cars, vehicles, and equipment, operational expenses, rolling stock investments, business development and marketing, and pursuit of federal grants for capital improvements.

The concession covers approximately 92 miles of rail lines (56 miles active). Regulated by Federal Rail Administration (FRA) and Surface Transportation Board (STB) under 49 U.S. Code, Title 49.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Two-step competitive procurement process: (1) Request for Information (RFI) stage with one-on-one meeting requests due April 9, 2025 and RFI responses due April 14, 2025; (2) Request for Qualifications (RFQ) stage with Statement of Qualifications due August 11, 2025 at 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time; (3) Shortlisted proposers advance to Request for Proposal (RFP) stage with Final Proposals due July 16, 2025. RFQ issued June 13, 2025. Request for Clarifications accepted during RFQ period. Proposers submit SOQ in two volumes: Volume 1 covering team experience and qualifications, Volume 2 covering financial capacity and funding commitment. Volume 2 includes Proposer Team Financial Experience and Resources documentation. Required forms include Forms A, B, C, E, F, G, H (now Form I), and J certifications. Shortlisted proposers gain access to data room with financial information; confidentiality provisions apply. Formal protest procedures are available. Prospective partners must register in eMMA system and submit responses to RFQ documents and any addenda. Meeting requests and RFI responses should be directed to freightrailp3@mdot.maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded, competitive, reimbursable grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) that supports the development of connected bike networks and biking infrastructure. Established in 2012, the program provides grant support for a wide range of bicycle network development activities, including design, minor retrofits, and construction of bikeways infrastructure. Projects must maximize bicycle access and enhance last-mile connections to work, school, shopping, and transit, with priority for projects that improve safety and access for disadvantaged communities. The program funds projects that exemplify MDOT's Complete Streets policy vision and create safe, comprehensive, integrated and connected transportation networks. The program supports local economies and enhances quality of life through biking and walking.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grant program with three project types: Design projects (up to $400,000 maximum) for engineering design plans and feasibility assessments up to 65 percent design; Minor Retrofit projects (up to $200,000 maximum) for installation of low-cost treatments such as bicycle route signing, pavement markings, bicycle parking, drainage grates, automated bicycle counters, and similar improvements; Construction projects (up to $500,000 maximum) for construction or installation of bikeways infrastructure that has reached at least 65 percent design. Applicants must provide a minimum 20 percent match of total project cost as cash or in-kind contribution. Educational and promotional materials are eligible up to 10% of award or $10,000, whichever is less. Up to 20% of construction awards may be used for final design completion (65% to final design). Technical assistance is provided by the Department to help local jurisdictions develop feasible projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Mid-May (April-May application window)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local governments, state agencies, Metropolitan Planning Organizations, transit entities, non-profit organizations, and federal public lands agencies interested in developing bicycle network infrastructure and communities developing connected bike networks. Emphasis on communities with disadvantaged populations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Engineering design plans and feasibility assessments for proposed bikeways; installation of low-cost bicycle route enhancements including signs, pavement markings, bicycle parking, drainage grate replacement, and automated bicycle counters; construction and installation of bikeways infrastructure including transportation trails, shared-use paths, bicycle and pedestrian bridges, cycle tracks, and protected bike lanes; state of good repair maintenance projects; Complete Streets intersection treatments; bike lane infrastructure and cycling facilities; capital equipment (racks, benches, repair stations); educational and promotional materials directly related to infrastructure (up to 10% or $10,000 of award). Cannot be used for operations, maintenance, recreational wayfinding, or general bicycle planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Projects must meet at least two of six eligibility criteria: location within three miles of rail transit or major bus hub; identified as county transportation priority; located in Sustainable Community or Bicycle and Pedestrian Priority Area; enhances access to Main Streets or major institutions; enhances access for disadvantaged communities; or provides significant safety intervention. Projects may also be located within missing links, or provide access to points of interest.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible applicants submit a letter of intent to MDOT describing the project, including title, description, physical limits, estimated cost, anticipated funding request, and contact information. Full applications open in April and close mid-May for the FY27 funding cycle. MDOT staff may provide guidance following letter of intent submission to ensure key application elements are included. Applications are submitted in phases: feasibility/preliminary design, semi-final (65%) design, and construction. Apply through the MDOT Grants Roadshow process. Upon award, grantees must submit a Work Plan within 30 days of award notification and submit quarterly update reports. Final Report required upon project completion before final reimbursement can be processed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local and Regional Project Assistance Program (BUILD)
structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive federal grant program providing funding for planning and capital projects that deliver significant local or regional improvements to surface transportation infrastructure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive federal grant funding for planning and capital projects. Planning grants support planning, preparation, and design work for eligible capital projects with no minimum award size. Capital grants range from $1 million (rural areas) to $5 million (urban areas), with a maximum of $25 million. Federal cost share up to 80% standard; up to 100% for rural areas, Areas of Persistent Poverty, or Historically Disadvantaged Communities. Eligible projects include highway/bridge improvements, public transportation, passenger and freight rail, port infrastructure, airport surface transportation components, Tribal land projects, intermodal projects, and culvert replacement/stormwater improvements for aquatic habitat enhancement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded, competitive, reimbursable grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Transportation that provides state grant assistance to help preserve railroad corridors, support economic development, and foster sustainability and innovative technologies in Maryland's freight rail network. The program supports freight rail infrastructure and development projects through targeted investments in the freight network, enhancing rail transportation efficiency and capacity, and helping create a safe, secure, and resilient multimodal freight network. Funding supports design phase projects (design plans and feasibility assessments completed within 2 years) and construction phase projects (rail corridor improvements including sidings/sidetracks, grade crossing improvements, bridges/structures, and drainage improvements completed within 3 years). Grants are reimbursable, requiring recipients to pay for costs upfront and receive reimbursement from the state with a minimum 20% local funding cash match required.

Construction phase funding supports construction or installation of rail corridor improvements including sidings/sidetracks, grade crossing improvements, bridges/structures, and drainage improvements (must be completed within 3 years). Grants are reimbursable, meaning recipients pay for costs first and then receive reimbursement from the state. Minimum 20% local funding cash match required (maximum 80% grant funding).

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Commuter Tax Credit and Commuter Choice Employer Partner Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive state program that provides employers and commuters with financial incentives and technical assistance for implementing commuter benefits and telework subsidy programs. The program includes multiple complementary components: (1) a tax credit that allows Maryland-based employers, including nonprofits, for-profits, government entities, and higher education institutions, to claim a 50% tax credit against the cost of providing commute alternative programs and telework-related expense subsidies to employees, up to $100 per employee per month, with the credit claimable against state personal income tax, corporate income tax, or insurance premium tax; (2) a technical assistance and recognition program (Commuter Choice Maryland Employer Partner Program) providing support to employers implementing commuter benefits and alternative transportation programs, including assistance with planning tools, employee surveys, site assessments, and public recognition for leadership; and (3) the CommuterCash mobile app that allows individual commuters to log commute trips using alternatives to driving alone to earn points redeemable for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. Eligible commuter benefits include transit subsidies, carpool and vanpool subsidies, bike-related expenses, active commuting equipment, telework and flexwork support, guaranteed ride home services, parking cash out programs, parking or toll subsidies, and multi-modal last mile connection options. Telework-related expenses include internet access, computer equipment, telephone service, co-working memberships, and job-related software. Federal law allows employers to offer employees up to $265 per month as a pre-tax deduction or tax-free subsidy for use on transit, vanpools, and eligible parking, with money spent on transit benefits exempt from payroll taxes up to $115 per month. Benefits must be employer-funded and used for commuting to Maryland worksites during typical weekday commuting hours or for qualifying telework expenses. The program encourages employees to reduce automobile use for commuting while helping employers attract and retain talent and reducing traffic congestion and air pollution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers multiple forms of assistance to Maryland employers and commuters. Employers can claim a 50% tax credit equal to 50 percent of the cost of providing commute alternative programs and telework-related expense subsidies to employees, up to $100 per employee per month. The credit can be claimed against state personal income tax, corporate income tax, or insurance premium tax. Federal payroll tax-free commuter benefits up to $270 per month are available through employer-supported option, employee pre-tax option, or combination approach. Eligible commuter benefits include transit subsidies (up to $265 per month federally), carpool and vanpool subsidies, bike-related expenses, active commuting equipment, parking or toll subsidies, guaranteed ride home services, parking cash out programs, and multi-modal last mile connection options. Eligible telework expenses include internet access, computer equipment, telephone service, co-working memberships, and job-related software. Employers must register for the credit, track eligible expenses, and file required Maryland tax forms each year to claim it. The program also provides one-stop shop technical support on implementing and evaluating commuter benefits programs, assistance with employee surveys and site assessments, employer transportation plan development with goals, survey analysis and implementation planning, program administration guidance, promotional materials and enrollment support, program evaluation assistance, and public recognition for leadership in offering commute options. Individual commuters can download the CommuterCash mobile app to log commute trips using alternatives to driving alone and earn points redeemable for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits.

Individual commuters can use earned points for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. Technical assistance for developing and evaluating commuter benefits programs.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers can register for the tax credit by reviewing the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit guidelines to determine qualifying programs, tracking eligible commuter benefit and telework subsidy expenses throughout the year, and filing the required Maryland tax forms to claim the credit. Employers can also check the Commuter Choice Maryland website or contact the program office at 410-865-1100 or commuterchoice@mdot.maryland.gov to learn about participation and available benefits. Applications can also be submitted through the one-stop portal for Maryland licenses and permits. To participate in the Employer Partner Program, employers can register through the SurveyMonkey registration link provided to become an Employer Partner and receive technical assistance. Alternatively, employers can email the Commuter Choice Maryland Team or complete the online application form. Individual commuters can download the CommuterCash mobile app to log commute trips and earn rewards.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ride Together Rewards: CharmPass Incentive for New Transit Riders
structured_extraction.program_description: A promotional program offering free transit passes to new riders of the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) system in the Greater Baltimore area. New transit users can download the CharmPass mobile app during select promotional periods (May 1-8, June 1-8, and July 1-8, 2026) and receive free transit passes for use on MTA services including buses, metro, light rail, commuter bus, and MARC. Passes are loaded directly onto the participant's CharmPass account, expire after 90 days, and are not redeemable for cash or transferable to other users.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free transit passes loaded directly onto the participant's CharmPass account. Passes are available during select promotional periods (May 1-8, June 1-8, and July 1-8, 2026). Passes expire after 90 days and are not redeemable for cash or transferable to other users.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Select promotional periods: May 1-8, 2026; June 1-8, 2026; July 1-8, 2026. Outside these periods, signup is available for alerts about future promotional periods.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New transit users in the Greater Baltimore region who have not previously used the MTA transit system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free transit passes can be used for travel to, from, or within the Greater Baltimore region using MTA transit services including local buses, metro, light rail, commuter bus, and MARC trains.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Greater Baltimore region accessible to MTA stations and services.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time (new) user of the MTA transit system
Must download the CharmPass mobile application
Must set up an account with email, name, and phone number
Must select desired type of transit pass
Account must be verified within 48 hours
Participants must share feedback by taking part in periodic brief surveys about their transit experience
Free transit passes expire after 90 days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Determine eligibility as a new transit rider. 2. Download the CharmPass mobile application and set up an account with email, name, and phone number. 3. Select the desired type of transit pass. 4. Once the account is verified (within 48 hours), the free transit passes are loaded directly onto the CharmPass account. 5. Travel using MTA transit services. 6. Participate in periodic brief surveys about transit experience.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ride Together Rewards: FareShare Incentive for Employers
structured_extraction.program_description: An employer incentive program that provides businesses in the Greater Baltimore area with funds to purchase transit passes for their employees. Employers can receive up to $3,000 ($1,000 per month over three continuous months) to offset the cost of transit fares, delivered as a credit on the employer's CharmPass account. Credits are used to load selected fare products directly into employees' digital CharmPass app accounts for use on MTA services including local buses, metro, light rail, commuter bus, and MARC trains. Participating employers are also registered as MDOT Commuter Choice Maryland Employer Partner Program participants and receive free resources and tools to offer additional commuter benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers receive up to $3,000 ($1,000 per month over three continuous months) as a credit on their CharmPass account to purchase transit fares for employees. The incentive is delivered as a credit that can be used to load selected fare products directly into employees' digital CharmPass app accounts. Employers must enroll by the 15th of the month prior to their starting month, and submit their next month's purchase by the 25th of the month.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing program with monthly enrollment deadlines. Employers should enroll by the 15th of the month prior to their desired starting month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers in the Greater Baltimore area with locations or employment centers accessible to MTA stations through local transit services, commuter bus, and MARC.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are provided as a credit to purchase transit passes and fare products for employees to use on MTA services including local buses, metro, light rail, commuter bus, and MARC trains.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Greater Baltimore area with locations or employment centers accessible to MTA stations through local transit services, commuter bus, and MARC.
requirements_list: Employer must have locations or employment centers in the Greater Baltimore area accessible to MTA stations through local transit services, commuter bus, and MARC
Employer must express interest in joining the FareShare Program
Employer must fill out a quick questionnaire to set up an agreement
Employer must enroll by the 15th of the month prior to starting month
Employer must submit next month's purchase by the 25th of the month
Employees must set up a CharmPass account to access employer-provided passes
Participate in periodic brief surveys about transit experience
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Confirm eligibility based on location in the Greater Baltimore area. 2. Express interest in joining the FareShare Program and email mdot.tso@maryland.gov. 3. MTA will set up a meeting to discuss options. 4. Fill out a quick questionnaire to set up an agreement with MTA. 5. MTA verifies the employer's account and applies the incentive as a credit. 6. Selected fare products are loaded directly to participants' digital CharmPass app accounts. 7. Employees must access the CharmPass app and set up an account to use their employer-provided pass. 8. Participate in periodic brief surveys about transit experience.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federally-funded, reimbursement program administered by the Maryland State Highway Administration that enables and encourages children in K-12 to walk, roll, and bike to school by making bicycling, walking, and rolling to school safer and more appealing through eligible Transportation Alternatives (TA) projects. The program supports safe routes to school projects that improve pedestrian and bicycle access to schools, including infrastructure improvements, sidewalks, bike paths, feasibility studies, design projects, and safety programs around schools.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive, federally-funded reimbursement grant program providing funding for feasibility studies, design projects, construction projects, and safety awareness and program coordination projects to improve pedestrian and bicycle access to schools, including infrastructure, sidewalks, and bike paths around schools.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual basis
structured_extraction.contact_name: Cheryl Ladota, Division Chief, Grants and Programs Management (GPMD) Division

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, development, and implementation of projects and activities to improve safety and reduce traffic related to active transportation to school, including feasibility studies, design projects, construction projects, and safety awareness programs. Safe pedestrian and bicycle pathways to schools, sidewalks, bike paths, and school-related safety improvements around schools.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Projects are competitively selected through annual solicitation. Apply through the Maryland State Highway Administration with school route safety project proposals. Consult program guidelines for specific requirements. Visit www.roads.maryland.gov/mdotsha for latest updates.

structured_extraction.program_name: Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A)
structured_extraction.program_description: U.S. Department of Transportation program providing grants to local, regional, and Tribal communities for implementation, planning, and demonstration activities to prevent deaths and serious injuries on roadways using a systematic approach. The program funds development and enhancement of safety action plans, supplemental planning and demonstration initiatives, and implementation of projects and strategies identified through those plans using data-driven, systemwide approaches grounded in the Safe System Approach. Implementation grants may construct projects or fund operational strategies identified in an approved Safety Action Plan and complete project feasibility, design, and development. Planning grants may develop Safety Action Plans, supplemental planning activities, road safety audits, or demonstration activities including feasibility studies using quick-build strategies, MUTCD engineering studies, pilot programs for behavior or operational activities, and pilot projects utilizing innovative technologies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Planning grants fund Safety Action Plan development, plan updates, topical sub-plans, road safety audits, and demonstration activities. Implementation grants construct projects or fund operational strategies from approved Safety Action Plans; fund feasibility, design, and development. Eligible demonstration activities include quick-build strategies (paint, plastic posts, barriers), MUTCD engineering studies, pilot programs for behavior and operational activities, and innovative technology pilots. Funds support construction projects, operational strategies, project feasibility and design, high-visibility crosswalk and marking evaluations, and testing innovative technologies. Cost share requirement: 80% federal/20% local.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sean Winkler, Senior Policy Advisor; Christy Bernal, Discretionary Grant Manager – Rotation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local, regional, and Tribal communities; Metropolitan planning organizations; Political subdivisions of a state (local jurisdictions); Multijurisdictional combinations of eligible applicants. State, local, and regional transportation agencies, nonprofits, and community organizations of varying sizes and capacities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction of safety projects; Funding operational strategies; Project feasibility, design, and development; Safety Action Plan development; Quick-build infrastructure improvements (paint, plastic posts, barriers); High-visibility crosswalk and marking evaluations; Pilot programs for behavior and operational activities; Innovative technology pilots.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: National program with approximately $1 billion guaranteed annual funding through IIJA. Maryland administration coordination. Serves local, regional, and Tribal communities. States are not directly eligible, but jurisdictions proposing projects on state facilities are encouraged and required to receive state concurrence.

Focus on improving safety outcomes
Advance equitable investments

Pilot programs must include at least one element of the Safe System Approach
Metropolitan planning organizations, political subdivisions of a state, Tribal governments, or multijurisdictional combinations of eligible applicants may apply
80/20% federal/local cost share required
State concurrence required for projects on state facilities

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's program provides state recognition of intentional efforts by a local jurisdiction to advance Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) at eligible sites. TOD Designation is valid for 10 years and can be extended for an additional 10 years. The designation recognizes comprehensive planning that addresses land use, housing, transportation connectivity, parking strategy, green infrastructure, economic development, and community cohesion to maximize use of transit, walking, and bicycling. TOD Designation unlocks opportunities for State support, including MDOT's TOD Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund, additional points in competitive application rounds for the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Low Income Housing Tax Credit program, priority advocacy with MDOT and associate modes in supporting development, and additional points from DGS and MDOT when evaluating requests for proposals to lease or purchase office or laboratory space.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State recognition and designation status that unlocks eligibility for MDOT's TOD Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund, additional points in competitive application rounds for the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Low Income Housing Tax Credit program, priority advocacy with MDOT and associate modes in supporting development, and additional points from DGS and MDOT when evaluating requests for proposals to lease or purchase office or laboratory space. Designation itself does not provide direct funding but unlocks access to funding programs and competitive advantages for TOD projects involving mixed-use development with commercial, residential, and parking facilities near transit stations. Use of funds for designation-unlocked programs may include land use planning and development proposals, housing creation (units and affordability), economic development (anchor employers, business attraction/expansion), green infrastructure development, transit connectivity and pedestrian/bicycle infrastructure, parking strategy implementation, streetscape improvements, utilities, parks and open space, and mixed-use development.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/Ongoing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and multicounty agencies with land use and planning authority seeking State TOD Designation for a site or transit corridor. Communities with existing or planned transit stations and corridors including subway, light rail, bus rapid transit, or bus transit systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Designation itself does not provide direct funding but unlocks access to funding programs and competitive advantages for TOD projects. Use of funds for designation-unlocked programs may include land use planning and development proposals, housing creation (units and affordability), economic development (anchor employers, business attraction/expansion), green infrastructure development, transit connectivity and pedestrian/bicycle infrastructure, parking strategy implementation, streetscape improvements, utilities, parks and open space, and mixed-use development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property that is adjacent to the passenger boarding and alighting location of a planned or existing transit station, property any part of which is located within one-half mile of the passenger boarding and alighting location of a planned or existing transit station, property adjacent to a planned or existing transit corridor, or a geographically bound set of two or more contiguous transit stations. Maryland statewide program applicable to areas adjacent to planned or existing transit corridors (subway, light rail, bus rapid transit, or bus transit stations). No specific geographic restrictions beyond transit accessibility.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government or multicounty agency with land use and planning responsibility for the relevant area
Develop a deliberate plan or strategy for TOD
Demonstrate plan addressing eight categories: Land Use, Bike/Pedestrian/Complete Streets, Housing, Action Plan, Parking, Transportation Network, Cohesion, Green Infrastructure, Economic Development
Local legislative body must adopt a resolution in support of State TOD Designation
Plan must maximize use of transit, walking, and bicycling by residents and employees
Comprehensive planning and development vision for TOD throughout corridor
Planning for both station areas and connecting parcels
Transit corridor applicants must request pre-application meeting before applying
Land use plan with mixed uses and target densities
Pedestrian, bicycle, and personal mobility connectivity plans
Rationalized parking strategy
Multi-modal transit connectivity strategy
Housing creation goals with affordability component
Consistency with local and regional comprehensive plans
Green infrastructure plans or jurisdiction-wide policies
10-year action plan with timeline, community engagement, zoning, and funding sources
Economic development support documentation
Strong real estate market conditions preferred
Coordination among multiple stakeholders and parties
Extensive stakeholder engagement and outreach
Must submit complete application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local jurisdiction develops a deliberate plan or strategies and has the local legislative body adopt a resolution. Applicant submits application to MDOT via the TOD Designation Application Form (multi-section accordion form with 5+ sections). Section 4 focuses on TOD Designation Plan Questions requiring text descriptions and supporting document uploads. MDOT circulates the plan to modes and Smart Growth Subcabinet (SGSC) members, coordinates any issues with the local jurisdiction, and develops a recommendation to SGSC for approval or approval with conditions. SGSC deliberates on the proposed plan or strategies, considers MDOT recommendation, and issues a resolution approving or denying Designation. Navigation between sections via Previous/Next buttons. Transit corridor applicants should request a pre-application meeting with MDOT before submitting formal application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A $5 million annual statewide competitive program to financially assist local jurisdictions and their development partners in the advancement of transit-oriented development. Provides financial assistance to promote equitable and inclusive development of transit-oriented developments throughout Maryland. Eligible project types include design plans, public infrastructure improvements, and gap funding for development within eligible TOD areas that advance TOD goals. Supports development and improvements in areas near transit hubs that promote walkable, mixed-use communities with reduced vehicle dependency and enhance transportation options and economic development near transit facilities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and revolving loans to local jurisdictions and development partners. The fund has $5 million allocated in its first year and must maintain that balance as a minimum going forward. Local jurisdictions applying for a grant must commit a 10% match. Loan candidates must demonstrate the ability to repay. Eligible project types for local jurisdictions include design plans and public infrastructure improvements. Development partners, with local jurisdiction as co-applicant, can receive gap funding for development within an eligible TOD. Grant funding supports transit-oriented development projects that promote economic development and transportation options near transit facilities. FY25 funding is allocated from the Transportation Trust Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Additional rounds of funding anticipated later this year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, development partners, developers, transit agencies, and organizations seeking to develop transit-oriented projects at State-designated TOD sites. Priority considerations for projects enhancing access to transit for low-income and minority residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design plans, public infrastructure improvements, and gap funding for development within eligible TOD areas that advance equitable and inclusive development and TOD goals. Transit-oriented development projects including mixed-use development, infrastructure, and community improvements near transit facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program. Projects must be located within State-designated TOD areas and directly benefit a State-designated TOD site. Refer to the current MD Designated TOD Map for eligibility. Ground rent/land sale proceeds must benefit transit-oriented developments in the same county where property is located.

Local jurisdictions applying for a grant must commit a 10% match

Projects must be within a State-designated TOD area
Proposed development must meet equity goals established by the Department

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that supports local efforts to improve transit reliability, improve access and connections to activity centers, and improve transit mobility options. The program funds cost-effective public transportation projects that reduce delays and improve connectivity between regional and economic population centers. Projects may incorporate bus, rail, or other transit modes, including bus rapid transit, and support transportation goals outlined in the Maryland Transportation Plan.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Transportation Maryland Transit Administration (MDOT MTA)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant program for public transportation projects in planning, design, engineering, or construction phases. Eligible activities include corridor studies, feasibility studies, bus rapid transit corridors, dedicated bus lanes, transit signal prioritization, bus operations improvements, innovative fare payment upgrades, connected and autonomous vehicle pilot programs, real-time transit signage and information systems, mobile ticketing and fare payment systems, transit security infrastructure, bus stop improvements, microtransit pilots, and other transit innovations. Requires minimum 20% local match contribution. Projects must be completed within 36 months of grant award. Construction phase projects over $50,000 may require 30% design plans. An engineer's cost estimate is highly recommended for construction projects. Funds cannot support full-time staff salaries/benefits, land purchases, general roadway/sidewalk construction, employee training, paid media/marketing, or general operating expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applicants must submit all materials between grant announcement and June (see website for specific application deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local governments, locally operated transit providers, counties, municipalities, and organizations that currently receive MDOT MTA grant funds
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, engineering, or construction of public transportation projects including corridor studies, feasibility studies, bus rapid transit corridors, dedicated bus lanes, transit signal prioritization, bus operations improvements, innovative fare payment upgrades, connected and autonomous vehicle pilot programs, vehicle purchases, bus upgrades, first-mile/last-mile connections, safety improvements, mobility hubs, transit stations, real-time transit signage and information systems, mobile ticketing and fare payment systems, transit security infrastructure, bus stop improvements and accessibility enhancements, and other transit innovations. Cannot fund maintenance or operations.

Applications are graded based on ability to meet program goals and demonstrate project innovation for the local area.

structured_extraction.program_name: MDOT Urban Tree Reforestation Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program in partnership between the Maryland Department of Transportation and Maryland Department of Natural Resources supporting tree planting and urban forestry projects that enhance urban environments, improve air quality, and provide community benefits. The program is part of Maryland's Five Million Trees initiative and supports MDOT's efforts to become the greenest department of transportation in the country. The program has particular focus on tree replanting in areas where canopy was lost due to transportation infrastructure projects, with funding supporting communities impacted by major transportation projects such as Purple Line construction, urban heat islands, and environmental justice concerns throughout Maryland's urban areas. Works in partnership with the Maryland Urban and Community Forest Committee (MUCFC). Awards up to $5,000 for planting projects with additional funds available for pocket forest projects, with up to 5% of grants available for volunteer outreach, signs, or project promotion.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Transportation and Maryland Department of Natural Resources
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support tree planting and urban forestry projects in urban areas across Maryland, awarding up to $5,000 for planting projects with additional funds available for pocket forest projects. Up to 5% of the grant can be used for volunteer outreach, signs, or project promotion. Emphasis placed on tree replanting in areas where canopy was lost due to transportation infrastructure projects, including communities impacted by major projects such as Purple Line construction, urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns. Replanting may occur on both public and private property subject to project approval. Funding supports projects that enhance urban environments, improve air quality, and provide community benefits. Funds can also be used for project maintenance costs including watering, weeding, and mulching. Maintenance funding covers up to 1 year for tree planting projects and up to 3 years for pocket forest projects. Eligible uses include tree and plant material, planting supplies (mulch, soil amendments, compost), tree pits and similar planting systems, and signage.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 15 and July 15 (applications reviewed twice yearly for spring and fall planting seasons); Spring planting deadline January 15 at 11:59pm, Fall planting deadline July 15 at 11:59pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities, organizations, municipalities, agencies, property owners, local governments, non-profits, county governments, schools, community groups, community/neighborhood associations, community business associations, businesses, places of worship, homeowners associations, business service/youth/civic groups, and higher education institutions in areas impacted by transportation infrastructure projects seeking to restore urban tree canopy and implement urban forestry projects. Focus on urban areas with at least 2,000 housing units or population of 5,000+.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund - Onsite Disposal Systems Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program funded by fees collected from users of onsite sewage disposal systems that provides grants and subsidies for upgrading septic systems to best available technology for nitrogen removal and for implementing cover crops to reduce nitrogen loading to the Chesapeake Bay. The program funds the replacement of conventional septic tanks with nitrogen-reducing units or connections to public sewer where available. Effective July 1, 2012, a $60 annual fee is collected from each user served by an onsite system, generating approximately $27 million per year, with 60% used for septic system upgrades and 40% for cover crops. Upgraded systems reduce nitrogen loads by approximately 50% compared to conventional systems and lower coliform and enterococci counts. The program has already upgraded over 12,000 septic systems across Maryland. For low-income households, funding can be used to replace failing septic systems. Regional implementations available in multiple counties including Worcester, Talbot, Charles, and Prince George's counties, with grants covering the cost and installation of BAT units plus maintenance. The program aims to reduce harmful nutrients like nitrogen discharged into the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Program also supports community wastewater treatment systems and sewer connections to municipal treatment plants with enhanced nutrient removal standards.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Effective July 1, 2012, a $60 annual fee is collected from each user served by an onsite system. The total estimated program income is $27 million per year. Sixty percent of these funds are used for septic system upgrades and the remaining 40 percent are used for cover crops. Funds can be provided for upgrades of existing systems to best available technology for nitrogen removal or for the marginal cost of using best available technology instead of conventional technology. Grant funding from the Bay Restoration Fund covers the cost of installing nitrogen removal units on on-site septic systems or funding connections to public sewer where available. For new construction, grants cover the cost differential between conventional and BAT systems. For low-income households, grants can be used to replace failing septic systems, cover drainfield costs, and fund non-BAT component repairs. Community wastewater treatment systems may replace multiple on-site systems. Sewer connections to municipal wastewater treatment plants with enhanced nutrient removal are eligible, with funding up to $25,000 per connection for infrastructure costs. Grants include the cost and installation of BAT units plus 2 years of operations and maintenance. Properties with failing or non-conforming systems in the Critical Area (within 1,000 feet of tidal waters) receive priority. Income-based grant levels: households with income under $300,000 receive up to 100% funding; income over $300,000 receives 50% funding. The grant cannot be used for permit or recordation fees.

Grant money may be used for the cost and installation of Best Available Technology units plus 2 years of operations and maintenance, and for costs to abandon an existing septic system and connect to public sewerage with enhanced nutrient removal. For qualifying low-income owners, the grant may also cover drainfield costs and non-BAT component repairs. Community wastewater treatment system installation with enhanced nutrient removal standards. structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund - Onsite Disposal Systems Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive, statewide grant and subsidy program that provides funds for upgrading septic systems to best available technology (BAT) for nitrogen removal, connecting properties to public sewer systems, installing holding tanks, and implementing cover crops. The program is funded by fees collected from users of onsite sewage disposal systems to reduce nitrogen loading to the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Upgraded systems reduce nitrogen loads by approximately 50% compared to conventional systems and lower coliform and enterococci counts. The program has already upgraded over 12,000 septic systems across Maryland. Effective July 1, 2012, a $60 annual fee is collected from each user served by an onsite system, with an estimated program income of $27 million per year. Sixty percent of funds support septic system upgrades and 40 percent support cover crops. Implementation occurs at the county level, with local County Health Departments administering applications. Funding varies by property type: residential properties with household incomes under $300,000 per year receive 100 percent funding, all nonprofit entities receive 100 percent funding, and non-residential properties receive 50 percent funding. Low-income households may receive additional support for failing system replacement. The program aims to improve water quality and restore the health of the Chesapeake Bay ecosystem. Between 2007 and 2011, the program funded nitrogen removal unit installations on 95 septic systems in Charles County. There are 420,000 onsite systems in Maryland eligible for the program. The program also provides funding for new construction cost differential between conventional and BAT systems, community system replacement costs, and includes two years of operations and maintenance by certified service providers.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Effective July 1, 2012, a $60 annual fee is collected from each user served by an onsite system. The total estimated program income is $27 million per year. Sixty percent of these funds are used for septic system upgrades and the remaining 40 percent are used for cover crops. Funds can be provided for upgrades of existing systems to best available technology for nitrogen removal, connection to public sewer systems, holding tank installation, or for the marginal cost of using best available technology instead of conventional technology. For best available technology installation, grant covers the cost and installation of the unit plus two years of maintenance, but does not cover drainfield costs (except for qualifying low-income owners) or permit or recordation fees. For public sewer connections, grant covers connection costs, sewer system connection fees, and permits, with funding up to $25,000 per connection for infrastructure costs. Holding tank installation grants are also available for qualifying properties. Residential properties with household incomes under $300,000 per year receive 100 percent funding. All nonprofit entities receive 100 percent funding. Non-residential properties receive 50 percent funding. Properties with failing or non-conforming systems in the Critical Area (within 1,000 feet of tidal waters) receive priority. For low-income households, grants can be used to replace failing septic systems and may cover drainfield costs and non-BAT component repairs. Community wastewater treatment systems may replace multiple on-site systems. Sewer connections to municipal wastewater treatment plants with enhanced nutrient removal are eligible. Grant funds are provided from the State's Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fund. Additional 50% operations and maintenance grant available for low-income households beyond the initial two years of funded maintenance. Income-based grants ranging from 50-100% of eligible costs depending on applicant type and income level. Funding caps per EDU (Equivalent Dwelling Unit): $23,500-$25,000 depending on project type and applicant category.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications will reopen in December 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners throughout Maryland with septic systems, holding tanks, or wastewater disposal needs, prioritizing those with failing or non-conforming systems in Critical Areas near tidal waters, and low-income households. Includes owners of onsite sewage disposal systems and property owners with existing dwellings in Maryland. Local County Health Departments administer the program and process applications. Eligible applicants include residential property owners with household incomes under $300,000 per year, all nonprofit entities, non-residential property owners, and residents of eligible counties including Charles, Prince George's, Worcester, Talbot, and Anne Arundel counties seeking to improve water quality and comply with Chesapeake Bay restoration requirements. Developers undertaking new construction and local governments also eligible. Homeowners with failing or non-conforming onsite disposal systems, housing cooperatives, and small businesses also eligible. Individual homeowners with onsite sewage disposal systems. Properties within Chesapeake Bay Critical Areas, Coastal Bays Critical Areas, or Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Septic system upgrades including connection to public sewer or installation of nitrogen-removing Best Available Technology (BAT) septic tanks or biosolids absorbent treatment systems, holding tank installation, replacement of failing septic systems for low-income households, drainfield costs and non-BAT component repairs for qualifying low-income owners, implementation of cover crops to reduce nitrogen loading to the Chesapeake Bay, community wastewater treatment system installation with enhanced nutrient removal standards, capital costs for sewer connection infrastructure to municipal treatment plants, cost differential between conventional and BAT systems for new construction, and operations and maintenance support (two years included with BAT installation, with additional 50% O&M grant available for low-income households). Installation of Best Available Technology (BAT) pre-treatment units. Inspection costs. 2 years of operation and maintenance services. BAT system components only.

Regional implementations available in Worcester, Talbot, Charles, Prince George's, and Anne Arundel counties. Implementation occurs at the county level through local County Health Departments. Prioritization follows state law ranking: failing systems in Critical Areas first, then failing systems outside Critical Areas, then non-conforming systems in Critical Areas, then non-conforming systems outside Critical Areas, then other systems. Properties within 1,000 feet of mean high tide receive highest priority in Worcester County. Baltimore County properties prioritized by proximity to Chesapeake Bay Critical Area. Charles County residents also eligible. Projects must be consistent with County Water and Sewer Plans. Projects outside Critical Areas also eligible. Worcester County, Maryland properties. Properties within Chesapeake Bay Critical Areas, Coastal Bays Critical Areas, or Priority Funding Areas (prioritized). Projects must be located in Priority Funded Areas or have an exception. Projects must be consistent with County Water and Sewer Plan.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: As of July 1, 2010, the program is implemented by local County Health Departments. There are 420,000 onsite systems in Maryland eligible for the program. Property owners should contact their county health department or county Environmental Health Division for application procedures and eligibility determination. Regional contact offices include Charles County Department of Health, Talbot County Public Works, Prince George's County Environmental Engineering, and Worcester County Department of Environmental Programs. structured_extraction.program_description: The Bay Restoration Fund finances capital projects to implement Enhanced Nutrient Removal at wastewater treatment plants in Maryland to reduce nitrogen and phosphorus discharges into the Chesapeake Bay. The program is funded by a $5.00 monthly fee collected from each home served by a wastewater treatment plant and $5.00 per month per equivalent dwelling unit from commercial and industrial users, generating an estimated $100 million per year. The Department issues bonds backed in full or in part by these funds to expedite implementation. Funding supports nutrient removal upgrades, combined sewer overflow abatement, sewer rehabilitation, conveyance system upgrades, sewer extensions to connect septic homes to treatment plants, nitrogen reduction at community septic systems, stormwater projects by local governments, and flood mitigation, resilience, and watershed restoration projects. Enhanced Nutrient Removal technology enables plants to achieve wastewater effluent quality of 3 mg/l total nitrogen and 0.3 mg/l total phosphorus, helping meet commitments under the 2000 Chesapeake Bay Agreement. The program also supports incremental costs of wastewater treatment plant Enhanced Nutrient Removal operations and maintenance (up to 10% of annual revenue or approximately $6 million per year starting FY 2010) and provides income-based grant assistance for on-site sewage disposal system upgrades.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 100 percent state grant funds for eligible project costs including planning, design, and construction costs. Funds are provided on a reimbursable basis after a payment request is made by the grantee. Capital financing is available for wastewater treatment plant upgrades and related sewer infrastructure improvements. The 67 major publicly owned facilities discharging to the Chesapeake Bay have priority for funding. After Enhanced Nutrient Removal upgrades at the 67 significant wastewater treatment plants are complete, funding is allocated to minor wastewater treatment plants for ENR upgrades, then remaining funds are allocated based on project priority ranking. Grants also support stormwater projects by local governments and flood mitigation, resilience, and watershed restoration projects. Additionally, incremental costs of wastewater treatment plant Enhanced Nutrient Removal operations and maintenance are supported (up to 10% of annual revenue or approximately $6 million per year starting FY 2010). For minor and other WWTPs, cost effectiveness criteria apply (less than $150 per pound of total nitrogen reduced). For on-site sewage disposal systems, income-based grant assistance is available: homeowners with income ≤$300K receive up to 100% grant, homeowners with income >$300K receive up to 50% grant, non-profits receive 100%, small businesses receive 75%, and for-profit businesses receive 50%, with maximum sewer connection grants of $25,000 (100%), $18,750 (75%), or $12,500 (50%). Planning and design grants for minor WWTPs are funded at 100% by BRF to protect owners from financial risk.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland wastewater treatment plants, particularly the 67 major publicly owned facilities with a design flow of 500,000 gallons per day or greater that discharge to the Chesapeake Bay, as well as municipalities responsible for wastewater systems, wastewater treatment plant operators, local governments, minor WWTP owners and operators, homeowners with failing or non-conforming on-site sewage disposal systems, non-profit entities, small and for-profit businesses, health departments, and property owners in Critical Areas and State Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhanced Nutrient Removal upgrades at wastewater treatment plants, combined sewer overflow abatement, sewer rehabilitation, conveyance system upgrades including pumping stations, planning and design costs, sewer extensions to connect homes on septics to a BNR/ENR wastewater treatment plant, nitrogen reduction technology at community septic systems, stormwater projects by local governments, flood mitigation, resilience, and watershed restoration projects, incremental costs of wastewater treatment plant operations and maintenance, engineering evaluations for ENR system upgrades, on-site sewage disposal system upgrades using best available technology for nitrogen removal including cost of upgrading existing systems, cost differentials for new construction, community system replacements, sewer connections to municipal treatment plants, repair/replacement of non-BAT components for low-income failing systems, comprehensive engineering evaluations of existing ENR systems, and operations and maintenance support for 2 years post-installation of OSDS upgrades.

Projects must be consistent with county water and sewer plans and Executive Order 01.01.2003.33 – Maryland's Priority Places Strategy. On-site sewage disposal system upgrades prioritize properties in Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Areas, with additional consideration for State Priority Funding Areas. Major WWTPs are located across Maryland and the District of Columbia.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The 67 major publicly owned facilities discharging to the Chesapeake Bay have priority for funding. The Department may consider other facilities on a case-by-case basis based on cost effectiveness of the upgrade and other factors. Submit funding applications during the December through January application window annually. Applications will reopen in December 2026. For minor and other WWTPs: Pre-planning project selection with CPP criteria evaluation, planning phase with PER and alternatives analysis, design phase re-evaluation at 90%+ engineering estimates, bidding phase re-evaluation using lowest bid, and MDE issues eligibility determinations at planning and design phases. Projects are evaluated at planning, design, and bidding phases and must remain cost effective through all phases or funding will be capped. For ENR Refinement Program: Complete comprehensive engineering evaluation, receive preliminary eligibility determination from MDE, accept BRF funding with new TN goal (or pursue SRF loan only), execute new ENR agreement with MDE, apply to WIFA during regular solicitation process for design and construction funding, and receive final eligibility determination from MDE. For on-site sewage disposal system upgrades, assistance is provided based on income levels and entity type, with installation costs and 2 years of operations and maintenance support by certified service providers. Grantees make payment requests for reimbursement of eligible project costs after work is completed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund Financial Hardship Exemption Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment that allows billing authorities and individual jurisdictions to grant waivers or exemptions from paying the Bay Restoration Fee (flush tax) to residential dwellings and properties that demonstrate substantial financial hardship. The exemption removes the Bay Restoration Fee from water bills or real property tax accounts for specified time periods (typically one year). Exemptions must be reapplied for annually. Applicants must meet eligibility criteria established by their local billing authority, which may include receiving energy assistance subsidies, public assistance (supplemental security income or food stamps), veterans or social security disability benefits, or meeting income criteria established by the Maryland Department of Human Services Office of Home Energy Programs. Some jurisdictions, such as Baltimore County and Allegany County, restrict eligibility to property owners whose primary residence is in the county and who currently receive specific tax credits or meet hardship criteria. Individual billing authorities establish their own financial hardship exemption programs and submit proposed plans to the Maryland Department of the Environment for approval. The State of Maryland requires all participating counties to collect mandated fees to support Chesapeake Bay restoration efforts.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual exemption from or reduction of the Bay Restoration Fee that removes the fee from either water utility bills or real property tax accounts. The exemption is granted for a specified time period not to exceed one year without re-verification of eligibility, typically applying only to the current fiscal tax year. Eligibility criteria vary by jurisdiction. Some jurisdictions require applicants to meet at least two of the following conditions: receiving energy assistance subsidy, receiving public assistance (supplemental security income or food stamps), receiving veterans or social security disability benefits, or meeting income criteria established by the Maryland Department of Human Services Office of Home Energy Programs. Other jurisdictions, such as Baltimore County, restrict eligibility to property owners whose primary residence is in that county and who currently receive specific qualifying tax credits. Property owners receive an exemption from the Bay Restoration Fee if they currently receive one of three specified tax credits or exemptions and their property is their primary residence. Exemptions must be reapplied for annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds the purchase and installation of electric vehicle charging equipment to expand EV charging infrastructure across Maryland, including Level 2 workplace charging equipment and Level 3 DC Fast Charging stations along alternative fuel corridors and at charging hubs. This program is part of Maryland's commitment to cleaner transportation and is funded by the state's settlement with Volkswagen over its emissions violations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide funding for the purchase and installation of Level 2 workplace charging equipment and Level 3 DC Fast Charging stations. For CAGP (Charge Ahead Grant Program): grants cover up to 60% of costs to purchase and install light-duty electric vehicle supply equipment, with a cap of $4,500 per port for networked chargers; $2,500 per port for non-networked chargers; maximum $600,000 total award per parent company or lead agency. For ECGP (Electric Corridors Grant Program): funds cover up to 80% of costs to purchase and install light-duty electric vehicle supply equipment, with up to $150,000 per 175 kW (or greater) charging port or up to $100,000 per 60 kW (or greater) charging port; total amount awarded per project site limited to $900,000. Grants are competitive (not first-come, first-served) and reimbursement-based.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program authorized under the Inflation Reduction Act and Bipartisan Infrastructure Law that provides grants to states, local governments, tribes, and territories for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and other harmful air pollution. The program has two phases: Phase 1 provides planning grants to develop climate action strategies, and Phase 2 provides competitive implementation funds to carry out emissions reduction projects. Maryland's comprehensive state program aims to achieve 60% GHG emissions reductions by 2031 and attain net-zero emissions by 2045. Funding is distributed through the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (approximately $1 billion annually) and multiple state agencies for decarbonization projects across electricity, transportation, buildings, industry, waste, agriculture, and forestry/land use sectors. The program encompasses clean energy, vehicle electrification, building decarbonization, industrial emissions reduction, natural and working lands conservation, waste management, and workforce development initiatives. Maryland's comprehensive climate action plan implements 21 measures across multiple sectors and focuses on reducing GHG emissions and harmful air pollution while delivering benefits to disadvantaged communities and addressing environmental justice concerns. The program funds tackle climate pollution while supporting job creation and lowering energy costs, addresses environmental injustice in overburdened neighborhoods, and delivers cleaner air by reducing harmful air pollution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides $5 billion in total grants across two phases: Phase 1 provided $250 million for noncompetitive planning grants to develop climate action plans ($3 million for Maryland; $3 million for DC/Metro MSA; $1 million for Baltimore Metro Area MSA; $1 million for Philadelphia Metro Area MSA), and Phase 2 provides approximately $4.6 billion for competitive implementation grants to fund emissions reduction projects. Competitive implementation grants were awarded in July 2024 with funds distributed in October 2024. Maryland received $133 million from IRA's CPRG Program. The Strategic Energy Investment Fund distributes approximately $1 billion annually for decarbonization projects. Specific assistance mechanisms include: EV Tax Credit (up to $3,000); EVSE Rebate (50% of costs up to $700 residential or $5,000 commercial); Clean Vehicle Rebate ($2,500 new EV or $1,000 used EV, plus $5,000/$3,000 bonus for low-to-moderate income; superuser bonus $5,000/$3,000); Home Efficiency Rebates (up to $4,000 or 50% of project costs for 35%+ energy savings; up to $2,000 or 50% for 20-34% energy savings); Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates (heat pump systems up to $8,000, electric panel upgrades up to $4,000, electric wiring up to $2,500, heat pump water heaters up to $1,750 federal or up to $8,000 state for low-moderate-middle income households); Federal tax credits up to $2,000 for heat pump installation; State rebates up to $8,000 for heat pump installation (eligible low-, moderate-, middle-income households); School bus rebates from electric utilities; Competitive grants for commercial zero-emission vehicle purchases (up to 75% of incremental costs); Building energy efficiency and electrification support; Renewable Energy Production Tax Credits; Investment Tax Credits for renewable energy systems; Community solar programs with 40% LMI subscriber requirement; Energy storage programs; Workforce development programs; Prevailing Wage/Apprenticeship bonus tax credits; Domestic Content bonus tax credits; Energy Communities bonus tax credits; Low-Income Communities bonus tax credits; Elective pay option for tax-exempt entities under IRA direct pay provisions; Low-interest loans, forgivable loans, and principal forgiveness programs; HFC technician training support; Environmental Product Declaration Assistance Fund for eligible construction materials producers ($15 million for HFC phase-out support); Landfill methane compliance support; School Waste Reduction and Composting Program grants; Agricultural decarbonization funding (Cover Crop Plus program, Healthy Soils Competitive Fund); Tree planting and forest management grants (5 Million Trees Initiative targeting 500,000 trees in urban areas); Coastal wetland restoration funding; Bay Restoration Fund grants ($45 million FY21-FY23); Energy-Water Infrastructure Program grants ($40 million distributed FY17-FY20); Revolving Loan Fund Programs with low-interest rates and principal forgiveness; Technical assistance grants for small fleet electrification planning; $63 million in NEVI funds for EV charging corridor infrastructure (23 EV Alternative Fuel Corridors statewide); Point-of-sale rebates for energy efficiency and EV equipment; Contractor incentives; Consumer education campaigns; Federal Clean School Bus Program grants; Home electrification incentives (up to 100% for low/moderate income; 50% for middle income); Community engagement and environmental justice support programs; Medium and heavy-duty zero-emission vehicle grants offsetting up to 75% of incremental costs; Transit bus fleet electrification funding (350+ buses over 5 years); Cargo handling equipment replacement programs at Port of Baltimore; Workforce training grants through Partnership for Workforce Quality; Good Jobs Challenge grant (~$23 million for offshore wind workforce); Maryland Works for Wind program; $2.5 million funding (July 2025) for offshore wind industry preparation; EARN Maryland program; Innovation Investment Tax Credit program; Advantage Maryland conditional loans; More Jobs for Marylanders tax credit; Job Creation tax credit; No matching fund requirement for implementation grants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Phase 1 (planning) closed. Priority Climate Action Plan (PCAP) due March 1, 2024. Comprehensive Climate Action Plan (CCAP) due two years after planning grant award or by 2025. Phase 2 (implementation) competitive awards announced July 2024. Implementation Grant applications due April 2024. Environmental product declarations due end of 2024. Food residuals diversion law thresholds: November 1, 2023 (2 tons/week) and November 1, 2024 (1 ton/week). School districts must purchase/contract ZEV school buses starting 2024 (with funding availability). Status Report due to EPA: June 2027. CCAP due to EPA: July 2025.
