structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for greenhouse gas emissions reduction projects and actions that address climate change and air pollution, including: electric vehicle charging infrastructure (23 Alternative Fuel Corridors, NEVI funding for medium and heavy-duty charging along I-95 corridor), zero-emission vehicles (new and used EVs), natural carbon sequestration through forest management (5 Million Trees Initiative targeting 400,000 acres for afforestation, at least 10% in urban underserved areas), protection and restoration of coastal habitats and wetlands, climate resilience projects along Maryland's forests and coastal areas, building energy performance improvements and energy efficiency retrofits, renewable energy and clean energy projects (solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal, offshore wind, energy storage), energy efficiency programs including home electrification and appliance upgrades (heat pumps, electric panel upgrades, electric wiring), transportation and transit initiatives, fossil fuel heating equipment transition to electric alternatives, grid modernization and transmission system upgrades, public transportation infrastructure (transit bus electrification), micro-mobility projects, school bus electrification, industrial decarbonization (cement manufacturing and other industrial sectors), waste diversion and recycling infrastructure, composting programs and facilities, food residuals management, HFC technician training, methane emissions detection and control (landfill gas capture), sustainable materials management, agricultural best practices for manure management and enteric fermentation reduction, soil health practices (Cover Crop Plus program, Healthy Soils Competitive Fund), tree planting and urban greening, sustainable land use practices, sustainable forest management (certification standards, conservation plans, no net forest loss requirements), afforestation and forest preservation initiatives, workforce development and apprenticeship programs in clean energy sectors (electricians, HVAC-R mechanics, plumbers, solar installers, roofers, insulation workers, heat pump installers, clean energy jobs, offshore wind careers), environmental justice initiatives, consumer education campaigns, technical assistance and project planning, design, financing, and implementation support, HFC reduction and phaseout, embodied carbon reduction in construction materials (Environmental Product Declaration support), port infrastructure improvements including cargo handling equipment upgrades at Port of Baltimore, research and innovation, community solar programs, power purchase agreements, feasibility studies and capacity building when tied to emissions reduction projects, GHG emission reductions across sectors (electricity, buildings, transportation, industry, agriculture, waste management), community benefits and infrastructure deployment particularly in low-income areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide through EPA; in Maryland, the statewide planning grant is led by MDE. Three of Maryland's Metropolitan Statistical Areas (Baltimore-Columbia-Towson, Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington, and Washington-Arlington-Alexandria MSAs) received additional planning grants. Specific Maryland coverage: Baltimore MSA includes Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Harford, Howard, and Queen Anne's. Philadelphia MSA includes Cecil County. Washington DC MSA includes Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's. Counties outside the MSAs (Allegany, Calvert, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester) are eligible for support through the Maryland Local Government Climate Action Support Program. Approximately 278 census tracts (19.8% of Maryland) identified as disadvantaged by CEJST. Approximately 1,048 census block groups (25.7% of Maryland) identified as disadvantaged by EPA EJScreen. Population of 930,142-1,412,787 Marylanders in identified LIDACs. Approximately 9,000 covered buildings statewide (35,000+ sq ft). I-95 corridor priority for medium and heavy-duty EV charging. Offshore wind development in federal Atlantic waters. East Coast regional coordination for renewable energy initiatives. Specific focus on Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Prince George's County, and Allegany County for environmental justice investments. Eastern Shore and Garrett County (Western Maryland) also eligible. Statewide emphasis on overburdened and underserved communities with at least 10% of tree planting targeted to urban underserved areas.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Phase 1 (planning) was a noncompetitive process. Phase 2 (implementation) is a competitive process. Competition winners for Phase 2 were announced in July 2024 with funds awarded in October 2024. Maryland's Priority Climate Action Plan (PCAP) was required by March 1, 2024. Comprehensive Climate Action Plans (CCAP) due two years after planning grant award or by 2025. For counties outside MSAs, applicants can request assistance through the Maryland Local Government Climate Action Support Program by filling out a form. Multiple state agencies administer specific programs with varying application processes. Some programs offer point-of-sale rebates, while others require competitive grant applications. Technical assistance grants available for small fleet electrification planning. Grant writing assistance and project planning, design, financing, and implementation support available. Three-step process for planning: (1) Advisory group engagement through MDE's EJ Office and Commission; (2) Public outreach via MDE webpage with webinar links and comment submission form; (3) Environmental Justice Listening Sessions with MDE Secretary and EJ Advisory Council. Coordination through Governor's Federal Office for statewide initiatives. Monthly and quarterly meetings and annual reporting requirements for ongoing programs. Contact local government support program for 12-county local support initiative. EPA contact for regional questions (Regions 3 contact information provided). Governmental entities serve as direct recipients; private entities and nonprofits may submit project proposals for MDE consideration. Multi-phase process: Planning grants → Priority Climate Action Plan → Implementation Grant applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's state program established in 1976 that provides matching grants to local jurisdictions and property owners for implementing capital projects included in comprehensive flood management plans, infrastructure repairs, watershed restoration, and emergency protection work associated with flood events. The program funds flood mitigation and resilience projects, including acquisition, elevation, and relocation of flood-prone structures and houses; construction of flood control infrastructure and warning systems; infrastructure retrofits; emergency preparedness measures; and watershed restoration to reduce flooding risks, restore natural floodplain, and mitigate future flooding impacts from climate change.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants to local governments and property owners for projects that increase flood resilience and restore natural floodplain. When federal funds do not participate, CFMGP may fund up to 75% of project costs with a 25% local government cost share. When federal Hazard Mitigation Assistance grants (HMGP, BRIC, FMA) fund up to 75% of costs, the remaining 25% can be split evenly between state CFMGP and local governments. State funds are also provided on a 50/50 basis matched with local government funds. Grant awards are made after Maryland Board of Public Works approval. Eligible uses include acquisition, elevation, and relocation of flood-prone structures and houses; construction of flood control infrastructure and warning systems; infrastructure retrofits; emergency preparedness measures; watershed restoration; and implementation of capital projects in comprehensive flood management plans.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typically December 1 through January 31 annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal governments and property owners in Maryland working to reduce flooding risks and improve floodplain management and resilience.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of capital projects in comprehensive flood management plans, infrastructure repairs, watershed restoration, emergency protection work associated with flood events, purchase, relocation, and elevation of houses and flood-prone structures, establishment of warning systems, construction of flood control infrastructure, infrastructure retrofits, and emergency preparedness measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Available to local governments and property owners throughout the state. Departments in collaboration with Department of Planning and Department of Agriculture designate a priority list of watersheds for studies and flood management.
requirements_list: Must be a County or municipal government entity or property owner
Must provide matching funds (50% or 25% depending on federal participation)
Project must increase flood resilience and restore natural floodplain
Government agency or property owner must file an application requesting funding
Evidence of ability to fund the required cost share amount must be included
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: County and municipal governments and property owners submit applications during the annual solicitation period, typically December 1 through January 31. Communities work with MDE to identify flooding risks and develop eligible mitigation projects. Complete applications and supporting documents must be submitted before the close of the solicitation period. Notification of project selection is made after the Maryland General Assembly approves the state capital budget, approximately 1.5 years after application submission. Grant awards are made after Maryland Board of Public Works approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program established by the 1985 Farm Bill that provides cost sharing and land rental payments to farmers for establishing permanent cover on highly erodible lands, planting filter strips and riparian forest buffers adjacent to streams and waterbodies, and restoring wetlands and shallow water areas for wildlife.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners enter into contracts for 10 to 15 years and receive annual rental payments. For some conservation practices such as riparian buffers, filter strips, grassed waterways, contour buffer strips, and shallow water areas for wildlife, land can be enrolled at any time through continuous sign-up. Other practices require competitive ranking during announced sign-up periods.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Sign-up periods usually occur once or twice per year; continuous sign-up available for certain practices
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and landowners
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing permanent cover on highly erodible lands, planting filter strips and riparian forest buffers adjacent to streams and waterbodies, restoring wetlands and shallow water areas for wildlife
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maximum of 25 percent of a county's eligible cropland may be enrolled. The Chesapeake Bay region has been designated as a national conservation priority area for CRP.

Haying, grazing, and harvesting of CRP acreage for agricultural or commercial purposes prohibited during contract period

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners can offer to enroll land during announced sign-up periods (competitive process) or through continuous sign-up for certain practices (non-competitive). Contact local USDA Service Center for enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cybersecurity Training for Water and Wastewater System Operators
structured_extraction.program_description: Free online training program covering cybersecurity fundamentals for water and wastewater system operators. The training is required for all water and wastewater operators in Maryland as part of their certification renewal process and covers establishing and managing cybersecurity programs, account security, device security, data security, vulnerability management, supply chain/third-party considerations, response and recovery, and network segmentation. The training helps operators understand and implement critical cybersecurity measures to safeguard water systems against evolving threats.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training delivered through the EPA covering cybersecurity awareness and fundamentals. Operators must complete the training as part of their certification renewal process. The training includes access to EPA materials, a video, and a quiz that must be completed in a timely manner before the renewal application deadline. Training covers establishing and managing cybersecurity programs, account security, device security, data security, vulnerability management, supply chain considerations, response and recovery, and network segmentation. OT-specific cybersecurity training is available for those using operational technology systems.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Before renewal application deadline (specific date not stated)
structured_extraction.program_audience: All water and wastewater system operators in Maryland who are renewing their certification, and all public water system personnel.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training must be completed to fulfill cybersecurity certification requirements for operator license renewal.

Training must be completed as part of certification renewal process
Training must be completed in a timely manner to allow sufficient time for processing quiz results
Operators are responsible for allocating time to complete this requirement before the renewal application deadline

Step 3: Complete the EPA Cybersecurity Training Quiz. Step 4: Submit results for processing. Operators must complete all steps before their renewal application deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides below market rate of interest loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness to eligible water systems and local governments for projects that achieve or maintain compliance with the Federal Safe Drinking Water Act and provide safe drinking water while protecting the quality of Maryland's drinking water supply. The fund supports water treatment plant construction and upgrades, source water protection plan development and implementation, raw water intake and conveyance infrastructure, finished water storage facilities, water distribution system rehabilitation including lead service line replacement, system consolidation, and planning, design, and construction efforts. Receives federal funding from the United States Environmental Protection Agency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below market rate of interest loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness to eligible public and private community water systems and local governments for drinking water projects. Assistance covers water treatment plant construction and upgrades, source water protection plan development and implementation, raw water intake and conveyance infrastructure, finished water storage facilities, water distribution system rehabilitation including lead service line replacement, system consolidation, and planning, design, and construction of eligible drinking water projects to achieve or maintain compliance with the Federal Safe Drinking Water Act. The Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration can provide financial advisory services to help borrowers determine water rate structures and assess the financial impact of loans.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water treatment plant construction and upgrades, source water protection plan development and implementation, raw water intake and conveyance infrastructure, finished water storage facilities, water distribution system rehabilitation including lead service line replacement, consolidation of water systems, and planning, design, and construction of eligible drinking water projects to achieve or maintain compliance with the Federal Safe Drinking Water Act

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to Maryland counties and municipalities that have established separate collection and recycling programs for computers and video display devices. The program supports local eCycling infrastructure and operations.

structured_extraction.program_description: An energy efficiency program managed by electric and gas utility companies and the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. The program provides energy efficiency and conservation services to reduce per capita energy consumption and demand, lower electricity and gas bills, reduce wholesale energy prices, and decrease greenhouse gas emissions. EmPOWER targets energy savings of 2% annually for electric utilities and requires support for beneficial electrification and increased savings for limited-income households.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EmPOWER programs provide energy efficiency improvements, conservation services, and training. Programs are managed by Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE), Potomac Edison Company (PE), Delmarva Power & Light (Delmarva), Potomac Electric Power Company (PEPCO), Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative (SMECO), Washington Gas Light Company (WGL), and DHCD. DHCD provides additional programs targeting limited-income households. The program requires utility companies to achieve annual energy savings targets: 2.25% in 2025-2026 and 2.5% in 2027 and thereafter. DHCD requires energy savings of 0.53% in 2024, 0.72% in 2025, and 1% in 2026 for limited-income households.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial customers of participating utility companies in Maryland, with particular focus on limited-income households through DHCD programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements, conservation services, electrification measures, and related training and technical assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide through participating utilities
requirements_list: Customers of participating utility companies
DHCD programs prioritize limited-income households
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Customers access EmPOWER programs through their utility provider or through DHCD for limited-income household programs. Specific application procedures vary by utility company and program type.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program designed to help communities respond to emergencies created by natural disasters such as floods, fires, and windstorms. It provides assistance for emergency measures like removing debris from waterways, repairing eroded banks, and restoring damaged areas to reduce threats to life and property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NRCS bears up to 75 percent of the construction cost of emergency measures. The remaining 25 percent must come from local sources and can be in the form of cash or in-kind services. Work must be sponsored by a political subdivision of the State such as a city, county, general improvement district, or conservation district.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private landowners represented by a project sponsor that is a public agency of state, county, or city government, or a special district
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Removing debris from stream channels, road culverts, and bridges; reshaping and protecting eroded banks; correcting damaged drainage facilities; repairing levees and structures; reseeding damaged areas; and purchasing floodplain easements

Work must be sound from an engineering standpoint
Applications must be submitted within 10 days of the disaster for exigency situations and within 60 days for nonexigency situations
Local cost share of 25 percent must be secured
Landrights to do repair work must be provided
Necessary permits must be secured

Sponsor is responsible for providing landrights, securing permits, furnishing local cost share, and accomplishing installation of work.

structured_extraction.program_name: Forest Stewardship Program and Stewardship Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps private landowners protect or enhance their forest lands and associated wetlands by providing technical assistance and cost-sharing to implement forest management practices.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Forest Stewardship Program provides technical assistance to help landowners enhance or protect timber, fish/wildlife habitat, water quality, wetlands, and recreational/aesthetic values. Stewardship Incentive Program provides cost-sharing for implementing FSP plans with nine eligible categories. The maximum amount a landowner may receive in a year is $10,000. Approximately $100,000 is distributed annually to 150 landowners for practices covering 2,000 acres. Practices must be maintained for a minimum of 10 years.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with five or more acres of forest land or non-forest land that can be planted to trees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Management plan development, afforestation, forest improvement, windbreaks and hedgerows, streamside and wetlands protection, fisheries and aquatic habitat improvement, wildlife habitat enhancement, forest recreation habitat enhancement, and soil and water protection
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide

Practices receiving cost-share assistance must be maintained for a minimum of 10 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowner applies for Forest Stewardship Program technical assistance, which results in a forest management plan. Landowner then applies for cost-share assistance through Stewardship Incentive Program to implement practices from the plan.

structured_extraction.program_name: General Permit for Discharges of Stormwater Associated with Construction Activity (20-CP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide NPDES permit (MDRC0000) that authorizes discharges of stormwater associated with construction activity, including earth-disturbing activities, construction support activities, and related stormwater runoff. The permit applies to construction projects that disturb one or more acres of land, or disturb less than one acre but are part of a common plan of development that will ultimately disturb one or more acres. The permit requires implementation of erosion and sediment control measures, stormwater pollution prevention plans, and compliance with water quality standards to protect waters of the state. It includes standards for use of chemical additives for sediment control, procedures for reviewing and approving chemical additives based on aquatic toxicity testing, and requirements for dewatering inspections and turbidity benchmark monitoring. The permit also provides stormwater pollution prevention guidance addressing stormwater hotspots at commercial, industrial, institutional, municipal, or transport-related operations, covering vehicle maintenance and repair, fueling, washing or storage, loading and unloading, outdoor storage, and pavement or building wash water management. The permit replaces the previous construction stormwater general permit (14-GP), which expired December 31, 2019, and implements Clean Water Act Section 402 requirements and EPA Construction and Development (C&D) Rule requirements for stormwater management. The permit is effective April 1, 2023, and expires March 31, 2028 (as modified May 2, 2023).
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The permit provides regulatory authorization and technical guidance for managing stormwater runoff at construction sites and stormwater hotspots. It includes free training opportunities, access to stormwater pollution prevention plan templates and guidance documents, erosion and sediment control standards per 2011 Maryland Standards and Specifications, inspection forms, Stream Protection Zone requirements, antidegradation checklists for Tier II watersheds, turbidity monitoring benchmarks (150 NTU for Maryland; 50 NTU standard for EPA CGP), chemical additive approval procedures, and compliance documentation. A Notice of Intent must be submitted electronically through the ePermits system at least 14 days prior to construction for new operators, or within 7 calendar days for emergency authorization. Permit coverage requires compliance with effluent limits, proper operation and maintenance of controls, monitoring and reporting requirements, and pollution prevention measures. Fees apply based on COMAR 26.08.04.09-1, except for local and state government projects which are exempt. Emergency authorization for earth-disturbing activities prior to obtaining general permit coverage is available and valid upon submission of complete NOI within 7 calendar days. Chemical additives require case-by-case review and approval based on toxicity testing data; additives must be certified under ANSI/NSF Standard 60 for drinking water and applicants must submit complete toxicity testing data for whole product formulation including acute and chronic bioassay test results. Dewatering inspections must be conducted daily when discharge occurs, with turbidity benchmark monitoring (50 NTU standard) for discharges to sensitive waters, documented in inspection reports and corrective action logs. Technical guidance for stormwater hotspots includes pollution prevention practices documentation, checklists for vehicle maintenance and repair, fueling, washing or storage, loading and unloading, outdoor storage, and pavement/building wash water, as well as best management practices (BMPs) for pressure washing and building wash down operations to minimize stormwater pollution. Requirements for hotspot activities include no detergents or hazardous cleaning products, filtration of washwater, implementation of control measures to minimize solids and pollutants, personnel training, use of dry clean-up methods, and proper capture or permitting of chemical cleaner discharge.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: At least 14 days prior to construction for new operators, transfers, or increase in construction activity. Varies by project type; see Part II, Table 1 of the 20-CP permit. Emergency authorization must be obtained within 24 hours of initiating earth-disturbing activities. Complete NOI must be submitted within 7 calendar days after commencing earth-disturbing activities. Quarterly turbidity monitoring reports due April 30, July 30, October 30, January 30 (no later than 30 days after end of monitoring quarter) for sites discharging to sediment-impaired receiving waters or Tier II watersheds. For chemical additive reviews, submit Additive Review Request Worksheet and supporting documentation with NOI or separate additive review request. Continuation of Registration statements must be submitted at least 60 days before permit expiration. For existing sites (14-GP coverage): within 6 months of effective date. New sites: minimum 60 days prior to commencing construction. New operator/transfer: minimum 30 days prior to transfer date. Change in construction activity: one week prior to initiating change.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Construction site operators, developers, contractors, and other entities conducting construction activities that disturb soil (≥1 acre or <1 acre but part of common plan disturbing ≥1 acre) and may generate stormwater runoff. Includes general contractors, subcontractors, and parties with operational or day-to-day control of construction activities. Also includes responsible corporate officers, site owners/developers, architectural/design firms, single family home builders, and construction support activity operators (e.g., concrete/asphalt batch plants, equipment staging yards). Construction operators must be registered to do business in Maryland and discharge to State Waters. Inspectors with Responsible Personnel Certification conducting routine, pre-storm, during-storm, and post-storm inspections of construction sites. Applicants seeking to use chemical additives for sediment control at construction sites. Permittees engaged in dewatering activities requiring inspection and turbidity monitoring. Facility operators at stormwater hotspots including commercial operations (regional malls, stadiums, big box retail, car dealerships, rental car companies, quick lubes, service stations, marinas, bus depots), industrial operations (trucking companies, fleet operations, distribution centers, warehouses, landfills, auto recyclers/body shops, recycling centers, composting facilities, power plants), institutional operations (airports, school bus depots), municipal operations, and transport-related operations. Examples include petroleum wholesalers, grocery stores, building supply outlets, lawn and garden centers, nurseries, boat building/repair, and ports. Mining operators conducting pre-mining earth-disturbing activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Regulatory authorization and guidance for implementation of stormwater controls, erosion and sediment control measures, pollution prevention practices, and management of construction site runoff and stormwater hotspots, including stream protection, sediment reduction, and water quality protection. Funds are used to develop and implement Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs), install erosion and sediment control BMPs, conduct inspections and maintenance, achieve site stabilization, manage dewatering and turbid water treatment, and manage solid waste and hazardous materials. Chemical additive usage for sediment control must be evaluated for aquatic toxicity and approved based on Secondary Acute Values (SAV) and Secondary Chronic Values (SCV) calculations. Pollution prevention guidance supports implementation of BMPs for stormwater hotspot activities including vehicle maintenance and repair facilities, fueling stations, vehicle washing and storage areas, loading and unloading operations, outdoor storage areas, and pavement and building wash water management. Implementation includes design and installation of natural buffers (50 feet for Tier I watersheds, 100 feet average for Tier II watersheds), erosion and sediment controls per good engineering practices, soil compaction minimization, native topsoil preservation, steep slope disturbance minimization, perimeter control installation, and site stabilization with deadlines of 3-7 days based on area type.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; applies to all waters of the State including surface and underground waters, Chesapeake Bay and tributaries, ponds, lakes, rivers, streams, wetlands, and public drainage systems. Specific requirements vary by watershed tier (Tier I vs. Tier II) and for sediment-impaired receiving waters. Construction sites in Tier II watersheds must complete antidegradation checklists. Dewatering monitoring requirements apply to sites discharging to sensitive waters. Sites discharging to waters with PCB impairments or impaired for sediment receive priority consideration and enhanced monitoring requirements. Construction sites located in areas identified in Part I.B of permit. MDE office located at 1800 Washington Blvd, Ste. 455, Baltimore, MD 21230-1708.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Notice of Intent (NOI) through the ePermits website (https://egov.maryland.gov/mde/npdes/Account/Login) electronically signed by a person in authority. Complete MDE NPDES Subscriber Agreement to authorize electronic submissions. The system allows agents and consultants to prepare the NOI, which is then submitted by the responsible party. Federal regulations require submission of a Subscriber Agreement Template to validate authorization. A 14-day public notification period follows submission, during which interested parties may review the NOI and submit concerns to the Erosion and Sediment Control approval authority and MDE. Applicants must also submit approved Erosion and Sediment Control (E&SC) plans, Stormwater Management (SWM) plans, and Antidegradation Checklists (if applicable) along with the NOI. For emergency authorization, obtain written or electronic authorization from MDE within 24 hours of initiating work; submit complete and accurate NOI within 7 calendar days of commencing earth-disturbing activities. If denied, immediately stabilize earth disturbance and complete regular authorization process. Quarterly turbidity monitoring reports must be submitted through ePermits for sites discharging to sediment-impaired or Tier II waters; log into ePermits, locate NOI, access Documents for Upload, add file with Turbidity Monitoring Report description, upload report, and save. For chemical additive approvals, complete the Additive Review Request Worksheet and Cationic Form (or other additive form), attach relevant PPP/SWPPP documentation with treatment system design/operation/maintenance sections, obtain certified signature from responsible corporate officer or authorized representative, and submit with required supporting documentation including general product information, dosage information, and aquatic toxicity test results. MDE reviews chemical additive data using Secondary Value Calculator or Non-Soluble Additives review process and makes case-by-case approval determination. For dewatering inspections, conduct daily inspections when discharge occurs, complete inspection report using provided template documenting inspection location, discharge start/end times, rates, and pollutant indicator findings, take corrective action if pollutant indicators observed, sign and certify report by responsible party or authorized representative, attach required photographs, and retain inspection reports for at least 3 years after permit coverage expires. Maintain corrective action logs documenting triggering conditions and corrective actions taken, completing Section B within 24 hours of discovering triggering condition and Section C within 24 hours after completing corrective action, with corrective action completion meeting specified deadlines (same business day, 7 calendar days, or extended if infeasible). Update SWPPP within 7 calendar days of completing corrective work. Submit site-specific SWPPP identifying all site operators and areas of control, designating stormwater team with assigned responsibilities, describing nature and schedule of construction activities, and providing legible site map(s) showing property boundaries, construction activity locations, water resources, stockpile locations, vehicle exit points, slopes, demolition areas, impaired/Tier II waters, and other relevant features. Develop SWPPP prior to submitting NOI when using chemical additives for sediment control, potential for non-stormwater discharges exist, activities requiring pollution prevention measures, or sharing liability among multiple operators.

These funds help reduce the risk of future loss of life and property through long-term hazard mitigation projects, including property purchases, house relocations, and house elevations in 100-year floodplains and other mitigation measures during the recovery phase.

Grants are provided to eligible entities for hazard mitigation projects including property purchases, house relocations, house elevations, and other projects to reduce future disaster risk, particularly for properties within the 100-year floodplain.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance for replacement of older diesel vehicles with newer EPA-compliant models. The program includes two main components: (1) replacement of older diesel school buses with electric school buses and associated charging infrastructure for school districts and county governments, providing up to 45 percent of the purchase price; and (2) replacement of older drayage trucks operating at the Port of Baltimore with MY2017 or newer EPA-compliant trucks (or MY2012 or newer with EPA 2010-compliant engine), paying up to half the purchase price to a maximum of $30,000-$35,000 per truck depending on program year. In all cases, the recipient provides the remainder of the purchase price. For drayage trucks, scrappage income from replaced trucks may be used toward the owner's share of the purchase price.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Voluntary Cleanup Program is a state-administered program that encourages voluntary cleanup and redevelopment of contaminated properties through a streamlined cleanup process. The program allows property owners, prospective purchasers, responsible parties, and other eligible entities to clean up contaminated property and receive liability protections from the State. Participants can receive either a No Further Requirements Determination (NFRD) or Certificate of Completion (COC) upon successful cleanup, providing releases from state liability for identified contamination subject to certain reopeners. The program provides certainty regarding environmental requirements, allows parties to predict costs and timelines, and enables eligible purchasers to substantially limit liability for past contamination before purchasing property. The VCP works with the Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program administered by the Maryland Department of Business and Economic Development, which provides incentives including tax credits, loans and grants for redevelopment of eligible brownfield properties in participating jurisdictions. The program streamlines the cleanup process while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations, and increases certainty for participants through a Memorandum of Agreement with the EPA. The program issues closure documents with Environmental Covenants that legally restrict activities on contaminated sites and specifies land use and institutional controls for properties with residual contamination. The program was enacted in February 1997 to encourage investigation, cleanup, and redevelopment of eligible properties with known or perceived controlled hazardous substance contamination. As of October 1, 2004, the program also covers properties contaminated by oil or petroleum. Phase I Environmental Site Assessments must be prepared in accordance with ASTM International standards and identify recognized environmental conditions (RECs), controlled RECs (CRECs), and historic RECs (HRECs). Phase II Environmental Site Assessments involve field investigation and sampling to confirm or deny presence of contamination. The program requires detailed Response Action Plans (RAPs) for properties requiring remediation, with specific requirements for monitoring, inspection, maintenance, and long-term oversight. Environmental Covenants are recorded in land records to legally restrict activities on contaminated sites and specify land use and institutional controls.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The VCP provides a streamlined cleanup process with technical oversight by MDE during the investigation and cleanup process, along with liability releases and protections for participants who clean up contaminated property according to state-approved cleanup standards. Participants may receive an NFRD (if no further requirements are needed) or a COC (if long-term monitoring is required). Upon completion, the program records Environmental Covenants in land records within 30 days and issues regulatory determination and closure documentation. Application fees are required: $10,000 for the initial application (effective June 1, 2025) and $2,000 for subsequent applications on the same property, expedited determinations, or Expedited Inculpable Person approval. An additional $2,000 fee may be required upon issuance of NFRD or COC if conditioned on permissible use. A fee waiver is available for renewable energy siting and development projects. MDE provides itemized statements tracking oversight costs that are deducted from the application fee. Fees are non-refundable for applications received after October 1, 2004. The program works with the Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program which provides incentives including tax credits, loans and grants for redevelopment of eligible brownfield properties in participating jurisdictions. Program participants receive federal liability protection through an EPA agreement that considers sites in Maryland's program of no interest. Long-term oversight includes ongoing monitoring and maintenance requirements with annual summary reports required to MDE, 30-day correction timelines for deficiencies, and 48-hour notification of system failures. Property owners must maintain compliance with site-specific land use and institutional controls, including operations and maintenance of remedial systems (HVAC, sub-slab depressurization), regular inspections and monitoring (monthly, quarterly, or annual), and confirmatory soil/vapor sampling before residential development if required.

Response Action Plan (RAP) implementation including contamination assessment, remediation activities, health and safety measures, and property stabilization.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Pre-application meetings are encouraged to discuss application and participation requirements. Submit VCP application with required fee ($10,000 for initial application; $2,000 for subsequent applications, expedited determinations, or Expedited Inculpable Person approval) and complete application package including Phase I and Phase II environmental assessments and all known environmental information to the Maryland Department of the Environment. Applicant must post public notice at property with applicant name and address, MDE office contact information, and 30-day public comment period deadline. MDE reviews application and notifies applicant within 45 days whether application is incomplete, accepted, or denied. If application is accepted, MDE performs data screening risk evaluation to determine whether conditions pose risk to human health or environment. Based on this evaluation, MDE either issues NFRD (if no further requirements) or requires submission of Response Action Plan (RAP) before issuing COC. For expedited determination, applicant may submit written request and $2,000 fee if meeting specific requirements under Environmental Article Section 7-506(a)(1)(i), (ii), and (iii). For expedited inculpable person approval, submit the Expedited IP Form (Final Copy CPExIP Application) with completed Inculpable Person Affidavit and $2,000 fee via hand delivery or mail to 1800 Washington Blvd, Suite 625, Baltimore, Maryland 21230 (not PO Box), and email a copy to mde.exipvcp@maryland.gov. Department responds to expedited inculpable person requests within 5 business days with approval, additional information request, or disapproval. Submit electronic copy of Phase II site characterization work plan for Department review or submit documentation demonstrating sufficient site characterization has been performed to waive Phase II requirement. Phase II assessment submission triggers deadline extensions for public notice and Department action. RAP must include Site Overview with property description, site history, maps, and data summaries; Additional Investigatory Information if applicable; Exposure Assessment including current/future use, media of concern, exposed populations, exposure pathways, ecological receptors; Cleanup Criteria demonstration; Remedial Approaches and Institutional Controls with construction details; Public participation requirements including newspaper notice (two consecutive weeks) and public informational meeting; Quarterly or monthly status reports during implementation; RAP Completion Report before Certificate of Completion issuance. Upon completion of RAP, COC is issued and recorded in land records with Environmental Covenant within 30 days of receipt. After receiving NFRD or COC, applicant must: record determination in land records within 30 days, submit copy to one-call system within 30 days, sign and return certification within 10 days, record Environmental Covenant as Declaration concurrently, and if applicable, pay $2,000 fee upon issuance if conditioned on permissible use. Property owners must maintain compliance with land use controls and institutional controls, submit annual summary reports, notify MDE of any system failures within 48 hours and any deficiencies within 30 days, and notify MDE 5 days prior to property transfer. Applicants may withdraw from the VCP at any time before or after approval of application or RAP, including after receiving COC and prior to completing long-term monitoring. Upon withdrawal, different obligations apply to inculpable persons vs. responsible persons, and participants must stabilize and secure property and forfeit application fees.

Registered professionals are listed on the state's registry and may hold specific certifications including Property Transfer Inspector (PTI), Sand Mound Installer, At-Grade Installer, BAT (Best Available Technology) Installer, and BAT O&M certified professional. Individuals must satisfy Property Transfer Inspection licensing requirements per COMAR 26.31.01 to hold a PTI license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual registration to perform on-site wastewater services; includes listing on public registry. Individuals must pay a $150 registration fee every 2 years to register with the Maryland Department of the Environment and be listed on the state's registry of registered on-site wastewater service professionals. This allows them to legally provide on-site wastewater services in Maryland and enables local approving authorities to verify their credentials. Payment must be submitted as check or certified cashier's check. Registered professionals are tracked with licensing status and expiration dates; licenses must be renewed on specified dates.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Many PTI licenses must be renewed by 6/30/26; renewal notices and applications to be mailed in April; ongoing registration requirement
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who provide on-site wastewater services including pumpers, haulers, installers, maintenance and repair professionals, property transfer inspectors, plumbers, excavators, and environmental contractors
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registration fee covers the cost of registering individuals to provide on-site wastewater services and maintaining the professional registry
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; some registered professionals from neighboring states (Delaware, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia) and Canada
requirements_list: Complete application with all requested information
$150.00 registration fee (check or certified cashier's check)
Submission to MDE P.O. Box 2057, Baltimore, MD 21203
Must provide on-site wastewater services (design, installation, operation, maintenance, pumping, repair, or property transfer inspection)
Must satisfy Property Transfer Inspection (PTI) licensing requirements described in COMAR 26.31.01 for PTI licensure
Must attest that information provided is true and complete
Employees who act as primary leads must register individually; laborers and helpers do not need to register
Licensed engineers who design septic systems must register
Plumbers working only inside structures or replacing supply lines within 10 feet of the building do not need to register
Individuals seeking specific certifications must be certified for Sand Mound Installation, At-Grade Installation, BAT Installation, or BAT O&M
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application with $150 fee via mail to Maryland Department of the Environment, P.O. Box 2057, Baltimore, MD 21203. Registration confirmation letter sent to applicant's mailing address. Applicant listed on MDE website upon approval. Renewal notices and applications for PTI licenses expiring 6/30/26 will be mailed in April.

structured_extraction.program_name: Partners for Fish and Wildlife Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program is a technical and financial assistance program administered by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service that works in voluntary partnership with private landowners to restore wetlands, streams and river corridors, prairie, grasslands, and other important fish and wildlife habitats for federal trust species, including migratory birds, threatened and endangered species, anadromous fish, and some marine mammals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical and financial assistance to private landowners to voluntarily restore wetlands and other fish and wildlife habitats. Assistance may include informal advice on project design and location or funding of restoration projects under a voluntary cooperative agreement. Landowners agree to maintain the restoration project for a minimum of 10 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private (non-federal) landowners interested in voluntarily restoring wetlands, streams, prairies, grasslands, and other fish and wildlife habitats on their land.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration and enhancement of wetlands, streams, riparian areas, prairie, grasslands, and other fish and wildlife habitats through plugging drainage ditches, installing water control structures, planting native vegetation, removing exotic species, prescribed burning, streambank revegetation, and other bioengineering techniques.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide, with many states having waiting lists. Projects often located near National Wildlife Refuge System lands or State Wildlife Management Areas.
requirements_list: Must be a private (non-federal) landowner
Projects must benefit federal trust species (migratory birds, threatened and endangered species, anadromous fish, some marine mammals)
Restoration projects must meet habitat restoration standards
Landowner must agree to maintain the restoration project for a minimum of 10 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners contact the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Division of Habitat Conservation to discuss potential restoration projects. Program staff provide technical advice and design assistance, and may fund implementation through a voluntary cooperative agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A summer internship program that places college and university students at Maryland manufacturing companies to identify pollution prevention opportunities, process and equipment improvements, provide cost-benefit information, and assist with implementation of accepted changes. Students are trained in relevant industry sectors and general pollution prevention practices. The program is a partnership between the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) and University of Maryland Technology Enterprise Institute (MTECH), developed jointly with the University of Maryland's Technology Extension Service (MTES). Interns have identified over $3.7 million in cumulative cost savings through energy efficiency, waste reduction, and material use efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Student interns conduct summer employment working at participating Maryland manufacturing facilities to conduct pollution prevention assessments and identify cost-saving opportunities. Students research and assist with implementation of waste reduction, water usage reduction, hazardous waste reduction, energy efficiency, and material use efficiency improvements. The program is funded through a combination of State funding, a federal U.S. EPA grant, MDE support, and participating companies. Interns have identified over $3.7 million in cumulative cost savings. Example: one intern identified potential annual savings of $35,000 to $45,000 in water usage, waste and wastewater treatment, and chemical usage for a manufacturing company.
structured_extraction.program_audience: College and university students (particularly environmental health majors and environmental engineering students) enrolled at University of Maryland, College Park or Salisbury State University, and Maryland manufacturing companies interested in pollution prevention and process improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Student internship salaries and placement to conduct pollution prevention assessments at manufacturing facilities, identifying opportunities for waste reduction, water usage reduction, hazardous waste reduction, energy efficiency, and material use efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to manufacturing facilities throughout Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a college or university student
Enrolled at University of Maryland, College Park or Salisbury State University
Host facility must be a Maryland manufacturing company
Selected by university representatives and MDE managers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: University faculty recruit and select students from participating universities. MDE and MTECH managers identify participating manufacturing companies. Companies interested in hosting an intern should contact Laura Armstrong at MDE or Paul Gietka at Maryland Technology Enterprise Institute. University representatives at UMD College Park and Salisbury State University coordinate student selection and placement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pollution Prevention Technical Assistance for Maryland Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: Free, on-site technical assistance provided through the Maryland Manufacturing Extension Partnership to help businesses make more efficient use of energy and raw materials, reduce waste disposal costs, lower regulatory compliance costs, and decrease worker exposure to hazards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free on-site technical assistance visits lasting approximately one hour, conducted by engineers from the Manufacturing Extension Partnership. Visits include an assessment of pollution prevention opportunities and voluntary measures to improve efficiency. Following the visit, businesses receive a confidential report summarizing recommendations and an offer for further assistance to implement them.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses seeking to lower operating costs and increase competitive edge through improved efficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance is applied to making more efficient use of energy and raw materials, reducing waste disposal and handling costs, reducing regulatory compliance and liability costs, and decreasing worker exposure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Maryland
Participation is voluntary and non-regulatory
Facility must be available for on-site visit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Maryland Department of the Environment's Pollution Prevention Program to express interest and schedule a visit. An engineer from the Manufacturing Extension Partnership will contact you to answer questions and schedule the on-site visit. Following the visit, you receive a confidential report with recommendations and an offer for further implementation assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Port of Baltimore Dray Truck Replacement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance for replacement of older drayage trucks operating at the Port of Baltimore with newer EPA-compliant trucks. The program pays up to half the purchase price of qualifying trucks, with maximum assistance varying by program year ($30,000-$35,000). Scrappage income from replaced trucks may be used toward the owner's share of the purchase price.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance paying for up to half the purchase price of a drayage truck with an EPA-compliant engine (MY2012 or newer with EPA 2010-compliant engine, or MY2017 or newer EPA-compliant engine depending on program year), to a maximum of $30,000-$35,000 per truck. Scrappage income from replaced trucks may be credited toward the owner's share of the purchase price.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Drayage truck operators at the Port of Baltimore seeking to replace older trucks with newer EPA-compliant models
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of EPA-compliant drayage trucks to replace older trucks operating at the Port of Baltimore
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Port of Baltimore and surrounding communities
requirements_list: Vehicle must be a drayage truck operating at the Port of Baltimore
New truck must have EPA-compliant engine (MY2012 or newer with EPA 2010-compliant engine, or MY2017 or newer)
Owner must provide the remainder of purchase price beyond the grant assistance
Replaced trucks must be destroyed
Scrappage income from replaced truck goes toward owner's share
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of the Environment for information on applying for grants under this program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of the Environment awards CO2 offset allowances for projects that demonstrate real, additional, verifiable, enforceable and permanent avoidance of CO2 emissions or reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels. Projects may be located in any participating RGGI state or other approved jurisdiction. Eligible project types include landfill methane capture and destruction, energy efficiency improvements in end-use combustion, avoided methane emissions from agricultural manure management, sulfur hexafluoride reduction, and various carbon sequestration projects through reforestation, improved forest management, or avoided conversion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CO2 offset allowances are awarded for qualifying emission reduction or avoidance projects. Eligible project types include landfill methane capture and destruction, energy efficiency improvements in end-use combustion, avoided methane emissions from agricultural manure management, sulfur hexafluoride reduction, and various carbon sequestration projects through reforestation, improved forest management, or avoided conversion. For landfill methane projects: within six months of commencing the offset project (projects commenced December 20, 2005 – December 31, 2008 had deadline of June 30, 2009). For carbon sequestration projects: within one year after project commencement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: For landfill methane projects: within six months of commencing the offset project. For projects commenced December 20, 2005 – December 31, 2008: June 30, 2009. For projects commenced on or after January 1, 2009: within six months of commencement. For carbon sequestration projects: within one year of project commencement. For SF6 reduction projects: within six months after project commencement for projects commenced on or after January 1, 2009; June 30, 2009 for projects commenced December 20, 2005 – December 31, 2008.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Scott Zacharko; Air Quality Planning Program, Offsets
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landfill operators, agricultural operations with anaerobic digesters, electric transmission and distribution entities, forest owners, building owners/operators, and other project sponsors with projects that reduce or avoid CO2 emissions or sequester carbon in participating RGGI states or approved jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are awarded as offset allowances for projects demonstrating real, additional, verifiable, enforceable and permanent avoidance of CO2 emissions or reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels, including landfill methane capture, agricultural methane management, energy efficiency improvements, SF6 emissions reductions, and forest-based carbon sequestration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects may be located in any participating RGGI state or other approved jurisdiction. For reforestation projects: RGGI participating states (excluding NY and CT), or anywhere in the United States if the Project State has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with RGGI states. For SF6 reduction projects: Maryland only. For landfill and agricultural methane projects: Maryland and other RGGI participating states. For improved forest management and avoided conversion projects: RGGI participating states (excluding NY and CT) or anywhere in the United States if the Project State has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with RGGI states.
requirements_list: Project must demonstrate real, additional, verifiable, enforceable and permanent avoidance of CO2 emissions or reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels
Consistency application must be submitted to MDE within the specified deadline for the project type
Applications failing to meet submission deadlines will be denied and the project will remain ineligible
Project must meet specific standards outlined in COMAR 26.09.03

For landfill methane projects: landfill gas collection system with continuous metering of volumetric flow rate and CH4 concentration; monthly flow meter performance tests (±5% accuracy); daily methane concentration records; annual third-party methane composition verification; maintenance and calibration records required
For landfill methane projects: project must have commenced on or after December 20, 2005 and must not be required by law or regulation; cannot receive funding from Strategic Energy Investment Fund

For agricultural methane projects: monthly influent flow and composition monitoring; daily biogas flow rate measurement (15-minute intervals); weekly or daily methane concentration monitoring; quarterly third-party laboratory analysis; annual equipment calibration; comprehensive QA/QC program

For energy efficiency projects: baseline energy use documentation; professional engineer certification; ASHRAE Guideline 14-2002 and RESNET 2006 standards compliance; IPMVP guidelines; energy simulation modeling using BESTEST or RESNET certified software if applicable; QA/QC procedures; independent accredited verifier certification

For SF6 reduction projects: Entity-wide SF6 Inventory Tracking System; comprehensive baseline emissions calculations; cylinder-specific logs with certified scale weighing; documentation of SF6 procurement/disbursal; entity-wide QA/QC procedures; personnel contact information; service territory description with map; must commence on or after December 20, 2005; must not be required by law/regulation or judicial order; cannot include electric generation component used for renewable energy compliance; cannot receive Strategic Energy Investment Fund support; cannot receive credits under other mandatory/voluntary GHG programs; must include incremental actions beyond baseline year; must be consistent with IEC TR 61634 guidance; annual review of at least 10% of records for newly installed and retired equipment; calibrated meters and scales per manufacturer recommendations; periodic master sheet cylinder log reviews; annual emissions calculations review with identification of unusual changes; Entity-wide QA/QC training plan for SF6 inventory management; Original signature required on Statement of Truth, Accuracy, and Completeness

For reforestation projects: must not be required by law or regulation; project must not receive credits/allowances under other greenhouse gas programs; Forest Owner requirements under RGGI U.S. Forest Protocol; Natural Forest Management compliance (95%+ native species); reforestation land eligibility (less than 10% tree canopy for 10+ years OR significant disturbance removing 20%+ above-ground biomass); reversal risk rating assessment; conservation easement documentation if applicable; land ownership documentation (deeds/titles); reforestation eligibility demonstration; baseline modeling and forest growth projections using approved forest growth model; Monitoring and Verification Plan with inventory methodology, field measurements, plot documentation; no broadcast fertilization allowed; third-party forest certification if commercial harvesting occurs; accredited independent verifier review and certification required

For improved forest management projects: land with greater than 10% tree canopy cover; at least 95% native species in standing live carbon pool; species diversity compliance per Assessment Area Data File; sustainable management certification (FSC, SFI, Tree Farm System, or equivalent) or uneven-aged silvicultural practices with minimum 40% canopy retention; standing and lying dead wood retention; no broadcast fertilization; project commencement date documentation; reversal risk rating assessment; baseline modeling methodology and preliminary data; legal constraints documentation and financial feasibility analysis; comprehensive Monitoring and Verification Plan with inventory documentation, field measurements, and quality assurance procedures; accredited independent verifier certification and report

For avoided conversion projects: forest land with greater than 10% tree canopy cover; at least 95% native species composition; species diversity compliance per Assessment Area Data File; project must not be required by law, regulation, or administrative/judicial order; appraisal demonstrating alternative land use and conversion risk; conservation easement or alternative legal protections; no broadcast fertilization; reversal risk rating assessment; modeling plan using approved forest growth model; project baseline characterization with conversion rate estimates; baseline calculations with uncertainty discounts; harvested wood products carbon estimates; Monitoring and Verification Plan with project inventory documentation; sampling plot identification with maps and photos; field measurement documentation; forest management certification (ATFS, FSC, SFI or equivalent) if timber harvest occurs; quality assurance procedures documentation; independent verifier certification and report

For all project types: establishment of RGGI COATS general account; independent verifier report required; comprehensive Monitoring and Verification Plan required; approved forest growth model documentation for forest projects; baseline calculations with uncertainty discounts for forest projects; complete hardcopy original and electronic copy (CD disk) submission required for forest projects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a consistency application to MDE within the specified deadline for the project type (six months for most project types; one year for carbon sequestration projects). Establish RGGI COATS general account. Submit application with comprehensive project documentation including monitoring and verification plan, independent verifier report, baseline calculations, and project-specific technical documentation. An accredited independent verifier must verify the project according to COMAR 26.09.03 requirements. Ongoing annual Monitoring and Verification Reports required with third-party verification for the duration of the offset project. For reforestation, improved forest management, and avoided conversion projects, submit complete M&V Report (one paper hardcopy original and one electronic copy on CD) with all required forms across three parts: General Information Forms, Category-Specific Information Forms, and Independent Verification Form.

structured_extraction.program_name: SCATR Program (Source Collection And Threat Reduction Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial assistance to Maryland radioactive material licensees to help pay for the proper disposal of unwanted radioactive sealed sources. The program recognizes that disposal options are limited and expensive, and offers rare opportunities for licensees to receive funding support combined with their own contributions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides financial assistance (to be combined with licensee funds) to cover costs of packaging, transportation, and disposal of unwanted radioactive sealed sources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland radioactive material licensees with unwanted radioactive sealed sources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Packaging, transportation, and disposal of unwanted radioactive sealed sources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland only - program available to Maryland radioactive material licensees
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland radioactive material licensee
Must have unwanted radioactive sealed sources
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Radioactive material to be disposed of is identified and registered, outlets for the material are found, commitment for SCATR funds is obtained, a contract is made for packaging, transportation, and disposal, the material is moved to a collection point, and collection of the radioactive material is made for disposal. More information and registration instructions are available at the CRCPD website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A full-day, in-person training course that certifies individuals to construct sand mound sewage disposal systems in Maryland for a five-year period. The course covers design, permitting, and construction standards and requires passing a written examination.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, full-day in-person training course lasting 7.5 hours at MDE headquarters in Baltimore. Course covers design, permitting, and construction standards for sand mound sewage disposal systems. Passing a written examination is required to obtain certification, which is valid for five years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Courses offered annually, generally late winter and early spring. Registration dates vary.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Wastewater Permits Program, Onsite Systems Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking certification to construct sand mound sewage disposal systems in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification to install sand mound sewage disposal systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Training is conducted at MDE headquarters in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Complete full-day in-person training course
Pass written examination
Meet registration requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the course through the provided form. If registration is not open, fill out the Course Interest List form to be contacted when registration opens. Complete the full-day training course at MDE headquarters in Baltimore and pass the written examination to obtain certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: An online renewal course for individuals holding an active sand mound installer certification. The course provides updated information on sand mound construction and is required every five years to maintain certification.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Wastewater Permits Program, Onsite Systems Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals holding active sand mound installer certification seeking renewal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Continuing education and certification renewal for sand mound installation.

requirements_list: Hold current sand mound installer certification
Complete online course prior to certification expiration
Watch embedded video presentation
Answer 10 knowledge check questions

Enter required information into the form, watch the embedded video presentation, and answer the 10 knowledge check questions. The entire process takes approximately 2 hours. Upon completion, certification is renewed.

structured_extraction.program_name: School Bus Retrofit Technology Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: MDE developed this program to reduce harmful pollutants emitted from diesel engines in school buses and provide a cleaner and healthier commute for students. The program retrofits school buses with special engine control modules and diesel-oxidation catalysts to cut average child exposure to pollutants by as much as 50 percent.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDE awards funding to local school districts to retrofit school buses with diesel oxidation catalysts and engine control modules. For example, MDE awarded nearly $300,000 to Montgomery County Public Schools. Retrofitting costs range from $792 per bus for Caterpillar engines to $2,048 per bus for International engines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school districts and school bus systems in Maryland counties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retrofitting school buses with diesel oxidation catalysts and engine control modules to reduce emissions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and Anne Arundel County school systems

structured_extraction.program_description: Awards grants to schools to reduce food waste and establish composting programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded to schools for food waste reduction and composting program establishment.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reducing food waste and establishing composting programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.assistance_description: On-site pollution prevention technical assistance to hospitals, hotels, food processing facilities, minor league baseball stadiums, and other specific industry sectors. Projects supported by U.S. EPA Pollution Prevention grant funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A regulatory permit program that authorizes entities to engage in sewage sludge utilization activities including treatment, composting, transportation, storage, distribution, application on agricultural or marginal land, energy generation, incineration, marketing, innovative or research projects, or disposal at a municipal landfill. The program establishes standards for beneficial use and management of sewage sludge (biosolids) from wastewater treatment plants, including PFAS monitoring requirements for land application. The program also provides formula grants to counties to conduct supplemental inspections and monitoring of sewage sludge utilization sites under contracts with the Maryland Department of the Environment. The program also allows mixing facilities to accept and mix Class A sewage sludge with other materials under General Authorization issued under COMAR 26.04.06.09C(8). Sewage sludge application to land returns nutrients to soil, adds organic matter, and improves soil tillability and moisture retention.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program issues Sewage Sludge Utilization Permits to regulate and oversee the beneficial use and management of sewage sludge, and provides formula grants to counties for supplemental inspections and monitoring of sewage sludge utilization sites. For permit applicants, a performance bond or liability insurance is required based on the activity type, ranging from $10,000 for transportation to $125,000 for in-state sewage sludge treatment facilities. The permit authorizes specific utilization activities after regulatory review and approval. Permits require submission of multiple copies of applications (4-6 copies depending on permit type), environmental justice screening via MDEnviroScreen, and proof of workers' compensation coverage. Applicants must comply with COMAR 26.04.06 regulations and may be subject to PFAS monitoring requirements with application rate restrictions based on PFOS/PFOA concentration levels (≥100 µg/kg prohibits land application; 50-100 µg/kg limits to ≤1.5 dry tons per acre; 20-50 µg/kg limits to ≤3 dry tons per acre). The program also allows mixing facilities to accept and mix Class A sewage sludge with other approved materials under General Authorization. EPA Method 1633 must be used for PFAS testing, and notification to MDE within 30 days of sample results is required.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually; ongoing program with rolling applications; PFAS sampling requirements effective January 1, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entities that generate, treat, transport, distribute, market, or apply sewage sludge or biosolids in Maryland, including wastewater treatment plants, composting facilities, land application operators, waste management companies, county governments, for-profit businesses, individuals, municipalities, non-profits, agricultural operators, farmers, and sewage sludge mixing facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The permit governs the utilization of sewage sludge through treatment, composting, transportation, storage, distribution, application on agricultural land or marginal land, energy generation, incineration, marketing, innovative or research projects, or disposal at a municipal landfill. For mixing facilities, authorization to combine Class A sewage sludge with other approved materials. County funds are used for supplemental inspections and monitoring of sewage sludge utilization sites. Sewage sludge returns nutrients to soil, adds organic matter, and improves soil properties and soil tillability and moisture retention.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Applicants must provide site information including latitude and longitude coordinates, watershed code if known, state legislative district if known, and Maryland grid coordinates. Special requirements apply for Coastal Plain soils regarding soil pH management and manganese deficiency prevention. Maryland wastewater treatment plants; in-state and out-of-state biosolids sources. Agricultural land located on the Coastal Plain may have special considerations.
