structured_extraction.program_name: Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) Clean and Renewable Energy Application Fee Waiver
structured_extraction.program_description: Fee waiver for development and siting of clean or renewable energy projects on properties subject to Maryland's Voluntary Cleanup Program. Enacted through Chapter 544, Acts of 2020 and effective January 1, 2022. The waiver reduces application fees to encourage renewable energy development on degraded lands. Eligible developers qualify for fee reductions when certifying intention to use a property for clean or renewable energy generation. The standard VCP application fee is $6,000 for new projects or $2,000 for a subsequent application if there is an active VCP application in progress. By obtaining the fee waiver, developers avoid these application costs. The program also encourages investigation, cleanup, and redevelopment of eligible properties with known or perceived contamination, providing predictability and finality to cleanup efforts.

structured_extraction.program_name: WIIN Act Section 2107 Grant Program for Lead Remediation in Schools
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to assist local educational agencies with testing for and removing sources of lead in drinking water at schools. Funding covers expenses associated with materials and labor for lead remediation in school drinking water systems, with preference given to permanent or long-term remediation measures over short-term measures. The program provides reimbursement for completed remediation work or funding for proposed projects.

Permanent or long-term remediation measures are preferred over short-term measures. Reimbursement provided for completed projects with valid documentation; funding for proposed projects disbursed after work completion and documentation receipt. Projects must occur between November 15, 2021, and September 1, 2022. Funding may be used for reimbursement of completed work or for estimates of work to be completed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free training offered by the Department to learn about various aspects of the Wastewater Pollution Prevention and Reclamation Program and the wastewater permits issued by the program, including training specific to different permit types such as construction stormwater, industrial stormwater, swimming pools, pesticides, and seafood processing. Training covers stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPPs), erosion and sediment control (E&SC), operator responsibilities, permit triggers, compliance procedures, chemical additives, dewatering requirements, turbidity standards, corrective actions, SWPPP development, BMP implementation, and regulatory requirements.

Training covers General Permit for Discharges of Stormwater Associated With Construction Activity (20-CP), General Permit for Discharges from Stormwater Associated with Industrial Activities (20-SW), General Permit for Discharges from Swimming Pools and Spas (17-SI), General Discharge Permit for Discharges from the Application of Pesticides (17-PE), and General Permit for Discharges from Seafood Processing Facilities (21-SE). Training includes technical guidance on permit compliance, SWPPP development, BMP implementation, regulatory requirements, erosion and sediment control plans, and operator responsibilities. Participants can sign up for newsletter notifications of future training events.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water Quality Revolving Loan Fund provides below market rate of interest loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness to eligible entities for projects to protect or improve the quality of Maryland's rivers, streams, lakes, the Chesapeake Bay and other water resources. The program supports both point source and nonpoint source pollution prevention projects consistent with the Federal Clean Water Act and the Maryland Bay Restoration Fund Act, as well as low-interest loans for cleanup costs at eligible contaminated sites on the State Master List (State Superfund sites or CERCLIS NFRAP sites) or sites in the VCP where water quality is an issue. The program receives federal funding from the United States Environmental Protection Agency.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below market rate of interest revolving loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness to eligible borrowers for water quality improvement projects. Point source pollution prevention projects are available to public entities and local governments only and include wastewater treatment plant improvements, sewerage collection systems, infiltration/inflow correction, sludge handling facilities, landfill leachate pretreatment facilities, and drinking water treatment plant backwash facilities. Nonpoint source pollution prevention projects are available to public and private entities and include stormwater best management practices, wellhead protection, landfill closure, stream corridor restoration, hazardous waste cleanup, shoreline erosion control, agricultural nutrient management plans, and forestry financing. The program also provides low-interest loans to cover cleanup costs for approved remediation plans at eligible contaminated sites. Financial advisory services are available to assist applicants in determining affordable user rate structures and modeling fiscal impact of loans. The program receives federal funding from the United States Environmental Protection Agency.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water Quality Revolving Loan Fund provides financial assistance in the form of low interest rate loans and/or grant funding (including principal forgiveness) for projects to protect or improve the quality of Maryland's rivers, streams, lakes, the Chesapeake Bay and other water resources, consistent with the Federal Clean Water Act and the Maryland Bay Restoration Fund Act. The program supports both point source pollution prevention projects and nonpoint source pollution prevention projects, including water quality point source projects, drinking water projects, non-point source pollution control projects, septic system upgrade projects using best available technology for nitrogen removal, and cleanup costs at contaminated sites with water quality concerns. Point source pollution prevention projects are available to public entities and local governments only and include wastewater treatment plant improvements, sewerage collection systems, infiltration/inflow correction, sludge handling facilities, landfill leachate pretreatment facilities, and drinking water treatment plant backwash facilities. Between FY21 and FY23, the Bay Restoration Fund component provided $45 million in revenues for 2,567 Best Available Technology installations and 497 connections to public sewer. The program also provides funding and technical assistance for water conservation and restoration services to support water quality improvement projects. The program receives federal funding from the United States Environmental Protection Agency.

Credits can be used to meet NPDES permit requirements. Agricultural credits are certified through the Maryland Nutrient Tracking and Trading Tool (MNTT).

Grants up to 87.5% of total eligible project cost for water supply facilities, not to exceed $1.5 million per project, with a required 12.5% local match.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides grant and loan assistance to small communities and local governments for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly-owned water supply facilities, wellhead protection projects, and direct loans for land acquisition for source water protection. Funds up to 87.5% of total eligible project cost for water supply facilities, not to exceed $1.5 million per project. Requires a 12.5% local match, which may be funded through the Drinking Water Revolving Loan Fund. Applicants may receive a combination of State grant and Drinking Water Revolving Loan. Planning, engineering, and project administration costs are eligible for loans only. Funding priority is given to disadvantaged communities and communities that are non-compliant with drinking water standards. Applications are accepted in December through January each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December through January each year; applications will reopen in December 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small communities, local governments, and water supply systems in Maryland seeking to improve publicly-owned water supply facilities or protect source water
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly-owned water supply facilities including upgrades to water treatment facilities, well development, water storage tanks, water distribution facilities up to private property lines, consolidation of smaller water systems, wellhead protection projects, and land acquisition for source water protection
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; projects must conform to Smart Growth Criteria and be consistent with the County Water and Sewer Plan. Water supply facility projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area.
requirements_list: Must be a small community, local government, or water supply system
Priority given to disadvantaged communities
Priority given to communities non-compliant with drinking water standards
Project must be eligible under Federal Safe Drinking Water Act
Must conform to Smart Growth Criteria
Located in a Priority Funding Area
Consistent with the County Water and Sewer Plan
Must submit a water audit
Water systems serving a population greater than 10,000 must submit a water conservation plan
Applicants must have insufficient or limited financial capability
Local match required
Award not to exceed $1.5 million
Based on system size, compliance status, and affordability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted from December through January each year. Applications are currently closed and will reopen in December 2026. Projects are rated and ranked based on the requirements of Environment Article 9-423 and COMAR 26.03.09.06. Priority rankings are determined on the basis of project benefits to public health, compliance with regulations, safety, water system reliability, applicant financial capability, previous correction efforts, and community size.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Protection and Flood Prevention Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Technical and financial assistance provided in cooperation with local sponsoring organizations, state and other public agencies, to voluntarily plan and install watershed-based projects on private lands that address natural resource and related economic problems on a watershed basis. NRCS provides both technical and financial assistance for watershed projects. Cost sharing is available for acquiring perpetual easements on wetlands or floodplains for conservation or flood prevention, with federal funding of 50 percent or more.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NRCS provides both technical and financial assistance for watershed projects. Cost sharing is available for acquiring perpetual easements on wetlands or floodplains for conservation or flood prevention, with federal funding of 50 percent or more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local sponsoring organizations including Native American tribes, state or local governments, soil or water conservation districts, flood prevention or control districts, nonprofit water users associations, and similar organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Watershed protection, flood prevention, erosion and sediment control, water supply, water quality, fish and wildlife habitat enhancement, wetland creation and restoration, and public recreation in watersheds of 250,000 or fewer acres.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Watersheds of 250,000 acres or fewer
requirements_list: Eligible organizations must be able to carry out and maintain improvement projects
Projects must address natural resource and related economic problems on a watershed basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible local sponsoring organizations work through NRCS to plan and implement watershed projects on private lands on a voluntary basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to protect public drinking water supplies by managing the land surface around a well where activities might affect water quality. The program provides technical assistance, information, and funding to local governments to help them protect their water supplies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest loans are available for communities to purchase land or conservation easements within wellhead protection areas. Technical assistance is provided to help communities delineate wellhead protection areas, inventory contaminants, develop management strategies, and plan for emergencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and public water suppliers seeking to protect their drinking water supplies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to purchase land or conservation easements within wellhead protection areas to prevent contamination of public drinking water wells.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to all Maryland communities with public water supplies.
requirements_list: Communities must form a planning team representing local interests
Communities must delineate wellhead protection areas
Communities must inventory potential contamination sources
Communities must develop management strategies for the wellhead protection area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities should contact the Water Supply Program to request technical assistance. MDE can assist in delineating wellhead protection areas, provide lists of regulated activities, and help communities develop management programs. Communities can apply for zero percent interest loans to purchase land or conservation easements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program offering private and tribal landowners the opportunity to protect, restore, and enhance wetlands on their property. Landowners with previously degraded or drained wetlands can enroll under permanent, 30-year, or term easements or 30-year contracts. The USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service provides technical and financial support, including payment based on agricultural value and cost-share assistance for restoration. Landowner retains ownership, controls access, and may request compatible uses such as haying, grazing, or timber harvesting under certain conditions.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners receive payment based on the agricultural value of the land for wetlands that have been drained and converted to agricultural or timber production uses. Three options are available: permanent easements, 30-year easements, or term easements/10-year restoration cost-share agreements. Payment rates and cost-share assistance for wetland restoration vary by option. Landowner retains ownership, controls access, and may request compatible uses such as haying, grazing, or timber harvesting under certain conditions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private and tribal landowners with restorable wetlands or land suitable for wildlife benefits, particularly those with previously degraded agricultural wetlands
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Protection, restoration, and enhancement of wetlands and associated uplands on private or tribal land; wetland restoration costs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide program. In Maryland, statewide eligibility. Contact USDA Service Centers located in each county or the NRCS Annapolis Service Center.
requirements_list: For permanent or 30-year easements, landowner must have owned the land for at least one year prior to enrollment (limited exceptions apply)
For term easements or 10-year restoration cost-share agreements, landowner need only show evidence of ownership
Private or tribal land ownership
Land must be restorable and suitable for wildlife benefits
Previously degraded wetlands due to agricultural use
Ineligible lands include: federal land, wetlands converted after December 23, 1985, certain Conservation Reserve Program contract lands, and land where restoration is impossible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowner contacts local USDA Service Center to inquire about program or enrolls property through USDA under an easement or contract arrangement. Eligible landowners prepare and submit an application. Upon approval, landowner agrees to install and maintain wetland restoration practices and allow NRCS access to monitor effectiveness.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that provides technical assistance and cost-share payments to help establish and improve fish and wildlife habitat primarily on private lands. Participants develop and implement a wildlife habitat development plan with NRCS support.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NRCS provides technical assistance and pays up to 75 percent of the cost of installing wildlife habitat practices. Cost-share agreements generally last 5 to 10 years. Cost-share payments may be used to establish new practices or replace practices that fail for reasons beyond the landowner's control.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners or controllers of private land who want to develop and improve wildlife habitat
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishment and improvement of fish and wildlife habitat on private land
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All lands eligible except: federal land, land currently enrolled in Water Bank Program, Conservation Reserve Program, Wetlands Reserve Program, or similar programs, land subject to Emergency Watershed Protection Program floodplain easement, and land where USDA determines impacts make success unlikely.
requirements_list: Participant must own or have control of the land
Land cannot be federal land
Land cannot be currently enrolled in Water Bank Program, Conservation Reserve Program, Wetlands Reserve Program, or similar programs
Land cannot be subject to Emergency Watershed Protection Program floodplain easement
WHIP funds cannot be used for mitigation or on land designated as converted wetland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowner contacts local NRCS office. NRCS helps participant prepare a wildlife habitat development plan in consultation with the local conservation district. Plan describes landowner's goals, lists practices and installation schedule, and details maintenance steps. USDA and participant enter into a cost-share agreement for wildlife habitat development.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant funding provided under Section 319(h) of the Clean Water Act to support nonpoint source pollution management and water quality restoration projects in Maryland. The program provides financial assistance for the implementation of best management practices, outreach initiatives, planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of projects that address and reduce nonpoint source pollution entering the state's waterways. Funds support projects that reduce or eliminate water quality impairments associated with nonpoint source pollution, particularly in watersheds where Total Maximum Daily Loads have been approved. The program is aligned with the Chesapeake Bay Agreement, Chesapeake Bay TMDL, and Maryland's Phase III Watershed Implementation Plan, focusing on reducing nitrogen, phosphorus, sediment, and other pollutants. Applications are submitted through an annual Request for Proposals (RFP) process released in Spring with a Summer submission deadline.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-style federal grant funding to support nonpoint source management projects and water quality restoration initiatives. Financial assistance is provided for planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of projects that reduce or eliminate water quality impairments listed on Maryland's List of Impaired Waters or addressed in Total Maximum Daily Loads. Funds support implementing best management practices (BMPs) and outreach/education initiatives to reduce nonpoint source pollution and result in quantifiable or measurable improvements in water quality and habitat, including pollutant load reductions for nitrogen, phosphorus, sediment, bacteria, chloride, PCBs, temperature, and trash. Typical grant range is $30,000 to $400,000 with approximately $1 million available annually. A Request for Proposals (RFP) is released annually with submission deadlines. Recipients must produce funding first before receiving grant reimbursement. Reimbursement is provided quarterly upon submission of invoices for satisfactory deliverables.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FFY27 RFP opens July 1, 2026; FFY26 RFP closed. FFY25 RFP submission deadline September 30, 2025 by 11:59 PM EST; early submissions encouraged.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local and state entities including county and municipal agencies, Soil Conservation Districts, state agencies, state institutions of higher learning, private firms, and nonprofit organizations working on nonpoint source pollution management and water quality restoration in Maryland. Eligible organizations include watershed partners, communities in watersheds with EPA-accepted watershed plans, agricultural operators, urban/suburban property owners, and municipalities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nonpoint source pollution management and water quality restoration projects including planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis. Funds support implementation of best management practices such as nutrient management, tillage management, cover crops, pasture management, forest buffers, wetland restoration and creation, stream and riparian restoration, stormwater management infrastructure, septic system improvements, agricultural drainage management, animal waste management systems, erosion and sediment control, urban forestry, and living shorelines. Funds also support technical assistance, outreach and education efforts, watershed-based plan development, and training programs. Cannot fund staff salaries already paid by §319(h) or other sources or activities required by NPDES, MS4, or CAFO permits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Projects must be located in watersheds with EPA-accepted nine-element watershed-based plans or have a waiver approved upon request. §319 Priority Watersheds with approved A-I plans include: Antietam Creek, Assawoman Bay, Back River (Tidal and Upper), Casselman River, Choptank River (Upper), Corsica River, Gwynns Falls (Middle), Jennings Run (Upper), Jones Falls (Lower), Monocacy River (Lower), Sassafras River, Spring Branch, and other approved watersheds. Approximately 95% of Maryland land is part of the eligible Chesapeake Bay watershed.
requirements_list: Project must reduce or eliminate water quality impairments listed on Maryland's List of Impaired Waters or addressed in Total Maximum Daily Loads
Project must result in quantifiable or measurable improvements in water quality and habitat
Project must address impairments identified in Total Maximum Daily Loads or on the 303(d) List
For implementation projects involving in-the-ground construction, a watershed plan must be EPA-accepted nine-element plan or waiver approved
Applicant must demonstrate capacity in grant management and funding
Project managers must have the capacity to produce funding prior to receiving reimbursement
Projects must be located within a §319 Priority Watershed with an EPA-approved watershed plan for implementation projects
Applicants must provide justification of their capacity in grant management and funding
Watershed must have an approved A-I Watershed Plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through a Request for Proposals (RFP) process released annually. The FFY25 RFP has a submission deadline of September 30, 2025 by 11:59 PM EST, with early submissions encouraged. The next RFP for FFY27 funding will open on July 1, 2026. FFY26 RFP is closed. Applicants must include justification of their capacity in grant management and funding. MDE may request additional documentation or provide oversight to ensure project completion. Successful applicants receive quarterly reimbursement of invoices for satisfactory deliverables. Technical assistance and guidance are available from MDE and partner agencies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund Financial Hardship Exemption Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program that allows eligible residential dwellers to request exemption or reduction from Bay Restoration Fund fees (flush tax) when demonstrating substantial financial hardship. The program is administered through local billing authorities statewide, with individual county implementations such as Allegany County and Calvert County establishing their own financial hardship exemption programs subject to Maryland Department of the Environment approval. The State of Maryland established the Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fund to support bay restoration efforts. Exemptions are granted for a specified time period not to exceed one year and require annual reapplication for continued consideration.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of the Environment and local billing authorities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential users meeting financial hardship criteria are exempted from or receive a reduction in the Bay Restoration Fee. Exemptions are granted for a specified time period not to exceed one year without re-verification of eligibility. Applicants must meet at least two of the following conditions: receiving energy assistance subsidy, receiving public assistance (supplemental security income or food stamps), receiving veterans or social security disability benefits, or meeting income criteria established by the Maryland Department of Human Services Office of Home Energy Programs. Annual reapplication is required for continued consideration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual application; exemption granted for one year at a time
structured_extraction.contact_name: Director, Maryland Water Quality Financing Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential water utility customers who demonstrate substantial financial hardship and are subject to Bay Restoration Fund fees; includes homeowners and lease holders
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from or reduction of Bay Restoration Fund fees on water bills to support Chesapeake Bay restoration efforts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide through local billing authorities. Allegany County and Calvert County serve as example implementation locations.
requirements_list: Must be a residential dwelling
Must be homeowner or lease holder of record
Must demonstrate substantial financial hardship by meeting at least two of the specified conditions
Must provide required supporting documentation for eligibility determination
Completion of the Bay Restoration Fund Financial Hardship Exemption Application
New application required every year for continued consideration
Must reapply if exemption period expires
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Billing authorities establish their own financial hardship exemption programs and submit proposed plans to the Maryland Department of the Environment for approval. Individual residential users then apply through their local billing authority using the procedures and forms established by that authority. Applicants complete the Bay Restoration Fund Financial Hardship Exemption Application and submit it to their local tax and utility office or county treasurer. The billing authority determines eligibility and grants exemptions. A new application must be submitted annually for continued consideration.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Business Ready Sites Program promotes site readiness as a direct pathway to economic competitiveness in the state. Created by Executive Order on December 19, 2024, the program enhances Maryland's industrial and commercial infrastructure by identifying and improving potential development sites. The program accelerates investment by providing financial support to defray the costs of site characterization and site improvements, and provides collaborative marketing support to grow an inventory of shovel-ready sites across the state for industrial and commercial development. The program offers three pillars of support: Site Characterization Grants providing in-kind services totaling up to $10,000 to assess the readiness of a potential site and assign it a Ready Score; Site Improvement Grants supporting infrastructure development, environmental remediation, and site development needs with grant amounts ranging from $125,000 to $450,000 in FY 2026, requiring a 3:1 or higher match; and Collaborative Marketing Support assisting local jurisdictions and the State with marketing sites through publication in the MBRSP Sites Dashboard and Site Characterization Reports.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers three pillars of support: (1) Site Characterization Grants providing up to $10,000 to offset costs of retaining a site development professional to assess the readiness of a potential site and assign it a Ready Score, requiring a 1:1 cash match from any source; (2) Site Improvement Grants supporting infrastructure development, environmental remediation, and site development needs with grant amounts ranging from $125,000 to $450,000 in FY 2026, requiring a 3:1 or higher match from all sources; and (3) Collaborative Marketing Support assisting local jurisdictions and the State with marketing sites through publication in the MBRSP Sites Dashboard and Site Characterization Reports.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis with priority cycle in May each year. Applications submitted in May receive notification by July 1; applications submitted June 1 or later receive notification within 60 days.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public sector entities including counties, municipalities, authorities, and economic development authorities; private sector entities that own or have development rights to eligible sites aligned with Maryland's growth industries and emerging sectors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Site characterization through third-party professional assessment by site selection professionals and engineering firms to evaluate development status and potential; site improvements including infrastructure upgrades, environmental remediation, due diligence studies (geotechnical engineering, final site engineering, grading plans, rail studies, traffic studies), and other site development improvements necessary to make sites competitive for industrial or commercial use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland for eligible sites that are greenfields, brownfields, or redevelopment sites in a pre-development phase with a minimum of 5 acres intended solely for industrial or commercial purposes aligned with county/municipality economic development goals and Maryland's growth industries.
requirements_list: Site must be at least 5 acres
Site must be a greenfield, brownfield, or redevelopment site in pre-development phase
Site must be intended for solely industrial or commercial purposes
Site must be intended to be occupied primarily by private sector companies in industries specified in the MBRSP Program Guidelines
Site must not be otherwise restricted from further development
Applicant must own or have development rights to the land; evidence of title or option to purchase required
Site must align with county/municipality economic development goals
Connection to Maryland's growth industries or jurisdiction-specific industries of focus required
Applicant must provide detailed site history and information
For Site Characterization Grants, a 1:1 cash match from any source is required
For Site Improvement Grants, a 3:1 or 4:1 match funding from all sources is required
Documentation of ownership required for approval
Utility infrastructure must be adequate for target industrial users
Due diligence studies required (environmental, geotechnical, wetlands, surveys, etc.)
Letters of support from county/municipal governments may be required
Detailed project budget with timelines and deliverables required
Applicant must agree to conditions outlined in the MBRSP Program Guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit completed application form with site and applicant information, required appendices, and supporting documentation to MEDCO. MEDCO conducts a collaborative review process and corresponds with applicants for additional documents as needed. MEDCO provides required specifications and guidelines to contractors. Submitted applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with priority consideration for May submissions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIF) Capital Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Capital grants that help organizations acquire, plan, design, add technology to, furnish, and refurbish secure work environments (SCIFs) that meet federal security standards for classified information handling. These facilities support the development and construction of secure facilities for security-cleared professionals and mission-critical work, helping Maryland retain skilled workers with security clearances and support national security needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEDCO awards capital grants to help recipients acquire, plan, design, add technology to, furnish, and refurbish SCIF spaces for capital projects and construction. The program has awarded $5 million to date across five regional projects. For every dollar invested in SCIF space, an additional two to three dollars of private, nonprofit, or government match funding is typically generated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations needing to develop or improve secure facilities for handling classified information.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring, planning, designing, purchasing technology for, furnishing, and refurbishing SCIF spaces; capital projects for SCIF construction and development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland regions.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with MEDCO as the program administrator to apply for grant funding through the Maryland Department of General Services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financing program that makes targeted investments into real estate and infrastructure projects that support transformative placemaking, transit-oriented development, community development, and inclusive and equitable economic growth objectives. The fund fills gaps in residential, commercial, mixed-use, and light industrial projects with flexible financing terms.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible term loans intended to fill gaps in financing for real estate and infrastructure projects. Uses may include acquisition of property or vacant sites, design and development, infrastructure improvements, and other costs associated with new construction, adaptive reuse, or extensive rehabilitation of residential, commercial, mixed-use, and light industrial projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and organizations undertaking real estate and infrastructure projects that support community development and economic growth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of property or vacant sites, design and development, infrastructure improvements, and costs associated with new construction, adaptive reuse, or extensive rehabilitation of residential, commercial, mixed-use, and light industrial projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within a Maryland Sustainable Community, Priority Funding Area, or Transit Oriented Development zone.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a Maryland Sustainable Community, Priority Funding Area, or Transit Oriented Development
Priority consideration for projects that activate underutilized government or institutionally owned property
Priority consideration for projects with significant development or redevelopment value
Priority consideration for projects that leverage private investment
Priority consideration for projects with significant job creation or retention potential

structured_extraction.program_description: Following a Presidentially declared disaster, the Individual Assistance Program assists individuals who are experiencing difficulties post-disaster through grants to eligible households for housing and other disaster-related needs when they are denied low-interest loans from the Small Business Administration and their insurance does not provide sufficient coverage.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Individuals and Households Program (IHP) component provides grants to eligible households for Housing Assistance (HA) and/or Other Needs Assistance (ONA). Housing Assistance includes temporary housing payments, repairs up to the IHP maximum, home replacement in rare conditions up to the IHP maximum, or semi-permanent or permanent housing construction in very unusual situations. Other Needs Assistance covers medical and dental expenses, funeral and burial costs, replacement of clothing and household items, specialized tools, educational materials, clean-up items, fuel for primary heat, vehicle repair or transportation costs, moving and storage expenses, and other necessary expenses or serious needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and households experiencing difficulties following a Presidentially declared disaster who have been denied Small Business Administration disaster loans and lack sufficient insurance coverage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing repairs and replacement, temporary housing, home construction, medical and dental expenses, funeral and burial costs, clothing and household item replacement, educational materials, clean-up items, fuel, vehicle repair or transportation, moving and storage, and other necessary disaster-related expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Maryland following a Presidentially declared disaster.
requirements_list: Disaster must be Presidentially declared
Household must be denied or ineligible for Small Business Administration disaster loans
Homeowners or flood insurance must not provide sufficient coverage
If home is in a Special Flood Hazard Area, homeowner must comply with flood insurance purchase requirements and local flood codes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals experiencing post-disaster difficulties should contact FEMA for information on how to apply and receive Individual Assistance benefits following a Presidentially declared disaster in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps eligible low-income households afford heating costs and make energy efficiency improvements to their homes, such as insulation, weather stripping, and caulking.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help pay heating costs and support home weatherization improvements for eligible low-income households.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households that cannot afford heating costs or home insulation improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heating costs and home weatherization improvements including insulation, weather stripping, and caulking.
requirements_list: Low income eligibility

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that provides funding for physical security enhancements, security-related activities, emergency response planning, and threat assessments to nonprofit organizations at high risk of terrorist or other extremist attacks, hate crimes, or other violence, including faith-based facilities, houses of worship, and schools. The program aims to integrate the preparedness activities of nonprofit organizations with broader state and local preparedness efforts and helps organizations enhance their security measures and emergency preparedness. In Montgomery County and Prince George's County, organizations apply through the National Capital Region via the District of Columbia, while state area and Baltimore Urban Area nonprofits apply directly through Maryland MDEM.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants providing funding for physical security enhancements, security-related activities, emergency response planning, and threat assessments. For FY2025, organizations can apply for a maximum of six locations total per nonprofit organization with no more than three locations in either NSGP-UA (Urban Area) or NSGP-S (State funding), and a maximum of $200,000 per location, not to exceed $600,000 total per state. The program provides up to $150,000 in funding towards meeting an organization's physical security needs. There is no cost share requirement for FY2025. Funds are distributed on a reimbursement basis only, not as advance funding. Eligible uses include facility hardening projects, physical and cybersecurity enhancements, contracted security services, project management and administration (if approved in the original application), classroom-based training, exercises, purchase of mobile and portable equipment, security systems, communication tower construction, and modification/renovation of existing buildings. Projects under $250,000 are exempt from Buy America domestic content procurement preference requirements. Funds cannot be used for procurement or operation of covered foreign unmanned aircraft systems per the American Security Drone Act and Executive Order 14305.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The NSGP application period is currently closed; interested applicants should register to receive the Office of Grants Management's newsletter to learn more about application procedures and reopening dates.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations described under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code that are exempt from tax under section 501(a), including private institutions of higher learning designated as 501(c)(3) entities, faith-based facilities, houses of worship, schools, and other facilities at high risk of terrorist or other extremist attacks, hate crimes, or other violence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical security enhancements, security-related activities, emergency response planning, threat assessments, and other measures to prevent, protect against, prepare for, and respond to terrorist or other extremist attacks, hate crimes, and other violence. Eligible uses include facility hardening projects, physical and cybersecurity enhancements, contracted security services, project management and administration (if approved in the original application), classroom-based training, exercises, purchase of mobile and portable equipment, security systems, communication tower construction, and modification/renovation of existing buildings. Funds cannot be used for procurement or operation of covered foreign unmanned aircraft systems per the American Security Drone Act and Executive Order 14305.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations in Montgomery County and Prince George's County must apply through the National Capital Region via the District of Columbia. State area and Baltimore Urban Area nonprofits apply directly through Maryland MDEM. Jurisdictions are divided into three categories: State Area Funding (16 counties), Baltimore Urban Area Funding (7 jurisdictions including Baltimore City and Baltimore County), and National Capital Region Urban Area Funding (Montgomery and Prince George's Counties). Maryland statewide coverage available.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit facility
Organization must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit exempt from federal income tax
Organization must be at high risk of terrorist or other extremist attack, hate crimes, or other violence
Must be a faith-based facility, house of worship, or school
Vulnerability assessment must be conducted within the last two years by a local law enforcement agency, security company, or CISA (for houses of worship, self-assessment permitted)
Organization must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) prior to receiving an award (not required at application)
Organization must submit investment justification form
Organization must provide mission statement on letterhead
Subapplicants and subrecipients must submit short bios and resumes including type of entity, organizational leadership, and board members with names and addresses, subject to approval
Organization must declare whether work or mission involves supporting aliens
Organization must declare whether organization has any DEI practices
Foreign nationals or noncitizens must not be included or must be properly vetted and adhere to government statutes, policies, and procedures
Proposed projects must address a National Priority Area (NPA) and align with stated NOFO objectives
Environmental and Historic Preservation (EHP) screening required for most projects before work begins
All documents must be submitted as PDFs in one email
Organizations must obtain W-9 form completed and submitted
Compliance with Executive Order 14305: Restoring American Airspace Sovereignty
Prohibition on use of covered foreign unmanned aircraft systems
Adherence to Uniform Guidance (2 C.F.R. Part 200) for federal awards
For subject programs: all iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials must be produced in the United States (except for projects under $250,000)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations must submit a complete application packet via email to nsgp.mdem@maryland.gov in PDF format. Applications are submitted through Grants.gov. Required documents include: (1) Investment Justification form downloaded and opened from the applicant's computer; (2) Vulnerability Assessment conducted within the last two years; (3) Organization's mission statement on letterhead; (4) Short bios and resumes for subapplicants and subrecipients with names and addresses; (5) W-9 form; (6) UEI if available; and (7) Environmental and Historic Preservation screening form. All documents must be delivered as PDFs in a single email. The Investment Justification is the principal application document and must be supported by the organization's Mission Statement and Vulnerability Assessment. Resources available include application checklists, grant writing tips, and investment justification checklist. MDEM screens and scores applications, then submits to FEMA. Successful applicants must attend a mandatory Subrecipient Grant Award Briefing. Interested applicants should register to receive the Office of Grants Management's newsletter to learn more about application procedures. During the grant period, organizations submit quarterly status reports and may request reimbursement for approved expenses with proper documentation. MDEM reviews and approves subrecipient applications for program criteria including technical feasibility, cost effectiveness, and Environmental and Historic Preservation review.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides federal grant assistance to state and local governments and certain private nonprofit organizations for response and recovery activities following a presidentially-declared disaster. Established under the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act, the program covers repair, replacement, or restoration of disaster-damaged publicly owned and uninsured facilities at a 75% federal and 25% applicant grant share ratio to alleviate the financial burden on applicants. The program covers debris removal, emergency protective measures, and permanent restoration of damaged facilities including roads, bridges, water control facilities, buildings, equipment, utilities, and parks/recreational facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding provided at 75% federal and 25% applicant cost-share ratio for repair, replacement, or restoration of disaster-damaged publicly owned and uninsured facilities. Covers labor, equipment, materials, contract costs, and management costs up to 5% for subrecipients and up to 7% for state recipients. Hazard mitigation improvements (Section 406) available to protect against future similar damage. Applicants must apply through the FEMA Grants Portal.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 30 days after disaster designation or Public Assistance Briefing
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sara Bender, State Public Assistance Officer; Nora Lagola, State Public Assistance Officer; John Harding, Deputy Public Assistance Officer
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local governments, counties, municipalities, cities, towns, townships, local public authorities, school districts, special districts, federally recognized tribal governments, and certain private nonprofit organizations (critical service facilities such as educational facilities, power utilities, water facilities, sewer/wastewater treatment, telephone service, emergency services, hospitals, and custodial care facilities; non-critical service facilities such as museums, zoos, community centers, libraries, homeless shelters, senior centers, and rehabilitation facilities) in Maryland affected by a presidentially-declared disaster.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Debris removal from public roads and rights of way; emergency protective measures including sheltering, evacuation, and temporary facilities; restoration of roads, bridges, water control facilities, buildings, equipment, and vehicles; utility system restoration; parks and recreational facility restoration; hazard mitigation measures; management and administrative costs for program administration and preliminary damage assessments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide for areas designated through Presidential Major Disaster or Emergency Declaration. Specific counties and jurisdictions determined by FEMA disaster declaration.
requirements_list: Presidentially-declared disaster must be in effect
Facility must be publicly owned or eligible private nonprofit facility with 501(c), (d), or (e) tax-exempt status
Facility damage must be disaster-related
Facility must be uninsured or underinsured
Applicants must provide a 25% cost share

Work must eliminate immediate threat to lives, public health, and safety OR eliminate threats of significant damage to improved public/private property OR ensure economic recovery OR mitigate risk through hazard mitigation
Request for Public Assistance (RPA) must be filed within 30 days from disaster designation
Applicant must designate an authorized agent as point of contact
Compliance with 2 CFR Part 200 (Uniform Guidance)
Contracts must be competitively bid and comply with local, State, and Federal contracting/procurement regulations
Documentation required including force account labor hours, equipment use information, GPS locations, contract details, and insurance policies
Entities expending $750,000+ in Federal awards must conduct single or program-specific audit
Record retention: 3 years from closeout date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants are encouraged to create accounts on the FEMA Grants Portal before a disaster declaration occurs. During a declared disaster event, applicants complete an Initial Damage Assessment Form and Impact Statement Form. Subrecipients must submit a Request for Public Assistance (RPA) at the Applicant's Briefing or no later than 30 days after disaster designation. Applicants then submit damage assessment information, insurance details, and necessary documentation through the portal. Contact information and supporting documents can be added and updated through the portal throughout the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal revolving loan fund authorized by the STORM Act (Safeguarding Tomorrow through Ongoing Risk Mitigation Act) that provides low-interest loans to local governments to finance hazard mitigation projects that reduce the negative effects of natural and human-caused hazards in Maryland. Local governments can apply on behalf of homeowners, businesses, nonprofit organizations, and communities. The program funds projects addressing floods, storms, erosion, wildfires, and other natural hazards, as well as low-impact development, conservation areas, floodplain reconnection, building code adoption, zoning and land use planning, stormwater management, and non-federal cost-share requirements for hazard mitigation grants. The program prioritizes serving underserved and economically disadvantaged communities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest revolving loans provided to local governments. Standard loans have interest rates of up to 1% with 20-year amortization. Loans to economically challenged areas feature reduced interest rates of 0.05% with 30-year amortization periods, with administrative fees waived for second-year loans. Funds can be used by local governments on behalf of homeowners, businesses, nonprofit organizations, and communities for disaster mitigation projects, low-impact development, wildland-urban interface management, conservation areas, floodplain reconnection and open space projects, building code adoption, zoning and land use planning, stormwater management, infrastructure resilience, and to meet non-federal cost-share requirements for hazard mitigation grants. Projects must address natural hazards including floods, snowstorms, tornadoes, extreme heat, severe storms, storm surges, high water levels, shoreline erosion, drought, wildfires, and earthquakes. Loan repayments begin one year after funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline stated; rolling program with ongoing applications; NOI and application links remain available year-round on MDEM's RLF webpage
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments in Maryland who can apply on behalf of homeowners, businesses, nonprofit organizations, and communities, with a priority goal of serving underserved and economically disadvantaged communities. Target audiences include local government officials, emergency managers, and public works, transportation, environmental, sustainability, planning, resilience, and floodplain managers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that mitigate effects of natural hazards including floods, snowstorms, tornadoes, extreme heat, severe storms, storm surges, high water levels, shoreline erosion, drought, wildfires, and earthquakes. Also funds low-impact development, wildland-urban interface management, conservation areas, floodplain reconnection and open space projects, building code adoption, zoning and land use planning, stormwater management and pond improvements, floodplain restoration, infrastructure resilience projects, and projects supporting critical national infrastructure (ports, power, water distribution, bridges, waterways). Non-federal cost-share requirements for HMGP, FMA, and BRIC grants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available to all local governments in Maryland. Economically challenged geographic areas receive prioritized and amplified consideration, including areas such as Crisfield in Somerset County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government
A presidential disaster declaration is not required
Participation in the National Flood Insurance Program is not required
Designed to be accessible to Maryland's underserved and economically challenged communities
Local government must have FEMA-approved Hazard Mitigation Plan
Legislative body must pass resolution identifying dedicated revenue source for loan repayment
Projects must comply with Environmental and Historic Preservation (EHP) requirements and NEPA
Underwriting process required to demonstrate ability to repay
Projects must comply with 42 U.S.C. §5135 and Maryland Public Safety §14-110.4
Projects must align with NOFO requirements and Maryland's Hazard Mitigation Plan goals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should express interest using the online form provided on MDEM's RLF webpage or submit a Notice of Intent (NOI). Projects undergo underwriting to assess repayment ability and are ranked based on federal and state prioritization criteria. Contact the Hazard Mitigation team for more information about the application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program designed to help states, local governments, rural areas, and territories address cybersecurity risks and threats to information systems. The program directs strategic investments to enhance the cybersecurity posture of government agencies and bolster the protection of critical infrastructure and essential public services. Funds support adoption and enhancement of cybersecurity best practices, policy and governance development, operational technology security improvements, and workforce development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The SLCGP is a reimbursement-based grant program. Eligible state agencies and local governments can submit approved grant project-related expenses for reimbursement. Funding supports five project categories: (1) adoption/enhancement of priority cybersecurity best practices (Asset Discovery & Vulnerability Management, MFA, EDR, Email Security, Security Awareness Training); (2) adoption/enhancement of general cybersecurity best practices; (3) cybersecurity policy and governance development; (4) addressing specific jurisdictional cybersecurity needs; (5) cybersecurity workforce development. Subrecipients must submit complete documentation demonstrating allowable purchases directly related to the scope of work from their approved proposal, including proof of purchase and proof of payment. Allowable costs include personnel costs and fringe benefits, travel expenses, equipment (including maintenance, warranty, licenses, repairs, upgrades), supplies, contractual services, training and exercises, planning activities, and management and administration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling deadline - projects accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. Application opens February 2026. Project completion deadline: September 30, 2027. Letters of Intent must be submitted within 30 days of approval notification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, local governments, rural areas, municipalities, school districts, special districts, councils of governments, regional/interstate government entities, and other public entities seeking to address cybersecurity risks and enhance their cybersecurity posture.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support cybersecurity technology adoption and enhancement including asset discovery, vulnerability management, multi-factor authentication (MFA), endpoint detection and response (EDR), email security, security awareness training, firewalls, enhanced logging, data encryption, end-of-life software/hardware replacement, system backup and recovery capabilities, and migration to .gov domain. Also supports cybersecurity policy and governance development, operational technology security improvements, and workforce development addressing specific jurisdictional cybersecurity gaps. Allowable uses include personnel costs and fringe benefits, travel expenses, equipment, supplies, contractual services, training and exercises, planning activities, and management and administration. All budget costs must be necessary to implement project objectives and accomplish project goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland state agencies and local governments are eligible. Eight FEMA-defined rural counties receive priority funding weighting: Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, and Worcester. Additional Maryland-defined rural communities may qualify with evidence of rural status. The Maryland State Cybersecurity Planning Committee prioritizes and approves projects based on state cybersecurity priorities.
requirements_list: Must register for the Cyber Hygiene (CyHy) service (one-time requirement)
Must complete the Nationwide Cybersecurity Review (NCSR) annually
Must submit Quarterly Status Reports (QSRs) with financial and programmatic information until project completion
Must have a signed Subrecipient Agreement (SRA) contract in place before starting project
Must receive FEMA approval notification from MDEM before beginning work
Must submit a Letter of Intent to Accept or Reject Funding within 30 days of approval
Must obtain a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) in SAM.gov (current requirement for successful applicants)
Must be registered in SAM (System for Award Management) with valid UEI number
Municipalities and local health departments must submit W-9 form
Cannot have suspended, excluded, or ineligible status for federal assistance
Must follow all federal and state compliance requirements including proper reporting and documentation
Must retain copies of quarterly reports and supporting documentation for at least 3 years after project completion
Must comply with Section 504 of Rehabilitation Act (accessibility/non-discrimination)
Must integrate needs of individuals with disabilities into projects
Applications must use provided budget narrative and project proposal templates
Must submit detailed line-item budget with budget justification explaining necessity of budget cost elements to project implementation
Rural applicants outside FEMA definition must submit evidence of rural status (planning/zoning designation or mapping)
Must demonstrate testing ability to reconstitute system backups within planned recovery objectives
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review informational guidance documents including the Funding Guide, Project Application & Budget Narrative Instruction Manual, and FAQs. 2. Ensure you have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) or apply for one at SAM.gov. 3. Download and complete the FFY2023 application documents: the Subgrant Project Proposal Application, Additional Application Documents Packet (including Budget Narrative, Appendix A: Cybersecurity Capabilities Assessment, and Appendix E: Measurable Milestones), and Form W-9 if applicable. 4. Prepare detailed line-item budget with budget justification explaining necessity of cost elements and how they relate to project implementation and goals. 5. Email completed forms to slcgp.grant@maryland.gov with subject line formatted as: FY[funding year] SLCGP - [Subrecipient name] - [Project title] Application Forms. 6. The Maryland State Cybersecurity Planning Committee reviews and scores applications based on established criteria. 7. Committee submits approved project proposals to FEMA. 8. FEMA approves or rejects projects. 9. If approved, you receive approval notification from MDEM and must sign the Subrecipient Agreement. 10. Submit a Letter of Intent to Accept or Reject Funding within 30 days to slcgp.grant@maryland.gov. 11. Upon full execution of the SRA, you may begin work and submit reimbursement requests within 90 days of expenditure.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Burning Wood and Pellet Stove Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Rebate program that has been in operation for nine years providing financial incentives for clean burning wood and pellet stoves. The program provides rebates to Maryland homeowners to purchase and install clean burning wood or pellet stoves at their primary residence. Rebates are offered for stoves that displace electric, non-natural gas fossil fuel heating systems, or old wood or pellet stoves. Awards are made on a first-come, first-served basis. The program is coming to an end.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates of $500 for EPA-certified wood burning stoves or $700 for EPA-certified pellet burning stoves. Stoves must meet EPA emissions limits and have an EPA-published Higher Heating Value efficiency rating of at least 75% to qualify. Wood burning stoves must not exceed 3.0 grams of particulate matter per hour and pellet burning stoves must not exceed 2.0 grams of particulate matter per hour.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Stoves must be purchased by December 1, 2023. All eligible stoves must be purchased by January 4, 2024 and all systems installed and applications received by MEA or postmarked by March 31, 2024, unless the Program Budget is exhausted prior to this date.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of clean burning wood or pellet stoves that displace electric, non-natural gas fossil fuel heating systems, or old wood or pellet stoves.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: State of Maryland only

Stove must be installed at primary place of residence
Wood burning stoves must not exceed 3.0 grams of particulate matter per hour
Pellet burning stoves must not exceed 2.0 grams of particulate matter per hour

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Solar Low-to-Moderate Income Power Purchase Agreement Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to Community Solar Subscriber Organizations and income-qualified Marylanders to access solar power through community solar projects. The program enables Community Solar Subscriber Organizations approved by the Maryland Public Service Commission to offset costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements (PPA), allowing clean energy to be offered to low-income households at lower cost. The FY26 program focuses on Low-Income households (≤200% federal poverty level or certified eligible for federal/state/local assistance programs). Two Areas of Interest are offered: AOI-1 for subscribing low-income households to community solar projects (requiring minimum 15% of energy output to low-income subscribers with 25% cost savings), and AOI-2 for developing solar projects on landfills/brownfields benefiting low-income residents (providing 50% at no cost plus 25% savings on remaining energy to low-income subscribers). The grants help community solar subscriber organizations offer lower subscription rates to low-income households and increase their participation, while also promoting access to solar energy for individuals who rent their homes or cannot install solar panels on their own properties, helping them reduce energy costs. Projects must guarantee savings over 20 years to low-income subscribers. The program offers competitive grant funding and incentives to maximize value to low-income subscribers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding totaling approximately $17 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund using Solar Alternative Compliance Payment funding to offset costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements for Community Solar Subscriber Organizations and to enable income-qualified Marylanders to access community solar projects and reduce energy costs. Initial funding is $5 million for AOI-1 and $12 million for AOI-2. At the agency's discretion, funding from other sources with varying restrictions may also be possible. AOI-1 provides monetary incentives to developers who subscribe low-income households to community solar projects, with minimum 15% of energy output to low-income subscribers at 25% cost savings. AOI-2 provides monetary incentives for solar projects on landfills/brownfields, offering 50% energy at no cost plus 25% savings on remaining energy to low-income subscribers. Grants are reimbursed upon project completion and operational status. Final grant amount is recalculated based on actual project capacity (kW-dc) and actual percentage of energy provided to low-income subscribers. Funds support solar photovoltaic (PV) array installation, project development costs, interconnection wiring costs, permits, inspections, and commissioning tests. Grant disbursement is tied to project milestones and production of creditable power. Incentives are designed to provide maximum value to low-income community solar subscribers.

Eligible organizations must be registered to do business in Maryland and in good standing, and may include units of state or local government.

Funds cannot be used to verify income for subscribers, for pre-execution project costs (unless MEA agrees in writing), or for project costs incurred before grant agreement. Funds offset costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements for community solar projects and must comply with Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration offers competitive grants to non-profit organizations and local government entities to support energy efficiency projects and related activities that benefit Maryland residents experiencing low and moderate incomes. The program focuses on electrification and zero direct emissions technologies. Grants are awarded for projects that generate significant reductions in energy usage and pass benefits to income-qualifying residents. FY25 includes competitive regional awards with a maximum of 40 total awards available. The program budget for FY25 is $11,238,450 distributed across Maryland by region based on the number of households experiencing low and moderate income using US Census data. The program prioritizes underserved and overburdened communities and maximizes energy savings and greenhouse gas emission reductions per dollar invested.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants allocated regionally based on the number of households experiencing low and moderate income using US Census data. The program budget for FY25 is $11,238,450 distributed across Maryland by region. Minimum request of $9,500 per regional application; maximum award amount not determined, with larger requests potentially subject to scaling. Grants support energy efficiency projects including incremental new construction, limited upgrades to residential-commercial buildings, whole building commercial upgrades, and whole house retrofits that reduce energy usage. Funds can be used for purchase and installation of eligible building materials and equipment for energy efficiency measures, energy audits (BPI certified for whole-home/building retrofits), required permitting and inspections, health and safety repairs enabling energy upgrades (capped at $1,500-$5,000 per home/building), electric panel or circuit upgrades to facilitate electrification, ENERGY STAR qualified appliance replacements, LED lighting replacements, and project-related workforce training (up to $1,500 per person). Grant administration costs capped at 15% combined with indirect costs; indirect costs capped at 10% for most organizations with negotiated rates allowed for tax-exempt organizations with federal grants. Maximum reimbursable costs vary by project type: $7,000-$18,000 per residential home. Cannot fund renewable energy technologies (separate Solar Energy Equity Grant Program exists).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Resilient Infrastructure for Sustainable Energy (RISE) Program provides grants to fund improvements to Maryland's electricity and related power infrastructure. Funding helps strengthen the electric grid against threats including severe weather, tropical storms, hurricanes, extreme temperatures, winter storms, cyberattacks, physical attacks, and aging components. Grants support non-generation measures that enhance grid resilience and reliability through grid hardening, distributed energy resources, microgrids, battery storage, weatherization, fire-resistant technologies, monitoring systems, undergrounding, pole and vegetation management, adaptive protection, advanced modeling, and conductor replacement. This competitive program is funded through Section 40101(d) of the 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and serves electricity grid operators, storage operators, generators, transmission owners/operators, distribution providers, fuel suppliers, and related stakeholders.

Funds support non-generation measures that enhance the resilience and reliability of the electricity grid. structured_extraction.program_name: Inflation Reduction Act Home Energy Rebate Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal rebate programs administered by the Maryland Energy Administration in partnership with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and the Maryland Department of the Environment that provide financial support for qualifying energy efficiency and electrification upgrades to single-family and multi-family homes, focusing on low-and-moderate income beneficiaries. Programs include the Home Efficiency Rebates Opportunity Program (HERO), which provides rebates for whole-home energy efficiency upgrades that reduce energy use by at least 20%, with up to $4,000 or 50% of project costs for projects achieving 35% or more energy savings, and up to $2,000 or 50% of project costs for projects with 20-34% energy savings. The Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates Program (HEAR) supports replacing fossil-fuel appliances with electric alternatives and supporting upgrades needed to enable electrification, as well as clean heating equipment improvements, including heat pump systems, electric panel upgrades, electric wiring, and heat pump water heaters. Rebates are available up to $8,000 for eligible households. Higher rebate amounts are available for households with income below 80% of area median income. Eligible households and multifamily buildings must have incomes up to 150% of area median income, or for multifamily buildings, at least 50% of residents must have incomes at or below 150% of area median income.

Rebates up to $4,000 or 50% of project costs are available for projects achieving 35% or more energy savings, and up to $2,000 or 50% of project costs for projects with 20-34% energy savings. Specific electrification measures include: heat pump air conditioning and heating systems up to $8,000; electric panel upgrades up to $4,000; electric wiring up to $2,500; heat pump water heaters up to $1,750. Higher rebate amounts are available for households with income below 80% of area median income. Programs prioritize low-and-moderate income households. Rebates support replacing fossil-fuel appliances (such as fuel oil and natural gas equipment) with electric alternatives, along with supporting upgrades necessary to enable electrification. The Maryland Energy Administration is partnering with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and the Maryland Department of the Environment to address low-income components required by the U.S. Department of Energy. Eligible service territories include Potomac Edison, Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative, Baltimore Gas & Electric, Pepco, and Delmarva Power & Light. Additional complementary programs include the Energy Efficiency Equity Grant Program, BeSmart Energy Efficiency Loans, and Maryland Clean Energy Advantage Loan Pilot Program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive loan program that finances energy efficiency and conservation projects for eligible Maryland organizations, including nonprofits, local governments, businesses, state agencies, individuals, and agricultural building owners. The program provides below-market rate financing for projects that result in significant energy savings and greenhouse gas emission reductions. Funds are provided at below-market rates to Maryland nonprofits and businesses and at zero financing cost to local governments and state agencies. The program helps applicants identify and install energy improvements in their facilities, including commercial and agricultural buildings, to reduce energy consumption, costs, and greenhouse gas emissions.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: First-come, first-serve loans with varying interest rates and terms: Microloans of $10,000–$50,000 at 3% interest for up to 10 years for eligible businesses and nonprofits; Traditional loans of $50,001–$500,000 at 2% interest for up to 18 years for eligible businesses and nonprofits; and up to $2,000,000 at 0% interest (plus 1% administrative fee) for up to 18 years for Maryland state and local governments and Department of General Services. Total FY26 budget is $4,281,842. During the first 90 days, $2,140,842 is reserved for nonprofits and $2,140,842 for state governmental bodies; all remaining funds become available to all eligible applicants beginning November 1, 2025. Loan funds can finance 100% of Net Total Project Cost for facility retrofits or Incremental Project Cost for new construction/rehabilitation. Loans support the identification and installation of energy conservation improvements, including in agricultural buildings and commercial facilities. Applicants must pay a $250 application fee (businesses/nonprofits/local governments) or 1% administrative fee (state agencies). Loan proceeds may reimburse project expenses incurred after execution of Commitment Letter but prior to loan closing.
