structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Government Energy Modernization Program (L-GEM) supports local governments in planning and implementing sustainable, long-term clean energy and energy efficient projects that reduce energy usage and greenhouse gas emissions, increase cost savings, and drive clean energy and economic development. For FY26, the program offers over $64 million in one-time funding across four areas of interest: formula block grants for planning and implementation, and competitive grants for planning, energy efficiency and renewable implementation, and electrification projects. This program replaces Maryland Smart Energy Communities (MSEC) for FY26. Funding can support planning activities including feasibility studies, energy audits, energy planning, and strategy development; renewable energy projects such as solar, geothermal, and landfill-gas-to-energy installations; energy efficiency measures including weatherization, insulation, and efficient equipment upgrades; and electrification projects to replace fossil fuel systems with electric systems. The program provides feasibility studies, site assessments, design and engineering services, and technical support for solar installations that can integrate with efficiency upgrades or battery storage. The program aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the building sector to align with Maryland's net-zero emissions goal by 2045 and empowers local governments to lead by example and inspire community-wide clean energy adoption.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers over $64 million in total funding for fiscal year 2026, divided as follows: approximately $50 million for planning activities and renewable energy projects, $10 million for energy efficiency projects, and $4 million for electrification projects. Area of Interest 1 provides non-competitive formula block grants with flexible funding secured upfront and usable over multiple years (36-month period of performance). Areas of Interest 2, 3, and 4 provide competitive, merit-based grants awarded to local governments proposing specific energy-related public facility projects. Grants support clean energy and energy efficiency projects that produce reduced energy usage, greenhouse gas emissions, and increased cost savings. Technical support includes feasibility studies, site suitability analysis, design and engineering services for solar photovoltaic systems, and integration with efficiency upgrades or battery storage. Funding is reimbursement-based, with applicants required to pay contractors upfront and submit invoices for reimbursement. MEA reimburses up to 90% of total project costs for planning grants (AOI2) and up to 50% of total project costs remaining after utility incentives are deducted for electrification projects (AOI4).

Solar projects can integrate with efficiency upgrades or battery storage.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete and submit applications electronically when possible by the deadline. Initial application submitted by December 5, 2025 with high-level project overview and funding request. For solar projects, contact technical partners for early support, assess site suitability, collect utility data, define project scope, decide ownership approach, and use RFP or state-supported procurement pathway to select developer. Area of Interest 1 applications are evaluated through a formula-based process with funding secured upfront. Areas of Interest 2, 3, and 4 applications are evaluated competitively based on merit against evaluation criteria aligned with program goals and priorities. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Offshore Wind Supply Chain Investment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides non-competitive, first-come-first-served grant funding to support new or existing businesses entering the offshore wind supply chain in Maryland. It offers funding for capital expenditures and industry event attendance to help businesses relocate, expand, or enter the state's growing offshore wind industry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides non-competitive grant funding with two areas of interest. Area of Interest 1 (Capital Expenditures) offers up to $400,000 per project in funding to offset capital expenditures for entering the offshore wind industry, including relocation costs, new construction, renovations, and equipment purchase and installation. Applicants must contribute minimum 50% matching funds (may include finance/loan agreements, cash on hand, business line of credit, or other grant awards from state, federal, or private sources). Area of Interest 2 (Industry Events) offers up to $5,000 per offshore wind or marine technology industry event with reimbursement provided after the event takes place (limited to one event per fiscal year per applicant). A total of up to $2,000,000 is anticipated to be available. Eligible expenses for AOI 2 include event registration fees, exhibition fees, economy/coach airfare, baggage, ground transportation, lodging (GSA/Department of State per diem rates), meeting space audio/visual, and sample product shipping (capped at $2,000). Not permitted for AOI 2: food/drink, printing, cell phones, computer equipment, gifts/giveaways, consulting fees, or personal entertainment.

Minority, woman, and veteran-owned emerging businesses and members of historically disenfranchised groups disproportionately impacted by environmental and climate risks are strongly encouraged to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Offshore Wind Workforce Training & Education Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that funds workforce training centers, academic institutions, businesses, labor unions, and government entities to develop or expand offshore wind training and education programs. The program supports education and training for careers in offshore wind and related industries including skilled trades, manufacturing, transportation, and logistics. Funding is organized into multiple Areas of Interest: AOI 1 (Industry Education) supports developing or expanding offshore wind education programs at any education level to expand the general public's knowledge and understanding of offshore wind energy and educate individuals on how to get involved in offshore wind as a career; AOI 2 (Workforce Training) supports workforce training centers in developing or expanding offshore wind certification-based training programs with technical trade skills and safety standards training. The program partners with the Maryland Department of Labor to ensure Maryland has a ready and able workforce capable of contributing to the construction, installation, and operation & maintenance of an offshore wind energy project. The program is intended to help establish a pathway for businesses and individuals entering the offshore wind industry by providing funding opportunities to support workforce development and education initiatives.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding for Fiscal Year 2025 with up to $3,000,000 total available. Applicants must provide 25% matching funds or in-kind services. For fiscal year 2026, the Maryland Energy Administration is working with the Maryland Department of Labor's EARN Maryland Program to fund projects. Grant funding supports workforce training and education initiatives targeting businesses, minority-owned emerging businesses, nonprofits, academic institutions, labor unions, and state, local, and municipal governments. Eligible activities include creating or expanding training programs, covering capital and operating costs, relocation, renovations, equipment purchase and installation, labor and personnel, permitting and inspections, curriculum development, and providing supportive services for trainees.

The credit is claimed in the year the vehicle is placed in service and requires the vehicle to have a sale price not exceeding $50,000 and a battery capacity of at least 5 kWh. structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that combines energy efficiency, electrification, and solar energy projects for residential buildings, including single-family and multi-family homes. The program supports non-profit organizations, local government entities, and low-to-moderate income Maryland residents in implementing energy efficiency upgrades, electrification, and solar installations that reduce residential energy usage and benefit Maryland residents with low-to-moderate incomes. The program includes two Areas of Interest: AOI1 (energy efficiency for renter and owner-occupied homes) and AOI2 (solar energy for owner-occupied homes only).
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded for energy efficiency, electrification, and solar projects. AOI 1 (Energy Efficiency Projects) has an anticipated budget of $17,246,905 with minimum award of $105,000, maximum $21,000 per residence, and maximum for first-time recipients of $400,000, competitive within defined regions. AOI 2 (Solar Energy Projects) has an anticipated budget of $8,000,000 with minimum award of $30,000, maximum $30,000 per home for design, installation, and commissioning, and maximum award of $1,500,000, competitive statewide. Organizations may apply for either or both areas of interest. Grants support energy efficiency, weatherization, HVAC replacements/repairs, water heater replacements, appliance replacements, LED lighting, window repairs, enabling repairs, and residential solar PV installations (3-15 kW capacity). Grant Administration Costs and Indirect Costs capped at 15% of total grant. Training assistance up to $6,000 per award for worker certifications (BPI or NABCEP PVIP). Solar systems include 25-year warranty on panels, 10 years on inverters, 10 years on workmanship.

Households ineligible for Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) or EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP). Single-family and multi-family homeowners and renters.

structured_extraction.program_name: Residential and Commercial Energy Storage (RCES) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to support the deployment of energy storage systems for both residential and commercial customers across Maryland. It aims to enhance grid reliability, increase energy resilience, and accelerate the adoption of clean energy technologies statewide. Grants help Maryland residents and organizations install qualified battery energy storage systems on their properties. This is a first-time announcement replacing the prior Maryland Energy Storage Income Tax Credit Program that sunset at the end of 2024. Grants are awarded to eligible projects on a first come, first served basis from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF).
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to eligible projects on a first come, first served basis. Grant amount is calculated as the lower of: 30% of total installed costs of the battery energy storage system (BESS), $5,000 for residential property BESS, or $150,000 for commercial property BESS. Partial grants are possible depending on application volume and funding availability. The total program budget is $2,000,000 available from RGGI-RE through the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF). As of April 6, 2026, 100% of funding has been requested and 90% has been reserved. Applicants use a two-step application process for approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding for Maryland organizations to develop and install microgrids, resiliency hubs, and other distributed energy resources for critical and community uses. Funding covers preconstruction planning, feasibility analysis, system design, and installation, helping Maryland communities, businesses, and critical infrastructure achieve reliable, clean, and affordable energy solutions. The program helps reduce reliance on utility power, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and protect vital services against outages by offsetting the costs of planning, designing, and constructing these resilient energy systems. The FY26 program provides up to $13 million in total funding split across three Areas of Interest: AOI 1 (Preconstruction Planning) provides $500,000 for feasibility analysis and planning activities; AOI 2 (Microgrids) provides $4.5 million in capital for equipment and installation; and AOI 3 (Resiliency Hubs) provides $8 million in capital for solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage systems at community resiliency hub facilities.

AOI 3 (Resiliency Hubs) provides $8 million in capital for solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage systems at facilities serving as community resiliency hubs. Grants offset costs of planning, designing, and constructing microgrids, resilient facility power systems, and resiliency hubs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) Financing
structured_extraction.program_description: C-PACE is a State of Maryland financing program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration and the Maryland Clean Energy Center that helps commercial building and property owners, as well as businesses and nonprofits, finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, water conservation, environmental remediation, and resiliency projects. Loans are structured as property tax assessments on the value of installed equipment with up to 100% financing and are typically repaid over 10-20 years (up to 30+ years in some cases) through annual or semi-annual surcharges on property tax bills. When a property is sold, the loan transfers to the new owner and the prior owner is no longer obligated to make payments. There is no upfront cost to the property owner, and repayment can be cash flow positive from day one. The program is administered by the Maryland Energy Administration, with the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) managing the MDPACE program for most participating counties. Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Frederick County, Anne Arundel County, and Garrett County administer their own independent C-PACE programs through their respective green banks, economic development corporations, or energy divisions. The program is available in Maryland counties that have enacted C-PACE-enabling legislation and provides standardized, low-cost financing to help county governments create jobs, retain businesses, and keep dollars in local economies without raising taxes. Private lenders (including Greenworks Lending and Nuveen Green Capital) provide the financing, which remains with the property through ownership changes. Borrowers can benefit from tax credits including the solar investment tax credit (ITC) and accelerated depreciation benefits (MACRS). The assessment can be passed through to tenants where appropriate. New construction, existing buildings with planned renovations, and buildings with completed renovations from the last 12 months are eligible.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Energy Administration; Maryland Clean Energy Center
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

structured_extraction.assistance_description: C-PACE loans are structured as property tax assessments on the value of installed equipment with up to 100% financing available. Repayment occurs through annual or semi-annual surcharges on property tax bills over typical periods of 10-20 years with terms up to 30+ years available depending on the project and lender. Loans are typically amortized over 15 to 25 years with options to capitalize interest (up to 36 months maximum) and defer initial payments. The loan remains affixed to the property itself rather than to the property owner so it transfers with the property upon sale with the new owner continuing payments until the loan is paid off or the assessment is transferred as applicable. There is no upfront cost to the property owner and repayment can be cash flow positive from day one. Financing is standardized with typical projects ranging from $50,000 to $100,000. Financing is provided through lending partners such as Greenworks Lending and Nuveen Green Capital. Eligible uses include energy audits, feasibility studies, design, installation, construction, insurance, and loan closing costs. Borrowers can benefit from tax credits including solar investment tax credit (ITC) and accelerated depreciation benefits (MACRS). In Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Frederick County, Anne Arundel County, and Garrett County, programs are administratively independent. All other participating counties are administered through MDPACE managed by the Maryland Clean Energy Center. Approved capital providers can offer loans to finance energy-efficient and resilient building improvements for both the C-PACE component and senior debt for projects. Combined loan-to-value (CLTV) ratio shall not exceed 100% when combined with existing mortgages/liens. Minimum loan amount is $50,000 with no maximum threshold. Loan terms cannot exceed Weighted Average Expected Useful Life (EUL) of improvements (capped at 35 years). Loans must be fully amortized. Surcharge is collected through county property tax billing system.

Includes private commercial property owners, properties exempt from real estate taxation with tax identification numbers, multifamily properties (5+ units), and residential properties with HUD-backed mortgages. Also includes registered contractors (general contractors, HVAC installers, lighting contractors, solar developers, energy engineering firms, licensed engineers and architects).

Hard costs (direct installation/construction: materials, labor, overhead). Soft costs (indirect project costs including project management, closing fees, architectural/engineering, permitting, appraisals, legal services, capitalized interest, energy savings performance guaranty/insurance). Ancillary costs (construction costs necessary for installation, e.g., roof structural improvements, electrical upgrades).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Jurisdictions: adopt enabling legislation through an ordinance adhering to state's legislation principles and sign a Locality Agreement with the Maryland Clean Energy Center. For property owners: contact the appropriate C-PACE/MD PACE administrator for your county. Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Frederick County, Anne Arundel County, and Garrett County have independent programs administered by their respective green banks, economic development corporations, or energy divisions with their own application processes. For all other participating counties, applications are processed through MDPACE managed by the Maryland Clean Energy Center. Interested businesses, nonprofits, property owners, builders, capital providers, and contractors should contact the program directly by phone or email, or send an email to the finance team at finance@mdcleanenergy.org or energy@garrettcountymd.gov to get an application started and discuss their project and financing options. Building owners, capital providers, and contractors interested in the program should contact the Montgomery County Green Bank to learn more about getting started. For capital providers interested in becoming registered MDPACE providers, email the finance team to express interest, execute the Standard Offer agreement with the Maryland Clean Energy Center, and complete the provider registration process. Property owners can connect with participating lending partners who evaluate the project, determine financing eligibility, and structure the loan terms. The application process includes: (1) Determine eligibility and complete pre-application; (2) Submit project analysis with technical review by approved technical reviewer; (3) Obtain mortgage holder consent from all existing secured lienholders; (4) Submit final application with supporting documentation; (5) Receive Final Approval Letter; (6) Close C-PACE Loan and record documents in land records; (7) Obtain completion certificate upon project completion; (8) Disburse loan proceeds by capital provider according to mutually agreeable terms. Explore your eligibility at md-pace.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program designed to assist and encourage transfer students from Maryland community colleges to attend four-year institutions within the state and complete their bachelor's degrees in a timely manner. Awards of $1,000 to $2,000 per year are provided, with higher amounts going to students pursuing workforce shortage fields of study such as teaching, STEM, science, engineering, computer science, mathematics, and nursing. Recipients are ranked by academic merit and financial need, and a waiting list exists each year for the award. Funds can be used toward tuition and mandatory fees at four-year Maryland institutions. The scholarship does not have to be repaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Recipients enrolling in science, teaching, engineering, computer science, mathematics, or nursing programs receive $2,000 annually ($1,000 per term). Recipients enrolling in all other programs receive $1,000 annually ($500 per term). Funds can be used toward tuition and mandatory fees. Awards are made on a rolling basis with availability of funds. The scholarship can be renewed for up to 3 years or six terms of study. File FAFSA and 2+2 Transfer Scholarship application through MHEC One-App by the deadline. Submit required documents including community college transcript by the specified deadline. Applicant pool ranked on academic merit and financial need with a waiting list each year. This is a need-based scholarship that does not have to be repaid.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 15, 2026 for initial application and FAFSA submission; November 15, 2026 for required documentation; February 15, 2027 for proof of associate's degree conferment if conditionally awarded.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Transfer students from Maryland community colleges to four-year institutions within Maryland who hold or will complete an associate's degree. Must be U.S. citizens or eligible non-citizens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at four-year Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents. Must be transferring from a Maryland community college to a Maryland public or private nonprofit four-year higher education institution.
requirements_list: Be a resident of Maryland
Obtain an associate degree from a Maryland community college before transfer or be graduating with an associate's degree in Fall 2025, Spring 2026, Summer 2026, or Fall 2026
Earn a minimum cumulative 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale at a Maryland community college
Must be enrolled in an eligible accredited Maryland postsecondary institution
Must be a transfer student from a Maryland community college
Be transferring to a Maryland public or private nonprofit four-year higher education institution as a full-time, degree-seeking undergraduate student
Have demonstrated financial need with a Student Aid Index (SAI) not exceeding $10,000
Have not received a bachelor's degree or associate's degree prior to July 2025
File FAFSA and 2+2 Transfer Scholarship application through MHEC One-App
Submit required documents by the deadline
Submit community college transcript showing current cumulative GPA by November 15, 2026
If conditionally awarded, submit proof of associate's degree via final community college transcript showing degree conferment date by February 15, 2027
If conditionally awarded and applicable, submit proof of Selective Service registration by February 15, 2027

Renewal recipients must remain eligible for in-state tuition, submit FAFSA annually, maintain full-time undergraduate enrollment at a Maryland public or private nonprofit four-year institution, maintain minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA, and maintain institutional standards
Be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen (undocumented students not eligible)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit the 2+2 Transfer Scholarship application through MHEC One-App, the FAFSA, and a transcript from their Maryland community college showing current cumulative GPA by October 15, 2026. Applications and documentation are reviewed on a rolling basis. Once conditionally awarded, applicants must submit proof of associate's degree via final community college transcript showing degree conferment date by February 15, 2027, and proof of Selective Service registration if applicable by the same date. Applicants are ranked on academic merit and financial need. Renewal recipients do not need to submit another application. A waiting list exists each year for the award.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition-savings program that allows Maryland residents to attend participating public colleges and universities in other states and receive a waiver of out-of-state tuition charges when pursuing degree programs (undergraduate, transfer, or graduate) that are not available at any public institution in Maryland. Students who meet eligibility requirements can pay in-state tuition rates instead of out-of-state rates at participating institutions that are members of the Southern Regional Education Board (SREB) Academic Common Market. The program operates through coordinated participation with SREB and requires Maryland residency certification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students who are accepted into an ACM-eligible degree program at a participating out-of-state public institution receive a waiver of out-of-state tuition charges, allowing them to pay in-state tuition rates instead of out-of-state rates. The program operates through three application cycles per academic year: March 1 to June 30 (for Fall semester), September 1 to November 15 (for Spring semester), and January 2 to February 28 (for Summer semester). Applications are processed on a rolling basis. Once certified, students do not need to reapply unless they change their major, add a second major or minor, or have a break in enrollment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Three application cycles: March 1 - June 30 (for Fall semester); September 1 - November 15 (for Spring semester); January 2 - February 28 (for Summer semester). Applications processed on rolling basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are accepted or enrolled as degree-seeking students (undergraduate, transfer, or graduate) in an eligible or approved program at a participating public college or university and whose intended major is not available at any public institution in Maryland. Students of any age are eligible; undergraduate students under age 24 require parent or legal guardian signature. Includes students pursuing Bachelor of Science, Bachelor of Arts, Master of Arts, or Master of Science degrees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs at participating out-of-state public institutions. The tuition waiver reduces out-of-state tuition costs to in-state tuition rates for eligible students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program available to Maryland residents attending participating public institutions in other states that are members of the Southern Regional Education Board (SREB) Academic Common Market. North Carolina does not participate in the ACM. Maryland residents must attend out-of-state institutions if their degree program major is not available at any public institution in Maryland. Applicants must reside in Maryland, own/rent/occupy living quarters in Maryland, keep most personal property in Maryland, pay Maryland income tax on earned income, register vehicles in Maryland, have valid Maryland driver's license or identification card, be registered to vote in Maryland (if registered to vote), and receive no public assistance from another state or entity. Active duty military (or dependents) stationed in Maryland, or Maryland residents in military stationed elsewhere, are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must reside in Maryland for at least the last six months of the year prior to college start
Must own, rent, or occupy living quarters in Maryland
Must keep most personal property in Maryland
Must pay Maryland income tax on earned income
Must register all vehicles in Maryland
Must have valid Maryland driver's license or identification card
Must be registered to vote in Maryland (if registered to vote)
Must receive no public assistance from another state or entity
Must be active duty military (or dependent) stationed in Maryland, OR be Maryland resident in military stationed elsewhere
Must be accepted or enrolled in an eligible or approved degree program at a participating public college or university
Must be a degree-seeking student (undergraduate, transfer, or graduate)
Must be admitted to the academic program prior to applying for ACM
Acceptance letter must include academic major and area of concentration if required
Must maintain full-time enrollment status (except summers/winter breaks)
Must maintain good academic standing
Must not change major or minor after certification without re-certification
Program must be unique to the out-of-state institution (not offered in Maryland with curriculum less than 51% similar)

For residency documentation, must provide two of the following: parent or both parents' Maryland income tax return (Form 502 & 502B) with student listed as dependent, or student's Maryland income tax return (Form 502 & 502B); student's driver's license, provisional license, or voter registration card; student's utility bill; student's vehicle registration; student's high school or college transcript; student's pay stub; or completed and signed ACM Student-Parent Affirmation form
Military students must attach a copy of earnings statement and military orders signed by their commander in addition to required documentation
Transfer students must email ACM coordinator for application submission instructions or follow specific submission requirements
Parent or legal guardian signature required for undergraduate students under age 24
All supporting documents must be true and complete copies of original documents
Student must agree to furnish additional documentation and permit MHEC access to college or university records as needed
MHEC does not conduct pre-evaluations
Must submit truthful and accurate information
Must notify MHEC and school ACM Coordinator of status changes (change in major, addition of minor, double major, or break in enrollment)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Confirm acceptance letter includes academic major and area of concentration. 2. Ensure full-time enrollment status and good academic standing. 3. Obtain Maryland residency certification through the OneStop Maryland portal by submitting the Application for Certification for Maryland Residency with required supporting documents. 4. Submit application with required documentation through the OneStop portal during one of the three application cycles. 5. Upload two required residency documents as a single PDF file (addresses on both documents must match). 6. Complete and submit the ACM Student-Parent Affirmation form with student signature; parent/legal guardian signature required for undergraduate students under age 24. 7. Sign affirmation under penalties of perjury. 8. Complete and submit the Contact Page on the SREB website with student's complete contact information. 9. Check with institution's ACM Coordinator for any additional requirements. 10. MHEC processes applications in order received on rolling basis. 11. Once approved and certified, ACM Certification will be emailed and can be viewed or downloaded from OneStop account. 12. Maryland ACM Coordinator forwards certification to University's ACM Coordinator for processing. 13. Institution notifies student via email or account update once certification is processed and forwards to Financial Aid Office for tuition savings implementation. 14. Previously certified students do not need to reapply unless they change their major or have a break in enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps (ROTC) Scholarship Program provides full college tuition, laboratory fees, textbook allowances, and a monthly stipend to eligible high school graduates in exchange for military service. The program covers tuition and various fees at over 500 colleges and universities throughout the country, with a non-taxable $100 monthly allowance during the school year, and requires a minimum four-year active duty service obligation after graduation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full college tuition coverage at over 500 colleges and universities throughout the country, plus laboratory, textbook, and incidental fees. Non-taxable monthly allowance of $100 during the school year. Requires minimum four-year active duty service obligation after graduation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than December 1 of senior year of high school
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students who are at least 17 years old and no more than 25 years old, U.S. citizens, interested in military officer training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, laboratory fees, textbooks, and incidental fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Student's choice of over 500 colleges and universities throughout the country.
requirements_list: Must be a high school graduate or in process of graduating
Must be age 17 to 25
Must be a U.S. citizen
Must meet minimum SAT or ACT scores
Must have acceptable GPA and class standing
Must pass interview
Must pass physical aptitude test
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply during junior year of high school or no later than December 1 of senior year. Submit application materials including test scores, transcripts, interview, and physical aptitude test results. Selection based on SAT or ACT scores, GPA, class standing, interview, and physical aptitude test.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Army Reserve Officer Training Corps (ROTC) Scholarship Program provides tuition coverage, laboratory fees, textbook allowances, and a tax-free subsistence allowance to eligible high school graduates in exchange for military service. Scholarship recipients are obligated to military service either by serving 2 to 4 years followed by service in the Army National Guard or Army Reserve, or by serving 8 years in the Army National Guard or Army Reserve.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Covers tuition, laboratory fees, and a standard amount for purchase of textbooks, classroom supplies, and equipment. Provides tax-free subsistence of up to $1,500 each school year of scholarship support. Four-year scholarship recipients must attend Army ROTC host institutions. Two and three-year recipients may attend any college offering Army ROTC. Scholarship winners are obligated to military service either by serving 2 to 4 years followed by service in the Army National Guard or Army Reserve, or by serving 8 years in the Army National Guard or Army Reserve.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Apply during junior year in high school
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school graduates and current high school students between 17 and 21 years old who are U.S. citizens interested in military officer training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, laboratory fees, textbooks, classroom supplies, and equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Four-year scholarship recipients must attend Army ROTC host institutions. Two and three-year recipients may attend any college offering Army ROTC.
requirements_list: Must be a high school graduate
Must be age 17 to 21
Must be a U.S. citizen
Must meet minimum SAT or ACT scores
Must have acceptable high school academic record
Must pass interview
Must pass physical aptitude exam
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply during junior year of high school. Submit application materials including SAT or ACT scores, high school transcripts, interview, and physical aptitude exam results. Awards based on test scores, academic review, interview performance, and physical aptitude exam.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided through state, special, and/or federal funding for campus safety initiatives, programs, and security improvements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: CLOSED

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campus safety initiatives, programs, and security improvements

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles W. Riley Firefighter and Ambulance and Rescue Squad Member Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that provides financial assistance to Maryland residents who are actively engaged members of fire-fighting, ambulance, and rescue organizations serving Maryland communities to pursue credited courses leading to degrees in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a minor or concentration in fire service technology or fire service management, with the goal of leading to employment in an organized fire department, ambulance, or rescue squad in the state. The scholarship does not have to be repaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual scholarship award of at least 50 percent of the student's actual annual tuition and mandatory fees at an eligible institution. The award may not exceed the annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate student at a two-year or four-year public institution within the University System of Maryland, other than the University of Maryland Global Campus or University of Maryland, Baltimore. Maximum combined state awards: $28,000 or cost of attendance, whichever is less. The scholarship provides financial assistance to firefighters, ambulance members, and rescue squad members pursuing education in their field. The scholarship does not have to be repaid.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Multiple deadlines: July 1 (annual), April 15 (annually), April 1 for 2025-2026, January 15 opens for 2026-2027 closing October 15, 2026. See Important Scholarship and Grant Deadlines page.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Higher Education Commission Office of Student Financial Assistance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Actively engaged career or volunteer firefighters, ambulance members, and rescue squad members in Maryland who are Maryland residents (dependent students' parents must also be Maryland residents) pursuing education leading to employment in organized fire departments, ambulance services, or rescue squads. Includes families of firefighters, ambulance members, and rescue squad members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees for credited courses leading to degrees in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a minor or concentration in fire service technology or fire service management, or credited courses leading to employment in organized fire departments, ambulance services, or rescue squads in Maryland. Cannot be used for courses not required for the degree program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Members of fire-fighting, ambulance, and rescue organizations serving Maryland communities. Maryland residents; dependent students' parents must also be Maryland residents. Employment and attendance at Maryland institutions required.
requirements_list: Must be a member of a firefighting, ambulance, or rescue organization serving Maryland communities

Must pursue credited courses leading to a degree in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a minor or concentration in fire service technology or fire service management
Actively engaged career or volunteer firefighter, ambulance or rescue squad member in organized Maryland service

Volunteer members: recorded at least 50 LOSAP (Length of Service Award Program) points or equivalent county/municipality points in at least two different categories in the tax year prior to award year
Career members: worked a minimum of 1,000 hours as part of fire, ambulance, or rescue squad in the tax year prior to award year
Maintain a 2.5 GPA
Meet Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) requirements
Enrolled in an eligible Maryland institution
Accepted for admission or enrolled at eligible Maryland institution as full-time (12+ credits) or part-time (6-11 credits) undergraduate student each semester
Must submit online application through Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS)
Degree-seeking student pursuing credited courses in fire service-related fields
Commitment to work in Maryland emergency services
MHEC One App and required documentation must be submitted by application deadline
Submit MHEC One App and required documentation by deadline
Post-graduation service requirement: serve 1 year as volunteer or career member in fire/ambulance/rescue service in Maryland
FAFSA not required
Drug-free pledge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit online application through Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us or through FAFSA or MHEC One App. Initial applicants must submit Riley Application, Service Verification Form, Fire Official Acceptance Letter or comparable documentation, and LOSAP or points documentation (for volunteers). All required documents must be submitted online through applicant's MDCAPS account by the closing date. Eligible renewal applicants receive priority over initial applicants. Within these groups, applicants are ranked and awarded according to the submission date of their completed online application form. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. If awarded, initial applicants must electronically sign Riley Fire Promissory Note and Riley Fire Employment Obligation Agreement in MDCAPS prior to receiving payment. Renewal applicants submit Service Verification Form and LOSAP or points documentation. Renewal applicants do not need to sign the Promissory Note or Employment Obligation Agreement again if awarded. Applicants not selected are placed on a waitlist pending funding availability and must reapply in subsequent academic years. Late applications are considered only if funds remain after on-time applicants are awarded.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program that supports college access and completion by providing financial support and fostering collaboration between Maryland's high-need school districts and higher education institutions. The program raises academic preparedness of low-income, economically and environmentally disadvantaged students to enable them to attend, persist, and succeed in college. It provides student support services, comprehensive mentoring, financial aid counseling, and exposure to various academic disciplines and career fields through intervention services designed to prepare students for college enrollment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grants awarded to accredited Maryland public or independent two- and four-year higher education institutions, and partnerships between a lead institution and school district partners. Awards provide financial support to fund college preparation activities, student support services, mentoring, and financial aid counseling for low-income and disadvantaged middle and high school students. Funding supports academic enrichment, remediation, tutoring, research opportunities, individualized academic support, financial aid advising, financial literacy services, college and career counseling, advising, academic planning, professional development for school staff, college visits, career exploration events, internships, and parent and family engagement programs. Funds support salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and indirect costs (up to 8%). Awards provide up to $150,000 per project with a 25% institutional match required from the lead applicant. Project period: August 5, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Fifty percent of funds are disbursed at project start, with the remaining 50% upon receipt of interim report. In 2018, six institutions received awards ranging from $125,000 to $148,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, July 25, 2025 at 4:00 PM
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland middle and high school students in grades 6-12 who are low-income and economically and environmentally disadvantaged, particularly students meeting Free and Reduced-price Meals (FARM) criteria and at risk of needing college remediation. Served through partnerships between two- and four-year higher education institutions and high-need school districts and Local Education Authorities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports college access and completion programs designed to raise academic preparedness of disadvantaged students to enable them to attend, persist, and succeed in college, including college preparation activities, student support services, comprehensive mentoring, financial aid counseling, and exposure to academic disciplines and career fields. Specifically: academic enrichment, remediation, tutoring, research opportunities, and individualized academic support in mathematics and English/language arts; financial aid advising and financial literacy services; college and career counseling, advising, and academic planning; professional development for school staff; college visits, career exploration events, and internships; parent and family engagement programs; salaries, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant services, and indirect costs (maximum 8%).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; service regions include Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Caroline County, Prince George's County, Somerset County, and Wicomico County. Service also available in other eligible Maryland school districts meeting high-need criteria (≥44.4% FARM in feeder middle schools, ≥39.6% FARM in feeder high schools, FARM cohort graduation rate below 77.93%, and college remediation rate below 32.7%). Must meet three of four eligibility criteria. All 24 Maryland school districts are eligible to apply. Maryland GEAR UP partnership districts include Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties.

Must partner with a Local Education Authority (LEA) or a nonprofit organization
Must serve low-income and disadvantaged middle and high school students in grades 6-12

Cooperative planning agreement required between institution and LEA, signed by college/university representative, LEA superintendent/CEO, LEA coordinator, school principal(s), and other designated partners
Must address one or more FY 2025 funding priorities

Project must supplement, not supplant, existing programs

Grant records must be retained for 5 years after project completion
Interim report due January 10, 2026

25% institutional match from the lead applicant is required
Proposal narrative not to exceed 15 pages
12-point Times New Roman, Arial, or similar font; single-spaced
Academic pre- and post-testing required for academic services activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit electronic and paper applications by the deadline to compete for funding. Applications must include: original proposal with signatures (preferably in blue ink) plus two hard copies and one electronic copy; abstract (Word document, 250 words or less); complete proposal (PDF format); budget request (Excel format); and five copies of hard copy proposal. All required signature forms and components must be received by the deadline and follow specified order. Applications should follow the request for proposal (RFP) guidelines and include all required forms and documentation as outlined in the appendices. Partner coordination required including LEA Coordinator, High School Principal, and other partners, with authorized signatures from each partner entity. The MHEC review panel evaluates and scores applications, convenes to discuss and recommend funding, and submits recommendations to Secretary of Higher Education for final decisions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Complete College Maryland – One Step Away Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive, state-funded grant program created by House Bill 16 that supports public and nonprofit independent two-year and four-year higher education institutions in identifying, re-engaging, re-enrolling, and graduating near-completer students. Near-completers are students who have earned 75 percent or more of their college credits toward an associate's or bachelor's degree and have postponed their education for at least 12 consecutive months, or have enough credits for a degree but stopped out or dropped out without obtaining a degree. The program encourages Maryland residents who started a degree but have not finished it to return and complete it to achieve a college education. The program provides financial assistance to institutions and eligible students to support tutoring, customized degree plans, dedicated advisors, and other efforts to help near-completers earn their degrees. Students who re-enroll at a community college are eligible for up to one-third of the in-county tuition charge, and those re-enrolling in a public four-year institution are eligible for up to one-third of the in-state undergraduate tuition charge. Awards are applied towards tuition only after all non-loan aid has been applied. Eligible applicants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. The program went into effect in time for the fall semester of 2019.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $60,000 per accredited Maryland institution to support identification, contact, re-enrollment, and graduation of near-completer students. Institutions receive state-funded grants and must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost. Funds support financial assistance, tutoring, customized degree plans, dedicated advisors, outreach and recruitment, prior learning assessments, competency-based testing, flexible or general studies degree programs, faculty and staff development, and other completion services. The grant period runs from August 5, 2025 to August 31, 2026. Funds may support salaries and wages for essential personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and indirect costs up to 8% of total project cost. Near completers who re-enroll at a community college are eligible for up to one-third of the in-county tuition charge. Near completers who re-enroll in a public four-year institution are eligible for up to one-third of the in-state undergraduate tuition charge. Awards are applied towards tuition only after all non-loan aid has been applied. Eligible applicants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, July 25, 2025 at 4:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited Maryland public and nonprofit independent two-year and four-year associate and bachelor's degree-granting colleges and universities, as well as Maryland residents who left college during the COVID pandemic or for other reasons and are now ready to return and complete their associate or bachelor's degree. Near-completers include degree-eligible students (who have completed all degree requirements but not yet received their degree) and degree-potential students (who have stopped out or dropped out with significant credits earned).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Degree audit infrastructure and software enhancements; degree program completion plans (individualized or templated); enhancement or redesign of degree programs (flexible, general studies, or other associate or bachelor's degree programs); establishment of concierge or near-completer counselor positions; faculty and staff development; marketing and outreach efforts; student financial support including emergency grants, tuition discounts, book vouchers, fee waivers, transportation vouchers, and childcare support; prior learning assessments and competency-based testing; outreach and recruitment strategies; academic, financial, and social advising; salaries and wages for essential personnel; fringe benefits; travel; equipment; materials and supplies; consultant and contractual services; and other direct costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; Maryland institutions and Maryland residents only. Program is open to Maryland community colleges and public four-year institutions of higher education as well as accredited Maryland nonprofit independent two- and four-year institutions.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Institutions apply through a competitive grant process according to the Request for Proposal (RFP) guidelines. Submit completed application including: cover sheet, abstract, narrative (maximum 15 pages) addressing Needs Assessment, Project Objectives and Projected Outcomes, Management Plan, Operations Plan, and Project Evaluation; Budget Summary (Excel spreadsheet format); detailed budget narrative; and signed assurances from authorized institutional authority (President or Provost). Students should log into the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) to complete the online application. After completing the application, use the Electronic File Upload Tool to submit required transcripts from previous institution. structured_extraction.program_name: Complete College Maryland – One Step Away Program (Near Completer Grant)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded competitive grant program created by House Bill 16 that supports public and nonprofit independent two-year and four-year higher education institutions in identifying, re-engaging, re-enrolling, and graduating near-completer students. Near-completers are students who have earned 75 percent or more of their college credits (or at least 45 credit hours toward an associate degree or 90 credit hours toward a bachelor's degree) and have postponed their education for at least 12 consecutive months. The program encourages Maryland residents who started a degree but have not finished it to return and complete it to achieve a college education. The program provides financial assistance, tutoring, customized degree plans, and dedicated advisors to help near-completers earn an associate's or bachelor's degree. Near-Completers who re-enroll at a community college are eligible for up to one-third of the in-county tuition charge, and those re-enrolling in a public four-year institution are eligible for up to one-third of the in-state undergraduate tuition charge. The program is available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who meet eligibility requirements under Maryland law, including those eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8. Institutions receive grants up to $60,000 and must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost. Awards are applied towards tuition only after all non-loan aid has been applied. Eligible applicants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Grants are supported through state, special, and/or federal funding to support college completion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State-funded grants awarded to higher education institutions and individual near-completer students to support enrollment and completion. Institutional grants up to $60,000 per accredited Maryland institution; institutions must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost. Funds support financial assistance, tutoring, customized degree plans, dedicated advisors, outreach and recruitment, prior learning assessments, competency-based testing, flexible or general studies degree programs, faculty and staff development, and other completion services. The grant period runs from August 5, 2025 to August 31, 2026. Funds may support salaries and wages for essential personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and indirect costs up to 8% of total project cost. Near-Completers who re-enroll at a community college are eligible for up to one-third of the in-county tuition charge. Near-Completers who re-enroll in a public four-year institution are eligible for up to one-third of the in-state undergraduate tuition charge. Awards are applied towards tuition only after all non-loan aid has been applied. Eligible applicants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Eligible applicants will be notified by email if awarded in the summer. Award must be accepted online through MDCAPS portal within 2 weeks of notification.

Near-completers include degree-eligible students (who have completed all degree requirements but not yet received their degree) and degree-potential students (who have stopped out or dropped out with significant credits earned).

The program supports students pursuing cybersecurity careers in public service through career-based scholarships, including qualified children of undocumented immigrants and DACA students who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8. Recipients receive scholarships to cover tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board, and must commit to working in cybersecurity roles in public education, government, or teaching cybersecurity education. Full-time students may renew for two additional years; part-time students may renew for five additional years. Award converts to a loan payable to the state if the recipient fails to complete an approved cybersecurity program or does not fulfill the service obligation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Program of Educational Excellence Awards (EEA)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's largest need-based financial aid program providing grants and scholarships to eligible students with demonstrated financial need to attend postsecondary institutions in Maryland. The program includes multiple components: the Educational Assistance (EA) Grant, providing up to $3,000 per year (minimum $400 annually) for up to four years for eligible undergraduate students; the Educational Excellence Awards (EEA) component providing awards up to $19,100; and the Guaranteed Access (GA) Grant, providing up to $18,000-$19,100 per year (maximum $20,200 annually in some years). The GA Grant is designed to support high school seniors completing college preparatory programs and recent high school graduates who were unable to attend college within one year of graduating. Students may receive awards covering up to 100% of calculated financial need. The GA Grant covers up to 100% of a student's calculated adjusted financial need for their first two academic years of enrollment, with the grant renewable for up to 3 years total. Award amounts are calculated based on cost of attendance, student living situation (on campus, off campus, or with parent), and demonstrated financial need. The GA Grant is available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article Section 15-106.8, as well as traditional students and U.S. citizens, eligible non-citizens, and undocumented Maryland residents eligible for in-state tuition. In the 2019-2020 academic year, approximately 46,000 students received over $86 million in awards; in 2023-2024, more than 43,000 students received awards exceeding $100 million in total funding, with more than 3,600 students receiving the Guaranteed Access Grant and more than 39,600 students receiving the Educational Assistance Grant in the first round. The program awards financial assistance to more than 65,000 students annually, totaling more than $130 million. The program is designed to support low-income Maryland students with demonstrated financial need to access higher education, including low-income high school graduates or GED recipients under age 26 planning to enroll as full-time degree-seeking undergraduate students at Maryland postsecondary institutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Need-based grants and scholarships awarded to students with multiple components. The Educational Assistance (EA) Grant component provides up to $3,000 per year (minimum $400 annually) for up to four years for eligible undergraduate students. The Guaranteed Access (GA) Grant provides up to $18,000-$19,100 per year (maximum $20,200 annually, minimum $100 per year), with awards equaling up to 100% of calculated adjusted financial need for the first 2 academic years of enrollment or up to the maximum award amount, whichever is lower. Maximum EEA award up to $19,100-$20,200 per year overall. Award amounts are calculated based on cost of attendance, student living situation, and demonstrated financial need. Awards are contingent on availability of funds. The grant can be renewed for up to 3 years total. Financial need is calculated as: OSFA Determined Cost of Attendance – SAI (+/- Regional Cost of Living Adjustment) – Certain State Scholarship Awards – Pell Grant = OSFA Adjusted Financial Need. In the 2019-2020 academic year, approximately 46,000 students received over $86 million in awards; in 2023-2024, more than 43,000 students in the first round received awards exceeding $100 million in total funding, with more than 39,600 students receiving the Educational Assistance Grant. Awards can cover up to 100 percent of financial need. The 2018-2019 academic year awards totaled more than $80 million to nearly 38,000 students. Of the awardees, 1,650 students received awards covering 100 percent of their financial need, with maximum award amounts up to $18,600. The program awards financial assistance to more than 65,000 students annually, totaling more than $130 million. Awarding begins in Spring/Summer (May for GA) and continues until funds are exhausted.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students apply through the Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA). Submit the 2026-2027 FAFSA (for U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens) or MHEC One-App (for undocumented students) by March 1, 2026 through the MHEC One-App portal at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/MDCAPS/login.aspx. The Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) is also available for undocumented students (including DACA) and qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are ineligible for federal aid. There is no separate application form for FAFSA applicants; students who meet basic eligibility requirements will be automatically considered by MDCAPS. Some students may be asked to submit additional documentation such as parent signature pages, proof of Selective Service registration, family size verification forms, GED transcripts, proof of independent status, or tax verification forms by August 1, 2026. Documentation is submitted online through the student's MDCAPS account. Students notified as potentially eligible must submit required documentation either at Document Drop-Off events held in March, by mail to MHEC, by email, or by using drop boxes at MHEC locations. Students can find their required documents through their MDCAPS account. Awarding begins the first week of April 2026 and continues until funds are exhausted. Students can also submit required documents at Document Drop-Off Events held at various community colleges in February and March, or by mail or in-person drop box at MHEC offices by the April 1 deadline. Students are considered for both Guaranteed Access and Educational Assistance grants based on financial need. The Maryland Higher Education Commission uses federal FAFSA data to determine eligibility. Students who have been notified by MHEC as potentially eligible can check their MDCAPS account to find their list of required documents. They can submit documents in person at Document Drop-Off events, by mail to the Maryland Higher Education Commission Office of Student Financial Assistance, by email to ga.mhec@maryland.gov or osfamail.mhec@maryland.gov, or by using drop boxes located at MHEC buildings at 6 North Liberty Street and 200 West Baltimore Street in Baltimore. Applicants must accept their award online within 2 weeks of notification by email.

structured_extraction.program_name: Douglas J.J. Peters Veterans of Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to United States Armed Forces personnel who served in the Afghanistan or Iraq Conflicts, and their eligible family members (spouse, son, daughter, stepson, stepdaughter) attending a Maryland postsecondary institution. The program serves current high school seniors and full-time or part-time, degree-seeking undergraduate students enrolled in an eligible accredited Maryland postsecondary institution. Annual scholarship awards are provided for on-campus, off-campus, and students living with parents, with funds usable for tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at eligible Maryland institutions. Renewal awards are available for up to 4 years of full-time enrollment or 8 years of part-time enrollment. Award amounts may not exceed 50% of the annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board of a resident undergraduate at the highest-cost four-year public University System of Maryland institution. The scholarship supplements federal education benefits and does not have to be repaid. Administered by the Office of Student Financial Assistance at Maryland Higher Education Commission.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship awards up to $9,189 for on-campus students, $5,756 for off-campus students, or $5,186 for students living with parents. Award amounts may not exceed 50% of the annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board of a resident undergraduate at the highest-cost four-year public University System of Maryland institution (excluding University of Maryland Global Campus and University of Maryland, Baltimore). Funds can be used for tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at eligible Maryland institutions. Renewal awards available for up to 4 years of full-time enrollment or 8 years of part-time enrollment. Awards are subject to funding availability and may be adjusted or canceled if total financial assistance exceeds cost of attendance. Assistance does not have to be repaid.
