Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with priority given to renewal applicants, then veterans over dependents or spouses, then ranked by application complete date. Required documentation must be submitted online through the applicant's MDCAPS account, including military orders, discharge papers (DD-214), marriage certificate (if spouse), or birth certificate (if child/stepchild). Renewal students do not need to reapply but must continue to meet eligibility requirements. Award notification is provided via email; recipients must accept the award within an established timeframe. Contact the Office of Student Financial Assistance at 800-974-0203 or osfamail.mhec@maryland.gov for additional application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Dr. Peg E. Daw Nurse Faculty Annual Recognition Award
structured_extraction.program_description: Annual award recognizing full-time Maryland nurse faculty members for outstanding contributions to nursing education. Recipients receive $10,000 each and are chosen for demonstrating excellence in teaching, student impact, engagement, innovation in education and technology, or contributions to nursing education. The program awards a total of $350,000 to 35 recipients annually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10,000 grant awarded to each selected full-time nurse faculty member at Maryland schools of nursing. Total of $350,000 awarded to 35 recipients in 2024. Faculty members are nominated by their Dean or Director of Nursing and must be full-time nurse faculty.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time nurse faculty members at Maryland schools of nursing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recognition award for demonstrated excellence in nursing education
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland schools of nursing statewide
requirements_list: Must be a full-time nurse faculty member at a Maryland school of nursing
Must be nominated by dean or director of nursing
Must demonstrate excellence in one or more of five categories: excellence in teaching, impact on students, engagement, innovation in education and technology, or contributions to nursing education
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Faculty are nominated by their dean or director of nursing at their respective Maryland school of nursing. Selection is made based on demonstrated excellence in specified categories.

structured_extraction.program_description: EARN Maryland provides funding for free training in a variety of industries including cybersecurity, information technology, healthcare, and construction. The program operates statewide and offers different training programs that students may enroll in.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides funding for free training in cybersecurity, information technology, healthcare, and construction through partnerships with various training programs statewide.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers seeking training in skilled trades and technical fields.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training programs in cybersecurity, information technology, healthcare, and construction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Operates statewide throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should visit the EARN Maryland website at http://www.dllr.maryland.gov/earn/ for a list of current program partnerships and enrollment information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community-based strategy to address concentrated child poverty in Maryland by providing targeted grants and technical support to eligible communities to develop solutions to deeply rooted challenges related to poverty. The program funds the creation of Neighborhood Action Plans and Community Voice Committees to identify resources needed and reduce childhood poverty through increased investments and improved economic mobility. A $20 million investment offering competitive grants and technical support, with partnership from the Governor's Office for Children, Maryland agencies, and a network of local, state and national organizations working with applicants and grantees to understand, develop and implement community-focused solutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $20 million investment offering competitive, targeted grants and technical support to eligible communities most in need to develop solutions to address concentrated child poverty. Grants support the development of Neighborhood Action Plans, creation of Community Voice Committees, collaboration with community partners, and implementation of community-focused solutions. The Governor's Office for Children, Maryland agencies, and a network of local, state and national organizations partner with applicants and grantees in understanding, developing and implementing strategies to end child poverty.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities most in need addressing concentrated child poverty in Maryland, specifically neighborhoods where concentrated child poverty requires targeted investment and support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing Neighborhood Action Plans, creating Community Voice Committees, increasing investments in high-poverty areas, improving economic mobility for residents, and implementing community-focused solutions to address concentrated child poverty and deeply rooted challenges related to poverty.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; communities most in need with high levels of child poverty. Examples include the Golden Mile area (Route 40 corridor on the west side of the City of Frederick in Frederick County), where more than one-third of children live in poverty.
requirements_list: Focus on communities with high levels of child poverty
Collaboration with local community partners
Development of a Neighborhood Action Plan
Creation of a Community Voice Committee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible communities can visit goc.maryland.gov to learn more and apply for competitive funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state need-based financial aid grant program available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15-106.8. The program is part of the Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Award Program, Maryland's largest need-based aid program. Applicants complete the MHEC One App (Maryland State Financial Aid Application/MSFAA) through the Maryland College Aid Processing (MDCAPS) portal at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/MDCAPS/login.aspx. Award amounts and specific terms are determined by MHEC and the applicant's institution and include campus-based grants. Applications open each year at the same time as FAFSA. Award notification occurs in late April or summer depending on program type, with awards administered through the applicant's institution. Students must accept their award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A state need-based financial aid grant for qualified children of undocumented immigrants eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15-106.8. Applicants are considered for various state financial aid programs through a single application (MHEC One App/MSFAA) submitted through the Maryland College Aid Processing (MDCAPS) portal. Award notification occurs in late April or summer depending on program type, with awards administered through the applicant's institution. Award amounts and specific terms are determined by MHEC and the institution. Students must accept their award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled. The application opens each year at the same time as FAFSA.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 (for 2023-2024 academic year); varies by program—see deadlines at https://mhec.maryland.gov/preparing/Pages/Important-Scholarship-and-Grant-Deadlines.aspx. Application opens at the same time as FAFSA each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified children of undocumented immigrants (including DACA students) who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15-106.8 and attend eligible Maryland public or private institutions. Not for U.S. citizens, eligible noncitizens with Alien Registration numbers, or international students on student visas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State financial aid for educational expenses and tuition at eligible Maryland institutions for college attendance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents with state of legal residence in Maryland; must have filed Maryland income tax returns for 3 years while attending public/nonpublic secondary school in Maryland plus each year between graduation and college registration (or similar requirements for community college transfers); statewide eligibility
requirements_list: Applicant must be a qualified child of undocumented immigrants or DACA student
Must be eligible for in-state tuition under §15-106.8 of the MD Education Article
Must not be a U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen with Alien Registration number
Must not be an international student on student visa
Must be ineligible for federal aid (cannot have completed FAFSA)

Must have filed Maryland income tax returns meeting specific requirements (3 years during secondary school plus years between graduation and enrollment, or years while enrolled at community college plus years between achieving 60 credits and registering at public senior institution)
Must have Social Security Number (SSN), Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), or be able to file taxes, though SSN is not required
Males ages 18-25 must register with Selective Service System and show proof of registration
Dependent students under age 24 (as of December 31 of award year) must provide parental information with at least one parent signature
Parent Signature Page submission mandatory for dependent students or applicant is disqualified
Must complete application through MDCAPS portal via MSFAA/MHEC One App
Must meet income and residency requirements
Must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution
Provide parent income and tax information from two years prior to award year (if dependent)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA)/MHEC One App through the Maryland College Aid Processing (MDCAPS) portal at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/MDCAPS/login.aspx. Create a MDCAPS account, complete the MSFAA Eligibility Wizard, provide dependency status information, enter parent income/tax data if dependent, select up to 10 institutions and housing plans, review and agree to terms and conditions, and submit the application. The application opens each year at the same time as FAFSA. Submit prior-prior-year tax information and meet the deadline for the specific grant or scholarship program (typically March 1). Monitor your MDCAPS account status page to verify no additional information is needed. If dependent, download and submit the Parent Signature Page with parent certification to OSFA. Applicants will be notified if awarded in late April or summer depending on program type. Your institution will notify you if you have been awarded. Students must accept their award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled. Award amounts and terms vary by institution.

structured_extraction.program_name: Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program and Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides student financial assistance to Maryland residents based on eligible military or public safety service, or family or marital relationship to such individuals, or to children and surviving spouses of school employees who died or sustained 100% disability as victims of violence in the line of duty. The Conroy program assists veterans and eligible dependents through both scholarship and need-based grant funding, while the Cryor program provides financial assistance to eligible children and surviving spouses of school employees who died or were 100% disabled in the line of duty. Scholarship awards up to $14,086 for the 2026-2027 academic year. Awards may be held for up to 4-5 years of full-time study (12+ credits per semester) or 7-8 years of part-time study (6-11 credits per semester). Awards cover tuition, mandatory fees, and other educational expenses at eligible institutions of higher learning within Maryland. Funds do not have to be repaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship and grant awards. Maximum award: $14,086 for the 2026-2027 academic year or equivalent to the highest annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate at a 4-year public University System of Maryland institution (whichever is applicable). Minimum award may not be less than equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of recipient's institution. Awards may be held for five years of full-time study (12+ credits per semester) or eight years of part-time study (6-11 credits per semester) or a combination of both. Funds support tuition, mandatory fees, and other educational expenses at eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions and do not have to be repaid.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 15 of each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students enrolled in undergraduate, graduate, professional, or certificate programs at eligible Maryland institutions who are at least 16 years old and meet military, public safety, or victim-related service requirements. Eligible categories include: children and stepchildren of deceased or 100% disabled military service members; surviving spouses of 100% disabled military service members; veterans with 25% or greater service-connected disability who have exhausted federal veterans' educational benefits; children, stepchildren, and surviving spouses of September 11, 2001 terrorist attack victims; prisoners of war or missing in action from the Vietnam Conflict (on or after January 1, 1960) and their descendants; children, stepchildren, and surviving spouses of public safety employees killed or 100% disabled in the line of duty; 100% disabled public safety employees; and children, stepchildren, and surviving spouses of school employees killed or 100% disabled in the line of duty due to an act of violence. Full-time (12+ credits per semester) and part-time (6-11 credits per semester) students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses including tuition, mandatory fees, and other postsecondary education expenses at eligible Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents at the time of application, except for certain dependents and surviving spouses of public safety employees killed or disabled in the line of duty, and disabled public safety employees. For prisoners of war or missing in action from the Vietnam Conflict, applicants must have been Maryland residents at the time of the prisoner of war/missing in action declaration. Available at institutions of higher learning within Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be at least 16 years old

Must be enrolled in a regular undergraduate, graduate, or professional program at an eligible institution at full-time or part-time enrollment, or in a 2-year terminal certificate program with transferable coursework, or in a private career school

Must qualify under at least one of the following conditions: son, daughter, or stepchild of a United States Armed Forces member who died from military service or suffered 100% service-connected permanent disability; surviving spouse of Armed Forces member with 100% service-connected permanent disability who has not remarried; veteran with 25% or greater service-connected disability who has exhausted federal veterans' educational benefits; son, daughter, stepchild, or surviving spouse of a September 11, 2001 terrorist attack victim; POW/MIA of Vietnam Conflict (on or after January 1, 1960) or their son, daughter, or stepchild and was Maryland resident at time of declaration; son, daughter, stepchild, or surviving spouse of state or local public safety employee who died in line of duty or was 100% disabled in line of duty (has not remarried if surviving spouse); state or local public safety employee or volunteer who was 100% disabled in line of duty; son, daughter, stepchild, or surviving spouse of school employee who died or was 100% disabled in line of duty as result of act of violence
Maryland resident at time of application
Veteran must have exhausted or no longer be eligible for federal veterans' educational benefits
Total financial assistance cannot exceed cost of attendance
Application must be submitted through your institution's financial aid office by July 15
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New and renewal applicants should contact their institution's financial aid office for application instructions or apply through FAFSA or MHEC One App. Students should not submit applications or supplemental documentation directly to the Maryland Higher Education Commission. All required documentation should be submitted directly to the institution. Institutions award eligible students and are reimbursed by the state. Initial awards are automatically renewed by the financial aid office for subsequent academic years. Renewal awardees do not need to reapply annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: An initiative to reduce inequities in college completion by providing coaching, financial support, and other community resources to bolster access to higher education and build a more educated workforce. The program uses evidence-based advising models to help students successfully complete their program of study. It is specifically targeted at students of color and students from low-income families pursuing postsecondary degrees or credentials at Maryland community colleges. Comprehensive student supports are designed to help improve college completion and economic mobility rates. Each of the three participating community colleges receives $125,000 in funding, with support and training provided by the Maryland Higher Education Commission and MDRC, including data analytics to track student retention and degree completion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each of the three participating community colleges receives $125,000 in funding. The Maryland Higher Education Commission and MDRC provide support and training to the participating colleges to launch the initiative, including data analytics to track student retention and degree completion. Comprehensive student supports are designed to help improve college completion and economic mobility rates for students through advising, coaching, financial support, and community resources.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Donna Thomas, Interim Vice President, Student Affairs (Baltimore City Community College); Crystal Smith, Dean of Student Success and Advisement (Prince George's Community College); Paul Fields, Director of Advising and Title III (Wor-Wic Community College)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students of color and students from low-income families pursuing postsecondary degrees or credentials at participating Maryland community colleges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Student support services including coaching, advising, financial support, and community resources to help students complete college degrees and credentials. Data analytics to track student retention and degree completion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Pilot program at three Maryland community colleges: Baltimore City Community College, Prince George's Community College, and Wor-Wic Community College. Wor-Wic Community College serves the Eastern Shore region (Wicomico, Worcester, and Somerset counties).
requirements_list: Enroll at one of the three participating community colleges
Program eligibility requirements vary by college
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program eligibility requirements will vary by college. Contact the respective community college for more information about eligibility and how to enroll.

structured_extraction.program_description: A college access and grant program established by the Maryland General Assembly in 2016 and administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that supports low-income, first-generation students in high-poverty school systems. The program provides cohort-based mentoring, college guidance, and educational support to students identified as early as 7th grade through high school graduation and into their first year of college. Services include high school graduation planning, summer work/internship opportunities, financial aid literacy assistance, career and interest assessments, mentorship and one-on-one counseling, college campus and workplace visits, intensive summer bridge programs, and college matriculation support. FY26 grants totaling $5,000,000 are awarded to nonprofit organizations that received funding in FY25, with an estimated 11 to 15 grants available. Grants support organizations providing services to cohort students in grades 7-12 who pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant in eligible school districts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FY26 grants totaling $5,000,000 will be awarded to nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) status that were awarded grants in FY25, with an estimated 11 to 15 grants available. Funds support organizations providing cohort-based mentoring, college guidance, and comprehensive college access services to students in grades 7-12 who pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant in eligible school districts. Grant funds support mentoring and college support from student identification through college transition and into their first year of college. Allowable expenses include salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and other costs approved by MHEC. Funds must supplement (not supplant) existing program funds. Capital improvements and gift purchases are not permitted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 5:00 p.m. EDT on July 1, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, first-generation students in grades 7-12 in eligible high-poverty school systems who pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant. Nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) status that were awarded grants under the Next Generation Scholars Program in FY25 are eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds support organizations in providing cohort-based mentoring, college guidance, and comprehensive college access services including high school graduation planning, summer work/internship opportunities, financial aid literacy assistance, career and interest assessments, mentorship and one-on-one counseling, college campus and workplace visits, intensive summer bridge programs, outreach and student registration, and college matriculation support. Allowable costs include salaries and wages (professional and other personnel), fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and other costs approved by MHEC. Indirect costs are permitted up to a maximum of 8% of direct costs. Funds must supplement new and/or existing programs and cannot supplant non-grant funds. Capital improvements and gift purchases are prohibited.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to nonprofit organizations serving students in Allegany County, Baltimore City, Caroline County, Dorchester County, Kent County, Prince George's County, Somerset County, and Wicomico County public school systems through their respective school districts. Program is administered statewide by the Maryland Higher Education Commission.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization with 501(c)(3) status that was awarded a grant under the Next Generation Scholars Program in FY25
Must support students in grades 7-12 in eligible school districts
Students must pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant

Must include at least one goal for each required program component (high school graduation planning, summer work/internship opportunities, financial aid literacy, career assessments, mentorship, college/workplace visits, summer bridge programs, student outreach/registration, and college matriculation support)
Must maintain records for five (5) years
Must comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Americans with Disabilities Act
Must comply with GEPA Section 427 equity access requirements
Must participate in statewide assessment and evaluation programs
Must provide MHEC access to all grant-related records
Must obtain prior written approval for significant changes (timeline, activities, key project staff, or budget modifications exceeding $1,000 or 10% of approved line item)
Project extension requests must be made no less than one month prior to established expiration date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the FY26 Next Generation Scholars Application form (available on MHEC Office of Grants Administration and Compliance website). Save the completed application as a PDF and obtain appropriate signatures. Email the signed PDF to tiffany.majors1@maryland.gov with subject line 'NGS FY26 Submission' by 5:00 p.m. EDT on July 1, 2025. Applications will be reviewed by the MHEC Review Committee from July 2-9, 2025, with applicants notified of award status by July 10, 2025. Reference the FY 2026 Guidance document for additional requirements. Grant recipients must submit interim progress reports on October 15, January 15, and April 15, and a final project evaluation within 60 days after the grant end date.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program providing tuition assistance to dependents and surviving spouses of fallen transportation workers to support their educational pursuits at accredited institutions. The assistance does not have to be repaid. Eligible students can receive scholarships with a maximum award amount not exceeding the lesser of $3,000 or the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees at the institution attended, not to exceed the highest annual expenses for a full-time resident undergraduate at a University System of Maryland four-year public institution. Awards may be held for up to five years of full-time study or eight years of part-time study, or a combination of both, and are automatically renewed for subsequent academic years. Supports postsecondary education including undergraduate, graduate, professional, and career programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The scholarship provides tuition and mandatory fees assistance with a maximum award amount not exceeding the lesser of $3,000 or the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees at the institution attended, not to exceed the highest annual expenses for a full-time resident undergraduate at a University System of Maryland four-year public institution (excluding UMD Global Campus and UMD Baltimore). Awards may be held for up to five years of full-time study (12 or more credits per semester) or eight years of part-time study (6-11 credits per semester), or a combination of both. Awards are automatically renewed for subsequent academic years. Does not have to be repaid. Contact your institution's financial aid office or apply through FAFSA or MHEC One App by July 15.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 15 of each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Dependent children, stepchildren, and surviving spouses (who have not remarried) of fallen transportation workers who are at least 16 years old and enrolled in eligible postsecondary programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents whose fallen transportation worker died as a result of an accident while performing duties related to transportation facility construction, maintenance, rehabilitation, or operation in Maryland. Student death must occur on or after January 1, 2022. Students attending eligible institutions in Maryland or elsewhere are eligible.
requirements_list: Be the child, stepchild, or surviving spouse (who has not remarried) of a fallen transportation worker
Be at least 16 years old
Fallen transportation worker must have died from a work-related accident while performing duties related to transportation facility construction, maintenance, rehabilitation, or operation in Maryland
Worker death must occur on or after January 1, 2022

Be enrolled in a regular undergraduate, graduate, or professional program at an eligible institution at full-time or part-time enrollment, OR in a 2-year terminal certificate program with course work acceptable for transfer credit to an accredited baccalaureate program, OR in a private career school
Remain drug-free for the full term of award
Continue meeting all eligibility requirements for renewal
Application must be made through institution's financial aid office, FAFSA, or MHEC One App by July 15
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your institution's financial aid office to apply by July 15. New and renewal applicants should contact their institution's financial aid office for application instructions. All applications and required documentation should be submitted directly to the institution, not to MHEC. Institutions will process applications with a deadline of July 15 each year. You may also apply through FAFSA or MHEC One App. Awards are automatically renewed by the institution for the next academic year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Gaining Early Awareness and Readiness for Undergraduate Programs (GEAR UP) Scholarship Award
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program providing financial assistance to students who participated in GEAR UP (Gaining Early Awareness and Readiness for Undergraduate Programs) activities during the 2014-2020 grant period and are pursuing undergraduate education at accredited institutions. Scholarships support early awareness and readiness for undergraduate education. Awards are made after federal Pell Grants, state aid, and other public or private aid (excluding loans and work-study) have been applied, with amounts varying based on financial need and cost of attendance. Scholarships are provided through grant funding supported by state, special, and/or federal funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $15,000 for fall and spring academic year and $10,000 for summer. Award amounts vary depending on the student's financial need and cannot exceed the cost of attendance. Awards are made after the drop/add period and after federal Pell Grants, state aid, and other public or private aid (excluding loans and work-study) have been applied. Scholarships support undergraduate education at accredited two- or four-year institutions, private career schools, or state/regional accredited trade schools/certificate programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FAFSA must be filed before March 1 each year. GEAR UP Scholarship Application - Summer 2023 - Due July 1, 2023. Applications accepted on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents under 22 years old who participated in GEAR UP activities at GEAR UP sites in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the 2014-2020 grant period and are enrolled or accepted for enrollment in undergraduate programs at accredited institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Scholarship aid to support undergraduate education at accredited two- or four-year institutions, private career schools, or state/regional accredited trade schools/certificate programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must have participated in GEAR UP activities at GEAR UP sites in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the 2014-2020 grant period. Students must be Maryland residents according to the institution's state residency policy.
requirements_list: Participated in GEAR UP activities at GEAR UP sites in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during 2014-2020 grant period
Maryland resident according to institution's state residency policy
Enrolled or accepted for enrollment in undergraduate program at accredited two- or four-year institution, private career school, or state/regional accredited trade school/certificate program
High school diploma or recognized equivalent
Less than 22 years old at time of first scholarship award
Maintain satisfactory academic progress per institution standards
File completed FAFSA before March 1 each year
File GEAR UP Scholarship Application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete FAFSA at www.fafsa.gov before March 1 each year. Submit GEAR UP Scholarship Application through the online form. Applications are processed and verified following the institution's drop/add period. Eligible students are notified via email listed on application. If student transfers or withdraws, student must notify MHEC immediately. Applications accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that provided emergency financial assistance to local education agencies, higher education institutions, and other educational entities to respond to the COVID-19 pandemic. In Maryland, $10 million of the allocated funds were directed to community colleges to provide workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure, primarily for individuals who lost employment due to COVID-19.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funds totaling $10 million were allocated to Maryland community colleges for workforce development and continuing professional education programs leading to government or industry certification or licensure. Individual community college awards ranged from $250,000 to $1,480,602.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Grant period ended December 30, 2021
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community colleges and educational institutions seeking to provide workforce development and continuing professional education to individuals impacted by COVID-19 employment loss, as well as students in crisis situations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure; emergency education relief.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties through community college service areas.
requirements_list: Programs must lead to government or industry certification or licensure
Primary focus on individuals impacted by COVID-19 through employment loss
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funds were allocated directly to Maryland community colleges based on the award amounts shown in the grant award table.

structured_extraction.program_name: Governor's Emergency Education Relief (GEER) Fund for Maryland Community Colleges
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that provided emergency financial assistance to Maryland's 16 community colleges to expand education and workforce development programs and respond to the COVID-19 pandemic. The funding supports workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure, with particular focus on individuals impacted by COVID-19 through employment loss. The program distributed $10 million in total grant awards to community colleges, with individual awards ranging from $250,000 to $1,480,602.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funds totaling $10 million were allocated to Maryland's 16 community colleges for workforce development and continuing professional education programs leading to government or industry certification or licensure. Individual community college awards ranged from $250,000 to $1,480,602. Funds could be used for direct aid to students, materials, supplies and equipment, curriculum development, salaries and wages, professional development and technical training, student recruitment and marketing, and technology training, certification, examination and licensure fees or vouchers for programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Grant period ended December 30, 2021
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland community colleges and individuals impacted by COVID-19 through employment loss seeking workforce development and professional education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct aid to students; materials, supplies, and equipment; curriculum development; salaries and wages; professional development and technical training; student recruitment, marketing, and advertising; technology training, certification, examination and licensure fees or vouchers for programs; workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all 16 Maryland community colleges are eligible. All Maryland counties served through community college service areas.
requirements_list: Programs must lead to government or industry certification or licensure
Primary focus on individuals impacted by COVID-19 through employment loss
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funds were allocated directly to Maryland community colleges based on the award amounts shown in the grant award table.

structured_extraction.program_name: Governor's Emergency Education Relief Fund II (GEER II)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program funded through the U.S. Department of Education and the CRRSA Act that provides supplemental emergency assistance to local education agencies, institutions of higher education, and other educational entities to address impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic. In Maryland, funds support community colleges and private nonprofit colleges and universities with workforce development courses, continuing professional education leading to government or industry-required certification or licensure, and institutional costs resulting from COVID-19. The program allocated $10 Million in grants: $7.4 Million to Maryland community colleges for workforce development and professional education leading to government or industry-required certification or licensure, particularly for individuals impacted by COVID-19 job loss, and $2.6 Million to Maryland independent colleges and universities to support institutional costs from COVID-19. Individual community college awards ranged from $185,000 to $1,095,645, and private nonprofit colleges and universities each received $200,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Governor Hogan allocated $10 Million total from GEER II: $7.4 Million to Maryland community colleges to provide workforce development and continuing professional education leading to government or industry-required certification or licensure, particularly for individuals impacted by COVID-19 job loss; $2.6 Million to Maryland independent colleges and universities to support institutional costs from COVID-19. Individual community college allocations range from $185,000 to $1,095,645. Private nonprofit institutions each received $200,000. Emergency grants provided through federal support for educational institutions and students in crisis situations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Howard P. Rawlings Campus-Based Educational Assistance Grant (CBEAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A need-based financial aid program that provides grants to full-time undergraduate students who missed the March 1st state financial aid application deadline and are therefore ineligible for other state grants. The program is state-funded and allocates money to participating colleges and universities each academic year to award qualified students. Students attending four-year institutions receive an award equal to 40% of OSFA adjusted financial need, while students attending community colleges receive an award equal to 60% of OSFA adjusted need. The minimum annual award is $400 and the maximum award is $3,000. The total dollar amount of all state awards may not exceed the cost of attendance as determined by the school's financial aid office or $28,000, whichever is less.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program that provides funding to Maryland public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers to address food insecurity among students by supporting food access initiatives, raising awareness of food services, and building partnerships to address basic food needs on campus. The program addresses student hunger and leverages sustainable solutions to address basic food needs on campus, raises awareness of services offered on campus that address basic food needs, and builds strategic partnerships at local, state, and national levels to address food insecurity among students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Higher Education Commission awards grant funding to eligible public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers to address campus hunger initiatives. FY 2025 awards totaled $150,000. FY 2026 awards total $150,000. Institutions must pledge a 25% matching contribution (in-kind or matching funds). Funds may support emergency assistance, hire staff to manage initiatives, operational activities, salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, food pantry operations, meal plan donation programs, SNAP enrollment support, and awareness campaigns and events. Indirect costs cannot exceed 8% of total direct costs.

The goal is to expand and improve higher education pathways for incarcerated individuals. Programs include credit-bearing coursework or industry-recognized certificate/license programs, support services (academic counseling, mentoring, tutoring, career counseling), individualized planning, and mentoring.

Grants support personnel compensation, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, supplies, consultant and contractual services, mentor stipends, and indirect costs (capped at 8%). Funds cannot supplant existing services or be used for capital improvements or pre-approval costs. Funds must supplement new and/or existing programs and cannot be used to supplant non-grant funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state loan repayment assistance program helping eligible individuals pay back educational loans when they work full-time in eligible public service fields, serving Maryland residents with low incomes or who live in underserved areas. The program provides locked-in three-year awards with guaranteed renewal eligibility. Programs are available for various professions including lawyers, nurses, nurse faculty, teachers, social workers, therapists, counselors, dentists, public defenders, prosecutors, veterinary practitioners, veterinary technicians, and foster care recipients. Annual payments range from $1,500 to $10,000 depending on total educational debt at the time of application, with recipients receiving awards based on debt tier. Some programs offer eligible residents up to $30,000 toward their student loan debt. Overall award limits are $4,500, $9,000, $18,000, and $30,000 respectively.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards are based on total educational debt at the time of application. Recipients receive locked-in three-year awards with guaranteed renewal eligibility. Annual payments range from $1,500 to $10,000 depending on debt tier: $1,500 per year for debt of $15,000 or below, $3,000 per year for debt between $15,001–$40,000, $6,000 per year for debt between $40,001–$75,000, and $10,000 per year for debt of $75,001 or more. Overall award limits are $4,500, $9,000, $18,000, and $30,000 respectively. Payment amounts cannot exceed total debt and will be adjusted accordingly. Award checks are issued to recipients to be applied toward loan repayment with eligible lenders. Recipients must remit payment to lender within 120 days with proof of payment required.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2026 for 2025-2026 academic year (postmark deadline); October 15, 2026 for 2026-2027 award year (postmark deadline); April 15, 2026 opening date for 2026-2027 application; October 1 for initial applications

Also available to foster care recipients employed by the state, county, or municipality. Income limits: Single applicants max $75,000 annual salary; married couples max $150,000 combined; nurse faculty members max $100,000 individual/$185,000 combined.

Qualified children of undocumented immigrants eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8 are also eligible for this state financial aid scholarship.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A last dollar scholarship providing up to $5,000 per student per academic year (minimum $100 annually or $50 per semester) to cover remaining tuition and mandatory fees after federal or state financial aid is applied. Awards are made to eligible students enrolling at Maryland's 16 community colleges or other eligible Maryland public or private institutions. Eligibility is based on adjusted gross income limits: $100,000 for single applicants or single parent households, and $150,000 for married applicants or two parent households (based on prior-prior-year tax information). Students must file FAFSA, MHEC One App (or MSFAA) and submit required documents by the final deadline of April 15 (priority deadline July 15). Students can submit required documents at Document Drop-Off Events held at various community colleges or by mail or in-person drop box at MHEC offices located at 6 North Liberty Street, Baltimore, MD 21201 or 200 West Baltimore Street, Baltimore, MD 21201. Additionally, qualified children of undocumented immigrants meeting specific income and residency requirements are eligible for this state scholarship. Renewal requires maintaining at least 2.5 community college GPA, filing FAFSA or MHEC One App annually by April 1, continuing to meet income requirements, and enrolling in at least 6 credits per semester in credit-bearing programs. Award amounts are determined by MHEC based on eligibility, and eligible applicants will be notified by email in the summer. Award must be accepted online through MDCAPS portal within 2 weeks of notification or will be canceled.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 15, 2025 (priority deadline July 15); April 1, 2026 for Academic Year 2025-2026; rolling deadline for Continuing Education applicants
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland high school graduates, GED recipients, and qualified children of undocumented immigrants planning to enroll or currently enrolled at a Maryland community college or other eligible Maryland public or private institution on a full-time or part-time basis in credit-bearing vocational certificate, certificate, associate degree programs, sequences of credit or non-credit courses leading to licensure or certification, or registered apprenticeship programs. Also eligible: DACA students, undocumented individuals eligible for in-state tuition, eligible non-citizens, T Visa holders, and permanent residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To cover remaining tuition and mandatory fee expenses and educational costs at Maryland community colleges or other eligible Maryland public or private institutions after Federal or State financial aid has been applied. Funds can support enrollment in credit-bearing vocational certificate, certificate, associate degree programs, sequences of credit or non-credit courses leading to licensure or certification, or registered apprenticeship programs. Does not cover books, room, and board.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available to students at Maryland's 16 community colleges or other eligible Maryland public or private institutions. Applicants must attend the community college located in their county, or in the case of a regional community college (Wor-Wic Community College, Chesapeake College, and College of Southern Maryland), the region in which they live. If the community college in the applicant's area does not offer the desired degree or program, the applicant may attend any other Maryland community college that offers the program. Applicants may also use the scholarship at community colleges with on-campus residential facilities. Maryland residents attending Maryland community colleges are eligible. Must be eligible for in-state tuition as determined by the community college per Title 15 of Education Article of Maryland Annotated Code.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete either the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA), MHEC One App (for students ineligible for FAFSA), or Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) through the Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/MDCAPS and contact your local community college to apply. Non-credit applicants must also complete the Promise Non-Credit Application online through MDCAPS. Submit all required documentation including high school transcript or GED and income verification directly to your institution or at Document Drop-Off Events held at various community colleges or by mail or in-person drop box at MHEC offices located at 6 North Liberty Street, Baltimore, MD 21201 or 200 West Baltimore Street, Baltimore, MD 21201. The final deadline to submit all required documentation is April 15 (priority deadline July 15 for non-credit courses). Dependent students must download and submit Parent Signature Page. Monitor your MDCAPS account status page to verify no additional information is needed. Eligible applicants will be notified by email if awarded in the summer. Award must be accepted online through MDCAPS portal within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland GEAR UP Leadership Development Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program supports Maryland's GEAR UP goals to increase the number of economically disadvantaged students who intend to pursue postsecondary education. It provides summer enrichment, skill-building, and inclusive programming to secondary GEAR UP students, while educating students and their families about the advantages of postsecondary education and college financing options. Funded activities include application workshops, counseling and advising, career counseling, comprehensive mentoring, self-discovery and career exploration workshops, project leadership and management, ideation and innovation sessions, communication effectiveness workshops, and cross-cultural leadership and diversity workshops.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $45,000 may be requested by the institution in their proposal. Grant period is from June 15, 2018 to August 15, 2019. Funding supports summer enrichment, skill-building, and inclusive programming for secondary GEAR UP students. Institutions must partner with Local Education Agencies (LEA) to select funded activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monday, May 7, 2018 at 4:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited Maryland public or not-for-profit independent two-year or four-year institutions of higher education that partner with Local Education Agencies (LEA) to serve economically disadvantaged secondary students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Summer enrichment, skill-building, and inclusive programming including application workshops, counseling and advising, career counseling, comprehensive mentoring, self-discovery and career exploration workshops, project leadership and management, ideation and innovation sessions, communication effectiveness workshops, and cross-cultural leadership and diversity workshops.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service regions include Baltimore City, Dorchester County, and Wicomico County.

Must partner with a Local Education Agency (LEA)
Must submit a completed and signed Cooperative Agreement by the submission deadline
Proposals must include both electronic and hard copies submitted by May 7, 2018 at 4:00 p.m.
Up to $45,000 may be requested

Develop a proposal in partnership with a Local Education Agency. Include a completed and signed Cooperative Agreement. Submit both electronic and hard copies to Kendall E. Cook at the Maryland Higher Education Commission by May 7, 2018 at 4:00 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland GEAR UP Workforce Employability and Leadership Skills Program (WELSP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal college access program funded by the U.S. Department of Education under Title IV of the Higher Education Act, providing workforce employability and leadership skills education to low-income and first-generation students in GEAR UP cohort. The program centers on career exploration and educational planning that promotes self-efficacy and connects youth to professional sectors. It focuses on training students to understand core values, sharpen soft skills, set obtainable goals, and hone interests through career and job exploration. The program offers in-school soft skills and leadership workshops, career counseling, summer programs, workplace readiness training, youth employment opportunities, and educates students and families about the benefits of postsecondary education and college financing. Activities include soft skills workshops (communication, collaboration, self-management, advocacy), leadership workshops (cross-cultural leadership, creative innovation, project management, commitment and responsibility), career and job exploration counseling, summer programming, workforce readiness training, rigorous academic curriculum support, college preparation, remedial academic support, college tours, professional development for educators, and family engagement activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to accredited public or not-for-profit two- or four-year institutions of higher education in partnership with local education agencies (LEAs). Grant awards range from $24,249 to $90,000 per institution with five or more awards anticipated. Grantees are required to provide a 25% matching contribution (cash and/or in-kind). Funds support in-school soft skill and leadership workshops, career exploration counseling, summer programs, workplace readiness training, youth employment activities, academic support, mentoring, and educational outreach. Grant funds are disbursed in two 50% payments, with the second payment contingent on interim report approval. Funds support salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and other approved project costs. Indirect costs cannot exceed 8%. Monthly time and effort reporting is required to track employee salary charges to grants and compliance with federal audit regulations. Funds supplement new and/or existing programs and cannot supplant non-grant funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, November 13, 2020 at 4:00 PM (FY2021); Thursday, September 5, 2019 at 4:00 PM (FY2020)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited public or not-for-profit two- or four-year institutions of higher education in partnership with local education agencies serving low-income and first-generation GEAR UP students in eligible school districts. Program serves secondary students (middle and high school, particularly 12th grade students), teachers, parents, and postsecondary faculty and administrators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries and wages for professional and support personnel; fringe benefits; travel expenses; equipment; materials and supplies; consultant and contractual services; rental of space; in-school/virtual soft skills and leadership workshops; career and job exploration counseling; summer programs; workplace readiness training; youth employment activities; academic support and mentoring; college access services and information; financial aid awareness programming; remedial course support (mathematics and English/language arts); food programs through extended FARMS programs; college tours; professional development for educators; family engagement and parent/guardian programming; indirect costs (maximum 8%). Funds must supplement new and/or existing programs and cannot be used to supplant non-grant funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program operates in Maryland GEAR UP school districts: Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties. Geographic service areas must be named in proposal with participating local education agencies. Travel limited to Maryland and District of Columbia metro area.

Unbound original proposal must be submitted to MHEC office with electronic copy sent to kendall.cook@maryland.gov. Each partner must summarize their responsibilities and duties. Signatures from authorized institutional authorities and all required partners are required. Multiple pages and duplicates are allowed if needed for additional partners. Grantees complete interim and final reporting with project status, evaluation results, participant data, activity descriptions, contact hours, budget summaries with expenditure narratives, and financial documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Higher Education Outreach and College Access Program (MD-HEOCAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program that provides funds to eligible nonprofit organizations to increase college and career awareness and college completion for low-income Maryland high school students. The program supports statewide outreach efforts that encourage low-income students to attend and complete college through college access initiatives and educational opportunities. Grants of up to $100,000 are awarded on a competitive basis for a 12-month grant period with a one-to-one matching funds requirement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 awarded on a competitive basis for a 12-month grant period. Funds are disbursed in two payments: 50% upon award and 50% upon receipt and approval of the interim report. Requires one-to-one matching funds equal to the total grant funds requested. Funding supports college outreach and access programs including personnel and fringe benefits, travel for essential personnel, equipment (non-expendable, useful life >1 year), supplies, consultant and contractual services, and all costs directly related to project activities and services. Indirect costs are capped at 8% of total direct costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monday, October 6, 2025 4:00 PM
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and public and private institutions of higher education working to increase college access for low-income Maryland high school students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel and fringe benefits, travel costs for essential personnel, equipment (non-expendable, useful life greater than 1 year), supplies (expendable and non-expendable), consultant and contractual services, and all costs directly related to project activities and services designed to increase college access and completion, including postsecondary awareness, college admission requirements education, and FAFSA/financial aid awareness. Indirect costs up to 8% of total direct costs are allowed. Funds must supplement rather than supplant existing programs. All publications must acknowledge MHEC and include required disclaimer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Organizations must be located in Maryland and serve low-income Maryland high school students statewide. Priority consideration given to communities with the highest concentrated child poverty rates in each county, particularly those eligible under the Governor's Office for Children ENOUGH Grant Program.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit applications according to the Request for Proposals (RFP). Applications must include a cover sheet with organization and project director information, a project abstract (250-300 words) summarizing project needs, purpose, and projected outcomes, and authorization by a VP-level or above official. Applications are submitted electronically as PDF proposal and Word abstract to Anthony Reiner by the deadline. Initial review for formatting and completeness is conducted, followed by review panel evaluation using a scoring rubric (100 points total). MHEC may request additional information or project changes if needed. Funding recommendations are approved by the Secretary of Higher Education prior to grant award notification. Selected grantees carry out approved projects during the 12-month grant period and submit interim progress reports (due March 16) and final reports (due September 30) documenting activities, outcomes, budget expenditures, project progress, and objectives met.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland John R. Justice Grant Student Loan Repayment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal-funded program designed to encourage qualified individuals to enter and continue employment as prosecutors and public defenders by providing student loan repayment assistance. The program provides grants to assist qualified state and federal Maryland public defenders and prosecutors who are licensed attorneys in repaying qualified student loans, including Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, consolidation loans, and Perkins loans. Recipients must commit to a minimum three-year initial service obligation agreement (minimum 1 year for subsequent terms), and the full grant award must be repaid if the service obligation is not fulfilled.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct loan repayment assistance for outstanding balances on qualified federal education loans, including Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, consolidation loans, and Perkins loans. Maximum of $10,000 per calendar year with an aggregate total of $60,000. Funds are distributed equally between prosecutors and public defenders, with each appellate court district receiving an equal share. Recipients are selected based on student loan debt to adjusted gross income (AGI) ratio and cost of living factor, with highest loan debt/AGI ratio within each district prioritized. Applicants not receiving other loan repayment or forgiveness benefits are prioritized. Recipients must sign a three-year initial service obligation agreement (minimum 1 year for subsequent terms) to receive the grant. If the grant recipient fails to fulfill the service obligation, they must repay the full grant award. Recipients must continue making personal loan payments and are responsible for any income tax obligations. Direct payments are made to loan holders on behalf of eligible beneficiaries, not to beneficiaries themselves.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application Closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time state and federal public defenders and prosecutors who are continually licensed attorneys. Must be employed by the state of Maryland, units of local government (including tribal government), nonprofit organizations operating under contract with state or local government, or as federal defender attorneys.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Student loan repayment for qualified federal education loans including Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, consolidation loans, and Perkins loans. Supplement to personal obligations, not a substitute.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be employed in Maryland as public defenders or prosecutors at the state or federal level, or with a local government unit, tribal government, nonprofit organization under contract with the state or local government, or as a federal defender attorney. Geographic distribution is by appellate court district and county of employment.

Provide Social Security Number for eligibility verification. Contact the office for current application procedures and availability.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Foster Care Recipients
structured_extraction.program_description: A state assistance program that provides financial assistance to help foster care recipients repay their educational loans. The program is available to foster care recipients who are employed by the state, county, or local government in Maryland and who earned an undergraduate or graduate degree from a Maryland college. The program provides direct repayment assistance equal to the lesser of 10% of the applicant's total educational loan debt or $5,000 per year. Awards are automatically renewed annually for up to a maximum of three years if required documentation is submitted each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct repayment assistance equal to the lesser of 10% of the applicant's total educational loan debt or $5,000 per year, contingent on the availability of funds. Awards are automatically renewed annually for up to a maximum of three years if required documentation is submitted each year.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of educational loans from a university, government, or commercial source that were used to pay college expenses for undergraduate or graduate degree programs at Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents who were placed in out-of-home placement by the state or a unit of state government's department of social services and must be employed in Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an online application and required documentation through the link on the program website to the Office of Student Financial Assistance by the closing date. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Required documentation includes employment verification form, institutional certification form, lender verification form, proof of foster care for at least 3 years, and signed 2025 Maryland state income tax return or Federal Form 1040 or a Non-filing statement letter from the IRS. One lender verification form is required per loan. Applicants should submit the paper application available on the MHEC website and supplemental documentation via Google form, then email careerbased.mhec@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Police Officers and Probation Agents
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides state financial assistance to help repay educational loans for individuals working as police officers, probation agents, or fire and explosive investigators in Maryland law enforcement, parole and probation, and fire marshal agencies. Awards are calculated based on the applicant's annual salary as a percentage of total loan debt, with percentages ranging from 10% to 40% depending on debt level. Recipients can receive renewal awards for up to three years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards are calculated based on the applicant's annual salary as a percentage of total loan debt. The percentage ranges from 10% to 40% depending on debt level: below $15,000 receives 10%, $15,000-$40,000 receives 20%, $40,000-$75,000 receives 30%, and over $75,000 receives 40%. The payment amount cannot exceed the total debt owed. Recipients can receive renewal awards for up to three years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2026 for the 2025-2026 academic year; October 15, 2026 for the 2026-2027 application
structured_extraction.program_audience: Police officers, probation agents, and fire and explosive investigators employed by eligible Maryland law enforcement, parole and probation agencies, and fire marshal offices who hold degrees from public colleges or universities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of educational loans for graduate, professional, or undergraduate degrees in criminal law, criminology, or criminal justice.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; degree must be from a public college or university in Maryland; employment must be with eligible law enforcement, parole and probation, or fire marshal agencies serving the state of Maryland.

All required documents are submitted online through the applicant's MDCAPS account. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Police Officer and Probation Agent Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program providing financial assistance to current police officers or probation agents, or individuals planning to become police officers or probation agents who are enrolled in academic programs that further their careers in law enforcement. Recipients must commit to working as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for at least five years during the eight-year period after graduation. The program provides annual scholarship awards equal to 50% of the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate student at eligible Maryland public senior institutions. The scholarship does not have to be repaid if the service obligation is fulfilled; if the service obligation is not fulfilled, it converts to a loan. The program also provides educational assistance to Maryland police officers and their families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship award equal to 50% of the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate student at eligible Maryland public senior institutions. Recipients must commit to working as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland upon completion of their studies. The scholarship does not have to be repaid if the service obligation is fulfilled; if the service obligation is not fulfilled, it converts to a loan. Scholarship funds are available for police officers and their families for educational expenses. The institution certifies eligibility at the beginning of each semester, and payment is processed approximately 4 weeks after certification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application for the 2025-2026 academic year will close April 1, 2026. The application for the 2026-2027 academic year will become available January 15, 2026 and will close October 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Higher Education Commission Office of Student Financial Assistance

Also includes Maryland police officers and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees for undergraduate or graduate academic programs that further the recipient's career in law enforcement and educational expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents or have graduated from a Maryland high school and must be enrolled at a Maryland public senior institution. Must work as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland upon completion of studies. Current police officers must work for qualifying Maryland law enforcement agencies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Teacher Quality and Diversity Competitive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides competitive grants to teacher preparation programs at Maryland accredited institutions of higher education to help students from groups historically underrepresented in teaching—including African Americans, American Indians/Alaska Natives, Hispanics/Latinos, students from low-income backgrounds, first-generation college students, and individuals with disabilities—achieve teacher preparation and certification requirements. It supports alternative accelerated pathways into teaching, consortium-based proposals, and comprehensive standards-aligned programming with mentoring for diverse teacher candidates, credit for prior learning, transfer pathways from community colleges, and targeted interventions for male-identifying students. Grants are supported through state, special, and/or federal funding to improve teacher quality and promote diversity in the teaching profession.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual competitive grants totaling $1,000,000 distributed through two tracks: Individual track awards between $50,000 to $150,000, and Consortium track awards between $250,000 to $500,000. 100% of total grant award disbursed at beginning of project period. Up to 8% of direct costs permitted for indirect cost recovery. Grants support teacher preparation program expansion, student support services, developing highly qualified teachers and leaders from diverse backgrounds, alternative accelerated pathways into teaching, comprehensive mentoring, and targeted interventions for male-identifying students. Eligible expenditures include salaries and wages for professional and support personnel, fringe benefits, travel for essential personnel, equipment (non-expendable, useful life >1 year), supplies and materials, consultant and contractual services, development and administration of competency-based curricula and assessments, student success services (academic advising, certification exam preparation), faculty or teacher mentor stipends, evaluation-related costs, and other specified expenditures (insurance, permits, space rental, etc.).

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Tuition Waiver for Homeless Youth
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Tuition Waiver for Homeless Youth provides financial assistance to homeless youth who are experiencing homelessness and are enrolled as candidates for an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate at a Maryland public institution of higher education. Eligible students are exempted from paying tuition and mandatory fees, including registration fees and other mandatory enrollment fees. The waiver applies to tuition and fees for credit-bearing and noncredit courses required as a condition of enrollment and covers all academic majors. Students remain exempt from paying tuition and fees until ten years after first enrolling as a candidate for a degree or certificate, or until they are awarded a bachelor's degree, whichever occurs first. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students are exempt from paying tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and other mandatory enrollment fees) at any Maryland public college or university. The waiver applies to tuition and fees for credit-bearing and noncredit courses required as a condition of enrollment and covers all academic majors, including credit-bearing and non-credit-bearing vocational certificate programs. Students remain exempt from paying tuition and fees until ten years after first enrolling as a candidate for a degree or certificate, or until they are awarded a bachelor's degree, whichever occurs first. The waiver covers up to four additional years of enrollment or until a bachelor's degree is awarded. The waiver is eligible for fall, winter, spring, and summer semesters. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation. Scholarships or grants received may not be applied to tuition as it is already waived. Applicants must file FAFSA or MHEC One-App and contact their financial aid office to apply.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1, 2025 (for Maryland state aid); June 30, 2026 (federal aid deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unaccompanied homeless youth and youth in unstable housing who have been verified as homeless under the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act at any time during the 24 months immediately preceding enrollment or while enrolled in a Maryland public institution of higher education. Students must be age 25 or younger at the time of enrollment. Must lack fixed, regular, and adequate housing and be living in shelters, parks, motels, hotels, public spaces, camping grounds, cars, abandoned buildings, or temporarily with others. May qualify if fleeing an abusive situation despite a parent offering housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, registration fees, and other mandatory fees required for enrollment at Maryland public institutions of higher education for candidate programs in associate degrees, bachelor's degrees, or vocational certificates. Can be used for federal and/or state student financial aid to pay the cost of attending an institution of higher education. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide—all Maryland public institutions of higher education. Students must have a consistent presence in Maryland for at least one year before enrollment, documented by school, employment, or other records. Court determinations of homelessness must be from the student's state of legal residence.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply for the Maryland Tuition Waiver for Homeless Youth, contact the financial aid office at the Maryland public college or university you are attending or plan to attend. Eligibility information is provided to Maryland public colleges and universities by the Maryland Department of Human Services. Eligible applicants are encouraged to complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa or the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) via the MHEC One App at http://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/. Awards between $5,000 and $60,000 support the completion of terminal degrees and practice and dissertation research. Individual grants typically range from $20,000 to $30,000. The program seeks to increase the number of Maryland nursing faculty with doctoral qualifications to teach future generations of nurses and conduct research that improves nursing science and practice.
