structured_extraction.program_description: NSP II is a competitive multi-year funding program that expands the capacity of nursing education programs at Maryland institutions to increase the number of highly-educated nurses with baccalaureate or doctorate degrees. The program provides up to $90 million in funding over five years ($18 million annually) to support nursing education, workforce development, and training. NSP II addresses Maryland's nursing shortage through support for nursing schools, faculty development, partnerships across community colleges, universities, and hospital health systems, and doctoral education for nurse educators. The program operates through two funding tracks: the Competitive Institutional Grant Program (for individual nursing schools seeking to increase nurse enrollment, expand educational capacity, develop new cohorts, implement entry-to-practice programs, and prepare students for licensure examinations) and Statewide Initiatives (including New Nurse Faculty Fellowships, Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research, Hal and Jo Cohen Graduate Nursing Faculty Scholarship, and Academic Nurse Educator Certification). Competitive institutional grants support initiatives like new program cohorts, curriculum development, exam preparation resources, career promotion activities, new nursing program instructor support, planning for PhD nursing education programs, building nurse-managed health centers, increasing nursing program enrollment, and developing certificate programs in research. Funding comes from an allocation of up to 0.1 percent of regulated gross hospital revenue. Funding helps address Maryland's nursing shortage by supporting innovative nursing education initiatives at higher education institutions. Recent awards include FY24 ($5.8 million across nine programs), FY 2023 ($4,101,847 across 13 proposals at 12 institutions), and FY 2019 ($9.6 million across 16 approved proposals).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NSP II provides up to $90 million in funding over five years ($18 million annually) to Maryland nursing programs through competitive institutional grants and statewide initiatives. Funding comes from an allocation of up to 0.1 percent of regulated gross hospital revenue. Grant types include one-year planning grants, three-year full implementation grants, continuation grants, one-year resource grants, and nursing resource grants. Award amounts vary based on the project's ability to impact the nursing shortage in a timely manner, the depth and breadth of the initiative, and budget feasibility. Funds support nursing school capacity building, faculty recruitment and retention, graduate tuition support, course release time for doctoral completion, leadership development programs, new nurse faculty fellowships (maximum $20,000 funding across multiple years), Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research (maximum $26,000 tuition/fees plus $50,000 living expenses), clinical simulation training, new nursing program instructor support, planning for PhD nursing education programs, building nurse-managed health centers, increasing nursing program enrollment, developing certificate programs in research, purchasing exam software and testing resources, clinical site development and coordination, classroom and lab facility expansion, student tutoring and mentoring, scholarships and tuition support, living expense assistance, curriculum redesign, ESOL training for diverse students, orientation and training for new nursing graduates, specialty credentialing, career advancement programs, reference materials, anatomical models, and certification examination review materials. Statewide initiatives include New Nurse Faculty Fellowships (NNFF), Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research (NEDG), Hal and Jo Cohen Graduate Nursing Faculty Scholarship (GNF), and Academic Nurse Educator Certification (ANEC). Funding is allocated to 28 nursing programs across 15 community colleges and 13 universities.

Funds support programs focused on nursing graduate outcomes and partnerships across community colleges, universities, and hospital health systems, with particular emphasis on creating opportunities for geographically underserved nursing students in western Maryland. Additional funding uses include clinical site development and coordination, classroom and lab facility expansion, student tutoring and mentoring, scholarships and tuition support, living expense assistance, curriculum redesign, clinical simulations development, ESOL training for diverse students, orientation and training for new nursing graduates, specialty credentialing, career advancement programs, reference materials, anatomical models, certification examination review materials, and professional development and loan repayment for nursing faculty.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nurse Support Program II (NSP II) - New Nursing Faculty Fellowship (NNFF)
structured_extraction.program_description: An ongoing fellowship program that awards financial support to nursing faculty members at Maryland universities and community colleges to recruit, retain, and develop new nurse faculty. New recipients receive either $50,000 disbursed over five years ($10,000 per year) or $20,000 over three years ($10,000 in year one, $5,000 in years two and three). Previously awarded faculty members receive annual disbursements ($10,000 annually or $5,000 annually based on program structure) based on continued full-time employment in good standing. The program increases the state's academic capacity to educate nurses and supports recruitment and retention of nursing faculty. Recipients are evaluated at specified employment milestones. Funding supports faculty salaries, technological advancements, and tools to meet healthcare workforce demands. This program has been in place since 2005 and awards funding based on nomination requests from Maryland Deans and Directors of Nursing Programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nurse Support Program II - Academic Nurse Educator Certification Awards
structured_extraction.program_description: Financial support for full-time nurse faculty at Maryland higher education institutions to complete professional development and continuing education requirements to obtain and maintain the Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential from the National League for Nursing, which demonstrates expertise in nursing education. Recipients receive $5,000 awards to support these requirements, including CNE examination fees, continuing education, professional certifications and licensing, and professional organization dues. Funds can be used for continuing professional certifications and licensing for clinical specialty, examination fees, continuing education requirements to maintain the credential, and payment of dues for professional organizations. The award program provides recognition and financial support to nurse faculty who have achieved or maintained their CNE credential through their institution's nomination. A total of 34 nurse faculty received awards, with $170,000 distributed to eligible faculty at 15 higher education institutions, including nine community colleges and six universities throughout Maryland.

Faculty nominated by deans and directors of nursing from Maryland higher education institutions receive the funds, which may be used for any professional development activity that enhances the faculty member's career. Total awards of $170,000 were distributed to 34 eligible faculty at 15 higher education institutions across Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Part-Time Grant Program provides state financial aid to part-time undergraduate students enrolled in degree-granting programs at Maryland public and independent colleges and universities, as well as students dually enrolled at a Maryland high school and an institution of higher education. The program supports students with demonstrated financial need, including qualified children of undocumented immigrants and DACA students who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland law. Grant awards range from a minimum of $200 to a maximum of $2,000 per academic year. Recipients are selected and awarded by the institution based on demonstrated financial need as determined by FAFSA or Maryland State Financial Aid Application. This need-based grant does not have to be repaid. Students may receive a Part-Time Grant for a total of eight years.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Need-based grant providing financial assistance to part-time degree-seeking undergraduates and students dually enrolled at a Maryland high school and postsecondary institution. Grant awards range from a minimum of $200 to a maximum of $2,000 per academic year. Awards are based on demonstrated financial need as determined by the FAFSA or Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MHEC One App). Funds are distributed by institutions to eligible part-time undergraduate students and do not have to be repaid. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students. Students may receive awards for a maximum of eight years total. Program is also available to undocumented students and DACA students who qualify for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state financial aid scholarship program supporting diverse undergraduate and graduate students who are members of Reserve Officer Training Corps (ROTC) programs at designated Maryland universities, as well as qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland law. The program promotes the state's interests in educating diverse student bodies and achieving diversity in higher education and ROTC programs by providing financial assistance to minority students and students from groups historically underrepresented in ROTC. Annual scholarship awards are prescribed by MHEC, not to exceed the recipient's education expenses, with a minimum award of $500 per semester ($1,000 per academic year). Recipients with financial need are prioritized and awards are renewable for up to three years if eligibility requirements are maintained.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program awarded by members of the Maryland General Assembly and administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC). Individual delegates provide financial assistance to Maryland residents who plan to pursue postsecondary credentials full-time or part-time at two-year or four-year Maryland colleges, universities, or private career schools. For 2026-2027, the minimum award is $200 with the maximum amount to be determined. The scholarship is not renewable; students must reapply each year. Educational expenses can be covered at Maryland institutions or, in certain cases, out-of-state institutions if the major is not available in Maryland, the applicant is on active military duty domiciled in Maryland, or the student is disabled and needs special provisions not available in Maryland. The program includes an appeal process for students enrolled in less than 6 credits due to disability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship award with 2026-2027 minimum of $200 and maximum amount not yet determined. Students may hold this scholarship with all state awards, but total state scholarship awards cannot exceed the student's cost of attendance. Contact your state delegate for application and deadline information. If OSFA administers the award, FAFSA or MSFAA must be filed by March 1. The scholarship is not renewable; students must reapply each year. Funding can be used for educational expenses including tuition and fees. Students enrolled in less than 6 credits due to disability may appeal during Fall (July 1 - December 15, 2026) or Spring (October 1, 2026 - April 15, 2027) appeal windows. OSFA will review appeals and make determinations within 45 business days.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Current or prospective students should contact their local State Delegate for instructions on how to apply. The student can find their local delegates and contact information by visiting the Maryland General Assembly website or the Maryland State Board of Elections website. structured_extraction.program_name: Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for Maryland taxpayers and residents who have incurred significant student loan debt (incurred by the applicant, not parent). The program provides annual tax credits that recipients must use to pay down their college loan balances. Eligible applicants must have incurred at least $20,000 in undergraduate and/or graduate student loan debt and have at least $5,000 in outstanding student loan debt when applying. Recipients who attended Maryland institutions receive $1,000 in tax credits, while those who attended out-of-state institutions receive $883 in tax credits. If the credit exceeds taxes owed, recipients receive a refund for the difference. Recipients must agree to pay the complete tax credit received into their outstanding loan balance within the specified timeframe (currently three years from the close of the tax year, two years for 2018 tax year) and provide proof of payment. The program is administered through the tax system by the Maryland Higher Education Commission.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit totaling up to $1,000 (for Maryland institution attendees) or $883 (for out-of-state institution attendees) is awarded to eligible Maryland taxpayers and applied to their state income tax return. If the credit exceeds taxes owed, recipients receive a refund for the difference. Recipients must pay the credited amount toward their outstanding student loan debt within the specified timeframe from the close of the applicable tax year (three years for current tax years, two years for 2018 tax year). Payments can be made in a lump sum or installments and may consist of principal and/or interest. Proof of payment is submitted through the OneStop portal or as required by the program. Failure to provide proof of payment within the required window results in recapture of the credit by the State through the Office of the Comptroller.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application from www.mhec.maryland.gov. Selection criteria for recipients are set out in the Code of Maryland Regulations (COMAR). After receiving the award, recipients must log into their OneStop account and attach proof of payment documents showing they have paid the credited amount toward their loan balances. Claim the credit on the Maryland income tax return when filing Maryland taxes. Residents can apply for next year's tax credit through the program website. MHEC staff processes applications and determines eligibility based on residency status and the location of the institution attended.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program awarded to students who commit to working as a public school or public prekindergarten teacher in Maryland upon completion of their studies. Recipients must teach in high-needs schools as identified by MSDE, schools where at least 50% of students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals, or in grade levels or content areas where there is a shortage of qualified educators. The program serves high school seniors, college students pursuing undergraduate or graduate degrees leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate, career changers, and teaching assistants with at least 2 years of experience. The scholarship covers tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at eligible Maryland institutions. Undergraduate recipients must work as teachers for one year for each year of scholarship received. Graduate recipients must work as teachers for two years for each year of scholarship received. Awards are reviewed and made on a weekly basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: At Maryland public senior higher education institutions, the scholarship covers 100% of annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board for a resident undergraduate or graduate student. At Maryland private nonprofit institutions, the award is either 100% of tuition and mandatory fees at University of Maryland College Park plus 100% of room and board at the recipient's institution, or 50% of the institution's tuition and mandatory fees plus 100% of room and board at the institution. Private nonprofit institutions must provide a matching scholarship for tuition and fees. A housing allowance based on room and board costs is included for students with off-campus or parental housing status. Undergraduate recipients must work as teachers for one year for each year of scholarship received. Graduate recipients must work as teachers for two years for each year of scholarship received. Recipients may renew annually for up to three years (or four years for programs requiring five years to complete) if they maintain full-time or part-time enrollment, make satisfactory progress toward their degree, and maintain institutional standards. Awards are reviewed and made on a weekly basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis - applications reviewed weekly. The 2025-2026 academic year application closes on April 1, 2026. The 2026-2027 academic year application opens on January 15, 2026, with an application deadline of October 15, 2026. Additional deadline: December 1.

Also includes students attending Maryland colleges or universities who want to become teachers in Maryland public schools or public prekindergarten programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board for undergraduate or graduate students enrolled in a course of study leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate. Funds support educational expenses for students pursuing teacher certification at eligible institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Applicants must commit to teaching in Maryland upon completion of studies. Recipients must teach in high-needs schools as identified by MSDE, schools where at least 50% of students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals, or in grade levels or content areas where there is a shortage of qualified educators. If no qualifying positions are available, recipients may teach in any public school or public prekindergarten program in Maryland. Applicants are no longer required to be Maryland residents. Maryland state residency is no longer required as of the 2024-2025 program year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title IX Campus Sexual Assault Proceedings - Attorney Reimbursement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Program providing attorney fee reimbursement for legal representation in Title IX campus sexual assault proceedings at Maryland colleges and universities. The Maryland Higher Education Commission pays attorney fees and certain costs for legal representation of students in Title IX proceedings covering investigation, mediation, hearing, and appeal phases. Attorneys may request reimbursement for legal services and reimbursable travel costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Attorneys representing students in Title IX proceedings may request reimbursement at $120 per hour, billed in increments of 6 minutes or less, for legal services provided on or after August 1, 2019. The program covers up to 20 hours per case; list attorneys must provide representation beyond 20 hours pro bono, while non-list attorneys' excess hours are billable to the student. MHEC list attorneys cannot charge clients fees exceeding $100/hour. Attorneys may also request reimbursement for travel costs to and from the university, including mileage at $0.70 per mile, tolls, public transit, and parking, up to $200 total, with receipts required. Office expenses are not covered. Payment requests must be submitted within 60 days of termination of representation and are subject to availability of appropriated funds. Reimbursement does not cover civil, criminal, or non-Title IX disciplinary proceedings.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tuition Reduction for Non-Resident Nursing Students
structured_extraction.program_description: A state aid program that provides out-of-state students enrolled in nursing programs at Maryland public institutions with a reduction in tuition to match in-state rates. The award amount equals the tuition differential—the difference between out-of-state tuition and in-state tuition at the same institution in the same nursing program for the identical number of credit hours. The institution adjusts tuition charges so the student pays the in-state rate. Awards renew automatically for an additional year if attending a two-year institution, or for an additional three years if attending a four-year institution, provided the student maintains satisfactory academic progress and remains enrolled in an eligible nursing program. Recipients must agree to serve as a full-time nurse in a hospital or related institution for a specified period or repay the scholarship with interest.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The annual award amount equals the tuition differential—the difference between out-of-state and in-state tuition at the same institution for the same nursing program and number of credit hours. The institution adjusts tuition charges so the student pays only in-state rates. Awards are automatically renewed for an additional year for two-year institution attendees or three additional years for four-year institution attendees, provided the student maintains satisfactory academic progress and remains enrolled in an eligible nursing program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tuition Waiver for Students with Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tuition assistance to students with disabilities receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits at Maryland public higher education institutions, including community colleges. The waiver covers tuition costs for degree or certificate programs designed to lead to employment, and continuing education instruction including life skills training. At community colleges, students are exempt from paying tuition for up to 12 credits per semester if enrolled in a degree or certificate program designed to lead to employment, limited to 6 credits for other community college credit courses. The waiver applies to the remaining tuition balance after any grants and scholarships are applied. A course must have at least 10 enrolled students for the waiver to apply. Students must file FAFSA and contact their financial aid office to apply.

For community colleges: up to 12 credits per semester if enrolled in a degree or certificate program designed to lead to employment, limited to 6 credits for other community college credit courses. The waiver applies to the remaining tuition balance after any grants and scholarships are applied. A course must have at least 10 enrolled students for the waiver to apply. Students are responsible for all other costs such as books. Eligible students must receive SSI or SSDI benefits.

structured_extraction.program_description: An incentive program that awards $50,000 college scholarships to young people ages 12 to 17 who get vaccinated against COVID-19. The scholarship covers full tuition and fees at a public, in-state institution of higher education in Maryland. Twenty winners are selected through random drawings, with two winners selected per week for eight weeks beginning July 12, and four additional winners selected on Labor Day. Winners receive the award as either a 4-Year Maryland Prepaid College Trust Account for winners ages 12-14, or a Maryland College Investment Plan contribution for winners ages 15-17. Winners may remain anonymous, though their county or city of residence will be published.

Two winners per week will be selected for eight weeks beginning July 12, with four additional winners selected on Labor Day (September 6). Each winner receives a $50,000 scholarship distributed as either a 4-Year Maryland Prepaid College Trust Account (for ages 12-14) or a Maryland College Investment Plan contribution (for ages 15-17), which covers full tuition and fees at a public, in-state institution of higher education in Maryland. Winners are selected using a random number generator and may remain anonymous, though their county or city of residence will be published.

structured_extraction.program_name: Workforce Shortage Student Assistance Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Workforce Shortage Student Assistance Grant Program provides financial assistance to Maryland residents pursuing degrees in fields with workforce shortages, including child development or early childhood education, human services, teaching in critical shortage areas, nursing, physical and occupational therapy, social work, law for public service, and other public service careers. Recipients must commit to working in their field in Maryland after graduation. Financial assistance is provided based on institution type and enrollment status. Community college students receive $2,000 per year for full-time enrollment (12+ credits per semester) or $1,000 per year for part-time enrollment (6-11 credits per semester). Four-year institution undergraduate students receive $4,000 per year for full-time enrollment (12+ credits per semester) or $2,000 per year for part-time enrollment (6-11 credits per semester). Graduate students at four-year institutions receive $4,000 per year for full-time enrollment (9+ credits per semester) or $2,000 per year for part-time enrollment (6-8 credits per semester). Awards are renewable for up to five years and do not have to be repaid. This non-repayable scholarship supports students attending two-year or four-year Maryland colleges and universities.

Graduate students at four-year institutions receive $4,000 per year for full-time enrollment (9+ credits per semester) or $2,000 per year for part-time enrollment (6-8 credits per semester). Awards are renewable for up to five years and do not have to be repaid. Educational expenses up to cost of attendance or $28,000 maximum (whichever is less) when combined with other state awards. FAFSA is optional but recommended for priority ranking and need-based consideration.

Funding supports preservation, restoration, rehabilitation, development of new facilities, stabilization of endangered properties, and planning services related to pre-construction work.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program for property owners and developers who rehabilitate income-producing historic buildings and districts listed in the National Register of Historic Places or certified by the National Park Service as historic structures. The Maryland Historical Trust serves as the State Historic Preservation Office and manages the state's role in the federal certification process. The program provides a federal income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified capital costs expended in the rehabilitation of eligible income-producing properties with no cap on the amount of the federal credit available. Rehabilitation projects must be substantial, defined as a minimum of $5,000 or the adjusted basis of the building, whichever is greater, and typically must be completed within a 24-month period. The program encourages private sector investment in the rehabilitation and re-use of historic buildings, creates jobs, and is one of the nation's most successful and cost-effective community revitalization programs, having leveraged $127.12 billion in private investment to preserve more than 50,000 historic properties since 1976.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: A federal income tax credit available to property owners and developers who undertake qualified rehabilitation projects on income-producing historic buildings and districts with no cap on the credit amount. The credit equals 20% of qualified capital costs expended. Rehabilitation projects must be substantial, defined as a minimum of $5,000 or the adjusted basis of the building, whichever is greater, and typically must be completed within a 24-month period. The credit is administered by the National Park Service and Internal Revenue Service, with Maryland Historical Trust providing certification recommendations and technical assistance. Applications are fully electronic through the MHT e106 portal and hard copy applications are not accepted.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Historical Trust offers capital loans to qualified borrowers to help preserve historic properties. Loans support acquisition, refinancing, rehabilitation, and predevelopment projects that benefit the public. Nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals may be eligible if they cannot access traditional financing. Energy projects as part of an acquisition, rehabilitation, or restoration are eligible expenditures. Certain qualified nonprofit organizations may also apply for nonrepayable fund transfers beginning in FY 2024.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital loans with a fixed annual interest rate set by adding 0.125% to the most recent general obligation bond rate. Nonprofits and local governments receive even lower rates. Loan terms are up to two years for pre-development projects and up to twenty years for other projects. Loan amounts typically do not exceed 80% of the appraised value and depend on available funds and the borrower's ability to repay. Loan funds support property acquisition, stabilization, rehabilitation, restoration, and predevelopment work including plans, specifications, and architectural or engineering services. Energy projects are eligible as part of acquisition, rehabilitation, or restoration activities. The program also offers non-repayable fund transfers (similar to grants) to qualified nonprofit organizations for acquisition, restoration, or providing loans to other organizations and individuals. The full loan process typically takes 6 to 9 months from application to settlement. If approved, a historic preservation easement must be conveyed to MHT.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Loan applications accepted year-round as funds become available. Transfer applications open in November and close in January.

Business entities and individuals must demonstrate they cannot obtain private financing. Qualified nonprofit organizations are eligible for nonrepayable fund transfers.

Stabilization, rehabilitation, or restoration of historic properties. Development of plans, specifications, and architectural, engineering, or other special services directly related to pre-construction work. Energy improvements as part of acquisition, rehabilitation, or restoration activities. Transfer funds for qualified nonprofits can be used to acquire properties for resale, restore properties, or provide loans to other organizations and individuals. Funds cannot pay for routine maintenance, fundraising expenses, research, exhibits, or work already started or completed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland income tax credit program that provides state income tax credits for qualified rehabilitation expenditures on certified historic properties. The program offers three separate credit structures: one for homeowners, one for owners of small commercial buildings, and one for major rehabilitations. Tax credits are available for eligible properties that are listed on the National Register of Historic Places, contributing to historic districts, or certified as contributing to heritage area importance. Credits can be applied to primary residences, secondary residences, or commercial properties and may be combined with county and federal tax credits. The program is designed to incentivize historic preservation by offsetting renovation expenses through state tax credits. Projects must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and be completed within a 24-month period. Eligible expenses include plumbing, HVAC, electrical system upgrades, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, architectural and engineering fees, interior finishes, restoration of historic landscape features, and energy improvements. Financing charges, building permit fees, new construction, and non-historic structures are not eligible.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland income tax credits for qualified rehabilitation expenditures on certified historic properties, including energy improvements. Three separate credit programs available: homeowner credits, small commercial building credits, and major rehabilitation credits. The homeowner and small commercial credits are equal to 20% of qualified capital costs. These credits are in addition to other state and county tax credits available for qualified rehabilitation work on historic structures and may be combined with county and federal tax credits. Projects must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and be completed within a 24-month period. Minimum cost threshold is $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects or the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $5,000 for all other projects. Eligible expenses include plumbing, HVAC, electrical system upgrades, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, architectural and engineering fees, interior finishes, restoration of historic landscape features, and energy improvements. Financing charges, building permit fees, new construction (such as patios and decks), and non-historic structures are not eligible. Applicants must apply before any renovations are started.

The credit equals 20% of the qualified capital costs expended, up to a maximum of $5 million per project. Projects are awarded competitively through an annual application process.

Tax credits are awarded through a competitive application process.

The credit equals 20% of the approved rehabilitation costs for projects with total expenses under $500,000, capped at $50,000 within a 24-month period. The program has a yearly funding cap of $2 million and helps strengthen Maryland's communities while encouraging local economic growth. Tax credits are available statewide for small commercial historic property rehabilitation.

The credit is capped at $50,000 within a 24-month period. Projects must have at least $5,000 in eligible expenses to qualify. Projects in Opportunity Zones may receive additional credits.

Funds cannot be used for landscaping, new construction, appliances, or tool purchases. Small commercial historic property rehabilitation is supported.
