structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact program staff early in the planning process. The application has three parts. Part 1 certifies that the building is a historic structure. Part 2 certifies that the proposed project meets program requirements. Part 3 certifies that the completed project meets program requirements. Applicants must submit all parts for approval before starting work.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program - Homeowner Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives homeowners a state income tax credit for restoring historic houses. The credit is 20 percent of qualified project costs, capped at $50,000 over a 24-month period. Projects must have a minimum of $5,000 in eligible expenses. The program encourages investment in historic neighborhoods and helps Marylanders preserve their homes for future generations.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners can receive a state income tax credit for 20% of qualified repair costs. The credit is capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period. Projects must have at least $5,000 in eligible expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kate Jaffe, Dana Marks, or Carey Jones
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners with historic properties who live in their single-family historic home, either as a primary or secondary residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic home rehabilitation and preservation. Funds can be used for projects that repair or alter a historic home while preserving its important features. Examples include: Roof repair or replacement; Chimney repair; Window restoration; New storm doors or windows; Masonry repointing; Floor refinishing; Structural repairs; Plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. The home must be a certified historic structure, meaning it is either listed in the National Register of Historic Places, is a contributing resource within a National Register Historic District, or is a locally designated structure that the Maryland Historical Trust determines is eligible for the National Register.
requirements_list: Must be a single-family, owner-occupied residence.
The building must be a certified historic structure.
Projects must have a minimum of $5,000 in eligible expenses.
All work must be reviewed and approved by the Maryland Historical Trust before starting.
The project must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, read the application instructions and contact tax credit staff for guidance. Second, download and complete the three-part application. Part 1 certifies that your home is a historic structure. Part 2 certifies that the proposed work meets program standards. Part 3 certifies that the completed project meets the standards and documents eligible expenses.

structured_extraction.program_description: Mini-grants available in Maryland's heritage areas for non-capital heritage-related projects such as educational programming or planning efforts under $5,000. Each of Maryland's 13 heritage areas may offer mini-grants for heritage-related non-capital projects under $5,000. The specific amount and application details vary by heritage area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each of Maryland's 13 heritage areas may offer mini-grants for heritage-related non-capital projects under $5,000. The specific amount and application details vary by heritage area.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ariane Hofstedt, Andrew Arvizu, Martha Waldron
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations, agencies, and local partners within Maryland's heritage areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heritage-related non-capital projects including educational programming and planning efforts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland heritage areas (13 designated heritage areas)
requirements_list: Projects must be heritage-related
Projects must be non-capital
Project cost must be under $5,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit individual heritage area websites to learn more and apply for mini-grants.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Museum Assistance Program provides grants to support Maryland museums and institutional collections. The program helps historical and cultural museums strengthen operations, build professional capacity, and improve long-term sustainability by funding eligible everyday operational costs and programs. The program aims to interpret Maryland's rich history, promote tourism, support public education, and encourage professionalism within museum practice.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $20,000 with typical awards between $10,000 and $15,000. No match is required. In FY26, $285,000 is available statewide for grants to support the operations and programs of historical and cultural museums.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and local government organizations that operate museums interpreting Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible activities include paying staff, training staff or volunteers, office or administrative costs such as insurance and accounting, environmental monitoring such as pest management and humidity control, and security and safety systems. Capital projects such as construction, restoration, or building repairs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Manage a museum that has been open and operating for at least three years
Be in good standing with the state
Be tax-exempt or have applied for tax-exempt status (for nonprofits)
Interpret Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology
Not be operated in whole or in part by the state or federal government
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must review the current grant guidelines, confirm project eligibility and applicant type, prepare required attachments such as cost estimates, photographs, and proof of ownership or site control, and submit a completed application through the grants portal before the posted deadline. If an applicant operates more than one museum, each museum seeking funding requires a separate application.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds projects that protect historic maritime resources and increase public awareness of the nation's maritime heritage. It supports education and preservation projects through a competitive grant process administered on behalf of the National Park Service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants of $10,000 to $100,000. Total project costs must be between $20,000 and $200,000. A one-to-one non-federal match is required. The total funding available for this competitive program is $380,192.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tribal governments, state governments, local governments, and nonprofit organizations working on historic maritime preservation and education projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include identification of historic maritime resources including archaeological sites, repair or rehabilitation of historic maritime buildings, structures, vessels and sites, and improvements that increase public access to maritime resources. All projects must include a public education component. Funds cannot support work that has already started or been completed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to projects throughout Maryland and potentially beyond, as this is a competitive national program administered by MHT on behalf of the National Park Service.
requirements_list: Projects must demonstrate clear public benefit
Projects must follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and Guidelines for Archeology and Historic Preservation
Projects must follow the Standards for Historic Vessel Preservation Projects where applicable
All projects must include a public education component

Projects must support at least one of the following: identification of historic maritime resources, repair or rehabilitation of historic maritime buildings/structures/vessels/sites, or improvements that increase public access to maritime resources
Grant funds cannot support work that has already started or been completed
Projects must have total costs between $20,000 and $200,000
A one-to-one non-federal match is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should review the grant guidelines and manual, confirm eligibility, prepare a complete application with scope of work and budget, and submit through the grants portal before the deadline. Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact MHT staff early in project planning for guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credits available for homeowners and for commercial and small commercial historic preservation projects.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits for homeowners and commercial property owners undertaking historic preservation work.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and commercial property owners restoring historic properties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic preservation and restoration work on eligible historic properties

structured_extraction.program_name: A&E District Admission and Amusement Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: An exemption from the state Admission and Amusement Tax on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges levied by arts and entertainment enterprises or qualifying resident artists located in designated Arts and Entertainment Districts. Local governments may grant this exemption to eligible entities operating in designated A&E Districts statewide, with implementation and eligibility determination handled on a case-by-case basis by local authorities and the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exemption from state Admission and Amusement Tax on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges collected by qualifying arts and entertainment enterprises or resident artists in designated Arts and Entertainment Districts. The exemption applies only to admissions or amusement charges, not other revenue streams. Eligibility is determined on a case-by-case basis by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation and local governments. Qualifying enterprises must register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Comptroller of Maryland Combined Registration Application (CRA) Form.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts and entertainment enterprises dedicated to visual or performing arts and qualifying resident artists operating in designated Arts and Entertainment Districts who charge admission or amusement fees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Admission and amusement tax exemption
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: A&E District (Arts & Entertainment District). Available in Maryland Arts and Entertainment Districts statewide where local governments choose to implement the exemption, including designated A&E Districts in Salisbury, Wicomico County, and Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an arts and entertainment enterprise or qualifying resident artist
Must be operating in a designated A&E District
Enterprise must be dedicated to visual or performing arts
Tax exemption applies only to admissions or amusement charges, not other revenue
Eligibility determined on case-by-case basis by Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Tax exemption is at discretion of local government
Businesses must qualify for the exemption and notify the State of Maryland Comptroller's Office
Must register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Comptroller of Maryland Combined Registration Application (CRA) Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Comptroller of the Treasury and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation local office for eligibility determination. Register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Comptroller of Maryland Combined Registration Application (CRA) Form. Consult the Comptroller's office at marylandtaxes.gov for current information on this tax exemption and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Arts & Entertainment District designation offers Maryland counties and municipalities tax incentives and other tools to encourage activity and investment in specific geographic areas where the arts are part of an economic development strategy.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax incentives are provided to designated Arts & Entertainment Districts to encourage activity and investment in specific geographic areas where the arts are part of an economic development strategy.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1st and October 1st
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties and municipalities seeking to develop Arts and Entertainment Districts as part of their economic development strategy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax incentives and tools to encourage activity and investment in designated Arts and Entertainment Districts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Districts must be located within designated Priority Funding Areas in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county or municipal government in Maryland
Geographic area must have a significant level of arts activity, entertainment venues, and/or arts businesses
Arts and entertainment must be included in the area's economic development strategy

Applicant must communicate with all municipalities and counties involved in the proposed district and obtain agreement with all impacted governments concerning the tax credits associated with the designation
Intent to Apply form must be completed online 90 days before the application deadline
Complete application as specified in the A&E District Designation Guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must first complete an Intent to Apply form 90 days before their chosen deadline. Districts then submit a complete application following the A&E District Designation Guidelines. Applications are reviewed in three steps: staff review for completeness and adherence to regulations, review by the MSAC A&E Districts Advisory Committee which includes representation from Commerce, Housing and Community Development, Transportation, and Planning departments plus current A&E District managers, and final decision by the Maryland Secretary of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_description: State program that develops, promotes, and supports diverse artistic and cultural centers in communities throughout Maryland. The program provides annual operating grants to appointed management entities of designated A&E Districts to support district priorities, preserve sense of place, provide unique local experiences, attract tourism, and spur economic revitalization and neighborhood pride. Funding supports district operations, activities, programs, and projects including district promotion, event/festival production, business attraction, artist support services, public art projects, real estate promotion, partnership management, fundraising, board management, and advocacy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual operating support grants provided to appointed management entities of designated A&E Districts. Funding supports district operations, activities, programs, and projects including district promotion, event/festival production, business attraction, artist support services, public art projects, real estate promotion, partnership management, fundraising, board management, and advocacy. Applicants apply either on-year (requesting funding in the fifth fiscal year post-designation with a more complete application including updated goals, objectives, strategies, outcomes, revised management and marketing plans, and proposed budget) or off-year (in all other years, including redesignation years, with a shorter application outlining proposed budget and updates). Upon execution of grant agreement, payment is processed for receipt in 6-8 weeks. Grantees must submit a final report at project completion and a brief report detailing fund use at fiscal year end.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Appointed management entities of designated Arts and Entertainment Districts in Maryland; arts and cultural organizations; artists; businesses; community members; residents of A&E Districts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: District operating activities, programs, and projects that support district priorities, including funding for operations and administration, programs or projects, and in-kind support (administration, services, etc.). Specific uses include district promotion, event/festival production, business attraction, artist support services, public art projects, real estate promotion, partnership management, fundraising, board management, and advocacy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Arts and Entertainment Districts throughout Maryland approved by the Secretary of Commerce
requirements_list: Applicant must be the appointed management entity of a designated A&E District in Maryland approved by the Secretary of Commerce
Applicant must complete a letter of agreement between the county or municipality holding the designation and the management entity
Applicant must have a current contract or MOU with a county or municipality to manage a designated A&E District
Applicant must be a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization or local government entity
Management entity must employ at least one paid employee (minimum 15 hours per week) coordinating A&E District activities
Must maintain Board of Directors or Advisory Board of at least 5 individuals representing diversity of populations and various constituencies served
Management entity must work toward A&E Districts Program goals and district-specific goals submitted in application/redesignation
Must adhere to MSAC grantmaking, crediting, and reporting requirements
Must maintain equitable, community-responsive programs and services
Must maintain website/webpage with district promotion and opportunities
Must maintain constituent distribution list
Must send regular communications promoting district and MSAC opportunities
Must maintain current profile on MSAC website
Must notify MSAC two months ahead of local grant opportunities for artists
Must provide ongoing updates on local needs through scheduled reports
Must arrange annual site visit with MSAC leadership
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The management entity for an A&E District must submit one of two forms annually: an on-year application (for the fifth fiscal year post-designation) with updated goals, objectives, strategies, outcomes, revised management and marketing plans, and proposed budget; or an off-year application (all other years including redesignation years) with a shorter format outlining proposed budget and updates. Applicant must complete a signed Letter of Agreement between local government and management entity. The A&E Districts Advisory Committee reviews on-year applications, provides feedback and opportunity for revision if needed, and recommends funding. MSAC staff reviews off-year applications. Funding recommendations are subject to approval by the Council and the Secretary of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant that provides financial support to fully developed and ready-to-implement public art initiatives in Maryland that celebrate America's semiquincentennial, marking the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The grant supports public art projects including conservation and promotion of existing works or creation and installation of new works. Eligible mediums include murals, tile mosaics, paintings, or sculptures. Awarded funding may be used for administrative fees (up to 15% of total request), artist fees and labor for Maryland-based artists and fabricators, materials for artwork including base, lighting, and landscaping, contracted services and equipment rental, studio or space rental for fabrication and assembly, signage or plaques to identify the artwork, community programming around America250 celebrations, and dedication event expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based nonprofit organizations with IRS-designated 501(c)3 status, units of state or local government, and established higher education institutions in Maryland with fully developed public art projects ready for immediate implementation. Artists and public art initiatives.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Administrative fees (up to 15% of total request), artist fees and labor for Maryland-based artists and fabricators, materials for artwork including base, lighting, and landscaping, contracted services and equipment rental, studio or space rental to fabricate and assemble the artwork, signage or plaques to identify the artwork, community programming around America250 celebrations, and dedication event expenses. Public art project creation, fabrication, and implementation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland and created by an artist, artisan, studio, or team based in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be Maryland-based nonprofit organization with IRS-designated 501(c)3 status, unit of state or local government, or established higher education institution in Maryland
Project must be located in Maryland and be the product of an artist, artisan, studio, or team based in Maryland
Artwork must be either an architectural enhancement of artistic significance or an installation of artwork with eligible mediums including murals, tile mosaics, paintings, or sculptures
Project must be fully developed and ready for immediate implementation with finalized artwork concept
All required permits and site permissions must have been acquired
Project must be entering the initial stages of implementation with ability to complete and fully install by June 30, 2026
Project must be aligned with America250 celebrations and goals
Public art project must be clear, specific, and aligned with America250 goals
Project must be site-responsive and engage the community
Lead artist and fabrication team must demonstrate artistic excellence and prior experience
Artwork must be safe, durable, and suitable for public environment
Timeline must be realistic and feasible for completion
Budget must be financially realistic and detailed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations must submit an online application by logging in or creating an account on SmartSimple, the grants management platform. Applicants are required to complete and submit applications by electronic means, including the use of an electronic signature. Applications are evaluated using a 5-point scoring rubric covering project clarity and alignment with America250 goals, site-responsiveness and community engagement, artistic excellence and prior experience of lead artist and fabrication team, feasibility and timeline for completion, and financial soundness and budget realism. Technical support for SmartSimple is available during regular office hours. Applicants must meet all revision deadlines after submission or the application will be withdrawn.

structured_extraction.program_name: Artist Income Tax Subtraction Modification for Arts and Entertainment Districts
structured_extraction.program_description: Qualified residing artists who live in Maryland and create, sell, or perform artistic work in Maryland Arts and Entertainment Districts can subtract income derived from their in-district work from their Maryland state and local income tax. For performing artists, this includes income from performances in a district; for all qualified artists, this includes sales of artistic work created in a district and internet sales originating in a district. Qualifying artists do not pay state or local income tax on this qualifying income (federal tax still applies). There is no limit on the amount that can be subtracted.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified residing artists subtract all qualifying arts and entertainment income from their Maryland state income tax and potentially local income tax (to the extent included in federal adjusted gross income). Qualifying resident artists deduct qualifying income on their tax form before state and local taxes are calculated, resulting in no state or local income tax owed on that income. Federal tax still applies. Income from performances in a district, sales of artistic work created in a district, and internet sales originating in a district all qualify. There is no limit on the amount that can be subtracted. Available to individuals and single-member LLCs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified residing artists who live in Maryland and work in any of the state's Arts and Entertainment Districts, including those in Salisbury and Wicomico County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Income tax reduction on qualifying artistic work sales, performances, or income derived from artistic work created and sold within an A&E District
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 29 Maryland Arts and Entertainment Districts and to all Maryland residents, with specific programs available in Salisbury and Wicomico County
requirements_list: Individual must own or rent residential property in Maryland
Individual must own or rent residential real property in an A&E District
Individual must conduct a business in an A&E District
Income must derive from the sale or performance of artistic work created in an A&E District
Artistic work must meet the definition of qualified work
For independent individual artists and sole proprietor businesses only
Cannot be claimed by employees of organizations
Can be claimed by individuals or single-member LLCs
Eligibility determined on case-by-case basis by Maryland Comptroller and State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Artist must be a qualified residing artist
For performing artists, income from performances in a district qualifies
For all qualified artists, internet sales originating in a district qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File Form 502AE with annual Maryland state income tax return. Contact the Maryland Comptroller of the Treasury for income tax subtraction modification guidance. Artists should retain receipts, books, accounts, and documentation proving income qualifies for the incentive. Eligibility is determined on case-by-case basis. Form 502AE is available at marylandtaxes.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides nonprofit organizations with direct access to state capital funding for projects that enhance, create, expand, renovate, or conduct major repairs to arts facilities. Grants range from $50,000 to $500,000. Projects that prioritize energy-efficient building methods, increase accessibility for people with disabilities, or expand programming to serve broader audiences are strongly encouraged.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Organizations receive capital grants for arts facility projects aligned with organizational mission and addressing facility-related challenges. Grants range from $50,000 to $500,000 for capital projects with a 2-year project period. The full award amount is provided in one payment after the grant agreement is signed by all required parties and the funded project is approved by the State Board of Public Works. The disbursement process takes a minimum of 6 months from notification of grant status to receipt of funds. Projects should support long-term organizational sustainability and job creation. Applications are evaluated using a 7-point rubric across 3 categories: Mission Alignment, Project Feasibility, and Community Impact.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 3, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based nonprofit organizations operating physical arts facilities, including arts organizations with capital project needs and community-based arts organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects including expansion, production, renovation, or major repairs to facilities or infrastructure operated by eligible organizations. Projects should address facility-related challenges, support organizational mission and future success, include accessibility improvements for people with disabilities, people of color, and low-income individuals, and support local workforce development and job creation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland-based and operate a physical property in Maryland that is either leased or owned by the applicant organization.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland-based 501(c)3 nonprofit organization
Operate a physical property in Maryland that is either leased or owned by the applicant organization
Have an annual operating budget of less than $3,000,000
Either participate in MSAC's Grants for Organizations or County Arts Development programs, or be open to the public and provide arts-based cultural education or experiences
Provide proof of property ownership or a lease agreement with minimum five years remaining at time of application
Have completed previous Arts Capital projects (if prior grantee) and received MSAC staff approval of final report
Not have received $500,000 or more in Arts Capital funds within a five-year period (if prior grantee)
Demonstrate clear alignment with organizational mission and goals
Provide specific facility-related challenges identification with supporting evidence
Present realistic 2-year project timeline with evidence of prior planning
Provide detailed, researched budget demonstrating financial feasibility and non-state funding leverage
Demonstrate leveraged non-state funding
Assemble project team with necessary skills, resources, and partnerships
Develop plans for long-term organizational sustainability and financial impact
Engage community and incorporate stakeholder input documentation
Include accessibility improvements for people with disabilities, people of color, and low-income individuals
Expand programs/services to increase access for marginalized populations
Implement local workforce development and inclusive hiring practices with evidence of job creation opportunities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations considering applying for the first time are encouraged to contact program staff to discuss their proposed project and eligibility. All applications are submitted via the secure online grants management system SmartSimple. Applicants must complete and submit applications by electronic means, including use of an electronic signature. Applicants must meet all revision deadlines after submission or the application will be withdrawn. A multi-disciplinary statewide grant panel electronically reviews applications using a 7-point rubric across 3 categories: Mission Alignment, Project Plans/Feasibility/Impact, and Community Involvement/Impact. All applicants receive electronic notification of grant award or denial after the review period.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that strengthen and promote lifelong learning in the arts by supporting teaching artists on the Maryland Teaching Artist Roster to implement arts education activities in Maryland's schools and communities. Funds support teaching artists to lead arts learning activities in school and community settings, including schools, libraries, community centers, detention centers, and other nonprofit or government locations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to a maximum of $6,000 to support teaching artists to lead arts learning activities in school and community settings. Individual lead artists may receive a maximum of $21,000 in grant awards for FY 2026, and teaching artist organizations may receive a maximum of $84,000 in grant awards for FY 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis between July 2025 and January 2026. Application deadlines are: September 5, 2025, November 5, 2025, January 5, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teaching artists on the Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) Teaching Artist Roster who collaborate with Maryland schools, nonprofit organizations, or government entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support teaching artists to implement arts education programs in Maryland schools, libraries, community centers, detention centers, and other nonprofit or government locations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Must be on the Maryland Teaching Artist Roster
The collaborating school or community site must be a 501(c)3 nonprofit, a unit of government, or a college/university in Maryland
The collaborating site must have operated for at least one full fiscal year with ongoing arts activities
A school or community site may participate in up to two grants per fiscal year
Individual lead artists may receive a maximum of $21,000 in grant awards for FY 2026
Teaching artist organizations may receive a maximum of $84,000 in grant awards for FY 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, the teaching artist and the school or organization agree to collaborate on services, timelines, and fees. Second, the school or organization identifies a coordinator for the project. Third, the teaching artist or their affiliated organization submits the application online using SmartSimple. A panel reviews applications, and the applicant receives notification the following month.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Percent-for-Art program that brings new, permanent artworks to state-owned buildings. For all new or renovated state-owned buildings, a portion of the construction budget is reserved for public art. MSAC manages each commission project from artist selection through installation, and completed artworks join the State's public art collection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For all new or renovated state buildings, 0.05% of the estimated construction cost is reserved to commission or purchase site-specific original artwork through a contractual agreement with an artist. Artists contract directly with the unit of State Government responsible for the project and work with the project design team to integrate the artwork into the project. Artists selected for a commission can expect to be committed to a project for approximately two to five years depending on the scale and timeframe of the construction project.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified; applications made through Public Artist Roster which is currently closed but anticipated to reopen in spring 2025
structured_extraction.contact_name: C. Ryan Patterson, Public Art Program Director; Nora Howell, Public Art Project Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists and artist-led teams who are residents of the United States and its territories
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commission or purchase of site-specific original artwork for state buildings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to all artists and artist-led teams who are residents of the United States and its territories. The Maryland Public Artist Roster can also be used by communities to find a public artist based in Maryland using the Maryland-Based Studio label.
requirements_list: Must be an artist or artist-led team
Must be a resident of the United States and its territories
Artists selected for commission contract directly with the state building user agency
Artwork must be intentionally and thoughtfully integrated into the project and accessible to the public
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Artists join the Maryland Public Artist Roster or respond to an open call when issued. An Artist Selection Committee composed of arts professionals, representatives from the user agency and building occupant, the project's lead design architect, and representatives from the Maryland Public Art Commission and MSAC staff review a diverse pool of artist candidates drawn from the Maryland Public Artist Roster. Selected artists contract directly with the unit of State Government responsible for the project.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that support Maryland's county arts agencies. These grants provide a vital connection between artists, arts organizations, and audiences throughout the state, encourage local arts activity in all disciplines across Maryland's diverse communities, and deliver equitable funding for the arts on the local level through transparent processes accessible to all county constituents. The program helps county arts agencies better serve their communities through grant-making and programming.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County arts agencies designated by their jurisdiction's government as the official arts agency or council submit applications annually. On-year applications (submitted every 3 years) include a three-year plan detailing how the county arts agency will meet constituent needs and MSAC goals through grant making and programs, which is reviewed by MSAC staff and a review panel before Council approval. Off-year applications (submitted in the intervening 2 years) detail changes to the three-year plan, required financial reporting, and requests for professional development. The program provides formula-based grants and technical assistance. Upon execution of the grant agreement, payment is processed for receipt within 6 to 8 weeks. Grantees must submit interim and annual reports detailing use of funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually. FY2026 deadlines are 12/31/25 (off-year) and 1/31/26 (on-year).
structured_extraction.contact_name: David D. Mitchell and Jess Porter
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local agencies or nonprofits officially designated by a county or municipal jurisdiction's government as the official arts agency or council of that jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for county arts agencies to provide connection with artists, arts organizations, and audiences; encourage local arts activity of all disciplines; and provide equitable funding for the arts on the local level. Funds support agency operations, grant-making activities, and programs that serve local artists, arts organizations, and audiences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is open to the officially designated arts agency or council for each of Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a local agency or nonprofit officially designated by the jurisdiction's government as the official arts agency or council of the jurisdiction.
Submit an application annually, which will be either a detailed three-year plan ('On-Year') or a shorter update ('Off-Year').
Must submit required financial reporting.
Grantees must submit interim and annual reports detailing use of funds and other relevant information.

MSAC staff, panelists, or councilors may require submission of a full application in any subsequent fiscal year for reasons including weak three-year plan, grant noncompliance, or significant changes in budget, programming, operations, or leadership.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Designated county arts agencies submit one of two types of applications annually. On-year applications (every 3 years): County arts agencies submit a three-year plan detailing how they will meet constituent needs and MSAC goals. A draft plan is reviewed by MSAC staff and a review panel, and feedback is given with technical assistance as needed. Revisions are made based on initial review, and the preliminary plan is submitted for Council approval. The Council reviews and either approves or requests revision. Off-year applications (intervening 2 years): County arts agencies submit an off-year application detailing any changes to the three-year plan, required financial reporting, and requests for professional development. Off-year applications are reviewed by MSAC staff and major changes are reported to the Council.

structured_extraction.program_name: Creativity Grants for General Operating Support
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that strengthen the vitality and sustainability of small arts organizations to maintain a strong and stable arts infrastructure in Maryland. Funds support an organization's overall operations for an entire season or fiscal year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $4,000 provided to support general operating expenses and overall operations for an entire season or fiscal year for eligible organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling. MSAC is currently accepting applications for the FY2026 application cycle.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small arts organizations in Maryland, including 501(c)3 nonprofits, local government units, and colleges or universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support an organization's overall operations for an entire season or fiscal year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The organization must be incorporated in Maryland. Statewide availability.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit in operation for at least one year, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university.
Must produce or present arts programs, services, or projects that are available to the public.
Cannot be a current participant in the Grants for Organizations (GFO), County Arts Development (CAD), or Arts & Entertainment District (A&E) programs.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit their application through the SmartSimple online portal. A panel reviews applications monthly. The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) notifies applicants of their status. If approved, the grantee receives a grant agreement to process payment, which can take up to 90 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant helps strengthen the vitality and sustainability of artists and small arts organizations and provides opportunities to serve the growing needs of relevant arts projects and collaborations within Maryland communities. The program offers two grant types: Planning & Development grants support early research and development, while Implementation grants support carrying out a specific arts project, event, or program. Grants ranging from $1,000 to $4,000 are provided to support specific arts projects and collaborations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants ranging from $1,000 to $4,000 to support specific arts projects and collaborations. Two types of grants are offered: Planning & Development grants support early research and development, while Implementation grants support carrying out a specific arts project, event, or program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independent artists, nonprofit arts organizations, local government units, schools, colleges, and universities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for two main purposes: Planning & Development grants support the early stages of a project such as research and development, while Implementation grants support carrying out a specific arts project, event, or program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be based in Maryland to be eligible. Statewide program.
requirements_list: Must be an independent artist, a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit organization in operation for at least one year, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college, university, or school.
Organizations applying through a fiscal sponsorship must use a Model A sponsorship.
Applicants must identify a specific event, activity, or project.
Organizations that receive funding through general operating programs from the Maryland State Arts Council are not eligible.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application in the SmartSimple portal. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed monthly. A panel of experts will review and score all applications. Applicants will receive a notification about the status of their application in the month after the review.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports the execution of specific arts projects, events, and programs. This grant helps independent artists and arts organizations implement and deliver their creative work to Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% of the award amount is paid upon execution of the grant agreement. Payment is processed for receipt in 6-8 weeks after the agreement is fully executed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026 with monthly review process. Applications submitted by the last day of each month are reviewed in the following month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independent artists and Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit arts organizations, units of Maryland local government, and Maryland colleges, universities, and schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for execution of specific arts projects, events, and programs. Funds support the implementation and delivery of arts work and collaborations within Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland residents and organizations.
requirements_list: Be an independent artist or a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit organization in operation for one year or more and within grant income requirements, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university/school.
Organizations applying through fiscal sponsorships must operate within a Model A sponsorship structure (where assets, liabilities, and exempt activities are housed within the fiscal sponsor).
Identify a specific event, activity, or project to occur within the application timeframe.
Applicants must be eligible for only one Creativity Grant per fiscal year.

Organizations that receive funding through general operating programs (Grants for Organizations, County Arts Agencies, Arts & Entertainment Districts, Folklife Network, or Creativity Grant for General Operating) are not eligible for project-based support.
Reference the program Guidelines for more specific details on eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through SmartSimple. Applications submitted by the last day of each month are reviewed by a panel of public members representing a range of discipline expertise in the following month. Applicants are notified of grant status as soon as possible after panel review. If approved, recipients receive a formal grant agreement form to process payment. All grantees must file a final report online in SmartSimple after receiving the grant award.

The program aims to provide artists with holistic support rather than support focused solely on particular products or project-based needs. A primary goal is to strengthen the creative workforce, which is a vital part of Maryland's economy and culture.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to support working and living expenses for eligible artists.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Working artists in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working and living expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides general operating support to strengthen and sustain Maryland's arts infrastructure. GFO grants help nonprofit and tax-exempt organizations, as well as units of government, that produce or present ongoing arts programming that is open to the public. These grants enable arts organizations to provide community access to the arts, build future audiences, uplift communities, and generate economic impact throughout the state. The program supports both arts organizations (whose primary mission is producing or presenting arts through public programs or services) and arts programs (whose primary mission may be other than arts but that provide ongoing arts programming or activities through public programs). New organizations must complete an Intent to Apply form to determine eligibility before submitting a standard application. In fiscal year 2025, MSAC awarded GFO grants to 309 arts organizations and programs across the state, totaling $18,136,157.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: General operating support grants to arts organizations. Grant amounts vary based on a five-tier system determined by organization budget size. In FY25, 309 arts organizations and programs across Maryland received GFO grants totaling $18,136,157. The new funding formula phases in over five years (FY24-FY28) with maximum grant caps: Year 1 (FY24) $1.4M, Year 2 (FY25) $1.3M, Year 3 (FY26) $1.2M, Year 4 (FY27) $1.1M, Year 5 (FY28) $1M. Organizations complete the application on an annual basis. New applicants and those who did not receive GFO funding in the most recent cycle must submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15 annually, then complete a standard application by November 15. Funds are generally distributed in full after the Grant Agreement Form and reports are submitted. Every cycle, organizations will have a conversation with a GFO program director and one site visit by a public panelist.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Intent to Apply form due September 15 annually; GFO application due November 15
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and tax-exempt organizations, as well as units of government, that produce or present ongoing arts programming open to the public. This includes both arts organizations (whose primary mission is producing or presenting arts through public programs or services) and arts programs (whose primary mission may be other than arts but that provide ongoing arts programming or activities through public programs). New organizations must complete an Intent to Apply to determine eligibility.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General operating support for eligible arts organizations and disciplines including dance, literary arts, music, public art, theatre, folk and traditional arts, multi-disciplinary, and visual arts/media.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Applicants must establish that the majority of the arts activities it produces and presents take place in Maryland and that most of the arts organization's or arts program's annual expenditures are devoted to activities that occur within the state of Maryland. Organizations must be incorporated in Maryland as a nonprofit or have significant physical presence in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit or tax-exempt organization or unit of government
Must produce or present ongoing arts programming that is open to the public
Must have a Unique Entity ID (UEI) from SAM.gov (required beginning April 2022)
Classified into one of five budget tiers for grant determination
New applicants must complete an Intent to Apply application to determine eligibility
Organization new to the Grants for Organizations program must submit Intent to Apply form by September 15th annually
Have 501(c)3 tax-exempt status from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service at the time of application, except for units of local government and colleges and universities
Be incorporated in Maryland as a nonprofit or have significant physical presence in Maryland
Have operated as an arts organization or arts program for one full fiscal year and be able to submit a financial statement for the most recently completed fiscal year at the time of application

Establish that the majority of the arts activities it produces and presents take place in Maryland and that most of the arts organization's or arts program's annual expenditures are devoted to activities that occur within the state of Maryland
Be governed by a legally-liable board of directors acting under a mission statement and budget specific to the organization

If your organization is a new applicant or if your organization did not receive a GFO grant in the most recent funding cycle, you must complete the Intent to Apply form in order to be eligible to apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New applicants and those who did not receive GFO funding in the most recent cycle must submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15 annually. After eligibility is determined, organizations then complete a GFO application by November 15. All organizations applying must have a Unique Entity ID (UEI) from SAM.gov. Organizations will have a conversation with a GFO program director and one site visit by a public panelist. MSAC relies on diverse experts from across the state to evaluate applications through panel review. Grant agreement forms are prepared and emailed after July 1 to those awarded funding. Forms must be signed and the grant recipient must meet all reporting requirements before grant funds are disbursed. Funds are generally distributed in full after the Grant Agreement Form and reports are submitted. If awarded, recipient organizations must file a final report in SmartSimple by deadlines specified in communications from MSAC. Application assistance resources are available including guidelines documents and webinar slides.

Eligible organizations then complete a standard application to be considered for funding in the next cycle.

requirements_list: Organization must be new to the Grants for Organizations program
Organization did not receive FY 2026 GFO funding
Must submit Intent to Apply form by September 15th annually
Must be an eligible arts organization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations new to GFO must complete an Intent to Apply application to determine eligibility by September 15th. Eligible organizations will then complete a standard application by Saturday, November 15th as a current GFO applicant would. Application assistance resources are available including guidelines documents and webinar slides.

structured_extraction.program_description: A list of juried Maryland-based professional performing artists who have demonstrated a successful history of touring engagements. MSAC uses the roster to promote collaboration between Maryland touring artists and presenters to increase touring opportunities for Maryland professional performing artists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Accepted artists are listed in a roster that is promoted to Maryland presenters to facilitate touring engagements. Artists are given an Arts Directory profile page and promotional visibility through the roster. Selection to a touring roster that connects artists/companies with potential presenter venues and provides marketing and promotional support to touring artists.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026 with application review every other month
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based professional performing artists and performing groups with a history of successful touring engagements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Touring engagements and performances; not applicable as direct financial assistance but rather promotional listing and directory services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents and groups with primary place of business in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident and 18 years or older (if a group, all members must be 18+ and at least 50% must be Maryland residents)
If a group, the company's primary place of business must be located in Maryland
College and university-based performers must perform regularly off-campus for professional fees
If the company or group has nonprofit status, the makeup of the performing ensemble must meet the eligibility criteria outlined for performing companies and groups
Must be able to demonstrate a successful history of professional touring engagements
Must meet all eligibility requirements outlined in the program guidelines
Artist/company description suitable for venue marketing materials
Artistic goals, qualifications, and experience documentation
Brief biographical information on key members
Tour management and programming arrangement details
Space requirements specification
Three work samples demonstrating artistic quality
List of touring engagements within past three years
Standard performance contract
Examples of promotional materials
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from July 2025 through March 2026, with reviews conducted every other month. Applicants submit applications through SmartSimple including all work samples. MSAC convenes a panel of jurors representing various disciplines statewide who electronically review and score applications according to review criteria. Applications are evaluated on rubric criteria across six categories with scoring from 0-5. Applicants are notified of roster status via SmartSimple following application review and receive instructions on setting up an Arts Directory profile if accepted. FY26 How to Apply webinar is available.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant provides funding to eligible Maryland-based nonprofit organizations, units of local government, and arts programs within colleges and universities to support the presentation of artists listed on the Maryland Performing Artists Touring Roster.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The grant provides funding from $500 to $5,000. The full award amount is provided upon execution of the grant agreement. Payment is processed for receipt in 6 to 8 weeks after the grant agreement is fully executed. Funds support artist fees, travel arrangements, marketing, technical needs, programming expenses, and engagement activities for constituents.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Laura Weiss and Emily Sollenberger Dobbins
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-incorporated nonprofit organizations with 501(c)3 tax exempt status, units of Maryland local government, and arts programs within colleges or universities that want to present touring artists.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports the presentation of artists from the Maryland Performing Artists Touring Roster, including artist fees, travel arrangements, marketing, technical needs, programming expenses, and engagement activities for constituents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland-incorporated organizations or Maryland-based units of government or college/university arts programs located within their geographic area of service.
requirements_list: Must be Maryland-incorporated organization with 501(c)3 tax exempt status, OR a unit of Maryland local government, OR an arts program within a college or university
Organizations using fiscal sponsorships must operate under a Model A sponsorship where the project assets, liabilities, and exempt activities are housed within the fiscal sponsor
Must select one or more artists from the Touring Roster and negotiate availability of dates, activities, fees, and performance details prior to applying
Must demonstrate artist involvement in planning including fees, dates, activities description, technical needs, travel, and terms
Must show public value and impact for constituents served
Must document sensory and emotional experience intended for audience
Must consider non-dominant norms, values, narratives, standards, and aesthetics
Must plan to engage currently unengaged constituents
Must provide detailed financial breakdown and funding sources
Must complete application in SmartSimple
If awarded, must file a final report online in SmartSimple by December 31, 2026
Must present an artist from the Maryland Performing Artists Touring Roster
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Select one or more artists from the Touring Roster and contact them to negotiate details. Submit application through SmartSimple during the rolling application period. Applications submitted by the last day of the month are reviewed by panelists in the following month, with notifications early the following month. Panel members score applications according to review criteria using a 5-0 point scale per category. After approval, applicants receive a formal grant agreement form. Upon execution of the grant agreement, payment is processed for receipt in 6 to 8 weeks.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program honors long-term achievement in traditional arts. Each year, it selects six winners from nominations in three categories: Person/People, Place, or Tradition. Award winners receive a $10,000 grant that can be used at their discretion. Awards are given annually and recognize six recipients.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Award winners receive a $10,000 grant that can be used at their discretion. Annual awards recognizing six recipients for long-term achievement in traditional arts.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 26, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: The program is for people, places, and traditions in Maryland that have a long history of achievement in the traditional arts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are awarded as a grant that can be used at the awardee's discretion for recognition and awards for traditional arts achievement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nominees must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must demonstrate long-term achievement in the traditional arts.
A nominee may receive the Heritage Award only once.
Awards are not given posthumously.
Self-nominations are accepted.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, create a profile in the MSAC's SmartSimple online system. Then, submit the nomination form. The form asks for a description of the nominee's long-term achievement in traditional arts. You can also include optional supplemental materials. You may ask the State Folklorist to review a draft of your nomination before you submit it.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Incentives for Arts & Entertainment Districts

The tax credit is based on the difference between pre- and post-renovation property assessments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local property tax credit determined by local government based on the difference between pre- and post-renovation assessments. Amount and duration are set by local government.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners of manufacturing, commercial, or industrial properties in A&E Districts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation of property for use by qualified residing artists or arts and entertainment enterprises
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Maryland's 29 A&E Districts. Contact local district manager for specific incentives available in each district.

Property must be wholly or partially renovated
Property must be for use by qualified residing artists or arts and entertainment enterprises
Owner must qualify under A&E District definitions

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Art Across Maryland Conservation Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants supporting the conservation and preservation of existing public artworks in Maryland. The program serves organizations and communities seeking to conserve local public artworks statewide through two funding tracks: (1) Planning Grants providing up to $10,000 to support conservation planning efforts including collection inventories, digitization of records, community outreach, research, assessments, project administration, consultancy fees, and collection management services and technology; and (2) Implementation Grants providing up to $30,000 to support direct conservation work including relocation, cleaning, structural repairs, landscape improvements, lighting upgrades, and interpretive signage. Both support permanent public artwork that is publicly accessible.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides grant funding to support the conservation and preservation of existing public artworks in Maryland. Planning Grants of up to $10,000 support artwork conservation planning efforts including project administration, consultancy fees, community engagement, and collection management services and technology. Implementation Grants of up to $30,000 support direct conservation work including relocation, cleaning, structural repairs, landscape improvements, lighting upgrades, and interpretive signage. Eligible uses include professional conservator fees, artists, structural engineers, materials specialists, historians, or preservationists; community engagement activities; collection management activities and technology; and organization administration/project management fees not to exceed 10 percent of the grant request.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with IRS 501(c)3 status based in Maryland, Maryland-based fiscal sponsor organizations, units of government, colleges and universities in Maryland, and public or private schools serving grades pre-K through 12 in Maryland seeking to conserve public artworks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Conservation and preservation of existing public artworks; relocating public artwork within or to Maryland to increase public access; conservation and maintenance activities conducted by professional service providers including cleaning, waxing, coating, and painting; replacement or addition of components providing structural integrity; landscape site improvements including drainage and plant maintenance; lighting and electrical work improving visibility, safety, or energy efficiency; conservation of existing or creation of new identification and interpretive signage; administrative fees for project management and planning; consultant fees such as professional conservators, artists, structural engineers, materials specialists, historians, or preservationists; community engagement activities including public meetings and education; and collection management activities and technology including inventory digitization, database creation, and collection management software.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Final location of artwork to be conserved must be in Maryland. Applicants can only submit one PAAM grant application per fiscal year.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization with IRS 501(c)3 status based in Maryland, or a Maryland-based fiscal sponsor with Model A fiscal sponsorship agreement, or a unit of government, college, university, or school in Maryland
Artwork must be considered public art as defined by MSAC
Final location of artwork must be in Maryland
Artwork must be publicly accessible
Artwork must comply with local jurisdiction regulations and permitting requirements
Conservation project must be fully developed with identified project team
Support and approval of artwork and site owners must be obtained
Applicants may only submit one PAAM grant application per fiscal year
Grantees receiving Project Grants in FY 2024 are not eligible to apply for any PAAM Project Grant in FY 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations apply through the secure online grants application software SmartSimple. Applicants must create a free account at marylandarts.smartsimple.com, complete and submit applications by electronic means with electronic signature, and meet all revision deadlines specified in writing or the application will be withdrawn.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Art Across Maryland New Artworks Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that support independent artists, collaborative groups, and organizations planning, creating, and installing new local public art projects across Maryland. Funding supports community outreach, visioning, research, planning, artist selection, and initial artwork design through to final creation and installation. Provides support for both the development phase (up to $10,000 for independent artists and organizations) and the fabrication and installation phase (up to $30,000 for organizations).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $10,000 to independent artists or organizations for planning, creating, and installing new public art projects, supporting community engagement, artist selection, design, and installation. Grants up to $30,000 to organizations for fabrication and installation of completed public artwork. Funds can support community engagement activities, artist fees and honorariums, consultant fees, facility rentals, online application software, artwork proposal design and development including digital renderings and permit applications, contracted services such as fabricators and installers, equipment and space rentals, artwork materials and tools, plaque and interpretive signage, artwork transportation, insurance and permitting fees, organization administration and project management (up to 10 percent of total grant request), and artwork dedication expenses.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps licensed child care centers and registered family child care providers in Maryland pay for costs associated with pursuing national accreditation and Maryland Accreditation. Support includes application fees for national accreditation (initial applications, renewal applications, and annual updates), instructional materials needed for Maryland Accreditation, and expenses related to obtaining National Accreditation with the National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC). The program also provides reimbursement for non-consumable instructional materials purchased in pursuit of Maryland Accreditation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants, subsidies, and reimbursement to cover required application fees for national accreditation (initial application fees, renewal application fees, and annual update fees), instructional materials associated with pursuing Maryland Accreditation, and expenses related to obtaining National Accreditation with the National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC). For Maryland Accreditation, maximum reimbursement is $2,500 for programs serving 100 or fewer children and $3,000 for programs serving more than 100 children. Funds are provided directly to cover these accreditation-related costs and cannot exceed the fees charged by the respective accrediting organization. Awards for national accreditation are paid directly to the accrediting organization on behalf of applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and registered family child care providers in Maryland seeking national accreditation or Maryland Accreditation, including early childhood, public prekindergarten, and school-age child care programs. Programs must be currently Maryland Accredited or have completed the Initial Self-Appraisal as part of the Maryland Accreditation process to be eligible for instructional materials reimbursement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For national accreditation: required application fees (initial application, renewal application, and annual updates) paid directly to accrediting organization. For Maryland Accreditation: non-consumable instructional materials including language and literacy materials, mathematics materials, discovery/science/nature materials, outdoor learning equipment, music and movement materials, dramatic/imaginative play materials, technology equipment and software, and other instructional materials. Instructional materials purchased must be within 12 months prior to application date. Funds cannot be used for facility improvement, association membership fees, staff training, costs paid through another funding source, consumable items (paint, crayons, markers, glue, paper), or any costs greater than those charged by the accreditation organization.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center or registered family child care provider
Must be pursuing accreditation from a recognized accrediting organization or Maryland Accreditation
Costs cannot be paid for through another funding source

For national accreditation: must submit copy of completed application submitted to accrediting organization, completed Accreditation Work Plan, copy of accrediting organization's fee page, and copy of current accreditation certificate if currently accredited

For Maryland Accreditation materials reimbursement: must have completed Initial Self-Appraisal or be currently Maryland Accredited, submit receipts for purchases within 12 months prior to application, complete Learning Materials Checklist(s) matching purchases, and submit application through Maryland OneStop portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application for accreditation support through the online forms available on the Maryland One Stop portal. Separate applications are available for national accreditation support and Maryland accreditation support. For national accreditation: gather required documents including copy of completed application to accrediting organization, Accreditation Work Plan, fee page, and accreditation certificate if applicable, then complete application on OneStop Portal. MSDE reviews application within 30 days and notifies via email; award paid directly to accrediting organization. For Maryland Accreditation materials: gather receipts for learning materials purchased within 12 months prior, complete appropriate Learning Materials Checklist(s), complete MSDE application through Maryland OneStop portal and upload documentation. Applications reviewed within 30 business days; approvals or requests for missing documentation sent via portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides scholarship awards for low-income students eligible for free or reduced-price school meals (FARMs) to attend eligible nonpublic schools. Priority granted to students who received BOOST awards in prior year and their siblings. Nearly 2,800 low-income students received awards in 2025-2026 school year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards provided to eligible students to help pay tuition and required fees at participating nonpublic schools. Approximately 2,500 awards are available with total funding of $9,000,000 plus carryover funds. Award amounts depend on household income, the academic level of the student, any financial assistance the school provides, and whether the student has a disability. Base awards and additional awards for special education students are determined by the BOOST Advisory Board. The scholarship check is sent to the school, and the parent or guardian must sign the back of the check. The award may be reduced if it exceeds the tuition owed to the school. Funds cannot be carried over to the next school year and cannot be split or transferred between children.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 8, 2026, no later than 11:59 p.m. EDT (parent applications); March 6, 2026 (nonpublic school applications); December 11, 2026 (final deadline for awards to be offered); September 25, 2026 (school reporting deadline)

Parents and guardians of eligible students. Nonpublic schools participating in the program.

The program includes 14 weeks of classroom instruction covering CVS programs and procedures, inventory management, and prescription medication measurements, along with 6 weeks of clinical on-the-job training, hands-on experience in a mock pharmacy, and externships in actual CVS locations throughout Maryland.

Training includes hands-on experience in a mock pharmacy and externships in actual CVS locations in the job seeker's local community. Classroom instruction is conducted at the DORS WTC location. The program prepares participants to pass the national Pharmacy Technician Certifying Board (PTCB) test and obtain national pharmacy technician certification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF)

The program supports providers in earning associate or bachelor's degrees in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education, with funds covering tuition, college fees, and textbooks. structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition assistance program for child care providers to obtain a college education at participating colleges/universities in Maryland. Scholarship and financial assistance is available for child care providers and staff to pursue associate or bachelor's degrees in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education, as well as other professional development and career advancement activities. The program covers tuition, college fees, and textbooks. Payments are made directly to the college or university; participants are not reimbursed directly. Funds cannot be used for previously incurred costs. MSDE notifies applicants of fund approval status. First-time applications deadline is March 1st; continuation applications deadline is June 30th.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to child care facilities and family providers to improve and enhance the quality of care for children and support school readiness. Grants can be used to purchase supplies, materials, and equipment that support better quality child care services and implement knowledge gained through professional training, creating learning environments aligned with early learning standards.
