Facilities with 10 to 29 children may receive up to $1,500. Facilities with more than 30 children may receive up to $2,500. Grants are awarded quarterly in January, April, July, and October. Child care providers are eligible for a grant award once every three years. Funds support supplies, materials, equipment, and resources to create stimulating learning environments and implement knowledge gained through professional training in early childhood development.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Scholarship (CCS) program provides financial assistance to help eligible Maryland families afford high-quality child care and early education programs. The program provides monthly subsidies or scholarships to cover part of child care costs for children under 13 or individuals 13-19 with qualifying disabilities. Eligible families can receive assistance from regulated, licensed, and approved informal child care providers. A Fast Track application process offers temporary 60-day assistance within 3 business days, with the option to apply for a full 52-week scholarship. Families apply through the online Family Child Care Portal or Money4ChildCare.com and may receive co-payment waivers based on income eligibility. The program works with licensed centers, licensed homes, and approved informal providers (relatives or non-relatives). Payment is made directly to providers after the approval process. Processing time for informal providers is a minimum of 60 days from submission of all documentation. Families with zero income or receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) have a $0 co-payment. The program serves approximately 37,000 children, 25,000 parents, and 3,500 early care and educational programs. The program is administered as a Federal Child Care Development Funds (CCDF) program providing subsidies to eligible families for child care services with attendance verification processes to ensure program integrity and accountability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides monthly subsidies or scholarships to eligible families to cover part of their child care costs. Families receive a scholarship showing the state-paid portion and their required co-payment. Temporary 60-day scholarships are processed within 3 business days. Full 52-week scholarships are available after submission of complete documentation. Payment is made directly to providers after the approval process. For informal providers, the approval process takes a minimum of 60 days. Families on Temporary Cash Assistance or Supplemental Security Income have a $0 co-payment. Other families pay a state-assigned co-payment that decreases for multiple children. Families use the scholarship at Maryland EXCELS participating providers (licensed child care centers or registered family homes) or informal providers (relatives or non-relatives in the child's home). The scholarship amount is determined by state rates and the family co-payment is based on family income and number of children in care. Co-payment waivers may be available based on income eligibility. Provider payments are processed via advance payments on the 1st and 15th of each month. Providers may also receive payments for voluntary closure days (up to 14 days per year). Providers receive reimbursement for child care services delivered through subsidized child care payments made on behalf of families using child care scholarships.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Temporarily stopped accepting new applications starting May 1, 2025. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis when the program reopens.

Child care providers (formal licensed centers, licensed homes, informal providers, and regulated providers receiving CCDF payments). Families experiencing homelessness. Extended day services (before/after school and summer care) for Head Start-enrolled children. For address changes, families must provide 5-day advanced notice and have an active scholarship.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Register for an account at the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal at https://family.childcareportals.org or Money4ChildCare.com. Step 2: Complete the Fast Track online application and submit three documents: proof of employment or enrollment in training/school, proof of residency (utility bill, lease, etc.), and proof of income (4 weeks of consecutive pay stubs). Step 3: The application is processed within 3 business days by CCS Central 2. Step 4: If eligible, a temporary 60-day scholarship is issued. Within 15 days, families can submit additional documentation to apply for a full 52-week scholarship (30 calendar days or 5 business days from receipt of all required documentation for determination). This requires submission of the full CCS application with verification of income (most recent 4 weeks of pay stubs), proof of identity, proof of approved activity, proof of all other income, and proof of address for all household members. For informal providers, background checks and clearances must be obtained and approved before payment begins (minimum 60 days). Redetermination of eligibility is also completed online. Some families may need referrals from DHS, Head Start, or other public agencies. Families experiencing homelessness should submit applications through the online portal with homelessness application coversheet. For parenting youth in out-of-home care, DHS must submit out-of-home referral form (must be signed and dated, not electronic signatures). Referral must be submitted within 45 days for Head Start extended day partnerships. Applicants can call 877-227-0125 or 1-855-435-7410 for assistance with the application process. Open office hours available through December 2026 from 12:00-1:00 PM. For providers: Register for portal account at https://provider.childcareportals.org/ with two-factor authentication required. Providers manage scholarship requests, attendance records, and program information through portal dashboard. Complete application forms (Informal Provider Application Form available). Upload required documents through Provider Portal. Submit forms and documentation through Document Center. Dispute resolution available through three pathways: (1) Informal Resolution for Advance Payment Disputes via Provider Inquiry Link; (2) Informal Appeal for Repayment/Program Integrity Audit Disputes via Provider Portal; (3) Formal Appeal for Intentional Program Violation Disputes to Office of Administrative Hearings. Families can submit changes through Portal Interim Change forms during active scholarships.

structured_extraction.program_description: CCEIS is a federal program under 34 CFR §300.646 that requires local education agencies identified by the state as having disproportionately high identification of students with disabilities by race or ethnicity to reserve 15 percent of their IDEA Part B funding to implement comprehensive systems addressing root causes of this over-identification. The program provides early intervening services to students with disabilities from underrepresented racial/ethnic groups and students without current special education identification who need academic and behavioral support. The program focuses on providing educational and behavioral evaluations, services, supports, and professional development to reduce disproportionality in identification, placement, and disciplinary actions. Key root causes addressed include lack of access to scientifically-based instruction, economic/cultural/linguistic barriers, inappropriate disciplinary removals, lack of diagnostic screenings, and achievement gaps.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local education agencies identified as having significant disproportionality must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds to implement CCEIS. Funds support hiring and contracting coaches and tutors; staff salaries for general education teachers, guidance counselors, psychologists, social workers, and RTI coordinators; extended contracts and hours; professional development; academic and behavioral interventions; instructional materials and software; computing devices; substitute teacher costs; staff travel related to CCEIS activities; progress monitoring; assessment; coaching and mentoring; educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and supports including evidence-based literacy instruction; and activities addressing root cause factors and systemic change to reduce over-identification and disproportionality. Funds must supplement, not supplant, state, local, and other federal funds. Funds cannot support core/universal programming, alternative education replacing core programming, child find activities, universal screening costs, special education evaluations, student transportation, furniture, or office equipment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Interim Report 1 due January 31; Interim Report 2 due January 31; Final Report due November 30
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (school districts and charter schools) identified by Maryland as having significant disproportionality in the identification, placement, or disciplinary actions involving students by race or ethnicity. Services target students ages 3-21 from racial/ethnic groups experiencing significant disproportionality, including students with disabilities and students without current special education identification who require academic and behavioral support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can support providing educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and supports including evidence-based literacy instruction; professional development and educational and behavioral support; addressing factors contributing to significant disproportionality including lack of access to scientifically-based instruction, economic/cultural/linguistic barriers, inappropriate disciplinary removals, lack of diagnostic screenings, and achievement gaps; reviewing and addressing policies, practices, or procedures contributing to over-identification; building systemic awareness and leadership supports; developing diverse stakeholder groups; engaging in self-assessment and data review; planning proactive and responsive actions; establishing professional learning experiences; developing comprehensive evaluation systems; hiring coaches and tutors; staff salaries and extended contracts; instructional materials and software; computing devices; substitute teacher costs; staff travel; and progress monitoring and assessment activities. Devices and software usage must align with approved CCEIS Plan narrative. Funds cannot support core/universal programming, alternative education replacing core programming, child find activities, universal screening costs, special education evaluations, student transportation, furniture, or office equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Only local education agencies identified by the state as meeting the criterion of significant disproportionality (one or more subgroups of students with a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years, unless the risk ratio declines by .15 if less than 4.0 or .5 if over 4.0) are required to implement CCEIS. Maryland local school systems identified as having significant disproportionality are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a local education agency identified by the state as having significant disproportionality based on risk ratio of greater than 2.0 in identification, placement, or disciplinary actions for two or more consecutive years (unless the risk ratio declines by .15 if less than 4.0 or .5 if over 4.0)
Must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds for CCEIS activities
Must address root cause factors contributing to significant disproportionality
Must address and review policies, practices, or procedures identified as contributing to over-identification
Must convene a local implementation team and establish diverse stakeholder group
Must conduct self-assessment and data review process
Must develop a comprehensive system for evaluation of plan outcomes
Must align expenditures with specific actions to mitigate root causes
Staff must be appropriately licensed for instruction provided
Staff delivering instruction must be appropriately licensed
Funds must address identified disproportionality factors
Time and effort records required for special education teacher and staff compensation
Software costs must be allocable between universal screening and intervention components
Materials and software must be exclusively for struggling students identified through universal screening or approved interventions
Devices and software usage must align with approved CCEIS Plan narrative
Must submit MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25 form(s) with separate Budget Detail Form for each C-1-25
Must submit interim progress reports and cumulative variance reports
Must submit grant amendment requests by August 15, 2026
Must submit final progress report and financial report by November 30, 2026
Conduct programmatic self-assessment and root cause analysis using approved MSDE tools
Develop Planned Response Actions (PRAs) with measurable goals and interim benchmarks
Obtain MSDE approval before changing distribution of Part B 611/619 allocations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: LEAs identified as having significant disproportionality must develop and submit a CCEIS Plan using the state template. The plan must address root cause factors, include specific actions and expenditures to reduce over-identification, establish implementation drivers (staffing, training, coaching, staff evaluation, data systems), identify job-embedded professional learning, and develop comprehensive evaluation systems. Plans are reviewed by the state using a review and feedback tool. LEAs must conduct self-assessment and root cause analysis, develop Planned Response Actions (PRAs) addressing identified root causes, include policy/procedure review for each disproportionality area, and establish measurable goals and interim benchmarks. LEAs may submit programmatic and fiscal amendments as needed. Progress is reported using the state progress report template with interim reports due January 31 and final report due November 30. Local system teams including Director of Special Education, Chief Academic Officer, Finance Officer, and Superintendent must submit forms, which require approval by MSDE Equity Specialist, Program Liaison, Fiscal Liaison, Resource Management Branch Chief, and Assistant State Superintendent. Amendment submissions must include planned response actions, data analysis, qualitative/quantitative data, and budget amendments (C-1-25 forms).

structured_extraction.program_description: Services that help people with disabilities explore, access, and participate in registered apprenticeship programs. Apprenticeships are paid jobs where workers earn a wage while learning a skilled trade through on-the-job training and classroom instruction. Apprentices are sponsored by employers or associations and paid according to progressive pay scales.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS provides consultation services including apprenticeship coordination, academic assessment, and exploration to help identify opportunities. Support services include academic instruction to prepare for apprenticeships, pre-apprenticeship program support, registered apprenticeship support, and youth apprenticeship tracking and transition assistance. Paid apprenticeships combine on-the-job training from skilled craftspeople with related classroom instruction. Financial incentives are available for employers. Connection to existing apprenticeship programs or development of customized registered apprenticeship programs. Workforce recruitment support through American Job Centers and partnership approval through Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 18+ seeking career training; Employers/sponsors looking to hire and develop apprentices; Marylanders with disabilities interested in pursuing registered apprenticeships
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-the-job training, related classroom instruction, apprentice wages, apprenticeship program administration and support, and services to support exploration, preparation, and participation in apprenticeship programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer (individual with a disability)
Must be interested in pursuing a registered apprenticeship
Be 18 years of age
Have high school diploma (graduation, GED® or NEDP)
Have transportation
Be drug free
Be physically able to perform required tasks
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For apprentices: Visit occupations.mdapprenticeship.com, call an apprenticeship navigator to connect with a program sponsor or employer, apply directly to the sponsor or employer. DORS will conduct assessments, explore apprenticeship opportunities with you, and provide ongoing support throughout your apprenticeship journey. For employers: Call navigator, connect with program, present plan for approval, recruit through American Job Centers.

For businesses and organizations, the program offers customized training creation, recruitment scheduling, information on financial incentives, disability awareness and reasonable accommodations education, and internship coordination.

Also addresses challenges with keeping a job and living independently.

Services are tailored for individuals with vision loss to achieve competitive employment and independence.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enhanced Child Care Support and Teacher Retention Award (ECSTRA) Retention Bonus Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A retention bonus program that provides monetary bonuses to early childhood educators who remain employed in eligible child care roles. The program uses American Rescue Plan Act funds to stabilize the child care workforce and includes a randomized controlled trial component to study whether larger bonuses improve retention and job satisfaction. Inspired by Virginia's Teacher Recognition Program, which reduced turnover by 50%. Retention bonuses ranging from $0 to $3,000 are distributed through a lottery system, with approximately 25% of eligible applicants randomly receiving no bonus and the remaining 75% split equally among $1,000, $2,000, and $3,000 tiers. Bonuses are paid in two installments based on continued employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Retention bonuses ranging from $0 to $3,000 are distributed through a lottery system. Approximately 25% of eligible applicants randomly receive no bonus; the remaining 75% are split equally among $1,000, $2,000, and $3,000 tiers. Bonuses are paid in two installments: the first half (50%) is paid after remaining employed in the same program for at least 5 months (by March 13, 2024), and the second half (50%) is paid after remaining employed for at least 8 months total (by June 5, 2024). Bonus funds have no restrictions and participants may use them as they choose.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 3, 2023, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual early childhood educators who hold a valid Maryland Child Care Credential (MCCC) and work directly with children birth to age 5 (not yet kindergarten) for at least 20 hours per week in MSDE licensed child care programs. Excludes public school teachers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retention bonuses with no restrictions; participants may use bonus funds as they choose and are not required to use funds for work-related expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland jurisdictions (23 counties and Baltimore City); lottery apportions spots by jurisdiction to ensure statewide access.
requirements_list: Hold a valid Maryland Child Care Credential (MCCC)
Work directly with children birth to age 5 (not yet kindergarten)
Work at least 20 hours per week in an eligible child care role
Be employed in an MSDE licensed child care provider (CTRs, LOCs, FCCHs, or LFCCHs)
Remain employed in the same program for at least 5 months to receive the first half of the bonus
Remain employed in the same program for at least 8 months to receive the second half of the bonus
Provide accurate and up-to-date employment information
Participate in the lottery system to determine bonus size
Apply by October 3, 2023 at 5:00 p.m. EDT
Not be employed in early childhood programs administered through local education agencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individual early educators must submit an application by October 3, 2023 at 5:00 p.m. EDT by providing their employment information to the Maryland State Department of Education. Selected applicants are notified in October 2023. Those selected to participate in the ECSTRA program receive bonuses in two installments based on their continued employment in the same program (first half at 5 months by March 13, 2024; second half at 8 months by June 5, 2024). FAQ and answers are available, and customer service support sessions are available on the MSDE Grants office website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Food Is Safe Here (FISH) Initiative - ServSafe Food Safety Training for School Nutrition Professionals
structured_extraction.program_description: An ongoing program of food safety training options and resources for school food service personnel in Maryland that participate in federally funded child nutrition programs. The program includes ServSafe Food Handler and Food Manager certification using the National Restaurant Association's nationally recognized curricula and certification exam. This credential meets or exceeds requirements for local jurisdictions requiring food service certification for managers and satisfies USDA Professional Standards training requirements. Training includes both Food Handler and Food Manager certification options, with review sessions available. The program provides free training and certification utilizing certified instructors from local education agencies and certified proctors who can teach classes, administer exams, and order materials at no cost. Minimum of 8 hours of food safety training is required to meet USDA Professional Standards training requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free ServSafe Food Handler and Food Manager certification training utilizing National Restaurant Association curricula. Certified instructors from local education agencies can teach classes and order materials at no cost. Certified proctors can order answer sheets and administer exams at no cost. Minimum of 8 hours of food safety training required to meet USDA Professional Standards training requirements. An ongoing program providing food safety training options and resources for school food service personnel in Maryland participating in federally funded child nutrition programs (NSLP, SBP, CACFP, SFSP). Training dates must be scheduled before ordering materials, and orders must be placed four weeks in advance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School nutrition professionals and other school food service personnel in Maryland schools and agencies participating in federally funded child nutrition programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food safety training and certification meeting USDA professional development standards, local jurisdiction requirements, and resources for school food service staff.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide for schools and agencies participating in federally funded child nutrition programs (NSLP, SBP, CACFP, SFSP).
requirements_list: Must be a School Nutrition Manager, Supervisor, Director, or other school nutrition professional required to meet USDA Professional Standards training requirements

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides mental health consultation and support services to promote positive mental and behavioral health practices for infants and young children with developmental, social, emotional or behavioral issues. Mental health professionals connect with licensed early care and education providers and families to help educators understand how relationships affect young children's social and emotional growth. Services include referrals, direct services, and individualized strategies for children, families, teachers, and caregivers. Mental health consultants work with families and child care staff to create supportive environments, reduce challenging behaviors, and prepare children for school success while reducing expulsions. The program builds the capacity of early care and education providers and family members to promote healthy social-emotional development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding and free mental health consultation services to support infant and early childhood mental health. Services include referrals and direct services for children, families, teachers, and caregivers. Mental health consultants gather information through observation and conversation with parents and child care staff, then develop individualized strategies to assist the child in the child care setting and at home. Parents receive resources and referrals as needed. Information from assessments is shared with other professionals such as pediatricians, occupational therapists, and speech therapists as requested by the family. Grant recipients must operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting positive mental and behavioral health practices for young children with developmental, social, emotional or behavioral issues through referrals, direct services, and mental health consultation to promote healthy social-emotional development, strengthen child care provider and family capacity, and prepare children for school success.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide with availability in Montgomery County; applicants must be licensed to do business within the State of Maryland. Services in Montgomery County are not provided in before and/or after school programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs (Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive early learning hubs located in elementary schools that serve families with children from birth through age 5. These centers provide full-day, full-year services including developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting classes and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based playgroups, referrals for services, early intervention identification, home visiting, case management and service coordination, meals for children and families, health screenings (dental, vision, hearing, mental health assessments), and interpreter services for multilingual families to prepare children for school readiness and success in life. The program prepares children and families for success in school and life by supporting families as a child's first and most important teacher, meeting them where they are. Founded in the 1990s by Judith P. Hoyer with legislation enacted in May 2000, the program has expanded through Blueprint for Maryland's Future (2021).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Judy Centersare grant-funded programs that provide full-day, full-year services (7-12 hours per day, year-round operation) including developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting classes and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups (minimum two on-site weekly; average three per week statewide), referrals for services and supports, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, case management with families and service coordination with community partners, meals for children and families, health screenings (dental, vision, hearing, mental health assessments), professional learning for staff (976 offered in FY2024), interpreter services for multilingual families, and outdoor learning spaces and classroom development. FY2024 budget: $28,380,000 total ($2,640,000 American Rescue Plan Funds, $8,798,620 MSDE General Funds, $16,941,380 Blueprint for Maryland's Future Funds), with $330,000 standard per-center allocation.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist (Spanish language assistance)

Community partners, school-based staff, and administrators.

Current sites operate in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester counties, and Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind
structured_extraction.program_description: Authorized by the federally mandated Randolph-Sheppard Act, the Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind provides persons who are blind and vision impaired with training, licensing, and oversight to manage and operate vending facilities, retail concessions, and food service operations in federal, military, DOD, state, and business partner facilities. The program prepares individuals with vision loss to run successful food service and retail businesses in public facilities. Approximately 50 long-term successful businesses are currently operated by BEP-licensed managers.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a three-phase training program. Phase one is an eight-week New Manager Training course at DORS' Workforce and Technology Center in Northeast Baltimore. Phase two includes formal food service training with certified instructors and chefs, with certification by the National Restaurant Association in food service sanitation. Phase three consists of three to six months of on-the-job training through an extended internship at various BEP facilities under an experienced manager. Upon completion of all training requirements and certification by DORS, individuals become licensed BEP managers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Persons who are legally blind or vision impaired with vision loss as their primary disability, are U.S. citizens, have an aptitude for business management, and are certified as eligible by DORS. Deaf-blind individuals and legally blind individuals over age 55 may also qualify for independent living goals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training, licensing, and oversight of vending facilities, retail concessions, and food service operations in federal, military, DOD, state, and business partner facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program operating in Maryland. Training is conducted at DORS' Workforce & Technology Center in Northeast Baltimore. Operations may be located at state office buildings in Annapolis and Baltimore, federal facilities in Maryland including the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Internal Revenue Service (IRS), Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), Social Security Administration (SSA), U.S. Coast Guard, and Fort George G. Meade.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: If you already have a DORS counselor, ask your counselor about the BEP program. If you are not already working with DORS, complete a Request DORS Services form through dors.maryland.gov, which can also be requested through a family member, medical provider, social worker, or others. You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where DORS will gather information and provide information about your eligibility for DORS services. Eligible individuals will then participate in the three-phase training program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland EXCELS is the State Quality Rating and Improvement System (QRIS) for early childhood education programs and school-age care programs. It establishes a comprehensive quality improvement program that rewards providers for achieving high quality ratings and serving families with Child Care Scholarships. The program increases the number of high-quality early childhood and school-age care programs through a structured rating system, targeted technical assistance, training, peer support, and financial incentives. Providers who achieve Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating levels 3, 4, or 5 receive increased reimbursements ranging from 10% to 44% based on child age, type of care, and provider quality rating level. Family child care homes receive: Level 3 increases of 11% (under 2) or 10% (2 and over); Level 4 increases of 22% (under 2) or 21% (2 and over); Level 5 increases of 29% (under 2) or 28% (2 and over). Child care centers receive: Level 3 increases of 22% (under 2) or 10% (2 and over); Level 4 increases of 37% (under 2) or 19% (2 and over); Level 5 increases of 44% (under 2) or 26% (2 and over). Programs also receive flat-rate bonuses ranging from $1,000 to $13,500 when they publish a first-time quality rating or re-publish a rating of 4 or 5.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides increased reimbursement payments to providers who achieve Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating Level 3, 4, or 5. For family child care: Level 3 provides 11% (under 2) or 10% (2 and over) increase; Level 4 provides 22% (under 2) or 21% (2 and over) increase; Level 5 provides 29% (under 2) or 28% (2 and over) increase. For child care centers: Level 3 provides 22% (under 2) or 10% (2 and over) increase; Level 4 provides 37% (under 2) or 19% (2 and over) increase; Level 5 provides 44% (under 2) or 26% (2 and over) increase. Child care programs also receive flat-rate bonuses ranging from $1,000 to $13,500 based on program type, capacity level, and quality rating achieved. Bonuses are processed within 60 days of quality rating publication and paid by check or direct deposit. Additionally, providers receive targeted technical assistance both online and in-person from Program Coordinators and Quality Assurance Specialists, peer support through workgroups and cohorts, free training, promotional tools, and discounts from vendors and organizations. Quality rating badges, certificates, and marketing resources are also provided to support program promotion. Providers are also eligible for state grants to support quality improvement efforts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early childhood and school-age child care programs (family child care homes, child care centers, and large family child care homes) participating in Maryland EXCELS and the Maryland Child Care Scholarship program who achieve and maintain Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating levels 3, 4, or 5, and are committed to quality improvement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Quality improvement in child care programs, increased reimbursement payments for providing high-quality child care and education services to families using the Child Care Scholarship program, purchase of high-quality learning materials, support for salary increases and hiring qualified staff, purchase of furniture and equipment, support for accreditation efforts, and bonuses that can be spent at the discretion of the program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland - available to all Maryland early childhood and school-age child care programs across all counties.
requirements_list: Must operate an early childhood or school-age child care program.

Program must achieve and maintain Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating Level 3, 4, or 5.
Program must be in compliance with all Maryland EXCELS regulations.

To receive a bonus, program must either publish a quality rating for the first time or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5 between July 1, 2023 and June 30, 2027.
Must be active during the bonus period (July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2027) to receive bonuses.
Program must be serving families using the Child Care Scholarship Program.
Quality Rating 3 required for Military Child Care in Your Neighborhood participation.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs participate in Maryland EXCELS and demonstrate commitment to quality improvement to access these benefits and resources. Providers participating in the Child Care Scholarship program are automatically eligible for increased reimbursement if their program achieves the required Maryland EXCELS quality rating level. No separate application is required. Providers who meet the eligibility requirements and achieve the required quality rating automatically receive the increased reimbursement payments shown in the Invoice Detail Report under EXCELS payments for each child. Bonus payments are processed within 60 days of quality rating publication and delivered by check or direct deposit. Program participants can check payment status on the General Accounting Division (GAD) website after registering. For technical assistance and support with quality improvement, providers can contact a Quality Assurance Specialist directly through the program. Apply through marylandexcels.org.

Programs receive a bonus each time they publish a first-time quality rating or re-publish a rating of 4 or 5. Funds can be used for staff salary increases, purchasing high-quality learning materials and educational resources, hiring additional qualified staff, purchasing furniture and equipment, achieving accreditation support, and other program improvements. Bonuses are typically processed within 60 days of the quality rating publication date and paid by check or direct deposit. Bonuses are considered taxable income.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide Medicaid home and community-based services waiver providing long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support to eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder ages 0 through the end of the school semester when they turn 21 years old. The program enables home and community living as an alternative to institutional care and includes service coordination and case management through local education agencies and county health departments. The waiver covers nine services including Adult Life Planning, Environmental Accessibility Adaptations, Family Consultation, Intensive Individual Support Services, Residential Habilitation, Respite Care, and Therapeutic Integration. Participants receive Service Coordination/targeted case management and qualify for full Medical Assistance benefits. Services are provided in the home and community outside school hours. Service coordination staff work with local education agencies and county health departments to identify and enroll eligible children in the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides community-based therapeutic services and support including respite care, environmental accessibility adaptations, family consultation and training, residential habilitation, intensive individual support services, therapeutic integration, adult life planning, and service coordination/case management. Services are delivered through Medicaid in the home and community outside school hours. Participants receive Service Coordination/targeted case management through their local education agency and county health departments, and qualify for full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing enrollment when slots become available; 45 days to accept invitation, establish contact, complete technical eligibility checklist, and submit financial application; 30 days to provide updated/additional information if needed; 15 day extension period granted if deadline not met

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based therapeutic services and support including adult life planning, home accessibility modifications, family consultation and training, one-on-one support services, residential habilitation, respite care, therapeutic integration programs, service coordination and case management, and full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Children and youth must reside in Maryland. Services are available statewide through over 60 approved provider agencies and county health departments. Montgomery County provides coordination through its Aging and Disability Services division.

Meet eligibility requirements for an Intermediate Care Facility for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) institutional level of care

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families interested in the Autism Waiver call the Autism Waiver Registry at 1-866-417-3480 or 240-777-1216 for initial screening. An initial screening is conducted by an MDH provider during an admission call based on parent self-report. If eligible, the child's name is added to the registry and waiting list. Waiver slots are filled through attrition on a first-come, first-served basis. When a vacancy occurs, eligible families from the registry are contacted to apply with a 45-day deadline to accept invitation, establish contact, complete technical eligibility checklist, and submit financial application. Families work with the AW Contact at their local education agency to complete the application and confirm technical, financial, and medical eligibility. The LEA or MSDE monitors application progress. Families receive notification if ineligible or if documents are not submitted within the timeframe. A 15-day extension period may be granted if the deadline is not met. Required documentation may include medical records, school records, and the child's IEP.

structured_extraction.program_name: Office for Blindness & Vision Services (OBVS) - Employment and Vocational Rehabilitation
structured_extraction.program_description: OBVS provides vocational rehabilitation services to help individuals who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind obtain competitive employment. Services include career guidance, assistive technology, career training, job placement, and other support to prepare people with vision loss for work. OBVS also offers transition services for students with disabilities, independent living programs for people 55 and over with vision loss, and business enterprise training opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: OBVS provides specialized training and technical assistance including career guidance and exploration, assistive technology such as screen reading software, magnifiers, and low vision aids, career training or academic education, orientation and mobility instruction, independent living skills training (safe cooking techniques, personal care, household task management, safe travel instruction, long white cane use), and job placement support. Services are provided by specially trained teachers, counselors, and technical specialists located throughout Maryland in three regional offices (Baltimore, Wheaton, and Annapolis).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind seeking employment or vocational rehabilitation services. Also serves students with disabilities (transition services) and people with vision loss age 55 and over (independent living programs).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career guidance and exploration, assistive technology provision, career training, orientation and mobility training, independent living skills development, and job placement support for individuals with vision loss.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. OBVS serves all Maryland counties through three regional offices: Baltimore office (Baltimore City, Baltimore, Cecil, Howard, Harford), Wheaton office (Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Montgomery, Washington), and Annapolis office (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Kent, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester).
requirements_list: Primary disability is vision loss (blindness or low vision)
Seeking employment or vocational rehabilitation services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Request DORS Services form online at dors.maryland.gov or contact your local DORS office to request services. The form can be completed by the individual, a parent, family member, medical provider, teacher, or other advocate. After submission, you will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where a DORS counselor will gather information and determine your eligibility. If eligible, you will be assigned a counselor or teacher who works in your community.

structured_extraction.program_description: Educational support services for job seekers with Autism in collaboration with community colleges throughout Maryland. The program includes adjustment to college life, assessment services, career guidance and counseling, employment and communication skills training, and individual and group sessions to support students in their vocational goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pathways provides individual and group sessions, career counseling, employment skills training, communication skills development, and coordination with Disability Support Services. Students enroll in credit/certificate classes and register with Disability Support Services at their community college. The program is offered throughout Maryland at multiple community colleges.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with documented diagnosis of Autism in Maryland attending community college for job preparation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational support services for college transition and employment preparation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at community colleges throughout Maryland including Anne Arundel Community College, Community College of Baltimore County, Howard Community College, Prince George's Community College, College of Southern Maryland, and Montgomery College
requirements_list: Have a documented diagnosis of Autism
Have an active DORS Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that supports college as part of a vocational plan
Register with the Disability Support Services program at the college
Attend weekly group sessions and schedule classes around standing appointment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local DORS Counselor or DORS office to request services and learn more about the program. Students must have a documented Autism diagnosis, establish an IPE with DORS, register with their college's Disability Support Services, and commit to attending weekly group sessions.

structured_extraction.program_description: PEAS provides instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to Pre-ETS students with Autism, exposing them to soft skills needed to obtain and maintain employment. The program includes introduction to education/training/employment options (apprenticeships, career training, job placement, college), college tours, and soft skills development. Part of the Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities (CPSEO) program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: PEAS provides self-advocacy instruction, social skills training, introduction to education/training/employment options (apprenticeships, career training, job placement, college), college tours, and soft skills development to Pre-ETS students with Autism. Classroom and other activities expose students to soft skills needed to obtain and maintain employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current high school, post-high school, or trade school students with Autism Spectrum Disorder; Pre-Employment Transition Services students with Autism diagnosis
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Self-advocacy instruction, social skills training, introduction to education, training, and employment options including apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college preparation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland; Available at DORS Workforce & Technology Center
requirements_list: Currently enrolled in high school, post-high school education program, or recognized educational program
At least 14 years old but less than 22 years old
Has an IEP, 504 plan, or medical records documenting disability
Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
Pre-ETS student status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS Counselor or local office to request services via QR code. Pre-ETS students with Autism diagnosis participate in classroom and other activities focused on employment-related soft skills.

structured_extraction.program_description: Services that prepare students with disabilities to transition from school to post-school life by providing job exploration counseling, instruction in self-advocacy, counseling on post-secondary education opportunities, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences. Services are specifically available for individuals who are blind or visually impaired as well as other students with disabilities. Services are offered at the Workforce & Technology Center campus and other locations throughout the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five specific services are provided: Job Exploration Counseling, Instruction in Self-Advocacy, Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities, Workplace Readiness Training, and Work-Based Learning Experiences. Services prepare students to transition from school to post-school employment and life.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities ages 14 to 21 who are enrolled in secondary, post-secondary, or other recognized educational programs and have a documented disability. Services are also available for students who are blind or visually impaired.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services focus on preparing students to transition from school to post-school employment and life through training and counseling services including job exploration, self-advocacy instruction, workplace readiness, post-secondary education counseling, and work-based learning experiences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Services are offered at the Workforce & Technology Center campus and other locations throughout the state.
requirements_list: Is enrolled in a secondary school (including home school or other alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program or other recognized educational program, and has not graduated or withdrawn
Is at least 14 years old but less than age 22
Has a disability documented with an Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan or medical records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Anyone may request DORS services by completing a Request DORS Services form. Contact your local DORS office or the staff specialist for students and transitioning youth.

structured_extraction.program_description: Academic instruction program for individuals with disabilities who are not yet at the skill level needed for GED instruction and want a high school diploma to pursue employment goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pre-GED instruction program offered at WTC and virtually. Participants must have at least 7th grade reading and math skills as measured by CASAS or TABE assessments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities seeking a high school diploma
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-GED academic instruction
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at WTC and virtually
requirements_list: Individuals should have at least 7th grade reading and math skills as recorded on the CASAS or TABE

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides funding to local education agencies and private providers to deliver high-quality full-day prekindergarten and school readiness services for three- and four-year-old children from families earning up to 300% of Federal Poverty Level at no cost to families. Aligns with The Blueprint for Maryland's Future.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding totaling $26,644,000 with estimated average grant amount of $400,000 for approximately 50 awards. Funding of $19,950 per full-day slot for three- and four-year-olds from families earning up to 300% of Federal Poverty Level. Grant period: July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027. Twenty percent (20%) advance payment available upon request. Funds support salaries and wages for teaching staff, contracted services, curriculum materials and supplies, professional learning and coaching, child assessments, CLASS observations, Maryland EXCELS accreditation support, and operational costs. Funds cannot be directed to tuition.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, March 11, 2026. No later than 5:00 pm EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Three- and four-year-old children from families with household incomes up to 300% of Federal Poverty Level, including children with disabilities, English and multilingual learners, and students experiencing homelessness. Local school systems and qualified private providers delivering prekindergarten services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries and wages for teaching and instructional staff, contracted services, curriculum materials and supplies, professional development and training, child assessments and CLASS observations, high-quality instructional materials (HQIM) implementation, Maryland EXCELS accreditation support, community and business partnerships, administrative and operational costs, and health screenings and family engagement activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. All 24 Maryland Local Education Agencies (LEAs), all counties, and Baltimore City are eligible. MSDE reserves the right to consider geographic distribution in award decisions.
requirements_list: Provider must hold a valid license or registration
Provider must be a Head Start program or meet other qualifying vendor requirements as defined in COMAR 13a.06.02
Serve children from families with household incomes up to 300% of Federal Poverty Level
Programs must participate in Maryland's EXCELS program
Lead teachers must have state certification in early childhood education or bachelor's degree with MAAPP alternative pathway
Programs must meet Maryland EXCELS rating of Level 3 or higher for private providers or Level 4 or higher for public providers
Full-day program with minimum 6.5 hours of instruction for 180 school days per year
Child-to-instructional staff ratio of 10:1 maximum, class size of 20 maximum with at least one highly qualified teacher
Inclusion of children with disabilities required
Developmentally appropriate, culturally and linguistically responsive instruction aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards
Instructional staff salaries comparable to local K-12 staff
Valid, reliable child assessment tool required
Health screenings in vision, hearing/speech/language, general health, and physical development
Programs receiving Blueprint funding must demonstrate track record of success
High-quality professional development for all staff with individualized plans and coaching
Program evaluation for continuous improvement
On-site or accessible comprehensive services and community partnerships with screening and referrals
Evidence-based health and safety standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through online Qualtrics form by March 11, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EDT. Four-section application: Applicant Information, Slots Requested, Application (Full or Modified based on eligibility responses), and Appendices. Full Application pathway or Modified Short Form option available for existing grantees with track record of success. Applicants can attend customer service support sessions and office hours for guidance. FAQs will be posted to the Prekindergarten webpage following support sessions. Funding opportunity details and attachments available through MSDE Office of Grants Administration and Compliance website. Applications reviewed by MSDE Review Committee. Responses are saved in browser on same device/browser. Must review application before submission and download PDF copy for records. Cannot make changes after submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: An initiative designed by a local school system to address the needs of an individual student or group of students at high risk of placement in a nonpublic special education school. The partnership uses wrap-around supportive services within the public school setting to meet targeted needs and is especially beneficial for school systems building local capacity to address specific, immediate needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Partnership initiative utilizing wrap-around supportive services within the public school setting to address the needs of individual students or groups of students at high risk of nonpublic special education placement.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sheila F. Philip, JD, Section Chief, Nonpublic Special Education
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems seeking to build local capacity to serve students at high risk of placement in nonpublic special education programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wrap-around supportive services within the public school setting for students at high risk of nonpublic special education placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland through Local School Systems.
requirements_list: Student or group of students must be at high risk of placement in a nonpublic special education school
Initiative designed by local school system
Partnership must address a targeted, specific, immediate need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Preventative Service Plan available upon request from the Nonpublic Special Education Section.

structured_extraction.program_name: Professional Learning in Early Literacy Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to Local School Systems to support professional learning targeted at Pre-K teachers on evidence-based reading instruction strategies based on the Science of Reading. The program supports training for Pre-K teachers, assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, and private childcare teachers of 3-year-olds and 4-year-olds. School administrators and childcare directors are also encouraged to participate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $40,000 to $80,000 to support professional learning programs in early literacy. Funding is used to provide training and materials to Pre-K educators aligned to Science of Reading research. Grant funds support facilitator/vendor fees, program evaluation, and dissemination activities. Estimated 12-24 grants to be awarded from a total of $1,000,000 in available funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 11, 2022, No later than 5:00 pm EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems seeking to provide professional learning in Science of Reading to Pre-K teachers, assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, and private childcare providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional learning and training for Pre-K educators on evidence-based reading instruction strategies, materials, and instruction aligned to Science of Reading research. Funds may support facilitator/vendor fees, program evaluation, dissemination activities, salaries and wages for program staff, contracted services for professional learning facilitators, supplies and materials for training, equipment, and other allowable charges including indirect costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Local School Systems in Maryland. The Maryland State Department of Education reserves the right to consider geographic distribution when making awards.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local School System (LSS)
Professional learning must be targeted at Pre-K teachers, assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, and private childcare providers of 3- and 4-year-olds
Training must be aligned to Science of Reading research
School administrators and childcare directors are encouraged to participate
Clearly state the problem and identify target population
Cite multiple data sources (qualitative and quantitative)
Define clear, ambitious, and attainable goals and outcomes
Identify approved vendor and qualified facilitator
Demonstrate alignment to Maryland Leads application
Engage private child care providers and Head Start staff
Include comprehensive timeline and evaluation plan for program success
Assign all grant tasks to qualified personnel with distributed workload
Include 1-page resumes for key personnel
Provide reasonable budget with aligned line items and accurate calculations
Submit C-125 MSDE budget form (signed)
Submit recipient assurances page (signed)
Include scope of work from approved vendor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit proposals via email to the contact address. Grant Information Guide was released September 13, 2022. Customer service support sessions were held to help applicants understand the application process. Applications are scored on a 100-point rubric across six categories: Extent of Need (10 points), Goals (20 points), Implementation Plan (30 points), Evaluation and Dissemination (10 points), Management Plan (10 points), and Budget (20 points).

structured_extraction.program_name: Project SELECT (Student Education, Lunchroom Environment, and Culinary Training)
structured_extraction.program_description: A team nutrition training grant from USDA that targeted middle schools with training and technical assistance in culinary and food service operations, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, and nutrition education. The goal was to increase student selection and consumption of vegetables and fruits and improve student knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors about healthy eating. A family engagement wellness toolkit was developed to support wellness policy implementation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Training and technical assistance in culinary and food service operations, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, and nutrition education provided to middle schools. A family engagement wellness toolkit was developed to support wellness policy implementation involving families and parents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle schools in targeted school systems in Allegany, Baltimore City, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Wicomico counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance in culinary and food service operations, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, nutrition education, and development of family engagement wellness toolkit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Five targeted school systems: Allegany, Baltimore City, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Wicomico counties.
requirements_list: Status as a middle school in a participating school system
Participation from Allegany, Baltimore City, Montgomery, Prince George's, or Wicomico school systems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The grant was implemented from 2016 through 2019. Participants included five targeted school systems, University of Maryland Food Supplement Nutrition Education (FSNE), and University of Maryland Baltimore Division of Growth and Nutrition.

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding agreement between a Local School System and a Maryland State Department of Education-approved nonpublic special education program to serve students with significant and intensive needs in the Least Restrictive Environment. The program enhances Individualized Education Program services for students in their community and is especially beneficial for students with short-term needs, requiring an alternative special education program, or experiencing a crisis while awaiting more intensive placement. It provides flexible funding based on full-time equivalent (FTE) seats rather than individual student enrollment. State tuition contributions are calculated based on actual FTE seats used, following the tuition contribution outlined in Education Article § 8-415.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State tuition contributions calculated based on actual full-time equivalent (FTE) seats used, following the tuition contribution outlined in Education Article § 8-415. Funding must be cost neutral to the State. Funding agreement for partnership classrooms or programs between Local School Systems and approved nonpublic special education providers to serve students with significant and intensive needs in the Least Restrictive Environment. Supports short-term placements, access to public school instruction and activities, and facilitates student transitions to less restrictive programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 (annually); applications must be submitted a minimum of 30 calendar days prior to requesting State funding for each fiscal year
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sheila F. Philip, JD, Section Chief, Nonpublic Special Education
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems seeking to partner with Maryland State Department of Education-approved nonpublic special education programs to serve students with significant and intensive special education needs, including students requiring short-term placements, students in crisis situations, and students awaiting more intensive placements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State tuition contributions and operational costs for nonpublic special education program seats, enhanced IEP services, wrap-around services for Preventive Service Partnerships, alternative programming, and support for student transitions to less restrictive programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; partnerships established between Local School Systems and approved nonpublic special education programs.
requirements_list: Student must have significant and intensive needs
Nonpublic special education program must be Maryland State Department of Education-approved
Partnership must serve students in the Least Restrictive Environment
Mid-year enrollment report and outcome data report due January 15
End-of-year enrollment report or outcome data report due June 1
Local School Systems must initiate discussions with MSDE regarding new proposals by February 1
Closed fiscal year reconciliation must be completed by July 30
Finalized and signed contracts must be submitted to MSDE prior to release of state funds
MSDE Public/Private Partnership Application required annually by June 1
Public/Private Partnership Agreement or Contract required
Budget completed by nonpublic provider using MSDE budget packet
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local School Systems initiate discussions with MSDE about new proposals by February 1. Applications are submitted by June 1. MSDE provides notice of intent to fund by July 15. Mid-year reports are due January 15, and end-of-year reports are due June 1. Multi-stage annual process beginning with proposal discussions, followed by application submission, MSDE funding decision, and contract finalization.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps child care providers expand their business and access state prekindergarten funding by providing guidance on grant requirements and simplifying the application process. Pre-K Specialists guide providers through the application process step by step.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides access to state prekindergarten funding and offers technical assistance to help child care providers meet the requirements for Pre-K grants and expand their services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers looking to expand their business and access state prekindergarten funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To expand child care services and support prekindergarten programming.
requirements_list: Read the Grant Information Guide (GIG) and understand it
Organization must meet eligibility criteria outlined in the GIG
Organization must have technical expertise, personnel, and financial capacity to provide services as described in the GIG
All organizational stakeholders must be supportive of applying for the grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a checklist of four qualifying questions before beginning the grant application process. Answer "yes" to each checklist question before proceeding. Pre-K Specialists guide providers through the application process step by step.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding for professional learning initiatives, the Child Development Associate credential for Prekindergarten Assistant Teachers, planning for coordinated Prekindergarten mixed delivery enrollment, and accreditation in the Maryland EXCELS program. Grant funds support continuous improvement using the Ready for Kindergarten comprehensive assessment system for Prekindergarten and Kindergarten, including assessment administration fidelity, professional development on assessment reliability, data-based instructional decision-making, and research-based teaching practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support administration of the Kindergarten Readiness Assessment and professional learning activities to improve teacher practices and increase Prekindergarten students' readiness for Kindergarten. Funds support program credentialing and coordination with private child care providers.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 3, 2022 by 5:00 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional learning initiatives, Child Development Associate credential for Prekindergarten Assistant Teachers, planning for coordinated Prekindergarten mixed delivery enrollment process, accreditation in the Maryland EXCELS program, assessment administration and professional development, data-based instructional decision-making, and research-based content and pedagogical best practices.

requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local School System
Grant funds must be used to support initiatives for continuous improvement using the R4K comprehensive assessment system for Prekindergarten and Kindergarten
Funds must support assessment administration fidelity and professional development focused on assessment reliability
Funds must support data-based instructional decision-making and research-based content and pedagogical best practices

Technical assistance sessions are available to help applicants understand requirements and ask questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A summer program collaboration for pre-employment transition services (Pre-ETS) and transitioning youth who are blind or visually impaired, focusing on career exploration, work readiness, and development of self-advocacy and independence skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Summer program offering career exploration, work readiness training, and skill development including college and vocational options, work skills, technology instruction, self-advocacy, independence and social skills instruction, interest inventory survey, guest speakers, and community resources. Services offered in the community, at WTC, and virtually.
