Must be Pre-ETS participant or transitioning youth

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides children with nutritious breakfast meals through federal reimbursement and state supplemental funding. Studies show breakfast correlates with higher test scores, decreased emotional and behavioral problems, reduced food insecurity, less frequent visits to the nurse, and fewer school absences. The Maryland Meals for Achievement program supplements federal reimbursements, allowing 581 participating schools to offer free breakfast in the classroom to all students. The program assists schools and residential child care institutions in providing breakfast to school-age children, with funds used to help offset costs of producing meals. Free or reduced-price meals are available to students from families with incomes at or below 130-185% of the poverty level, and to students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive federal reimbursement dollars for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards. State funds supplement federal meal reimbursements to enable participating schools to provide free breakfast in the classroom to all students. The program provides direct payments to help cover the costs of producing meals. Currently, 581 schools participate in the Maryland Meals for Achievement program. Free or reduced-price meals are available to students from families with incomes at or below 130-185% of the poverty level, and to students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: All students in Maryland public schools, participating non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions. Free or reduced-price meals available to students from eligible low-income families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Breakfast meals for students that meet USDA nutrition standards, including free breakfast offered in the classroom. Funds help offset costs of producing meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school systems and 17 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate. The Maryland Meals for Achievement program is currently available in 581 participating Maryland schools.
requirements_list: Meals must comply with USDA nutrition standards
Students from families with incomes at or below 130-185% of the poverty level may receive free or reduced-price meals
Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals
Schools must participate in the School Breakfast Program
Schools must be willing to offer free breakfast in the classroom
Schools must participate in the School Breakfast Program to receive state supplemental funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools participate in the program and receive federal reimbursement for compliant meals. Schools can apply to participate in the Maryland Meals for Achievement program and receive state supplemental funding. Students from eligible families can apply for free or reduced-price meals through their school district.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides milk to children in schools, child care institutions and eligible camps that do not participate in other federal child nutrition meal service programs. Reimburses schools and institutions for milk they serve. Schools in National School Lunch or School Breakfast Programs may also participate to provide milk to children in half-day pre-K and kindergarten programs without access to school meal programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct reimbursement to schools and institutions for milk provided to eligible children.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children in schools, child care institutions, and eligible camps.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Milk provision to children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Administered at federal level; state education agencies administer at state level.
requirements_list: Schools/institutions must not participate in other federal child nutrition meal service programs, or only provide milk to non-participating pre-K/kindergarten half-day programs

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations that offer enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Eligible programs provide learning experiences aligned with the State's curricular and educational priorities and the Blueprint for Maryland's Future that cannot be replicated in the classroom. Programs emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, and tutoring. Pre- and post-visit activities for teachers and professional development opportunities that connect SAI programs to classroom curriculum are also funded. Currently serves 57 organizations; in FY2024 served approximately 440,000 Maryland students and teachers. Grant period: July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027. Approximately $6,706,449 available with an estimated 60-65 grants to be awarded.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants provided to qualified non-profit organizations to fund enriching educational programs including experiential learning, field trips, mentoring, tutoring, teacher pre- and post-visit activities, and professional development for teachers. Grant period runs from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Approximately $6,706,449 available with an estimated 60-65 grants to be awarded. Funds support evidence-based educational activities aligned with state curricula, program outreach and expansion to new schools and LEAs, data collection and program evaluation, personnel and implementation costs, and salaries for key staff. Funds cannot be used for operating costs such as day-to-day operations, property repair/maintenance, property taxes, insurance, utilities, furniture, salaries for office/leadership staff, office supplies, or rent. Optional initial 25% disbursement available in July 2026. Funding augmentation available for organizations seeking additional funds. Less than 50% of budget can come from state grants (except Baltimore Zoo). Nonprofit organizations enter all funds on line 214 ("Community Services"). Funding requests should align with current funding levels for existing SAIs or historical award amounts for new applicants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland nonprofit organizations providing enriching educational programs to Maryland PreK-12 students and teachers, including individuals with disabilities. Public schools, nonpublic schools, and homeschools (with a maximum of 20% of participants from nonpublic schools and homeschools). Schools and Local Education Agencies (LEAs), including Title I schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, pre- and post-visit activities for teachers, and professional development opportunities for teachers connecting programs to classroom curriculum. Evidence-based educational activities aligned with state curricula, program outreach and expansion to new schools and LEAs, data collection and program evaluation, and personnel and implementation costs including salaries for key staff implementing programs. Funds should support direct educational program activities. Funds cannot be used for operating costs, day-to-day operations, property repair/maintenance, property taxes, insurance, utilities, furniture, salaries for office/leadership staff, office supplies, or rent.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open on Thursday, May 1, 2025. Applicants must submit their completed application by Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT. Applications include program narrative and required appendices (501(c)(3) documentation, liability insurance coverage, independent governing board member list, Fiscal Impact Statement, student safety response, and GEPA Section 427 response). structured_extraction.program_description: The Ticket to Work program connects people with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) with Employment Networks (EN) or state Vocational Rehabilitation programs like DORS. The program helps participants develop employment plans, receive training and career counseling, and achieve sustainable employment while providing protection from Continuing Disability Reviews as long as the Ticket remains in use and timely progress is demonstrated. Services provided include job training, career counseling, job placement, job coaching, vocational rehabilitation, benefits planning, and ongoing support services necessary to achieve a work goal. The program is free and voluntary with no costs to participate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services provided include job training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, job coaching, benefits planning, and ongoing support services necessary to achieve a work goal. The program provides work incentives including the ability to try working without immediately losing benefits, earn more money, keep health insurance, and restore benefits if unable to work. Healthcare benefits continuation includes Medicare for up to 93 months and Medicaid continuation options. The program is free and voluntary with no costs to participate.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment and vocational services to help achieve and maintain employment based on participant goals, including job training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, job coaching, and benefits planning.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title IV, Part B Nita M. Lowey 21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program authorized under section 4201 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965, as amended by the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA). The program creates community learning centers providing out-of-school time (OST) programming before school, after school, during summer, and on Saturdays. Centers offer academic enrichment opportunities in core academic subjects (language arts, mathematics, science, social studies) and services that complement students' regular school programs. Programming includes youth development, substance abuse prevention, service-learning, violence prevention, counseling, arts, music, recreation, and technology education. Centers provide literacy instruction and educational development programs for families of participating students. The program targets students and families in schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs or schools serving high percentages of low-income students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides federal grant funding to eligible organizations to operate 21st Century Community Learning Centers. Grants are awarded for a 3-year grant period with level funding contingent on performance and funding availability. FY2026 total funds available: $22.6 million with 93% of funds used to fund out-of-school time programs. Grants are awarded at 100% of the original award for all three years contingent on funding availability and satisfactory performance; awards may be reduced based on failure to meet goals or performance measures. Funds support academic instruction, enrichment activities, staff salaries (project director, site coordinators, academic instruction teachers, enrichment teachers, parent liaisons, evaluators), professional development, curriculum and materials, equipment, contracted services, background checks, and transportation. Grant funds are provided on a reimbursement basis with a 6-8 week turnaround for invoiced expenses. Grantees are expected to attend bi-monthly networking meetings that offer technical assistance from Maryland State Department of Education personnel, peer-to-peer technical assistance, and resources selected based on grantee needs. Local Education Agencies must provide dollar-for-dollar matching contributions (cash and third-party in-kind contributions). In-kind contribution requirements: Year I (10%), Year II (15%), Year III (20%) of direct costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, August 29, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies, interagency and interdepartmental organizations, community-based organizations, faith-based organizations, private or public organizations, institutions of higher education, and consortia of two or more of these entities. Specifically, schools, local education agencies, faith-based organizations, and community-based organizations that serve students in grades 1-12, particularly those attending low-performing schools or Title I schools serving at least 40% low-income students, high schools with graduation rates below 67%, limited English proficient students, and students in rural communities (locale codes 32, 33, 41, 42, 43). Services target students and families primarily attending Title I eligible schools or schools serving high percentages of low-income students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic enrichment opportunities and instructional services in core academic subjects (language arts, mathematics, science, social studies); youth development activities; substance abuse prevention; service-learning; violence prevention; counseling; arts, music, recreation, and technology education; family literacy instruction and educational development programs; behavioral health supports and wraparound services; college and career readiness activities; salaries and wages for program staff including project directors, site coordinators, academic instruction teachers, enrichment teachers, parent liaisons, evaluators, and finance agents/bookkeepers; contracted services; supplies and materials (maximum 8% of total requested); equipment (maximum 3% of total requested); professional development and training; travel; external evaluation services (maximum 7% of total requested); background checks; and transportation. Funds cannot be used for food, facilities, vehicles, new construction, interest expenses, debt services, or check cashing fees.

Competitive priority given to rural areas (locale codes 32, 33, 41, 42, 43).

structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-week retail training program for people with disabilities designed to prepare participants for competitive integrated employment in retail settings, particularly at CVS stores. The program combines classroom instruction in a mock CVS store setting, hands-on learning activities at actual CVS locations, and paid work experience. The program consists of four weeks of classroom instruction and mock store training delivered by Community College of Baltimore County instructors and DORS staff, followed by six weeks of paid in-store work experience at CVS Pharmacy stores throughout Maryland. The program is offered three times per calendar year through DORS Workforce & Technology Center locations, providing opportunities for approximately 24 participants annually. Participants develop retail skills including inventory management, customer service, cash register operation, phone and intercom etiquette, and non-verbal communication.

structured_extraction.program_name: Business Resource Information, Development, and Guidance Ecosystem (BRIDGE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's BRIDGE Program connects businesses to advisory services, access to capital, and region-wide resources to help grow and scale their business. The program provides legal, accounting, and financial advisory services specifically to Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI)-owned businesses and Very Small Businesses (VSBs) with fewer than 10 employees. BRIDGE delivers nine integrated services: diagnostic assessment and roadmap creation, financial literacy and credit repair training, CDFI technical assistance including loan application preparation, subsidized accounting and bookkeeping support, women's access to capital and entrepreneurship training, rural and urban business innovation advising, federal funding proposal development, free legal services through University of Maryland law clinics, and a loaned executive program providing up to 40 hours of executive advisory. These services help businesses become capital-ready and access funding from federal sources and state credit initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: BRIDGE delivers free or subsidized technical assistance through nine integrated services: BRIDGE Advising (diagnostic assessment and roadmap creation), Financial Literacy and Credit Repair training, CDFI Technical Assistance (loan application preparation and financial advisory), Back-Office-In-A-Box (subsidized accounting and bookkeeping support), Women's Access to Capital & Entrepreneurship training, Rural & Urban Business Innovation Initiative advising, BRIDGE Proposal Lab (federal funding proposal development), free legal services through University of Maryland law clinics, and Loaned Executive Program (up to 40 hours of executive advisory). These services are provided at no cost to eligible businesses. The program connects participants to advisory services, access to capital, and region-wide resources.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an application through the online form at https://tedco.tfaforms.net/184. Based on this assessment, Advisors create an Individualized BRIDGE Roadmap directing the business to specific legal, accounting, and financial technical assistance services. Advisors maintain contact with businesses throughout the program to support progress. Alternatively, businesses can attend an Open Forum to learn more about the program or contact TEDCO directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: An entrepreneurial resource hub and joint initiative between TEDCO, the Maryland Department of Commerce, Anne Arundel County, and the U.S. Department of Defense that helps entrepreneurs, technology companies, scientists, engineers, and DoD lab personnel commercialize defense technologies developed at National Security Agency/Fort Meade and other Maryland labs including Aberdeen Proving Ground, Fort Detrick, and other Maryland research facilities. The program connects Maryland businesses to federal labs for product development, testing, intellectual property licensing, and related services to help companies bring innovation to market faster and assists in identifying which technologies are right for businesses and determining viability for commercialization. Members and clients receive comprehensive support including access to technical experts, intellectual property and technology guidance, business support, research tools, information about the technology transfer process, networking opportunities with transfer staff and scientists, education on commercialization topics, and one-on-one mentoring for licensing technology from DoD labs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DefTech provides a highly competitive membership program with limited slots annually, focusing on high technology and bio innovation sectors, as well as free services to entrepreneurs and federal lab personnel. Members and clients receive: DefTech Academy & Certification courses on technology transfer and government contracting; pre-lab engagement training if needed; proprietary monthly distribution of federal funding opportunities; private meetings with federal labs to learn about collaborative research and available intellectual property; monthly virtual office hours with DefTech Advisors; technical assistance on navigating the Department of Defense technology transfer process; networking opportunities with technology transfer staff and scientists; education covering market-oriented product development, intellectual property and patent law, customer discovery, and T2 topics; and one-on-one mentoring for clients interested in licensing technology from DoD labs, including identifying relevant intellectual property, conducting market analysis, and developing commercialization plans. The program cost was waived for the initial 30 companies in the first program year due to DoD Office of Local Community Cooperation, Maryland Department of Commerce, and TEDCO funding. Graduate companies are eligible for alumni membership.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII) is a comprehensive program supporting the transition of promising technologies from qualifying universities to the commercial sector. The program operates through two complementary tracks: (1) Technology Assessment Awards, which provide funding to university researchers and faculty at seven eligible Maryland institutions to validate promising research technologies and assess their commercial market potential over a 9-month period; and (2) Company Formation support, which assists newly created Maryland-based start-up companies that have licensed technology from qualifying universities with commercial launch and early-stage development. Both tracks foster commercialization through technical validation, market assessment, licensing, or creation of start-up companies in Maryland. The program provides funding in the form of grants, convertible notes, or equity investments to help advance technologies toward commercialization and achieve technical and commercial milestones.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technology Assessment Awards: Grants of up to $130,000 for single university applications or up to $180,000 for joint applications from two or more qualifying universities (with minimum 25% budget allocation to at least two universities). Additional funding available: up to $15,000 for Commercialization Plan development, up to $5,000 for I-Corps participation, up to $4,500 for company formation or attorney costs for licensing, and up to $12,500 for patent expenses. Eligible expenses include personnel salaries and fringe benefits, equipment, materials and supplies, commercialization consultants, and other direct costs; no indirect charges allowed except for patent expenses. Company Formation Awards: Investments of up to $300,000 for a 9-month commercial launch period provided as either (1) Reimbursable Grants with 3% quarterly revenue repayment for 10 years or until 2x amount repaid, or (2) Convertible Debt Notes with 5-year maturity, 8% annual fixed interest rate, convertible to equity upon subsequent investor issuance of $500,000+, acquisition, or asset sale. Funds support product development, technology advancement, technical milestones, business development, market validation, and go-to-market strategy execution. Indirect costs up to $60,000 including patent and licensing costs up to $30,000 are allowed for company formation awards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Quarterly deadlines: January 15, April 15, July 15, and October 15, 2026 (and annually thereafter). Complete applications must be submitted by 5:00pm on the 15th day (or first business day thereafter) of each submission month.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technology Assessment Awards: Technology validation, market assessment, and commercialization activities for promising research technologies. Funding supports development and assessment of medical devices, therapeutics, biotechnology products, renewable energy systems, software applications, and other innovative technologies. Eligible uses include conducting technology validation and market assessment, customer discovery through I-Corps programs, market analysis, industry expert consultation, interim CEO engagement, regulatory strategy development, company formation activities and attorney costs, information gathering for commercialization planning, domestic travel for customer discovery, personnel salaries and fringe benefits, equipment purchases, materials and supplies, consulting and professional services, machining, subcontracts, tuition, and patent expenses. Company Formation Awards: Commercial launch and development activities for technology-based products and services derived from licensed university research technologies. Eligible costs include: personnel salaries and fringe benefits; equipment; materials and supplies; other direct costs (manufacturing, subcontracts, consulting); indirect costs (up to $60,000 including patent and licensing costs up to $30,000). Funds support technology development to achieve technical and commercial milestones, positioning company for product launch, customer acquisition, and follow-on investment.

The 'nerve center' of business must be in Maryland and company must lease or own a Maryland facility.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a one-time TEDCO registration ID. Engage with a Site Miner from your qualifying university at least one month (30 days) before submitting your application to discuss MII program requirements. Site Miner must provide a minimum of two weeks advance review of the application, providing feedback to strengthen submission. Obtain a current dated letter of approval from your Site Miner. Prepare your proposal and application materials addressing technology description, market analysis, business model, go-to-market strategy, risk assessment, detailed budget, and project milestones. Submit a complete application through the online platform (AmpliFund for Company Formation) by 5:00pm on a quarterly deadline date (January 15, April 15, July 15, or October 15, or first business day thereafter). Applications must include all required information with budget in tabular form and comprehensive commercialization plan components (Executive Summary, Business Plan, and Pitch Deck). Applications are evaluated using detailed rubric across five scored sections: Technology Description & IP, Market Analysis & Competition, Commercialization Pathway & Risk Assessment, Project Milestones & Budget, and Executive Summary & Team. If you do not know your Site Miner's name, email MII@tedcomd.com for assistance. After award completion, submit final report with required documentation within 30 days of award term end for review and approval by Program Committee before final payment disbursement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII) Technology Assessment Awards
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII) Technology Assessment Awards provide funding to university researchers and faculty at seven eligible Maryland institutions—Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, University of Maryland College Park, Frostburg State University, and Bowie State University—to validate promising research technologies and assess their commercial market potential. The program supports early-stage university research projects for a 9-month period to advance technologies toward commercialization, with focus on technical validation, market assessment, licensing to commercial partners, or creation of start-up companies in Maryland. Funding supports diverse technologies including medical devices, therapeutics, biotechnology, materials science, renewable energy, and software applications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $130,000 for a 9-month technology validation and market assessment period for single university applications. Joint applications from two or more qualifying universities may receive grants of up to $180,000 directed toward commercializing technologies existing at multiple universities or activities taking place at multiple universities (minimum 25% budget allocation to at least two universities required). Additional funding available: up to $15,000 for Commercialization Plan development, up to $5,000 for I-Corps participation, up to $4,500 for company formation or attorney costs for licensing, and up to $12,500 for patent expenses related to technology. Funding supports early-stage research for developing and assessing technologies including medical devices, therapeutics, biotechnology products, renewable energy systems, software applications, and other innovative technologies aimed at commercialization. Eligible expenses include personnel salaries and fringe benefits, equipment purchases, materials and supplies, commercialization consultants (FDA regulatory, business, company formation, I-Corps), and other direct costs such as machining, subcontracts, and tuition. No indirect/facilities and administrative charges allowed except for patent expenses.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program created through Maryland General Assembly legislation in 2022 that provides financial and technical assistance to support the growth and development of Makerspaces throughout Maryland. The program funds the establishment of new Makerspaces, expansion of existing Makerspaces, or development of programming for Makerspaces. The program serves shared workspace facilities that provide access to tools, technology, and knowledge for learners and entrepreneurs, results in the prototyping or creation of physical goods, and supports the development of technical education opportunities for personal growth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Type A (Establish New Makerspace): up to $100,000 per year for up to 3 years (maximum $300,000 total); feasibility study funding up to $25,000. Type B (Expand Existing Makerspace): up to $100,000 for one year. Type C (Develop Makerspace Programming): up to $25,000 for one year. Technical Assistance: up to 10 hours provided by Open Works for establishment, expansion, or operation needs. Applicants are required to provide a 1:1 matching funds contribution for Type A, B, and C grants, which can consist of cash or in-kind donations (such as donated materials, tools, space, or volunteer time). Allowable expenses include equipment, tools, technology, renovation costs, utility costs, operations, real estate purchase/renovations, planning, and educational programming.

Focus on entities operating or seeking to operate Makerspaces that serve as community spaces open to the general public.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used for establishment of a new Makerspace, expansion of an existing Makerspace, or development of programming for a Makerspace. Allowable expenses include operations, capital equipment, real estate purchase and renovations, planning, facility expansion, new tools and equipment, launching new services, and educational programming supporting personal growth, workforce training, and entrepreneurship.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural and Underserved Business Recovery from Impact of COVID-19 (RUBRIC)
structured_extraction.program_description: An economic relief initiative providing reimbursable grant funding to socially and economically disadvantaged and rural early-stage technology-based businesses harmed by the COVID-19 pandemic. The program is designed to bridge companies across the economic gap created by COVID-19 toward the next financing round or greater sustainability, helping attract and retain jobs and customers. Grants up to $100,000 per award provide bridge funding to help companies survive and scale to the next phase of fundraising.

Recipients reimburse through a royalty of 3% of quarterly revenues for a 5-year period, with a royalty cap at 150% of the award amount. Advance payment options available with a 10% discount reduction per year for early repayment. Funds are disbursed in two tranches: 50% at closing and 50% upon completion of an activity report. Second awards available after 6-month waiting period if first award successfully deployed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training and mentoring program that helps Maryland life science and technology businesses develop and submit Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) proposals to win federal grants. TEDCO selects up to 25 companies to participate in this comprehensive lab program designed to strengthen their proposals. The program provides comprehensive training materials, live workshops, hands-on mentoring, feedback on pitches and proposals, and guidance on government registrations to position companies for up to $305,000 of non-dilutive Phase I funding from the National Science Foundation and other federal agencies including NIH, NASA, Air Force, and USDA.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides comprehensive training materials, live workshops, and hands-on mentoring across two parts. Part I covers foundational business planning, commercialization, and pitch writing with 2 live workshops. Part II provides 6 additional workshops for companies with approved NSF pitches. Participants receive feedback from experienced reviewers, access to market research tools, guidance on government registrations (SAM.gov and Research.gov), and support on letters of support and teaming partners. TEDCO selects up to 25 companies to participate in the lab program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A social impact investment fund providing early-stage capital to pre-seed and early-stage technology startups founded by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals. The program addresses the gap between pre-seed and seed funding for businesses often overlooked by traditional sources of investment and financing. The fund includes multiple investment tracks: the Builder Fund typically invests initial amounts of $100,000 via convertible notes, while Social Impact and Inclusion Funds can invest up to $750,000 on a single deployment. Investments require a minimum 1:1 private capital match. Eligible startups must have their principal place of business in Maryland with more than half the workforce based in Maryland (for Social Impact Fund), at least one full-time employee, 30-50% or more founder ownership by individuals demonstrating economic disadvantage, fewer than 251 employees (Social Impact Fund), and equity raised to date of less than $15M (Social Impact Fund). Funded companies receive hands-on executive support, peer-to-peer mentorship, collaboration opportunities, and networking resources to help reach follow-on funding milestones and create jobs in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows federal agencies to provide funding to Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Phase I and Phase II awardees to enhance their project's commercialization potential. The program focuses on overcoming technical challenges, optimizing commercialization strategies, and minimizing risks associated with bringing innovative products or processes to market. Support includes technology assessment, market analysis and strategy, business model development, commercial roadmapping, investment readiness assessment, and intellectual property and regulatory guidance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Phase I awards provide up to $6,500 per award, which may be in addition to the SBIR/STTR award amount, depending on the federal agency. Phase II awards provide up to $50,000 per project, with the funding approach varying by agency—either as part of the award budget or in addition to it. Funds support technical and business assistance including technology assessment, market analysis, business model development, commercial roadmapping, investment readiness assessment, and intellectual property and regulatory guidance. Support can be used to help with business strategy, operations, product sales, intellectual property protection, market research, market validation, regulatory planning, and manufacturing plans.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive matching funds program that provides non-dilutive funding to small businesses that have received or are seeking federal Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) or Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) awards. The program aims to strengthen SBIR/STTR awards, promote job creation and economic development in Maryland, encourage commercialization of research by small businesses, facilitate technology transfer from universities and federal labs, and support economically disadvantaged small businesses in accessing federal funding. The program is administered at both the state level through TEDCO and locally through Montgomery County. For Phase I SBIR/STTR awards, companies receive a grant equal to the lesser of 25% of the Phase I award or $25,000. For Phase II SBIR/STTR awards, companies receive a grant equal to the lesser of 25% of the Phase II award or $75,000 (state level) or up to $50,000 (Montgomery County level). Montgomery County also provides Phase 0 grants that reimburse up to $5,000 of technical assistance expenditures associated with pursuing a first Phase I grant. Awards are issued on a quarterly basis or first-come-first-served basis, subject to fund availability. Up to 50% of matching grants may be used for reimbursement of technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance expenses. The program supports small businesses engaged in SBIR and STTR activities, with policies and procedures established at both state and local levels. Applicants must maintain at least 51% of R&D operations within Montgomery County for a minimum of 2 years from grant disbursement (county component).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) and Montgomery County

Phase 0 grants reimburse up to $5,000 of an applicant's technical assistance expenditures associated with pursuing their first Phase I grant. Awards are issued on a quarterly basis or first-come-first-served basis, subject to fund availability. Up to 50% of the matching grant may be used for reimbursement of technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance expenses. Matching grants are provided to support small businesses engaged in SBIR and STTR activities, with policies and procedures established at both state and local levels.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses that have received or are seeking a federal SBIR or STTR award, including economically disadvantaged small businesses, women-owned, and veteran-owned small businesses. Small businesses conducting innovation research and technology transfer activities in biotechnology, medicine, or life sciences, and Maryland-based companies. Montgomery County companies must conduct research in medicine, biotechnology, or life sciences and have a maximum of 20 employees at time of application.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Matching funds to complement SBIR/STTR federal awards and support Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer activities, including research in medicine, biotechnology, and life sciences. Funds may be used for research and development expenses, technical assistance costs, investment assistance, and commercialization assistance. Phase 0: Qualified reimbursable expenses for SBIR/STTR Phase I application preparation. Cannot reimburse expenses covered by Federal or State funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based companies for state program. Small businesses must be fewer than 250 employees and primarily engaged in technology or life sciences (not retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, or professional services). Montgomery County companies must conduct at least 51 percent of research and development operations in Montgomery County for county program. Applicant must maintain at least 51% of R&D operations within Montgomery County for a minimum of 2 years from grant disbursement.
requirements_list: Company must have received an SBIR or STTR award within six months of the application cycle (state level)
Company must have been awarded an SBIR or STTR Phase I or Phase II federal grant
Company must conduct research in medicine, biotechnology, or life sciences (for Montgomery County component)
Company must conduct at least 51 percent of research and development operations in Montgomery County (for Montgomery County component)
Application must be submitted online through TEDCO's application portal or Montgomery County Business Center website by the deadline at 5:00 pm Eastern Time
Small business status as defined by federal SBIR/STTR programs
Receipt of or eligibility for federal SBIR/STTR funding
Must be a small business with fewer than 250 employees
Must be primarily engaged in technology or life sciences
Not primarily engaged in retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, or professional services
Reports must be marked 'Confidential Business and Financial Information' at the top
Business must be in Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) (Montgomery County)
Maximum of 20 employees at time of application (Montgomery County)

For Phase 0: Business must have been in operation for 5 years or less and have received no prior SBIR/STTR awards and must have qualified reimbursable expenses related to a submitted SBIR/STTR Phase 1 proposal (Montgomery County)
For Phase 1: Business must have been in operation for 5 years or less and have received a maximum of 2 Phase 1 awards and zero Phase 2 awards in prior years (Montgomery County)
For Phase 2: Business must have been in operation for 7 years or less and have received a maximum of 4 Phase 1 awards and 1 Phase 2 award in prior years (Montgomery County)
Must maintain county-based R&D operations for minimum 2 years after grant disbursement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications online through TEDCO's application portal (state level) or Montgomery County Business Center website (county level) during the specified application cycle open dates or on a first-come-first-served basis. State level: Four cycles annually with open dates on January 1st, April 1st, July 1st, and October 1st, with deadlines at 5:00 pm Eastern Time on March 30th, June 30th, September 30th, and December 31st. Montgomery County: Phase 0, Phase 1, and Phase 2 applications are accepted through the County Business Center website and Montgomery County Business Portal during two application periods per calendar year on August 11 and February 15. Applications are reviewed on a quarterly basis according to announced cycle dates (state) or continuously (county). Applicants receive a confirmation email upon submission. For confirmation that an application was received, contact sbir-ta@tedcomd.com. For additional information on application procedures, contact TEDCO or the Department of Finance or Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_description: MarylandSaves is a state-facilitated workplace retirement savings program that allows Maryland employers to offer their employees an easy way to save for retirement and emergencies through automatic payroll deductions into portable Roth IRA WorkLife Savings Accounts. The program is free to set up and maintain, with no employer contributions required. Employers who register and submit payroll contributions or claim their exemption by December 31st each year receive a $300 waiver on their annual SDAT filing fee. Employees receive automatic enrollment through their employer with no action required, a default $1,000 emergency savings fund, and can make contributions with tax-free withdrawals during retirement. The program helps businesses recruit and retain employees while satisfying Maryland law requirements to offer a qualified retirement plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers who register with MarylandSaves and submit payroll contributions for their employees or claim an exemption before December 31st of each year receive a $300 waiver on their annual SDAT filing fee (also referred to as a $300 annual tax credit). Employers receive annual SDAT Annual Report fee waivers for each year they remain qualified, along with liability protection. The program itself is free to set up and maintain. Employers are not responsible for making employer contributions, establishing individual retirement accounts for employees, managing investment options, or processing withdrawals. Employees receive access to a portable retirement savings program with automatic payroll deductions into Roth IRA accounts, no employer contributions required, and a default $1,000 emergency savings fund. Employee participation is completely voluntary and can opt out at any time.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 31st annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers of any size who are required by Maryland law to offer their employees a retirement savings plan, and their employees seeking retirement savings options. Eligible entity types include incorporated entities, limited liability companies (LLCs), professional associations (P.A., P.C.), limited partnerships, corporations, and other registered Maryland business entities. Employees must be at least 18 years old and W-2 wage earners. Self-employed individuals may also participate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employees use the program to make retirement savings contributions from their paycheck into Roth IRA accounts, which are invested in retirement savings with tax-free withdrawals during retirement, for emergencies and retirement. Employers use the program to satisfy their legal obligation to offer a qualified retirement plan and receive SDAT filing fee waivers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland businesses conducting business in Maryland. Most Maryland employers are required to offer retirement savings plans under Maryland law. Statewide program. Must be registered and incorporated with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. Entities must have active, incorporated, or revived status. Business must be registered to conduct business in Maryland.

Employers must register with MarylandSaves and provide their Federal Employer Identification Number (EIN)
Employers must submit payroll contributions or claim an exemption by December 31st each year to receive the $300 filing fee waiver

Employers must update contribution rate changes, add new employees, and mark terminated employees appropriately
Businesses with no employees or that run manual payroll are exempt from registration requirements

Company must have at least one employee earning Maryland W-2 wages
Company must not currently offer a retirement savings program (or can request exemption if one exists)

Employees must pay through an automated payroll system
Company SDAT number and unique Access Code required for registration
Payroll provider information and schedule(s) required
Company bank information required
Current employee roster with personal information (name, contact info, DOB, SSN) required
Employees must be at least 18 years old
Employee participation is completely voluntary
Eligible to contribute to Roth IRA per federal IRS Code restrictions
Update employee deferral rates in payroll system within 30 days of onboarding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Register - Visit the MarylandSaves homepage or register through the online portal at marylandsaves.vestwell.com/register/employer using a step-by-step process. Set up identification and password, answer questions about the business and payroll process, complete payment setup, add employees, provide company SDAT number and unique Access Code, add payroll provider information and schedule(s), connect company bank account, and upload current employee roster with personal information. A payroll representative can be invited to help facilitate this process. Alternatively, employers who already offer a qualified retirement plan can claim their waiver using their EIN and SDAT number at marylandsaves.org/claim-fee-waiver/. Businesses that qualify for exemption can certify their exemption online at marylandsaves.vestwell.com/exempt. Step 2: Contribution Submission and Enrollment - After adding employees, MarylandSaves contacts them directly to explain options during a 30-day period to opt out or customize their account. Employees are auto-enrolled with a default 5% contribution rate of gross salary (adjustable) and receive a default $1,000 emergency savings fund. After 30 days, the employer records employee choices, begins payroll deductions, and submits contribution information and funding for employees who remain in the program. Step 3: Maintenance - Continue submitting payroll contributions per pay period and maintain current employee records, including updating contribution rates within 30 days of onboarding, adding new employees, and marking terminated employees. Employees can opt out at any time and have complete control over their savings amounts.

structured_extraction.program_description: A mental health and substance use disorder screening and referral program that provides assessment and linkages for low-income uninsured persons of all ages living in Montgomery County who need services for major mental health and/or substance abuse problems. The program offers in-person or telephone clinical assessment, financial screening, referral for public services, consultation to agencies and programs, and information about mental health services in the county.

Clinical assessment and financial screening to connect clients with public services. Consultation services available to agencies and programs. Bridges Transitional Psychiatry provides counseling and psychiatry services for uninsured clients transitioning to community services. Access staff assist with obtaining additional social service resources. Fees are charged on a sliding scale based on income using the Maryland Department of Health sliding fee schedule. The program accepts Maryland Medicaid and Medicare with client responsibility for co-payments. Clients will not be denied services based on ability to pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income uninsured persons of all ages living in Montgomery County who have no commercial insurance and need services for major mental health and/or substance abuse problems. Individuals must be Montgomery County residents age 18 or older and uninsured with no or low income, or have Medicaid or Medicare insurance. Telephone consultation and information and referral services are available for all residents and professionals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Behavioral health assessment, clinical evaluation, referral to appropriate services, psychiatry and counseling services, and social service resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only for in-person assessment and referral services. Telephone consultation and information services available to all residents and professionals.

Age 18 or older for in-person assessment and referral services
Must be uninsured with no or low income, or have Medicaid or Medicare insurance
Must provide identification and proof of residency for in-person services
Must provide proof of insurance and/or income information if applicable
For fee reduction eligibility, must provide verification of income through pay stubs, bank statements, tax returns, or letters of support from family members or shelters

It is recommended that individuals seeking behavioral health assessments arrive at 8:30 a.m. or 12:30 p.m. Apply in person at 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 101, Rockville, MD 20850. Bring identification, proof of residency, and proof of insurance and/or income if applicable.

structured_extraction.program_description: A residential care program for Maryland residents age 18 and older who cannot live independently due to mental, physical, or developmental disabilities. The program provides supervised housing and placements in certified residential environments where providers care for up to four clients in their home, and in small assisted living facilities in the community. Case management is provided without regard to income or assets, and placements are subsidized based on eligibility. A resident's contribution to the cost of care is based on the individual's income, and each resident is allowed to keep a small personal allowance each month ranging between $60-$139, depending on income and subsidy source.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Placements are subsidized for eligible applicants. A resident's contribution to the cost of care is based on the individual's income. Case management is provided without regard to income or assets. Each resident is allowed to keep a small personal allowance each month ranging between $60-$139, depending on the amount of income and subsidy source.

For Certified Residential Environments, applicants must be Maryland residents. For Assisted Living, applicants must be residents of Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County financing program that provides short-term and subordinate acquisition loans to developers, non-profits, tenant associations, and other entities to acquire properties at risk of losing affordability and develop, preserve, or convert affordable multifamily rental housing and limited-equity cooperatives. The program helps developers bid competitively to maintain affordability and enable current renters to remain in their community at affordable rents. The fund has a dedicated pool of $14 million in revolving County funds matched at least 3 to 1 with private lending, with expected total deployment of $20 million for affordable housing acquisitions in Montgomery County. Loans have advantageous terms, standardized processing, and pricing, with a typical three-year term requiring refinancing plans to ensure long-term affordability. The program is deployed in partnership with community development financial institutions and other lenders.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term and subordinate acquisition loan financing to acquire, develop, preserve, and convert affordable multifamily rental housing units and limited-equity cooperatives. The AHOF provides loans from a dedicated pool of $14 million in Montgomery County revolving funds, matched at least 3:1 with private lending, with expected total deployment of $20 million. The program offers three-year short-term loans with advantageous terms, standardized processing, and pricing to help developers acquire properties quickly. Developers must include plans for refinancing that will ensure long-term affordability and repay the AHOF funding. The program is deployed in partnership with community development financial institutions and other lenders. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as initial loans are repaid and the fund is replenished.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquire, develop, preserve, and convert affordable multifamily rental housing units and limited-equity cooperatives. Funds must be refinanced for long-term affordability and repayment of the AHOF loan.

Applications reviewed on rolling basis as loans are repaid and fund is replenished
Must be an affordable housing developer
Must seek to acquire properties to preserve affordability
Must provide plans for long-term refinancing ensuring affordability
Must plan to repay AHOF funding through refinancing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Find Term Sheet, FAQ, and application process information at the National Housing Trust Community Development Fund (NHTCDF) webpage. 2. Contact NHTCDF for additional information if needed. 3. Submit application to NHTCDF coordinated by the National Housing Trust Community Development Fund. 4. Application reviewed by DHCA's partner underwriter. 5. DHCA Director reviews recommendation and determines approval. 6. DHCA approval evidenced by conditional commitment letter detailing terms and conditions. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as initial loans are repaid and the fund is replenished.

structured_extraction.program_description: The ACRE Program provides matching grant cost-share assistance to farmers and agricultural entrepreneurs for agricultural business projects that improve, expand, and increase the profitability of the agricultural enterprise. MARBIDCO and the Office of Agriculture (OAG) contribute up to half of the total project cost, with MARBIDCO matching up to $3,000 per project and ACRE matching up to $3,000 per project, not to exceed $6,000 total. An additional $1,000 is available for projects totaling more than $20,000. Eligible projects include deer fence, agricultural well, vertical racks for microgreens, farm equipment and tools, hydroponics equipment, aquaponics equipment, and refrigeration. Farmers and agricultural entrepreneurs are responsible for paying at least half of the total project cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides matching cost-share grant assistance (reimbursement) for agricultural infrastructure projects. MARBIDCO matches up to $3,000 per project and ACRE matches up to $3,000 per project, for a total match of up to $6,000. An additional $1,000 is available for projects totaling more than $20,000. The applicant must invest at least half of the total project cost. The maximum lifetime amount allowed per farm, farmer, or agricultural operation is $15,000. Up to 2 applications per fiscal year are permitted for different projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County-based agricultural entrepreneurs and agricultural businesses registered with the State of Maryland, including table crop farmers, vineyards, commodity farmers, vertical farmers, horticulture businesses, and other non-traditional types of agriculture. Supports both new and existing agricultural enterprises.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure projects and equipment purchases that enable revenue and/or employment growth and improve or expand agricultural enterprises, including deer fence, agricultural well, vertical racks for microgreens, farm equipment and tools, hydroponics equipment, aquaponics equipment, and refrigeration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Agricultural enterprise must be headquartered in Montgomery County, Maryland, and the project must be located in Montgomery County.

Must be headquartered in Montgomery County

The applicant must apply to and receive approval from the Office of Agriculture before making any purchases or beginning any phase of the project for project expenses to be eligible for cost share
Lifetime maximum of $15,000 per farm, farmer, or agricultural operation (MARBIDCO funding)
Up to 2 applications per fiscal year permitted for different projects
Sole proprietors must provide Schedule F (Form 1040) as proof of legitimate agricultural business
Project must enhance agricultural economy or enable revenue/employment growth
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Office of Agriculture and receive approval before making any purchases or beginning any phase of the project. Apply through MARBIDCO's online portal.

Easement values are determined using an Agricultural Value Formula based on farm size, soil quality, road frontage, land tenure, and proximity to the edge of an agricultural zone. Applications typically are processed in 6 to 12 months.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The funds are paid to the landowner in exchange for placing an easement on the property that permanently restricts development.

Minimum property size of 50 acres, or 10 acres or more of cropland adjacent to other protected land
One Transferable Development Right (TDR) for every 25 acres of land must be retained with the property prior to easement application to be eligible for maximum easement value
At least 50 percent of the land must meet USDA Soil Classification Standards I-III or Woodland Classifications 1 and 2
The land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts and Entertainment District Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This tax credit is available to taxpayers for manufacturing, commercial, or industrial buildings located in Arts and Entertainment Districts that are wholly or partially renovated for use by a qualifying resident artist or arts and entertainment enterprise. The credit provides property tax relief for 10 years if the building continues to be used by a qualifying resident artist or arts and entertainment enterprise. The real property tax credit is based on growth in property assessments compared to a base year assessment. The base year assessment is the real property assessment for the year before any renovation is done. The credit is based on the increase in assessment for each of the next 10 years compared to the base year assessment. The credit is given on the actual taxes resulting from the assessment increase. For properties not allowed an Enterprise Zone Tax Credit: Years 1-5: 80% of assessment increase; Year 6: 70%; Year 7: 60%; Year 8: 50%; Year 9: 40%; Year 10: 30% (expires thereafter). For properties allowed an Enterprise Zone Tax Credit, the Arts and Entertainment Tax Credit is 20% as calculated above, added to the Enterprise Zone Credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A care coordination program that helps at-risk pregnant women connect with resources and stay healthy through their pregnancies. The program provides prenatal education, screening for depression and substance abuse, screening for intimate partner violence and environmental safety, and ensures participants attend prenatal care appointments and follow provider advice.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides care coordination services and prenatal education at no cost. Participants may receive tangible support including a portable crib (Pack n' Play), diapers, transportation to prenatal appointments, car seats, and other incentives for newborns as needed based on participant circumstances.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services and support for pregnant women including prenatal care coordination, education on preterm labor prevention, nutrition, breastfeeding, safe sleep for newborns, family planning, harmful effects of smoking and substance abuse, intimate partner violence prevention, and tangible support such as portable cribs, diapers, transportation to appointments, and car seats.

requirements_list: Participant must be Black/African American
Participant must be a Maryland Medicaid recipient
Participant must live in the Downcounty region of Montgomery County (zip codes 20903, 20904, or 20906)
Participant must be pregnant or at-risk for pregnancy complications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-3118 to apply. Self-referrals are encouraged. Referrals are also accepted from doctors, nurses, social service providers, and other community members. Participants should bring a Maryland Medicaid insurance card if available.

Grants are prorated based on the amount appropriated for the program and the portion of an investor's state tax credits compared to the total state tax credits received by all investors of County biotechnology businesses.

Grants are prorated based on the amount appropriated for the program and the portion of an investor's state tax credits compared to the total state tax credits received by all investors of County biotechnology businesses.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that purchases easements to permanently retire approved on-site waste disposal systems and eliminate development potential on lots in the Agricultural Reserve. BLTs may also be sold directly to developers for use in designated receiving areas to increase density.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases BLT easements that permanently retire an approved on-site waste disposal system and eliminate development potential on the lot. The price paid for BLT easements is higher than that of TDRs because the development potential has already been proven. BLTs may also be sold directly to developers in designated receiving areas (Life Science, Transit Mixed-Use, and Commercial/Residential zones).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in the Agricultural Reserve with lots that have approved on-site waste disposal systems who want to preserve their land and eliminate development potential.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: County-purchased BLT easements provide payment to the landowner in exchange for permanently retiring the septic system and eliminating development rights. Private BLT transactions generate funds for landowners from developers purchasing BLTs for designated receiving areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR) Zone. Receiving areas for BLT transactions include Life Science (LS), Transit Mixed-Use (TMX), and Commercial/Residential (CR) zones.
requirements_list: Land must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR) Zone
Property must be at least 50 acres in size, or smaller if contiguous to other protected lands
At least 50 percent of the land must meet USDA Soil Classification Standards I-III or Woodland Classifications 1 and 2
The land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
Land must not be encumbered by Federal/State/County agricultural or conservation easements, except BLT Easements may be eligible if protected by TDR Easements

Land must be able to achieve a percolation rate sufficient to support an individual on-site waste disposal system, as evidenced by a septic system site plan approved by the Department of Permitting Services
Any TDRs retained above the 1 TDR per 25 acres threshold must be created or severed from the land prior to or simultaneously with the BLT easement settlement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners should contact the County to discuss their property eligibility. The County Executive determines Base Value and Maximum Easement Value for the BLT Ranking Formula annually on July 1.

structured_extraction.program_name: By Right PILOT (Payment in Lieu of Taxes)
structured_extraction.program_description: An automatic tax abatement program that provides 100% abatement of County real property taxes for at least 15 years for rental properties owned or controlled by non-profits or the Housing Opportunities Commission with at least 50% of units affordable to low-income households earning 60% or less of area median income. In return for the tax exemption, property owners commit to provide affordable housing to low-income residents.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complete abatement of all County real property taxes for a term of at least 15 years for rental properties owned or controlled by non-profits or the Housing Opportunities Commission where at least 50% of units are leased to households with incomes no greater than 60% of the area median income (AMI) for the Washington Metropolitan Statistical Area. Property owners must still pay all State real property taxes, municipal taxes, front foot benefit charges, and other applicable fees unless waived. Property owners commit to maintain affordability requirements. A Regulatory Agreement is signed by the property owner and County and recorded among the land records for the term of the PILOT.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and the Housing Opportunities Commission that own or control rental housing properties seeking tax relief for affordable housing developments in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax abatement on County real property taxes for qualifying non-profit and government-controlled rental housing properties; reduces property taxes and special area taxes on qualified rental housing developments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Housing development must be owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission or a nonprofit housing developer
Rental property must be owned or controlled by a non-profit organization or the Housing Opportunities Commission
At least 50% of dwelling units must be affordable to households earning 60% or less of area median income
At least 50% of units must be leased to households with incomes no greater than 60% of the area median income (AMI) for the Washington Metropolitan Statistical Area
Legal description of the property
Project description concerning total number of units and number of affordable units with documentation of affordability (such as rent rolls or LIHTC Covenants)
Any other information or documentation reasonably required by the County to determine eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit required information electronically to DHCA.Multifamily@montgerymd.gov or by mail to Department of Housing and Community Affairs, 1401 Rockville Pike, 4th Floor, Attn: PILOT Request, Rockville, MD 20852. A Regulatory Agreement is signed by the property owner and County and recorded among the land records for the term of the PILOT. By right PILOTs may be transferable under certain conditions if the transferee meets all State and County PILOT requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County transportation program that provides subsidized taxi trips for low-income older adults and individuals with disabilities to help them travel to medical and personal appointments. The program serves Montgomery County residents through a swipe card system with participating taxi companies. Participants receive subsidies on a sliding fee scale based on household income, with additional Same Day Access (SDA) options available. The SDA component provides $60 value on swipe cards when participants pay $30 per month, with no income requirement for MetroAccess cardholders. All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with exceptions to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized taxi trips on a sliding fee scale determined by household income and eligibility status. Standard CNR Program: For single-person households earning up to $15,856 yearly, a $60 value voucher costs $5.25 monthly. For income levels up to $39,000 yearly, vouchers range from $5.25 to $30.00 monthly per $60 value. Same Day Access (SDA) Program: Eligible participants with current MetroAccess identification cards receive a $60 value on their Call-N-Ride swipe card when they pay $30 per month, regardless of income. Participants can add value to their swipe cards through the participant portal at www.eztransport.net/mococnr/members or by contacting the card services provider. Trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with exceptions to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who are low-income older adults age 65 and older, or low-income individuals ages 18-64 with a disability. MetroAccess cardholders may also qualify for Same Day Access options regardless of income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidized taxi trips to medical and personal appointments, or any approved trip within Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County. Special exceptions allow transportation to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas. Program available to all eligible Montgomery County residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident
Must be low-income and at least 65 years of age, OR low-income and 18-64 years of age with a disability
Household income documentation is required to determine subsidy level
Must have current MetroAccess identification card (for Same Day Access component)
A completed CNR Application Form with supporting documentation is required to verify eligibility
If age 18-64, CNR Disability Certification Form required
A completed SDA Application Form with supporting documentation is required to verify eligibility (for MetroAccess participants)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, contact Call-N-Ride at 301-948-5409 or email cnrorder@montgomerycountymd.gov. Customer service hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Complete the CNR Application Form and if age 18-64, the CNR Disability Certification Form, along with supporting documentation to verify eligibility and income. Submit by fax to 240-556-0999, by email to cnrorder@montgomerycountymd.gov, or by mail/hand delivery to Call-n-Ride Program, 101 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. Once approved, participants can add value to their Call-N-Ride swipe card through the participant portal at www.eztransport.net/mococnr/members or by calling the card services provider, and schedule trips.

structured_extraction.program_description: Commercial PACE is an innovative financing program administered by the Montgomery County Green Bank that allows commercial property owners in Montgomery County to finance building improvements through low-cost, long-term flexible financing from private lenders. Qualified commercial properties can receive financing for up to 100 percent of eligible property improvements, including energy efficiency, renewable energy, climate resiliency, climate adaptation, water conservation, and environmental health and safety upgrades. The financing is repaid as annual surcharges on the property tax bill for up to 20 years. The loan remains with the property if ownership changes, and subsequent owners continue paying the surcharge until the loan is paid off. Eligible projects include new construction, existing buildings with planned renovations, and buildings with completed renovations from the last 12 months.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides direct funding to nonprofit food assistance and food recovery organizations to strengthen their capacity to recover, handle, and redistribute surplus food and expand access to nutritious foods for Montgomery County residents. The program distributes grants to food assistance provider organizations that deliver regularly scheduled, no-cost food services, supporting the purchase and distribution of shelf-stable food, fresh food, and prepared meals to residents experiencing food insecurity. FY26 funding includes $290,785 in renewable CFA funding and $1.9M in expanded grants distributed to 53 nonprofit providers. Awards prioritize underserved communities, home delivery models, services to immigrant and unhoused residents, food recovery operations, high-performing returning grantees, and under-resourced ZIP codes. Partners are collectively expected to recover and redistribute more than 10 million pounds of food annually while closing service gaps, enhancing program impact, standardizing data collection, and strengthening the local food system. Applications are processed through a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) process.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards direct cash grants totaling approximately $2.1M (including $290,785 in renewable FY26 CFA funding and $1.9M in expanded appropriations) to nonprofit food assistance and recovery organizations serving Montgomery County. Award amounts range from $20,000 to $100,001+. Grants support flexible food sourcing from wholesale or retail outlets, or provide credits to order produce, shelf-stable products, and nutritious food items through bulk-food purchasing partnerships with Manna Food Center and the Capital Area Food Bank. Direct operational funding supports food recovery operations, emergency food distribution, home delivery services, food purchase and distribution, staffing for recovery operations, equipment for food recovery, and food-insecure resident support. Awards strengthen partner capacity to recover, handle, and redistribute surplus food with recipients collectively expected to recover and redistribute more than 10 million pounds of food annually. Priority given to under-resourced ZIP codes, home delivery models, services to immigrant and unhoused residents, food recovery operations, and high-performing returning grantees. Food distribution methods include Family Market, Choice Pantry, Pre-Packaged Boxes/Bags, and Prepared Meals. Grants provided through a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) process.

Households receiving food assistance and underserved community members needing food support.

Community food assistance programs and services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Limits the amount of assessment increase on which eligible homeowners pay county, municipal, and state property taxes each year. May significantly reduce the amount of property taxes owed. Eligibility stays in place as long as the dwelling remains the primary residence. The credit applies to the portion of reassessment that exceeds the limit from one year to the next. Homeowners pay no property tax on assessment increases above the limit. The credit does not apply in the first year following the purchase of a home. The credit is administered by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and limits annual growth to a rate set annually by county resolution.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit that limits assessment increases and reduces annual property tax liability. The credit limits taxable assessment increases to 10% per year (or 5% in the Town of Kensington). The homeowner pays no property tax on the portion of the reassessment that exceeds this percentage limit. The credit is applied against the tax due based on the assessment increase. The credit does not apply in the first year following the purchase of a home. Property owners must file an application with SDAT to receive this credit. Montgomery County uses a 10% homestead credit, meaning any annual assessment growth in excess of 10% becomes a credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 1, 2026 to ensure the County Income Tax Offset Credit appears on future bills (bills beginning July 1, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual homeowners who plan to live in a property as their principal residence.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. All municipalities in Montgomery County have adopted the 10% homestead tax credit limit, except for the Town of Kensington, which has a 5% limit.

Property address must match voter registration (if registered)
No portion of principal residence may be rented
Married couples may only have one principal residence
