Application information must be consistent with state income tax and motor vehicle records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check if you already have a homestead application on file by visiting the SDAT Real Property Search page, selecting Montgomery County, finding your property, and checking the Homestead Application Status row. Step 2: If your status says 'No application,' obtain your Real Property Account Number (from an SDAT letter or the SDAT website). Step 3: Choose one filing method - complete the online form at the Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application page on the SDAT website, or download and print the paper application and mail it to the address listed on the application. You can also apply online at Maryland OneStop or use a paper application available from SDAT. You only need to apply once; subsequent years are automatic if approved. This program is also administered automatically by SDAT for qualifying owner-occupied properties.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps households with incomes up to 120% of the area's average income afford homes in Montgomery County. It provides homeownership opportunities for public workers and other employees who cannot afford the high cost of housing near their workplaces, and helps reduce commute times for county employees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides homeownership opportunities for qualified households. Income limits are based on household size and area median income (up to 120% AMI). For a household of 1, the maximum income is $137,500; for 2, $157,500; for 3, $177,000; for 4, $196,500; for 5, $212,500; and for 6, $228,000. Homes are subject to a 20-year control period during which owners must occupy the home as their primary residence, cannot rent it out, and can only sell to other qualifying WFH program participants at a DHCA-set resale price. After the control period ends, if the home is sold, the owner must return half of any profit above the resale price to the County's Housing Initiative Fund.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit and tax incentive program offered by Montgomery County that provides three tiers of tax credits to make homes more universally accessible and encourage development of housing that accommodates a wider range of accessibility needs. The program offers property tax incentives to homeowners, builders, home care facility owners, and developers who make modifications to enhance home accessibility and design in compliance with Design for Life accessibility and aging-in-place standards. This voluntary certification program for Visit-Ability (Level I) and Live-Ability (Level II) applies to single-family attached and detached homes, townhouses, duplexes, and condominium units, with guidelines applicable to both new construction and renovation. Tier 1 offers tax credits for individual permanently installed accessibility features that improve access to or within a principal residence, up to $2,500 per property owner per tax year. Tier 2 provides Level I (VISITable) tax credits for permanent installations to new or existing single-family homes, townhomes, and duplexes meeting Level I accessibility standards, up to $3,000 per property owner per tax year. Tier 3 provides Level II (LIVEable) tax credits for permanent installations meeting Level II accessibility standards, up to $10,000 per property owner per tax year. The maximum amount of property tax credit that may be applied in any single tax year is $2,000, with excess credit carrying forward to future years. A school impact tax credit may also be available for new home construction projects meeting Level I and Level II standards. The program rewards property owners who install accessibility features in residential homes, helping County residents remain in their homes as physical needs change, while increasing property value and offering streamlined permitting for building professionals. Property owners can receive development impact tax credits for new residential developments meeting accessibility standards, and the program fast-tracks permits for qualifying properties. The tax credit is applied as a line item on the property owner's Montgomery County property tax bill and runs with the property upon transfer of title.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners of new or existing single-family homes, townhouses, duplexes, or condominium units can receive tax credits for accessibility improvements. The program provides three tiers of tax credits: Tier 1 — Accessible Feature tax credits for certain permanently installed features that improve access to or within a principal residence, up to $2,500 per property owner per tax year (lesser of 50% of eligible costs or $2,500). Tier 2 — Level I (VISITable) features, with tax credit up to $3,000 per property owner per tax year. Tier 3 — Level II (LIVEable) features, with tax credit up to $10,000 per property owner per tax year. The maximum amount of property tax credit that may be applied in any single tax year is $2,000. The tax credit allowed is the lesser of the eligible cost or the stated tier maximum, less any Development Impact Tax for School Improvements credit received and less any other funds or assistance received. If the credit exceeds the county property tax for a given year, the excess carries forward to future years. The credit runs with the property upon transfer of title. School Impact Tax Credit is available for Level I and Level II homes based on project percentages (5% to 30% of single family houses): $500 to $2,000 per Level I house. For new residential developments meeting Level I accessibility standards, developers can receive development impact tax credits ranging from $500 to $2,000 per residence depending on the percentage of units meeting Level I standards (5%, 10%, 20%, or 30%). Eligible costs must be incurred within 12 months prior to application and must exceed $500. Eligible improvements include no-step entrances, accessible routes, accessible bathrooms, accessible kitchens, accessible bedrooms, interior doorways with appropriate clear widths, ramps, elevators, lifts, stair glides, exterior lighting, sensory impairment accommodations, grab bar reinforcement, lever door handles, chair lifts, chair height toilets, and relocation of switches and electrical receptacles. The tax credit is applied as a line item on the property owner's Montgomery County property tax bill. Property owners receive tax credits that apply to their property taxes, with any balance carrying over to following years.

Property owners of residential dwellings (single-family homes, townhomes, duplexes, and condominium units) in Montgomery County who install accessibility features or build new homes meeting accessibility standards, where the property is the owner's principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs for purchasing and installing permanent accessibility features or meeting Level I or Level II accessibility standards in residential properties, including reasonable installation costs and required permit or inspection fees. Eligible improvements include no-step entrances, accessible routes, accessible bathrooms, accessible kitchens, accessible bedrooms, interior doorways with appropriate clear widths, ramps, elevators, lifts, stair glides, exterior lighting, sensory impairment accommodations, grab bar reinforcement, lever door handles, chair lifts, chair height toilets, and relocation of switches and electrical receptacles. Eligible costs must be incurred within 12 months prior to application and must exceed $500. The tax credit provides property tax reduction through credits for home and facility modifications that enhance accessibility and create aging-in-place environments, increase property value, create universally welcoming environments for all mobility needs, and development impact tax for school improvement.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Two-part process: First, obtain a building permit before work starts by applying for a residential or commercial building permit and checking the DFL application box (for online applications through eServices) or submitting a Building Permit Supplemental Design for Life Application (for paper applications) with architectural and/or engineering plans documenting the DFL renovations. Applications can be submitted online through eServices or in person at the Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services, 2425 Reedie Drive, 7th Floor, Wheaton, MD. Second, after all work is completed and final inspection is approved, submit a separate application for the property tax credit. Tax credit applications cannot be done online and must be submitted in person or by mail with required documentation including a copy of the building permit, cost documentation (receipts/invoices), copies of applications for other subsidies, and an affidavit confirming no previous owner or applicant received other subsidies for modifications. Optionally, submit School Impact Tax Credit Certification Agreement if applying for school impact tax credit. Department of Finance reviews documents, assesses the tax credit amount, and notifies the applicant. The tax credit appears as a line item on the next property tax bill. Homeowners and building professionals can explore resources through the program's dedicated pages for homeowners and building professionals. After the building permit is issued and work is completed, it must be certified by the Department of Permitting Services.

The State provides a separate tax credit at 31.5% for each of 24 years, applied against corporate or personal income taxes, financial institutions franchise tax, or insurance premiums tax. structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-year real property tax credit designed to spur economic growth in designated Enterprise Zone areas in Montgomery County. The credit is based on increases in real property assessments for nonresidential properties and provides tax relief on both local real property taxes and State income taxes for qualifying businesses and employees. The program is available in downtown Silver Spring, Takoma Park/Long Branch, Wheaton, and Gaithersburg Olde Towne Enterprise Zones. Additionally, the State provides an income tax credit for employees working at least 25 hours per week and spending at least 50% of work time in the Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credit based on increase in real property assessment compared to base-year assessment (the year before construction or refurbishing). Credit rates for property tax: Years 1-5: tax on 80% of assessment increase. Year 6: 70%. Year 7: 60%. Year 8: 50%. Year 9: 40%. Year 10: 30%, then expires. Additionally, the State provides an income tax credit for each employee working at least 25 hours per week and spending at least 50% of work time in the Enterprise Zone. For economically disadvantaged employees: $3,000 year 1, $2,000 year 2, $1,000 year 3. For other employees: $1,000 one-time credit.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY25 Food Recovery Network Infrastructure Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funding collaborative food recovery organizations to build capacity within the food recovery network, establish new donor relationships, increase access to higher-value food products, reduce climate impacts of food recovery operations, and leverage external resources. The program strengthens the local Food Recovery Network's capacity to transport, store, and distribute recovered food to address food insecurity through infrastructure improvements and operational support, including the purchase of refrigerated vehicles, refrigeration equipment, shelving, pallet jacks, and shared cold storage units to expand transportation and cold storage capacity. Funding supports projects reflecting collaborative, shared-use approaches that divert food from the waste stream and distribute to residents in need through food recovery runs and redistribution partnerships.

Funding supports capital and durable goods purchases including refrigerated vehicles, refrigeration equipment, shelving, pallet jacks, and shared cold storage units to enhance food recovery and distribution capacity. Grants may also support staff costs for food distribution activities, indirect and administrative costs, and operational costs such as fuel, vehicle maintenance, packing materials, training, and food-safety supplies. Funding supports collaborative, shared-use approaches that build network capacity, establish new donor relationships, increase access to fresh and limited availability food products, and reduce climate impacts of food recovery operations.

structured_extraction.program_description: FareShare is a Montgomery County commuter benefits program that matches employer contributions to help pay for employee transit and vanpool commuting costs. The county reimburses employers for transit subsidies they provide to employees, encouraging the use of public transportation and vanpooling to reduce traffic congestion and support transportation goals. The county reimburses employers up to a maximum of $325 per employee per month for transit and vanpool commuting costs. Employers can receive a Maryland state tax credit for their participation, and employees receive enhanced transit and vanpool benefits at a lower cost. Employees receive tax-free transit subsidies to help pay commuting costs, with tax-free subsidies beginning January 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county reimburses employers for any transit subsidy amount provided over a minimum $25 contribution, up to the full $325 per month permitted by federal tax law. Maximum reimbursement available is $40,000 in one year to any single employer. Employers are also eligible for a Maryland state tax credit of 50 percent of their contribution, up to a maximum of $100 per employee per month, available to both for-profit and non-profit organizations. Employees receive tax-free transit subsidies beginning January 1, 2025. Employers can offer benefits as tax-free subsidies or pre-tax payroll deductions.

Funds can be used to contribute to employee transit and vanpool commuting costs through tax-free subsidies or pre-tax payroll deductions. Employers can offer up to $325 per month per employee as a tax-free benefit or pre-tax payroll deduction, with the county reimbursing amounts over the $25 minimum contribution.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Community Development Block Grant Program (CDBG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program administered by Montgomery County that provides funding to develop viable communities by supporting community development activities that provide decent housing and suitable living environments and expand economic opportunities, principally for low and moderate income persons. The program serves multiple purposes: (1) funding to 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations for public service activities that benefit low- and moderate-income residents, including eviction prevention, employment, youth development, education, welfare, housing-related supportive services, crime prevention, health care, mental health, and recreation; (2) funding for affordable housing acquisition and preservation, including rehabilitation of housing units to serve low-income households; and (3) neighborhood revitalization, economic development, and improved community facilities and services. Construction projects for public services are not eligible, though rehabilitation of housing units is supported.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County received approximately five million dollars in CDBG funds in fiscal year 2026 (July 2025 - June 2026). Federal Community Development Block Grant funds are awarded for multiple categories of activities: (1) Grants to eligible non-profit organizations to support public service activities benefiting low- and moderate-income Montgomery County residents, with grant amounts varying based on organization and project selection through a competitive review process; (2) Grants for affordable housing acquisition and preservation, including rehabilitation of housing units; and (3) neighborhood revitalization and economic development activities. At least 51% of units assisted in any housing project must be income-certified at or below 80% AMI at occupancy or financing. Federal Davis Bacon wage rates apply for all rehabilitation work if more than eight units are included. The program does not fund construction projects for public services. The City of Takoma Park received $91,000 and The City of Rockville received $263,000 in FY26 for CDBG funded projects within their jurisdictions.

Construction projects for public services are not eligible.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process begins in August when the cycle opens. Applicants submit the CDBG Application form with required documentation by mid-September. DHCA staff screens applications for eligibility and sends an email receipt within one week. Eligible applications are reviewed by the Community Development Advisory Committee (CDAC) in October-November. The CDAC makes funding recommendations in December. The County Executive submits recommendations to the County Council, which makes final funding selections and approves the budget in late May. Application is available as a fillable PDF form.

Rental units must serve households at or below 60% AMI (Area Median Income), with at least 20% at or below 50% AMI for projects with more than five units. Homeownership assistance available for households up to 80% AMI. Funds are monitored for up to 20 years. Annual maximum subsidy per unit applies. Federal Davis Bacon wage rates apply at 12 or more units. In fiscal year 2026 (July 2025 - June 2026), Montgomery County received approximately 2 million dollars in HOME funds. Developers submit applications based on project size. Small project applications include an application form, loan request summary form, optional financial forms, cost estimates, and tenant housing reports. Large project applications include MD DHCD application documents, cover sheet, loan request summary form, and instructions.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, rehabilitation, new construction, tenant-based rental assistance, and construction of affordable rental and homeownership units; acquiring, constructing, and rehabilitating multifamily affordable housing developments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: 90% of rental units must be at or below 60% AMI
20% of units must be at or below 50% AMI if more than five units are involved
Homeownership projects assist persons earning up to 80% AMI
Funds must be proportional to the number of HOME units in a project
Federal Davis Bacon wage rates apply at 12 or more units
Subsidy layering review required if other federal funds are in the project
Code enforcement requirements must be met for the entirety of the monitoring period
Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act guidelines must be followed if residents are displaced
Units monitored for up to 20 years
Annual maximum subsidy per unit
Projects must comply with HOME program affordability requirements
Annual tenant certification required to ensure assisted units are occupied by income-eligible households
Property owners/managers must maintain up-to-date tenant files documenting compliance with affordability requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Non-profit and for-profit developers of housing may contact DHCA to see if their project qualifies for HOME funds. Large project applications include MD DHCD application documents, cover sheet, loan request summary form, and instructions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides zero-interest financing and cash incentives to mobile food service businesses (food trucks and trailers) licensed in Montgomery County to replace gasoline- and diesel-powered generators with clean and quiet battery power systems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified businesses can receive a 48-month loan at 7.99% annual percentage rate (APR) for up to $35,000 before purchasing eligible equipment from a participating vendor. Upon submitting proof of installation of eligible equipment, the business receives the incentive amount credited to the balance of the loan. Alternatively, the business may receive a direct cash payment of the incentive amount through the County's vendor payment system following submission of proof of installation. Incentive amounts range from $5,000 for 5-19 kilowatt-hour battery systems to $10,000 for systems with 40 or more kilowatt-hours of capacity.

Business must be registered with the State of Maryland and designated in good standing
Battery must replace a gasoline or diesel fuel generator in operations

Must purchase equipment meeting food truck's operating power requirements and minimum specifications (minimum 5 kilowatt-hours nominal energy capacity, minimum 5000 watts power output, 10 year or more warranty)
Must agree to provide photographs of installed equipment and invoices for installation
Must provide permission for Montgomery County DEP and/or Maryland Energy Administration to inspect and photograph the installed battery power system upon request
To receive financing incentives, must qualify for financing with Climate First Bank
To receive incentives as direct payments, must register as a vendor in the County Vendor Registration System
Battery power system must be installed by a Maryland licensed electrician; to receive financing incentives, electrician must be in Climate First Bank's qualified installer network
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the program application form online. Receive confirmation from the Department of Environmental Protection that you are eligible for incentives; DEP will connect you with participating vendors. Contact participating vendors to assess your power needs and receive quotes for battery power system equipment and installation. Send quotes to DEP for final approval. If financing incentive is needed, apply for your zero-interest loan with Montgomery County Green Bank partner Climate First Bank. Order and install your battery power system using a Maryland licensed electrician. Provide proof of installation to DEP and receive final incentives.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds innovative initiatives that screen pediatric patients for food insecurity and provide nutritious food and food education services. It addresses critical gaps in nutrition security and diet-related health challenges while increasing access to culturally diverse, medically relevant, nutritious, and locally produced food for children and families in underserved communities. Grants support healthcare and clinic-led Food as Medicine programs that use food as a medical intervention to address health outcomes. Funds support food provision (prioritizing Montgomery County and Washington Metropolitan/DMV region farms), staffing costs, operating costs, and indirect costs, with food-as-medicine programs providing medically tailored food assistance, nutrition education, and screening services through multiple formats including choice-style markets, pantries, and pre-packaged boxes/bags. Grantees must administer pre- and post-program surveys to evaluate outcomes including fruit and vegetable consumption, overall health, and healthcare utilization.

Assistance is provided through choice-style markets, pantry services, and pre-packaged box/bag services. Funds support food purchases (prioritizing Montgomery County and Washington Metropolitan/DMV region farms serving underserved communities), staffing costs, operating costs, indirect costs, and food-as-medicine program implementation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy, Efficient, Electrified, Climate-Adapted Pilot (HEECAP) Homes Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The HEECAP Homes Grants Program provides funding to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, repair health and safety problems in homes, support electrification to improve indoor air quality, and enhance climate resilience for low- and moderate-income households in Montgomery County. The program works through community partners to pilot strategies that address critical home repairs, remove fossil-fuel appliances, and prepare homes for state-offered efficiency and weatherization programs. Funding supports pre-weatherization repairs, electrification improvements, climate resilience enhancements, roof replacement, mold remediation, water damage repair, electrical upgrades, battery storage system pilots, and heat pump installations. The pilot began in June 2024 and continues with FY 2026 funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental assistance program providing Housing Choice Vouchers to help very low and extremely low-income households, low-income families, elderly individuals, and persons with disabilities (including nonelderly persons with disabilities ages 18-61) afford decent and safe housing in the private market. Participants use vouchers to rent private market housing (single-family homes, townhouses, apartments, or their present residence) and pay no more than 30-40% of their income as rent. The Housing Opportunities Commission pays the subsidy to the landlord directly. Vouchers are portable to any location in the United States, including territories, Guam, Puerto Rico, Alaska, Hawaii, and the Virgin Islands, providing flexibility for participants to choose their own housing.

The Housing Opportunities Commission pays the subsidy to the landlord directly. Income limit is approximately $0 to $52,750 for one person. Vouchers are portable to any location in the United States, including Guam, Puerto Rico, Alaska, Hawaii, and the Virgin Islands. Provides flexibility for participants to choose their own housing.

structured_extraction.program_description: Housing Stabilization Services provides case management and limited financial grants to support Montgomery County residents at risk of homelessness and eviction. The program helps households keep their current housing, obtain new housing, prevent utility shutoffs, and restore disconnected utility services. Emergency financial grants are available for eviction prevention, security deposits, first month's rent, utility assistance, and burial assistance. Eviction prevention grants are specifically available to eligible households that have received a court judgment for eviction or a put-out notice from their landlord.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides limited financial grants for emergency housing assistance, eviction prevention, utility assistance, security deposits, first month's rent, and burial assistance. Grants are limited to one eviction prevention grant per household within a 12-month period. Case management services are also provided to help households stabilize their housing situation. The amount of assistance is determined based on the household's specific circumstances and the total amount owed to the landlord.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents at risk of homelessness or eviction, including those facing housing instability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency financial assistance for eviction prevention, keeping current housing, obtaining new housing, preventing or restoring utility services, security deposits, first month's rent, and burial assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only. Residents of the City of Gaithersburg, City of Rockville, or City of Takoma Park may be eligible for services through those municipalities.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Household income must be at or below 60% of the area median income (AMI)
For eviction prevention: must have received a court judgment for eviction, a red and white notice from the Sheriff's Office, or a landlord-issued put-out notice
Must not have received an eviction prevention grant in the preceding 12 months
Must provide photo identification for all adults in the household
Must provide bank and financial statements from the last 30 days for all accounts
Must provide income documentation from the last 30 days for all adults in the household
Must provide proof of expenses such as utility bills, phone bills, rent, or mortgage statements
For eviction prevention cases: must provide emergency court or legal documentation and current rental ledger
For security deposit and first month's rent assistance: must provide welcome letter and lease
Meet program guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit one of the three office locations (Germantown, Rockville, or Silver Spring) to apply for services. Submit all required supporting documentation at the time of application. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with in-person sign-in available until 4:30 p.m. Contact HSS Customer Service at HSS@montgomerycountymd.gov or call 311 for more information. For housing emergencies, call 311 to be connected with Housing Stabilization Services. You may also contact the Gilchrist Immigrant Resource Center at (240) 777-4940 (Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm) for additional information about eligibility and how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Incentive Program for Electric Leaf Removal Equipment

Rebate amounts vary by applicant type: residents up to $100; revenue qualifying businesses (less than $250,000 annual revenue or 5 or fewer employees) up to $1,500 per 12-month period; non-revenue qualifying businesses (more than $250,000 annual revenue or 6 or more employees) up to $1,000 per 12-month period. Applicants must receive pre-approval from the Director before equipment purchase. One application and one rebate per 12-month period per applicant. The program is time-limited and provides partial reimbursement to eligible County residents and businesses.

Pre-approval from Director required before equipment purchase

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's program that grants county residents who own and live in their property a $692 annual tax credit on their county income tax. The credit is applied to county income tax bills for eligible homeowners and requires a one-time Homestead Property Tax Credit application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. The credit automatically applies to future years once approved.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $692 annual tax credit applied to county income tax bills for eligible homeowners. The credit appears as 'County Property Tax Credit' on tax bills. The credit is automatically applied to future years once the required Homestead Tax Credit application is filed with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. File by May 1, 2026 to ensure the credit appears on bills beginning July 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who own and live in residential property as their principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to county income tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Applicant must be a county resident living in the property they own as their principal residence.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must own the residential property
Must live in the property as primary residence
Must have Homestead Property Tax Credit application on file with SDAT by May 1, 2026
Must have Homestead Tax Credit application approved or received by Maryland SDAT
Property must be used as single principal residence
Tax return filing address must match property address
Maryland driver's license/ID address must match property (if applicable)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check if you already have a Homestead Application on file by visiting the Maryland SDAT Real Property search at https://sdat.dat.maryland.gov/RealProperty/, selecting Montgomery County, and searching for your property to view your Homestead Application Status. Step 2 (if needed): If your status shows 'No Application', obtain your Real Property Account Number and apply online through Maryland OneStop or by mail through the Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application at https://dat.maryland.gov/realproperty/Pages/Maryland-Homestead-Tax-Credit.aspx. Filing online is faster than mailing. You only need to apply once; the credit automatically applies to future years once approved. The application must be on file by May 1, 2026 to ensure the credit appears on bills beginning July 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant at Risk Home Visiting Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A case management program that serves mothers and newborns with medical or social problems that could affect their health, development, or well-being. Public health nurses provide home visits to support families identified through hospital referrals. The program facilitates coordination of home visiting and case management services statewide through the Maryland Postpartum Infant and Maternal Referral Form. Healthcare providers complete a referral form identifying risk factors and submit it via facsimile, encrypted email, or secure means to the local health department Maternal-Child Health Program. The program identifies maternal medical risks, psychosocial risks, pregnancy-related risks, and infant risks, and facilitates referrals for WIC, immunizations, mental health, substance use, smoking cessation, breastfeeding support, safe sleep/crib, infant/maternal medical follow-up, family planning, and intimate partner violence services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Public health nurses provide home visits and case management services to mothers and newborns. Healthcare providers complete a referral form identifying risk factors and submit it via facsimile, encrypted email, or secure means to the local health department Maternal-Child Health Program. The program identifies maternal medical risks, psychosocial risks, pregnancy-related risks, and infant risks, and facilitates referrals for WIC, immunizations, mental health services, substance use treatment, smoking cessation, breastfeeding support, safe sleep education, infant/maternal medical follow-up, family planning, and intimate partner violence services. There are no fees or payments required for this service.

HIPAA authorization not required for referral submission
Completion by healthcare providers at birth hospital or maternal care setting
Identification of at-risk status based on maternal medical risks, psychosocial risks, pregnancy-related risks, or infant risks
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Healthcare providers at the birth hospital or maternal care setting complete the Maryland Postpartum Infant and Maternal Referral Form identifying maternal medical risks, psychosocial risks, pregnancy-related risks, and infant risks. The referral form is submitted via facsimile, encrypted email, or secure means to the local health department Maternal-Child Health Program. For Montgomery County referrals, the form is typically faxed to either the Silver Spring Health Center (240-777-3054) or Germantown Health Center (240-777-4648). structured_extraction.program_name: Live Healthy – Health, Dental and Prescription Discounts
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive discount program that Montgomery County offers to provide residents with savings on health, dental, prescription, and vision services. The program includes a free prescription discount card (Montgomery RX) providing average 24% savings on retail prescription prices at 68,000+ pharmacies nationwide, low-fee dental discounts (15-50% savings) at over 110,000 participating dental professionals nationwide, and low-fee health discounts (15-75% savings) for vision services, hearing aids with complimentary screenings, diabetes supplies, prepaid lab work, and screenings. Services covered include prescriptions (brand name and generic), dental care (check-ups, cleanings, fillings, crowns, x-rays, root canals), vision services (eyeglasses, exams, lenses, contact lenses, and laser vision correction), hearing aids, and diabetes supplies. This is NOT insurance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Montgomery RX prescription discount program is free with no annual fees and provides average 24% off prescription medicine at 68,000+ retail pharmacies nationwide. Users present the card at pharmacies to receive automatic discounts on brand name and generic prescription drugs with no claim forms. The Health Discount program costs $6.95 per month or $69 per year for individuals ($8.95 per month or $79 per year for families) and provides 15-75% discounts on vision services (35% off eyeglass frames and lenses, 15% off Lasik and PRK), hearing aids with complimentary screenings (35% off), diabetes supplies, prepaid lab work, and screenings. The Dental Discount program costs $6.95 per month or $69 per year for individuals ($8.95 per month or $79 per year for families) and provides 15% to 50% off dental procedures with no deductibles or benefit maximums at over 110,000 participating dental professionals nationwide.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MC Groceries Program provides monthly benefits to eligible Montgomery County families with children under 18 who are not eligible for SNAP benefits to access fresh and shelf-stable food items through online shopping with Instacart Fresh Funds. Eligible households receive $100 in monthly benefits per eligible child under 18 years old, up to $400 per month maximum, with items available for delivery or pickup at participating retailers. Benefits are automatically loaded on participants' accounts on the 15th of each month and can be used to purchase eligible fresh produce, frozen items, seafood, dairy, eggs, meat, meat alternatives, bakery, deli, pantry staples, non-alcoholic beverages, driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees. Up to 700 families will be served. Program benefits are expected to be available from July 15, 2025, to July 15, 2026. Created through partnership between Montgomery County's Office of Food Systems Resilience (OFSR) and Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS).

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive $100 in monthly Fresh Funds credits (category-specific online grocery stipends) for each child under 18 years old, up to a maximum of $400 per month per household. Funds are automatically loaded on the participant's Instacart Fresh Funds account on the 15th of each month (or next business day) and can be used to purchase eligible fresh and shelf-stable food items from participating Instacart retailers for delivery or pickup. Fresh Funds credits can be used for fresh and frozen produce, seafood, dairy, eggs, meat, meat alternatives, bakery, deli, pantry staples, non-alcoholic beverages, driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees. Up to 700 families are eligible to participate.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program benefits are expected to be available from July 15, 2025, to July 15, 2026. Applications accepted on rolling/first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 301-818-3614 or 240-777-4141; Instacart Support: 1-888-246-7822; Senior Support Line: 1-844-981-3433 (8 a.m. to 11 p.m. ET daily)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County families with eligible children under 18 who are not receiving SNAP benefits and meet income requirements. Households must have at least one child under age 18 who is not eligible for SNAP benefits and have post-tax incomes below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level (approximately $124,000 per year for a family of 4). Seniors and families seeking grocery delivery assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of eligible fresh and shelf-stable food items available through Instacart Fresh Funds, including fresh produce, frozen produce, seafood, dairy, eggs, meat, meat alternatives, bakery items, deli items, pantry staples, and other grocery items marked with the Fresh Funds icon. Non-alcoholic beverages, driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees also covered. Items must be purchased through the Instacart Fresh Funds online platform for family food needs and delivered to registered address.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Households must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland throughout the program. Instacart service available to over 95% of households in U.S. and Canada; service available in all 50 U.S. states and Canada with over 14,000 cities covered.
requirements_list: Reside in Montgomery County throughout the program
Have at least one child under 18 who is not eligible for SNAP benefits
Have post-tax household income below 400% of Federal Poverty Level (approximately $124,000 per year for a family of 4)
Upload proof of income (pay stubs from last 30 days, employment letter, or similar documentation)
Upload valid photo identity for parent or guardian (driver's license, Maryland ID, or passport)
Upload proof of address (apartment lease, landlord letter, driver's license, or utility bill)
Upload government-issued proof of identity for all participating children (birth certificate or school documents)
Have access to backup electronic payment method such as debit card, credit card, Google Pay, Apple Pay, PayPal, or Klarna
Able to navigate English-language platform
Willing to participate in mid-year check-in and pre- and post-program surveys
Up to 700 families eligible
Orders must be placed, delivered, and/or picked up within same benefit period (monthly)
One Instacart account per person or household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a Nutrition Benefits Navigator for eligibility pre-screening via phone (301-818-3614 or 240-777-4141) or email (SNAP@mocofoodcouncil.org). If criteria are met, the Navigator assists with completing an online waitlist form. As openings become available, waitlist entries are notified in the order received and asked to complete a full application with required documentation including proof of income, identity, address, and child identity. Once enrolled, households receive instructions to create an Instacart Fresh Funds account with email, Google, or Facebook authentication. The head of household receives a unique code to redeem through their Instacart Fresh Funds account to access total monthly benefits available to their household. Benefits are automatically loaded on the 15th of each month or the next business day. Program enrollment is first-come, first-served based on completed applications. For seniors (age 60+), call Senior Support Line at 1-844-981-3433 (8 a.m. to 11 p.m. ET daily) for dedicated assistance with account setup and order placement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medicaid/Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program and Senior Dental
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive dental services and coverage for Montgomery County residents, including services for adults over age 21 with full Medicaid coverage, pregnant women who meet income and residency requirements, and seniors age 60 and above with low income. Services include exams, cleanings, fluoride treatments, fillings, extractions, root canals, crowns, and dentures. Eligibility for pregnant women is based on being a Montgomery County resident, U.S. citizen or non-citizen without immigration-based Medicaid eligibility, currently pregnant with application submitted before delivery, and income up to 250% of the federal poverty level. Senior dental services are available to seniors with income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level. The program provides no fees or costs associated with senior dental services, with eligibility confirmed by the Office of Eligibility and Support Services.

For seniors age 60 and above, dental care services are provided to eligible low-income individuals. Applications for senior dental services are available online through the Community Connect Portal starting January 1, 2025. Eligibility for seniors is confirmed by the Office of Eligibility and Support Services.

The program is available for ambulatory, wheelchair, and stretcher-bound transportation. Transportation can be scheduled up to seven days in advance, with next-day service guaranteed if requested by noon the working day before. The program does not provide emergency or same-day service except for hospital discharges. All costs are covered for covered medical services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive medication-assisted treatment program for Montgomery County residents addicted to narcotic drugs such as heroin, Oxycodone, or Percocet. The program combines FDA-approved medications including methadone, buprenorphine, naltrexone, and vivitrol with individualized counseling, mental health support, and care coordination to support healing, stability, and long-term recovery. The program gives priority to pregnant women and serves individuals age 18 and older with opioid use disorder and other substance use challenges.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides medication management and administration of FDA-approved medications, individual and group counseling, co-occurring mental health services through intensive outpatient and outpatient programs, care coordination, and referrals to community resources. Services are provided on a fee basis. Maryland Medicaid and Pharmacy Adult Care insurance are accepted. Uninsured individuals may qualify for a sliding scale fee based on income and household size. No one is refused services due to inability to pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents age 18 and older who are addicted to narcotic drugs such as heroin, Oxycodone, or Percocet. The program gives priority to pregnant women.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medication management and administration of FDA-approved medications for opioid use disorder treatment, individual and group counseling services, mental health support services, and care coordination to community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County only. Services are provided at DHHS Offices at 1500 East Gude Drive, Rockville, MD 20850, and at 981 Rollins Avenue, Rockville, MD 20852. Both locations are accessible by public transportation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery Cares - Medical Care for Uninsured Adults
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive medical and dental care program for uninsured adults who are Montgomery County residents with income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level (500% for Ryan White HIV Dental Program). The program is delivered through a group of community-based health care providers and County clinics offering medical services including doctor and nurse check-ups, sick visits, medications, lab tests, x-rays, specialist access, examinations, and preventive care at no charge. Dental services include routine examinations, cleanings, preventive care, non-surgical extractions, limited oral surgery, fillings, root canals, emergency treatment, crowns, dentures, and oral health education. Dental patients pay $20 per visit for routine care or $30 for emergency visits based on a county sliding fee scale, while medical services are provided free of charge. Applications are available online through the Community Connect Portal and MyMDThink.maryland.gov starting January 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medical and dental care services provided through participating health centers, County clinics, and local participating dentists throughout Montgomery County. Medical services include check-ups, sick visits, medications, lab tests, x-rays, specialist referrals, examinations, and preventive care at no charge to enrolled patients. Dental services include routine examinations, x-rays, cleanings, fluoride applications, sealants, preventive care, fillings, non-surgical extractions, limited oral surgery, root canals, emergency treatment, crowns, dentures, and oral health education. Dental patients pay $20 per visit for routine care or $30 for emergency visits using a county sliding fee scale based on family income. Applications are available online through the Community Connect Portal at https://communityconnect.montgomerycountymd.gov/ or MyMDThink.maryland.gov starting January 1, 2025, or by completing a fillable application form and submitting by email, mail, or in person.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Adults can apply online using the Community Connect Portal at https://communityconnect.montgomerycountymd.gov/ or MyMDThink.maryland.gov starting January 1, 2025, or by completing a fillable application form (available in English and Spanish) and submitting it by email to hhsdentalmailbox@montgomerycountymd.gov, by U.S. mail, or in person at one of the clinic locations. Alternatively, call the health center of your choice to enroll or call 311 for information about a health center near you. Submit application with all required documents. Processing time is 2-3 weeks. Applicants receive a letter with the outcome after processing. Bring required documents to your first appointment. Staff at participating health centers assist with eligibility determination. Once approved, call the clinic closest to your home to schedule an appointment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Energy-Efficient Buildings Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive two-tiered property tax credit incentive for newly constructed and existing commercial and multifamily buildings in Montgomery County that achieve energy efficiency performance above current building code requirements or obtain qualifying green building certifications, as well as for owners of existing buildings who install energy conservation devices. For new construction, the Tier 1 credit ranges from 5-10% (10-20% above code) to 82-100% (40%+ above code) based on energy efficiency performance above building code, applied for four years. For existing buildings, Tier 1 credit is calculated based on measurable energy reduction demonstrated through ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager data, with multipliers ranging 1.0 to 2.5 applied for two years. Buildings in Equity Emphasis Areas receive an additional 10% credit. Tier 2 provides an additional tax credit (25-75% depending on certification level) for four years (or five years for Living Building Certification) upon achieving LEED Gold/Platinum, NGBS Gold/Emerald, PHIUS+/Passive House, BREEAM-NC/In-Use Excellent/Outstanding, LBC Petal, or Living Building Certification. Combined credits cannot exceed 100% per year. This credit encourages building owners to exceed current Building and Zoning Code requirements and advances the County's climate goals of 80 percent greenhouse gas reduction by 2027 and zero emissions by 2035.

Credits can aggregate but cannot exceed 100% of County taxes per year. Property tax credit also available for installation of energy conservation devices on existing buildings.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Historic Preservation Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program that encourages the restoration and preservation of privately owned historic properties in Montgomery County. The program provides a tax credit equal to 25% of qualified costs expended on documented expenses for exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation of properties designated as historic sites on the Montgomery County Master Plan for Historic Preservation, located within historic districts, or designated historic by the City of Rockville. The credit applies to exterior work subject to an approved historic area work permit or ordinary maintenance expenses exceeding $1,000. No credit is granted for new construction. The credit is allowed for the tax year immediately following work completion and any unused portion may be carried forward for up to 5 tax years.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a tax credit equal to 25% of qualified exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation costs against Montgomery County real property taxes. The minimum qualifying expenditure is $1,000 in a calendar year, and the tax credit is applied against the following year's property taxes. Any unused portion of the tax credit may be carried forward for up to five years. Eligible expenses include approved storm windows and doors, chimney flue lining and repairs, exterior painting, drainage repairs affecting structural integrity, gutter replacement, termite treatment, architectural trim repair, roof repairs or replacement in-kind, window repairs, outbuilding maintenance, repointing foundations or chimneys, restoring documented features, uncovering or repairing original siding, and professional services such as architects, color consultants, and engineers. Owner's labor costs are not eligible; only material costs qualify. Work must be certified eligible by the Historic District Commission before being submitted to the Montgomery County Department of Finance for processing.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County-funded initiative that promotes a broad range of housing opportunities for residents by supporting the construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of affordable housing units, preserving affordability in existing rental units, and assisting in the development of housing or mixed-use developments that include affordable housing. The program provides flexible financing in the form of loans and grants to for-profit and nonprofit affordable housing developers to acquire, construct, and rehabilitate multifamily developments that meet county objectives and preference criteria.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County provides flexible financing and grants to support the development and preservation of affordable housing. The program offers loans and grants for new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of affordable housing projects. Loans feature a targeted interest rate of 3%, though rates can vary based on project purpose and financing. Loan terms are set by the Director based on project needs. Repayment structure is generally designed to meet the project's financial requirements and the property's ability to pay. Projects must demonstrate financial feasibility including a 20-year pro forma analysis, debt service coverage of 1.0, and loan-to-value ratios not exceeding 100%. An equity contribution of 10% is an expected goal from owners/sponsors. County seeks a 3:1 leverage ratio with other funding sources. Applications are differentiated by project size: small projects have fewer than 10 county-funded units or request less than $500,000 in county funds, while large projects have 10 or more county-funded units with $500,000 or more in county funds.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construct or acquire affordable housing units, buy and rehabilitate existing rental units to preserve affordability, and assist in development of housing or mixed-use developments that include affordable housing. Funds are generally not available for predevelopment costs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary rebate program that helps offset the installation costs of stormwater control practices including rain gardens, conservation landscaping, rainwater harvesting cisterns, green roofs, permeable pavement, pavement removal, and pavement replacement on residential, commercial, institutional, and community properties in Montgomery County. These practices manage stormwater runoff, reduce lawn area, slow down and allow stormwater to soak into the ground naturally while recharging groundwater, replace lawn and invasive plants with native plants and improved soil, and provide habitat for pollinators. The program offers cost-share rebates to help property owners install stormwater management techniques to improve water quality and manage stormwater runoff. Property owners pay the full upfront cost of the project and receive a rebate after installation and final inspection based on project type metrics. The program is administered as a rolling application on a first come, first served basis. Water harvesting cisterns and rain barrels collect and store rainwater from roof downspouts for reuse. Pavement removal allows property owners to remove pavement and replace it with natural vegetation such as rain gardens, conservation landscaping, or lawn to reduce stormwater runoff and improve the environment. The program provides financial incentives and educational guidance through the 'Slow it. Spread it. Sink it!' approach to implement Best Management Practices (BMPs).
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates are provided to help offset the cost of installing rain gardens, conservation landscaping, rainwater harvesting cisterns, green roofs, permeable pavement, and pavement removal. For residential cisterns: $1 per gallon of capacity with maximum rebate of $500 (exceptions to maximum amounts possible on case-by-case basis). For commercial or institutional cisterns: $2 per gallon of capacity with maximum rebate of $2,000 (exceptions possible on case-by-case basis). For water harvesting rain barrels and cisterns: $1 per gallon of water harvesting capacity installed, with rain barrel projects eligible for a maximum rebate of $250, cistern projects for a maximum of $500, with a total maximum of $750 per property if both rain barrels and cisterns are installed. For conservation landscapes: $5 per square foot for landscapes with no ponding, or $6 per square foot for landscapes with 3 inches of ponding. Minimum project size is 250 square feet for the ponding option. Community pools, HOAs, congregations, multi-family and institutional properties qualify for a lifetime maximum rebate of $20,000.00 per parcel based on tax ID number. Residential properties can receive rebates up to $7,500, while commercial, homeowners association, multifamily, or institutional properties can receive up to $20,000 per parcel. Permeable pavement retrofit is $14 per square foot. Pavement removal rebates are $3 to $7 per square foot depending on the replacement type—$3 per square foot when replacing pavement with sod (lawn), and $7 per square foot when replacing with conservation landscape plantings. The final rebate amount is based on total acceptable receipts up to the approved rebate amount, excluding sales tax. Applicants receive rebate checks within 8 to 12 weeks after final inspection. Program includes free educational workshops and free on-site stormwater runoff evaluations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; applications accepted on a first come, first served basis; no deadline specified
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County property owners (outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park), homeowner associations, community pools, private schools, congregations, multi-family properties, and institutional properties interested in installing rain gardens, conservation landscaping, rainwater harvesting cisterns, green roofs, permeable pavement, pavement removal, or pavement replacement for stormwater reduction and water quality improvement. Educational guide available for homeowners implementing sustainable home drainage best management practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of stormwater control practices including rain gardens, conservation landscaping, rainwater harvesting cisterns, green roofs, permeable pavement retrofits, pavement removal, permeable pavement on driveways, patios, and parking areas, and other Best Management Practices (BMPs) to manage stormwater runoff, prevent erosion or flooding, and conserve water through rainwater collection and reuse. Conservation landscapes replace lawn, invasive plants, or erosion-prone areas with native plants and improved soil. Pavement removal involves removal of asphalt, concrete patios, driveways, or pool decks and replacement with rain gardens, conservation landscaping, or lawn to allow rainwater infiltration with decompacted soil. Rain garden establishment and technical design and implementation also included. Eligible costs include plant materials, mulch, compost, stone, hardware, equipment rental, design fees, and labor directly related to the project.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within Montgomery County but outside of the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park, which collect the Water Quality Protection Charge separately and administer their own programs. Citywide programs are also available in Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park through their own rebate programs. Programs also apply to Montgomery County watersheds including Rock Creek Watershed, Watts Branch Watershed, and Cabin John Creek.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the application process and requirements, then submit an application through the RainScapes Application Portal or RainScapes Rewards portal or electronically online. Applicants can check the status of a current application through the online portal. Applications are reviewed and approved on a first come, first served basis. Define your property concerns and goals and assess your property for water issues. Select and learn about your project type. Find your Property Tax ID. Contact the RainScapes program to request a site assessment where staff help identify potential project locations and recommend appropriate projects. Schedule a site assessment with a RainScapes planner, conducted in-person or virtually, to evaluate project eligibility. Within 2-4 weeks, you will be assigned a planner who will contact you and conduct a site assessment. Receive site assessment report with observations and recommendations. After application submittal, the applicant will be contacted for a preliminary inspection to ensure site suitability. Submit your plan to your planner for review within three months of receiving the site assessment. Receive official project approval email. Obtain project approval for installation. Call MISS Utility (811) before installation. Install your project meeting minimum standards. Upon project installation, submit itemized receipts and electronically sign and submit the Property Owner Agreement. Contact RainScapes planner to schedule final inspection after installation. Submit all receipts, photos, and measurements for verification. Schedule and pass a final inspection to receive the rebate. Receive rebate check within 8 to 12 weeks after final inspection. Optionally apply for a Water Quality Protection Charge credit. Property owners can choose a RainScapes professional from the contractor list or complete the work themselves. Submit required supporting documents including location plan and HOA approval letter if applicable. For water harvesting projects, review Water Harvesting Project Manual and design criteria. Conduct DIY property evaluation to identify suitable BMPs. Consult qualified professionals for site-specific design and implementation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program available to businesses that establish new or expand existing premises and create new permanent full-time employment positions in Montgomery County. A standard six-year tax credit is available to businesses that increase their space by at least 5,000 square feet and hire at least 25 new permanent full-time employees within a 24-month period. The credit is based on increases in real and personal property tax assessments from the business expansion. Years 1-2: 52% of tax attributable to assessment increase; Years 3-4: 39%; Years 5-6: 26%. Additionally, the State provides a separate income tax credit at 28% (years 1-2), 21% (years 3-4), and 14% (years 5-6). State credits may be rolled forward up to five years if unused. An Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit is also available for large expansion projects in specific industries including manufacturing, mining, transportation, communications, agriculture, forestry, fishing, research and development, biotechnology, computer services, financial services, insurance services, central administrative offices, company headquarters, public utilities, warehousing, and business services. The Enhanced credit is a 12-year credit calculated at 58.5% of additional local tax liability for all 12 years. Established under Maryland State law (§9-230 of Tax-Property Article) and Montgomery County Code (Chapter 52, Article X).

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The New Jobs Tax Credit is based on increases in real and personal property tax assessments. Additionally, the State provides a separate income tax credit at 28% (years 1-2), 21% (years 3-4), and 14% (years 5-6). State credits may be rolled forward up to five years if unused. Tax credits can be applied to state and/or county tax liability including local real and personal property taxes, state corporate or personal income taxes, financial institutions franchise tax, or insurance premiums tax. The Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit is a 12-year credit for large expansion projects meeting specific criteria and is calculated at 58.5% of additional local tax liability for all 12 years. The 25 new jobs must be permanent full-time positions lasting at least 24 months, and the new space must be occupied during the period the business retains the required employees.

structured_extraction.program_name: Opioid Overdose Prevention and Naloxone (Narcan) Training
structured_extraction.program_description: A free community training program that teaches participants how to identify opioid overdose situations, administer naloxone (Narcan) to reverse overdoses, call 911, and provide appropriate care during and after an overdose emergency. The 2-hour course covers what to do and what not to do in an overdose situation, how to administer Narcan, provides overdose prevention tips, and information about local and national resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 2-hour training session on opioid overdose identification, naloxone (Narcan) administration, emergency response procedures, and overdose prevention. Training teaches what to do and what not to do in an overdose situation, how to call 911, how to administer Narcan, and what to do after administering it. Participants receive training materials and information about local and national resources.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 18 and older, including Montgomery County residents and community members who are concerned about a friend, family member, or associate with opioid addiction or who want to learn overdose response and Narcan administration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education on opioid overdose recognition, naloxone (Narcan) administration, emergency response procedures, and overdose prevention.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be at least 18 years old
Must be concerned about a friend, family member, or associate with opioid addiction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Overdose Response Program by phone at 240.777.1836, email OverdoseResponseProgram@montgomerycountymd.gov, or call 311 to register for an available training session in your community.

structured_extraction.program_name: Partnership Fund for Victims of Hate/Violence
structured_extraction.program_description: A fund created to support victims of hate crimes and incidents in Montgomery County. Administered by the Montgomery County Committee Against Hate/Violence and the Office of Human Rights, the program works to eradicate acts of hate and intimidation through community education, advocacy, collaboration and legislation. It provides partial compensation and reimbursement to individuals and private institutions for property damage and medical expenses resulting from hate crimes or hate violence based on race, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or disability. The program provides reimbursement up to $2,000 per hate or violence act for property damage and up to $4,000 for medical expenses from physical injury. Total compensation cannot exceed $8,000 to any one victim within a 12-month period. The program aims to demonstrate community support for victims and help ease the financial consequences of such violence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement for property damage up to $2,000 per hate or violence act, and up to $4,000 for medical expenses from physical injury. Total compensation cannot exceed $8,000 to any one victim within a 12-month period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Victims of hate crimes and incidents, families or significant others of victims, and Montgomery County residents who are individuals and private institutions and have experienced hate crimes or hate violence based on race, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or disability in Montgomery County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for property damage and medical expenses incurred as a result of hate crimes or hate violence incidents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Victim of a hate crime or hate violence act in Montgomery County
Property damage or medical expenses resulting from the hate crime or hate violence act
Must be eligible under Montgomery County law
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Report hate crime or incident to Montgomery County Police Department (911 for emergencies, 301-279-8000 for non-emergencies) or contact the Montgomery County Office of Human Rights at 240-777-8450 or email Human-RightsAdministration@montgomerycountymd.gov to apply for reimbursement from the fund. A member will contact the victim, listen to the complaint, convey concern, and offer assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) Exemptions
structured_extraction.program_description: The PILOT program supports affordable housing by allowing the County to negotiate agreements with rental property owners to lower county real property and special area taxes in exchange for commitments to provide affordable housing to low-income residents.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County negotiates PILOT agreements with rental property owners to reduce county real property and special area taxes in exchange for commitments to provide affordable housing to low-income residents. Following legal, budgetary, and procedural review, the County Department of Housing and Community Affairs recommends a PILOT to the Director of Finance for approval. The Department of Finance computes the fiscal impact and, subject to guidelines and an annual funding limit, approves or denies the recommended PILOT. The exemption is applied to real property tax bills once the agreement is executed. The County Council sets the maximum annual funding amount for PILOT programs for a 10-year period only for properties not owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunity Commission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rental property owners committing to provide affordable housing for low-income residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduced property taxes on rental properties providing affordable housing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Rental property
Commitment to provide affordable housing to low-income residents
Property not owned or controlled by Housing Opportunity Commission (for 10-year funding limit)
Must meet negotiated agreement terms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Rental property owner works with County Department of Housing and Community Affairs which recommends PILOT agreements to Director of Finance for approval.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of exterior security camera systems with digital video recording capability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within a Priority Area designated by the Police Chief. Priority areas are identified based on crime levels and public safety indicators. Applicants can check eligibility via the Department's camera application website.

Written agreement to comply with program

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County program that allows affordable housing to be developed in commercial and industrial zones where residential use is normally not permitted. Developers can build housing affordable to households earning 75 percent of County median income through a special exception approval process. Housing can be developed at base density of 6 units per acre, or up to 21.5 units per acre if at least 35 percent of units are affordable.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program allows developers to receive approval to build residential housing in commercial and industrial zoning areas that normally do not permit residential development. Developers must apply for and receive a Special Exception approval from the Montgomery County Board of Appeals. Once approved, developers can build housing at higher densities (up to 21.5 units per acre) if they include affordable units. The program sets affordability requirements, rental rates, and sales prices for productivity housing units, with for-sale units controlled for 10 years and rental units controlled for 20 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Real estate developers seeking to build residential housing projects in commercial and industrial zones in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program enables development of affordable housing units in commercial and industrial zoned areas. Affordable units must be priced or rented affordably to households earning 75 percent of County median income. Sales prices are limited to 175 percent of comparable Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit prices. Rental rates are set at 30 percent of household income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Eligible zones include C-1 Convenience Commercial, C-2 General Commercial, C-3 Highway Commercial, C-4 Limited Commercial, O-M Office Building Moderate Intensity, I-1 Light Industrial, I-3 Technology and Business Park, and I-4 Low Intensity Light Industrial. No more than 25 percent of land zoned commercial and industrial in each master plan area can be used for multifamily housing.
requirements_list: Developer must apply for and receive Special Exception approval from Montgomery County Board of Appeals
Developer must execute written agreement with Department of Housing and Community Affairs before building permit issuance
Agreement must include subdivision name, marketing name, and staging plan for construction
Productivity housing units must be built along with or before other dwelling units per staging plan
Developer must record productivity housing agreement in County Land Records
Copy of recorded agreement must be provided to County promptly
Copy of executed agreement must be submitted to Department of Permitting Services with first building permit application
Single-family productivity housing units must have at least two or more bedrooms
For multifamily projects, ratio of efficiency and one-bedroom affordable units cannot exceed ratio of market-rate efficiency and one-bedroom units
Maximum sales prices limited to 175 percent of comparable MPDU sale price
Rental rates set based on 75 percent of area median income adjusted for family size
Maximum rents including utilities cannot exceed 30 percent of calculated gross household income
For-sale units occupied by owner as primary residence during control period
Rental units cannot be sublet unless permitted and approved by Department
For-sale units controlled for 10 years; rental units controlled for 20 years
Upon resale after control period expires, owner must pay one-half of excess profit to Housing Initiative Fund
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Developer applies for Special Exception, which must be approved by Montgomery County Board of Appeals per zoning ordinance Section G-2.36.2. Step 2: Before building permit issuance, developer executes written agreement with Director of Department of Housing and Community Affairs containing subdivision name, marketing name, and staging plan. Step 3: Developer records productivity housing agreement in County Land Records and provides copy to County. Step 4: Copy of executed agreement is submitted to Department of Permitting Services with first building permit application. Building permits will not be issued unless PHUs are part of the staging plan.
