structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Disabled Veterans
structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credit program for disabled veterans in Montgomery County, Maryland under County Code Section 52-113. The credit reduces County Property Tax for qualified disabled veterans and their qualified surviving spouses based on the severity of their service-connected disability. The credit equals 50% of County Property Tax for veterans with a service-connected disability of 75% or more, or 25% of County Property Tax for veterans with a service-connected disability between 50% and 74%.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit for disabled veterans whose principal residence meets specific criteria. The credit equals 50% of County Property Tax for veterans with a service-connected disability of 75% or more, or 25% of County Property Tax for veterans with a service-connected disability between 50% and 74%. Veterans who qualify for a Property Tax Exemption under Section 7-208 of the Tax Property Article of the Maryland Code are not eligible for this credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 before the tax year for which credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans with honorable discharge who own property in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability for principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Property must be principal residence and occupied by no more than 2 families.
requirements_list: Honorable discharge from U.S. Armed Forces
Permanent service-connected disability of at least 50% OR 100% non-permanent service-connected disability
Federal adjusted gross income not exceeding $100,000 (prior tax year)
Property is principal residence occupied by no more than 2 families
Submit DD-214, VA disability certification, and prior year federal tax return
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application with required documentation (DD-214, VA disability certification, prior year federal tax return) to Division of Treasury. All three required documents must be submitted or application will not be processed. Sign under penalties of perjury.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Elderly Individuals and for Military Retirees (Bill 42-16)
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program for Montgomery County residents who are 65 years or older or retired from the U.S. armed forces or uniformed services. Eligible 65+ homeowners must have owned and lived in their home for at least 40 consecutive years, or be retired military personnel. The program provides a 20% credit on county property taxes for owner-occupied dwellings for 7 consecutive years (not renewable after that period). Property assessments must not exceed $700,000 for 40-year homeowners or $550,000 for military retirees. Surviving spouses of eligible military retirees may also qualify under certain conditions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 20% credit on Montgomery County property taxes for owner-occupied dwellings only. The credit is granted for 7 consecutive years and is not renewable after that period. For 40-year homeowners, the dwelling must have an assessment of $700,000 or less at the time of application. For military retirees, the dwelling must have an assessment of $550,000 or less at the time of application. Surviving spouses of military retirees may also receive the credit if the retiree would have been eligible at the time of death and the spouse has not remarried.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals 65 years and older who are long-term homeowners or retired military service members, surviving spouses of eligible military retirees, and other eligible elderly individuals and military retirees residing in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit to reduce property tax liability on owner-occupied dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Applicant must be 65 years old or older with a birthday on or before June 30, 1960 to receive the credit beginning July 1, 2025
For 40-year homeowners: Must have owned and lived in the dwelling for at least 40 consecutive years; deed must be dated June 30, 1985 or earlier; dwelling assessment must be $700,000 or less

For retired military: Must be retired from the U.S. Air Force, Army, Coast Guard, Marine Corps, Navy, or uniformed services of NOAA or Public Health Service, or retired from military reserves or National Guard; must have retired status, not just veteran status; dwelling assessment must be $550,000 or less
Property owner must be on the deed
Dwelling must be owner-occupied

For surviving spouses: Retiree must have been at least 65 years old at time of death and had retired status; surviving spouse must not have remarried; must provide death certificate, signed affidavit of non-remarriage, and proof of retiree's retired status
For properties titled in a trust: Must complete, sign, and submit an Affidavit Re Trust Ownership
Application must be received on or before April 1
Proof of age required (driver's license or birth certificate)
Original deed copy required for 40-year owners or retired military I.D. for military retirees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the appropriate application form (standard application for individuals 65 and above or retired military, or surviving spouse application). Gather required documentation including proof of age, ownership, residency or military retirement status, and any required affidavits. For properties in trusts, submit the Affidavit Re Trust Ownership. Mail the complete application to the Department of Finance, Division of Treasury, Attn: Bill 42-16 Tax Credit, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, Maryland 20850 by April 1. Approved applications submitted by April 1 will be processed on the property tax bill issued in July of the same year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit – Local Income Tax Offset
structured_extraction.program_description: This tax credit is available to owners of owner-occupied residential property to offset increases in county income tax revenues resulting from a county income tax rate in excess of 2.6%. The County establishes the amount of the credit by resolution. The County may grant a property tax credit against the county tax imposed on real property to offset increases in county income tax revenues. The credit is applied against county property tax and is available only to owners of owner-occupied residential property (principal residence), as determined by SDAT.

Determined by SDAT

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit – Nonprofit Swim Clubs
structured_extraction.program_description: This tax credit provides real property tax relief for nonprofit swim clubs that use their facilities exclusively to provide recreational outlets for local communities. The program offers exemptions against general County tax and special service area taxes. A nonprofit swim club is eligible for a real property tax credit against the general County tax and special service area taxes, provided it uses its facilities exclusively to provide a recreational outlet for a local community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit applies to County Taxes only (General County Tax and Special Service Area Taxes). A nonprofit swim club is eligible for a real property tax credit and exemption against the general County tax and special service area taxes, provided it uses its facilities exclusively to provide a recreational outlet for a local community. The nonprofit swim club must provide the County with documentation showing it is a nonprofit entity and must certify that its facilities are used solely for these stated purposes. Required documentation includes a copy of Articles of Incorporation and a current Certificate of Good Standing from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. First-year applicants must provide Articles of Incorporation and Certificate in Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.

Articles of Incorporation (first year and if changes occur)
Current Certificate in Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit – Renewable Energy (Energy Conservation Devices for Owner-Occupied Residential)
structured_extraction.program_description: This tax credit provides property tax relief to owners of owner-occupied residential properties who install energy conservation devices that reduce demand for conventional fuels or increase fuel efficiency.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An owner of an owner-occupied residential property who installs an energy conservation device may receive a real property tax credit against the County tax on the property. The credit is limited to $250 per property in any fiscal year. The energy conservation device must reduce demand for conventional fuels or increase efficiency of these fuels, meet safety and performance standards set by a nationally recognized testing laboratory, and must not be a standard household appliance. Annual funding for this credit is limited to $100,000 total. Credits are granted in the order applications are received.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of owner-occupied residential properties installing energy conservation devices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit for energy conservation device installation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Owner-occupied residential property
Energy conservation device reduces demand for conventional fuels or increases fuel efficiency
Device meets safety and performance standards of nationally recognized testing laboratory
Device is not a standard household appliance
Credit limited to $250 per property per fiscal year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owner must submit completed application to Montgomery County Department of Finance demonstrating device eligibility. Credits granted in order received.

structured_extraction.program_description: A public campaign financing program that provides matching public funds to eligible candidates running for Montgomery County offices. The program aims to encourage greater voter participation in County elections, increase opportunities for more residents to run for office, and reduce the influence of large contributions from businesses, political action groups, and other large organizations. Montgomery County was the first county in the United States to establish a public campaign finance program for a local election.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Candidates receive matching public funds based on qualifying contributions at tiered ratios (up to 7:1 for County Executive). Maximum public contributions are: County Executive $870,170; At-Large Councilmember $290,060; District Councilmember $145,030 per election. During the 2018 election cycle, 23 qualifying candidates received approximately $5.25 million in matching public funds total. In 2022, 20 qualified candidates received approximately $3.7 million. Distributions are made within 3 business days of Board authorization. Matching funds are distributed to certified candidates' publicly funded campaign accounts based on eligible contributions received and calculated separately for primary and general elections.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Notice of Intent: April 15 of election year; Qualifying Period: January 1 following last election through 45 days before primary election; For 2026 election cycle - Notice of Intent April 15, 2026; Qualifying Period Close May 9, 2026; Receipt Submission Period Close Primary Election date (6/23/2026) or General Election date (11/3/2026); Distribution period: June 23, 2025 through December 3, 2026; Initial certification reports and matching fund reports due first and third Tuesday of each month
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maurice Valentine; Kevin Gillogly; David Crow
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual candidates running for Montgomery County Council and County Executive offices in contested elections. Participation is voluntary.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campaign expenditures directly related to election campaign activities during primary or general election periods. Allowable uses include campaign promotion, candidate defeat campaigns, and ongoing services such as website maintenance fees contracted after filing notice of intent. All campaign materials must include proper authority lines. Prohibited uses: personal expenses, holding office expenses, personal endorsements, late filing fees, expenses before Board certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Candidate must be a Montgomery County resident. Qualifying contributions must be from Montgomery County residents ($5-$500 each). Primary and general elections are treated separately. Other Maryland counties may establish similar programs under state law.
requirements_list: Must be a candidate running for an eligible County office (County Council or County Executive)
Must file intent to participate in the program
Must meet qualification requirements set by the State of Maryland Board of Elections
Must file with the Maryland Campaign Reporting Information System (MDCRIS)
Candidate must be in a contested election (more candidates than positions available)
Must obtain minimum qualifying contributions ($5-$500 each from County residents; minimums vary by office: 500 for County Executive, 250 for At-Large, 125 for District)
Must register public financing committee in MDCRIS prior to filing notice of intent
Must establish publicly funded campaign account
Must satisfy certification requirements from the Board
Must comply with contribution limits and matching formula
Cannot be member of a slate
Cannot pay campaign expenses from any account other than publicly funded campaign account after filing notice of intent

Must return unspent funds to the Public Election Fund within 90 days after general election certification (except up to $10,000 may be retained for post-election expenses if new declaration filed by January 31)
All campaign materials must include proper authority lines
Must retain copies of campaign materials for one year
Employer/occupation information required for contributions of $500
In-kind contributions and candidate/spouse contributions do not qualify for matching
Receipts must be linked to contributions in MDCRIS
Must maintain $0.00 balance for final report filing
Contributors must be Montgomery County residents for contributions to qualify for matching
Candidate must not participate in primary election OR must meet certification requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Candidates must file a notice of intent to participate in the Public Election Fund by April 15 of the election year. Candidates must register a public financing committee and publicly funded campaign account in MDCRIS prior to filing notice of intent. Candidates must obtain qualifying contributions ($5-$500 each from Montgomery County residents) during the qualifying period. The State of Maryland Board of Elections certifies candidates' eligibility. Initial certification reports and matching fund reports are available the first and third Tuesday of each month. Candidates submit contributions with proper documentation through MDCRIS. Campaign finance reports must be filed on statutory deadlines through MDCRIS. Candidates upload and link receipt documents to contributions. The Director of Finance processes contributions in order received until fund balance is exhausted or all authorized contributions are satisfied. The Montgomery County Department of Finance administers the program and authorizes distributions to approved candidates within 3 business days. The Office of Consumer Protection serves as the PEF Liaison and assists candidates with questions throughout the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A conditional grant program that provides grants or conditional grants to local for-profit small businesses and non-profit organizations in Montgomery County that are experiencing significant adverse impact due to a communicable disease resulting in a Federal, State, or County Public Health Emergency order restricting business operations. The program is funded through the Economic Development Fund to support economic development and the continued operation of eligible businesses and organizations during public health emergencies. Grants support up to $10,000 for actual documented revenue loss reimbursement and up to $2,500 for purchasing technology equipment and software to facilitate employee teleworking. Additional disbursements up to $75,000 maximum for revenue loss are possible based on demonstrated additional revenue loss.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A conditional grant program established under the Economic Development Fund to assist local for-profit small businesses and non-profit organizations experiencing significant adverse impact due to public health emergency orders restricting business operations. Provides up to $10,000 based on actual documented revenue loss, with initial disbursement of $10,000 for businesses demonstrating Significant Financial Loss, and up to $75,000 maximum for revenue loss through multiple disbursements based on demonstrated additional revenue loss. Also provides up to $2,500 for purchasing technology equipment and software to facilitate employee teleworking. Eligible businesses must have 100 or fewer full-time-equivalent employees, exist prior to the public health emergency, demonstrate significant financial loss of 50% or greater in adjusted revenue, and enter into a grant agreement with the County including audit rights and penalty of perjury certification. Grant funds cannot cover losses already reimbursed by federal or state assistance, insurance-covered losses, or wages for employees eligible for unemployment insurance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 31, 2020
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local for-profit businesses and non-profit organizations in Montgomery County with 100 or fewer full-time equivalent employees affected by public health emergency orders restricting business operations. Restaurants and retail storefront establishments receive priority consideration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset actual revenue losses from public health emergency and purchasing technology equipment and software for employee teleworking. structured_extraction.program_name: Residential Real Property Tax Deferral - General
structured_extraction.program_description: This program allows eligible homeowners to defer payment of county property taxes on residential real property used as their principal residence. Deferred taxes accrue interest and must not exceed 50% of the property's full cash value. A taxpayer may defer payment of County property taxes due on residential real property used as the owner's principal residence. The amount of taxes that may be deferred for any one year is the amount that County taxes due exceeds the amount of County property taxes paid in the prior taxable year. Taxes eligible for deferral are the General County tax and Special Service Area taxes. Interest accrues on deferred taxes at a rate set annually by the County that does not exceed the prime lending rate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A taxpayer may defer payment of County property taxes due on residential real property used as the owner's principal residence. The amount of taxes that may be deferred for any one year is the amount that County taxes due exceeds the amount of County property taxes paid in the prior taxable year. Taxes eligible for deferral are the General County tax and Special Service Area taxes. Interest accrues on deferred taxes at a rate set annually by the County that does not exceed the prime lending rate. The accumulation of deferred taxes and accrued interest must not exceed 50% of the full cash value of the property.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides short-term temporary relief to unpaid full-time caregivers and families providing care to frail elderly adults, functionally disabled adults (including those with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias), children with challenging behaviors, children and adults with developmental disabilities, and children with severe medical conditions. Care is provided by trained, certified care workers in the family's home, adult medical day programs, or in a respite care facility. Respite care services can be arranged for a few hours, a day, a weekend, or longer. Services are provided at no cost to eligible primary caregivers, with limited subsidies available to help pay for respite care services when funds are available. Respite care is not an entitlement and eligibility for a subsidy does not guarantee funds for each respite occasion requested. Limited funding is available, with the goal to assist as many families as possible each month.

Respite staff work with families to locate appropriate providers for direct services after application approval and orientation. Limited funding is available, with the goal to assist as many families as possible each month. Services are provided at no cost to eligible primary caregivers.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that requires property owners to offer Montgomery County, the Housing Opportunities Commission, or certified tenant organizations the opportunity to purchase multifamily rental housing developments of 4 or more units before selling to another buyer. The County can assign its right of first refusal to qualified affordable housing developers and organizations, helping to preserve affordable housing and prevent tenant displacement by giving the county or designated nonprofits the opportunity to purchase multifamily housing properties before they are sold on the open market.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides the opportunity to purchase multifamily rental housing before it is sold to a third party. When the County assigns its right of first refusal to a qualified entity, that entity must enter into an assignment agreement with the County and a covenant recorded on the property. The agreement requires landlords to limit rent increases to no more than the Voluntary Rent Guidelines for 15 years, provide existing tenants the right to return to their unit at the same rent level after rehabilitation, and restrict evictions to specific circumstances.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.contact_name: Lawrence Cager, Manager of the Multifamily Section
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified affordable housing developers and organizations, property owners of multifamily rental housing with 4 or more units, and certified tenant organizations seeking to preserve affordable multifamily housing in Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Multifamily rental housing developments must include 4 or more units to trigger ROFR requirements.
requirements_list: Property must be multifamily rental housing with 4 or more units
Qualified entities must apply to the Department of Housing and Community Affairs and be approved by the County Executive
Qualified entities must remain approved for a 5-year period
Qualified entities must enter into an assignment agreement with the County
A covenant must be recorded on the property at closing
Qualified entities cannot evict tenants except for specific lease violations, nonpayment of rent, disturbance of peace, illegal activity, or refusal to allow property access
Rent increases limited to Voluntary Rent Guidelines for 15 years
Existing tenants have the right to return to their unit or equivalent unit at the same rent level after rehabilitation or redevelopment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Property owner enters into a contract for sale and sends a complete ROFR packet to DHCA within 5 days of executing the contract. Step 2: DHCA receives the packet and forwards it to approved qualified entities. Step 3: DHCA and qualified entities review and inspect the property. Step 4: If interested, DHCA requests interest from qualified entities who have 45 days to notify DHCA of their intent to exercise ROFR. If more than one entity is interested, DHCA selects based on regulatory parameters. Step 5: If the County chooses to exercise ROFR through assignment, it executes an assignment agreement with the designated qualified entity before the 60-day period expires. The sale must be completed within 180 days of DHCA receiving the ROFR packet unless extended.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grant funding to support projects that address critical gaps in healthy food access for children and families by implementing innovative approaches to co-locating food assistance at Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS) school sites. The program awards multi-year grant funding to non-profit organizations, government entities, and school partners to establish, expand, and maintain school-based food assistance programs in partnership with MCPS, supporting various food assistance models including food pantries, pre-packed snack bags, grocery distributions, and prepared meals across approximately 99 MCPS school sites serving an estimated 50,000 students. The program supports student nutrition and food security and anticipates continued expansion of reach across Montgomery County Public Schools sites.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program awards multi-year grant funding to non-profit organizations, government entities, and school partners to establish, expand, and maintain school-based food assistance programs in partnership with MCPS. In FY26, a total of $2,303,775 was awarded to 13 organizations to support programs at 99 MCPS school sites serving an estimated 50,000 students. In FY25, $1,250,274 was awarded to 11 organizations supporting 60+ school sites. In FY24, $480,452 was awarded to 8 organizations supporting 30+ school sites. Funding supports various food assistance models including food pantries, pre-packed snack bags, grocery distributions, prepared meals, food purchases, nutrition education for families, and in-school food assistance services. Multiple service formats include Family Market/Choice Pantry, Pre-Packaged Boxes/Bags (household and individual size), Pre-Packaged Snack Bags, Prepared Meals, and Gift Cards. Food types supported include shelf-stable items, meat, dairy, eggs, produce, and prepared food/meals. The program prioritizes sourcing from Montgomery County farms and DMV region underserved community farms. Funding covers staffing costs, food purchases, operating costs, and indirect costs. The program anticipates expanding reach by over 30% with new budget funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Citizens Real Property Tax Deferral Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows eligible senior citizens in Montgomery County to defer payment of increases in their residential property taxes. Eligible homeowners who are 65 years or older and have lived in their home for five consecutive years can defer the amount their property tax increased from one year to the next. The deferred amount accrues no interest and remains as a lien on the property. The deferred amount becomes due when the homeowner sells the property, stops occupying it as their principal residence, or passes away and the surviving owner is not eligible. Homeowners can end the deferral at any time by providing written notice and paying the deferred taxes.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program defers payment of the amount by which county property taxes increase from one year to the next. The deferred amount accrues no interest and remains as a lien on the property. The deferred amount becomes due when the homeowner sells the property, stops occupying it as their principal residence, or passes away and the surviving owner is not eligible. Homeowners can end the deferral at any time by providing written notice and paying the deferred taxes. The deferred amount can be applied toward the second installment of property taxes or refunded if the tax bill has been paid in full.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive congregate meal program funded under the Older Americans Act (Public Law 109-365) administered by Montgomery County's Department of Health and Human Services, Aging and Disability Services. The program promotes better health through improved nutrition and helps older adults remain healthy, independent, and active. It encourages fellowship and reduces isolation through socialization while providing access to supportive services throughout the county. The program provides nutritious hot, cold, and vegetarian meals at meal locations throughout Montgomery County served at noon or 11:30 AM at some locations. Participants age 60 and over are asked to make voluntary contributions or donations toward meal costs. The program also connects eligible homebound individuals to home-delivered meals through partner Meals on Wheels organizations. Individuals under 60 may participate at the full meal price.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hot meals are provided at lunchtime at designated senior centers and recreation centers throughout Montgomery County, with nutritious congregate meals including hot, cold, and vegetarian options served at noon or 11:30 AM at some locations. Seniors ages 60 and over are asked to make voluntary contributions or donations (recommended $3 per meal) toward meal costs. Donations accepted in cash, check, or credit card. Home-delivered meals are also available through partner Meals on Wheels organizations for homebound seniors who cannot prepare their own meals or travel to lunch sites. Individuals under 60 may participate at the full meal price. Meals include whole grain breads/pastas, 100% fruit juice, milk or yogurt, proteins (beef, chicken, fish, pork), vegetables, fruits, grains, and dairy. Monthly menus are available in multiple languages. Some centers offer a stand-by or waiting list for individuals wishing to have a meal at the last minute if extra meals are available. Nutritious meals served at 13 partnering locations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Assistance Program (SBAP) / Impact Assistance Fund (IAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by Montgomery County that provides financial assistance and/or technical assistance to small businesses adversely impacted by County redevelopment projects. The program has two components: (1) the Small Business Assistance Program (SBAP), a sub-program of the Economic Development Fund that provides loans and grants to small businesses up to $125,000 through an established award process governed by Executive Regulation 24-12AM, and (2) the Impact Assistance Fund (IAF), which provides one-time financial assistance up to $25,000 and/or technical assistance to financially healthy small businesses in designated areas adversely impacted by County-funded redevelopment projects, redevelopment projects on County-owned property, or County facility projects. Both components provide assistance to businesses in identified geographic areas that are adversely impacted by redevelopment activities.

The SBAP component provides loans and grants from the Economic Development Fund awarded according to criteria established in Executive Regulation 24-12AM. The IAF component provides one-time financial assistance to financially healthy small businesses in designated areas. Assistance is provided periodically over the duration of County-related redevelopment projects to businesses adversely impacted by County-funded redevelopment projects or redevelopment projects on County-owned property or County facilities.

structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Stage 1 application is now closed. Applicants selected for the program will be notified by the end of March 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current graduate level students (Masters or PhD programs) in policy-related fields who have completed at least their first year of study and will not have graduated by the program start date.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a fellowship providing stipend support and professional development experience in local government, not a traditional grant for project funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live in the Washington, D.C. region during the fellowship period. Telework agreements may be discussed on an individual basis with supervisors, but in-person hours are still expected. Many County office buildings are a 10-minute walk from either the Rockville Metro Station or the Wheaton Metro Station. Other placements may be elsewhere in the County.
requirements_list: Be a current graduate level student (Masters or PhD program)
Cannot have graduated before the program start date (June 1, 2026)
Have completed at least first year of graduate study by program start date
Study public policy, public administration/affairs, public health, planning, law, or related fields
Have a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale
Live in the Washington, D.C. region during the fellowship period
Be enthusiastic to learn about local government
Demonstrate innovative ideas and approaches to policy problems
Embody strong interpersonal skills and collaborative mindsets
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Two-stage written application followed by an interview for selected candidates. Stage 1 application is now closed. Selected applicants receive Stage 2 application by mid-January, which requires two reference letters (preferably including at least one graduate professor or supervisor), first semester graduate school transcript, a writing sample (5-10 pages), and responses to four short answer questions. Selected Stage 2 applicants advance to Stage 3 interview. Program participants are notified by end of March 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides County tax credits for homeowners in Montgomery County who qualify for the State Homeowners Tax Credit. The credit is based on a homeowner's household income compared to their property tax bill. The supplemental credit works in combination with the state credit to provide additional tax relief. The program is administered by Montgomery County in coordination with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). Combined credits with the state credit averaged $1,276 last year, benefiting thousands of County residents annually. The credit is applied against the General County and Special Service Area real property tax on a progressive scale tied to combined gross income levels.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County Supplement provides an additional tax credit applied only against the General County and Special Service Area real property tax. The credit amount is calculated based on a progressive scale tied to combined gross income levels, with amounts ranging from 0% to 8% depending on income. For the July 1, 2026 tax year, the assessed value threshold is $383,100, combined income eligibility is $76,620, and net worth criteria is $255,400. Combined credits with the state credit averaged $1,276 last year. No additional application is necessary—the credit is included in the application for the Homeowners Property Tax Credit. Qualified retirement savings are excluded from net worth calculations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1st each year to be applicable for that tax year. Taxpayers age 70 or older may submit retroactive applications for the current and 3 prior levy years at any time.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners of all ages who qualify for the State Homeowners Tax Credit, including households earning less than $60,000
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied against General County and Special Service Area real property taxes to reduce property tax obligations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must qualify for the State Homeowners Tax Credit
Must apply for the State HOTC to be considered for the County Supplement
Assessed property value must not exceed $383,100 (as of July 1, 2026)
Combined household income must not exceed $76,620 (as of July 1, 2026)
Net worth must not exceed $255,400 (as of July 1, 2026)
Must be a homeowner
Household income must be less than $60,000
Owner-occupied residential property (principal residence)
Qualified retirement savings are excluded from net worth requirements
Household income threshold requirements
Net worth requirements (excluding principal property and qualified retirement savings)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Taxpayers must apply for the State Homeowners Tax Credit through the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). There is no separate application for the County Supplement. Applications can be submitted online or through SDAT. Eligible taxpayers automatically receive the County Supplement if they qualify for the State HOTC. Applications should be submitted by October 1st to be applicable for that tax year. For additional assistance, call 1-800-944-7403 or visit the SDAT program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit for Spouse of Fallen Law Enforcement Officer or Rescue Worker
structured_extraction.program_description: This tax credit provides full property tax relief to surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers or fallen rescue workers who meet specific ownership and residency requirements. The credit covers 100% of the County real property tax on the dwelling of a surviving spouse (who has not remarried).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit is 100% of the County real property tax on the dwelling of a surviving spouse (who has not remarried) of a fallen law enforcement officer or fallen rescue worker, if: (1) The dwelling was owned by the fallen law enforcement officer or rescue worker at the time of their death; or (2) The fallen officer or worker or surviving spouse was domiciled in Maryland as of the death date, and the dwelling was acquired by the surviving spouse within 2 years of the death; or (3) The dwelling was acquired after the surviving spouse qualified for a credit for a former dwelling under conditions 1 or 2 above.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full property tax relief for surviving spouse dwellings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland

Dwelling owned by fallen officer or worker at time of death, OR acquired within 2 years if spouse or officer was domiciled in Maryland at time of death
Maryland domicile requirement must be met at time of officer's or worker's death
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application for the tax credit should be submitted to the Division of Treasury by April 1 to receive the tax credit for the next taxable year.

structured_extraction.program_name: WMATA PILOT (Payment in Lieu of Taxes) - Accelerate Housing Development at Metro Rail Stations
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax incentive program that exempts new high-density residential developments built on property leased from the Washington Metro Transit Authority (WMATA) at metro stations throughout Montgomery County from all County property taxes for their first 15 years, provided they meet affordable housing requirements. The program aims to accelerate housing development to meet the County's ten-year housing goals and create economic development opportunities near metro stations. Property owners must still pay all State real property taxes, municipal taxes, and other applicable fees unless waived.

Properties must include at least 50 percent rental housing with at least 25 percent of rental units reserved as moderately priced dwelling units (MPDUs) for individuals with incomes at 50 percent or less of area median income. Additionally, 25 percent of workers hired for construction must be county residents.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and tax exemption on County real property taxes for new high-density rental residential developments near metro stations

structured_extraction.program_name: Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) Stormwater Management Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A credit program that reduces property owners' Water Quality Protection Charge by up to 60-80% (up to 100% for properties treating offsite stormwater) if they own and maintain on-site stormwater management practices such as rain gardens, rain barrels, permeable pavement, green roofs, conservation landscaping, dry wells, grass swales, and other approved water management systems. Credits are based on the volume of water captured or treated by the stormwater management system. For single-family residential properties, credits can reach up to 80%. For non-residential and multifamily residential properties, credits are 60-80% for environmental site design (ESD) practices or 45-60% for non-ESD practices. Stormwater management practices capture and treat runoff to prevent direct flow into storm drains or streams, remove pollutants, protect public health, reduce flooding risk, and prevent stream damage and erosion. This property tax credit is available to residential, agricultural, nonprofit, business, and government property owners who own and maintain eligible on-site stormwater management practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit (reduction) of up to 60-80% off the annual Water Quality Protection Charge for property owners who install and maintain eligible stormwater management practices. For single-family residential properties: up to 80% credit reduction. For non-residential and multifamily residential properties: 60-80% credit for environmental site design (ESD) practices or 45-60% credit for non-ESD practices. Up to 100% credit is available for properties treating offsite stormwater in addition to onsite required volume. The credit amount is based on the volume of water captured or treated by the system. Property owners must renew their credit application every 3 years and maintain the stormwater management system according to Montgomery County Code Section 19-28 and Department of Environmental Protection standards. For single-family residential properties, completion of an Inspections and Maintenance Checklist is required.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credits reduce the Water Quality Protection Charge on property tax bills. Eligible stormwater management practices include rain barrels and cisterns, rain gardens, permeable pavement, stormwater ponds, conservation landscaping, dry wells, green roofs, grass swales, bioretention, sheet flow to conservation areas, and other approved practices. The credit applies only to the WQPC bill and cannot be used for other purposes. Property owners maintain stormwater management practices on their properties to capture and treat runoff.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners apply using WQPC forms to request a credit through the online portal or by submitting forms. Applicants must provide account information (Property tax Account ID), verify whether it is a new or renewal application, and provide contact details including owner name as it appears on the property tax bill, physical and mailing addresses, telephone number, and email address. Applicants submit evidence of installed practices through photographic documentation and technical design information if practices are not permitted through Department of Permitting Services. Properties with permitted plans through DPS or RainScapes projects generally do not require additional submission of design information. For applicants with design data available, input the design volume into the Credit Calculator; if no design data exists, the Credit Calculator automatically calculates an Assumed Treatment Volume based on practice type and permit era. County DEP processes the application and verifies design treatment volumes. A site visit may be coordinated to verify the stormwater management practice. Applications and renewals are due by September 30. Credits must be renewed every 3 years. Consult the Water Quality Protection Charge Credit Procedures Manual for detailed guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) Stormwater Management Credit for Nonprofit Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: Credit program allowing property owners to receive credits off their annual Water Quality Protection Charge by maintaining stormwater management practices on their properties. Credits range from 45% (non-ESD practices treating 1-inch rainfall) to 80% (ESD practices treating full ESDv). Credits of up to 100% available for properties treating offsite stormwater in addition to onsite required volume. Based on volume of water captured by stormwater management practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a reduction off their annual Water Quality Protection Charge based on the volume of water treated by stormwater management systems. Credits are valid for three years and must be renewed. Credits can achieve up to 60% reduction with combined environmental site design and stormwater management, or up to 80% reduction if the property is completely treated by environmental site design practices. Additional credits up to 100% can be achieved for offsite stormwater treatment. Credit calculated as percentage of WQPC charge, up to maximum thresholds. Formula: WQPC Credit = Percent Credit × WQPC Charge (before credit).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30
structured_extraction.program_audience: IRS-designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that own property in Montgomery County and are exempt from property taxes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stormwater management practice installation and maintenance including swales, roof leader disconnection, dry wells, green roofs, rain gardens, permeable pavements, rainwater harvesting, conservation landscaping, bioretention, submerged gravel wetlands, and other environmental site design (ESD) practices. The credit reduces the Water Quality Protection Charge owed on a property.

Stormwater management practices must be maintained in accordance with Montgomery County Code Section 19-28
Credit must be renewed every 3 years
Design plans or design data must be provided, or the Credit Calculator will use an Assumed Treatment Volume
Engineer certified plans must include total impervious area, year of installation, facility size and units, and impervious area treated by stormwater management system, plus photograph of the system
Onsite impervious/pervious area data required
Hydrologic soil group data required (assumes HSG 'C' if unavailable)
Design volume information for stormwater treatment practices required
MDE-recognized stormwater management practices required
For offsite credit: minimum 60% onsite credit already achieved
Photographic evidence of practice installation and maintenance required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nonprofit property owners apply using WQPC forms available through the online portal. Applicants input property information including Account ID, owner name, property address, mailing address, telephone number, and email address. If design data is available, applicants input the design volume into the Credit Calculator. If no design data exists, the Credit Calculator automatically calculates an Assumed Treatment Volume. The calculator evaluates assumed or provided treatment volumes and prorates credit based on treatment depth provided relative to WQv (1-inch) or ESDv requirements. Applications are due by September 30 each year for renewal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Montgomery County Department of Finance that provides one-time financial support to help businesses and property owners offset expenses related to their first commercial lease, expansion of existing office space by at least 500 square feet, or conversion of vacant office spaces into productive use in Montgomery County. The program is designed to attract new businesses to the County and help businesses relocate to, expand in, or revitalize Class A and B office or flex space. Grant amounts are tiered based on eligible square footage of the signed lease: less than 7,500 square feet receives $8 per square foot with a maximum of $60,000; 7,501 to 10,000 square feet receives $10 per square foot with a maximum of $100,000; more than 10,000 square feet receives $12.50 per square foot with a maximum of $150,000; businesses in strategic industries receive $15 per square foot with a maximum of $150,000. Awards are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis based on the date all required documentation is received.

structured_extraction.program_description: An inclusionary zoning program that requires developers of residential projects with 20 or more units to make a percentage of housing units available at affordable prices for low- and moderate-income households. The MPDU program provides affordably priced homes—both new and resale—to first-time homebuyers and renters with moderate household incomes in Montgomery County and the City of Annapolis. For-sale units are priced from approximately $150,000 for a 2-bedroom condominium to $220,000 for a 3-bedroom townhouse. Through a random selection process, qualified applicants can purchase or rent an MPDU with long-term restricted resale or rental restrictions to keep it affordable for future occupants. Renters and first-time homebuyers with incomes up to 70 percent of the Washington Metro Area Median Income in Montgomery County (approximately $79,500 for a family of two or $99,500 for a family of four) or at or below 100% of median income in Annapolis are eligible. Control periods require resale and occupancy restrictions: 30 years for for-sale units (some resale homes have 10-year control periods) and 99 years for rental units. The program issues certificates of eligibility to qualified households that meet income and asset requirements. Over the past decade, more than 300 MPDUs have been produced annually. The program includes an online application portal where eligible buyers submit their purchase applications and provides comprehensive homebuyer education through required classes.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County requires developers to make a percentage of units available as MPDUs at below-market prices. For-sale units are priced from approximately $150,000 for a 2-bedroom condominium to $220,000 for a 3-bedroom townhouse. Units are offered to renters and first-time homebuyers with incomes up to 70 percent of the Washington Metro Area Median Income in Montgomery County (approximately $79,500 for a family of two or $99,500 for a family of four) or at or below 100% of median income in Annapolis. Buyers must obtain their own mortgage financing (minimum pre-qualification of $150,000 in Montgomery County). Homes are placed under a restrictive covenant typically lasting 30 years for for-sale units (some resale homes have 10-year control periods) and 99 years for rental units, during which owners must occupy as their primary residence, cannot refinance above the controlled resale price, and can only sell through the MPDU program at the established controlled resale price. After the control period expires, the owner may sell at market price but must share 50% of any excess profit with the jurisdiction. The program issues certificates of eligibility to qualified households that meet income and asset requirements and provides required training courses and an online application portal. Processing time for application review is 30 days.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Montgomery County: Step 1: Complete a pre-screening intake form and submit to the Greater Washington Urban League (GWUL). Step 2: Attend the MPDU Orientation Seminar (virtual, 2.5 hours, offered second and fourth Thursdays of each month in evening). Must have completed Orientation Seminar within past two years. Pass post-test and complete evaluation form to receive course completion certificate. Step 4: Receive email from MPDU office with instructions to access MPDU Application Portal. Step 5: Complete Application Tutorial (online) within the portal by validating attendance at previous classes. Step 6: Submit completed application form and required supporting documents via MPDU Application Portal. Step 7: MPDU staff reviews application (30-day processing time). structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit for Surviving Spouses and Disabled Law Enforcement Officers and Rescue Workers
structured_extraction.program_description: This tax credit provides property tax relief to surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers, rescue workers, or emergency medical services officers, and to permanently and totally disabled law enforcement officers and rescue workers. The credit applies to County real property taxes on dwellings owned and occupied as primary residences. Available in Montgomery, Baltimore, Cecil, Anne Arundel, Prince George's, and Charles Counties with varying credit structures—in Montgomery and Baltimore Counties, the credit equals 100 percent of the property tax obligation on the eligible primary residence and continues year to year without requiring further application. In Cecil County, the credit applies to the County portion of property taxes for surviving spouses of law enforcement officers who died from an injury or disease incurred during employment. In Anne Arundel County, the credit is also available for permanently and totally disabled law enforcement officers and rescue workers and equals 100% of total tax due on the dwelling. In Prince George's County and Charles County, the credit is available for surviving spouses of fallen officers. Eligibility requires specific ownership and domicile requirements at the time of death or disability determination.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County; Baltimore County; Cecil County; Anne Arundel County; Prince George's County; Charles County
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit provides property tax relief on County real property taxes on the dwelling of a surviving spouse (who has not remarried) of a fallen law enforcement officer, rescue worker, or emergency medical services officer, or a permanently and totally disabled law enforcement officer or rescue worker. In Montgomery and Baltimore Counties, the credit equals 100% of the County real property tax obligation on the eligible primary residence and continues annually without requiring reapplication. In Cecil County, the credit applies to the County portion of property taxes. In Anne Arundel County, the credit equals 100% of total tax due on the dwelling for eligible applicants and is applied only to County real property taxes after mandatory credits, supplements, and deferrals, and does not apply to State taxes or other assessments. In Prince George's County and Charles County, the credit is applied to property taxes for surviving spouses. The credit applies only to real property tax and does not include other charges on the tax bill. Eligibility requires one of the following: (1) The dwelling was owned by the fallen law enforcement officer, rescue worker, or emergency medical services officer at the time of death or disability determination; (2) The fallen officer or worker or surviving spouse was domiciled in Maryland as of the death or disability date, and the dwelling was acquired by the surviving spouse or disabled officer within required timeframes; or (3) The dwelling was acquired after the surviving spouse or disabled officer qualified for a credit for a former dwelling under prior conditions. For Anne Arundel County, if the property was not in Anne Arundel County at time of death, applicant must have Maryland residency established within 5 years of officer's/worker's death, and the current property must have been purchased within 10 years of death.

Applicant or fallen officer/worker must have established Maryland domicile within the timeframe specified in Tax-Property Article § 9-210. For Anne Arundel County, if property was not in Anne Arundel County at time of death, applicant must have Maryland residency established within 5 years of death and current property must have been purchased within 10 years of death.

structured_extraction.program_description: An elective partnership between Prince George's County and qualified tax-exempt faith-based organizations or other nonprofit organizations to improve water quality by treating and reducing polluted stormwater runoff. Participating organizations qualify for a reduction in their Clean Water Act Fee through three elective options: Option 1 provides a 50% impervious area fee reduction if the organization provides easement for the county to install stormwater best management practices and maintains them; Option 2 provides a 25% fee reduction if the organization participates in education and outreach campaigns or hosts environmental activities; Option 3 provides a 25% fee reduction if the organization uses certified landscaping companies and practices good housekeeping standards. The administrative fee ($20.58) per tax account applies annually and cannot be waived.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Energy Program - Energy Efficiency Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by Prince George's County Department of the Environment Sustainable Energy that provides supplemental funds to homeowners in Energy Resiliency Communities for residential energy efficiency improvements and rooftop solar photovoltaic system installation. Grants of up to $6,250 are available for energy efficiency measures (with no longer funding electric incentives; all-electric homes do not qualify), with up to $10,000 available for homeowner-owned solar systems and up to $2,000 for third-party owned solar systems. The program works in conjunction with EmPOWER Maryland energy incentives and utility company incentives to reduce energy costs and improve home efficiency. Grant funds are allocated with a maximum of $2,500 toward natural gas incentives and up to 60% ($3,750) toward air sealing and insulation. Solar systems must be a minimum of 2.0 kW with no maximum size limit. Low-income homeowners receive energy audits at a discounted rate with reimbursement, while market rate residents may pay $100 upfront for audits, which will be reimbursed. Grant funds are paid both as reimbursement of upfront costs and before panel installation upon receipt of invoice after grant prequalification. The program helps reduce energy costs and carbon emissions through comprehensive energy efficiency retrofits and is designed to assist single-family residents, townhouse residents, and condominium residents in designated Energy Resiliency Communities with becoming more energy efficient and installing solar on their homes.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Clean Energy Program provides up to $6,250 in grants for residential energy efficiency measures, of which $2,500 can be allocated toward natural gas incentives. Up to 60% of the total grant award amount ($3,750) can be allocated toward air sealing and insulation. The program no longer funds electric incentives; all-electric homes do not qualify. For rooftop solar photovoltaic systems, the grant provides up to $10,000 in incentive funds for homeowner-owned systems or up to $2,000 for third-party owned systems. Solar water heaters are also eligible, with up to $7,500 for homeowner-owned systems or up to $2,000 for third-party owned systems. Solar systems must be a minimum of 2.0 kW with no maximum size limit. Grant funds are paid both as reimbursement of upfront costs and before panel installation upon receipt of invoice after grant prequalification. The grant covers up to $100 cost of required home energy assessment. Low-income homeowners receive energy audits at a discounted rate, and the audit cost will be reimbursed as part of the grant. Market rate residents may pay $100 upfront for audits, which will be reimbursed. Professional services may be funded to address barriers to energy efficiency adoption. Eligible improvements include natural gas system retrofits and upgrades for energy efficiency. Program operates on first-come, first-served basis; incentives dependent on cost effectiveness and funding availability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family homeowners, townhouse residents, condominium residents, and other residential property owners in Prince George's County, particularly those in designated Energy Resiliency Communities who are customers of Pepco and/or Washington Gas. Program targets residents of single-family homes, townhouses, or individually-metered condominiums built before March 23, 2016.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential energy efficiency improvements such as air sealing, insulation, HVAC equipment upgrades, water heater replacement, window and door replacement, smart thermostat installation, duct sealing, appliance upgrades, lighting upgrades, and other energy-saving measures. Rooftop solar photovoltaic system installation and solar water heater installation. Professional services needed to address barriers to energy efficiency adoption. Home energy assessments and direct install weatherization measures. For condominiums: ENERGY STAR certified appliances are eligible, though air sealing and insulation are not.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nine designated neighborhoods in Prince George's County classified as Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs): Bladensburg-East Riverdale, Forestville, Hillcrest Heights-Marlow Heights, Kentland-Palmer Park, Oxon Hill-Glassmanor, Silver Hill, Suitland-Coral Hills, Langley Park, and Woodlawn-West Lanham. Address verification using the ERC Address Locator is required. Program is available to Pepco and Washington Gas customers living within these designated Energy Resiliency Community areas.
requirements_list: Must be a residential property owner in a single-family home, townhouse, or individually-metered condominium built before March 23, 2016
Must be a resident in a designated Energy Resiliency Community
Must be a utility customer of Pepco and/or Washington Gas
Must live within an Energy Resiliency Community area as verified by the ERC Address Locator
Must apply to the applicable EmPOWER Maryland incentive program (Home Performance With ENERGY STAR Program for market-rate residents or Low Income Energy Efficiency Program for low-income residents)
For solar systems, minimum system size of 2.0 kW required
Homeowner must select a contractor from the pre-approved vetted network of certified contractors or have the power to choose their contractor
Receive a comprehensive energy assessment from a certified professional using a whole-house approach
Selected contractor completes proposed work on the home
Recent utility bill (within 3 months) from Pepco and/or Washington Gas required
Home energy audit report from certified HPwES contractor required
Proof of application to EmPOWER Maryland incentive program
Completed IRS Form W-9
Signed Affidavit of Income with household size and annual gross income
Signed Terms and Conditions Agreement
Contract and itemized scope of work with equipment specifications (AHRI certificates, Energy Star labels, AFUE/UEF/SEER ratings)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Verify address in an Energy Resiliency Community using the ERC Address Locator. Select a pre-approved contractor to schedule and perform an energy audit as part of EmPOWER Maryland participation. The contractor performs the energy audit and provides a prioritized list of improvement measures. Homeowners elect which measures they want installed and sign a proposal. Complete Form W-9 (Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification) with correct legal entity name and TIN. Provide recent utility bill, affidavit of income, and proof of EmPOWER Maryland program application. Upon approval, the contractor completes the work. Grant application is completed by the contractor for the homeowner to sign, date, and submit with required supporting documents. Grant funds are paid upon receipt of invoice after prequalification.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program to evaluate and build a climate-smart local producers program that supports farmers and producers, particularly those of color and from underserved communities, in implementing climate-centric and climate-smart practices in farming. The program addresses marketing products grown using climate-smart practices and aims to reduce barriers to practice implementation on existing and new farms by combining the values of eating locally, utilizing on-farm climate-smart practices, supporting women and minority-owned farms, and increasing the availability of healthy food throughout Prince George's County. The program includes greenhouse gas reduction monitoring and analysis in partnership with Bowie State University. Funded by a $3.25 million grant from the USDA's Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $3.25 million grant from the USDA's Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities program supporting a five-year pilot program. The funding supports implementation of climate-smart practices, development of monitoring methodologies for greenhouse gas reductions in partnership with Bowie State University and University of Maryland Extension, building marketing strategies for locally-grown products from climate-smart farms targeting County residents, reducing barriers to practice implementation for farm owners and operators in underserved communities, and increasing the availability of healthy food throughout the county.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for implementing climate-smart farming practices, greenhouse gas reduction monitoring and analysis, marketing strategy development targeting County residents and climate-smart commodities, breaking down barriers to practice implementation on existing and new farms, farm operations that contribute to healthy food availability, and commitment to local production.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Commercial Property Improvement Program (CPIP) provides matching grant incentives to support the revitalization of underperforming retail centers and main street storefronts through assistance with exterior façade enhancements, placemaking, lighting, and major building systems improvements. The program aims to boost the economic performance of obsolete and underperforming retail centers, especially those in strong trade areas with high visibility, by improving appearance and enhancing the retail experience for Prince George's County residents. The program assists owners of smaller neighborhood retail centers, strip malls, main street retail space, and stand-alone retail storefronts to improve the look and feel of surrounding commercial areas and boost economic development activity.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive matching grants totaling $250,000 available for the FY2025/2026 funding cycle. Matching grant of up to 50% of approved project costs, with a minimum grant award of $25,000 (requiring at least $50,000 in total project costs) and maximum grant award of $125,000 (requiring at least $250,000 in total project costs). Program requires a 50% applicant match. CPIP reimburses construction costs on a cost-reimbursable basis after the awardee pays for improvements in full, with funds disbursed upon verification of the applicant's matching expenditure, work completion, inspection, payment, and contractor lien release. Architectural design and permit costs are not reimbursed until construction is complete.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Right of First Refusal Program: Multifamily Rental Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: The program gives Prince George's County the right to purchase multifamily rental properties with 20 or more dwelling units before they are sold to other buyers, with the goal of preserving affordable rental housing for low- to moderate-income households. Established in 2013, the program aims to prevent displacement and is codified in County Municipal Code, Section 13-1110, et seq. Prince George's County exercises the right to purchase multifamily rental properties or assign its purchase rights to a third party (such as a non-profit developer or community development financial institution) to preserve them as affordable housing. The County may provide financing through the ROFR Preservation Fund to support acquisition and preservation.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Prince George's County exercises the right to purchase multifamily rental properties or assign its purchase rights to a third party (such as a non-profit developer or community development financial institution) to preserve them as affordable housing. The County may provide financing through the ROFR Preservation Fund to support acquisition and preservation. The ROFR Preservation Fund provides flexible financing for acquisition, rehabilitation, and stabilization of rental apartment complexes with subordinate loans up to $3,000,000 at zero percent (0%) interest rate with loan terms up to 40 years and amortization up to 40 years. No loan payments are due prior to December 31, 2026. The program also provides property tax relief via PILOT (Payment in Lieu of Taxes) and establishes affordability restrictions for a minimum 30-year period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Multifamily rental property owners and pre-qualified developers on the ROFR Developer Roster seeking to acquire and preserve affordable rental housing; prospective buyers and developers interested in acquiring and preserving affordable rental housing; low- to moderate-income households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property acquisition, rehabilitation, and stabilization of multifamily rental properties. Property owners must provide written notice of sale intent. The County uses the right of first refusal to acquire or facilitate the acquisition of multifamily rental properties to preserve them as affordable housing for low- to moderate-income households. Funds may also be used for typical transaction costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All areas of Prince George's County, Maryland, including municipalities within county boundaries. The program was expanded county-wide in 2015. For ARPA-funded loans, properties must be located within Qualified Census Tracts (QCTs) in Prince George's County. For properties within municipalities, municipal approval is required.
requirements_list: Property must be a multifamily rental facility consisting of 20 or more dwelling rental units
Property owner must provide written notice to the Director of DHCD after entering into a bona fide contract of sale
For exceptions to the ROFR requirement, prospective buyers must execute a Written Agreement with DHCD prior to entering into a bona fide contract of sale
Borrower must be pre-qualified developer on the ROFR Developer Roster or approved by the Department as eligible participant
Department must have exercised or provided exception to County's ROFR
Affinity Agreement for minimum 30-year affordability period restricting rent and tenant income
Resident Empowerment & Community Support Plan with economic mobility initiatives required
40% County-Certified Small Business participation requirement for maintenance and capital improvements
30% County-Certified Minority Business Enterprise participation requirement
Local hiring goals for on-site staff consistent with HUD Section 3 requirements
Diversity and Equity Policy compliance for renovations and development per County Code Section 10-335
Annual compliance documentation submission
ARPA and Maryland DHCD compliance
Department-approved property manager required
Municipal approval for properties within municipalities
LTV up to 110% (up to 120% for high public purpose properties)
Owner must submit comprehensive ROFR documentation within 5 business days of contract execution (19 items including contract, site plan, financial statements, rent roll, inspections, etc.)
County has 60 days to exercise ROFR option from receipt of complete documentation
County has 180 days to complete purchase
Annual Financing Reporting from Borrower
Timely completion of required forms and reports for U.S. Treasury Department and Maryland DHCD
Supplier Diversity and Equity Plan approval by County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners seeking to sell a multifamily rental facility of 20 or more units must notify DHCD in writing after entering into a bona fide contract of sale. Owner must notify tenants within 5 business days of executing bona fide contract and submit comprehensive ROFR documentation to the Department by certified mail within 5 business days. The County then has 60 days from receipt of complete documentation to exercise its right to purchase the property or assign its rights to a qualified third party, and 180 days to complete the purchase. Prospective buyers seeking an exception to the ROFR requirement must contact DHCD to negotiate and execute a Written Agreement before entering into a contract with the property owner. Borrowers approved for ROFR Preservation Fund financing must submit plan documents for Department approval and provide annual reporting and compliance documentation.

Grants support energy and water efficiency retrofits for existing office and multifamily buildings located within PEPCO and/or Washington Gas service territories in Prince George's County.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides rental and utility assistance to eligible households experiencing financial hardship and housing instability due to or during the COVID-19 pandemic. The program serves two pathways: direct assistance to tenants who have received court documentation for eviction (court summons, judgment, Warrant of Restitution, or Warrant for Possession), and landlord-applied assistance for tenants in eligible census tracts meeting specific risk factors. Tenants must have household income at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI), with priority for households at or below 50% of AMI. Tenants with household income above 50% AMI must have eviction documentation to qualify, while those at or below 50% AMI do not require eviction documentation but are encouraged to submit available documentation. The program can provide up to 18 months cumulative of assistance for past due rent and utilities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental and utility assistance provided through two application pathways: (1) Direct rental assistance to eligible tenants facing eviction with court documentation, and (2) Direct rental assistance payments made to landlords on behalf of eligible tenants with household income at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI). Assistance can provide up to 18 months cumulative of assistance for past due rent, current rent, and utilities. Assistance is subject to available funding and DHCD review and approval. The final approved amount is determined by DHCD and is non-negotiable. Tenants with household income above 50% AMI must have eviction documentation (such as a court summons, judgment, warrant for possession, or active eviction case) to qualify. Tenants with household income at or below 50% AMI do not require eviction documentation.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Two application pathways: (1) Tenant pathway: Apply through the ERAP Portal at https://erentalassistance.princegeorgescountymd.gov/ or call the ERAP Call Center at (301) 883-6504, option 9. (2) Landlord pathway: Landlords coordinate with tenants to gather required documentation including rent ledger, lease copy, income verification documents, tenant attestations, and landlord information. Both landlord and tenant information and documents are submitted through the application portal. DHCD reviews the application and contacts applicants by email regarding any discrepancies or missing information. Upon approval, landlords receive a non-negotiable Rental Assistance Agreement and tenants receive an affidavit. Both must accept the final assistance amount determined by DHCD to receive payment. Work with your landlord to gather and submit landlord-required documents such as rent ledger, rental license copy, W-9 form, and banking information for payment processing. Call ERAP Hotline → Get Access Code → Apply on Portal → Screen for Prioritization → Assign to Reviewers → Conduct Review and Quality Control → Obtain Finance/DHCD Approval → Send to County Finance → Payment sent to Landlord.
