structured_extraction.program_description: A state and local incentive program that offers tax credits to businesses that expand or relocate within designated enterprise zones in Prince George's County. Two types of zones offer different levels of tax credits: standard Enterprise Zones and Enterprise Zone Focus Areas. Businesses can claim credits against state income taxes for hiring disadvantaged or non-disadvantaged employees, and credits against local property taxes for real and personal property improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In standard Enterprise Zones, businesses receive state income tax credits of $6,000 per disadvantaged employee (spread over 3 years: $3,000 year 1, $2,000 year 2, $1,000 year 3) or $1,000 per non-disadvantaged employee (one-time). Local property tax credits are 80% of eligible assessment for the first 5 years, then decrease by 10% annually for the next 5 years (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%). In Enterprise Zone Focus Areas, state income tax credits are higher at $9,000 per disadvantaged employee (spread over 3 years: $4,500 year 1, $3,000 year 2, $1,500 year 3) or $1,500 per non-disadvantaged employee (one-time). Local property tax credits on real property are 80% of eligible assessment for the full 10-year period. Local personal property tax credits are also 80% of eligible assessments for the full 10-year period.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2025 HUD Continuum of Care (CoC) Competition
structured_extraction.program_description: The Continuum of Care Program is a federal funding source from the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development that provides competitive grants to communities to support a comprehensive, coordinated approach to preventing and ending homelessness. The program promotes community-wide commitment to ending homelessness and provides funding for rapid rehousing of individuals and families experiencing homelessness, and serves persons experiencing trauma and lack of safety from domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking. It supports youth experiencing homelessness (ages 24 and younger, including unaccompanied and pregnant/parenting youth), minimizes trauma and dislocation caused by homelessness, and promotes access to mainstream programs and self-sufficiency. Funding supports permanent housing solutions through Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH), Rapid Re-Housing (RRH), and Joint Component Projects. Organizations can apply for competitive grants to support homeless assistance programs including shelter, transitional housing, permanent supportive housing, rapid rehousing, outreach, case management, and supportive services. The program operates on six pillars: equity, data and evidence, collaboration (foundations) and housing/supports, crisis response, and prevention (solutions).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funding through HUD to support homeless assistance programs. Competitive grants for Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH), Rapid Re-Housing (RRH), Transitional Housing (TH), and Joint Component Projects. Projects may include HMIS projects, Coordinated Entry systems, and specialized funding for DV Bonus, CoC Bonus, and YHDP. Permanent Housing Bonus: approximately $690,223 available; DV (Domestic Violence) Bonus: $544,115 available; YHDP (Youth Homeless Demonstration Program) renewal/replacement funding: approximately $188,000,000. Total funding approximately $3,524,000,000. Funds support housing, leasing, operating costs, tenant-based/project-based/sponsor-based rental assistance, supportive services including health care, behavioral health, substance use treatment, emergency transfer assistance, and case management for homeless individuals and families. Eligible costs include emergency transfer assistance (moving costs, travel, security deposits, utilities, housing fees), supportive services (substance use disorder and mental health treatment, mainstream benefits assistance, healthcare coordination), staff training, HMIS administration, CoC planning, and project administrative costs (limited to 10%). Specific award amounts, terms, and details are determined through the competitive application process.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH), Rapid Re-Housing (RRH), Transitional Housing (TH), and Joint Component Projects. Housing provision, leasing, operating costs, rental assistance (tenant-based, project-based, sponsor-based), and supportive services aligned with Housing First and Evidence-Based practices. Eligible costs: emergency transfer assistance, moving expenses, security deposits (up to 2 months rent), housing damage payments (up to 2 months rent), household cleaning supplies, housing start-up expenses (furniture, household goods up to $300), cellular phones, emergency shelter, transitional housing, case management, housing navigation, VAWA emergency transfer support, rural emergency lodging, staff training and professional development, HMIS administration and data contribution, CoC planning activities, Coordinated Entry systems design and implementation, mainstream benefits assistance (Food Stamps, SSI, SSDI, TANF), substance use disorder and mental health treatment coordination, new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation (capital costs), capital improvements including climate resilience and energy efficiency, project administrative costs (limited to 10% for most projects), and UFA (Unified Funding Agency) costs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal block grant program under HUD designed to create affordable housing for low-income households. Prince George's County is a Participating Jurisdiction (PJ) that provides gap financing for building, buying, and/or rehabilitating affordable rental and homeowner housing. The program assists in expanding the supply of decent, affordable housing for low and very low-income families through loans to developers, first-time homebuyer assistance, group home acquisition and improvement, and support for Community Housing Development Organizations. The program operates under Title 24, Code of Federal Regulations, Part 92.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance is provided to eligible projects and beneficiaries in the form of subordinate loans with simple interest at 2% during the permanent loan period and 0% during construction. Loan terms include up to $2,500,000 (exceptions may be approved), 40-year amortization from the beginning of the permanent loan period, secured by subordinate lien Deed of Trust, and prepayment allowed without penalty if in compliance. For HOME-ARP Assisted Units, financing can be up to 100% of Total Development Costs plus operating cost assistance reserve up to $45,000 per unit ($250/unit/month for 15 years) with up to 40-year term. Prince George's County receives approximately $3.5 million annually in federal HUD appropriation. Gap financing covers eligible costs including construction, acquisition, professional fees, soft costs, and project reserves. Annual payments due by April 30. Minimum 25-cent County match per HOME dollar spent and minimum 10:1 leverage ratio required.

structured_extraction.program_description: HOPWA funds support rental and emergency housing assistance through a voucher system to address the specific needs of persons living with HIV/AIDS and their families in the Washington, D.C. Eligible Metropolitan Area, which includes Prince George's County, Calvert County, Charles County, and neighboring jurisdictions. Housing Counseling Services, Inc. (HCS) administers the Metropolitan Housing Access Program (MHAP) as the centralized source for housing services and housing information. Funds are distributed using a statutory formula based on AIDS cases reported to the CDC, with three quarters of formula funding going to states and metropolitan areas with the highest number of AIDS cases, and one quarter going to metropolitan areas with higher than average per capita incidence of AIDS.

(HCS) administers the Metropolitan Housing Access Program (MHAP) as the centralized source for housing services and housing information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pathway to Purchase Home Buyer Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A first-time homebuyer assistance program that provides down payment and closing cost support to help eligible buyers purchase residential properties in Prince George's County. The program offers up to $50,000 in assistance through a 0% interest, deferred payment loan with a 10-year affordability period. Assistance includes down payment assistance, closing cost support, and mortgage principal reduction. The loan is forgiven after 10 years if the property remains the borrower's primary residence. The program is funded by the Federal HOME Investment Partnership Program (HOME) pursuant to 24 CFR Part 92. Financing assistance is provided through participating lenders, housing counseling agencies, and title companies to assist with home purchase costs and other homeownership-related expenses, with favorable loan terms available to qualified borrowers.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $50,000 in down payment assistance, closing cost support, and/or mortgage principal reduction through a second mortgage/deed of trust loan. The loan carries 0% interest with deferred payment terms. Funds are provided to help first-time homebuyers with home purchase costs. The loan is structured with a 10-year affordability period with graduated recapture provisions based on length of primary residency (100% owed if sold/transferred within 1 year; decreasing percentages thereafter; 0% owed at 10 years or more). Interest at 5.75% annual simple interest rate is only charged upon Event of Default. The outstanding loan balance is forgiven after 10 years if the property remains the borrower's primary residence and no recapture event occurs. Funds are disbursed at settlement and must be used only for down payment and closing costs. Funds cannot be used for tenant relocation activities, design/acquisition/construction of sectarian religious worship buildings, cash reimbursement for pre-closing repairs, or any purposes other than down payment and closing costs. The program facilitates home purchases through a network of participating lenders, housing counseling agencies, and title companies. Borrowers cannot refinance the senior mortgage without County consent and cash repayment of the loan.

Applicants must intend to occupy the property as their primary residence and are not investors or second home purchasers.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective borrowers contact a participating lender or HUD-certified housing counseling agency. Borrower completes 8-hour HUD-certified homebuyer education course and obtains Certificate of Completion. Buyer obtains executed sales contract and secures conditional first mortgage loan approval. Borrower completes Pathway to Purchase Loan Application and gathers required documentation including income verification, HUD Income Calculation Worksheet, property appraisal, termite inspection, and valid identification. Property undergoes HQS inspection by approved inspector. Complete application package submitted to the contact person via email with all required documents and completed Lender Submission Checklist. Lender certifies compliance with subprime mortgage lending standards. Seller completes required affidavits. Upon approval, funds are provided through participating lender as second mortgage/deed of trust loan. Property must pass final verified move-in inspection before loan closure. Borrower files application with County. Document execution with notarization and annual certification process required.

Participants receive a year-long program with three phases: Phase 1 (weekly sessions), Phase 2 (bi-weekly sessions), and Phase 3 (every four weeks). Each session is led by a trained lifestyle coach and includes support from other participants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A healthcare transformation program that collaborates with medical care practices to improve health outcomes for patients with or at risk for diabetes, hypertension, or heart disease. The program provides care coordination, technical assistance, and community health worker support to help practices prevent and manage chronic diseases. structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Solar Energy Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps Prince George's County residents and businesses make solar energy more affordable by providing financial assistance for installing solar photovoltaic panels and solar water heater systems. The program is conducted as a research pilot targeting nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities, with awards made on a first-come, first-served and rolling basis. Federally-funded through the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant Program (EECBG) under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL) from the U.S. Department of Energy State Energy Program. Grant amounts vary depending on whether the applicant is in an Energy Resiliency Community or elsewhere in the county, and whether the system is homeowner-owned or third-party owned. For homeowner-owned systems, grant awards up to $10,000 cover eligible costs of installing a solar photovoltaic system for residents in Energy Resiliency Communities, $5,000 for other homeowner-owned systems county-wide, and up to $2,000 for purchasing and installing a solar power outlet in case of grid failure. For solar water heaters, homeowner-owned systems receive up to $7,500, while third-party owned systems receive up to $2,000 for solar PV installation and up to $2,000 for a solar power outlet. Funding is available on a rolling basis to help residents install solar systems after successfully implementing energy-efficiency measures. Limited awards are available. The grant works in conjunction with state energy incentives and utility company incentives. The program also includes energy efficiency grant components providing up to $6,250 to $7,500 for residential energy efficiency improvements in designated Energy Resiliency Communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides financial assistance to help residents and businesses adopt and install solar photovoltaic panels and solar water heater systems. For homeowner-owned rooftop solar photovoltaic systems, grant awards are $10,000 for Pepco customers located in an Energy Resiliency Community (ERC), or $5,000 for all other homeowner-owned rooftop solar photovoltaic systems in the county. For solar water heaters, homeowner-owned systems receive up to $7,500; third-party owned systems up to $2,000. For third-party owned solar PV systems, grant awards up to $2,000 cover eligible costs of solar PV installation. Grant awards up to $2,000 are available for purchasing and installing a solar power outlet in case of grid failure. Solar systems must be a minimum of 2.0 kW with no maximum size limit and must maintain minimum 70% Total Solar Resource Fraction across array with expected reduction in annual electricity costs of at least 10% and minimum 800 kWh annual production per installed kW. Eligible costs include parts, components, and accessory equipment necessary to operate and install the device, professional services needed to address barriers to energy efficiency adoption, up to 15-20% for ancillary costs such as tree trimming, service panel upgrades, roof repairs, mold remediation, and safety measures. Up to 15 percent of the grant award can be spent on reasonable measures to facilitate installation. Funding is contingent upon prior successful implementation of energy-efficiency measures for residents in Energy Resiliency Communities or application to applicable EmPOWER Maryland incentive programs. For condominiums, ENERGY STAR certified appliances are eligible. Awards are available on a first-come, first-served and rolling basis with a limited number of awards available. The grant works in conjunction with state energy incentives and utility company incentives. Grant funds are paid both as reimbursement of upfront costs and before panel installation upon receipt of invoice after grant prequalification. Home energy assessments up to $100 included in total award. Low-income homeowners receive energy audits at a discounted rate with reimbursement as part of the grant; market rate residents pay $100 upfront for audits which will be reimbursed. Minimum 10-year workmanship warranty required; minimum 25-year manufacturer material warranty for photovoltaic modules; minimum 10-year manufacturer warranty for inverters. All major system components must be new, not rebuilt or refurbished. Subject to Buy America Requirements for iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials. Davis-Bacon Act compliance required for construction work over $2,000. Energy efficiency grant component provides up to $6,250 to $7,500 for residential energy efficiency improvements including air sealing, insulation, HVAC service/repair, water heating, lighting, duct sealing, and ENERGY STAR certified appliances, with up to $2,500 allocated for natural gas incentives and up to 50-60% for air sealing and insulation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis: February 10, 2025, through August 15, 2025, and November 10, 2025, through February 27, 2026 (may be extended depending on funding availability)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents and homeowners in single-family residences, townhouses (dwelling units where you own the roof), and individually-metered condominiums (built prior to March 23, 2016) located in nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities, as well as other homeowners and businesses throughout the county interested in adopting solar energy. Particularly Pepco and Washington Gas utility customers who have completed energy-efficiency measures or are considering solar installation. Includes both low-income and market-rate homeowners with priority given to low and moderate-income residents per funding source requirements. Those who have not previously received a Solar Energy Grant from Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of solar photovoltaic panels and solar water heater systems on residential and commercial properties; installation of new rooftop solar photovoltaic systems through cash purchase, loan, or financing arrangements; solar energy adoption and installation; parts, components, and accessory equipment necessary to operate and install solar devices; reasonable measures to facilitate installation such as tree trimming, service panel upgrades, roof repairs, mold remediation, and safety measures; solar power outlets in case of grid failure; home energy assessment costs; professional services needed to address barriers to energy efficiency adoption. Does NOT fund battery or energy storage components. Subject to Buy America Requirements for iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials. Energy efficiency improvements including air sealing, duct sealing, insulation, water heating systems, lighting, HVAC service/repair and equipment, comprehensive remodeling, and ENERGY STAR certified appliances.

Residents located in an Energy Resiliency Community and who are Pepco or Washington Gas utility customers receive priority consideration with higher grant amounts. Address verification using the ERC Address Locator is required. All homeowners in Prince George's County are eligible for solar grants on a first-come, first-served basis. Systems must remain in Prince George's County for 10 years following installation. Property must be served by Pepco (electric) and/or Washington Gas (natural gas) utilities.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Verify address in an Energy Resiliency Community using the ERC Address Locator and confirm eligibility by verifying residency, property type, utility service, and prior grant receipt. Scan for eligibility by confirming residency, property type, and utility provider. Step 2: Residents in Energy Resiliency Communities must first complete energy-efficiency upgrades through applicable energy efficiency programs or apply to the applicable EmPOWER Maryland incentive program (Home Performance With ENERGY STAR Program for market-rate residents or Low Income Energy Efficiency Program for low-income residents). Note: electric incentives no longer funded; all-electric homes do not qualify. Step 3: Select a pre-approved contractor with NABCEP PVIP certification from the Maryland Solar Access Program list or from the vetted network to schedule and perform a comprehensive energy audit as part of EmPOWER Maryland participation. Step 4: The contractor performs the comprehensive energy audit using a whole-house approach and provides a prioritized list of improvement measures. Step 5: Homeowners elect which measures they want installed and sign a proposal. Step 6: Upon successful completion of energy-efficiency measures addressing findings from audit, residents may apply for solar PV grants. Step 7: Obtain financial assistance information and explore additional financing options including Federal Tax Credit coordination. Step 8: Find an eligible solar contractor from the Maryland Solar Access Program list. Step 9: Compile and submit prequalification application materials including: completed grant application, invoice template, recent electricity bill, contractor qualifications and NABCEP PVIP certification, solar analysis, proposal, contractual agreement, and affidavit signed under oath (with witness signature; can be contractor performing service, need not be notary public). Applicant must provide full name, address, city, state, zip, phone number(s), email address, income information, and complete IRS Form W-9 with correct Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). Step 10: County reviews documents within approximately 30 business days and sends prequalification notice. Step 11: Applicant has 2 weeks to accept grant award. Step 12: Installation must be completed within 4-6 months of prequalification approval with all necessary permits obtained. Step 13: After installation, submit final invoice, Utility Authorization to Operate letter, permits, inspection stickers, installation photos, proof of PSC registration, and proof of one month of solar generation. Step 14: County conducts final site visit and verification within approximately 15 business days. Step 15: Grant funds are paid upon receipt of invoice after grant prequalification and verification of completed work. Waiver requests for Buy America Requirements must be submitted in writing to the Contracting Officer with processing time up to 90 calendar days. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from February 10 through August 15, 2025, and November 10, 2025, through February 27, 2026 (deadlines may be extended depending on funding availability and research progress). Work completion deadline is April 30, 2026 (Federal Period of Performance). Early submission strongly encouraged due to limited funding and first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Stormwater Stewardship Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Stormwater Stewardship Grant Program provides competitive grants to support community-wide climate resilience, water quality improvement, and address local flooding through focused outreach, community engagement, and installation of small to medium-scale green infrastructure practices. Established in 2012 as the Stormwater Management Retrofit Program and expanded in 2013 with the Local Watershed Protection and Restoration Fund, the program funds on-the-ground restoration and program activities that improve communities and water quality while engaging county residents in the restoration and protection of local waterways. Eligible activities include water quality improvement, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education, trash reduction in the Anacostia River, and installation of green infrastructure practices such as cisterns, rain gardens, conservation landscaping, and pavement removal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants are awarded to qualified tax-exempt or other 501(c) nonprofit organizations, municipalities, faith-based organizations, educational institutions, community associations, civic groups, homeowners, and businesses for stormwater management and restoration projects. Grants fund Community Stormwater Management initiatives that include outreach, community engagement, water quality improvement, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education, trash reduction projects, and installation of small to medium-scale green infrastructure practices. Cash and in-kind match are not required but are considered favorably in the review process.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stormwater management capital improvement projects, public education and outreach related to stormwater management or stream and wetland restoration, restoration and protection of local waterways, water quality improvement, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education, and trash reduction projects in the Anacostia watershed

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal housing program that provides rental assistance vouchers tied to specific affordable housing properties throughout Prince George's County. Unlike tenant-based vouchers, PBV assistance is attached to designated units at approved properties and remains with the unit if a family moves out. The program provides rental assistance to eligible low-income households, enabling them to afford rent at designated project-based properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance is provided to eligible households at designated properties. Assistance covers a portion of the rent at specific approved properties where units are available. Selected applicants are placed on a waitlist and receive instructions on eligibility verification and required documentation. Eligibility is based on household income, family size, and the size of the available rental unit.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply online through the Rent Café portal during the open application period. Once selected from the waitlist for a specific unit, applicants are referred to complete the property's application and screening process. After landlord approval, the application is reviewed by HAPGC for program eligibility.

This government-funded program provides rental housing to low-income households in privately owned and managed rental units through project-based vouchers. The subsidy stays with the building; when a tenant moves out, rental assistance ends. Most units' rental cost is 30% of household adjusted gross income. Available housing types include single-family homes, townhomes, or apartments.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County offers rebates to property owners, nonprofit organizations, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, housing cooperatives, and commercial entities who install approved stormwater management practices that improve stormwater runoff quality, reduce runoff quantity, and enhance local waterways and build climate resilience. The program supports installation of practices such as cisterns, conservation landscaping, green roofs, permeable pavement, rain barrels, rain gardens, urban tree canopy, and pavement removal to manage stormwater. Tree canopy projects provide rebates up to $150 per tree for the purchase and planting of native trees at residential or commercial properties. The program is implemented by the Stormwater Management Division in partnership with the Chesapeake Bay Trust. Contractors who have completed the Rain Check Rebate Contractor Training Course are listed on the county's completion list. Rebates are provided on a first-come, first-served basis with lifetime limits of $6,000 for residential properties and $20,000 for commercial properties, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, multi-family dwellings, and nonprofit organizations.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates are provided based on the type of stormwater management practice installed or tree purchase. Residential properties can receive up to $6,000 in lifetime rebates for stormwater practices. Commercial properties, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, multi-family dwellings, and nonprofit organizations can receive up to $20,000 in lifetime rebates for stormwater practices. Specific rebate amounts vary: cisterns earn $2 per gallon stored (250 gallon minimum); green roofs earn $10 per square foot ($20 per square foot for more than 6 inches of planting material on commercial properties); pavement removal earns $6 per square foot; permeable pavement earns $12 per square foot; rain barrels earn $2 per gallon stored (50 gallon minimum for residences, 100 gallon minimum for commercial/organizations); rain gardens earn $10 per square foot (100 square foot minimum); and urban tree canopy earns $150 per tree (minimum 5-foot height). Native trees are reimbursed up to $150 per tree for residential or commercial properties. Rebate amounts cannot exceed the project cost. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline specified; program accepting applications on ongoing basis. Trees must be planted between October 1 and May 1.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, businesses, nonprofit entities, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, multi-family dwelling residents, housing cooperatives, and commercial property owners in Prince George's County seeking to improve stormwater runoff quality, reduce quantity, enhance urban tree canopy and build climate resilience.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of stormwater management practices including cisterns, conservation landscaping, green roofs, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrels, rain gardens, and urban tree canopy enhancements on residential or commercial properties; purchase of native trees for planting on residential or commercial properties to manage stormwater and build climate resilience.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County unincorporated areas. Properties must be located in Prince George's County, Maryland. Residents of the City of Bowie, Town of Cheverly, Town of University Park, and City of College Park are not eligible for most projects; however, residents of the City of Bowie are not eligible for any projects as it manages its stormwater program independently. The Town of Cheverly, Town of University Park, and the City of College Park offer their own tree rebate programs; properties in these areas are eligible for cistern, green roof, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrel, and rain garden programs but are not eligible for urban tree canopy projects. Property cannot be located within a municipality that has a similar stormwater management rebate program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that encourages revitalization in existing communities by providing property tax relief on the increased assessed value created by qualified real property improvements. The program applies to construction, reconstruction, or extension of non-residential structures, residential structures, and new single-family homes in Revitalization Tax Credit Districts established by Prince George's County Council. Non-residential properties receive a tax credit of 100% of county property tax on increased assessment in year 1, then 80%, 60%, 40%, and 20% in years 2-5. Residential properties receive 100% in year 1, then 66% and 33% in years 2-3, with a maximum of $200,000 in eligible improvements per dwelling unit. The county phases in tax increases over time based on improvement type.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit on eligible county real property taxes based on the value of eligible improvements. Non-residential properties receive a tax credit of 100% of county property tax on increased assessment in year 1, then 80%, 60%, 40%, and 20% in years 2-5. Residential properties receive 100% in year 1, then 66% and 33% in years 2-3, with a maximum of $200,000 in eligible improvements per dwelling unit. Eligible improvements include construction, reconstruction, or extension of non-residential structures; reconstruction or extension of existing residential structures; construction of new single-family homes on razed, demolished, or vacant lots; and new construction in developments of less than 10 one-family dwellings. County Council approval is required for developments of ten or more single-family dwellings or multifamily units.

structured_extraction.program_name: School Facilities Surcharge Reductions and Exemptions
structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County offers reductions and exemptions from the school facilities surcharge applied to new residential developments or redevelopments. The surcharge normally covers anticipated increases in public educational services. Multifamily properties near transit can receive a 50% reduction (reducing the surcharge from $15,489 per unit to $7,745 per unit outside the Capital Beltway, or from $9,035 per unit to $4,518 per unit inside the Capital Beltway or near WMATA mass transit rail stations), and studio or efficiency apartments in eligible transit-oriented areas may be fully exempt from the surcharge. This incentive promotes transit-oriented development and affordable housing by reducing the cost burden on multifamily housing projects.

Studio apartments and efficiency apartments located within one-quarter mile of a metro, within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone, or in other limited circumstances are fully exempt from the school facilities surcharge.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive youth employment and enrichment program that connects young people ages 14-24 with paid summer work experiences at host organizations, community organizations, private sector companies, and government agencies throughout Prince George's County. Participants gain meaningful work experience, develop job skills, professional development, and career exploration while earning income. The program includes job readiness training, industry training, safety training, health protocols, and networking opportunities. Participants earn $13/hour (ages 16-17, maximum 32 hours/week) or $15/hour (ages 18-24, maximum 40 hours/week), with additional stipends of $300 (ages 14-15), $400 (ages 16-17), or $500 (ages 18-24) for completing 75% of training programs. Organizations can participate as host worksites or as sponsorship partners to support youth employment through financial contributions at Capstone Sponsorship levels ($5,000–$100,000) or Student Sponsorship levels ($1,500–$5,000 per youth at nonprofit locations). Sponsors receive recognition on marketing materials and social media.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program places youth ages 14-24 in paid summer employment positions from late June through mid-August. Participants earn $13/hour (ages 16-17, maximum 32 hours/week) or $15/hour (ages 18-24, maximum 40 hours/week). Additional stipends of $300 (ages 14-15), $400 (ages 16-17), or $500 (ages 18-24) are provided for completing 75% of training programs. Sponsorship partners can make financial contributions at Capstone Sponsorship levels ($5,000–$100,000, funding program curriculum, workforce training, and transportation) or Student Sponsorship levels including Fulfilling the Promise Partner ($5,000 per youth ages 16-22), Prince Georgeis Pride Partner ($3,500 per youth ages 14-15), or Transportation Partner ($1,500 for youth transportation). Host organizations can hire youth directly or serve as designated worksites. Sponsorships support transportation subsidies, technology access, professional development, and expanded work opportunities.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in hosting youth must complete the 2026 SYEP Partner Participation Survey by January 30, 2026. After survey submission, organizations can email SYEPPartners@co.pg.md.us to discuss next steps. Selected organizations will be presented with the appropriate agreement (Referral Agreement for corporate partners or Memorandum of Understanding for nonprofit and government partners). Organizations must then provide required documentation including Certificate of Insurance, IRS Form W-9, and Personnel Policy. Partner Information Sessions are held monthly from January through August 2026. Youth participants may apply March 1-31, 2026 and complete onboarding including Code of Conduct acknowledgement and worksite orientation. Participants work from late June through mid-August and earn wages for hours worked. Businesses can also sponsor the program by completing a sponsorship form, selecting a sponsorship level (Capstone or Student Sponsorship), and submitting payment to the Community Foundation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A mechanism that helps fund public improvements related to economic development, such as parking facilities, roadways, stormwater management, and other public infrastructure. When a development or redevelopment project creates additional tax revenues, the county can issue bonds to pay for related infrastructure improvements and finance those bonds through the incremental increase in revenue that the project generates. Within pre-designated TIF Districts, projects have increased certainty of TIF bond approval. The base-year assessed valuation for the area is taxed as before, and tax revenues from the incrementally higher assessed value above the base that is attributable to the new project are remitted to a special fund and used to pay debt service for identified improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county designates TIF Districts as pre-qualified and eligible areas for development projects. Within these areas, projects have increased certainty of TIF bond approval. The county issues bonds to pay for public infrastructure improvements (roads, parking, stormwater management) and finances those bonds through the incremental tax revenue generated by the development project. The base-year assessed valuation for the area is taxed as before. Tax revenues from the incrementally higher assessed value above the base that is attributable to the new project are remitted to a special fund and used to pay debt service for identified public improvements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Countywide program providing funds to civic, neighborhood, community and homeowner organizations, local municipalities and libraries to plant native trees and shrubs in public or common areas. Provides hands-on opportunity for residents to learn proper tree planting and care while increasing native tree canopy. Community-based projects and landscape initiatives support tree planting in parks, playgrounds, memorial areas, street tree plantings, and reforestation projects along streams. Beautifies the County one tree at a time.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided on a reimbursement basis with required 50% match (cash, volunteer hours at $25/hour, or in-kind contributions). Community-based organizations and civic associations receive up to $5,000 per year; municipalities receive up to $10,000 per year. Funds support planting native trees and shrubs, soil preparation and amendments, invasive plant removal, tree protectors and gator bags, protective fencing, and mulch. Cost per plant (including soil amendment, gator bags, and other expenditures) cannot exceed $150 for 5-foot tall/5-gallon trees. Technical advisory services provided on site selection and development of planting and maintenance plans.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded program that provides healthy supplemental foods and nutrition counseling and breastfeeding promotion and support for pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children under the age of five who meet income and nutritional risk requirements.

The program also provides nutrition education and counseling, breastfeeding education and support, and referrals to healthcare providers and community-based organizations. There are no fees for participation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A four-year STEM demonstration grant that provides high school students in Prince George's County with mentoring, skills training, tutoring, college preparation, job readiness training, paid summer internship opportunities, and work-based learning experiences in healthcare and information technology fields. The program prepares students for immediate workforce entry or college following high school graduation. Students receive college credits, college entrance exam preparation, college tours, and competitive scholarships for participating seniors heading to college. Internship placements are made at companies such as Lockheed Martin, CVS, Dimensions Healthcare, and National Institutes of Health.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students receive job readiness training, paid summer internships and capstone experiences, skills training, tutoring, mentoring, college entrance exam preparation, college credits, college tours, and access to mentoring from employer partners. Internship placements are available at major employers including Lockheed Martin, CVS, Dimensions Healthcare, and National Institutes of Health. A competitive scholarship is available for participating seniors heading to college. Students are notified of work assignments by April and begin internships in July.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Youth Homelessness Demonstration Program is an initiative designed to reduce the number of youth experiencing homelessness. The goal is to support selected communities, including rural, suburban, and urban areas, in the development and implementation of a coordinated community approach to preventing and ending youth homelessness. structured_extraction.program_description: A temporary and permanent employment program for young adults ages 18 to 24 who are residents of Prince George's County and former participants in the Summer Youth Enrichment Program (SYEP). Interns receive performance reviews and mentorship with potential for conversion to permanent hiring.

structured_extraction.program_description: A $50 million economic development initiative administered by Prince George's County and Queen Anne's County that provides loans and grants to eligible businesses to support economic development, job creation, business expansion, and redevelopment initiatives. The programs focus on expanding the commercial tax base, retaining and attracting jobs, supporting small and local businesses, promoting development and redevelopment opportunities, and growing key industry sectors. In Prince George's County, the EDI Fund provides up to $7 to $11 million per year from a $50 million one-time appropriation to support business expansion, job creation and retention, and strategic development projects, with financing at record low projected interest rates for projects that create a high volume of jobs. The fund also sets aside $1 million to help small businesses get lines of credit from traditional banks. To date, 44 projects have been approved with $36 million in awards generating $1 billion in private investment and creating or retaining over 12,000 jobs. In Queen Anne's County, the fund provides loans and conditional loans that may become grants if the business meets certain goals, assisting businesses in expanding operations, starting new businesses, or relocating operations. Strong consideration is given to businesses in Advanced Manufacturing, Agriculture and Seafood, Technology, or Hospitality and Tourism. Both programs are available through their respective county administrations and emphasize projects demonstrating significant economic impact and alignment with county development goals.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance provided through loans and grants to support business development, expansion, working capital, equipment purchases, real estate acquisition, business purchases, job creation and retention, small and local business development, economic growth and enhancement, and redevelopment initiatives. Land and building acquisitions, building construction and improvement, equipment acquisition, and working capital are also eligible uses. The EDI Fund provides up to $7 to $11 million per year from a $50 million appropriation. In Prince George's County, loans are provided with interest rates set on a case-by-case basis depending on credit and personal history, generally at competitive market rates or slightly lower, with record low projected interest rates for projects that create a high volume of jobs. An application fee of 1% of the loan amount is required after the application meets basic requirements. For loans up to $1,000,000, an upfront fee of $2,500 is due; for loans of $1,000,000 and above, an upfront fee of $5,000 is due with the balance due at closing. The balance of the 1% fee may be financed as part of the total loan amount. The Prince George's prime rate is 4%. In Queen Anne's County, loan amounts up to $480,000 may be provided to eligible businesses, with funding amount determined based on project review and available program funds. Funding is awarded as grants or loans based on project merit and applicant financial soundness. Conditional loans may become grants if the business meets certain goals. Disbursement is authorized by the County Commissioners following review by the Economic Development Incentive Fund Commission.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Prince George's County: Download an application from the website (edif.princegeorgescountymd.gov), fill out an online application, or pick one up from the office. Complete the application with all required sections and gather the necessary prequalification documents. Mail, submit online, or drop off the completed application at the office. Applications are reviewed for consistency with statutory goals and purposes, independent credit and financial analysis, and financial projections. The review process takes approximately 90 days. A business development specialist will contact you after the application has been reviewed. Check the progress of your application online at the EDI Fund portal. Businesses can also contact the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation for information about the application process and services. Applications are submitted to the Prince George's County EDC and FSC First for review and approval by the County Council. For Queen Anne's County: Submit application online or download and submit paper application. First, prepare an application package that must include a project description, the completed application form, financial projections, and other supporting documents. County staff review the package and submit it to the EDIF Commission for consideration. Application is reviewed by the Queen Anne's County Economic Development Incentive Fund Commission with disbursement authorization from the County Commissioners as program funding becomes available.

structured_extraction.program_name: CatalystQ: The Catalyst for Minority Business Excellence in Queen Anne's County
structured_extraction.program_description: A minority business training accelerator program designed to help minority-owned businesses and entrepreneurs in Queen Anne's County scale their operations and strengthen the ecosystem for minority entrepreneurs. The program is a continuation and expansion of a pilot program launched in 2023, expected to serve 5-10 participants over a 3-6 month program duration. Participants receive hands-on business coaching and mentoring, guidance on business planning and marketing, connections to local financial and professional services, targeted support addressing key barriers including access to capital, business knowledge, legal and regulatory compliance, and networking opportunities. The program provides micro-grants for strategic growth initiatives and professional assistance (accounting, legal, certificates, marketing, business planning). Mini-grants are not available for working capital or equipment purchases. Funding is provided through the Rural Maryland Economic Development Fund with up to $100,000 total award funding the program through December 2025. Training is largely in-person with possible virtual components integrated.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive hands-on business coaching and mentoring to guide development of business plans, creation of marketing materials, and establishment of relationships with local banks, accountants, insurance providers, and attorneys. Technical assistance includes accounting & bookkeeping, legal advice & services, marketing/communications/branding/PR, strategic & business planning, HR & payroll services, IT, website development, business funding pitch & grant writing, supply chain & procurement, e-commerce, and innovation/technology adoption. Entrepreneur support services include co-working space, business start-up training, mentorship programming, networking opportunities, workshops, business registration assistance, licensing training, access to capital & banking education, DEDI directory registration, government contracting readiness, and translation services. Each selected business receives micro-grants for professional assistance and strategic growth initiatives aligned with their mission and needs. Mini-grants are not available for working capital or equipment purchases. Up to $100,000 total award funding the program through December 2025. Largely in-person training with possible virtual components integrated.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enterprise Zone Commercial Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A ten-year credit against local property taxes available to companies that locate, expand, or substantially improve business properties within the Queen Anne's County Enterprise Zone. The property tax credit equals 80% of the difference between the base property value (assessed value prior to new construction or improvement) and the newly assessed value after the investment. For the first five years, the credit is 80%. During the last five years, the credit declines 10% annually: 70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, and 30% respectively. This credit is administered through property taxes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Ten-year property tax credit equal to 80% of the increase in assessed value for the first five years. During years 6-10, the credit declines 10% annually (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%). Not available to fast-food restaurants, convenience stores, stand-alone gas stations, adult entertainment, or gambling facilities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Queen Anne's County Micro Agricultural Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by Queen Anne's County Economic & Tourism Development in partnership with the Upper Shore Regional Council that provides periodic financial assistance to agricultural businesses and micro farms in Queen Anne's County. The program supports businesses looking to expand, diversify, or improve their marketing efforts, implement capital improvement projects, conduct agricultural research initiatives, or develop agritourism projects. Approximately $64,000 to $69,000 is available to fund applications per funding cycle, with grant requests ranging from $2,500 to $10,000 considered on a competitive basis. This is a cost reimbursable grant where grantees must complete a reimbursement request showing proof of expenses, with expenses incurred dating back to October 2021 eligible for retroactive reimbursement. Grant funding can be used for strategic marketing campaigns, technology innovation or implementation, climate resiliency projects, capital improvements for business start-up, expansion or value-added production, research projects, animal welfare improvements, and agritourism projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Fund (MAERDAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: MAERDAF provides grants to rural-serving nonprofit organizations, government entities, and rural community colleges that promote statewide and regional planning, economic and community development, and agricultural and forestry education. The program aims to increase the capacity of these organizations to meet rural development challenges and establish new public and private partnerships for leveraging non-state sources of funding. Eligible uses include agricultural technology transfer programs, educational facilities and workshops, educational seminars for rural leaders, public health programs, environmental education competitions, business development workshops, agricultural market access initiatives, community resource development, historical document preservation, combined heat and power systems, and other economic and rural development activities. Community colleges can use funds for training and technical assistance to small and agricultural businesses. The program also provides technical assistance to rural communities, particularly those applying to other programs like the Health Enterprise Zones. The RMC is particularly interested in proposals that address Agriculture, Energy, Rural Broadband, Healthcare, Youth Engagement, and Workforce/Economic Development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded to eligible rural-serving nonprofit organizations, government entities, and community colleges through a two-phase application process. FY2026 total allocation is $599,735 in General Funds. Maximum award is $45,000, subject to funding availability. Awards are highly competitive. The average grant over the program's life is about $18,000. Historical examples include $167,000 in total grants dispersed in Fiscal Year 2014 and $130,000 distributed among 15 selected organizations in fiscal year 2011. Priority is given to applicants that have secured matching funds from non-state sources, though matching funds are not required. Federal funds are considered matching funds. Unused grant funds must be returned by July 15 of the grant year. The program also provides technical assistance to rural communities seeking assistance with program applications and rural development initiatives.

Trade associations are not eligible. Rural communities seeking technical assistance for program applications and rural development initiatives. The applicant does not have to be located in a rural area or in the area it serves.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive grant program providing funding to support economic development and community projects in rural Maryland areas. Established in 2006 to address disparities in Maryland's rural areas, the program provides targeted investments to promote economic prosperity in traditionally disadvantaged and underserved rural communities. The program funds Rural Maryland Council activities, capacity-building grants to rural nonprofit service providers, regional infrastructure projects (broadband, water, wastewater, transportation, workforce housing, commercial/industrial facilities, GIS services, renewable energy), rural entrepreneurship development, agricultural development, workforce development, cooperative development, rural community development, and rural health care organizations. The program aims to raise the overall standard of living in rural areas to meet or exceed statewide benchmark averages by 2030 while preserving cultural heritage and rural way of life through targeted investments in economic and community development programs and regional cooperation.

Regional Planning and Development Councils receive grants with no match requirement for multi-county rural improvement efforts. Specific award amounts and terms are detailed in program guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to help foster growth in Wicomico County's emerging agriculture and resource-based industries. The program provides financial assistance to eligible agricultural and resource-based businesses through a partnership between Wicomico County, PNC Bank, and the Maryland Agricultural & Resource Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO). It supports both new and existing for-profit businesses involved in farming, forestry, seafood industries, agritourism, and the production, packaging, processing, or marketing of agricultural products. Grants are provided on a reimbursement basis with targeted grant amounts of $2,500 or less per applicant, with a maximum total grant not exceeding $25,000. The applicant must make a financial contribution of at least 50% of the project cost, meaning SWED and MARBIDCO co-fund projects with the business contributing the other half or more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to for-profit agricultural and resource-based businesses in Wicomico County through a cost-share model on a reimbursement basis. Targeted grant amounts are $2,500 or less per applicant, matched by MARBIDCO, with a maximum total grant not exceeding $25,000. The applicant must make a financial contribution of at least 50% of the project cost, meaning SWED and MARBIDCO co-fund projects with the business contributing the other half or more. Eligible uses include agri-tourism (new or expansion), agricultural business diversification (new or expansion), deer fencing, and other uses as determined by MARBIDCO. Ineligible uses include operating expenses, personal expenses, refinancing, loan payoffs, and vehicles.

Specific eligible uses include agri-tourism (new or expansion), agricultural business diversification (new or expansion), and deer fencing. Ineligible uses include operating expenses, personal expenses, refinancing, loan payoffs, and vehicles.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides subsidies to help eligible low-income households afford broadband and Internet service. Qualified households receive monthly service credits of up to $30 toward Internet and mobile services, or up to $75 per month if located on Tribal lands. The program is offered through a partnership with Comcast as Internet Essentials and Internet Essentials Plus, with two service speed tiers available: Internet Essentials (up to 50 Mbps, 4 devices) and Internet Essentials Plus (up to 100 Mbps, 5 devices). No activation fees and free equipment included. Eligible households must receive benefits from the National School Lunch Program, SNAP, Medicaid, Federal Public Housing Assistance, Lifeline, Federal Pell Grants, WIC, or other qualifying federal benefit programs.

No activation fees and free equipment included. The program provides subsidies to eligible households to help them afford broadband service through participating providers including Comcast Xfinity.

structured_extraction.program_description: A judicially supervised treatment program for individuals with substance abuse issues who have committed crimes. The program aims to break addiction, promote public safety, and reduce crime in the community by providing treatment, case management, and support to help participants achieve abstinence and become productive members of society. Court-supervised recovery program combining counseling/treatment with criminal case resolution, involving a minimum 12-18 month commitment with possible extension. The program includes judicially supervised treatment, regular drug and alcohol testing, case management, frequent court appearances, treatment provider services, recovery support meetings, employment and housing support, anger management, parenting and relationship counseling, job training and vocational/employment training, and education programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a minimum of one year of participation (typically 12-18 months) including judicially supervised treatment, regular drug and alcohol testing (random and scheduled, minimum 2 tests per week), case management, frequent court appearances, treatment provider services, recovery support meetings, employment and housing support, anger management, parenting and relationship counseling, job training and vocational/employment training, and education programs. Inpatient treatment and mental health treatment services are available. Participants are responsible for paying some fees for treatment and drug testing, including alcohol monitoring (SCRAM bracelet), in addition to standard probation and parole fees. Sanctions range from warnings to jail confinement to program termination for non-compliance.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested candidates submit a completed application to the Recovery Court Coordinator. The application is reviewed by the Recovery Court Team. If accepted, participants are notified of court entry date and may be placed on a waiting list. Participants enter the program on a voluntary basis and must enter post-plea or post-admission. The program involves four phases lasting a minimum of 30, 60, 90, and 180 days respectively, with participants advancing after meeting phase requirements and receiving ARC team approval. Graduation requires successful completion of all requirements.

The program is funded by the Maryland Office of Statewide Broadband.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive federal grant program that helps homeowners at high risk of flood damage reduce disaster losses by funding eligible mitigation measures. The program provides up to 75 percent federal funding for projects that reduce flood damage to homes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 75 percent federal funding with a 25 percent non-federal cost share requirement. Homeowners must contribute 25 percent of the total project cost to an escrow account upon project approval. The grant is offered on an annual basis, with funding amounts and specific project costs determined based on submitted proposals and FEMA availability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual basis; due dates communicated each year based on fund availability from FEMA
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County homeowners whose homes are at high risk for flood damage and are actively insured through the National Flood Insurance Program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible mitigation measures that reduce flood damage to homes, such as elevation, floodproofing, acquisition, or relocation of flood-prone properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County residents whose homes are located within a flood zone
requirements_list: Home must be actively insured through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
Home must be located within a flood zone
Homeowner must be willing and able to commit to providing 25 percent of the total project cost in an escrow account upon approval of the project
Elevation Certificate required prior to applying
Copy of NFIP Declaration required prior to applying
Documentation of previous losses due to flooding if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact EMA@stmaryscountymd.gov with all required documents and state your interest in applying for FMA grant funding. 2. Emergency Management staff will connect with you regarding the next available application cycle for funding and any additional requirements. The grant is offered on an annual basis and due dates are communicated each year. 3. Emergency Management staff will work with you to obtain project proposals and additional required documentation and will submit the application on your behalf. The application process may take several months. Once submitted, approval may take approximately one year, and if approved, it may take an additional year for funding to be released.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding and assistance for design and construction of non-structural shorelines, also known as living shorelines, which consist of small stone structures with sand and marsh grasses planted behind to create stable buffers and protect property along shorelines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County shoreline properties.
requirements_list: Property owner must be experiencing shoreline erosion on their property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners should contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Chesapeake and Coastal Program's Shoreline Conservation Section. DNR will help determine which types of living shoreline devices would best fit the particular property and assist throughout the funding, design, and construction process.

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County program that freezes commercial property taxes for 7 or 10 years for owners who invest in renovations, rehabilitation, and upgrades of commercial real property in designated challenged areas. Eligible property owners who invest at least 10% of the property's assessed value with a minimum investment of $25,000 may qualify for tax incentives. The program aims to stimulate and incentivize investment in commercial real estate.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property taxes are held constant for either 7 or 10 years depending on the investment amount. If 10% to 15% of assessed value is invested (minimum $25,000), taxes are frozen for 7 years. If 16% or more is invested, taxes are frozen for 10 years. During the incentive period, property owners are not subject to increases in tax rates or assessed valuations. After the incentive period ends, property owners pay taxes based on the current rate and assessed value at that time. The total value of the assessment reduction cannot exceed 25% of the property's assessed valuation at the time of the award. The specific amount and terms of the tax incentive are subject to approval by the Commissioners of St. Mary's County and will be detailed in a Developer's Rights and Responsibilities Agreement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners located in designated challenged areas in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovations, rehabilitation, and upgrades of commercial real property, including exterior improvements to building facades, exterior painting and cleaning, structural improvements, mounted signage, canopies, shutters, awnings, screening of utility and storage enclosures, enhanced exterior lighting, replacement or enhancement of streetscape amenities including walkways, landscaping, bike racks and lighting, sidewalks, and new construction that enhances the building or property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Lexington Park Development District is the primary targeted area for revitalization. Projects in the Charlotte Hall Town Center and the Town of Leonardtown's Downtown area will also be considered. Projects must be in alignment with the Lexington Park Development District Master Plan and the St. Mary's County Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance. Commercial property must be located in a challenged area of St. Mary's County.
requirements_list: Must be a commercial property owner
Located in a designated or challenged area (Lexington Park Development District, Charlotte Hall Town Center, or Town of Leonardtown Downtown area)
In alignment with the Lexington Park Development District Master Plan and St. Mary's County Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance
Invest at least 10% of the property's assessed value
Minimum investment of at least $25,000
Property must be commercial real property
Eligible investments must be a one-time investment occurring within a 12-month period
Total value of assessment reduction may not exceed 25% of the property's assessed valuation at the time of award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Property Tax Challenge application with project details, including business name, property address, contact information, total investment amount, assessed property value, project description, implementation timeline, and economic benefit statement. Submission of the application is a first formal step; completion does not guarantee approval. The award of an incentive is subject solely to the approval of the Commissioners of St. Mary's County. If approved, a Developer's Rights and Responsibilities Agreement will be prepared and signed by both parties. Applications are available online through the program website.

requirements_list: Age 65 or older
Current St. Mary's County resident
Meet income and asset guidelines
Severely or moderately disabled per nursing assessment
At risk of entering nursing facility per nursing assessment

structured_extraction.program_description: Program for establishing Shore Erosion Control taxing districts to address erosion on private property for communities or groups of property owners. The program helps prevent sediment loss, reduce non-point source pollution, protect and restore tidal marshes, and protect structures and improvements through structural and vegetative projects.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DNR prepares need and feasibility reports; complete construction plans and cost estimates are prepared; construction is awarded and completed for erosion control projects. Matching grants are available for private landowners (45/55 matching grants where landowners pay 45% and the program pays 55%) and for eligible public land protection projects (75/25 grants where public entities pay 25% and the program pays 75%). Vegetative or non-structural projects consist of clean sand fill placed along the shoreline and planted with appropriate grasses to provide stable vegetative buffers and fringe tidal marshes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private property owners and groups of property owners experiencing shore erosion problems in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Shore erosion control construction and project costs, including funding and project management assistance for the design and construction of non-structural shorelines, also known as living shorelines, which consist of small stone structures with sand and marsh grasses planted behind to create stable buffers and protect property along shorelines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County shoreline properties experiencing erosion problems within established district boundaries.
requirements_list: Property owner must be experiencing shoreline erosion
For establishment of a Shore Erosion Control District, a Letter of Interest (petition) and an Exhibit showing a bold boundary around the lots to be included within the proposed District are required
75% of confirming petitions must be returned in support of the district
District assumes responsibility for all project costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 12-step process: Letter of Interest submission → DNR review → Need & Feasibility Report → informational meeting → Confirming Petition (75% threshold) → Public Hearing for District establishment → construction plans → final Public Hearing → construction bidding → escrow account → construction award → final Public Hearing for annual assessment. Property owners should contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Chesapeake and Coastal Program's Shoreline Conservation Section. DNR will help determine which types of devices would best fit a particular property and can assist with funding, design, and construction of living shoreline projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County Façade and Streetscape Improvement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that reimburses commercial property and business owners for a portion of expenses incurred when completing projects that rehabilitate buildings, storefronts, and adjacent streetscapes in designated historic commercial core areas, including Lexington Park (Downtown and Great Mills Corridor) and Charlotte Hall. The program aims to create positive visual impact, stimulate private investment, improve safety, and complement public revitalization efforts. Eligible uses include façade repair and restoration, signage installation and repair, exterior lighting, awnings, canopies and shutters, removal of security gates, ADA-compliant exterior accessibility improvements, and landscaping improvements visible from the public right-of-way or shared parking facility.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses up to 50% of eligible project costs, with a maximum reimbursement of $6,000 per project. Minimum project cost is $1,000 (for $500 grant) or $12,000 (for $6,000 grant). Funding comes from a Community Legacy grant from Maryland's Department of Housing and Community Development. One application is allowed per address per calendar year. Eligible projects include façade repair/restoration (cleaning, repointing, paint, window/door replacement, architectural detail restoration), signage installation/repair, exterior lighting, awnings/canopies/shutters, removal of security gates, ADA-compliant exterior accessibility improvements, and landscaping improvements visible from the public right-of-way or shared parking facility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and tenants with written authorization from property owner located within the Façade and Streetscape Grant Area in Lexington Park (Downtown and Great Mills Corridor) and Charlotte Hall. Eligible uses include non-residential, commercial, mixed-use, industrial, or office buildings, including vacant buildings zoned for these uses. Home occupation businesses are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cleaning and repair of building exteriors; cleaning and repointing of brick and masonry; exterior paint or like finishes; replacement of deteriorated or damaged windows, doors, siding, and framing; restoration of exterior architectural details for historic buildings; signage installation and repair (ordinance-compliant, attractively integrated); exterior lighting for signage; awnings, canopies, and shutters (removal, repair, installation); removal of security gates; ADA-compliant exterior accessibility improvements; landscaping improvements visible from the public right-of-way or shared parking facility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the Façade and Streetscape Grant Area as delineated in the Lexington Park Master Plan (Downtown and Great Mills Corridor) and the Charlotte Hall footprint of the Sustainable Communities designation.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the Façade and Streetscape Grant Area
Proposed work must align with eligible reimbursement projects outlined in Program Guidelines
Applicant must obtain estimates from licensed and insured contractors
Maximum reimbursement is 50% of project cost, capped at $6,000
Minimum project cost is $1,000 for $500 grant or $12,000 for $6,000 grant
One application per address per calendar year
Application must be complete and accurate
Work must be visible from public right-of-way or shared parking facility
Property must be non-residential or multiuse with commercial, mixed-use, industrial, or office uses
Tenants must provide written authorization from property owner
Home occupation businesses are not eligible
Structure must be legally used for or zoned for commercial, mixed-use, industrial, or office uses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Verify property location within the grant area using the provided map. 2. Confirm proposed work aligns with eligible projects in the Program Guidelines. 3. Obtain cost estimates from licensed and insured contractors. 4. Determine the requested reimbursement amount (50% of project cost, maximum $6,000, with minimum project costs of $1,000 for $500 grant or $12,000 for $6,000 grant). 5. Gather all required documentation by reviewing the sample application. 6. Complete and submit the application through the online form. Note: applications cannot be saved and returned to later, so have all information and documents ready before submission.
