structured_extraction.program_name: Statewide Specialized Transportation Assistance Program (SSTAP) / ADA Paratransit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive transportation program providing general purpose transit services and door-to-door paratransit service for elderly individuals and persons with disabilities in St. Mary's County. The program aims to provide efficient transportation and encourage coordination of services across providers. General purpose transit is available on demand routes in rural areas organized into five service zones with service to different locations on different days of the week, with Thursday service available to all zones. ADA Paratransit service provides curb-to-curb or door-to-door transportation for certified users with disabilities who are unable to use regular public transit, with on-call pickup and dropoff during normal public transportation operating hours using wheelchair-accessible vehicles with platform lifts. Service is also provided to four senior nutritional centers daily. The State provides $130,000 to $175,000 per year in funding to support the program, with an additional local match requirement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State provides between $130,000 to $175,000 per year in funding to support the program, with an additional local match requirement. General purpose transportation is provided on demand routes in rural areas between 10:00 A.M. and 1:00 P.M. on a first come, first served basis, with preference given to individuals with scheduled medical appointments. Riders pay $6.00 per round trip for SSTAP service or $2.00-$4.00 round trip for ADA Paratransit service, with additional stops costing $2.00-$3.00 each. Appointments can be scheduled up to 30 days in advance. Door-to-door or curb-to-curb paratransit transportation is provided to certified users using wheelchair-accessible vehicles with platform lifts. ADA Paratransit serves passengers within 3/4 mile of a fixed public transportation route, with service offered during normal public transportation operating hours on an on-call basis, Monday through Sunday. SSTAP serves passengers living beyond 3/4 mile from public transportation routes, Monday through Friday. Service is organized into five zones on different days of the week: Zone 1 serves Charlotte Hall, Golden Beach, Helen, Chaptico, Budds Creek, Wicomico, and Clements (Monday); Zone 2 serves Oakville, Loveville, Hollywood, Leonardtown, Avenue, Compton, and Mechanicsville (Tuesday); Zone 3 serves California, Lexington Park, and Great Mills (Wednesday); Zone 4 serves Piney Point, Ridge, Park Hall, Callaway, and St. Inigoes (Friday); Thursday service is available to all zones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elderly individuals age 60 and above, persons with disabilities, and low-income residents in St. Mary's County who do not have sufficient access to public transportation routes, particularly those unable to use regular public transit service
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Door-to-door or curb-to-curb transportation services for eligible individuals to medical appointments, senior nutritional centers, employment, shopping, personal errands, hair appointments, health department visits, and other destinations. Service is available between 10:00 A.M. and 1:00 P.M. on a first come, first served basis for general transit, with preference given to individuals with scheduled medical appointments. Paratransit users must call the STS Office the day before they wish to make a trip or by 5pm the day before travel, or email to make a reservation. Riders pay $2.00-$6.00 per round trip depending on service type with additional stops costing $2.00-$3.00 each or may require rescheduling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland, and surrounding tri-county area (Charles County and Calvert County for coordinated services). For ADA Paratransit: within 3/4 mile of fixed public transportation routes, operates Monday-Sunday. For SSTAP: areas beyond 3/4 mile from public transportation routes, Monday-Friday, divided into five service zones: Zone 1 serves Charlotte Hall, Golden Beach, Helen, Chaptico, Budds Creek, Wicomico, and Clements (Monday); Zone 2 serves Oakville, Loveville, Hollywood, Leonardtown, Avenue, Compton, and Mechanicsville (Tuesday); Zone 3 serves California, Lexington Park, and Great Mills (Wednesday); Zone 4 serves Piney Point, Ridge, Park Hall, Callaway, and St. Inigoes (Friday); Thursday service is available to all zones. For home or building pickup, locations must have a wheelchair ramp or an assistant to help the rider.
requirements_list: Be elderly age 60 or older, or a person with disabilities
Reside in St. Mary's County or tri-county area
Have a disability that prevents use of regular public transit (for paratransit service), documented by doctor, SSI/SSDI, Veterans Administration, TDAP, or other certification
Do not have sufficient access to public transportation routes
Live within 3/4 mile of a fixed public transportation route (for ADA Paratransit service) or beyond 3/4 mile (for SSTAP service)
Have an accessible home or building pickup location with a wheelchair ramp or available assistant (for paratransit service)
Present proof of age to receive senior discount fares
Complete and submit an Application for Paratransit Transportation (for paratransit service)
For ADA eligibility: Must be unable to board, ride, or disembark without assistance beyond driver assistance, or have impairments preventing travel to public transportation stops
Must be ready at scheduled pickup time
Must pay exact fare at time of pickup in cash, checks, or ADA tickets
Appointments must be made by 5pm the day before travel
Re-certification required every 2 years
Driveways must be accessible with safe turnaround for pickup
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For general purpose transit: Call the STS Office at (301) 475-4200 ext. 1120 or 1121 or (301) 863-8400 ext. 1120, or email SDispatchers@stmaryscountymd.gov or sdispatchers@stmarysmd.com to request service and schedule appointments up to 30 days in advance. For paratransit service: Complete an Application for Paratransit Transportation form (mailed upon request) and submit by mail or fax to (301) 866-6797. Application will be evaluated within 21 days by transportation supervisor and staff. Applicant will be notified within 5 days of evaluation. Eligible persons receive identification card and must re-certify every 2 years. Denial can be reviewed by Transportation Manager with appeal rights. Once approved, call (301) 475-4200 ext. 1120 or 1121 or (301) 863-8400 ext. 1120 the day before or by 5pm the day before each trip, or email to make a reservation. Seniors need to present proof of age to drivers. Special identification cards are available and issued by the STS Transit office at 44829 St. Andrews Church Road, California, Maryland 20619. Out-of-town visitors with ADA certification from their home system are limited to 21 days per 365-day period.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Waterway Improvement Program is a State of Maryland program administered at the local level through St. Mary's County that provides financing, interest-free long-term loans, and matching grants for marking channels and harbors, clearing debris from waterways, dredging channels, and constructing jetties and marine facilities that benefit the boating public.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complete project financing, interest-free long-term loans, or matching grants are available for eligible marine construction projects. Grants of 100% are available if the project benefits the general boating public. Matching fund grants (50/50) may be provided if the general boating public is not significantly benefited, with the State and County/residents splitting the cost. The maximum allocated by the State per year per project is $25,000. Property owners in eligible districts repay through special assessments over a loan term not to exceed 25 years. The County is reimbursed by the established Taxing District over a specified period not to exceed twenty-five years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with real property abutting natural or artificial bodies of water in St. Mary's County seeking to improve waterways and marine facilities; the boating public.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Marking channels and harbors, clearing waterway debris, dredging channels, constructing jetties and marine facilities, providing accessibility to sheltered water bodies, suitable anchorage conditions, water access for fueling, repair, dry storage, individual storage berths, or relieving congestion on waterways. Funding also covers engineering services, construction inspection, and future maintenance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grounded in a restorative justice approach to public investment, the Community Repair and Reinvestment Fund directs cannabis tax revenue from Maryland's Cannabis Reform Act of 2023 into community-based initiatives that benefit disproportionately impacted and low-income communities. The program supports initiatives addressing harms from disparate cannabis law enforcement, strengthening community well-being, expanding access to services, and building community capacity and leadership. It is administered locally by Talbot Family Network on behalf of the Talbot County Reinvestment and Repair Commission, with support from the Maryland Office of Social Equity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two grant pathways: Small Community Grants (up to $10,000 for targeted, time-limited, transactional efforts addressing immediate community needs; $50,000 total available) and Community Impact Grants (minimum $25,000 for comprehensive, transformational strategies addressing root causes and sustained community change; $150,000 total available). Grant period runs from May 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Funds support three priority areas: community-based services and supports, reentry/legal/stabilization supports, and economic opportunity/workforce development. Cannot be used for law enforcement agencies/activities or to supplant existing local government funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, and public entities serving disproportionately impacted and low-income communities in Talbot County, particularly Easton (ZIP code 21601). Target populations include children, youth, single adults, seniors, families, and justice-impacted individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early childhood education and quality childcare, afterschool enrichment, community-based services and supports, reentry/legal/stabilization supports, economic opportunity and workforce development, and other community-led solutions that strengthen individuals, families, and neighborhoods and create pathways to long-term opportunity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program focuses on Talbot County, Maryland, with the disproportionately impacted area identified by the Maryland Office of Social Equity being Easton, ZIP code 21601. While this area is prioritized, funding is available for other Talbot County zip codes and specific sites. The fund is administered locally by Talbot County.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that supports economic and social development in the Appalachian Region by merging local, state, and federal funds to implement job-creating infrastructure and community development projects. Funding supports projects aligned with regional economic and community development goals, including economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building. Maryland's integration includes five investment areas: Building Appalachian Businesses, Building Appalachia's Workforce Ecosystem, Building Appalachia's Infrastructure, Building Regional Culture and Tourism, and Building Community Leaders and Capacity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funds are merged with local, state, and other funding sources to implement infrastructure and economic development projects. Grants are provided for projects that align with one of five strategic goals: Economic Opportunities (entrepreneurial and business development), Ready Workforce (education, skills, and health), Critical Infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater systems), Natural and Cultural Assets (leveraging regional heritage), and Leadership and Community Capacity (building skills and organizational capacity). Additional eligible uses include technology development, energy projects, recovery ecosystems, downtown revitalization, and heritage tourism. All grants require a 50% local match, and matching funds must be identified and committed at the time of application. Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact, and funding may be reduced to allow maximum number of projects to be funded.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 3, 2026 for FY27 Project Submission
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible entities including local development districts, municipalities, and non-profit organizations in the Appalachian Region of Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties) seeking to advance economic development, workforce readiness, infrastructure, cultural assets, or community capacity. Also includes Appalachian businesses, entrepreneurs, workers, students, healthcare professionals, community organizations, and local leaders seeking to administer federal grant projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to economic opportunities and entrepreneurship; workforce education and health; critical infrastructure including broadband, transportation, water/wastewater systems, and energy; natural and cultural heritage assets and tourism; downtown revitalization; leadership and community capacity building; technology development; research facilities; healthcare services; construction purposes; and other job-creating infrastructure and economic development initiatives. Must include quantifiable outputs and outcomes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves the three-county Appalachian region of Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties) as part of the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland service area. Project proposals are submitted to local county offices or development districts, reviewed and ranked by County Commissioners, then submitted to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that generates jobs, helps retain existing jobs, and stimulates industrial and commercial growth in economically-distressed areas of the United States. EDA provides assistance to rural and urban areas experiencing high unemployment, low income, or other severe economic distress by helping communities overcome barriers to economic growth and building local capacity through strategic investment planning. In Western Maryland, the program is implemented through the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland's Comprehensive Economic Development Strategy (CEDS) 2023-2027, a five-year regional economic development plan designed to create or retain full-time permanent jobs and improve income characteristics for unemployed and underemployed citizens. The strategy addresses regional economic priorities including manufacturing, workforce development, infrastructure, broadband access, and economic resilience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EDA provides strategic investment planning and financial assistance to help distressed communities build local capacity, plan for new technologies, create job opportunities, and support enterprise development. Assistance includes Revolving Loan Funds, grant assistance, GIS assistance, education coordination, regional strategy building and planning, workforce training programs, broadband infrastructure development, manufacturing facility support, and economic recovery and resilience initiatives. The program makes strategic investments in physical, financial, and human capital to help communities stabilize local economies and create new opportunities for employment and private enterprise. Funding can support infrastructure development (water/wastewater, industrial parks, broadband, roads, bridges), workforce training and development programs, business incubation and support, equipment and facility improvements, and job creation initiatives.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Generally submitted by a deadline in April
structured_extraction.program_audience: Economically-distressed communities in rural and urban areas experiencing high unemployment, low income, or other severe economic distress. Local, state, and regional planning partnerships targeting assistance to economically distressed areas. Unemployed and underemployed citizens in Western Maryland, local businesses and manufacturers, educational institutions, small to medium-sized businesses, entrepreneurs, job seekers, workforce development organizations, healthcare professionals, community leaders, nonprofits, and local jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Strategic investments in physical, financial, and human capital; modern infrastructure development; local capital markets; technologies for the digital economy; job creation initiatives; enterprise development; and strategic economic planning. Specifically includes Revolving Loan Funds for startup and expanding businesses, business plan development, workforce development and training programs, broadband infrastructure deployment, water and sewer improvements, industrial park development and maintenance, educational facility and curriculum improvements, technology centers and makerspaces, healthcare access improvements, tourism and outdoor recreation development, downtown revitalization, and energy solutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program targets economically-distressed areas of the United States. In Western Maryland, the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland administers EDA assistance for Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties in the Appalachian Maryland region. Allegany County has an At-Risk designation with 70% ARC match rate; Garrett County has a Transitional designation with 50% ARC match rate; Washington County receives assistance through the regional economic development district.

structured_extraction.program_description: A revolving loan fund that provides gap financing to small businesses seeking to locate or expand in Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties in western Maryland. Established in 1980, the program facilitates creation and expansion of businesses in the Appalachian region. Borrowers repay loans and the money returns to the fund to make additional loans, creating an ongoing financial tool for job creation and retention. The program operates by participating with banks and other lenders.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides gap financing for small business projects. Loan amounts range from $10,000 to $500,000. Interest rates are tied to the prime interest rate, currently prime plus 1 percent with a floor of 5 percent. Maximum loan terms are 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets. Application fee of $250 (non-refundable) for loans over $25,000, or $25 for loans between $10,000-$25,000. Approved borrowers pay a 1.5 percent loan origination fee at closing (zero for loans $10,000-$25,000). The project must create or retain a minimum of one job for each $30,000 of RLF funds requested. Collateral required includes Deeds of Trust, Machinery and Equipment liens, Personal Guarantees, and Key Man Life Insurance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A ten-year federal tax incentive program established by Congress in the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 and administered by the U.S. Department of Treasury that encourages investors to reinvest unrealized capital gains into Opportunity Funds dedicated to investing in economically distressed communities designated as low-income census tracts. The program allows investors to defer, reduce, or permanently exclude capital gains taxes when reinvesting gains into designated Opportunity Zones through Qualified Opportunity Funds over a 10-year period. Investors can defer capital gains taxes until December 31, 2026, reduce tax liability based on investment duration (up to 10% reduction after 5 years, up to 15% reduction after 7 years), or receive permanent tax exemption on gains accrued after a 10-year investment period. Investments must be made within 180 days of the capital gain event and can include single asset real estate, company stock, and Opportunity Funds (O-Funds) that are privately-managed vehicles with at least 90% of assets in Opportunity Zones. These funds pool capital to support investments in small businesses and real estate to improve communities and quality of life for residents. The program aims to spur investment and entrepreneurialism that will result in business creation and economic prosperity while addressing challenges such as promoting economic vitality, funding workforce and affordable housing development, funding new infrastructure, investing in start-up businesses, and upgrading underutilized assets. Investments can be made nationwide into low-income or underserved urban and rural communities, with designated Opportunity Zones in Maryland including areas in Washington County, St. Mary's County, Caroline County, Garrett County, Anne Arundel County, and cities such as Hagerstown, Salisbury, Federalsburg, Denton, Odenton, and Brooklyn Park. Maryland has 149 designated Opportunity Zones across all counties.
list_of_prioritized_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three types of tax incentives are available for capital gains reinvested in Qualified Opportunity Funds: (1) Temporary Deferral allows deferral of capital gains taxes until the earlier of fund disposal or December 31, 2026; (2) Step-Up in Basis increases the investment basis by 10% if held at least 5 years, plus an additional 5% if held at least 7 years, excluding up to 15% of original gains from taxation; (3) Permanent Exclusion provides permanent tax exclusion of capital gains from investments held for at least 10 years, applying only to gains accrued after the initial fund investment. The program has no authorized cap on the amount of capital available. Investments must be made within 180 days of the capital gain event. Eligible investments include single asset real estate, company stock, and Opportunity Funds (O-Funds) that are privately-managed vehicles with at least 90% of assets in Opportunity Zones. Funds submit Form 8996 to the IRS for compliance. Program continues through year 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Defer taxes by December 31, 2026; program continues through year 2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: Investors with capital gains and businesses seeking to reinvest capital gains into designated Opportunity Zones, particularly those seeking to defer or reduce federal tax liability through investments in distressed communities. Fund investors making investments in Opportunity Zone projects in economically distressed low-income census tracts and investors and businesses seeking to invest capital gains in low-income or underserved urban and rural communities. Private investors with unrealized capital gains.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital gains must be reinvested into eligible property located in designated Opportunity Zones through Qualified Opportunity Funds. Real estate development, company stock purchases, capital investments and investments through Opportunity Funds in Opportunity Zone designated areas to support small businesses and real estate projects to improve communities and quality of life for residents and business growth. Investments in low-income census tracts including economic development, workforce and affordable housing development, new infrastructure, start-up businesses with export potential, and capital improvements to underutilized assets. Investment in Opportunity Zone property (stock, partnership interest, or business property) with QOF required to invest 90% of assets into QOZ property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Investments must be located in one of Maryland's or nationwide designated Opportunity Zones, which are low-income census tracts with individual poverty rates of at least 20% and median family income no greater than 80% of area median income. In Maryland, designated Opportunity Zones are located in Washington County, St. Mary's County, Caroline County, Garrett County, Anne Arundel County, and the cities of Hagerstown, Odenton, Brooklyn Park, Federalsburg, and Denton. Specific areas include Lexington Park in St. Mary's County located directly outside Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Opportunity Zone areas in Hagerstown, Federalsburg, and Denton, four designated tracts in Anne Arundel County (one in Odenton and three in Brooklyn Park), and in Garrett County including Keyser's Ridge Business Park (approximately 240 acres), Southern Garrett Business & Technology Park (4.2-acre site), and commercial pads along Francis Sanders Drive in Mountain Lake Park. Of 149 designated Opportunity Zones in Maryland, investments can be made nationwide into low-income or underserved communities. The program is effective for 10 years from designation. All counties in Maryland have at least one Opportunity Zone.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Opportunity Zone Map to identify eligible investment areas. This is a federal tax program administered through the U.S. Department of the Treasury. Investors work with qualified Opportunity Funds to make investments in designated zones. Final guidelines on fund formation and eligible investments are provided by U.S. Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service.

structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) and SBA Disaster Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Small Business Administration provides low-interest, long-term loans to help small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, homeowners, renters, and private nonprofit organizations recover from economic injury and repair or rebuild after disasters. Eligible entities can borrow up to $2 million for businesses and nonprofits, up to $500,000 for homeowners to replace or repair primary residences, and up to $100,000 for homeowners and renters to replace or repair personal property. Funds support working capital needs, normal operating expenses including payroll, accounts payable, fixed debts, inventory, and other bills during the disaster recovery period, as well as repairs, rebuilding efforts, and replacement of lost or damaged property. The program includes both physical damage loans and Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) for entities affected by declared disasters, including the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse in the Mid-Atlantic region and flooding in Allegany County and contiguous areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest, long-term SBA disaster loans with terms up to a maximum of 30 years, determined on a case-by-case basis. Maximum interest rate is 4% for small businesses and 3.25% for private nonprofits, with fixed interest rates for the life of the loan. Interest accrual and repayment begin 12 months after the first disbursement. Homeowners may borrow up to $500,000 to replace or repair primary residences and up to $100,000 to replace or repair personal property. Businesses and most private nonprofits may apply for up to $2 million to cover disaster losses not fully covered by insurance. Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDLs) up to $2 million assist small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, homeowners, renters, and private nonprofit organizations through disaster recovery periods. Installment payments are based on the borrower's financial condition. Funds can be used to pay normal operating expenses such as payroll, accounts payable, fixed debts, inventory, and other bills that cannot be paid due to disaster, as well as to fund repairs, rebuilding efforts, and replace lost or disaster-damaged property.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Physical damages deadline July 21, 2025; EIDL deadline February 23, 2026; December 30, 2024 for Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse impact and MD-20258 disaster areas

structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, sole proprietors, homeowners, renters, and private nonprofit organizations affected by disasters in disaster-declared areas, including the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse in the Mid-Atlantic region and flooding in Allegany County and contiguous areas. Eligible applicants must be unable to obtain credit elsewhere.

Funds can also be used to cover temporary loss of revenue due to the disaster.

structured_extraction.program_description: Low-interest, long-term disaster loans provided by the U.S. Small Business Administration for small businesses, agricultural cooperatives, aquaculture businesses, non-profits, homeowners, and renters in disaster-declared areas who sustained damage from qualifying disasters including the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse (March 26, 2024), flooding events, severe storms including an EF-1 tornado that occurred on November 2, 2018, and drought (March 15, 2025). The program includes both physical damage loans for repairing or replacing primary residences and personal property, and economic injury disaster loans (EIDL) for businesses and non-profits experiencing economic hardship. Loans support economic recovery, business continuity, normal operating expenses, fixed debts, payroll, repairs, rebuilding efforts, and replacement of lost or damaged property. Business recovery centers and online portals facilitate applications. The program helps small business owners and workers overcome temporary loss of revenue resulting from declared disasters and port disruption.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The SBA offers low-interest, long-term disaster loans with flexible repayment terms up to 30 years. Interest rates range from 3.25% to 4% depending on organization type (4% for small businesses; 3.25% for private nonprofit organizations). Interest does not accrue and payments are not due until 12 months from the date of the first loan disbursement. Homeowners can borrow up to $500,000 to replace or repair primary residences and up to $100,000 for personal property replacement or repair. Renters can borrow up to $100,000 for personal property. Businesses and most private non-profits may apply for up to $2 million (waivable if business is major source of employment) to cover disaster losses not fully covered by insurance and to help overcome temporary loss of revenue. Small businesses and private nonprofit organizations with substantial economic injury may qualify for Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) to cover operating expenses, fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills that cannot be paid due to disaster-related disruption. Collateral may be required; real estate is preferred collateral. The SBA sets loan amounts and terms based on each applicant's financial condition. Loans are administered through online portals, Business Recovery Centers, and direct customer service. Applications can be submitted online at DisasterLoan.sba.gov, by calling the SBA Customer Service Center, or in person at Disaster Loan Outreach Centers.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Filing deadlines vary by disaster: Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse deadline was December 30, 2024 (applications still being accepted); Physical damages deadline July 21, 2025; EIDL deadline February 23, 2026 (with 60-day grace period). For November 2, 2018 severe storms and tornado: February 5, 2019 for physical property damage; September 9, 2019 for economic injury applications. For March 15, 2025 drought: February 2, 2026 with a 60-day grace period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, non-profits, homeowners, renters, and private nonprofit organizations in disaster-declared areas affected by qualifying disasters including the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse, flooding events, severe storms, and drought.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replace or repair primary residences and personal property; cover business disaster losses not fully covered by insurance; support economic injury recovery and business continuity; overcome temporary loss of revenue; pay normal operating expenses, fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, repairs, and rebuilding efforts following disasters; meet working capital needs caused by the disaster. Loans are available even if the business or nonprofit did not suffer any physical damage. For EIDL, funds cannot be used for facility expansion, fixed assets, physical damage repairs, refinancing debt, dividends/bonuses, or loans to stockholders/principals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Disaster-declared areas as determined by FEMA, including the mid-Atlantic region, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, Allegany County, Carroll County, Frederick County, Howard County, Cecil County, Harford County, Kent County, Montgomery County, Washington County, and contiguous areas affected by qualifying disasters. Eligible contiguous areas include: District of Columbia; Delaware (Kent, New Castle, Sussex); Pennsylvania (Fulton, Franklin, Adams, York, Bedford, Fayette, Lancaster, Somerset, Chester); Virginia (Arlington, Alexandria, Loudoun, Accomack, Fairfax County); and West Virginia (Morgan, Berkeley, Jefferson, Hampshire, Mineral, Grant, Preston). Applications must demonstrate financial impact directly caused by the declared disaster. Multiple disaster declarations may apply (e.g., Maryland Disaster Number MD-20001 for Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse, Pennsylvania Disaster Number PA-20019 for flooding, and Maryland disaster declarations for the November 2, 2018 severe storms and EF-1 tornado, and March 15, 2025 drought). Recovery centers are located in Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, and Baltimore County.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Washington County Gaming Commission that distributes funds collected from charitable gaming operations (tip jar sales) within Washington County to eligible non-profit organizations. Grants are awarded from the Washington County Gaming Fund through a competitive application and scoring process in accordance with state statute and county regulations. The Commission reviews applications and determines award amounts and terms based on the application review and scoring process. Funds derived from tip jar gaming collections are allocated to local charitable organizations, with 50% of gaming funds statutorily allocated to the Washington County Volunteer Fire & Rescue Association; remaining funds available for other local charities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded from the Washington County Gaming Fund, which is funded by charitable gaming operations revenue. The exact grant amounts and terms are determined through the competitive application and scoring process conducted by the Gaming Commission in accordance with state statute and county regulations. Funds can be used for Health and Human Services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities. Maximum grant amount is $100,000 per application. Organizations may submit multiple applications for separate projects. All funds must be expended within one year of receipt and used exclusively within Washington County.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credit program offering property tax credits, employment (income) tax credits, and personal property tax credits for businesses and developers in designated Enterprise Zones. Approximately 5,500 acres in Washington County within three state-designated Enterprise Zones where economic incentives are available to new and existing businesses that expand through capital investments and/or job creation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying businesses located in designated Enterprise Zones may be eligible for state income tax credits, local real property tax credits, and exemption from commercial building excise tax. Income tax credits: up to $1,000 per non-disadvantaged employee; up to $3,000/$2,000/$1,000 for disadvantaged employees (years 1-3). Real property tax credits: 80% of property taxes on increased assessment (years 1-5), decreasing 70%-30% (years 6-10). No commercial building excise taxes on new construction in zones. Personal property tax credits available in Focus Areas based on personal property assessment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and developers operating in Washington County Enterprise Zones, including new businesses/start-ups, businesses relocating, and existing businesses expanding in designated Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements (building/land acquisition, new construction, rehabilitation), new machinery and equipment, and job creation activities in designated Enterprise Zones
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Approximately 5,500 acres in Washington County within three state-designated Enterprise Zones including the Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone and the Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone. Personal property tax credits available in Focus Areas.
requirements_list: Business must be located in a designated Enterprise Zone
Business must create jobs and/or make capital investments
Application must be submitted prior to project completion and issuance of Use/Occupancy Permits for property tax credits
Property owner must co-sign if developer/company applies on behalf of owner
Employees must meet qualified employee requirements per Maryland Department of Commerce
For employment credits: business must be located, relocating, or newly established in Enterprise Zone
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete applicable sections (C, D, or E) based on credit type requested. Submit application to Linda Spence with all required data. Property owner concurrence/co-signature required for property improvements applications. Contact the Washington County Department of Business Development for application materials and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for individuals who are fallen heroes, providing tax relief on Washington County property taxes. The program provides tax credits to eligible fallen heroes and their dependents. The credit is applied to real property taxes owed to Washington County.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Fallen heroes or their eligible family members and dependents who own real property in Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To reduce property tax liability on real property in Washington County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland only.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Washington County Real Property Tax Credit for Fallen Heroes Application to the Treasurer's Office. Contact the Washington County Treasurer's Office for information and application requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credit granted against County real property taxes based on the amount expended by a taxpayer for restoration or preservation of a historic property.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit equal to 10% of the owner's expense for restoration and preservation of any existing structure up to the total amount of County real estate property taxes. A credit of 5% is allowed for new construction attached to an existing historic structure. Unused credit may be carried forward for up to 5 tax years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners restoring or preserving historic properties designated on the master plan for historic preservation or within historic districts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration or preservation of historic properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be designated as historic sites on the master plan for historic preservation or be within a historic district designated on the master plan in Washington County

Work must be for restoration or preservation of existing structure or new construction attached to existing historic structure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Washington County Planning Department for information and applications. Credit is allowed for the tax year immediately following completion of work.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit limits the annual assessment increase for principal residences. Assessment increase is capped at 10% by the State of Maryland, 5% by Washington County, and 5% by municipalities.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Credit is automatically applied to properties listed as principal residence. Contact the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation if eligible but have not received credit or to learn more.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funding to stimulate and assist organizations, agencies, and businesses in Washington County in developing tourism attractions, enhancing economic development, and supporting cultural and recreational projects. The program helps organizations undertake activities that would not happen without special funding and aims to establish activities and events that can eventually grow and succeed independently. Funds can be allocated for personnel, operating expenses, equipment, advertising, facility rental, contracted services, and other project-related costs intended to generate hotel/motel room nights and community/economic impact.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded from Washington County's 6% hotel rental tax, which are invested back into the community through the Convention and Visitors Bureau, local municipalities, and designated local projects. Funds can be allocated for personnel, operating expenses, equipment, advertising, facility rental, contracted services, and other project-related costs intended to generate hotel/motel room nights and community/economic impact. Projects are classified under categories: Develop Tourism Attraction, Economic Development, Cultural, or Recreational.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Washington County municipalities, businesses, organizations, residents, and visitors interested in tourism development, economic development, or cultural and recreational projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing tourism attractions, enhancing economic development, supporting cultural and recreational projects, tourism advertising and marketing, and other project-related expenses. Funds may support personnel, operating expenses, equipment, advertising, facility rental, and contracted services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must qualify under Maryland Code, Article 24, 9-318
Must generate overnight stays in the County
Should encourage support of County business, restaurants and attractions
Should reach a broad segment of the community
Should seek multiple funding sources and not rely solely on Hotel Rental Tax Funding
Must yield benefits to the community
Should promote cooperation among event organizers
Must enhance or improve the community
Organization must not have budget deficits prior to application
Cannot be for normal/routine operating and administrative expenses
Cannot support political candidates or legislation
Cannot fund endowments
Must demonstrate hotel/motel room nights generated
Must describe community and local economic impact
Must submit all receipts and supporting documentation
Expenses must align with approved event/project
Must complete grant report form with all project details
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Hotel Rental Tax Funding Application form. The application must be saved to your computer before completing. Guidelines and instructions are provided in the Program Guidelines document. Submit completed grant report form with project details, expense breakdown, attendance figures, and impact description to the Office of Grant Management.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that accelerates land preservation easement purchases by allowing agricultural landowners to sell their development rights to the County. Payment is made through an Installment Purchase Agreement over ten years at a fixed interest rate. Qualifying landowners sell their agricultural preservation easement to the County and receive payment over ten years, with ten percent of the principal paid at settlement and ten percent paid annually for the remaining nine years, plus a fixed interest rate.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying landowners sell their agricultural preservation easement to the County and receive payment through an Installment Purchase Agreement. structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proceeds from the sale of agricultural preservation easements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County only.
requirements_list: Property must meet minimum qualifications as agricultural land
Applicant must own the land
Easement covers entire contiguous acreage minus one acre per existing dwelling on the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowner applies to the County. Upon approval, an Installment Purchase Agreement is created detailing the total purchase price and payment terms.

structured_extraction.program_name: LMB ENOUGH Capacity Building Fiscal Year 2026
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding through the Governor's Office for Children (GOC) supporting the ENOUGH Initiative and Local Management Board (LMB) work to support innovative programs that bridge transportation and healthcare services in underserved communities of Washington County. The program aims to provide greater access to healthcare for seniors, individuals with disabilities, and low-income households with children who face significant mobility barriers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Washington County intends to award 1-3 grants with individual awards ranging from $10,000.00 to $40,000.00. The total funding pool is $74,000.00. The performance period runs from May 15, 2026 through September 30, 2026. Funding may support operating expenses, capital investments, or a combination thereof for capacity building in three priority areas: Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT), Expansion of Existing Networks, and Last-Mile Solutions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 6, 2026, at 3:00pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and local government agencies providing services to Washington County residents, particularly seniors, individuals with disabilities, and low-income households with children facing significant mobility barriers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports innovative programs addressing non-emergency medical transportation (NEMT) for primary care, dialysis, mental health, and pharmacy pickups; expansion of existing volunteer driver programs or specialized transit services; or last-mile solutions for residents in underserved areas not currently reached by public transit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must provide services exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland. Organizations must be located in Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or a local government entity
Must be in 'Good Standing' with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must provide services exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland
Must demonstrate a proven track record of fiscal responsibility and programmatic effectiveness
Projects must address at least one priority area: Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT), Expansion of Existing Networks, or Last-Mile Solutions
No unpaid obligations to any government entity
Must not discriminate based on race, creed, sex, age, color, national origin, physical or mental disabilities
Data collection and reporting systems must be in place
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit an electronic application with all required documents to cahrens@washco-md.net by Friday, March 6, 2026, at 3:00pm. The application includes a Statement of Need, Organizational Capacity description, Program Plan, and Collaborations/Partnerships sections. Required documents include the Application Submission Form, budget narrative, letters of support, 501(c)(3) nonprofit determination letter, and proof of Good Standing with SDAT. Applications are subject to public disclosure under the Maryland Public Information Act.

structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation service that provides general purpose transportation for elderly individuals age 60 and over and individuals with disabilities who cannot use fixed-route buses. Participants purchase vouchers at a reduced rate to cover taxi fares, saving at least 50% compared to regular taxi costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants purchase vouchers at a reduced rate from the Washington County Transit office or by mail. Vouchers can be purchased in a set number per month and provide at least 50% savings on taxi fares. Vouchers come in various denominations and are used to pay drivers directly. Business checks, personal checks, money orders, and credit cards are accepted for purchase. Vouchers expire June 30 of each year.
structured_extraction.contact_email: Transit Department email available through website
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 60 and over and individuals with disabilities who cannot utilize Washington County Transit fixed-route buses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General purpose transportation via taxi services for eligible individuals who cannot use fixed-route buses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or over, or have a documented disability
If under age 60, applicant must have application certified by a healthcare professional acknowledging disability
Must have an annually updated application on file with Washington County Transit
Cannot utilize Washington County Transit fixed-route buses for one or more reasons
Applications expire June 30 of every year and must be renewed annually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Washington County Transit office at 240-313-2750 to have an application mailed, or pick one up in person at 1000 West Washington Street, Hagerstown, Maryland. If under age 60, have your application certified by a healthcare professional. Mail or drop off the completed application at the WCT office (faxes not accepted). You will be notified by mail of your eligibility. Once approved, purchase vouchers at the WCT office or by mail using checks, money orders, or credit cards.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Maryland Economic Development Fund Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds infrastructure projects to support economic development, stimulate private investment, and create jobs in rural Maryland counties. Eligible uses include public infrastructure such as utilities, transportation, and broadband; commercial or industrial properties for business parks; workforce development and entrepreneurship initiatives, and planning and feasibility studies. Administered through five tri-county councils serving rural regions of Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds up to $10,000,000 per award with no matching requirements provided by the Maryland Department of Commerce to state tri-county councils for infrastructure projects that support economic development in rural regions. Funds can be used for developing public infrastructure, purchasing commercial or industrial properties, workforce development, planning and feasibility studies, capital and operational expenses (administrative costs capped at 3% of award). All funds must be expended within 24 months of grant award date.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 31 – hard deadline set by Maryland Department of Commerce; extensions will not be granted. Submit project applications to county by July 26, then to tri-county council by August 10, and to Maryland Department of Commerce by August 31.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State tri-county councils serving rural regions of Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, Washington counties), local government entities, institutions of higher education, workforce development organizations, and not-for-profit entities coordinating with local jurisdictions to identify priority projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public infrastructure such as utilities, transportation, and broadband to support business attraction, retention or expansion; commercial or industrial property purchases for business parks; industry-specific infrastructure for manufacturing, clean energy, life sciences, cybersecurity, and agribusiness; workforce development; entrepreneurship and innovation stimulation; planning and feasibility studies; and capital and operational expenses (up to 3% administrative costs). Direct private sector incentives, subsidies, grants, loans, and residential or housing projects are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rural counties served by the state's five tri-county councils in Maryland, specifically Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties.
requirements_list: Projects must be proposed by state tri-county councils
Regional councils must coordinate with local jurisdictions to identify priority projects
Projects must support economic development activity
Projects must stimulate private investment or grow jobs
Granting land or buildings purchased or constructed with funds to private entities is prohibited, but sale or lease of properties is permitted
Project must have significant economic development impact
Project summary required (250 words or less)
Budget documentation required with funding sources, amounts, and uses
Primary contact information required
All funds must be expended within 24 months of grant award date
Interim reports due at 6-month and 18-month marks
Final report due at end of year 2
Demographic and MBE information required for all contractors and vendors
Funds not expended within 24 months subject to clawback
Identification of existing projects previously funded by Maryland Department of Commerce required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit project summary form by August 31 with project details, contact information, budget documentation (including funding sources and amounts), and description of economic development impact (250 words or less) to the appropriate tri-county council and Maryland Department of Commerce. Projects must be submitted through county by July 26, then to tri-county council by August 10.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive program providing tax incentives, workforce training, infrastructure connectivity, capital investment support, and energy efficiency financing for businesses in Washington County, Maryland. Includes real property tax credits for job creation and capital investment, training reimbursement, utility incentives, C-PACE loans for energy efficiency projects, brownfield revitalization tax credits, and apprenticeship programs. Multiple tax credit and incentive programs designed to support business expansion, relocation, job creation, and capital investment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Job Creation & Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit Program (6-15 years of tax credits). New Jobs Tax Credit Program (6 years of tax credits). Brownfield Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) (50-70% real property tax credits for 5-10 years). C-PACE Program (commercial clean energy loans with up to 100% fixed-rate financing, 20-year payback). Research & Development Equipment Tax Exemption. Manufacturing Machinery & Equipment Tax Exemption. Business Inventory Tax Exemption. Maryland Sales & Use Tax Exemptions on equipment and materials. Apprenticeship & Training Grants (up to $4,500 per worker through Western Maryland Consortium). One Maryland Tax Credit: Income tax credit against state taxes up to $5 million. State Lottery Terminal Fund (SLoT): Loans $10,000-$500,000. Rural Business Development Grants (RBDG) up to $500,000. Technical Assistance Grants for professional services. Western Maryland Revolving Loan Fund (WMD RLF): Working capital and fixed asset financing. Telecommunications Infrastructure Loans & Guarantees.

Cannot have unpaid or past due obligations to the Washington County Treasurer or any other government entity
Must have submitted required grant reports and have no outstanding obligations to the County
Organizations may only submit one request for funding
Must be able to expend awarded funds within one year of receipt
Must provide measurable outcomes and program evaluation processes
Must practice non-discriminatory practices
Must provide IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter
Must provide most recent audit or detailed financial statement
Must provide most recent IRS Form 990
Must provide W-9 & Vendor Remittance Form if organization has not previously received County funds or has address change
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations must complete a grant application on approved forms and submit one paper hard copy (one-sided printing, no dividers/binding) by December 20, 2022, at 3:00 pm. Applicants must include a recent audit or detailed financial statement, IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter, most recent IRS Form 990, and W-9 & Vendor Remittance Form if applicable. Application must include cover page, statement of need, organization capacity and staffing plan, program/project plan, collaborations/partnerships, sustainability/continuity plan, authorized official signature, and budget narrative spreadsheet. Applications are evaluated on a point-based system: Statement of Need (20 points), Organizational Capacity (15 points), Program/Project Plan (25 points), Collaborations (15 points), and Sustainability (15 points). A grant report must be submitted after funds are received providing an accounting of the funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: High Performance Commercial Building Tax Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A three-year property tax credit program for commercial buildings achieving LEED certification (Silver, Gold, or Platinum). Applies to new construction, renovation, or remodeling projects. Property owners receive tax credits applied against the increase in assessed value of their property. The credit is 30% of the increase for LEED Platinum certification, 25% for Gold certification, and 20% for Silver certification. Buildings must maintain their certification level for the three-year credit period, and applicants must submit annual letters of compliance. Credits cannot be reapplied after the three-year period and can be combined with other State, County, and municipal tax credits.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three-year property tax credit applied against the increase in assessed value of a property. The credit is 30% of the increase for LEED Platinum certification, 25% for Gold certification, and 20% for Silver certification. Credit cannot exceed the increase in assessed property value and cannot be carried over to another tax year. Credit is non-renewable after the three-year period. Can be combined with other State, County, and municipal tax credits provided the cumulative total does not exceed the property tax levied.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must apply within 1 year after building receives LEED certification
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial building owners in Washington County completing new construction, renovation, or remodeling projects to achieve LEED certification.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction for commercial buildings achieving LEED Silver, Gold, or Platinum certification through new construction, renovation, or remodeling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: The property must be a commercial building.
The building must achieve a LEED Silver, Gold, or Platinum rating from USGBC.
The building must achieve certification through LEED-NC, LEED-EB, or LEED-CS rating systems.
A use and occupancy certificate is required.
The application must be submitted within one year of the building receiving its LEED certification.
The building must maintain its certification level for the three-year credit period.
Applicants must submit an annual compliance letter attesting that conditions remain unchanged.
Written notice of any anticipated changes impacting LEED certification must be provided.
All drawings, specifications, and supporting documentation must be retained.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, the building owner submits a completed application form with LEED certification documentation and a copy of their LEED certification request. After the project is finished, the owner must provide a use and occupancy certificate and proof of final LEED certification. Annually, applicants must submit a compliance letter attesting that conditions remain unchanged and provide written notice of any anticipated changes impacting certification. The Washington County Department of Business Development reviews the materials to approve the tax credit. Contact the Department at 240-313-2280 or edcinfo@hagerstownedc.org for application materials and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credit program for qualified businesses that expand or locate and increase employment in Washington County. The program provides six to fifteen years of tax credits on the County portion of real estate taxes based on investment and job creation thresholds. Three credit options are available: Section 4(a) for existing businesses expanding by at least 1,500 sq. ft. with 1+ new jobs; Section 4(b) for new businesses obtaining 2,500+ sq. ft. with 5+ new jobs; and Section 4(c) for major investments of $10,000,000+ with 100+ new jobs. Priority Funding Area location is required, and Enterprise Zone locations are not eligible.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit program with three options: Section 4(a) provides 52% credit years 1-2, 39% years 3-4, 26% years 5-6. Section 4(b) provides 30% credit years 1-2, 20% years 3-4, 10% years 5-6. Section 4(c) provides 100% credit years 1-5, 75% years 6-10, 50% years 11-15. Credits are applied to the County portion of real estate taxes for up to fifteen years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, before project construction is complete
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing businesses expanding operations or new businesses locating in Washington County that meet specific investment and job creation thresholds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits applied to County portion of real estate taxes for job creation and capital investments in Washington County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business property must be located in a Priority Funding Area in Washington County. Businesses located in an Enterprise Zone are not eligible for this program.
requirements_list: Must be located in a Priority Funding Area.
Cannot be located in an Enterprise Zone.
Submit an application before construction is complete.
Meet specific investment thresholds
Meet specific job creation thresholds
Section 4(a): Obtain at least 1,500 square feet new or expanded premises and employ at least 1 new permanent full-time employee during 12-month period paying at least 150% of federal minimum wage
Section 4(b): Obtain at least 2,500 square feet and employ at least 5 new permanent full-time employees during 24-month period paying at least 150% of federal minimum wage
Section 4(c): Invest $10,000,000 in capital improvements and create 100 new permanent full-time employees
Must provide annual employment reports to maintain the credit.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, a business must notify the county of its intent to apply for the credit. Then, it submits an application to the Department of Business Development before finishing construction. Submit the Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit Application Packet. The department will certify the business if it is eligible. After certification and project completion, the business must create the required number of new jobs. The business must submit yearly reports on employment to maintain the credit. Contact the Washington County Department of Business Development for application materials and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Senator George C. Edwards Fund provides grants and loans to capital infrastructure projects and business development projects to improve economic conditions in Western Maryland. The fund seeks projects that make substantial economic impact, bringing significant employment opportunities and/or increasing the tax base in the region.
structured_extraction.agency: Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board (Tri-County Council of Western Maryland)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides grants and loans for two categories: Infrastructure Funding (broadband connectivity, road access improvement, utility connections, property purchases, building or housing construction and improvements) and Business Development Funding (business expansion and job creation). Infrastructure projects require a minimum 20% match of total project costs from local government, the business itself, or another source. Business development projects require a minimum 10% match. Both categories must lead to creating new jobs that pay at least 120% of the State Minimum Wage. The minimum grant amount is $150,000, though projects less than this amount may be considered on a case-by-case basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, local governments, and organizations proposing capital infrastructure or business development projects in Western Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital infrastructure projects (broadband connectivity, road access improvement, utility connections, property purchases, building or housing construction and improvements) and business development projects that create new jobs paying at least 120% of the State Minimum Wage and increase the tax base in Western Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Western Maryland counties served by the Tri-County Council of Western Maryland
requirements_list: Project must make substantial economic impact with significant employment opportunities or tax base increases
New jobs created must pay at least 120% of the State Minimum Wage
Infrastructure projects require minimum 20% match of total project costs from local government, business, or other source
Business development projects require minimum 10% match of total project costs from local government, business, or other source
Higher matches given preference
Minimum grant amount is $150,000 (projects under this may be considered case-by-case)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Inquiries should be made to the Executive Director Jake Shade, a Member of the Board, or the Economic Development Director in the county where the project will take place. The Board reviews, evaluates, and rates applications for funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 12-month, FAA Part 147 Certified training program that prepares students for Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) certification, a highly valued credential in the aviation industry. The program creates a pipeline of mechanics and enhances the aviation and aeronautics sector for the region. A $3.298 million grant from the Rural Maryland Economic Development Fund established the program, which provides training with an initial cohort of 25 students to prepare students for FAA A&P certification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $3.298 million grant from the Rural Maryland Economic Development Fund established the program, which provides 12-month aviation maintenance training with initial cohort of 25 students. The program prepares students for FAA A&P certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Federal Communications Commission program that helps families and households struggling to afford internet service. It provides a monthly discount toward broadband service and a one-time discount to purchase computers or tablets from participating providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive a discount of up to $50 per month towards broadband service. Households can also receive a one-time discount of up to $100 to purchase a laptop, desktop computer, or tablet from participating providers if they contribute more than $10 and less than $50 toward the purchase price.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and households struggling to afford internet service during the COVID-19 pandemic who meet income or assistance program eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Broadband service payments and purchase of laptops, desktop computers, or tablets from participating providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide through participating broadband providers in your state or territory.
requirements_list: Household member has income at or below 135% of Federal Poverty Guidelines or participates in certain assistance programs such as SNAP, Medicaid, or Lifeline

Approved to receive benefits under the free and reduced-price school lunch program or school breakfast program, including through the USDA Community Eligibility Provision in the 2019-2020 or 2020-2021 school year
Received a Federal Pell Grant during the current award year

Experienced a substantial loss of income due to job loss or furlough since February 29, 2020, and the household had a total income in 2020 at or below $99,000 for single filers and $198,000 for joint filers
Meets the eligibility criteria for a participating provider's existing low-income or COVID-19 program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible households can apply in three ways: contact their preferred participating broadband provider directly to learn about their application process, go to GetEmergencyBroadband.org to apply online and find participating providers, or call 833-511-0311 to request a mail-in application and return it with copies of documents showing proof of eligibility to the Emergency Broadband Support Center in London, Kentucky. After receiving an eligibility determination, households can contact their preferred service provider to select an Emergency Broadband Benefit eligible service plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to upgrade failing septic systems with Best Available Technology (BAT) units for nitrogen removal to reduce nutrients entering the Chesapeake Bay. The program serves Worcester County property owners and covers the cost and installation of BAT units plus two years of maintenance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The grant covers the cost and installation of Best Available Technology (BAT) septic units plus two years of maintenance. For qualifying low-income homeowners, the grant may also cover drainfield costs. The grant can also be used to pay for abandoning an existing septic system and connecting to public sewerage with enhanced nutrient removal. The grant does not cover permit or recordation fees. Funding is prioritized based on system failure status, location within critical areas, and property income levels.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Worcester County property owners with septic systems, especially those with failing systems or systems located in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area or Maryland Coastal Bays Critical Area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The grant money may be used for the cost and installation of Best Available Technology units plus two years of maintenance, and for costs to abandon an existing septic system and connect to public sewerage with enhanced nutrient removal. For qualifying low-income owners, the grant may also cover drainfield costs. The grant cannot be used for drainfield costs (except for qualifying low-income owners), permit fees, or recordation fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Worcester County. Properties within 1,000 feet of mean high tide (Chesapeake Bay Critical Area and Maryland Coastal Bays Critical Area) receive highest priority. Other properties may be eligible depending on funding availability.
requirements_list: Property owner must be a Worcester County resident
Owner must submit application form with required documentation
Owner must provide proof of income
Owner must allow Department of Environmental Programs to conduct initial site inspection
If approved, owner must sign and record an agreement acknowledging the system must be maintained by a qualified operator for as long as the septic system is in use
Owner must allow county to conduct periodic onsite inspections to ensure the BAT unit operates satisfactorily
If property has access to public sewer, the grant request may be denied
Residential properties are evaluated based on homeowner income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the application form. Submit the application to the Department of Environmental Programs by mail, fax, or email along with proof of income and required documentation. The department will review the application, conduct an initial site inspection, and assess availability of public sewer. If approved, the property owner must sign and record an agreement with the county.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants and low-interest loans to owner-occupied properties in Worcester County for general rehabilitation work and lead abatement services to bring homes up to the County's Minimum Livability Code. Grants are secured with a recorded property lien and have terms of 5-15 years for general rehabilitation with no payment due unless the property is sold or refinanced. Lead abatement grants have no minimum term and require no repayment if the house is sold or refinanced, with a 10% match required if family income exceeds 80% of the median. Low-interest loans (0-7% interest) are also available with payments scaled to the family's ability to repay, and loans may be completely deferred. The full loan balance is due when the property is sold, transferred, or refinanced. Up to 40% of rehabilitation work may be cosmetic in nature.
